Outdated or unpatched e-commerce platform/plugins
Insufficient monitoring of checkout page script integrity
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: Content Security Policy (CSP) restricting script sources on payment pages
Subresource Integrity (SRI) for third-party scripts
Checkout page script integrity monitoring/tamper detection
ITID-51242.detection: Detectable via CSP violation reporting, script integrity monitoring, and outbound network monitoring from the web tier; often first identified by card-brand fraud pattern analysis rather than internal tooling.
ITID-51242.response: Remove the malicious script immediately, rotate any exposed keys/credentials for third-party integrations, and engage a PFI for scope assessment.
metrics: Duration skimmer was active before detection
Transactions/customers potentially affected
Third-party scripts under active integrity monitoring
ITID-51242.notes: Cross-referenced against ITID-30000's Exploitation/web-application-attack leaves during overlap review; no existing leaf there specifically covers checkout-page card skimming, so this leaf is scoped strictly to the PII/payment-card breach-classification angle rather than the general web-application-compromise angle.

playbook.name: E-Commerce Payment Page Skimmer (Magecart-Style Web Skimming)
playbook.description: Malicious JavaScript injected into the checkout page skimmed customer payment card data submitted during online transactions.

steps.title: Detect the malicious skimming script on the checkout page
steps.desc: Confirm the presence of unauthorized JavaScript on the payment/checkout page via code integrity monitoring, Content Security Policy violation reports, or third-party skimmer-detection alerts.
steps.guidance: Compare current checkout-page code/dependencies against a known-good baseline; check for compromised third-party scripts/tag-manager entries as the injection vector.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious script identified with its exfiltration destination.
steps.abort: If no unauthorized script is found, close as false positive with documentation.

steps.title: Determine the injection window and volume of transactions exposed
steps.desc: Use deployment history, CDN/tag-manager logs, and web server access logs to establish when the skimmer was injected and how many checkout transactions occurred during that window.
steps.outcome: A defined exposure window and transaction count for PCI forensic reporting.

steps.title: Remove the malicious script and block its exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Immediately strip the injected code from the checkout page (or roll back to a known-good deployment) and block the attacker's exfiltration domain at the network/CDN level.
steps.guidance: Preserve the malicious script and a copy of the compromised page before remediation for forensic purposes.
steps.outcome: No further card data is being skimmed from the checkout page.

steps.title: Engage a PCI Forensic Investigator and notify the acquirer/card brands
steps.desc: Engage a PCI SSC-approved forensic investigator and notify the acquiring bank/card brands per PCI-DSS requirements once card-data compromise is confirmed.
steps.outcome: PFI engaged and required notifications made within contractual timeframes.

steps.title: Close the injection vector (CMS, third-party tag, supply-chain compromise)
steps.desc: Identify and remediate how the script was injected — compromised admin credentials, vulnerable plugin/CMS, or a compromised third-party JavaScript dependency — and patch/rotate accordingly.
steps.guidance: Magecart-style attacks frequently originate from a compromised third-party script; audit all externally loaded scripts on the payment page.
steps.outcome: The injection vector is closed and cannot be reused.

steps.title: Implement Subresource Integrity and a strict Content Security Policy on payment pages
steps.desc: Deploy SRI hashes and a restrictive CSP limiting which scripts can execute/exfiltrate on the checkout page to prevent future skimmer injection from succeeding silently.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized scripts are blocked or immediately flagged going forward.

steps.title: Validate checkout page integrity and resume normal e-commerce operations
steps.desc: Confirm with the PFI and internal validation that the checkout page is clean before resuming full transaction processing.
steps.outcome: Checkout environment confirmed clean and fully operational.

steps.title: Complete PCI incident report and harden web supply-chain security practices
steps.desc: Document findings and remediation for the acquirer/card brands, and track adoption of ongoing third-party script monitoring and SRI/CSP enforcement.
steps.outcome: Formal PCI incident report filed with tracked remediation actions.

ITID-51243.def: An incident in which a payment processor, payment gateway, or card-transaction switch used by the organization is itself compromised, exposing card data the organization's transactions passed through it.
ITID-51243.purpose: Captures payment card data breaches originating at a third-party payment processor or gateway rather than the merchant's own systems.
scopeIncludes: Breach of a third-party payment gateway/processor's infrastructure
Compromise of a hosted payment page (iframe/redirect) provided by the processor
Processor-side tokenization or vaulting system breach
scopeExcludes: POS malware within the merchant's own environment (POS Malware leaf)
Web skimming injected into the merchant's own checkout page (E-Commerce Payment Page Skimmer leaf)
Physical skimming devices (Physical Card Skimming Device Breach leaf)
ITID-51243.severity: High; a processor-level breach can affect many merchants simultaneously and card data volumes are typically large.
ITID-51243.priority: P1 upon notification from the processor; treat as an active incident requiring coordinated response until scope is confirmed.
ITID-51243.escalation: Escalate to PCI compliance and legal immediately upon processor notification; review the processor agreement for liability, notification timelines, and shared PCI DSS responsibility (SAQ) obligations.
indicators: Formal breach notification from the payment processor/gateway
Card brand alert citing the processor as a common point of compromise across multiple merchants
Unusual authorization/settlement discrepancies traced to the processor
vectors: Compromise of the processor's own infrastructure (credential theft, vulnerability exploitation)
Insider misuse within the processor's organization
Compromise of the processor's tokenization/vaulting environment
rootCauses: Insufficient due diligence on processor PCI DSS compliance status prior to selection
Lack of contractual notification-timeliness requirements with the processor
Absence of monitoring for processor-side anomalies (settlement/authorization irregularities)
controls: Contractual PCI DSS compliance validation for payment processors
Tokenization to minimize card data held/transmitted outside the processor
Ongoing monitoring of processor security posture and incident history
ITID-51243.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; the organization typically learns of the breach via processor or card-brand notification rather than its own monitoring, since the compromise occurs outside its infrastructure.
ITID-51243.response: Confirm scope of affected transactions with the processor, assess contractual and PCI DSS obligations, and coordinate merchant-level notification as required by card brands.
metrics: Time from processor notification to internal escalation
Transactions/cardholders potentially affected
Processors under active security monitoring/review
sops: Third-Party Payment Processor Breach Response SOP
ITID-51243.notes: This leaf's causal chain is deliberately vendor-side, distinguishing it from POS malware and web-skimming leaves where the compromise occurs within the merchant's own environment.

playbook.name: Payment Card Data Breach via Compromised Payment Processor/Gateway
playbook.description: A third-party payment processor or gateway used by the organization was breached, exposing payment card transactions routed through it.

steps.title: Receive and validate the processor's/gateway's breach notification
steps.desc: Formally receive the processor's breach notification and validate the claim against the organization's own transaction records and contractual relationship.
steps.guidance: Request the processor's forensic report and confirm which of the organization's transactions/merchant IDs were within scope.
steps.outcome: Confirmed understanding of the processor's breach and its relevance to the organization.
steps.abort: If the organization's transactions were not within the breached scope, document and close.

steps.title: Independently determine transaction volume and time window affected
steps.desc: Cross-reference the processor's stated compromise window against the organization's own transaction logs to independently verify scope.
steps.guidance: Do not rely solely on the processor's self-reported scope; card-brand/acquirer guidance may require independent verification.
steps.outcome: An independently verified scope of affected transactions.

steps.title: Suspend or reroute transactions through the compromised processor if still active
steps.desc: If the processor's compromise is ongoing, work with the processor or switch to an alternate gateway to stop routing further transactions through the compromised path.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with the processor's incident response team and the acquiring bank on timing to avoid unnecessary business disruption if containment is already confirmed on their end.
steps.outcome: No further transactions are exposed to the compromised processor infrastructure.
steps.abort: If the processor confirms containment is already complete, this step may be marked complete based on their attestation.

steps.title: Engage a PCI Forensic Investigator and notify the acquirer/card brands
steps.desc: Engage a PCI SSC-approved forensic investigator for the organization's own scope assessment and notify the acquiring bank/card brands per PCI-DSS requirements, in coordination with the processor's own notifications.
steps.outcome: PFI engaged and required notifications made, avoiding duplicate or conflicting reporting with the processor.

steps.title: Confirm processor remediation and reassess the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation of the processor's remediation and root-cause fix, and reassess the organization's vendor risk rating and contractual security requirements for that processor.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring updated PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance (AOC) or a third-party assessment before continuing the relationship.
steps.outcome: Confirmed processor remediation and updated vendor risk documentation.

steps.title: Evaluate alternate or redundant payment processing paths
steps.desc: Assess whether the organization should diversify payment processing across multiple gateways/processors to reduce single-point-of-failure risk for future processor-side compromises.
steps.outcome: Reduced dependency risk on any single payment processor going forward.

steps.title: Execute customer and regulatory notifications as required
steps.desc: Notify affected customers and regulators per PCI-DSS/state law requirements, coordinating messaging with the processor where appropriate.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met within required timeframes.

steps.title: Review third-party payment processor security oversight
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to payment-processor vendor assessment criteria and contractual security/notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked vendor-oversight improvements.

ITID-51244.def: An incident in which a physical skimming device (an overlay on an ATM/POS card reader, a hidden internal skimmer, or a shimmer inserted into a card slot) is used to capture card data directly from the magnetic stripe or chip interface during a legitimate transaction.
ITID-51244.purpose: Captures payment card data theft via physical skimming hardware attached to a card reader, an entirely physical-world attack vector.
scopeIncludes: Overlay skimmer attached to an ATM or gas pump card reader
Internal skimmer/shimmer installed inside a POS terminal or ATM
Hidden camera or PIN pad overlay used alongside a skimmer to capture PINs
scopeExcludes: Software-based POS malware capturing card data digitally (POS Malware leaf)
Web-based checkout page skimming (E-Commerce Payment Page Skimmer leaf)
Breach at the processor/gateway level (Compromised Payment Processor leaf)
ITID-51244.severity: Medium-High; individual devices typically affect fewer cardholders than a digital breach, but the physical/covert nature complicates detection and requires physical security involvement.
ITID-51244.priority: P2, escalating to P1 upon confirmed device discovery or a cluster of related fraud reports at a single location.
ITID-51244.escalation: Escalate to physical security and PCI compliance immediately upon discovery; preserve the device for law enforcement and notify the acquiring bank/card brands.
indicators: Physical inspection reveals an unauthorized attachment on a card reader
Cluster of fraudulent card use reports tracing to transactions at a single terminal/location
Card reader showing signs of tampering (loose fit, unusual color/texture, security seal broken)
vectors: Attacker physically attaches an overlay skimmer to an unattended or poorly monitored terminal
Attacker gains brief unsupervised access to install an internal skimmer/shimmer
Attacker adds a hidden camera or fake PIN pad overlay to capture PINs alongside the skimmer
rootCauses: Insufficient physical inspection routine for card readers/ATMs
Lack of tamper-evident seals or tamper-detection sensors on terminals
Inadequate physical security monitoring (CCTV coverage, foot traffic) at terminal locations
controls: Routine physical inspection of card readers/ATMs with tamper-evident seals
Tamper-detection sensors integrated into terminal hardware
CCTV coverage of card reader/ATM locations
ITID-51244.detection: No meaningful network or endpoint telemetry; detection relies entirely on physical inspection routines, tamper-detection hardware, and downstream fraud reporting.
ITID-51244.response: Remove and preserve the device, notify law enforcement and the acquiring bank, and inspect all terminals of the same make/model at the location for additional devices.
metrics: Number of skimming devices discovered per period
Time between device installation and discovery (estimated from fraud dating)
Percentage of terminals on a documented physical inspection schedule
detections: CCTV review triggered by fraud pattern reports
ITID-51244.notes: Physical skimming hardware has no clean ATT&CK Enterprise mapping; ATT&CK Enterprise models network/endpoint intrusion techniques and does not cover physical-hardware tampering of payment terminals, so tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty.

playbook.name: Physical Card Skimming Device Breach
playbook.description: A physical skimming device was covertly installed on a card reader (e.g. ATM, gas pump, POS terminal) to capture card data from in-person swipes/inserts.

steps.title: Discover and confirm the physical skimming device
steps.desc: Confirm a reported or discovered skimming device on a card reader through physical inspection, tamper-seal verification, or card-brand CPP fraud-pattern alerts pointing to the location.
steps.guidance: Physically inspect the terminal for tamper evidence (loose components, added overlay, mismatched color/material) and check tamper-evident seal logs if in place.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence (or confirmed absence) of a skimming device.
steps.abort: If inspection finds no device despite the report, document and continue heightened monitoring rather than closing outright.

steps.title: Determine the installation window and number of affected transactions
steps.desc: Use terminal service/maintenance logs, camera footage if available, and transaction records to establish how long the device was in place and how many cards were swiped/inserted during that window.
steps.outcome: A defined exposure window and estimated card count.

steps.title: Remove the skimming device and take the terminal out of service
steps.desc: Physically remove the device, preserve it as evidence, and take the affected terminal offline pending inspection and law-enforcement engagement.
steps.guidance: Do not disturb potential fingerprint/forensic evidence on the device more than necessary; involve physical security/loss prevention.
steps.outcome: The device is removed and the terminal is no longer capturing card data.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement and engage a PCI Forensic Investigator; notify acquirer/card brands
steps.desc: Report the physical skimming device to local law enforcement (a criminal act), and engage a PFI and notify the acquiring bank/card brands per PCI-DSS requirements.
steps.guidance: Physical skimming device cases often support a fraud investigation across multiple merchants — coordinate with law enforcement's existing casework if applicable.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement engaged, PFI retained, and required card-brand notifications made.

steps.title: Inspect and harden all similar terminals against physical tampering
steps.desc: Physically inspect all comparable terminals across locations for similar devices, and deploy anti-skimming hardware (tamper-evident seals, skimmer-detection sensors) where not already present.
steps.outcome: No other terminals are compromised and physical tamper-resistance is improved fleet-wide.

steps.title: Deploy skimmer-detection sensors and increase inspection frequency fleet-wide
steps.desc: Roll out electronic skimmer-detection technology (e.g. Bluetooth/RF skimmer detectors) and increase the frequency of scheduled physical tamper inspections across all terminals.
steps.outcome: Future physical skimming attempts are detected faster fleet-wide.

steps.title: Return terminal to service and notify affected cardholders as required
steps.desc: Restore the terminal to service after confirming it is clean and hardened, and notify affected cardholders/regulators per the PFI's findings and applicable law.
steps.outcome: Terminal returned to safe operation and notification obligations met.

steps.title: Update physical terminal security inspection program
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of routine tamper inspections, staff training to spot skimming devices, and anti-skimming technology investment.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked physical-security improvements.

ITID-51245.def: An intake classification for incidents involving exposure or theft of payment card data where the mechanism (POS malware, web skimming, processor compromise, or physical skimming) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51245.purpose: Captures a confirmed payment card data breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Payment Card Data Breach.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed card data exposure of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
Card fraud patterns identified before the compromise vector is known
scopeExcludes: Confirmed POS malware (POS Malware leaf)
Confirmed web-page skimming (E-Commerce Payment Page Skimmer leaf)
Confirmed processor/gateway compromise (Compromised Payment Processor leaf)
Confirmed physical skimming device (Physical Card Skimming Device Breach leaf)
ITID-51245.severity: High by default given PCI DSS notification obligations, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51245.priority: P1 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the compromise vector is confirmed.
ITID-51245.escalation: Escalate to PCI compliance and the acquiring bank/card brands immediately; do not wait for reclassification before beginning forensic engagement if required by card brand rules.
indicators: Card brand common-point-of-purchase alert with insufficient detail to determine mechanism
Fraud reports referencing the organization with no confirmed technical root cause yet
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard PCI DSS breach intake and triage process
ITID-51245.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51245.response: Rapidly triage to determine the compromise vector and reclassify; engage a PFI in parallel if card brand rules require it regardless of classification status.
metrics: Number of unclassified payment card breach incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51245.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Payment Card Data Breach leaf as soon as the compromise vector is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Payment Card Data Breach
playbook.description: Payment card data was exposed to unauthorized parties through a mechanism not otherwise classified, triggering PCI-DSS incident response obligations.

steps.title: Confirm the card-data exposure and identify the affected system or process
steps.desc: Validate the initial report or alert and identify the system, process, or channel through which payment card data was exposed.
steps.guidance: Pull relevant logs and interview involved staff before assuming a specific vector; consider card-brand CPP alerts as a possible trigger.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure with an identified source.
steps.abort: If the report cannot be substantiated, document and close as unsubstantiated.

steps.title: Scope card data elements and transaction volume affected
steps.desc: Determine which card-data elements (PAN, expiry, CVV, track data) were exposed and estimate the number of affected transactions/cards and the exposure window.
steps.outcome: A defined scope statement for PCI forensic reporting.

steps.title: Stop the ongoing exposure
steps.desc: Take the necessary action to halt further unauthorized access or capture of card data, based on the identified vector.
steps.guidance: Preserve logs and system state before remediation for forensic purposes.
steps.outcome: No further exposure of payment card data is occurring.

steps.title: Engage a PCI Forensic Investigator and notify the acquirer/card brands
steps.desc: Engage a PCI SSC-approved forensic investigator and notify the acquiring bank/card brands per PCI-DSS requirements once card-data compromise is confirmed or suspected.
steps.guidance: This is typically a contractual obligation — do not delay pending full internal investigation.
steps.outcome: PFI engaged and required notifications made within contractual timeframes.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause enabling the exposure
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability, misconfiguration, or process gap identified during investigation, per the PFI's findings.
steps.outcome: The identified root cause can no longer result in card-data exposure.

steps.title: Sweep for related exposure across similar payment systems
steps.desc: Proactively check other payment-processing systems/channels sharing the same root-cause characteristic for similar exposure risk.
steps.outcome: No other payment systems carry the same exposure risk.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and resume normal payment operations
steps.desc: Notify affected customers/regulators as required and confirm the affected system/process has returned to secure, PCI-compliant operation.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and operations confirmed secure.

steps.title: Complete PCI incident report and drive compliance remediation
steps.desc: Document the PFI's findings and remediation, and track required PCI-DSS compliance gaps closed as a result.
steps.outcome: Formal PCI incident report with tracked remediation actions.

ITID-51311.def: An intake and cross-reference classification for incidents involving unauthorized access to or exfiltration of proprietary source code, where the incident is being tracked primarily as a data breach rather than as a targeted espionage campaign.
ITID-51311.purpose: Captures theft of source code classified under the data-breach angle (unauthorized access/exfiltration), as a lone-child cross-reference stub pointing to the more detailed espionage-domain treatment.
scopeIncludes: Source code repository accessed or exfiltrated without a confirmed espionage actor/motive
Source code exposure discovered via a misconfigured repository or leaked credentials
Incidents pending triage to determine whether an espionage classification is more appropriate
scopeExcludes: Source code theft attributed to a targeted, motive-driven espionage actor (ITID-52321 Unclassified/General Source Code Theft under the Espionage domain, and its sibling leaves)
Trade secret exposure not embodied in source code (Trade Secret Exposure leaf)
R&D theft not specific to source code (R&D Theft leaf)
ITID-51311.severity: High; source code exposure can enable downstream vulnerability discovery, counterfeiting, or competitive harm regardless of attacker motive.
ITID-51311.priority: P1 for confirmed exfiltration of production/proprietary source code; P2 for suspected access pending confirmation.
ITID-51311.escalation: Escalate to engineering leadership, legal, and the SOC immediately; assess whether motive/actor indicators point to espionage and reclassify to the espionage-domain leaf if so.
indicators: Unusual bulk clone or download activity from a source code repository
Source code fragments found on a public repository, paste site, or dark web forum
Repository access from an unrecognized account or location
vectors: Compromised developer or CI/CD credentials used to access repositories
Misconfigured repository permissions (public instead of private)
Leaked API tokens/keys granting repository access
rootCauses: Insufficient repository access control review
Secrets/tokens committed to code or leaked via misconfiguration
Lack of monitoring for anomalous repository access/clone volume
mitreTechniques: T1213.003 Data from Information Repositories: Code Repositories
controls: Repository access control and least-privilege review
Secrets scanning and repository misconfiguration detection
Anomalous clone/download volume monitoring
ITID-51311.detection: Source-control platform audit logs and secrets-scanning tooling provide reasonable signal for anomalous access and exposed credentials.
ITID-51311.response: Confirm scope of accessed/exfiltrated code, rotate any exposed secrets, and triage motive/actor indicators to determine whether the espionage-domain classification (ITID-52321 branch) is more appropriate.
metrics: Number of source code exposure incidents per period
Percentage reclassified to the espionage domain after triage
Time to secrets rotation post-incident
ITID-51311.notes: This is a lone-child cross-reference stub. ITID-52321 ('Unclassified / General Source Code Theft (Espionage Context)') under Tier-1 ITID-50000's Espionage domain is the probable cross-reference for source code theft with a confirmed targeted/espionage motive; that branch is being documented in parallel by another author. Use this leaf when motive/actor attribution is absent or the incident is being tracked purely as a data exposure.

playbook.name: Source Code Theft (IP Theft Context)
playbook.description: Proprietary source code was accessed and exfiltrated by an unauthorized internal or external party.

steps.title: Detect anomalous access to source code repositories
steps.desc: Identify unusual clone/download volume, off-hours access, or access from unexpected locations/devices against source-control systems via DLP or repository audit logs.
steps.guidance: Correlate repository access logs with VPN/SSO login context to distinguish legitimate bulk operations (e.g. CI/CD) from anomalous human activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous access event and identified account(s) involved.
steps.abort: If the activity is explained by legitimate automation or authorized bulk export, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine which repositories/code and how much was exfiltrated
steps.desc: Identify the specific repositories, branches, or code modules accessed and exfiltrated, and assess sensitivity (e.g. core product IP vs. non-sensitive tooling).
steps.guidance: Engage engineering leadership to assess the business impact of the specific code exposed.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of exfiltrated code and its sensitivity/value.

steps.title: Revoke access and credentials used for the exfiltration
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the account's repository access, API tokens, and SSH keys used to perform the exfiltration.
steps.guidance: If an insider is implicated, coordinate with HR/Legal before account action per insider-threat evidence-preservation procedures.
steps.outcome: The exfiltration channel is closed and no further access is possible.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal for IP-protection and litigation-hold assessment
steps.desc: Engage Legal immediately to evaluate IP-protection options (cease-and-desist, DMCA/takedown if published, litigation) and to issue a litigation hold on relevant evidence.
steps.guidance: Preserve forensic evidence of the access and exfiltration before any remediation that could alter logs.
steps.outcome: Legal has opened a formal IP-protection assessment with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Review and tighten access controls to source code repositories
steps.desc: Conduct an access review of all repositories containing sensitive IP, removing excessive permissions and enforcing least-privilege and mandatory code-access approval workflows.
steps.outcome: Access to sensitive source code is restricted to those with a demonstrated need.

steps.title: Deploy code watermarking or canary tokens in sensitive repositories
steps.desc: Embed watermarking/canary techniques in high-value source-code repositories to help detect and attribute future unauthorized copies or use.
steps.outcome: Future unauthorized use of the code base is more detectable and attributable.

steps.title: Monitor for external disclosure or use of the stolen code
steps.desc: Monitor public repositories, dark web forums, and competitor products for signs the stolen code has been published or used, informing ongoing legal action.
steps.outcome: Established ongoing monitoring with any findings routed to Legal.

steps.title: Implement DLP and watermarking controls for sensitive code repositories
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of DLP monitoring on source-control bulk-export activity and code watermarking/canary-token techniques to detect future exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection and control improvements.

ITID-51321.def: An intake and cross-reference classification for incidents involving unauthorized access to or exposure of trade secrets (formulas, processes, business methods, confidential know-how) where the incident is being tracked primarily as a data breach rather than as a targeted espionage campaign.
ITID-51321.purpose: Captures exposure of trade secrets classified under the data-breach angle, as a lone-child cross-reference stub pointing to the more detailed espionage-domain treatment.
scopeIncludes: Trade secret documents accessed or exfiltrated without a confirmed espionage actor/motive
Trade secret exposure discovered via misconfigured document repositories or file shares
Incidents pending triage to determine whether an espionage classification is more appropriate
scopeExcludes: Trade secret theft attributed to a targeted, motive-driven espionage actor (the corresponding leaf under ITID-50000's Espionage domain, Intellectual Property Theft branch)
Source code theft (Source Code Theft leaf)
R&D-specific theft (R&D Theft leaf)
ITID-51321.severity: High; trade secret exposure can cause lasting competitive harm regardless of attacker motive.
ITID-51321.priority: P1 for confirmed exfiltration of trade secret material; P2 for suspected access pending confirmation.
ITID-51321.escalation: Escalate to legal, business unit leadership, and the SOC immediately; assess motive/actor indicators and reclassify to the espionage-domain leaf if warranted.
indicators: Unusual bulk access or download of documents tagged as trade secret/confidential
Trade secret material found circulating externally or with a competitor
Access to trade secret repositories from an unrecognized account or location
vectors: Compromised credentials used to access document management or file-share systems
Misconfigured file share or document repository permissions
Insider exfiltration via email, cloud upload, or removable media
rootCauses: Insufficient classification and access control of trade secret material
Lack of DLP coverage on confidential document repositories
Absence of monitoring for anomalous bulk document access
controls: Data classification and access control for trade secret material
DLP on confidential document repositories
Anomalous bulk document access monitoring
ITID-51321.detection: Detection depends on DLP and document repository access logging; coverage is moderate and requires accurate data classification to be effective.
ITID-51321.response: Confirm scope of accessed/exfiltrated material, assess business impact with legal, and triage motive/actor indicators to determine whether the espionage-domain classification is more appropriate.
metrics: Number of trade secret exposure incidents per period
Percentage reclassified to the espionage domain after triage
Confidential repositories under active DLP coverage
detections: DLP alerts on confidential document repositories
ITID-51321.notes: This is a lone-child cross-reference stub. The corresponding Trade Secret Exposure leaf under Tier-1 ITID-50000's Espionage domain (Intellectual Property Theft branch, documented in parallel by another author) is the probable cross-reference for exposures with a confirmed targeted/espionage motive.

playbook.name: Trade Secret Exposure (IP Theft Context)
playbook.description: Confidential trade secret information was accessed and exposed or exfiltrated by an unauthorized internal or external party.

steps.title: Detect anomalous access to trade secret repositories or documents
steps.desc: Identify unusual access patterns (bulk download, off-hours access, access outside job function) to systems or file shares holding designated trade secret material, via DLP alerts or document-access audit logs.
steps.guidance: Confirm the material in question meets the organization's formal trade-secret designation/classification before proceeding, as this affects legal remedies available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous access event and identified account(s) and material involved.
steps.abort: If access is explained by legitimate business need, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine what trade secret material was exposed and its business value
steps.desc: Identify the specific documents/data exposed and engage the business owner to assess competitive or strategic value at risk.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of exposed material and its assessed business impact.

steps.title: Revoke access and credentials used for the exposure
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the account's access to the trade secret repository and any credentials/tokens used in the exposure.
steps.guidance: If an insider is implicated, coordinate with HR/Legal before account action per insider-threat evidence-preservation procedures.
steps.outcome: The exposure channel is closed.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal for trade-secret protection and litigation-hold assessment
steps.desc: Engage Legal to evaluate trade-secret protection measures (cease-and-desist, injunctive relief, litigation under trade secret law) and issue a litigation hold on relevant evidence.
steps.guidance: Trade secret protection depends on demonstrating reasonable measures were taken to maintain secrecy — document these measures as part of the legal record.
steps.outcome: Legal has opened a formal protection assessment with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Review and tighten access controls and classification handling for trade secrets
steps.desc: Conduct an access review of systems holding trade secret material, remove excessive permissions, and reinforce classification/handling requirements.
steps.outcome: Access to trade secret material is restricted to those with a demonstrated need.

steps.title: Deploy DRM or watermarking on trade secret documents
steps.desc: Apply DRM controls or visible/invisible watermarking to documents classified as trade secrets to deter and help detect future unauthorized copying.
steps.outcome: Future unauthorized copies of trade secret documents are more detectable and attributable.

steps.title: Monitor for external use or disclosure of the trade secret
steps.desc: Monitor competitor activity, patent filings, and public disclosures for signs the trade secret has been used or exposed, informing ongoing legal action.
steps.outcome: Established ongoing monitoring with findings routed to Legal.

steps.title: Implement DRM/watermarking and classification controls for trade secret material
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of DRM or watermarking on sensitive documents and stronger classification-handling enforcement to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked control improvements.

ITID-51331.def: An intake and cross-reference classification for incidents involving unauthorized access to or exposure of R&D materials (experimental data, prototypes, unpublished research) where the incident is being tracked primarily as a data breach rather than as a targeted espionage campaign.
ITID-51331.purpose: Captures exposure of research and development (R&D) material classified under the data-breach angle, as a lone-child cross-reference stub pointing to the more detailed espionage-domain treatment.

R&D material exposure discovered via a misconfigured research data repository
Incidents pending triage to determine whether an espionage classification is more appropriate
scopeExcludes: R&D theft attributed to a targeted, motive-driven espionage actor (the corresponding leaf under ITID-50000's Espionage domain, Intellectual Property Theft branch)
Finished product plans/blueprints (Product Plans or Blueprints leaf)
General trade secret exposure not specific to R&D (Trade Secret Exposure leaf)

ITID-51331.priority: P1 for confirmed exfiltration of active R&D material; P2 for suspected access pending confirmation.
ITID-51331.escalation: Escalate to R&D leadership, legal, and the SOC immediately; assess motive/actor indicators and reclassify to the espionage-domain leaf if warranted.

R&D material found circulating externally or referenced by a competitor's filings/products
Access to R&D systems from an unrecognized account or location

Misconfigured research data repository permissions
Insider exfiltration of R&D data via email, cloud upload, or removable media

Lack of DLP coverage on R&D data repositories
Absence of monitoring for anomalous bulk R&D data access

Anomalous bulk R&D data access monitoring

ITID-51331.response: Confirm scope of accessed/exfiltrated material, assess business impact with R&D leadership, and triage motive/actor indicators to determine whether the espionage-domain classification is more appropriate.

Percentage reclassified to the espionage domain after triage
R&D repositories under active DLP coverage
detections: DLP alerts on R&D data repositories
Anomalous bulk R&D data access monitoring

The corresponding R&D Theft leaf under Tier-1 ITID-50000's Espionage domain (Intellectual Property Theft branch, documented in parallel by another author) is the probable cross-reference for exposures with a confirmed targeted/espionage motive.

playbook.name: Research and Development (R&D) Theft (IP Theft Context)
playbook.description: Confidential research and development data or materials were accessed and exfiltrated by an unauthorized internal or external party.

steps.title: Detect anomalous access to R&D systems or repositories
steps.desc: Identify unusual access patterns (bulk download, unfamiliar accounts, off-hours activity) to R&D data repositories, lab systems, or electronic lab notebooks via DLP or system audit logs.
steps.guidance: R&D data often spans specialized systems (ELNs, CAD/PLM tools) — ensure logging coverage on these systems specifically, not just general file shares.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous access event and identified account(s) and material involved.
steps.abort: If access is explained by legitimate research collaboration, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine what R&D data was exfiltrated and its development-stage sensitivity
steps.desc: Identify the specific projects/data exposed and engage R&D leadership to assess the stage of development and competitive impact if disclosed or used by a competitor.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of exfiltrated material and its assessed impact.

steps.title: Revoke access and credentials used for the exfiltration
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the account's access to affected R&D systems and any credentials/tokens used.
steps.guidance: If an insider is implicated, coordinate with HR/Legal before account action per insider-threat evidence-preservation procedures.
steps.outcome: The exfiltration channel is closed.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal for IP-protection and litigation-hold assessment
steps.desc: Engage Legal to evaluate protection options (patent-filing acceleration if applicable, litigation) and issue a litigation hold on relevant evidence.
steps.guidance: If the R&D is patent-pending, coordinate urgently with patent counsel given filing-priority implications.
steps.outcome: Legal has opened a formal IP-protection assessment with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Review and tighten access controls to R&D systems
steps.desc: Conduct an access review of R&D repositories and lab systems, removing excessive permissions and enforcing project-based least-privilege access.
steps.outcome: Access to R&D data is restricted to those with a demonstrated project need.

steps.title: Deploy watermarking/DRM on R&D data and lab systems
steps.desc: Apply DRM controls or watermarking to sensitive R&D data and enforce stricter export controls from ELN/PLM systems.
steps.outcome: Future unauthorized extraction of R&D data is more detectable and constrained.

steps.title: Monitor for competitor products or filings reflecting the stolen R&D
steps.desc: Monitor competitor product releases, patent filings, and industry publications for evidence the stolen R&D has been used, informing ongoing legal action.
steps.outcome: Established ongoing monitoring with findings routed to Legal.

steps.title: Implement DLP and watermarking/DRM controls for R&D data
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of DLP monitoring on R&D system bulk-export activity and document watermarking/DRM to deter and detect future theft.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked control improvements.

ITID-51341.def: An intake and cross-reference classification for incidents involving unauthorized access to or exposure of product plans, engineering blueprints, or design specifications where the incident is being tracked primarily as a data breach rather than as a targeted espionage campaign.
ITID-51341.purpose: Captures exposure of product plans or blueprints classified under the data-breach angle, as a lone-child cross-reference stub pointing to the more detailed espionage-domain treatment.

playbook.name: Product Plans or Blueprints Theft (IP Theft Context)
playbook.description: Confidential product plans, designs, or blueprints were accessed and exfiltrated by an unauthorized internal or external party.

steps.title: Detect anomalous access to product design repositories
steps.desc: Identify unusual access patterns (bulk download, unfamiliar accounts, off-hours activity) to CAD/PLM systems or design file shares holding product plans or blueprints, via DLP or system audit logs.
steps.guidance: CAD/PLM systems often have separate logging from general file shares — confirm coverage exists before concluding no anomaly occurred.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous access event and identified account(s) and material involved.
steps.abort: If access is explained by legitimate design collaboration, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine which product plans were exfiltrated and their launch-stage sensitivity
steps.desc: Identify the specific product(s)/designs exposed and engage product leadership to assess impact given the product's development/launch timeline.
steps.guidance: Pre-launch product plans carry acute competitive risk — treat proximity to launch as a severity factor.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of exfiltrated material and its assessed business impact.

steps.title: Revoke access and credentials used for the exfiltration
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the account's access to affected design systems and any credentials/tokens used in the exfiltration.
steps.guidance: If an insider is implicated, coordinate with HR/Legal before account action per insider-threat evidence-preservation procedures.
steps.outcome: The exfiltration channel is closed.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal for IP-protection and litigation-hold assessment
steps.desc: Engage Legal to evaluate protection options (patent-filing acceleration, design-patent/trade-dress protection, litigation) and issue a litigation hold on relevant evidence.
steps.outcome: Legal has opened a formal IP-protection assessment with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Review and tighten access controls to product design systems
steps.desc: Conduct an access review of CAD/PLM systems and design repositories, removing excessive permissions and enforcing project-based least-privilege access.
steps.outcome: Access to product plans is restricted to those with a demonstrated project need.

steps.title: Deploy watermarking/DRM on product design files

steps.title: Monitor for competitor product launches or counterfeit goods reflecting the stolen plans

steps.outcome: Established ongoing monitoring with findings routed to Legal.

steps.title: Implement DLP and watermarking/DRM controls for product design data
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of DLP monitoring on PLM bulk-export activity and design-file watermarking/DRM to deter and detect future theft.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked control improvements.

ITID-51411.def: Unauthorized disclosure or exfiltration of customer bank account numbers and/or routing numbers held by the company, distinguished from broader transaction history or full core-banking database exposure.
ITID-51411.purpose: Classifies breaches specifically exposing customer bank account and routing numbers, the data elements enabling direct ACH/wire fraud.
scopeIncludes: Theft of a customer account-number/routing-number field set from any system (CRM, payment processor integration, support ticketing)
Exposure of stored ACH/wire payment details used for billing or payroll
scopeExcludes: Transaction history disclosure without underlying account/routing numbers (ITID-51412)
Full core-banking database compromise (ITID-51413)
Cryptocurrency wallet data (ITID-5144x)
ITID-51411.severity: High. Account/routing numbers enable direct fraudulent fund transfers against victims.
ITID-51411.priority: P1 given direct financial fraud risk to affected customers.
ITID-51411.escalation: Escalate immediately to fraud/financial-crimes teams and legal/regulatory for breach notification assessment.
indicators: Unusual bulk export/query of fields containing account or routing numbers
Customer reports of unauthorized ACH withdrawals following the incident window
Discovery of exfiltrated account-number datasets on dark web forums
vectors: SQL injection or API abuse against payment-data endpoints
Compromised third-party payment integration
Insider export of banking-detail fields
rootCauses: Storing raw account/routing numbers without tokenization
Insufficient field-level access controls on payment data
Inadequate logging on payment-data queries
controls: Tokenization of stored account/routing numbers
Field-level access controls and query auditing on payment data
DLP on outbound transfer of financial-identifier patterns
ITID-51411.detection: Database query auditing and DLP pattern-matching on account/routing-number formats provide direct detection capability.
ITID-51411.response: Identify affected customers, coordinate with banking partners on fraud monitoring, and initiate regulatory breach notification per applicable financial-data-breach requirements.
metrics: Number of customer accounts with exposed banking identifiers
Time to notify affected customers and banking partners
ITID-51411.notes: Cross-reference: probable overlap with ITID-53xxx digital-payment/fraud leaves for the monetization angle (fraudulent transfers using stolen account data) being developed in parallel; this leaf scopes strictly to the exposure of the data itself.

playbook.name: Customer Bank Account Number/Routing Data Breach Response
playbook.description: Unauthorized access or exfiltration of customer bank account and routing numbers from company systems requiring GLBA/state breach-law notification.

steps.title: Confirm exposure of account/routing number data
steps.desc: Review the alert, log source, or external report to confirm which datasets containing customer bank account and routing numbers were accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Check database access logs, DLP alerts, and any external notification (bank fraud team, customer report, dark-web monitoring) that triggered the case. Identify exact tables/files/fields involved.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of affected records and data fields, with access/exfiltration timeline established.
steps.abort: If no evidence of actual access to account/routing data is found, downgrade to monitoring and document the false-positive rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected customer population and record count
steps.desc: Query the source systems to determine the total number of unique customers and accounts whose bank account/routing data was exposed.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference logs with the customer database to build an accurate affected-record count; this number drives notification thresholds under state breach laws.
steps.outcome: Documented, defensible count of affected customers and accounts.

steps.title: Determine attack vector and entry point
steps.desc: Identify how the attacker or insider obtained access to the systems or exports holding banking data (e.g., compromised credentials, SQL injection, misconfigured export job).
steps.guidance: Review authentication logs, application logs, and recent config changes on the systems storing banking data.
steps.outcome: Root-cause vector identified and documented for containment planning.

steps.title: Revoke compromised credentials and sessions
steps.desc: Immediately disable any compromised accounts, API keys, or active sessions used to access the banking data.
steps.guidance: Force password resets and session invalidation for all implicated accounts; rotate service-account credentials for the affected data store.
steps.outcome: Attacker access path fully cut off; no further access observed post-revocation.

steps.title: Isolate affected data store and restrict exports
steps.desc: Restrict network and application access to the database/system holding banking data to only essential personnel, and disable bulk export functionality temporarily.
steps.guidance: Apply firewall/ACL restrictions and pause any ETL or export jobs touching the affected tables.
steps.outcome: No further data can be extracted from the affected store.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for breach-notification clock
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Compliance immediately given financial account data exposure; establish the regulatory notification timeline under GLBA and applicable state breach-notification statutes.
steps.guidance: Provide Legal with confirmed record counts, states of residence of affected customers, and data fields exposed so they can calculate notification deadlines (often 30-60 days depending on state).
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has opened a formal breach-notification tracking item with deadlines assigned.

steps.title: Close the exploited vulnerability or access gap
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause identified during identification (patch vulnerability, fix misconfiguration, remove unauthorized access grant).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with application/infrastructure owners to apply the fix and verify via re-scan.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability or misconfiguration confirmed remediated.

steps.title: Rotate encryption keys/tokens protecting banking data at rest
steps.desc: Where the affected data store uses field-level encryption or tokenization for account numbers, rotate the relevant keys/tokens.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the data security team on re-encryption of stored banking data if keys may have been exposed.
steps.outcome: Encryption keys rotated with no residual exposure risk.
steps.abort: If encryption was not in use, document as a lessons-learned gap rather than performing this step.

steps.title: Notify affected customers and coordinate credit monitoring
steps.desc: Send breach notifications to affected customers per the Legal-approved timeline, offering credit monitoring/identity protection where required.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Communications and Legal on notification content; ensure call-center scripts are ready for customer inquiries.
steps.outcome: All affected customers notified within the regulatory window; monitoring services active.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review of banking-data safeguards
steps.desc: Document root cause, response timeline, and gaps in banking-data access controls; produce remediation action items.
steps.guidance: Include a review of least-privilege access to banking data stores and whether tokenization/encryption coverage should be expanded.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report with tracked remediation items.

ITID-51412.def: Unauthorized disclosure or exfiltration of customer banking transaction history records (dates, amounts, counterparties, descriptions) without necessarily including raw account or routing numbers.
ITID-51412.purpose: Classifies breaches exposing customer banking transaction history, distinct from exposure of the underlying account/routing identifiers themselves.
scopeIncludes: Theft of transaction logs, statements, or ledger extracts tied to customer accounts
Exposure of spending-pattern or transaction-metadata datasets
scopeExcludes: Exposure of account/routing numbers themselves (ITID-51411)
Full core-banking database compromise encompassing both (ITID-51413)
ITID-51412.severity: Medium-High. Transaction history enables profiling, social engineering, and privacy harm even without direct fraud capability.
ITID-51412.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for large-scale or high-net-worth customer exposure.
ITID-51412.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal for notification assessment; loop in fraud teams if transaction detail could enable targeted social engineering.
indicators: Bulk export of transaction-log tables or reporting datasets
Discovery of transaction-history datasets offered for sale
Anomalous reporting/analytics queries pulling full customer transaction sets
vectors: Compromised reporting/analytics platform access
API abuse against transaction-history endpoints
Insider misuse of read access to transaction data
rootCauses: Overly broad access to transaction-history datasets
Lack of query volume monitoring on financial reporting systems
controls: Row/query-volume anomaly detection on transaction datasets
Least-privilege access to reporting and analytics platforms
DLP on bulk export of transaction records
ITID-51412.detection: Data-access auditing on reporting platforms provides good detection coverage for bulk transaction extraction.
ITID-51412.response: Determine scope of exposed transaction records, assess privacy notification obligations, and monitor for downstream social-engineering attempts against affected customers.
metrics: Number of transaction records exposed
Time to identify exfiltration scope
detections: Bulk data export/DLP alerting on reporting platforms
ITID-51412.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51411 by data type: transaction metadata/history rather than the account-identifying numbers themselves.

playbook.name: Banking Transaction History Data Breach Response
playbook.description: Unauthorized access to or exfiltration of customer banking transaction history records.

steps.title: Confirm transaction-history data exposure
steps.desc: Validate the alert or report indicating transaction history records (dates, amounts, counterparties, merchant data) were accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Review DLP alerts, database query logs, and export logs for the transaction history tables/reports.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of transaction records and date ranges exposed.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, close as false positive with documented rationale.

steps.title: Assess sensitivity and volume of exposed transaction data
steps.desc: Determine whether exposed data includes patterns that reveal sensitive customer behavior (e.g., payments to sensitive merchants) and quantify total records.
steps.guidance: Work with the data owner to classify sensitivity level and total affected customer count.
steps.outcome: Documented sensitivity classification and record count.

steps.title: Trace access path and reporting/BI tool involvement
steps.desc: Determine whether the breach occurred via a reporting/analytics tool, API, or direct database access, since transaction history is often exposed through BI dashboards.
steps.guidance: Review BI platform audit logs and API gateway logs in addition to database logs.
steps.outcome: Access vector and originating tool identified.

steps.title: Revoke access and disable exposed reporting endpoints
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account, API key, or BI report/dashboard that allowed unauthorized access to transaction data.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the BI/analytics team to pull down or restrict the specific report if that was the vector.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access path closed; no further queries against transaction history observed.

steps.title: Restrict transaction-history query scope organization-wide
steps.desc: Temporarily tighten row-level security and query permissions on transaction history data pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Apply emergency row-level security policies limiting queries to need-to-know roles.
steps.outcome: Query surface reduced to only essential personnel.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance on GLBA/state notification obligations
steps.desc: Loop in Legal and Compliance to determine notification requirements given exposure of nonpublic financial information.
steps.guidance: Provide confirmed scope and customer jurisdictions so Legal can start the notification clock.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has an active tracked notification workflow.

steps.title: Remediate the access-control or query vulnerability
steps.desc: Fix the underlying flaw (overly broad report permissions, missing row-level security, compromised credential) that allowed the exposure.
steps.guidance: Validate the fix with a follow-up access review before restoring normal permissions.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Audit and re-baseline all reporting/BI access grants
steps.desc: Review all users/roles with access to transaction-history reports and remove excess privileges.
steps.guidance: Cross-check against job function to ensure least privilege.
steps.outcome: Access grants re-baselined to least privilege.

steps.title: Notify affected customers and restore normal reporting access
steps.desc: Issue customer notifications per Legal guidance and restore reporting access under the tightened controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing of notification with restoration of business-as-usual reporting operations.
steps.outcome: Customers notified; reporting operations resumed under hardened access controls.

steps.title: Review reporting/BI data-governance controls
steps.desc: Document findings and drive remediation of row-level security and reporting access-governance gaps.
steps.guidance: Include recommendations on periodic access recertification for BI tools touching financial data.
steps.outcome: After-action report with tracked governance improvements.

ITID-51413.def: Unauthorized access to and exfiltration from the core banking system's underlying database, resulting in bulk exposure of customer account numbers, routing data, balances, and transaction history in a single event.
ITID-51413.purpose: Classifies the most severe banking-data-leak scenario: direct compromise of the core banking system database itself, exposing account identifiers and transaction history together at scale.
scopeIncludes: Direct database-level compromise of the core banking platform (on-prem or hosted)
Bulk exfiltration events spanning multiple data categories from the banking system of record
scopeExcludes: Isolated exposure of account/routing numbers only (ITID-51411)
Isolated exposure of transaction history only (ITID-51412)
ITID-51413.severity: Critical. This is a full-system compromise with the broadest possible customer financial-data impact.
ITID-51413.priority: P1, treated as a top organizational crisis requiring executive and board notification.
ITID-51413.escalation: Immediate escalation to CISO, executive leadership, legal, regulators, and law enforcement given the scale and regulatory exposure.
indicators: Anomalous privileged database access to the core banking system
Large-volume data transfer out of the core banking environment
Ransomware or extortion notes referencing the core banking database
vectors: Exploitation of a core banking system vulnerability
Compromised privileged database administrator credentials
Supply-chain compromise of a core banking software vendor
rootCauses: Insufficient network segmentation isolating the core banking database
Excessive standing privileged access to production banking data
Delayed patching of core banking infrastructure
controls: Network segmentation and privileged access workstations for core banking systems
Database activity monitoring with real-time alerting
Immutable, monitored backups of core banking data
ITID-51413.detection: Database activity monitoring and network egress monitoring around the core banking environment provide the primary detection surface.
ITID-51413.response: Full incident response activation: containment of the core banking environment, forensic scoping of all data categories affected, and coordinated regulatory/customer notification at scale.
metrics: Total customer records affected
Time to containment of the core banking environment
Regulatory notification timeliness
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
ITID-51413.notes: This is the aggregate/severe sibling of ITID-51411 and ITID-51412; use it only when the compromise spans the core system of record rather than an isolated data category.

playbook.name: Compromised Core Banking System Database Response
playbook.description: Direct compromise of the core banking system database exposing account, balance, and transaction records at scale.

steps.title: Confirm core banking database compromise
steps.desc: Validate indicators that the core banking system's underlying database was directly accessed or exfiltrated (not just an application layer).
steps.guidance: Review database server logs, DBA activity logs, and core-banking vendor alerts. Confirm with the core-banking platform owner.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with identified database instance(s) and scope.
steps.abort: If evidence points only to an application-layer issue, redirect to the appropriate application-specific playbook.

steps.title: Determine full scope across accounts and subsystems
steps.desc: Because core banking databases are highly interconnected, assess whether other linked subsystems (loans, cards, wire transfer) were also touched.
steps.guidance: Engage core-banking platform architects to map data flows and confirm blast radius.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive scope document covering all affected subsystems.

steps.title: Identify privileged access or admin account used
steps.desc: Determine whether the compromise leveraged a DBA, service, or privileged application account.
steps.guidance: Review privileged access management (PAM) session logs for the core banking environment.
steps.outcome: Compromised privileged account(s) identified.

steps.title: Emergency isolate core banking database from external access
steps.desc: Immediately restrict network access to the core banking database to break the attacker's active access, while preserving availability for critical banking operations where possible.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with operations to apply emergency network segmentation without triggering a full outage unless necessary.
steps.outcome: Attacker access severed; core banking services maintained or gracefully degraded.
steps.abort: If isolation would cause unacceptable customer-facing outage, escalate to executive leadership for a risk-accepted interim control.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate all privileged database credentials
steps.desc: Force rotation of all DBA, service, and application credentials with access to the core banking database.
steps.guidance: Use PAM to rotate credentials in bulk; verify no stale sessions remain.
steps.outcome: All privileged credentials rotated and old sessions terminated.

steps.title: Activate executive/regulatory escalation for core banking compromise
steps.desc: Given the severity of a core banking system compromise, escalate immediately to executive leadership, Legal, and Compliance for GLBA and financial-regulator notification obligations.
steps.guidance: This scale of breach may trigger obligations to state/federal banking regulators in addition to standard breach notification law.
steps.outcome: Executive and regulatory notification workflow activated with assigned owners.

steps.title: Eradicate attacker persistence from core banking environment
steps.desc: Remove any backdoors, malicious database objects (triggers, jobs), or unauthorized accounts found during investigation.
steps.guidance: Work with the core-banking vendor's security team if the platform is vendor-managed.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean via forensic re-scan.

steps.title: Patch and harden the exploited entry point
steps.desc: Apply vendor patches or configuration hardening for the vulnerability that enabled database compromise.
steps.guidance: Validate patch deployment across all core banking nodes.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated and verified.

steps.title: Restore full core banking operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Progressively restore full access and transaction processing with enhanced monitoring in place, then execute customer/regulator notifications.
steps.guidance: Phase the restoration with heightened logging and anomaly detection before returning to normal operating mode.
steps.outcome: Core banking system fully operational with no recurring indicators; notifications issued.

steps.title: Conduct executive-level post-incident review
steps.desc: Produce a comprehensive after-action report covering root cause, response effectiveness, and required architectural/control improvements to the core banking environment.
steps.guidance: Include a specific review of privileged access architecture and network segmentation for the core banking platform.
steps.outcome: Executive-approved remediation roadmap with owners and deadlines.

ITID-51414.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed banking data leaks where the specific data category (account/routing numbers, transaction history, or full core-system compromise) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51414.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for banking-data-leak incidents not yet resolved to a specific sub-category.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of a banking data leak pending scoping
Ambiguous or mixed banking-data exposures spanning multiple categories at a scale not warranting the core-system-compromise classification
scopeExcludes: Confirmed account/routing-number-only exposure (ITID-51411)
Confirmed transaction-history-only exposure (ITID-51412)
Confirmed core banking system database compromise (ITID-51413)
ITID-51414.severity: High by default until scope is determined; adjust to match the eventual specific classification.
ITID-51414.escalation: Escalate to fraud/financial-crimes and privacy/legal immediately upon report; re-triage to a specific leaf as soon as scope is known.
indicators: Unconfirmed reports of banking data exposure from a third party or customer
Preliminary alerting that has not yet been scoped to a data category
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard financial-data breach detection and DLP controls pending scoping
ITID-51414.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51414.response: Rapidly scope the incident to determine the specific banking-data category affected and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to specific classification
detections: General DLP and data-access anomaly alerting
ITID-51414.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51411, -51412, or -51413 as soon as scope permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Banking Data Leak Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed leak of banking-related customer data that does not fit a more specific sub-category, requiring triage to determine actual scope and vector.

steps.title: Triage and classify the reported banking data leak
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the reported leak (source, tip, dark-web listing, internal alert) and determine what type of banking data appears involved.
steps.guidance: Interview the reporting party or reviewer, and correlate with internal logs to determine if this fits a more specific known sub-category.
steps.outcome: Leak classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed as a general/mixed banking data leak.
steps.abort: If the report cannot be substantiated after reasonable investigation, close as unconfirmed with documented rationale.

steps.title: Identify affected systems and data fields
steps.desc: Determine which systems, files, or data stores are the source of the leaked banking data and what specific fields are exposed.
steps.guidance: Use log correlation and data-matching against known internal records to confirm authenticity of leaked samples.
steps.outcome: Confirmed source system(s) and specific data fields involved.

steps.title: Restrict access to the suspected source system
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the system(s) identified as the likely source pending full investigation.
steps.guidance: Balance business continuity against the need to stop ongoing leakage.
steps.outcome: Potential ongoing leakage halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Loop in Legal/Compliance for preliminary notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with current findings so they can begin assessing whether GLBA/state notification thresholds are likely to be triggered.
steps.guidance: Even before full scope is known, early Legal engagement avoids missed notification deadlines.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance tracking the matter with a preliminary risk assessment.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Once the source and vector are confirmed, remediate the specific vulnerability, misconfiguration, or insider-access issue responsible.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the relevant system owner for the fix.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to banking data systems
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access or persistence mechanisms remain in the affected banking data systems after the primary remediation.
steps.guidance: Perform a targeted access review and log review covering the two weeks following remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Finalize scope determination and issue required notifications
steps.desc: Complete scope determination and execute any customer/regulatory notifications required based on Legal's final assessment.
steps.guidance: Ensure notification content accurately reflects the confirmed (not preliminary) scope.
steps.outcome: All required notifications completed; case ready for closure.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update detection playbooks
steps.desc: Record why this incident did not fit an existing sub-category and whether new detection rules or a new playbook variant are warranted.
steps.guidance: Feed findings back into the ITID taxonomy review process if a recurring pattern is identified.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations for taxonomy/detection improvements.

ITID-51421.def: Unauthorized modification of employee direct-deposit banking details within a payroll system, resulting in both a data exposure (attacker viewed/altered banking data) and financial diversion of payroll funds.
ITID-51421.purpose: Classifies breaches where a compromised payroll system was used to redirect employee direct-deposit destinations, exposing and manipulating payroll banking data.
scopeIncludes: Attacker-modified direct-deposit account details within the payroll platform
Compromise of employee self-service payroll portals used to alter deposit destinations
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the payroll provider's own infrastructure at the vendor level (ITID-51422)
General/unscoped payroll system compromise (ITID-51423)
ITID-51421.severity: High. Directly diverts employee wages and exposes banking details.
ITID-51421.priority: P1 given active financial loss to employees.
ITID-51421.escalation: Escalate immediately to HR, payroll operations, and finance to halt pending payroll runs and reverse fraudulent redirections where possible.
indicators: Unexpected direct-deposit account changes shortly before a pay cycle
Employee reports of missing paychecks
Payroll portal logins from anomalous locations followed by banking-detail edits
vectors: Phished employee self-service portal credentials used to alter deposit details
Business email compromise impersonating an employee requesting a deposit change
rootCauses: Lack of verification/callback confirmation for direct-deposit changes
Absent MFA on payroll self-service portals
No alerting on bulk or off-cycle deposit-detail changes
controls: Out-of-band verification for direct-deposit changes
MFA on payroll self-service systems
Alerting on deposit-detail change velocity
ITID-51421.detection: Payroll system audit logs on deposit-detail changes provide strong, direct signal.
ITID-51421.response: Freeze affected payroll runs, verify and restore legitimate deposit details, and notify affected employees of the exposure.
metrics: Number of employees affected by deposit redirection
Funds recovered vs. diverted
ITID-51421.notes: Differentiated from siblings by attack surface: this leaf is company-side payroll-portal compromise, not vendor infrastructure (ITID-51422).

playbook.name: Payroll Direct-Deposit Redirection Fraud via System Compromise
playbook.description: Attacker compromises the payroll system or employee self-service portal to redirect direct-deposit destinations to attacker-controlled accounts.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized direct-deposit changes
steps.desc: Validate reports (from employees not receiving pay, or payroll anomaly alerts) that direct-deposit routing/account details were changed without authorization.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference payroll system change logs against employee self-service authentication logs to identify unauthorized modifications.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of employee records with unauthorized direct-deposit changes and change timestamps.
steps.abort: If changes appear legitimate/authorized, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify compromise vector (portal credentials vs. system compromise)
steps.desc: Determine whether the fraud occurred via phished employee/HR credentials, a compromised payroll admin account, or a deeper system compromise.
steps.guidance: Review authentication logs, MFA status, and any phishing reports correlating with the timeframe of changes.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector identified.

steps.title: Urgently contact payroll bank to halt/reverse pending transfers
steps.desc: Immediately contact the company's payroll processing bank and any receiving banks to request a halt or recall of pending direct-deposit transfers to the fraudulent accounts before funds settle.
steps.guidance: Time is critical — same-day or next-day ACH transactions can often be recalled if reported within hours. Provide the bank with transaction details and fraud confirmation.
steps.outcome: Pending transfers halted or recall requests filed with receiving banks.
steps.abort: If the settlement window has already passed, document the loss and proceed to employee remediation and law-enforcement reporting.

steps.title: Lock affected employee accounts and revert deposit details
steps.desc: Lock the compromised self-service accounts and revert direct-deposit information to the last known-good verified account for affected employees.
steps.guidance: Require out-of-band verification (phone call, in-person) before reverting to avoid further fraud.
steps.outcome: Direct-deposit details restored to verified accounts; accounts secured against further changes.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance and Finance for notification and loss tracking
steps.desc: Engage Legal, Compliance, and Finance to track financial loss, assess breach-notification obligations for exposed employee banking data, and coordinate any law-enforcement filing.
steps.guidance: File a report with the FBI IC3 and local law enforcement given the wire-fraud nature of the incident.
steps.outcome: Legal/Finance actively tracking loss recovery and notification obligations; law enforcement report filed.

steps.title: Remediate the credential/portal compromise root cause
steps.desc: Reset credentials, enforce MFA, and close the specific vulnerability (phishing susceptibility, missing MFA, session hijack) that enabled the fraudulent changes.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring MFA re-enrollment for all HR/payroll self-service users.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified; MFA enforced on payroll self-service.

steps.title: Reimburse affected employees and confirm normal payroll processing
steps.desc: Ensure affected employees are made whole for any missed pay (via manual payment if funds could not be recovered) and confirm subsequent payroll cycles process correctly.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance on emergency off-cycle payments where needed.
steps.outcome: All affected employees paid correctly; normal payroll cycle resumed without recurrence.

steps.title: Review payroll self-service security controls
