steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of controls such as mandatory MFA, change-notification alerts to employees on direct-deposit edits, and delayed-effect windows for banking changes.
steps.guidance: Recommend a 24-48 hour hold period with employee notification before any direct-deposit change takes effect.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved control enhancements for payroll self-service.

ITID-51422.def: Unauthorized access to or exfiltration of company payroll data resulting from a security incident at a third-party payroll processing provider or platform.
ITID-51422.purpose: Classifies data breaches originating from the compromise of a third-party payroll provider or platform, rather than the company's own payroll portal.
scopeIncludes: Third-party payroll vendor breach notifications affecting company employee payroll data
Compromise of a payroll platform's shared infrastructure affecting multiple customer tenants including the company
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the company's own payroll self-service portal (ITID-51421)
General/unscoped payroll system compromise (ITID-51423)
ITID-51422.severity: High. Vendor-side breaches are outside direct company control and often affect large employee populations at once.
ITID-51422.priority: P1 upon vendor breach notification affecting company data.
ITID-51422.escalation: Escalate to vendor risk management, legal, and HR immediately upon vendor breach notification; activate third-party incident response coordination.
indicators: Breach notification received from the payroll provider
Anomalous activity reported by the vendor affecting the company's tenant
Employee reports correlating with a publicly disclosed vendor breach
vectors: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the payroll provider's platform
Compromise of the vendor's internal systems or supply chain
rootCauses: Insufficient vendor security due diligence and monitoring
Lack of contractual breach-notification SLAs with the payroll provider
controls: Vendor risk assessment and contractual breach-notification requirements
Data minimization in third-party payroll integrations
Monitoring of vendor status/security advisories
ITID-51422.detection: Detection largely depends on the vendor's own telemetry and notification; company-side coverage is limited to integration-log review.
ITID-51422.response: Coordinate with the vendor on scope determination, assess employee impact, and fulfill notification obligations even though the root cause was external.
metrics: Time from vendor breach notification to internal impact assessment
Number of employees affected
ITID-51422.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51421 by locus of compromise: vendor infrastructure rather than company-controlled systems.

playbook.name: Compromised Payroll Provider/Third-Party Platform Response
playbook.description: A third-party payroll service provider suffers a breach exposing the company's employee payroll and banking data.

steps.title: Validate third-party payroll provider breach notification
steps.desc: Confirm details of the breach notification received from the payroll provider, including scope, timeline, and data types affected.
steps.guidance: Request the provider's incident report, forensic summary, and specific data elements exposed for the company's employee population.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the provider's breach scope as it pertains to this company's data.
steps.abort: If the provider cannot yet confirm scope, escalate immediately for a formal update timeline rather than closing the case.

steps.title: Determine internal exposure and integration touchpoints
steps.desc: Assess whether the provider breach could have also exposed data via integrations (SSO, API feeds) into internal systems.
steps.guidance: Review API/SSO logs between the company and the payroll provider for anomalous activity during the breach window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether internal systems were also touched via the integration.

steps.title: Rotate integration credentials and API keys with the provider
steps.desc: Immediately rotate all API keys, SSO certificates, and service credentials shared with the payroll provider.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with the provider to avoid a payroll processing outage while rotating credentials.
steps.outcome: All shared credentials rotated; no unauthorized use observed post-rotation.

steps.title: Engage vendor-relationship manager and contract review
steps.desc: Engage the vendor relationship manager and Legal to review the contract's breach-notification, liability, and data-protection clauses, and demand a formal incident report from the provider.
steps.guidance: Check contractual SLAs for notification timing compliance and whether the provider owes indemnification or remediation support.
steps.outcome: Vendor contract obligations reviewed; formal demand for provider cooperation issued.

steps.title: Notify Legal/Compliance of downstream notification obligations
steps.desc: Because the underlying breach occurred at the vendor, confirm the company's own independent notification obligations to affected employees under GLBA/state law.
steps.guidance: A vendor breach does not eliminate the company's own notification duty to its employees as the data owner.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has an active tracked notification workflow independent of the vendor's own notifications.

steps.title: Verify provider remediation before restoring full integration
steps.desc: Obtain and review evidence from the provider that the root cause of their breach has been remediated before resuming normal data flows.
steps.guidance: Request a remediation attestation or third-party audit report from the provider.
steps.outcome: Provider remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If the provider cannot demonstrate remediation, escalate to leadership to consider suspending the relationship or requiring compensating controls.

steps.title: Restore payroll processing and notify affected employees
steps.desc: Resume normal payroll processing with the provider under verified remediation, and complete employee notifications with recommended protective actions.
steps.guidance: Offer credit monitoring to affected employees where warranted by exposed data types.
steps.outcome: Payroll operations normalized; employees notified and protected.

steps.title: Review third-party payroll vendor risk management
steps.desc: Document lessons learned and update vendor risk assessment criteria, including required security certifications and incident-notification SLAs for payroll providers.
steps.guidance: Consider whether a vendor security reassessment or alternative provider evaluation is warranted.
steps.outcome: Updated vendor risk management requirements documented and approved.

ITID-51423.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed payroll system compromise where the locus (company-controlled portal vs. third-party provider) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51423.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for payroll system compromises not yet attributed to a company-side portal or a third-party vendor.
scopeIncludes: Initial payroll-compromise reports pending attribution
Ambiguous payroll data exposure not yet traced to a specific system
scopeExcludes: Confirmed company-side direct-deposit redirection (ITID-51421)
Confirmed third-party payroll provider compromise (ITID-51422)
ITID-51423.severity: High by default until scope is determined.
ITID-51423.escalation: Escalate to HR and payroll operations immediately; re-triage once the compromise locus is identified.
indicators: Unconfirmed reports of payroll data or fund irregularities
Preliminary indicators not yet scoped to a specific system
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard payroll fraud detection controls pending scoping
ITID-51423.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51423.response: Rapidly determine whether the compromise originates from the company payroll portal or a third-party provider and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to specific classification
ITID-51423.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51421 or ITID-51422 as soon as scope permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Payroll System Compromise Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed compromise of payroll systems or data not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported payroll system compromise
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected compromise and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (direct-deposit redirection, provider breach) or is a general/mixed compromise.
steps.guidance: Interview the reporting party, review payroll system logs, and check for known indicators of the specific sub-types.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general compromise.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected systems, employees, and data types
steps.desc: Determine which payroll systems, employee records, and data fields (SSNs, bank details, salary data) were touched.
steps.guidance: Use payroll/HRIS audit logs to determine access scope and timeline.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected systems and employee records.

steps.title: Lock down affected payroll accounts and access paths
steps.desc: Disable compromised accounts and restrict access to affected payroll modules pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Payroll operations to minimize business disruption while containing the threat.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access path closed.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed scope to assess GLBA/state notification obligations for exposed employee financial data.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance tracking notification obligations.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or access issue identified as the root cause of the compromise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the payroll system owner/vendor for the fix.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to payroll systems
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access, backdoor accounts, or persistence mechanisms remain in the payroll environment after the primary remediation.
steps.guidance: Perform a targeted access review and log review covering the two weeks following remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Restore normal payroll operations and notify affected employees
steps.desc: Resume normal payroll processing and complete any required employee notifications.
steps.outcome: Payroll operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update controls
steps.desc: Record findings on why the incident did not fit an existing sub-category and recommend detection/control improvements.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51431.def: Theft of employee or customer tax filing data that is subsequently used by the threat actor to submit fraudulent tax refund claims in the victim's name.
ITID-51431.purpose: Classifies incidents where stolen tax filing data (e.g. SSNs, income data) is used by an attacker to file fraudulent tax refund claims, tying the data exposure to a specific downstream fraud outcome.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed downstream fraudulent refund filings traced to a company-held data breach
Tax authority or employee reports of fraudulent filings correlated with a known company incident
scopeExcludes: Compromise of tax preparation software/platform itself without confirmed downstream fraud (ITID-51432)
W-2/1099 phishing breach without confirmed refund fraud (ITID-51433)
ITID-51431.severity: High. Confirmed downstream fraud indicates realized harm to affected individuals, not just theoretical exposure.
ITID-51431.priority: P1 given active financial fraud against employees or customers.
ITID-51431.escalation: Escalate to HR/legal and advise affected individuals to file identity-theft affidavits with the relevant tax authority immediately.
indicators: Employees reporting rejected tax filings due to a duplicate return already filed
Tax authority correspondence indicating a suspected fraudulent claim
Correlation between affected individuals and a known prior data exposure
vectors: Reuse of previously stolen SSN/income data to file fraudulent returns
Purchase of stolen tax data from a dark web marketplace
rootCauses: Prior inadequate protection of tax-related PII
Delayed breach notification allowing time for fraudulent filing before affected individuals could act
controls: Encryption and access controls on stored tax/PII data
Rapid breach notification enabling proactive IRS/tax-authority identity-theft filings
Credit and tax-fraud monitoring services for affected individuals
ITID-51431.detection: Detection is largely reactive, driven by employee/customer reports and tax-authority correlation rather than internal telemetry.
ITID-51431.response: Support affected individuals with identity-theft affidavits and credit monitoring; determine and remediate the original data-exposure source.
metrics: Number of confirmed fraudulent filings tied to the breach
Time from breach to affected-individual notification
ITID-51431.notes: This leaf classifies the realized-fraud outcome; the originating exposure should also be traced and remediated at its source system.

playbook.name: Stolen Tax Filing Data Used for Fraudulent Refund Claims Response
playbook.description: Stolen employee or customer tax filing data (SSNs, W-2/1099 details) is used by criminals to file fraudulent tax refund claims with the IRS or state tax authorities.

steps.title: Confirm reports of fraudulent refund claims tied to company tax data
steps.desc: Validate employee/customer reports of rejected tax filings (indicating a fraudulent return was already filed) and correlate with any known data exposure from company systems.
steps.guidance: Collect employee/customer reports, and cross-reference the timing against any known prior breach or data leak involving tax data.
steps.outcome: Confirmed pattern linking fraudulent refund claims to company-sourced tax data.
steps.abort: If no plausible link to company data can be established, document and refer affected individuals to standard identity-theft resources without opening a full breach case.

steps.title: Identify the source and scope of the original tax data exposure
steps.desc: Trace back to determine how the underlying tax filing data (W-2s, 1099s, SSNs) was originally exposed — e.g., prior phishing, breach, or insider access.
steps.guidance: Review historical logs and prior incident records for a matching exposure event.
steps.outcome: Root exposure event identified and linked, or confirmed as a new/unknown exposure requiring separate investigation.

steps.title: Secure the current source of tax data if still exposed
steps.desc: If the original exposure vector is still active, immediately lock it down (revoke access, disable exposed export, patch vulnerability).
steps.guidance: Prioritize stopping any ongoing exposure before focusing on remediation of already-stolen data.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further tax data is being exposed.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance for IRS and state tax authority coordination
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance and Payroll/Tax teams to coordinate with the IRS Identity Theft Victim Assistance unit and relevant state tax authorities on behalf of affected individuals.
steps.guidance: Legal should also assess GLBA/state breach-notification obligations given the sensitivity of tax/SSN data exposure.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively coordinating with tax authorities and tracking notification obligations.

steps.title: Provide affected individuals with IRS Identity Protection PIN guidance
steps.desc: Direct affected employees/customers to file IRS Form 14039 (Identity Theft Affidavit) and enroll in the IRS Identity Protection PIN (IP PIN) program to prevent further fraudulent filings.
steps.guidance: Prepare a support communication with step-by-step instructions and a company point of contact for questions.
steps.outcome: Affected individuals equipped with identity-theft affidavit and IP PIN guidance.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed root-cause vulnerability
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability or process gap that allowed the original tax data exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the relevant system/process owner (payroll, HR, tax vendor) for remediation.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Support affected individuals through refund-fraud resolution
steps.desc: Provide ongoing support resources (dedicated hotline, identity-theft-resolution service) until affected individuals' legitimate tax filings are processed.
steps.guidance: Track resolution status per individual case where feasible.
steps.outcome: Affected individuals' legitimate returns processed; support resources in active use.

steps.title: Review tax-data handling and IRS coordination process
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether proactive IP PIN enrollment or additional tax-data protection controls should be implemented company-wide.
steps.guidance: Consider partnering with a dedicated identity-theft-resolution vendor for future incidents.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved proactive control recommendations.

ITID-51432.def: Unauthorized access to or exfiltration of tax data resulting from a compromise of the tax preparation software, platform, or vendor system used to process company or employee tax filings.
ITID-51432.purpose: Classifies breaches originating from compromise of the tax preparation software or platform the company uses, distinct from confirmed downstream refund fraud.
scopeIncludes: Vulnerability exploitation or credential compromise against the tax prep platform itself
Vendor-side breach notifications from the tax software provider
scopeExcludes: Confirmed downstream fraudulent refund filings (ITID-51431)
W-2/1099 phishing breach not involving the platform (ITID-51433)
ITID-51432.severity: High. Platform-level compromise can expose bulk tax data across many individuals at once.
ITID-51432.escalation: Escalate to vendor risk management and legal; assess bulk exposure scope before individual notification begins.
indicators: Vendor security advisory or breach notification for the tax prep platform
Anomalous administrative access to the tax filing platform
Bulk export activity from the tax software's data store
vectors: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the tax preparation software
Compromised administrator credentials for the tax platform
rootCauses: Delayed patching of tax preparation software
Insufficient vendor security oversight for tax-data processors
controls: Vendor security assessment for tax-data processors
Prompt patching and access monitoring on tax preparation platforms
ITID-51432.detection: Platform audit logs and vendor telemetry provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-51432.response: Coordinate with the vendor to determine breach scope, notify affected individuals, and monitor for downstream fraudulent filings.
metrics: Number of individuals whose tax data was exposed via the platform
Time to vendor-confirmed scope
ITID-51432.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51431 by focus: platform-level compromise itself, prior to (or absent) confirmed downstream fraud.

playbook.name: Compromised Tax Preparation Software/Platform Response
playbook.description: The tax preparation software or platform used to process company/employee tax filings is compromised, exposing filing data.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of the tax preparation platform
steps.desc: Validate indicators or vendor notification that the tax preparation software/platform was compromised, and determine whether it is internally hosted or a third-party SaaS product.
steps.guidance: Review vendor security advisories, internal application logs, or endpoint alerts on systems running the tax software.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise with platform type (internal vs. third-party) identified.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, close as false positive with documented rationale.

steps.title: Determine scope of tax filing data accessed
steps.desc: Identify which tax filings, employee/customer records, and data fields were processed through the compromised platform during the exposure window.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference platform processing logs against the affected time window.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected filings and individuals.

steps.title: Disconnect or restrict the compromised platform
steps.desc: Immediately disable access to or disconnect integrations with the compromised tax preparation platform to stop further data exposure.
steps.guidance: If third-party SaaS, work with the vendor to suspend the affected instance or your organization's tenant access.
steps.outcome: No further tax data flowing to/from the compromised platform.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance for notification and IRS coordination
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations and coordinate with the IRS/state tax authorities regarding potential fraudulent filing risk for affected individuals.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking notification and regulator coordination.

steps.title: Confirm platform remediation before resuming use
steps.desc: Obtain evidence (vendor patch notes, internal forensic clearance) that the compromise has been fully remediated before resuming filing operations on the platform.
steps.guidance: If vendor-hosted, request a formal remediation attestation.
steps.outcome: Platform confirmed remediated and safe to resume use.
steps.abort: If remediation cannot be confirmed, escalate to leadership to consider switching tax preparation providers.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and API keys used with the tax platform
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, API keys, and integration secrets associated with the tax preparation platform.
steps.outcome: All associated credentials rotated with no unauthorized use post-rotation.

steps.title: Resume filing operations and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Resume tax filing operations under verified remediation and complete notifications to affected employees/customers, including IP PIN guidance where refund fraud risk exists.
steps.outcome: Filing operations resumed; affected individuals notified and protected.

steps.title: Review tax software vendor security posture
steps.desc: Document lessons learned and reassess the security requirements/certifications required of tax preparation software vendors.
steps.outcome: After-action report with updated vendor security requirements.

ITID-51433.def: A phishing-driven breach in which an attacker impersonates an executive or authority figure to solicit bulk W-2 or 1099 employee tax documents from HR/payroll staff, typically timed to the tax filing season.
ITID-51433.purpose: Classifies the seasonal, well-known pattern of phishing attacks specifically targeting HR/payroll staff for bulk W-2/1099 data during tax filing season.
scopeIncludes: Business email compromise requesting bulk W-2/1099 exports from HR/payroll
Confirmed disclosure of bulk employee tax documents via a phishing pretext
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the tax preparation platform itself (ITID-51432)
Confirmed downstream fraudulent refund filings as the primary classification focus (ITID-51431)
ITID-51433.severity: High. A single successful request can expose the entire employee population's tax data at once.
ITID-51433.priority: P1 given the bulk, all-employee exposure profile typical of this pattern.
ITID-51433.escalation: Escalate immediately to HR, legal, and executive leadership; this pattern typically requires company-wide notification.
indicators: Spoofed executive email requesting a bulk W-2 export, especially in January-April
HR/payroll staff reporting an unusual urgent request for tax documents
Bulk W-2/1099 file sent externally shortly before the request is discovered fraudulent
vectors: CEO/executive impersonation phishing (business email compromise)
Spoofed domain lookalike emails targeting payroll staff
rootCauses: Lack of verification procedures for bulk sensitive-data requests
Insufficient seasonal phishing awareness training ahead of tax season
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement for bulk tax-document requests
Seasonal phishing awareness campaigns timed to tax filing season
Email authentication (DMARC/SPF/DKIM) to reduce spoofing
ITID-51433.detection: Email security gateway detection of spoofed/lookalike domains provides partial coverage; much of this pattern is caught only by staff vigilance.
ITID-51433.response: Immediately identify all employees whose data was sent, notify them and relevant tax authorities, and offer identity-theft protection services.
metrics: Number of employees affected
Time from disclosure to company-wide notification
ITID-51433.notes: This is a well-documented, seasonally recurring attack pattern; differentiate from siblings by its phishing/social-engineering vector rather than platform compromise or downstream fraud.

playbook.name: W-2/1099 Data Breach via Phishing (Tax Season Targeted) Response
playbook.description: Attacker impersonates an executive or HR to phish payroll/HR staff into sending employee W-2 or 1099 forms during tax season.

steps.title: Confirm the phishing-driven W-2/1099 disclosure
steps.desc: Validate that an HR/payroll staff member sent W-2 or 1099 forms in response to a phishing email (often a spoofed executive 'W-2 request' email), a classic seasonal social-engineering pattern.
steps.guidance: Obtain the phishing email, sender headers, and confirmation of exactly which files/employee records were sent and to whom.
steps.outcome: Confirmed disclosure with exact list of employees whose W-2/1099 data was sent to the attacker.
steps.abort: If the email was not acted upon, close as an attempted-but-unsuccessful phishing case per standard phishing playbook.

steps.title: Determine full scope of forms disclosed
steps.desc: Confirm the exact set of employees (could be entire company payroll) whose W-2/1099 forms were included in the disclosure.
steps.guidance: Request the exact file/attachment sent from the HR/payroll staff member involved.
steps.outcome: Definitive list of affected employees and years/forms disclosed.

steps.title: Block sender domain and search for similar phishing attempts
steps.desc: Block the phishing sender/domain across email security controls and search mailboxes for similar emails sent to other staff that may indicate a broader campaign.
steps.guidance: Use email security tooling to retroactively search and quarantine similar messages.
steps.outcome: Phishing sender blocked; no additional successful disclosures found.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance for IRS coordination and notification
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance immediately given SSN/wage data exposure; this scenario has a well-known IRS guidance path (Publication 4557/business email compromise tax data guidance) requiring rapid IRS notification.
steps.guidance: Legal/Compliance should contact the IRS via the phishing@irs.gov reporting channel and state tax agencies promptly, per IRS guidance for W-2 phishing incidents.
steps.outcome: IRS and state tax authorities notified per guidance; breach-notification timeline established.

steps.title: Offer IP PIN enrollment guidance to all affected employees
steps.desc: Provide all affected employees with guidance to file IRS Form 14039 and enroll in the IRS Identity Protection PIN program given the high fraudulent-refund risk.
steps.outcome: Affected employees equipped with proactive fraud-prevention guidance.

steps.title: Reinforce HR/payroll phishing controls and verification procedures
steps.desc: Implement or reinforce out-of-band verification requirements for any request to send bulk employee tax/wage data, and add targeted phishing-simulation training for HR/payroll staff.
steps.guidance: Consider technical controls such as DLP rules blocking bulk W-2/1099 attachments from leaving via email without additional verification.
steps.outcome: Verification procedure and DLP control implemented and tested.

steps.title: Notify affected employees and provide identity-protection resources
steps.desc: Complete notifications to all affected employees, offering credit monitoring and identity-theft protection services.
steps.outcome: All affected employees notified and enrolled in protective services as needed.

steps.title: Conduct seasonal phishing-readiness review
steps.desc: Document the incident and schedule recurring tax-season phishing awareness training and verification-control reviews for HR/payroll ahead of future tax seasons.
steps.outcome: After-action report with a scheduled recurring seasonal readiness program.

ITID-51434.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed tax information breaches where the specific mechanism (downstream refund fraud, platform compromise, or phishing-driven bulk disclosure) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51434.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for tax information breaches not yet attributed to a specific sub-category.
scopeIncludes: Initial tax-data-breach reports pending attribution
Ambiguous tax data exposure not yet traced to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Confirmed downstream fraudulent refund filings (ITID-51431)
Confirmed tax preparation platform compromise (ITID-51432)
Confirmed W-2/1099 phishing breach (ITID-51433)
ITID-51434.severity: High by default until scope is determined.
ITID-51434.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal immediately; re-triage once the mechanism is identified.
indicators: Unconfirmed reports of tax data exposure
Preliminary indicators not yet scoped to a specific mechanism
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard tax-data protection controls pending scoping
ITID-51434.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51434.response: Rapidly determine the specific mechanism of tax data exposure and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to specific classification
detections: General DLP and data-access anomaly alerting
ITID-51434.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51431, -51432, or -51433 as soon as scope permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Tax Information Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed breach of tax-related data not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported tax information breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected tax data breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (fraudulent refund claims, compromised tax software, W-2 phishing) or is a general/mixed exposure.
steps.guidance: Interview the reporting party, review relevant system logs, and check for indicators matching known sub-types.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general breach.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected individuals and tax data fields
steps.desc: Determine which employees/customers and which specific tax data elements (SSN, wages, filing status) were exposed.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference source system logs with HR/tax records.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected individuals and data fields.

steps.title: Restrict access to the suspected source of exposure
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the system(s) identified as the likely source of the tax data exposure.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification and IRS coordination assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with current findings to assess breach-notification obligations and potential need for IRS/state tax authority coordination.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability, misconfiguration, or access issue responsible for the exposure once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to tax data systems
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access or persistence mechanisms remain in the affected tax data systems after the primary remediation.
steps.guidance: Perform a targeted access review and log review covering the two weeks following remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Finalize notifications and provide identity-protection guidance
steps.desc: Complete any required notifications and provide IP PIN/identity-theft guidance to affected individuals where SSN data was involved.
steps.outcome: All required notifications and protective guidance delivered.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update detection playbooks
steps.desc: Record findings on why the incident did not fit an existing sub-category and recommend detection/control improvements.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51441.def: Unauthorized access to or exfiltration of private key material for a company-operated hot (internet-connected) cryptocurrency wallet, exposing the means to move funds directly.
ITID-51441.purpose: Classifies breaches where a company-controlled hot wallet's private key material was directly compromised, distinguishing exposure of the key from social-engineering or contract-based drain methods.
scopeIncludes: Theft of a private key or seed material stored in a hot wallet's key management system
Compromise of an application or server holding hot-wallet key material in memory or at rest
scopeExcludes: Exchange-hosted wallet breach via the exchange's own infrastructure (ITID-51442)
Malicious smart-contract approval drains (ITID-51443)
Seed phrase obtained via phishing rather than direct key-store compromise (ITID-51444)
ITID-51441.severity: Critical. Private key compromise typically allows immediate, irreversible fund transfer.
ITID-51441.priority: P1 — treat as an active financial-loss event requiring immediate key rotation/fund migration.
ITID-51441.escalation: Escalate immediately to treasury/finance and security engineering to migrate remaining funds to a secure wallet before further loss occurs.
indicators: Unauthorized outbound transactions from a known company wallet address
Anomalous access to key management infrastructure or HSM
Unexpected process access to key material in memory
vectors: Malware targeting key-storage files or in-memory key material
Compromised server or application hosting hot-wallet keys
Insufficient encryption of private key storage
rootCauses: Storing private keys unencrypted or in application memory without HSM protection
Lack of multi-signature requirements on hot wallets
Insufficient monitoring of wallet key-access systems
controls: Hardware security module (HSM) storage for private keys
Multi-signature wallet requirements
Withdrawal limits and anomaly-based transaction holds
ITID-51441.detection: On-chain transaction monitoring and key-store access logging provide strong detection signal once instrumented.
ITID-51441.response: Immediately migrate remaining funds, rotate all key material, and pursue blockchain-forensic tracing of stolen funds where feasible.
metrics: Value of funds lost vs. recovered
Time to key rotation/fund migration
ITID-51441.notes: Cross-reference: probable overlap with ITID-53713 (Stolen Cryptocurrency Wallet Used for Immediate Fund Transfer Out) in the parallel Financial Fraud domain, which covers the monetization/transfer-out angle; this leaf scopes strictly to the key-exposure/breach mechanism.

playbook.name: Hot Wallet Private Key Compromise Response
playbook.description: An attacker obtains the private key(s) of a company-controlled hot cryptocurrency wallet, enabling unauthorized outbound transactions.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized outbound transactions from the hot wallet
steps.desc: Validate blockchain explorer records and internal wallet monitoring alerts showing unauthorized outbound transfers from the company hot wallet.
steps.guidance: Review the wallet's on-chain transaction history and correlate with internal treasury/finance authorization records to confirm transactions were not authorized.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of unauthorized transactions, destination addresses, and amounts.
steps.abort: If transactions match authorized activity, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine how the private key was obtained
steps.desc: Investigate the likely vector for key compromise: malware on the signing device, insecure key storage, insider access, or compromised key-management service.
steps.guidance: Review endpoint security logs on any device used for signing, and key-management system access logs.
steps.outcome: Root-cause vector for key compromise identified.

steps.title: Move remaining funds to a new secured wallet immediately
steps.desc: Given blockchain transactions are irreversible, prioritize moving any remaining funds in the compromised wallet to a newly generated, secured wallet before the attacker can drain further balance.
steps.guidance: Use a verified clean device and freshly generated keys; do not reuse any component of the compromised key-generation environment.
steps.outcome: Remaining funds secured in a new wallet with no further unauthorized withdrawals possible from the old wallet.
steps.abort: If funds have already been fully drained, skip to documenting the loss and proceed with law-enforcement reporting.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised key and disable associated signing infrastructure
steps.desc: Decommission the compromised private key and any signing infrastructure or device implicated in the compromise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the treasury/finance team managing the wallet to formally retire the key.
steps.outcome: Compromised key and signing path fully retired.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Finance/Compliance for loss assessment and reporting
steps.desc: Engage Legal, Finance, and Compliance to assess financial loss, breach-notification implications for any customer funds affected, and file a report with law enforcement (FBI IC3) and any applicable financial regulators.
steps.guidance: Because blockchain theft is generally irreversible, focus escalation on loss quantification, disclosure obligations, and law-enforcement/exchange cooperation to flag the destination addresses.
steps.outcome: Legal/Finance actively tracking loss and reporting obligations; law-enforcement report filed.

steps.title: Harden key-generation and signing environment
steps.desc: Rebuild or replace the compromised signing environment with hardened controls (hardware security modules, multi-signature requirements, air-gapped key generation).
steps.guidance: Consider migrating to a multi-signature wallet architecture requiring multiple independent approvals for outbound transactions.
steps.outcome: New signing environment verified secure and operational.

steps.title: Resume treasury operations under hardened wallet architecture
steps.desc: Resume normal cryptocurrency treasury operations using the new wallet and hardened controls, with any affected customer balances reconciled.
steps.outcome: Treasury operations resumed with no recurring unauthorized activity.

steps.title: Review hot wallet key-management practices
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of multi-signature controls, cold-storage allocation limits for hot wallets, and hardware-based key protection.
steps.guidance: Recommend limiting hot wallet balances to operational minimums with the majority of funds held in cold storage.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved key-management architecture improvements.

ITID-51442.def: Unauthorized access to company cryptocurrency holdings resulting from a compromise of the exchange or custodial platform's own infrastructure, rather than direct theft of a company-held private key.
ITID-51442.purpose: Classifies wallet breaches occurring at the level of an exchange or custodial platform's infrastructure, rather than a company-controlled key or contract interaction.
scopeIncludes: Exchange-side breach notifications affecting company-held custodial balances
Compromise of an exchange's hot wallet infrastructure affecting multiple customer accounts including the company's
scopeExcludes: Direct compromise of a company-controlled wallet's private key (ITID-51441)
Malicious smart-contract approval drains (ITID-51443)
ITID-51442.severity: High-Critical, scaling with the value of custodial holdings affected.
ITID-51442.priority: P1 upon confirmed exchange breach affecting company funds.
ITID-51442.escalation: Escalate to treasury/finance and legal immediately; engage the exchange's incident response and consider fund withdrawal to self-custody where still possible.
indicators: Exchange breach notification or public disclosure
Unexplained balance discrepancies on the custodial platform
Exchange-wide trading/withdrawal suspension following a security event
vectors: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the exchange's hot wallet infrastructure
Compromise of exchange employee credentials with custodial access
rootCauses: Over-reliance on custodial (vs. self-custody) holding of significant funds
Insufficient exchange due diligence prior to fund placement
controls: Diversification away from single-exchange custodial concentration
Regular exchange security-posture due diligence
Withdrawal alerting on custodial account balance changes
ITID-51442.detection: Detection is largely dependent on the exchange's own disclosure and on-chain monitoring of company-associated addresses.
ITID-51442.response: Coordinate with the exchange on recovery/compensation processes and reassess custodial exposure policy going forward.
metrics: Value of custodial funds affected
Recovery/compensation amount from the exchange
detections: On-chain monitoring of company-associated exchange addresses
ITID-51442.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51441 by locus: exchange/custodial infrastructure rather than company-controlled key material.

playbook.name: Exchange-Hosted Wallet Breach via Compromised Exchange Infrastructure
playbook.description: A cryptocurrency exchange hosting company funds suffers an infrastructure compromise, exposing or draining company-held wallet balances.

steps.title: Confirm exchange infrastructure compromise affecting company holdings
steps.desc: Validate the exchange's incident disclosure or on-chain evidence of unauthorized withdrawal from company-held exchange wallets.
steps.guidance: Review exchange status pages/incident notices, and cross-reference the company's account transaction history for unauthorized withdrawals.
steps.outcome: Confirmed impact on company holdings with transaction details.
steps.abort: If the exchange incident does not touch company-held funds, monitor but do not open a full breach case.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposed account credentials and API keys
steps.desc: Assess whether company API keys, account credentials, or 2FA methods tied to the exchange account may have also been exposed in the breach.
steps.guidance: Request details from the exchange on whether account-level credentials (not just custodied funds) were affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any credential exposure in addition to fund loss.

steps.title: Withdraw remaining funds to a company-controlled wallet
steps.desc: If the exchange is confirmed compromised, immediately attempt to withdraw any remaining company funds to a secure, company-controlled wallet.
steps.guidance: Verify the exchange's own withdrawal functionality has not itself been compromised before initiating; use out-of-band confirmation with the exchange if possible.
steps.outcome: Remaining funds relocated to secure company-controlled custody where possible.
steps.abort: If the exchange has frozen withdrawals or funds are already drained, document status and proceed with exchange claims process.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate exchange API keys and account credentials
steps.desc: Rotate all API keys, account passwords, and 2FA methods associated with the exchange account.
steps.outcome: All exchange account credentials rotated.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Finance for loss recovery and exchange claims process
steps.desc: Engage Legal and Finance to pursue the exchange's compensation/insurance process, assess disclosure obligations for any affected customer funds, and file law-enforcement reports as needed.
steps.guidance: Document all correspondence with the exchange for potential claims or litigation.
steps.outcome: Legal/Finance actively pursuing recovery and tracking disclosure obligations.

steps.title: Reassess and diversify exchange custody risk
steps.desc: Reduce reliance on the compromised exchange for fund custody; move to self-custody or diversify across multiple reputable custodians.
steps.guidance: Evaluate the exchange's post-incident security posture before considering any future use.
steps.outcome: Custody risk reduced through diversification or migration to self-custody.

steps.title: Resume treasury operations under revised custody model
steps.desc: Resume cryptocurrency operations under the revised, diversified custody model with any recovered/compensated funds reconciled.
steps.outcome: Treasury operations resumed with reduced concentration risk.

steps.title: Review third-party exchange custody risk policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update policy on acceptable exchange custody concentration limits and due-diligence requirements for custodians.
steps.outcome: After-action report with updated custody risk policy.

ITID-51443.def: Loss of cryptocurrency or tokens from a company wallet after the wallet holder unknowingly granted a malicious smart contract approval (allowance) that was subsequently exercised by an attacker to drain funds.
ITID-51443.purpose: Classifies wallet drains resulting from a malicious or over-permissioned smart contract approval, a distinct mechanism from key theft or exchange compromise.
scopeIncludes: Draining via a previously granted token approval to a malicious or compromised contract
Interaction with a fraudulent decentralized application (dApp) that requested and exploited excessive approval scope
scopeExcludes: Direct private key theft (ITID-51441)
Exchange-side custodial compromise (ITID-51442)
Seed phrase phishing leading to full wallet takeover (ITID-51444)
ITID-51443.severity: High. The wallet's private key remains secure, but funds are still directly lost.
ITID-51443.priority: P1 upon detection of an active drain in progress; P2 for retrospective discovery of prior approval abuse.
ITID-51443.escalation: Escalate to treasury/finance; revoke all outstanding token approvals for the affected wallet immediately.
indicators: Unexpected token transfer authorized by a previously granted approval, not a new signature
Wallet interaction history showing approval to an unfamiliar or since-flagged contract address
Blockchain security service flagging the wallet's approval history
vectors: Malicious dApp requesting unlimited token approval during a routine-seeming transaction
Exploited or rug-pulled smart contract that the wallet had previously approved
rootCauses: Granting unlimited/unbounded token approvals rather than per-transaction limits
Lack of periodic approval review and revocation
Interacting with unverified/unaudited smart contracts
controls: Periodic token approval review and revocation process
Use of approval-limiting wallet tools
Restricting dApp interactions to audited, allow-listed contracts
ITID-51443.detection: On-chain approval and transaction monitoring tools provide good detection coverage once integrated.
ITID-51443.response: Revoke all outstanding approvals for the affected wallet, migrate remaining funds to a new wallet, and review policy on dApp interaction.
metrics: Value drained via approval abuse
Number of outstanding risky approvals identified and revoked
ITID-51443.notes: Differentiated from key-theft and exchange-compromise siblings by mechanism: the private key is never stolen; the attacker exploits a previously granted contract permission.

playbook.name: Wallet Drained via Malicious Smart Contract Approval Response
playbook.description: An attacker tricks the company into signing a malicious smart contract approval, granting unlimited token transfer rights that are then used to drain the wallet.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized token drains via malicious contract approval
steps.desc: Validate on-chain evidence showing tokens were transferred out via a smart contract approval (allowance) rather than a direct private-key compromise.
steps.guidance: Use a blockchain explorer or approval-checker tool to identify the malicious contract address and the approval transaction that granted it access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious contract address and the approval transaction that enabled the drain.
steps.abort: If the transaction pattern indicates direct key compromise instead, redirect to the hot wallet key compromise playbook.
steps.tool: Blockchain explorer / approval checker (e.g., Revoke.cash-style tooling)

steps.title: Identify how the malicious approval was signed
steps.desc: Determine the circumstance under which the wallet signer approved the malicious contract (phishing site, fake airdrop, spoofed dApp, malicious browser extension).
steps.guidance: Interview the individual who signed the transaction and review browser/wallet activity around the time of signing.
steps.outcome: Root-cause vector for the malicious approval identified.

steps.title: Revoke all active token approvals for the affected wallet
steps.desc: Immediately use an approval-revocation tool to revoke the malicious contract's approval and audit/revoke any other suspicious outstanding approvals on the wallet.
steps.guidance: Revoking is a paid on-chain transaction and must be executed quickly before the attacker uses remaining allowance.
steps.outcome: All malicious and unnecessary token approvals revoked; no further unauthorized transfers possible via the approval.
steps.abort: If the allowance has already been fully consumed, document and move to fund-recovery efforts.

steps.title: Move remaining unaffected assets to a new secure wallet
steps.desc: Transfer any remaining tokens/assets not covered by the malicious approval to a newly generated, secure wallet as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Remaining assets secured in a new wallet.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Finance for loss assessment and reporting
steps.desc: Engage Legal and Finance to quantify the loss, assess disclosure obligations, and file law-enforcement reports; recognize that blockchain drains via approval are typically irreversible.
steps.outcome: Legal/Finance actively tracking loss and reporting obligations.

steps.title: Implement approval-monitoring and dApp-vetting controls
steps.desc: Deploy tooling to continuously monitor outstanding token approvals on company wallets and establish a vetting process before interacting with any new smart contract or dApp.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring multi-person review before any wallet interacts with a new/unverified contract.
steps.outcome: Approval-monitoring tool deployed and vetting process documented.

steps.title: Resume wallet operations under enhanced approval governance
steps.desc: Resume normal wallet operations with the new approval-monitoring and vetting controls in place.
steps.outcome: Wallet operations resumed with no recurring unauthorized approvals.

steps.title: Review smart-contract interaction training and controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and mandate training for personnel who interact with smart contracts on recognizing phishing/spoofed dApp patterns.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved training and control improvements.

ITID-51444.def: Compromise and drain of a cryptocurrency wallet after its seed phrase (mnemonic recovery phrase) was obtained through a phishing or social-engineering pretext, granting the attacker full wallet control.
ITID-51444.purpose: Classifies wallet breaches resulting from social-engineering theft of a wallet's seed phrase or recovery material, distinguishing the phishing vector from technical key-storage compromise.
scopeIncludes: Fake wallet-support or 'verify your wallet' phishing pages soliciting seed phrase entry
Impersonation of wallet vendor support requesting seed phrase for 'recovery' or 'verification'
scopeExcludes: Direct technical compromise of key-storage infrastructure without a phishing pretext (ITID-51441)
Smart-contract approval abuse where the seed phrase is never disclosed (ITID-51443)
ITID-51444.severity: Critical. Seed phrase disclosure grants complete, irreversible control of the wallet.
ITID-51444.priority: P1 — treat as an active total-loss event for the affected wallet.
ITID-51444.escalation: Escalate immediately to treasury/finance; assume full compromise and cease using the wallet entirely.
indicators: Employee report of entering a seed phrase into an unfamiliar site or support chat
Immediate, complete fund drain following a support interaction
Phishing site impersonating a known wallet vendor's support/recovery flow
vectors: Fake customer support chat or phishing site requesting seed phrase 'for verification'
Malicious browser extension or fake wallet app capturing seed phrase entry
rootCauses: Lack of employee awareness that no legitimate service ever requests a seed phrase
Absence of hardware wallet usage isolating seed phrase entry from networked devices
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Hardware wallet usage for significant holdings
Awareness training that no legitimate entity requests a seed phrase
Vendor domain/brand-impersonation monitoring
ITID-51444.detection: Detection is largely reactive; on-chain monitoring can confirm the drain but rarely catches the phishing act itself in advance.
ITID-51444.response: Confirm total loss, review how the pretext reached the employee, and reinforce seed-phrase-handling training organization-wide.
metrics: Value lost per seed-phrase phishing incident
Number of employees who received the same phishing pretext
ITID-51444.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51441 by vector: social engineering targeting the human holder rather than technical compromise of key infrastructure.

playbook.name: Seed Phrase Phishing Leading to Wallet Breach Response
playbook.description: An employee is phished into revealing a wallet's seed phrase/mnemonic, giving the attacker full control over the wallet.

steps.title: Confirm the seed phrase disclosure and resulting wallet compromise
steps.desc: Validate that a wallet seed phrase was disclosed via phishing (fake wallet-support site, fraudulent recovery request, malicious app) and correlate with on-chain evidence of unauthorized full-wallet access.
steps.guidance: Interview the individual who disclosed the phrase and obtain the phishing artifact (email, site URL, app) for analysis. Confirm via blockchain explorer that funds were moved using the compromised wallet's full authority (not just an approval).
steps.outcome: Confirmed seed-phrase disclosure and resulting unauthorized wallet control/drain.
steps.abort: If evidence points to an approval-based drain instead, redirect to the malicious smart contract approval playbook.

steps.title: Assess whether the same seed phrase was reused elsewhere
steps.desc: Determine if the compromised seed phrase or a related one was reused across other wallets, exchange accounts, or systems.
steps.guidance: Interview the affected individual and check any wallet-management inventory for reuse.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of all wallets/accounts affected by the seed-phrase reuse.

steps.title: Move any remaining funds and decommission the compromised wallet
steps.desc: Since the seed phrase grants total wallet control, immediately move any remaining recoverable funds to a brand-new wallet with a freshly generated seed phrase, and treat the old wallet as permanently compromised.
steps.guidance: Generate the new seed phrase on a trusted, verified-clean device; never reuse any component of the old phrase.
steps.outcome: Remaining funds secured; old wallet fully decommissioned.
steps.abort: If funds are already fully drained, document loss and proceed to reporting.

steps.title: Rotate any other credentials tied to the same phishing campaign
steps.desc: If the phishing campaign also captured other credentials (email, exchange logins) alongside the seed phrase, rotate those as well.
steps.outcome: All related credentials rotated.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Finance for loss assessment and reporting
steps.desc: Engage Legal and Finance to quantify loss, assess disclosure obligations for any customer-impacting funds, and file law-enforcement reports (FBI IC3) flagging destination addresses.
steps.outcome: Legal/Finance actively tracking loss and reporting obligations.

steps.title: Eliminate unsafe seed phrase storage/handling practices
steps.desc: Identify and correct the unsafe practice that led to seed phrase exposure (e.g., stored in plaintext, entered on an unverified site, shared over chat).
steps.guidance: Migrate to hardware wallets with seed phrases stored in secure offline mediums (e.g., metal backup) and never entered into any online form.
steps.outcome: Unsafe practice eliminated and secure handling procedure documented.

steps.title: Resume wallet operations under hardened seed-phrase handling policy
steps.desc: Resume operations using the new wallet under a documented, hardened seed-phrase handling and storage policy.
steps.outcome: Operations resumed with no recurring exposure.

steps.title: Deliver targeted crypto-phishing awareness training
steps.desc: Document the incident and require targeted training for all personnel handling crypto wallets on recognizing seed-phrase phishing techniques.
steps.outcome: After-action report with scheduled training program.

ITID-51445.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed cryptocurrency wallet breaches where the specific mechanism (private key theft, exchange compromise, malicious contract approval, or seed phrase phishing) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51445.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cryptocurrency wallet breaches not yet attributed to a specific mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of an unexpected wallet balance change pending root-cause determination
Ambiguous crypto-loss events not yet traced to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Confirmed private key compromise (ITID-51441)
Confirmed exchange-hosted breach (ITID-51442)
Confirmed malicious contract approval drain (ITID-51443)
Confirmed seed phrase phishing (ITID-51444)
ITID-51445.severity: Critical by default until scope is determined, given the typically irreversible nature of crypto loss.
ITID-51445.escalation: Escalate to treasury/finance immediately; freeze/migrate any remaining funds in related wallets pending root-cause determination.
indicators: Unexplained wallet balance decrease not yet attributed to a specific mechanism
Preliminary on-chain alert pending forensic review
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard cryptocurrency security controls pending scoping
ITID-51445.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51445.response: Rapidly determine the specific mechanism of wallet compromise and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to specific classification
ITID-51445.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51441 through -51444 as soon as scope permits. Cross-reference ITID-53713 in the parallel Financial Fraud domain for the fund-transfer-out/monetization angle.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cryptocurrency Wallet Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed cryptocurrency wallet breach not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported cryptocurrency wallet breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected wallet breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (key compromise, exchange breach, malicious approval, seed phrase phishing) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review on-chain transaction history and interview relevant personnel to classify the mechanism of loss.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general breach.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Quantify total funds affected
steps.desc: Determine the total value and specific assets lost or exposed across all implicated wallets.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss/exposure figure.

steps.title: Secure remaining funds and revoke relevant access
steps.desc: Move any remaining recoverable funds to a secure wallet and revoke any compromised keys, approvals, or credentials identified.
steps.guidance: Given blockchain irreversibility, prioritize speed over full root-cause certainty at this stage.
steps.outcome: No further unauthorized outflow possible.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Finance for loss and disclosure assessment
steps.desc: Engage Legal and Finance to assess disclosure obligations and coordinate law-enforcement reporting.
steps.outcome: Legal/Finance actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause once identified
steps.desc: Once the specific mechanism of compromise is confirmed, apply the appropriate remediation (key rotation, approval hardening, custody diversification).
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Audit remaining wallet approvals and access grants
steps.desc: Review all remaining token approvals, API keys, and signer access on the affected wallet(s) to confirm no additional unauthorized access paths remain after the primary remediation.
steps.guidance: Use an approval-checking tool to confirm a clean state.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized approvals or access remain.

steps.title: Resume wallet operations under revised controls
steps.desc: Resume normal wallet operations under whatever hardened controls were identified as necessary.
steps.outcome: Operations resumed with no recurring unauthorized activity.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update wallet security controls
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements for company cryptocurrency wallet management.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51511.def: An incident in which internal operational documents (internal reports, process documentation, non-customer/non-employee operational data) are exposed due to a cloud storage bucket or container being configured to allow public/anonymous access.
ITID-51511.purpose: Captures internal operational documents exposed through a cloud storage bucket configured for public access, a common and preventable misconfiguration breach.
scopeIncludes: Cloud storage bucket set to public-read discovered by internal scanning or external researcher
Bucket indexed by search engines or bucket-scanning tools, exposing internal documents
Misconfigured bucket policy granting broader access than intended (e.g., 'authenticated users' interpreted as any AWS user)
scopeExcludes: Exposure via a shared/public link that was deliberately created and left active (Shared/Public Link leaf)
Exposure of a database backup or snapshot specifically (Cloud Storage Snapshot/Backup leaf)
Customer or employee PII-specific exposure (PII Exposure leaves), even if the mechanism is a public bucket
ITID-51511.severity: Medium-High, scaling with the sensitivity and volume of internal operational documents exposed and the duration of exposure.
ITID-51511.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the exposed documents include sensitive operational, security, or strategic information, or if external discovery/media attention is confirmed.
ITID-51511.escalation: Escalate to cloud/infrastructure engineering to remediate the misconfiguration immediately, and to legal/privacy if any regulated data is present among the operational documents.
indicators: Cloud security posture management (CSPM) alert flagging a publicly accessible bucket
External researcher or bug bounty report of discovered internal documents
Bucket access logs showing anonymous/unauthenticated requests
vectors: Bucket created or modified with an overly permissive access policy
Default cloud provider settings not hardened during bucket creation
Infrastructure-as-code template propagating a misconfigured bucket policy across environments
rootCauses: Lack of automated guardrails preventing public bucket configuration
Absence of periodic cloud storage configuration audits
Insufficient training on cloud storage access control models
controls: Automated CSPM guardrails blocking public bucket creation
Periodic cloud storage configuration audits
Bucket access logging and anonymous-access alerting
ITID-51511.detection: Strong when CSPM tooling is deployed and actively alerting; without it, exposure is often discovered externally rather than internally.
ITID-51511.response: Immediately restrict bucket access, determine what was exposed and for how long, and assess whether external access occurred via access logs.
metrics: Number of public bucket misconfigurations detected per period
Mean time to remediate a public bucket finding
Buckets covered by CSPM policy enforcement
ITID-51511.notes: Root cause is characteristically a misconfiguration rather than an active exfiltration technique, per the Operational Data Breach MITRE mapping guidance for cloud storage exposure.

playbook.name: Publicly Accessible Cloud Bucket Containing Internal Operational Documents
playbook.description: A cloud storage bucket containing internal operational documents is discovered to be configured with public read access.

steps.title: Confirm public accessibility of the cloud bucket
steps.desc: Validate the report or scanner alert confirming the bucket's access control configuration and its actual public accessibility, and inventory the documents/objects it contains.
steps.guidance: Use cloud provider console/CLI to check bucket ACLs/policies directly, and attempt an unauthenticated access test (from an isolated network) to confirm exposure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed public accessibility with a full inventory of exposed objects.
steps.abort: If the bucket is confirmed private/properly restricted, close as false positive.

steps.title: Review access logs to determine if the bucket was actually accessed
steps.desc: Beyond confirming the exposure existed, review cloud storage access logs to determine whether any unauthorized parties actually accessed or downloaded objects during the exposure window, not just whether it was theoretically exposed.
steps.guidance: Pull object-level access logs (e.g., S3 server access logs / CloudTrail data events) and filter for external/unrecognized IP addresses or user agents during the exposure period.
steps.outcome: Documented determination of whether actual unauthorized access occurred, and if so, by whom/how much data.
steps.abort: If access logging was not enabled for the bucket, document this gap explicitly rather than assuming no access occurred.

steps.title: Lock down bucket access controls immediately
steps.desc: Immediately change the bucket's access policy to block all public access and restrict to authorized principals only, as the top-priority containment action.
steps.guidance: Apply the cloud provider's account-level public-access-block setting in addition to the bucket-level policy fix to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Bucket confirmed no longer publicly accessible via independent verification test.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance if unauthorized access is confirmed
steps.desc: If access-log review confirms unauthorized access occurred, escalate to Legal/Compliance to assess notification obligations based on the sensitivity of the exposed operational documents.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged with a documented risk determination.
steps.abort: If no unauthorized access is confirmed and logging was reliable, document the risk-based decision not to escalate further.

steps.title: Audit and remediate all similarly configured buckets
steps.desc: Scan the entire cloud environment for other buckets with similar misconfigurations to ensure this was not a systemic issue.
steps.guidance: Use a cloud security posture management (CSPM) tool to run an organization-wide public-access scan.
steps.outcome: All buckets confirmed compliant with least-privilege access policies.

steps.title: Verify no cached or mirrored copies of exposed objects remain accessible
steps.desc: Check for cached, mirrored, or search-engine-indexed copies of the exposed bucket contents and request removal where found.
steps.guidance: Search common search engines and web caches for the bucket's object paths.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no cached/mirrored copies remain publicly accessible.

steps.title: Restore appropriate authorized access and confirm business continuity
steps.desc: Ensure legitimate internal users/systems retain necessary access under the corrected, restricted configuration, and confirm no business processes were broken.
steps.outcome: Authorized access confirmed functional; no unintended business disruption.

steps.title: Implement preventive guardrails for cloud storage configuration
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of automated guardrails (e.g., policy-as-code, continuous CSPM monitoring) to prevent future public-bucket misconfigurations.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved preventive guardrail implementation.

ITID-51512.def: An incident in which a shared or public link to cloud-stored operational data, generated for legitimate temporary sharing, remains active and accessible long after its intended purpose, resulting in unauthorized access.
ITID-51512.purpose: Captures exposure caused by a shared or 'anyone with the link' cloud storage link that was deliberately created for a purpose but left active beyond its intended use.
scopeIncludes: Shared link to a document/folder set to 'anyone with the link' and never revoked
Link shared externally (e.g., with a vendor) that continues to grant access after the engagement ends
Link discovered and accessed by an unintended party via forwarding, search indexing, or guessing
scopeExcludes: Bucket-level public access misconfiguration not tied to a specific shared link (Publicly Accessible Cloud Bucket leaf)
Exposure of a backup/snapshot object specifically (Cloud Storage Snapshot/Backup leaf)
ITID-51512.severity: Medium, scaling with how long the link remained active and the sensitivity of the shared content.
ITID-51512.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if access logs confirm the link was used by an unintended party.
ITID-51512.escalation: Escalate to the data owner and information security for impact assessment once an over-exposed link is identified; revoke access immediately.
indicators: CSPM or DLP tooling flagging long-lived 'anyone with the link' shares
Access logs showing views/downloads from unrecognized accounts or IP addresses
Periodic sharing-permission audit surfacing stale external shares
vectors: Link created for a one-time external share and never expired or revoked
Link forwarded beyond its intended recipient(s)
Search engine or third-party indexing of a publicly shared link
rootCauses: No default expiration policy on shared links
Lack of periodic review/audit of active external shares
No offboarding process to revoke vendor/partner link access at engagement end
controls: Default expiration on externally shared links
Periodic audit of active external shares
Offboarding process to revoke vendor/partner access
ITID-51512.detection: Moderate; depends on whether the cloud platform's sharing-audit and access-log capabilities are actively monitored rather than reviewed only reactively.
ITID-51512.response: Revoke the link immediately, review access logs to determine who accessed the content and when, and assess the sensitivity of exposed data.
metrics: Number of stale/over-exposed shared links identified per audit cycle
Average link lifetime before expiration/revocation
Percentage of shares with confirmed unintended access
ITID-51512.notes: Differentiated from the public-bucket leaf by mechanism: this leaf is a deliberately created share that outlived its purpose, not a baseline misconfiguration.

playbook.name: Cloud Storage Exposure via Shared/Public Link Left Active
playbook.description: A shared or public access link to cloud-stored data was created for legitimate purposes but left active indefinitely, resulting in unintended exposure.

steps.title: Confirm the active shared link and its scope
steps.desc: Validate the reported/discovered shared link, confirm it remains active, and inventory the specific files/folders it grants access to.
steps.guidance: Check the cloud storage platform's sharing management console for link creation date, permissions (view/edit), and expiration settings.
steps.outcome: Confirmed active link with full inventory of accessible content.
steps.abort: If the link is already expired/inactive, close as no ongoing exposure but still assess historical access.

steps.title: Review link access history to determine actual access
steps.desc: Determine who accessed the link and when, distinguishing intended recipients from unexpected/unauthorized viewers, since the link may have been shared further than originally intended.
steps.guidance: Pull link access logs/analytics from the platform; identify unrecognized IP ranges or email domains.
steps.outcome: Documented access history identifying any unauthorized viewers.
steps.abort: If access logs are unavailable, document this limitation explicitly.

steps.title: Disable or restrict the shared link immediately
steps.desc: Revoke or restrict the shared link's access as the top-priority containment action.
steps.guidance: Replace with a restricted, authenticated-access-only sharing method if continued access is needed.
steps.outcome: Link confirmed disabled/restricted via verification test.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance if unauthorized access is confirmed
steps.desc: If unauthorized viewers are confirmed from the access history review, escalate to Legal/Compliance to assess notification obligations based on data sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged with a documented risk determination.
steps.abort: If no unauthorized access confirmed, document the risk-based decision.

steps.title: Audit organization-wide sharing link policies and stale links
steps.desc: Scan for other stale or overly permissive shared links across the cloud storage environment.
steps.guidance: Use platform admin tools or a CASB to run an organization-wide report on active external sharing links.
steps.outcome: All stale/overly permissive links identified and remediated.

steps.title: Verify no cached or forwarded copies of the shared link content remain accessible
steps.desc: Check for cached, mirrored, or further-forwarded copies of the content that was accessible via the shared link.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no cached/forwarded copies remain publicly accessible.

steps.title: Establish authenticated access for legitimate ongoing sharing needs
steps.desc: Set up a properly authenticated and time-limited access method for the legitimate business need originally served by the link.
steps.outcome: Legitimate access restored via a controlled mechanism.

steps.title: Implement default link-expiration policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of a default expiration policy for all externally shared links across cloud storage platforms.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved default expiration policy.

ITID-51513.def: An incident in which a snapshot, image, or backup copy of a system or dataset stored in cloud infrastructure is configured to allow public or unauthorized access, exposing a point-in-time copy of operational data.
ITID-51513.purpose: Captures exposure of a cloud storage snapshot or backup object left publicly accessible, distinct from live/active data exposure.
scopeIncludes: Publicly accessible cloud VM/disk snapshot containing operational data
Publicly accessible backup archive object in cloud storage
Snapshot shared across accounts/projects beyond its intended scope
scopeExcludes: Live/production bucket exposure (Publicly Accessible Cloud Bucket leaf)
Exposure via a shared link to active documents (Shared/Public Link leaf)
Physical/on-premises backup media loss (Backup Data Breach leaves under Operational Data Breach)
ITID-51513.severity: High; snapshots and backups often contain a complete, unfiltered copy of a system's data, including historical records no longer in the live environment.
ITID-51513.priority: P1 upon confirmation of public snapshot/backup exposure, given the typically comprehensive nature of the exposed data.
ITID-51513.escalation: Escalate to cloud/infrastructure engineering and data protection immediately; assess snapshot contents in full since it may include data not present in the current live system.
indicators: CSPM alert flagging a publicly shared snapshot or backup object
External researcher report of an accessible snapshot
Snapshot/backup access logs showing unauthenticated or cross-account access
vectors: Snapshot created for migration/testing and left with default or overly permissive sharing settings
Backup automation script misconfigured to write to a public location
Cross-account snapshot sharing intended for a specific account left open to all
rootCauses: Lack of guardrails on snapshot/backup sharing permissions
Absence of a snapshot lifecycle and access-review process
Backup automation not covered by the same security review as production systems
controls: Guardrails restricting snapshot/backup sharing scope
Snapshot lifecycle management with periodic access review
Security review of backup automation pipelines
ITID-51513.detection: Strong when CSPM tooling explicitly covers snapshot/backup resources in addition to primary storage; many organizations under-monitor this resource type.
ITID-51513.response: Restrict snapshot/backup access immediately, determine the full scope of data contained (including historical data no longer live), and assess exposure duration via access logs.
metrics: Number of exposed snapshots/backups identified per period
Mean time to remediate
Snapshots/backups covered by CSPM policy enforcement
sops: Snapshot and Backup Access Review SOP
