ITID-51513.notes: Distinguished from live bucket exposure by the point-in-time, potentially historical nature of the exposed data.

playbook.name: Cloud Storage Snapshot/Backup Publicly Accessible
playbook.description: A cloud storage snapshot or backup artifact (e.g., a database snapshot or VM image backup) is discovered publicly accessible.

steps.title: Confirm public accessibility of the snapshot/backup artifact
steps.desc: Validate the report or scanner alert confirming the snapshot/backup's sharing/permission settings and its actual public accessibility.
steps.guidance: Check cloud provider snapshot-sharing settings (e.g., public snapshot flags) and attempt an unauthenticated access/download test.
steps.outcome: Confirmed public accessibility of the specific snapshot/backup artifact.
steps.abort: If confirmed private, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine data contents and whether the snapshot was accessed
steps.desc: Identify what data the snapshot/backup contains (full database, VM disk image, etc.) and review access/download logs to determine if unauthorized parties actually retrieved it.
steps.guidance: Because backups often contain full historical data beyond current production state, treat the scope assessment as potentially broader than a live-system exposure.
steps.outcome: Documented data contents and access history for the exposed artifact.

steps.title: Restrict snapshot/backup sharing settings immediately
steps.desc: Change the snapshot/backup's sharing configuration to private/restricted as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Artifact confirmed no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance based on data sensitivity and access findings
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to assess notification obligations based on the sensitivity of data contained in the snapshot and whether unauthorized access was confirmed.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged with a documented risk determination.

steps.title: Audit all backup/snapshot sharing configurations organization-wide
steps.desc: Scan for other snapshots/backups with similarly permissive sharing settings across all cloud accounts.
steps.guidance: Use a CSPM tool with backup/snapshot-specific policy checks.
steps.outcome: All backup/snapshot artifacts confirmed compliant with restricted sharing policy.

steps.title: Verify no downstream copies of the exposed snapshot remain accessible
steps.desc: Check whether the exposed snapshot was copied or shared to any other accounts/regions before lockdown, and remediate any such copies.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no downstream copies remain publicly accessible.

steps.title: Confirm backup/restore processes remain functional under corrected settings
steps.desc: Verify that legitimate backup and disaster-recovery processes still function correctly after the sharing settings were locked down.
steps.outcome: Backup/restore processes verified functional under restricted settings.

steps.title: Implement automated backup-sharing guardrails
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of policy-as-code guardrails preventing snapshots/backups from ever being set to public sharing.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved automated guardrail implementation.

ITID-51514.def: An intake classification for incidents involving unauthorized or public access to cloud-stored operational data where the specific mechanism (bucket misconfiguration, stale shared link, or exposed snapshot/backup) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51514.purpose: Captures a confirmed cloud storage exposure that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Cloud Storage Exposure.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed cloud storage exposure of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
Cloud exposure reports lacking sufficient detail to identify the specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Confirmed public bucket misconfiguration (Publicly Accessible Cloud Bucket leaf)
Confirmed stale shared link (Shared/Public Link leaf)
Confirmed exposed snapshot/backup (Cloud Storage Snapshot/Backup leaf)
ITID-51514.severity: Medium-High by default, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment based on data sensitivity.
ITID-51514.priority: P2 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the exposure mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51514.escalation: Escalate to cloud/infrastructure engineering for immediate access restriction while triage to a specific mechanism proceeds.
indicators: External or internal report of accessible cloud data with insufficient detail to determine mechanism
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard cloud exposure intake and triage process
ITID-51514.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51514.response: Restrict access immediately regardless of classification, then rapidly triage to determine the specific mechanism and reclassify.
metrics: Number of unclassified cloud storage exposure incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51514.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Cloud Storage Exposure leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud Storage Exposure Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed cloud storage exposure not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported cloud storage exposure
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected exposure and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (public bucket, stale shared link, exposed snapshot) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Check the cloud provider console for the resource's actual access configuration.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general exposure.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Review access logs to determine if exposure resulted in actual access
steps.desc: Determine whether the exposed resource was actually accessed by unauthorized parties, not just whether it was theoretically exposed.
steps.outcome: Documented access determination.

steps.title: Lock down the exposed resource immediately
steps.desc: Restrict access controls on the exposed resource as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Resource confirmed no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance based on findings
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance if unauthorized access is confirmed or data sensitivity warrants assessment.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged as appropriate.

steps.title: Audit for similar misconfigurations organization-wide
steps.desc: Scan the broader cloud environment for similar exposure patterns.
steps.outcome: All similar resources confirmed compliant.

steps.title: Verify no cached or downstream copies of the exposed resource remain accessible
steps.desc: Check for cached, mirrored, or forwarded copies of the exposed resource's contents and remediate any found.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no cached/downstream copies remain publicly accessible.

steps.title: Restore authorized access and confirm business continuity
steps.desc: Ensure legitimate access remains functional under corrected configuration.
steps.outcome: Authorized access confirmed functional.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements for cloud storage configuration management.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51521.def: An incident in which an adversary exploits a SQL injection vulnerability in an application to extract a full or substantial dump of an underlying database's contents.
ITID-51521.purpose: Captures theft of a complete database via SQL injection, a classic and highly technical exfiltration pathway distinguished by its exploit-driven initial access vector.
scopeIncludes: SQL injection exploited to run bulk SELECT/UNION queries extracting table contents
Blind or time-based SQL injection used iteratively to reconstruct database contents
SQLi used to obtain database credentials that are then used for direct bulk export
scopeExcludes: Database backup files exposed on a public server without an active exploit (Database Backup File Exposed leaf)
Insider-driven database dump exfiltration (Database Dump Sold/Leaked via Insider Access leaf)
General web-application SQL injection attempts without confirmed bulk data extraction (tracked under ITID-30000's Exploitation domain if no data was extracted)
ITID-51521.severity: High; SQL injection dumps frequently expose the entirety of a database's records in a single event.
ITID-51521.priority: P1 upon confirmation of a successful SQLi-driven data extraction.
ITID-51521.escalation: Escalate to application security, legal/privacy, and the SOC immediately; patch the vulnerability in parallel with breach assessment.
indicators: Web application firewall (WAF) or application logs showing SQL injection payloads followed by large response sizes
Anomalous, high-volume database query activity from the application's service account
Database contents found on a paste site, forum, or dark web marketplace
vectors: Unsanitized user input passed directly into a SQL query
Exploitation of a known, unpatched SQL injection vulnerability in application code or a third-party component
Automated SQLi scanning/exploitation tooling
rootCauses: Lack of parameterized queries/prepared statements in application code
Insufficient input validation and output encoding
Absence of a WAF or inadequate WAF rule coverage for injection patterns
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements in all application data access
WAF with SQL injection rule coverage
Database query volume anomaly monitoring
ITID-51521.detection: Good where WAF and application logging are in place and actively monitored; blind/time-based SQLi with low-and-slow extraction can evade volume-based detection.
ITID-51521.response: Patch the vulnerability immediately, determine the full scope of extracted data from logs, and assess breach notification obligations.
metrics: Number of confirmed SQLi-driven data extraction incidents per period
Records exposed per incident
Time from exploit to detection
ITID-51521.notes: Cross-referenced against ITID-30000's Exploitation/Data Exfiltration leaves during overlap review; this leaf is scoped strictly to confirmed bulk database exposure resulting from SQLi, complementing (not duplicating) any general SQL injection attempt/exploitation leaf tracked under ITID-30000.

playbook.name: Full Database Dump Exfiltrated via SQL Injection Response
playbook.description: An attacker exploits a SQL injection vulnerability in a company application to exfiltrate a full database dump.

steps.title: Confirm SQL injection exploitation and data exfiltration
steps.desc: Validate WAF/application logs and database query logs showing SQL injection payloads and confirm evidence of large-scale data extraction consistent with a full dump.
steps.guidance: Look for anomalous query patterns (UNION SELECT, stacked queries, information_schema enumeration) and unusually large outbound response sizes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed SQL injection exploitation with evidence of dump-scale exfiltration.
steps.abort: If injection attempts were blocked/unsuccessful, close as an attempted-but-failed attack per standard web-attack playbook.

steps.title: Identify the vulnerable endpoint and full data scope
steps.desc: Pinpoint the specific application endpoint/parameter vulnerable to injection and determine the full scope of tables/records exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Reproduce the injection in a controlled test environment to confirm the vulnerable parameter and query it would allow.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint identified and full data scope documented.

steps.title: Block the exploited endpoint/attacker source at the WAF
steps.desc: Apply an immediate WAF/network rule blocking the injection payload pattern and/or the attacker's source IP(s) to stop ongoing exploitation.
steps.outcome: No further injection attempts succeeding against the endpoint.

steps.title: Coordinate with application security team on the underlying vulnerability
steps.desc: Engage the application security/development team to review the vulnerable code path and confirm the injection cannot be exploited through any related endpoint or parameter.
steps.guidance: This is essential since SQL injection often has multiple entry points sharing the same vulnerable data-access layer.
steps.outcome: AppSec team has confirmed and scoped all related vulnerable code paths.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed scope of exfiltrated data to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking notification obligations.

steps.title: Patch the SQL injection vulnerability (parameterized queries)
steps.desc: Remediate the vulnerability by implementing parameterized queries/prepared statements or an ORM layer, removing any dynamic string-concatenated SQL.
steps.guidance: Verify the fix with a follow-up penetration test or code review before closing.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability confirmed remediated via re-test.

steps.title: Rotate database credentials and review database user privileges
steps.desc: Rotate the application's database credentials and review whether the application's database user had excessive privileges that enabled the full dump.
steps.guidance: Apply least-privilege database roles to limit the blast radius of any future injection.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and database privileges reduced to least privilege.

steps.title: Restore normal application operation and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Restore normal application service under the patched code and complete required notifications to affected customers/employees.
steps.outcome: Application operating normally; notifications completed.

steps.title: Review secure coding practices and SAST/DAST coverage
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to secure coding standards, code review requirements, and automated SAST/DAST scanning coverage to catch injection vulnerabilities earlier.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved SDLC security improvements.

ITID-51522.def: An incident in which a database backup file (a .sql, .bak, .dump, or similar export) is discovered accessible on a public-facing web server, misconfigured file share, or otherwise improperly secured location.
ITID-51522.purpose: Captures exposure of a database backup file left accessible on a public-facing or improperly secured server, distinct from an active exploitation-driven dump.
scopeIncludes: Backup file left in a web-accessible directory on a production server
Backup file placed on a misconfigured file share or FTP server
Backup file discovered via directory listing or search engine indexing
scopeExcludes: Active SQL injection exploitation to extract data directly (Full Database Dump via SQL Injection leaf)
Insider-driven deliberate leak/sale of a dump (Database Dump Sold/Leaked via Insider Access leaf)
Cloud storage-hosted backup exposure (Cloud Storage Snapshot/Backup leaf, if the mechanism is cloud storage rather than a web/file server)
ITID-51522.severity: High; backup files typically contain a complete, unfiltered copy of database contents.
ITID-51522.priority: P1 upon confirmation that the backup file was publicly accessible and may have been downloaded.
ITID-51522.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure/operations for immediate removal or access restriction, and to legal/privacy for breach assessment.
indicators: External researcher or scanner report of a discoverable backup file
Web server access logs showing requests for backup file extensions (.sql, .bak, .dump)
Backup file content found circulating externally
vectors: Backup script writing output directly into a web-accessible directory
Backup file transferred to a server for convenience and never removed
Misconfigured file share/FTP permissions exposing backup storage
rootCauses: Lack of separation between backup storage and web-accessible infrastructure
Absence of automated scanning for exposed backup files
No retention/cleanup policy for temporary backup copies
controls: Backup storage isolated from web-accessible infrastructure
Automated external scanning for exposed backup file patterns
Retention/cleanup policy for temporary backup files
ITID-51522.detection: Moderate; depends on proactive external attack-surface scanning, since the exposure itself generates no anomalous behavioral signal beyond normal file access.
ITID-51522.response: Remove or restrict access to the file immediately, review access logs to determine if/when it was downloaded, and assess breach notification obligations.
metrics: Number of exposed backup file incidents per period
Mean time to detect exposed backup files via scanning
Records exposed per incident
detections: External attack surface scanning for backup file patterns
Web server access log review for backup file requests
ITID-51522.notes: Differentiated from the SQLi leaf by vector: this is a static exposure/misconfiguration finding rather than an active exploit, and from the cloud snapshot leaf by hosting location (web/file server rather than cloud storage).

playbook.name: Database Backup File Exposed on Public Server Response
playbook.description: A database backup file is discovered exposed on a publicly accessible server (e.g., a misconfigured web server or FTP site).

steps.title: Confirm the backup file's public exposure and accessibility
steps.desc: Validate the report confirming the backup file's location, server configuration, and actual public accessibility.
steps.guidance: Attempt an unauthenticated access/download test from an isolated network to confirm exposure and note the file's timestamp/version.
steps.outcome: Confirmed public accessibility of the specific backup file.
steps.abort: If access is confirmed restricted, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine data contents and review server access logs
steps.desc: Identify the full contents of the backup file (tables, records, PII fields) and review web/FTP server access logs to determine if unauthorized parties downloaded it.
steps.guidance: Check for download requests from unrecognized IPs/user agents, and note file download counts.
steps.outcome: Documented data contents and access history for the exposed file.
steps.abort: If access logging was insufficient, document this gap explicitly.

steps.title: Remove the backup file from the public server immediately
steps.desc: Delete or move the backup file off the publicly accessible server/path as the top-priority containment action.
steps.guidance: Also check for cached/CDN copies that may still be accessible after removal from origin.
steps.outcome: Backup file confirmed no longer publicly accessible, including via CDN cache.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance based on exposure and access findings
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed data contents and access history to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged with a documented risk determination.

steps.title: Remediate the misconfiguration that allowed public exposure
steps.desc: Fix the server/deployment misconfiguration (e.g., backup written to a public web root, missing directory access controls) that allowed the file to be exposed.
steps.guidance: Review deployment scripts/CI-CD pipelines to determine why the backup ended up in a public location.
steps.outcome: Root misconfiguration remediated and verified.

steps.title: Audit backup storage locations organization-wide
steps.desc: Scan for other backup files that may be similarly misplaced in publicly accessible locations across all servers.
steps.outcome: All backup storage locations confirmed compliant with restricted access policy.

steps.title: Establish a proper secured backup storage process and notify as required
steps.desc: Move backup storage to a properly secured, access-controlled location and complete any required notifications to affected individuals.
steps.outcome: Backup process secured; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Update backup deployment and storage standards
steps.desc: Document the incident and update deployment standards to ensure backups are never written to publicly accessible paths, with automated checks in CI/CD.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved deployment standard updates.

ITID-51523.def: An incident in which an insider (employee, contractor, or other authorized user) with legitimate database access deliberately extracts and leaks or sells a database dump.
ITID-51523.purpose: Captures database dump theft attributable to insider access and deliberate leak or sale, distinct from external technical exploitation.
scopeIncludes: Authorized database administrator exporting and selling data to a third party
Employee with legitimate query access extracting bulk records for personal gain or grievance
Contractor retaining and later leaking a database export obtained during legitimate work
scopeExcludes: External SQL injection-driven extraction (Full Database Dump via SQL Injection leaf)
Passive discovery of an exposed backup file (Database Backup File Exposed leaf)
General insider threat behavior not resulting in a confirmed database dump (tracked under the appropriate Insider Threat ITID)
ITID-51523.severity: High; insiders often have broader access and better knowledge of high-value data than external attackers, increasing the scope of potential exposure.
ITID-51523.priority: P1 upon confirmation of deliberate insider extraction; treat as an active insider threat investigation requiring HR and legal coordination.
ITID-51523.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, and insider threat/counter-insider-threat functions immediately in addition to the SOC; preserve evidence in a manner suitable for potential employment or legal action.
indicators: Anomalous bulk export query from an authorized user account outside normal work patterns
Database dump found for sale on a criminal marketplace or offered to a competitor
User behavior analytics flagging access inconsistent with job role
vectors: Legitimate credentials used to run an unusually large export query
Data copied to removable media or personal cloud storage during normal working hours to blend in
Access retained after role change or offboarding delay
rootCauses: Insufficient least-privilege enforcement allowing broader access than role requires
Lack of user behavior analytics/anomaly detection on database access
Delayed access revocation upon role change or termination
controls: Least-privilege access enforcement for database systems
User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) on data access patterns
Timely access revocation upon role change/termination
ITID-51523.detection: Moderate; requires behavioral/anomaly monitoring rather than signature-based detection, since the access itself is technically authorized.
ITID-51523.response: Revoke access immediately upon confirmation, preserve forensic evidence, and coordinate with HR/legal on employment and potential criminal/civil action.
metrics: Number of confirmed insider-driven database dump incidents per period
Records exposed per incident
Time from anomalous access to detection
ITID-51523.notes: Differentiated from the other Database Dump leaves by the human/motive axis rather than the technical vector: access here is legitimate, and the breach is a trust/authorization failure.

playbook.name: Database Dump Sold/Leaked via Insider Access Response
playbook.description: An insider with legitimate database access extracts and sells or leaks a database dump.

steps.title: Confirm the insider-sourced database dump
steps.desc: Validate evidence (dark-web listing, tip, or internal discovery) that a database dump matching internal records was leaked or sold, and confirm it originated from insider access rather than external compromise.
steps.guidance: Compare sample leaked records against internal data to confirm authenticity, and cross-reference access patterns with known external attack indicators to rule those out.
steps.outcome: Confirmed insider-sourced dump with authenticity verified.
steps.abort: If evidence points to external compromise instead, redirect to the appropriate external-breach playbook.

steps.title: Identify the responsible insider via access log forensics
steps.desc: Review database query/export logs, DLP alerts, and access patterns to identify which insider(s) had access and behavior consistent with the extraction.
steps.guidance: Look for unusual bulk export queries, off-hours access, or use of removable media/personal cloud storage correlating with the leaked dataset's scope.
steps.outcome: Responsible insider(s) identified with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Suspend the insider's access immediately
steps.desc: Immediately suspend the identified insider's database, network, and physical access pending investigation, in coordination with HR and Legal.
steps.guidance: Coordinate carefully with HR/Legal on timing and communication to preserve evidentiary integrity and comply with employment law.
steps.outcome: Insider's access fully suspended with no further extraction possible.
steps.abort: If the insider cannot yet be conclusively identified, apply broader temporary access restrictions to the affected data while investigation continues.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence and engage HR/Legal/Law Enforcement
steps.desc: Preserve all relevant logs, device images, and communications; engage HR, Legal, and law enforcement given the criminal nature of insider data theft and sale.
steps.guidance: Follow proper chain-of-custody procedures for any forensic evidence collected.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal/law enforcement actively engaged.

steps.title: Escalate to Compliance for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Compliance with the confirmed scope of the insider-sourced dump to assess breach-notification obligations to affected customers/employees.
steps.outcome: Compliance actively tracking notification obligations.

steps.title: Close the access gap that enabled excessive insider extraction
steps.desc: Reduce database access privileges and export capabilities to eliminate the ability for a single insider to extract a full dump undetected in the future.
steps.guidance: Implement export volume limits, mandatory approval workflows for bulk exports, and enhanced DLP monitoring for the affected data.
steps.outcome: Access controls and export monitoring hardened and verified.

steps.title: Complete personnel action and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Complete HR/Legal-directed personnel action against the insider and issue required notifications to affected customers/employees.
steps.outcome: Personnel action completed; notifications issued as required.

steps.title: Review insider-threat detection and data-access governance
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to insider-threat detection (UEBA), export monitoring, and periodic access recertification for sensitive databases.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved insider-threat program improvements.

ITID-51524.def: An intake classification for incidents involving theft or exposure of a database dump where the mechanism (SQL injection, exposed backup file, or insider extraction) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51524.purpose: Captures a confirmed database dump breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Database Dump.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed database dump exposure of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
Database contents found circulating externally with no confirmed root cause yet
scopeExcludes: Confirmed SQL injection extraction (Full Database Dump via SQL Injection leaf)
Confirmed exposed backup file (Database Backup File Exposed leaf)
Confirmed insider extraction (Database Dump Sold/Leaked via Insider Access leaf)
ITID-51524.severity: High by default given the typically comprehensive nature of database dumps, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51524.priority: P1 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51524.escalation: Escalate to legal/privacy and the SOC immediately; do not wait for reclassification before beginning breach assessment.
indicators: Database contents found on a paste site, forum, or dark web marketplace with no confirmed root cause
Third-party report of exposed database records of unclear origin
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard database breach intake and triage process
ITID-51524.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51524.response: Rapidly triage to determine the mechanism and reclassify; begin breach assessment in parallel regardless of classification status.
metrics: Number of unclassified database dump incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51524.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Database Dump leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Database Dump Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed database dump exfiltration not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported database dump incident
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected database dump and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (SQL injection, exposed backup, insider theft) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review application, database, and access logs to identify the likely mechanism.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected tables, records, and data sensitivity
steps.desc: Determine the specific tables, record counts, and sensitivity classification of the dumped data.
steps.outcome: Documented scope and sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected database pending investigation
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the affected database as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed scope to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability, misconfiguration, or access issue responsible for the dump once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized database access remains
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access, credentials, or export capability remains against the affected database after the primary remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Restore normal database operations and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update detection playbooks
steps.desc: Record findings on why the incident did not fit an existing sub-category and recommend detection/control improvements.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51531.def: An incident in which internal team collaboration platform (Slack, Microsoft Teams, or similar) message history is exposed or exfiltrated, revealing internal discussions, decisions, or shared files.
ITID-51531.purpose: Captures leaks of internal team collaboration (Slack/Teams) message history, distinct from email and meeting-recording leaks by channel and typical bulk-export mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Bulk export of channel/workspace message history via compromised admin or export credentials
Exposure of a message archive/export file left in an unsecured location
Third-party integration/app compromise granting access to workspace message history
scopeExcludes: Leaked email thread chains (Leaked Internal Email Thread Chain leaf)
Leaked meeting recordings/transcripts (Leaked Internal Meeting Recording/Transcript leaf)
Files shared within messages but stored in a separate cloud storage system (Cloud Storage Exposure leaves, if the storage system itself is the point of exposure)
ITID-51531.severity: Medium-High, scaling with the sensitivity of discussions exposed (e.g., legal, HR, security incident discussions) and the volume of history involved.
ITID-51531.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if exposed content includes credentials, legal privilege material, or security incident details.
ITID-51531.escalation: Escalate to legal and communications/PR if exposed content touches privileged, regulatory, or reputationally sensitive discussions.
indicators: Workspace admin audit log showing an unusual bulk export event
Message content found circulating externally (leak site, competitor, media)
Third-party app/integration granted unusually broad message history scope
vectors: Compromised workspace administrator credentials used to trigger a full export
Over-permissioned third-party app/bot with message history access, later compromised
Insider export of message history for personal retention or leak
rootCauses: Insufficient restriction on who can trigger workspace-wide exports
Lack of review of third-party app permission scopes
No retention/deletion policy limiting how much history is exportable
mitreTechniques: T1213.003 Data from Information Repositories: Messaging Apps
controls: Restricted admin export permissions with approval workflow
Third-party app permission scope review
Message retention/deletion policy
ITID-51531.detection: Moderate; workspace admin audit logs provide good signal for bulk exports if actively monitored, but ordinary message access generates little distinguishing telemetry.
ITID-51531.response: Revoke the compromised credential/app access immediately, determine scope of exported history, and assess sensitivity of exposed discussions with legal.
metrics: Number of confirmed message history leak incidents per period
Volume of message history exposed
Third-party apps under active permission review
ITID-51531.notes: T1213.003 maps to messaging-app data repositories per the Operational Data Breach MITRE mapping guidance for internal communications leaks.

playbook.name: Leaked Internal Slack/Teams Message History Response
playbook.description: Internal Slack or Microsoft Teams message history is leaked externally, exposing internal discussions.

steps.title: Confirm the leaked message history and its source
steps.desc: Validate the leaked content against internal Slack/Teams records to confirm authenticity and identify the workspace/channels involved.
steps.guidance: Compare leaked message samples (timestamps, participants, content) against internal export/audit logs to confirm the source platform and channel(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity and scope of leaked channels/messages.
steps.abort: If the leaked content cannot be verified as authentic internal data, document as unconfirmed and monitor.

steps.title: Determine the exfiltration vector
steps.desc: Investigate how the message history was obtained: compromised account, malicious export by an insider, third-party app/integration compromise, or platform-level vulnerability.
steps.guidance: Review authentication logs, third-party app integration audit logs, and export activity logs for the affected workspace.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector identified.

steps.title: Revoke compromised access and third-party app integrations
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account, session, or third-party integration identified as the exfiltration vector.
steps.guidance: Review and revoke any third-party apps with broad export/read scopes as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector closed; no further unauthorized export possible.

steps.title: Assess reputational and legal exposure from message content
steps.desc: Beyond standard breach response, review the substance of the leaked messages for content that could create additional legal exposure (e.g., discriminatory remarks, trade secrets, executive communications, discussions of pending litigation) or reputational harm.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal and Communications early to jointly review a sample of leaked content and prepare a risk assessment distinct from a standard PII breach review.
steps.outcome: Documented assessment of reputational and legal exposure with a coordinated response plan.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance on notification and disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Determine whether any personal data or regulated information within the messages triggers standard breach-notification obligations, separate from the reputational assessment.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance tracking notification obligations as applicable.

steps.title: Remediate the account/integration compromise root cause
steps.desc: Reset credentials, enforce MFA, and tighten third-party app approval processes to close the vulnerability that enabled the leak.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Coordinate public/internal communications response
steps.desc: Execute a coordinated internal and (if needed) public communications response addressing the leak, informed by the legal/reputational risk assessment.
steps.outcome: Communications response executed with stakeholder alignment.

steps.title: Review collaboration-platform data governance
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to third-party app governance, message retention policy, and sensitive-topic communication guidelines for collaboration platforms.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved governance improvements.

ITID-51532.def: An incident in which an internal email thread or chain is disclosed to an unauthorized external party, whether through mailbox compromise, misdirected forwarding, or deliberate leak.
ITID-51532.purpose: Captures leaks of internal email thread chains, distinct from collaboration-platform and meeting-recording leaks by channel and forwarding-driven propagation.
scopeIncludes: Compromised mailbox exposing internal email threads to an attacker
Email thread inadvertently or deliberately forwarded to an external recipient
Bulk email export via compromised mail server/admin access
scopeExcludes: Collaboration platform message history leaks (Leaked Internal Slack/Teams Message History leaf)
Leaked meeting recordings/transcripts (Leaked Internal Meeting Recording/Transcript leaf)
PHI-specific misdirected medical communications (Misdirected Medical Communication leaf, if the content is specifically PHI)
ITID-51532.severity: Medium-High, scaling with the sensitivity of the thread content and the breadth of external disclosure.
ITID-51532.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the thread contains legal privilege, M&A, security, or executive-sensitive content.
ITID-51532.escalation: Escalate to legal and communications/PR immediately if the leaked thread touches privileged, regulatory, or reputationally sensitive matters.
indicators: Mailbox audit log showing anomalous forwarding rules or bulk export activity
Leaked email content found circulating externally (leak site, media, competitor)
Recipient reports of receiving an email chain they were not an intended party to
vectors: Business email compromise (BEC) granting attacker read access to mailbox history
Auto-forwarding rule silently added to a compromised mailbox
Deliberate forwarding by an insider to an external party
rootCauses: Lack of monitoring for anomalous mailbox forwarding rules
Weak email account authentication enabling compromise
Insufficient data handling training on forwarding sensitive threads
controls: Monitoring for anomalous mailbox auto-forwarding rules
Multi-factor authentication on email accounts
DLP scanning on outbound email
ITID-51532.detection: Good where mailbox audit logging and forwarding-rule monitoring are enabled; deliberate insider forwarding to external addresses is harder to distinguish from legitimate business communication without DLP.
ITID-51532.response: Remove any malicious forwarding rules, secure the mailbox, and assess the scope and sensitivity of the exposed thread with legal.
metrics: Number of confirmed email leak incidents per period
Mailboxes with anomalous forwarding rules detected/removed
Time from compromise to detection
ITID-51532.notes: T1114 (Email Collection) is used here as the closest ATT&CK Enterprise technique for email-thread-based collection preceding exfiltration.

playbook.name: Leaked Internal Email Thread Chain Response
playbook.description: An internal email thread chain is leaked externally, exposing sensitive internal discussions.

steps.title: Confirm the leaked email thread and its source mailbox(es)
steps.desc: Validate the leaked content against internal email records to confirm authenticity and identify the originating mailbox(es)/thread.
steps.guidance: Compare leaked email headers and content against mail server logs/archives to confirm authenticity and scope.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity and scope of the leaked thread and participants.
steps.abort: If the leaked content cannot be verified as authentic, document as unconfirmed and monitor.

steps.title: Determine the exfiltration vector
steps.desc: Investigate whether the leak occurred via a compromised mailbox, forwarding rule, insider forwarding, or third-party mail app compromise.
steps.guidance: Review mailbox audit logs for suspicious forwarding rules, mail exports, or delegate access changes.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector identified.

steps.title: Remove malicious forwarding rules and secure the mailbox
steps.desc: Remove any unauthorized forwarding rules, reset credentials, and secure the affected mailbox(es).
steps.guidance: Check all mailboxes in the thread chain, not just the originally reported one, for similar unauthorized rules.
steps.outcome: Mailbox(es) secured with no further unauthorized forwarding.

steps.title: Assess reputational and legal exposure from email content
steps.desc: Review the substance of the leaked thread for content creating legal exposure or reputational harm beyond standard PII concerns.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal and Communications to jointly assess the content and prepare a coordinated response plan.
steps.outcome: Documented risk assessment with coordinated response plan.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance on notification obligations
steps.desc: Determine whether any personal or regulated data within the emails triggers standard breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance tracking notification obligations as applicable.

steps.title: Remediate the mailbox compromise root cause
steps.desc: Reset credentials, enforce MFA, and audit mail-rule creation permissions to close the vulnerability that enabled the leak.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Coordinate communications response
steps.desc: Execute a coordinated internal and (if needed) public communications response addressing the leak.
steps.outcome: Communications response executed with stakeholder alignment.

steps.title: Review email security controls and sensitive-topic guidelines
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to mail-rule monitoring, DLP for outbound email, and guidelines on discussing sensitive topics via email.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved control improvements.

ITID-51533.def: An incident in which a recording or transcript of an internal meeting is disclosed to an unauthorized external party, whether through storage misconfiguration, compromised meeting-platform access, or deliberate leak.
ITID-51533.purpose: Captures leaks of internal meeting recordings or transcripts, distinct from text-based communications by their audio/video/transcript medium and typically richer disclosure of tone and detail.
scopeIncludes: Meeting recording stored in a misconfigured cloud location and accessed externally
Meeting platform account compromise exposing recording/transcript libraries
Deliberate leak of a recording/transcript by a meeting participant or insider
scopeExcludes: Text-based collaboration platform or email leaks (Leaked Internal Slack/Teams Message History and Leaked Internal Email Thread Chain leaves)
Recording/transcript stored in a general cloud bucket where the root cause is a bucket-level misconfiguration unrelated to the meeting platform (Cloud Storage Exposure leaves)
ITID-51533.severity: Medium-High; recordings and transcripts often reveal more candid detail and speaker attribution than written communications, increasing reputational and legal risk.
ITID-51533.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the recording contains legal privilege, M&A, security, or executive-sensitive discussion.
ITID-51533.escalation: Escalate to legal and communications/PR immediately given the heightened reputational risk of audio/video leaks (verifiable speaker attribution, tone, informal remarks).
indicators: Meeting platform audit log showing anomalous access to recording/transcript libraries
Recording or transcript content found circulating externally (leak site, media)
Unrecognized download activity from the meeting platform's recording storage
vectors: Compromised meeting platform account credentials
Recording auto-saved to an inadequately secured storage location
Insider recording a meeting without authorization and leaking it externally
rootCauses: Lack of access control granularity on recording/transcript libraries
Default recording storage settings not aligned with data sensitivity
Insufficient policy on recording retention and access
controls: Access control on meeting recording/transcript storage
Recording retention and deletion policy
Meeting platform audit log monitoring
ITID-51533.detection: Moderate; meeting platform audit logs provide reasonable signal for anomalous access if actively monitored, but unauthorized recording by a legitimate participant generates no technical signal.
ITID-51533.response: Restrict access to the recording/transcript immediately, determine scope of exposure, and assess sensitivity with legal and communications.
metrics: Number of confirmed recording/transcript leak incidents per period
Recordings under active access control review
Time from leak to detection
detections: Meeting platform recording access anomaly monitoring
ITID-51533.notes: Differentiated from the other Internal Communications Leak leaves by medium (audio/video/transcript) rather than by attack vector.

playbook.name: Leaked Internal Meeting Recording/Transcript Response
playbook.description: An internal meeting recording or transcript is leaked externally, exposing sensitive discussions.

steps.title: Confirm the leaked recording/transcript and its source meeting
steps.desc: Validate the leaked content against internal recording/transcript records to confirm authenticity and identify the specific meeting and platform (Zoom, Teams, etc.) involved.
steps.guidance: Compare leaked audio/video/transcript against internal recording storage metadata to confirm authenticity and scope.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity and identified source meeting/platform.
steps.abort: If the leaked content cannot be verified as authentic, document as unconfirmed and monitor.

steps.title: Determine the exfiltration vector
steps.desc: Investigate whether the leak occurred via a compromised cloud recording storage location, an attendee sharing the file, or unauthorized meeting access (e.g., meeting-bombing/uninvited attendee).
steps.guidance: Review recording storage access logs and meeting attendee lists/join logs for the session in question.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector identified.

steps.title: Remove/restrict access to the recording and secure storage location
steps.desc: Restrict or remove the recording from any accessible storage location and secure the platform account/integration identified as the vector.
steps.outcome: Recording no longer accessible via the identified vector.
steps.tool: Cloud storage / meeting platform admin console

steps.title: Assess reputational and legal exposure from recorded content
steps.desc: Review the substance of the recording/transcript for content creating legal exposure or reputational harm.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal and Communications to jointly assess the content and prepare a coordinated response plan, particularly if executives or sensitive strategic discussions are involved.
steps.outcome: Documented risk assessment with coordinated response plan.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance on notification obligations
steps.desc: Determine whether any personal or regulated data within the recording triggers standard breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance tracking notification obligations as applicable.

steps.title: Remediate meeting/recording security controls
steps.desc: Implement or tighten meeting access controls (waiting rooms, authentication requirements) and recording storage access restrictions to close the vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Coordinate communications response
steps.desc: Execute a coordinated internal and (if needed) public communications response addressing the leak.
steps.outcome: Communications response executed with stakeholder alignment.

steps.title: Review meeting recording policy and access governance
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to recording retention policy, storage access governance, and meeting security defaults.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved policy improvements.

ITID-51534.def: An intake classification for incidents involving disclosure of internal communications where the medium or mechanism (collaboration platform, email, or meeting recording) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51534.purpose: Captures a confirmed internal communications leak that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Internal Communications Leak.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed internal communications leak of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
Leaked content spanning multiple communication channels
scopeExcludes: Confirmed collaboration platform leak (Leaked Internal Slack/Teams Message History leaf)
Confirmed email thread leak (Leaked Internal Email Thread Chain leaf)
Confirmed meeting recording/transcript leak (Leaked Internal Meeting Recording/Transcript leaf)
ITID-51534.severity: Medium-High by default, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51534.priority: P2 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the medium/mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51534.escalation: Escalate to legal and communications/PR for an initial sensitivity assessment while triage to a specific leaf proceeds.
indicators: Report of leaked internal content with insufficient detail to determine the source channel
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard internal communications leak intake and triage process
ITID-51534.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51534.response: Rapidly triage to determine the source channel and reclassify; begin sensitivity assessment in parallel regardless of classification status.
metrics: Number of unclassified internal communications leak incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51534.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Internal Communications Leak leaf as soon as the source channel is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Internal Communications Leak Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed internal communications leak not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported internal communications leak
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected leak and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (Slack/Teams, email, meeting recording) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review relevant platform logs to identify the likely source and mechanism.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Assess reputational and legal exposure from leaked content
steps.desc: Review the substance of the leaked communications for content creating legal exposure or reputational harm in addition to any PII/data concerns.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal and Communications for a joint content review.
steps.outcome: Documented risk assessment.

steps.title: Secure the identified source system/account
steps.desc: Restrict or secure access to the platform/account identified as the likely source of the leak.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with findings to assess breach-notification obligations if personal or regulated data is involved.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking the matter as applicable.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or access issue responsible for the leak once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to the communications platform remains
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access, forwarding rules, or third-party app integrations remain active after the primary remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Coordinate communications response and complete notifications
steps.desc: Execute a coordinated communications response and complete any required notifications.
steps.outcome: Communications response executed; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update governance controls
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements for internal communications platforms.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51541.def: An incident in which physical backup media (tape, external hard drive, removable disk) containing organizational data is lost in transit, misplaced, or stolen, and was not adequately encrypted.
ITID-51541.purpose: Captures loss or theft of unencrypted physical backup media, a legacy but still-occurring breach vector distinguished by its physical, non-network nature.
scopeIncludes: Backup tape lost during transport to/from an offsite storage facility
Backup media stolen from a vehicle, courier, or storage location
Backup media misplaced during a data center move or decommissioning
scopeExcludes: Network-based breach of a backup storage server (Backup Storage Server Breached via Weak Access Controls leaf)
Breach occurring at a third-party backup service provider's own infrastructure (Third-Party Backup Service Provider Breach leaf)
ITID-51541.severity: High if the media was unencrypted; Medium-Low if encryption is confirmed and no other compromise indicators exist.
ITID-51541.priority: P1 pending confirmation of encryption status; downgrade to P3 once encryption is verified.
ITID-51541.escalation: Escalate to legal/privacy immediately; encryption status is the key determinant of reportable-breach status under most data protection regimes.
indicators: Courier or logistics tracking showing a lost or undelivered shipment of backup media
Physical security report of theft from a vehicle or facility
Inventory reconciliation discovering missing backup media
vectors: Opportunistic theft during transport or storage
Loss due to inadequate chain-of-custody tracking
Media discarded/decommissioned without proper destruction
rootCauses: Lack of encryption on physical backup media
Insufficient chain-of-custody controls for offsite media transport
No secure destruction process for decommissioned media
mitreTechniques: T1052.001 Exfiltration Over Physical Medium: Exfiltration over USB
controls: Mandatory encryption of all physical backup media
Chain-of-custody tracking for offsite media transport
Certified secure destruction process for decommissioned media
ITID-51541.detection: No technical detection surface; reliant entirely on inventory reconciliation, courier tracking, and physical security incident reporting.
ITID-51541.response: Confirm encryption status immediately, notify the offsite storage/courier provider, and route to legal/privacy for breach risk assessment.
metrics: Number of lost/stolen backup media incidents per period
Percentage of backup media confirmed encrypted
Time from loss to detection via reconciliation
ITID-51541.notes: No ATT&CK Enterprise mapping applies; physical media loss/theft is outside ATT&CK Enterprise's network-intrusion technique set.

playbook.name: Unencrypted Backup Tape/Media Lost or Stolen Response
playbook.description: A physical backup tape or storage medium containing unencrypted data is lost in transit or stolen.

steps.title: Confirm the loss/theft and encryption status of the media
steps.desc: Validate the report of lost/stolen physical backup media, confirm chain-of-custody records, and determine definitively whether the media was encrypted.
steps.guidance: Review courier/transport tracking records, media inventory logs, and the backup system's configuration to confirm encryption status at the time of loss.
steps.outcome: Confirmed loss/theft event with definitive encryption status established.
steps.abort: If the media is later located and confirmed unaccessed, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Determine data contents and affected population
steps.desc: Identify exactly what data was on the lost/stolen media (backup date, systems/databases covered) and the resulting affected individual count.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the specific backup job/version with the media inventory to determine contents as of that backup date.
steps.outcome: Documented data contents and affected population count.

steps.title: Notify courier/facility and initiate physical recovery efforts
steps.desc: Notify the courier/transport provider or facility security, file a police report if stolen, and initiate any available recovery/tracking efforts.
steps.outcome: Recovery/tracking efforts initiated; police report filed if applicable.
steps.abort: If recovery is not feasible, proceed directly to loss documentation and notification planning.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance immediately given unencrypted status
steps.desc: Because the media was unencrypted, escalate immediately to Legal/Compliance — unencrypted data loss typically triggers mandatory breach notification under GLBA/state law with no safe-harbor exemption.
steps.guidance: Provide confirmed data contents and affected population so Legal can begin the notification timeline without delay.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has an active tracked notification workflow.

steps.title: Remediate the encryption gap as the core corrective action
steps.desc: Implement mandatory encryption for all backup media (tape, portable drives) going forward, and encrypt/re-issue any similar media currently in circulation.
steps.guidance: This is the central eradication action for this incident type — the root failure was the absence of encryption at rest on physical backup media, not merely the loss event itself.
steps.outcome: All backup media confirmed encrypted; unencrypted media inventory eliminated.

steps.title: Review physical media handling and transport procedures
steps.desc: Assess and tighten chain-of-custody and transport procedures for physical backup media (locked containers, tracked couriers, reduced physical media reliance).
steps.guidance: Consider transitioning to encrypted cloud/network-based backup to reduce reliance on physical media transport altogether.
steps.outcome: Updated handling procedures documented and implemented.

steps.title: Notify affected individuals and offer protective services
steps.desc: Complete notifications to all affected individuals per the Legal-approved timeline, offering credit monitoring/identity protection given the unencrypted nature of the exposure.
steps.outcome: All affected individuals notified and offered protective services.

steps.title: Conduct encryption-gap remediation review
steps.desc: Document the incident with a specific focus on how the encryption gap arose and formalize a policy mandating encryption for all backup media as a non-negotiable control.
steps.outcome: After-action report with an approved mandatory-encryption policy for all backup media.

ITID-51542.def: An incident in which an adversary gains unauthorized access to a backup storage server or repository due to weak, default, or improperly managed access controls, and exfiltrates or exposes backed-up data.
ITID-51542.purpose: Captures compromise of a backup storage server via weak access controls, a network-based breach vector distinct from physical media loss.
scopeIncludes: Backup server accessed via default or weak credentials
Backup repository exposed due to missing network segmentation from general corporate access
Backup management console compromised via unpatched vulnerability or weak authentication
scopeExcludes: Physical loss/theft of backup media (Unencrypted Backup Tape/Media Lost or Stolen leaf)
Breach occurring at a third-party backup service provider's own infrastructure (Third-Party Backup Service Provider Breach leaf)
Cloud-hosted backup/snapshot exposure via misconfiguration (Cloud Storage Snapshot/Backup leaf)
ITID-51542.severity: High; backup servers often hold aggregated, comprehensive copies of organizational data spanning multiple systems and time periods.
ITID-51542.priority: P1 upon confirmation of unauthorized backup server access, given the typically broad scope of data held.
ITID-51542.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure/backup administration and legal/privacy immediately; assess the full scope of systems whose data resides on the compromised backup server.
indicators: Backup server authentication logs showing access from an unrecognized account or unusual login pattern
Backup management console accessed outside normal administrative hours
Anomalous bulk restore/export activity on the backup server
vectors: Default or weak credentials on the backup management console
Lack of network segmentation allowing lateral movement to the backup server from a compromised endpoint
Exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability in backup software
rootCauses: Weak or default access controls on backup infrastructure
Insufficient network segmentation isolating backup systems
Delayed patching of backup software vulnerabilities
controls: Strong, unique authentication on backup management systems
Network segmentation isolating backup infrastructure
Timely patching of backup software
ITID-51542.detection: Moderate; depends on whether backup infrastructure is included in the same authentication and access monitoring scope as production systems, which is often overlooked.
ITID-51542.response: Isolate the backup server immediately, determine scope of data accessed/exfiltrated, and assess breach notification obligations.
metrics: Number of confirmed backup server compromise incidents per period
Systems/datasets whose backups were exposed
Time from compromise to detection
ITID-51542.notes: T1530/T1213 combined with a weak-access-control root cause per the Operational Data Breach MITRE mapping guidance for backup breaches.

playbook.name: Backup Storage Server Breached via Weak Access Controls Response
playbook.description: An attacker breaches a backup storage server due to weak access controls, exposing backed-up data.

steps.title: Confirm the backup storage server breach
steps.desc: Validate alerts or evidence of unauthorized access to the backup storage server and identify the weak access control that was exploited (default credentials, exposed management interface, weak password policy).
steps.guidance: Review server authentication logs, network exposure scans, and any recent configuration changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed breach with the specific weak-control vector identified.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope backup data accessed or exfiltrated
steps.desc: Determine which backup sets/data stores on the server were accessed, downloaded, or deleted by the attacker.
steps.guidance: Review server access/transfer logs for the affected time window.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected backup data.

steps.title: Isolate the backup storage server from the network
steps.desc: Immediately isolate the compromised backup server from the network to prevent further access or exfiltration.
steps.guidance: Ensure isolation does not disrupt in-progress legitimate backup jobs unnecessarily; coordinate with backup operations.
steps.outcome: Attacker access fully severed.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and close the weak access control
steps.desc: Rotate all administrative and service credentials for the backup server and immediately close the specific weak control identified (disable default accounts, close exposed management ports, enforce strong password/MFA policy).
steps.outcome: Weak control closed; all credentials rotated.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed scope of exposed backup data to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking notification obligations.

steps.title: Harden backup server access architecture
steps.desc: Implement network segmentation, MFA, and least-privilege access for the backup storage environment to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Consider placing backup infrastructure on an isolated management network not directly internet-accessible.
steps.outcome: Hardened access architecture verified via follow-up scan.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity and restore secured operations
steps.desc: Verify remaining backups were not tampered with or deleted, restore normal backup operations under the hardened configuration, and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Backup operations resumed with verified integrity; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review backup infrastructure security baseline
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish a hardened security baseline (network isolation, MFA, credential policy) required for all backup infrastructure.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved security baseline for backup infrastructure.

ITID-51543.def: An incident in which a third-party backup-as-a-service or managed backup provider experiences a breach that exposes organizational data it holds on the organization's behalf.
ITID-51543.purpose: Captures backup data breaches originating at a third-party backup service provider rather than the organization's own infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: Breach of a cloud backup service provider's infrastructure
Breach of a managed backup/disaster-recovery vendor
Provider-side insider misuse of organizational backup data
scopeExcludes: Breach of backup infrastructure the organization directly operates (Backup Storage Server Breached via Weak Access Controls leaf)
Physical loss of media in the organization's own custody or transport (Unencrypted Backup Tape/Media Lost or Stolen leaf)
ITID-51543.severity: High; the organization retains data protection responsibility even though the breach originated with the provider, and backup data typically spans a wide historical range.
ITID-51543.priority: P1 upon notification from the backup provider; treat as an active incident until scope and affected data are confirmed.
ITID-51543.escalation: Escalate to legal and vendor/procurement management immediately upon provider notification; review the service agreement for liability, notification timelines, and data protection terms.
indicators: Formal breach notification received from the backup service provider
Media or regulatory disclosure naming a backup provider used by the organization
Anomalous restore/access activity reported by the provider
vectors: Compromise of the provider's own infrastructure (credential theft, ransomware, misconfiguration)
Insider misuse within the provider's organization
Weak access controls on the provider's customer-facing management portal
rootCauses: Insufficient due diligence on provider security posture prior to engagement
Service agreement lacking specific security control or notification-timeliness requirements
Lack of ongoing monitoring of provider security incidents
controls: Contractual security and notification requirements with backup service providers
Periodic vendor security risk assessments for backup providers
Encryption of data prior to transmission to third-party backup services (client-side encryption)
ITID-51543.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; the organization typically learns of the breach via provider notification rather than its own monitoring, since the compromise occurs outside its infrastructure.
ITID-51543.response: Confirm scope of affected data with the provider, assess contractual obligations, and coordinate notification as required.
metrics: Number of third-party backup provider breaches per period
Time from provider notification to internal escalation
Providers under active security monitoring/review
sops: Third-Party Backup Provider Breach Response SOP
ITID-51543.notes: Cross-reference the Supply Chain Data Breach category (Vendor Data Breach leaves) for the general vendor-breach pattern this leaf specializes for backup services.

playbook.name: Third-Party Backup Service Provider Breach Response
playbook.description: A third-party backup service provider suffers a breach, exposing the company's backed-up data.

steps.title: Validate third-party backup provider breach notification
steps.desc: Confirm details of the breach notification received from the backup service provider, including scope, timeline, and data types affected.
steps.guidance: Request the provider's incident report and specific data elements exposed for this company's backed-up data.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the provider's breach scope as it pertains to this company's data.
steps.abort: If the provider cannot yet confirm scope, escalate for a formal update timeline rather than closing the case.

steps.title: Determine data sensitivity and encryption status at the provider
steps.desc: Assess whether the company's data was encrypted at the provider (client-side encryption keys retained by the company vs. provider-managed encryption) which significantly affects actual exposure risk.
steps.guidance: Review the service agreement and technical architecture to confirm who controlled the encryption keys.
steps.outcome: Documented encryption/key-custody status and resulting exposure risk assessment.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and API keys shared with the provider
steps.desc: Immediately rotate all credentials, API keys, and encryption keys shared with or accessible to the backup provider.
steps.outcome: All shared credentials/keys rotated.

steps.title: Engage vendor-relationship manager and contract review
steps.desc: Engage the vendor relationship manager and Legal to review contractual breach-notification, liability, and data-protection clauses, and demand a formal incident report and remediation plan from the provider.
steps.guidance: Check contractual SLAs for notification timing compliance.
steps.outcome: Vendor contract obligations reviewed; formal demand for provider cooperation issued.

steps.title: Notify Legal/Compliance of the company's own independent notification obligations
steps.desc: Confirm the company's own notification obligations to affected customers/employees under GLBA/state law, independent of the vendor's own notifications.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has an active tracked notification workflow.

steps.title: Verify provider remediation before resuming full data transfer
steps.desc: Obtain and review evidence from the provider that the root cause of their breach has been remediated before resuming normal backup operations.
steps.guidance: Request a remediation attestation or third-party audit report.
steps.outcome: Provider remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If the provider cannot demonstrate remediation, escalate to leadership to consider suspending the relationship or migrating providers.

steps.title: Resume backup operations and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Resume normal backup operations with the provider under verified remediation (or a new provider) and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Backup operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review third-party backup vendor risk management
steps.desc: Document lessons learned and update vendor risk assessment criteria for backup providers, including encryption/key-custody requirements and incident-notification SLAs.
steps.outcome: After-action report with updated vendor risk management requirements.

ITID-51544.def: An intake classification for incidents involving exposure or theft of backup data where the mechanism (physical media loss, backup server compromise, or third-party provider breach) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51544.purpose: Captures a confirmed backup data breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Backup Data Breach.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed backup data exposure of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
scopeExcludes: Confirmed physical media loss/theft (Unencrypted Backup Tape/Media Lost or Stolen leaf)
Confirmed backup server compromise (Backup Storage Server Breached via Weak Access Controls leaf)
Confirmed third-party provider breach (Third-Party Backup Service Provider Breach leaf)
ITID-51544.severity: High by default given the typically comprehensive nature of backup data, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51544.priority: P1 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51544.escalation: Escalate to legal/privacy immediately; do not wait for reclassification before beginning breach assessment.
indicators: Report of exposed or compromised backup data with insufficient detail to determine mechanism
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard backup breach intake and triage process
ITID-51544.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51544.response: Rapidly triage to determine the mechanism and reclassify; begin breach assessment in parallel regardless of classification status.
metrics: Number of unclassified backup data breach incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51544.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Backup Data Breach leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Backup Data Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed backup data breach not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported backup data breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (lost/stolen unencrypted media, breached backup server, third-party provider breach) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review backup system logs and incident details to identify the likely mechanism.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Determine data sensitivity, encryption status, and affected scope
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of affected backup data, whether it was encrypted, and the affected individual/record count.
steps.outcome: Documented scope, sensitivity, and encryption status.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected backup system
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the affected backup system/media as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed scope and encryption status to assess breach-notification obligations, noting that unencrypted data typically has no safe-harbor exemption.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause, including any encryption gap
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or process gap responsible for the breach, with particular attention to closing any encryption gap discovered.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified, including encryption coverage where applicable.

steps.title: Verify encryption coverage across all backup media and systems
steps.desc: Conduct an inventory check to confirm encryption is applied consistently across all backup media and storage systems, closing any gaps beyond the specific incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed complete encryption coverage across backup systems.

steps.title: Restore normal backup operations and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Restore normal backup operations under corrected controls and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update backup security controls
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements, including encryption coverage, for backup systems.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51611.def: An incident in which a third-party vendor holding organizational customer data on the organization's behalf experiences a breach originating entirely within the vendor's own environment, exposing that customer data.
ITID-51611.purpose: Captures the scenario where a vendor entrusted with the organization's customer data suffers its own independent breach.
scopeIncludes: Vendor's own systems (unrelated to any shared integration) compromised, exposing customer data stored or processed there
Vendor breach discovered via the vendor's own incident disclosure
Ransomware or external attack against the vendor's infrastructure holding organizational customer data
scopeExcludes: Breach caused by a vendor employee's deliberate insider action (Vendor Employee Insider Breach leaf)
