Breach discovered only through downstream fraud/credential reuse rather than vendor disclosure (Vendor Breach Discovered via Downstream Fraud leaf)
Breach occurring within a shared API/integration point (Shared API Integration Breach leaf, under Partner Integration Breach)
ITID-51611.severity: High; the organization retains customer notification responsibility even though the failure originated with the vendor.
ITID-51611.priority: P1 upon notification from the vendor; treat as an active incident until scope and affected customer count are confirmed.
ITID-51611.escalation: Escalate to legal, privacy, and vendor/procurement management immediately upon vendor notification; review the vendor contract/DPA for liability and notification-timeliness terms.
indicators: Formal breach notification received from the vendor
Media or regulatory disclosure naming a vendor used by the organization
Customer complaints referencing data known only to have been shared with a specific vendor
vectors: External attack against the vendor's infrastructure (phishing, ransomware, vulnerability exploitation)
Vendor's own subcontractor breach flowing upstream
Vendor misconfiguration exposing organizational customer data
rootCauses: Insufficient vendor security due diligence prior to onboarding
Data processing agreement (DPA) lacking specific security control or notification-timeliness requirements
Lack of ongoing vendor risk monitoring
controls: Data processing agreement (DPA) with defined security and notification terms
Periodic vendor security risk assessments
Data minimization (limiting what customer data is shared with vendors)
ITID-51611.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; the organization typically learns of the breach through vendor notification, media disclosure, or customer complaints rather than its own monitoring.
ITID-51611.response: Confirm scope of affected customers with the vendor, assess DPA/contractual obligations, and coordinate customer notification as required by applicable law.
metrics: Number of vendor-originated customer data breaches per period
Time from vendor notification to customer notification
Vendors with overdue security assessments
ITID-51611.notes: Differentiated from downstream-fraud discovery by disclosure path: here the vendor proactively discloses, rather than the breach being inferred from fraud patterns.

playbook.name: Vendor Holding Customer Data Suffers Own Breach Response
playbook.description: A vendor entrusted with company customer data suffers its own security breach, exposing that data.

steps.title: Validate the vendor's breach notification and confirm data implicated
steps.desc: Confirm the details of the breach notification received from the vendor (often the first and only source of awareness), including scope, timeline, and which company customer data elements were affected.
steps.guidance: Request the vendor's formal incident report; note that the company may have no independent visibility into the vendor's environment and must rely heavily on vendor disclosure.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the vendor's breach scope as it pertains to company customer data.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot yet confirm scope, escalate for a formal update timeline rather than closing the case.

steps.title: Identify all internal systems/processes dependent on the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Map which internal business processes, customer segments, and data flows depend on this vendor to fully understand the scope of impact.
steps.guidance: Consult vendor inventory/data-flow documentation maintained by procurement/vendor management.
steps.outcome: Documented map of affected internal dependencies.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and API keys shared with the vendor
steps.desc: Immediately rotate all credentials, API keys, and access tokens shared with the vendor as a precaution.
steps.outcome: All shared credentials rotated.

steps.title: Engage vendor-relationship manager and review contractual notification obligations
steps.desc: Engage the vendor relationship manager and Legal/procurement to review the contract's breach-notification, liability, indemnification, and audit-right clauses, and formally demand full incident details from the vendor.
steps.guidance: Since the company may only learn of the breach via the vendor's own disclosure, ensure the contractual notification-timing obligation was actually met and document any breach of that obligation.
steps.outcome: Vendor contract obligations reviewed; formal demand for cooperation and remediation evidence issued.

steps.title: Notify Legal/Compliance of the company's own independent notification obligations
steps.desc: Confirm the company's own notification obligations to its customers under applicable breach-notification law, independent of the vendor's own notifications to its other clients.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has an active tracked notification workflow.

steps.title: Verify vendor remediation before resuming full data sharing
steps.desc: Obtain and review evidence (remediation attestation, third-party audit) that the vendor has fully remediated the root cause before resuming normal data flows.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot demonstrate remediation, escalate to leadership to consider suspending the relationship or requiring compensating controls.

steps.title: Resume vendor data sharing and notify affected customers
steps.desc: Resume normal data sharing with the vendor under verified remediation and complete required customer notifications.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; customers notified as required.

steps.title: Review vendor risk management and contractual notification requirements
steps.desc: Document lessons learned and update vendor risk assessment/contractual requirements, including stricter breach-notification SLAs and audit rights for vendors holding customer data.
steps.outcome: After-action report with updated vendor risk management requirements.

ITID-51612.def: An incident in which an employee or contractor of a third-party vendor deliberately misuses their access to expose, leak, or sell organizational data entrusted to the vendor.
ITID-51612.purpose: Captures vendor breaches caused specifically by a vendor employee's deliberate insider action, distinct from external attacks against the vendor.
scopeIncludes: Vendor employee accessing and exfiltrating organizational data outside their authorized scope
Vendor employee selling or leaking organizational customer data to a third party
Vendor contractor retaining organizational data after contract termination and later leaking it
scopeExcludes: External attack against the vendor's infrastructure (Vendor Holding Customer Data Suffers Own Breach leaf)
Breach discovered only through downstream fraud/credential reuse (Vendor Breach Discovered via Downstream Fraud leaf)
ITID-51612.severity: High; insider misuse at a vendor is particularly difficult to detect since the organization has no direct visibility into the vendor's internal personnel controls.
ITID-51612.priority: P1 upon confirmation of vendor insider misuse; treat as an active incident requiring joint investigation with the vendor.
ITID-51612.escalation: Escalate to legal and vendor/procurement management immediately; request the vendor's insider threat investigation findings and assess contractual remedies.
indicators: Vendor notification of a confirmed internal investigation into employee misuse
Organizational data found for sale or leaked with characteristics indicating vendor-insider origin (e.g., a specific subset of records unique to that vendor relationship)
Vendor employee's suspicious departure coinciding with data misuse discovery
vectors: Vendor employee with legitimate access exceeding authorized use for personal gain
Vendor employee retaining data access after role change or termination due to vendor offboarding gaps
Vendor employee colluding with an external party to exfiltrate organizational data
rootCauses: Vendor's own insufficient least-privilege access controls for its staff
Lack of contractual requirement for vendor background checks/insider threat controls
Vendor offboarding gaps not covered by the service agreement
controls: Contractual requirement for vendor insider threat and access controls
Data minimization limiting vendor staff exposure to organizational data
Right-to-audit clauses covering vendor personnel access controls
ITID-51612.detection: Minimal direct technical detection from the organization's side; detection depends almost entirely on the vendor's own internal controls and disclosure.
ITID-51612.response: Request full scope details from the vendor's investigation, assess contractual remedies, and notify affected customers/employees as required.
metrics: Number of vendor insider misuse incidents per period
Records affected per incident
Vendors with contractual insider threat control requirements
ITID-51612.notes: Differentiated from the vendor's-own-external-breach leaf by the human/motive axis: this is a trust failure within the vendor's workforce, not a technical compromise of the vendor's systems.

playbook.name: Vendor Employee Insider Breach Affecting Client Data Response
playbook.description: An employee of a vendor with access to the company's data misuses that access, resulting in a data breach affecting the company's data.

steps.title: Validate the vendor's disclosure of the insider incident
steps.desc: Confirm details from the vendor regarding the identified insider employee, the nature of the misuse, and which company data was affected.
steps.guidance: Request the vendor's formal incident report and any evidence of the specific data accessed or exfiltrated by their employee.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the vendor-side insider incident as it pertains to company data.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot yet confirm scope, escalate for a formal update timeline.

steps.title: Cross-reference internal access logs for corroborating evidence
steps.desc: Where the vendor's insider had direct access to company systems (not just vendor-hosted data), review internal access logs to corroborate the vendor's account and identify any additional scope.
steps.outcome: Internal access records reviewed and cross-referenced with vendor's account.
steps.abort: If the insider had no direct access to company systems, note this and rely on vendor-provided scope.

steps.title: Revoke the vendor employee's access to company systems and data
steps.desc: Immediately revoke any direct access the vendor employee had to company systems, applications, or shared data repositories.
steps.outcome: Vendor employee's access to company resources fully revoked.

steps.title: Engage vendor-relationship manager on contractual liability and remediation
steps.desc: Engage the vendor relationship manager and Legal to review contractual liability, indemnification, and required remediation actions (personnel action, enhanced monitoring) from the vendor regarding their employee.
steps.outcome: Vendor contractual obligations reviewed; remediation demands issued.

steps.title: Notify Legal/Compliance of independent notification obligations
steps.desc: Confirm the company's own notification obligations to affected customers/employees under applicable breach-notification law.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance has an active tracked notification workflow.

steps.title: Review and tighten vendor employee access model
steps.desc: Reassess the level of access granted to vendor personnel and implement least-privilege, time-bound, and monitored access going forward.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring named-user access reviews and periodic recertification for all vendor personnel with access to company data.
steps.outcome: Vendor access model tightened and documented.

steps.title: Resume vendor operations under enhanced access governance and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Resume normal vendor operations under the tightened access model and complete required customer/employee notifications.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review vendor personnel access governance policy
steps.desc: Document lessons learned and formalize requirements for vendor personnel background checks, access recertification, and monitoring as part of vendor risk management.
steps.outcome: After-action report with updated vendor personnel governance policy.

ITID-51613.def: An incident in which a vendor breach is inferred or confirmed through observed downstream harm (fraudulent transactions, credential stuffing success, targeted phishing using vendor-sourced details) before or without formal notification from the vendor itself.
ITID-51613.purpose: Captures vendor breaches first identified indirectly through downstream fraud or credential reuse patterns, rather than through vendor self-disclosure.
scopeIncludes: Credential stuffing success rate spike traced to credentials known to have been shared only with a specific vendor
Fraud pattern analysis identifying a common vendor as the likely source of compromised data
Targeted phishing referencing details that could only have come from a specific vendor relationship
scopeExcludes: Breach the vendor has already formally disclosed (Vendor Holding Customer Data Suffers Own Breach leaf)
Confirmed vendor employee insider misuse (Vendor Employee Insider Breach leaf)
ITID-51613.severity: High; by the time downstream fraud is observed, exposure may have existed undetected for an extended period.
ITID-51613.priority: P1 upon establishing a credible correlation between fraud patterns and a specific vendor relationship.
ITID-51613.escalation: Escalate to legal, fraud/risk management, and vendor/procurement management immediately; formally request the vendor investigate and disclose findings.
indicators: Statistically significant fraud/credential-stuffing correlation with a customer cohort unique to one vendor
Common point of compromise analysis pointing to a specific vendor integration
Customer reports of fraud referencing data elements known only to a specific vendor
vectors: Unconfirmed at the organization level; underlying vendor compromise vector typically only becomes clear once the vendor investigates
Credential or data reuse by fraudsters following an undisclosed vendor breach
rootCauses: Vendor breach that went undetected or undisclosed by the vendor
Lack of proactive fraud-pattern-to-vendor correlation analysis by the organization
Insufficient contractual obligation on the vendor to proactively monitor and disclose
controls: Fraud pattern correlation analysis against vendor relationships
Contractual requirement for proactive vendor breach monitoring and disclosure
Credential rotation/monitoring for accounts shared with vendors
ITID-51613.detection: Requires dedicated fraud analytics capability to correlate patterns back to a specific vendor; this is inherently a lagging-indicator detection path rather than a real-time one.
ITID-51613.response: Formally engage the vendor to investigate based on the correlation evidence, rotate any shared credentials/keys, and monitor for continued fraud impact.
metrics: Number of vendor breaches first identified via downstream fraud correlation per period
Time from fraud pattern detection to vendor confirmation
Estimated undisclosed exposure window
ITID-51613.notes: This leaf's key differentiator is the discovery path (indirect, fraud-driven) rather than the underlying vendor compromise mechanism, which may ultimately resemble either of the sibling leaves once confirmed.

playbook.name: Vendor Breach Discovered via Downstream Fraud/Credential Reuse Response
playbook.description: A vendor breach is first discovered not through vendor disclosure but through downstream fraud or credential-reuse attacks against the company's own customers/systems.

steps.title: Correlate downstream fraud/credential-reuse pattern to a vendor as the likely source
steps.desc: Analyze the pattern of downstream fraud (e.g., credential-stuffing success rate spikes, account-takeover attempts) to identify a shared vendor as the likely common source of exposed credentials/data.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference affected customer/employee accounts against vendor customer lists or data-sharing scope to identify the common vendor.
steps.outcome: Vendor identified as the likely source with supporting correlation evidence.
steps.abort: If no vendor correlation can be established, treat as a standalone credential-stuffing/fraud incident under the appropriate playbook.

steps.title: Contact the suspected vendor to confirm or investigate a breach
steps.desc: Since the vendor has not proactively disclosed a breach, proactively contact the vendor with the correlation evidence and demand investigation and confirmation.
steps.guidance: Be prepared for vendor pushback or denial; document the request and any response (or non-response) formally.
steps.outcome: Vendor has confirmed or is actively investigating a potential breach based on the company's evidence.
steps.abort: If the vendor denies any breach and no further evidence can be obtained, document the inconclusive finding and continue monitoring downstream fraud independently.

steps.title: Force credential resets for affected customer/employee accounts
steps.desc: Force password resets and enforce MFA for all accounts showing downstream fraud indicators tied to the suspected vendor exposure.
steps.outcome: Affected accounts secured against further credential-reuse attacks.

steps.title: Rotate credentials/tokens shared with the vendor as a precaution
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials, API keys, or tokens shared with the vendor even before full confirmation, as a precautionary containment measure.
steps.outcome: Shared credentials rotated as a precaution.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance and vendor-relationship manager on findings and obligations
steps.desc: Engage Legal, Compliance, and the vendor relationship manager to formally document the correlation findings, pursue confirmation from the vendor, and assess notification obligations given the downstream fraud already observed.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance and vendor management actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Implement enhanced fraud/credential-reuse monitoring
steps.desc: Deploy or tune fraud-detection and credential-stuffing protection controls to reduce the impact of similar downstream exploitation in the future.
steps.guidance: Consider deploying breach-credential-checking services (e.g., checking against known compromised-password lists) for affected accounts.
steps.outcome: Enhanced monitoring/controls deployed and verified.

steps.title: Notify affected customers/employees and reduce vendor data-sharing scope pending confirmation
steps.desc: Complete notifications to affected individuals as warranted and consider limiting the scope of data shared with the suspected vendor pending full confirmation and remediation.
steps.outcome: Notifications completed; data-sharing scope adjusted as a precaution.

steps.title: Review proactive vendor-breach detection capability
steps.desc: Document the incident and the fact it was discovered via downstream indicators rather than vendor disclosure; recommend improved fraud-analytics correlation capability to catch such patterns earlier.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved detection-capability improvements.

ITID-51614.def: An intake classification for incidents involving a vendor-originated data breach where the mechanism or discovery path (vendor's own breach, vendor insider misuse, or downstream fraud correlation) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51614.purpose: Captures a confirmed vendor data breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Vendor Data Breach.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed vendor data breach of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
scopeExcludes: Confirmed vendor-side external breach (Vendor Holding Customer Data Suffers Own Breach leaf)
Confirmed vendor insider misuse (Vendor Employee Insider Breach leaf)
Confirmed downstream-fraud-discovered breach (Vendor Breach Discovered via Downstream Fraud leaf)
ITID-51614.severity: High by default, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51614.priority: P1 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51614.escalation: Escalate to legal and vendor/procurement management immediately; do not wait for reclassification before requesting vendor cooperation.
indicators: Vendor breach report with insufficient detail to determine mechanism
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard vendor breach intake and triage process
ITID-51614.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51614.response: Rapidly triage with vendor cooperation to determine the mechanism and reclassify.
metrics: Number of unclassified vendor data breach incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51614.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Vendor Data Breach leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Data Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed vendor data breach not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported vendor data breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected vendor breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (vendor's own breach, vendor insider, downstream-discovered breach) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review available vendor communications and internal correlation data to classify the incident.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected data and internal dependencies
steps.desc: Determine which company data and internal processes are affected by the vendor breach.
steps.guidance: Consult vendor management/data-flow documentation.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected data and dependencies.

steps.title: Rotate shared credentials and restrict vendor access
steps.desc: Rotate credentials/API keys shared with the vendor and restrict access pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Shared credentials rotated; access restricted.

steps.title: Engage vendor-relationship manager and Legal/Compliance
steps.desc: Engage the vendor relationship manager for contractual review and Legal/Compliance for notification obligation assessment.
steps.outcome: Vendor management and Legal/Compliance actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Verify vendor remediation once root cause confirmed
steps.desc: Obtain evidence of vendor remediation before resuming normal data flows.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If remediation cannot be confirmed, escalate to leadership regarding the vendor relationship.

steps.title: Verify vendor has remediated the confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Obtain and review evidence from the vendor confirming remediation of the root cause before resuming normal data flows.
steps.guidance: Request a remediation attestation or audit report from the vendor.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot demonstrate remediation, escalate to leadership regarding the vendor relationship.

steps.title: Resume vendor operations and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Resume normal vendor data sharing under verified remediation and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update vendor risk management
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend improvements to vendor risk assessment and monitoring.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51621.def: An incident in which a shared API integration between the organization and a partner is exploited or misconfigured in a way that exposes data flowing through or accessible via that integration, affecting both parties.
ITID-51621.purpose: Captures breaches at a shared API integration point that expose data belonging to both the organization and its integration partner.
scopeIncludes: API vulnerability (broken object-level authorization, injection) exploited to access data belonging to either party via the shared integration
Misconfigured API access scope exposing more data than the integration requires
Rate-limiting/authentication failure allowing bulk data extraction via the API
scopeExcludes: Breach via a compromised OAuth/service account rather than an API design/implementation flaw (Partner's Compromised OAuth/Service Account leaf)
Vendor's own independent breach unrelated to the shared integration (Vendor Data Breach leaves)
ITID-51621.severity: High; because the integration is bidirectional, a single flaw can expose data belonging to both organizations simultaneously.
ITID-51621.priority: P1 upon confirmation of exploitable API access to shared data.
ITID-51621.escalation: Escalate to application security, legal, and the partner organization jointly and immediately; coordinate a synchronized fix and disclosure timeline.
indicators: API access logs showing requests outside the integration's expected data scope or object ID range
Partner reporting an anomaly on their side of the same integration
Unusual volume of API calls from a single integration credential
vectors: Broken object-level authorization (BOLA) allowing access to another tenant's/partner's records via the API
Overly broad API scope granted during integration setup
Lack of rate limiting enabling bulk enumeration
rootCauses: Insufficient authorization checks at the API object level
API scope not reviewed/minimized after initial integration setup
Lack of joint security testing of the shared integration prior to launch
controls: Object-level authorization enforcement on all API endpoints
Periodic API scope review for active partner integrations
Joint security testing prior to and periodically after integration launch
ITID-51621.detection: Moderate; requires API-level logging and anomaly detection that many organizations under-invest in relative to conventional network/endpoint monitoring.
ITID-51621.response: Disable or restrict the affected API endpoint immediately, coordinate scope assessment jointly with the partner, and remediate the underlying flaw before restoring the integration.
metrics: Number of shared API integration breaches per period
Time from discovery to joint remediation
Active integrations under periodic security testing
ITID-51621.notes: Differentiated from the OAuth/service account leaf by root cause: this is a design/implementation flaw in the integration itself, not a credential compromise.

playbook.name: Shared API Integration Breach Exposing Both Organizations' Data Response
playbook.description: A shared API integration between the company and a partner organization is breached, exposing data belonging to both parties.

steps.title: Confirm the API integration breach and mutual data exposure
steps.desc: Validate evidence (API gateway alerts, anomalous request patterns, or partner notification) that the shared API integration was breached and confirm data belonging to both organizations was exposed.
steps.guidance: Review API gateway logs for anomalous authentication, unusual request volumes, or payload sizes on the shared integration endpoint.
steps.outcome: Confirmed breach with data exposure scope for both organizations documented.
steps.abort: If evidence does not confirm actual exposure, close as false positive with documented rationale.

steps.title: Jointly determine the exploited vulnerability with the partner
steps.desc: Coordinate with the partner organization's security team to jointly investigate whether the vulnerability originated on the company's side, the partner's side, or in the shared integration layer itself.
steps.guidance: Establish a joint incident channel/bridge call with the partner's security team as early as possible.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability source jointly confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Disable the compromised API integration immediately
steps.desc: Immediately disable or restrict the shared API integration endpoint to stop further data exposure, coordinating timing with the partner to manage business impact.
steps.outcome: No further data flowing through the compromised integration.

steps.title: Rotate API keys/OAuth tokens shared between organizations
steps.desc: Rotate all API keys, OAuth tokens, and shared secrets used for the integration on both sides.
steps.guidance: Coordinate rotation timing with the partner to avoid a mismatch that breaks the integration further.
steps.outcome: All shared credentials rotated on both sides.

steps.title: Establish joint incident coordination and notification plan with the partner
steps.desc: Formally establish joint incident coordination with the partner organization covering investigation responsibilities, communication cadence, and a joint or independently coordinated customer/regulator notification plan.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal on both sides to align on notification obligations and avoid conflicting public statements.
steps.outcome: Joint coordination plan documented and active with both organizations.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed vulnerability in the integration layer
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability (authentication flaw, missing rate limiting, overly broad scope) identified as the root cause, whether on the company's side or coordinated with the partner's side.
steps.guidance: Consider adding mutual TLS, stricter scope limitations, and rate limiting to the integration as part of remediation.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated and verified by both parties before reconnection.

steps.title: Restore the integration under hardened controls and notify affected parties
steps.desc: Restore the API integration under the hardened, jointly verified configuration and complete any required notifications to affected customers.
steps.outcome: Integration restored with no recurrence; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review joint API security governance with partner organizations
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish joint security review requirements (periodic security assessments, shared incident response protocols) for all shared API integrations with partners.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved joint governance improvements.

ITID-51622.def: An incident in which a partner organization's OAuth token, API key, or service account used to access a shared integration is compromised, and the resulting unauthorized access exposes shared data.
ITID-51622.purpose: Captures breaches of shared data caused by compromise of a partner's OAuth token or service account, distinct from a flaw in the integration's design.
scopeIncludes: Partner's OAuth token or API key stolen and used by an attacker to access shared data
Partner's service account credentials compromised via phishing or credential stuffing, then used against the shared integration
Leaked/exposed API key (e.g., committed to a public repository) enabling unauthorized access
scopeExcludes: Breach caused by a flaw in the API integration's own design/authorization logic (Shared API Integration Breach leaf)
Compromise of the partner's broader environment unrelated to the shared integration credential (Vendor Data Breach leaves)
ITID-51622.severity: High; a compromised integration credential often grants the same scope of access as the legitimate partner, making the breach difficult to distinguish from normal integration traffic.
ITID-51622.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a partner integration credential has been compromised and used maliciously.
ITID-51622.escalation: Escalate to application security, legal, and the partner organization jointly and immediately; revoke and rotate the compromised credential without delay.
indicators: API/integration traffic from the partner's credential originating from an unexpected IP range or geography
Partner reporting a phishing or credential compromise incident affecting their integration account
Anomalous data access volume/pattern via the partner's credential inconsistent with normal integration behavior
vectors: Phishing targeting partner staff with access to integration credentials
Credential/API key leaked via a public code repository or misconfigured secrets store
Credential stuffing against the partner's service account
rootCauses: Lack of credential rotation policy for long-lived integration tokens
Insufficient secrets management practices at the partner organization
No behavioral baseline/anomaly detection on integration credential usage
controls: Short-lived, regularly rotated OAuth tokens/API keys for integrations
Behavioral anomaly detection on integration credential usage
Secrets scanning to detect leaked integration credentials
ITID-51622.detection: Moderate; effective detection requires baselining normal integration traffic patterns to distinguish compromised-credential usage from legitimate partner activity.
ITID-51622.response: Revoke and rotate the compromised credential immediately, review access logs for the scope of unauthorized activity, and coordinate with the partner on root cause and joint disclosure.
metrics: Number of compromised partner credential incidents per period
Average token/credential rotation interval for active integrations
Time from compromise to credential revocation
detections: Secrets scanning for leaked API keys/tokens
ITID-51622.notes: Differentiated from the API design-flaw leaf by root cause: here the integration itself is sound, but the credential authenticating to it has been stolen or leaked.

playbook.name: Partner's Compromised OAuth/Service Account Exposing Shared Data Response
playbook.description: A partner organization's OAuth token or service account used for data sharing is compromised, exposing shared data.

steps.title: Confirm the compromised OAuth token/service account and its origin
steps.desc: Validate evidence or partner notification confirming that the partner's OAuth token or service account used for the data-sharing integration was compromised.
steps.guidance: Review OAuth/API access logs for anomalous usage patterns from the partner's credential (unusual times, IPs, or data volumes).
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise with usage anomalies documented.
steps.abort: If evidence does not confirm actual misuse, close as false positive with documented rationale.

steps.title: Determine the scope of shared data accessed via the compromised credential
steps.desc: Determine exactly what data the compromised OAuth token/service account had access to and what was actually retrieved during the compromise window.
steps.guidance: Review the token's granted scopes and correlate with actual API call logs during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of data actually accessed.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised OAuth token/service account immediately
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the compromised token/service account's access as the top-priority containment action.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the partner to confirm revocation and prevent automatic token refresh from restoring access.
steps.outcome: Compromised credential fully revoked; no further unauthorized access possible.

steps.title: Rotate all related API keys and secrets for the integration
steps.desc: Rotate any additional API keys, client secrets, or related credentials tied to the integration as a precaution, on both sides.
steps.outcome: All related credentials rotated.

steps.title: Coordinate joint incident response with the partner organization
steps.desc: Establish joint incident coordination with the partner to determine how their credential was compromised and align on notification obligations to affected customers.
steps.outcome: Joint coordination plan documented and active.

steps.title: Verify the partner has remediated their credential-compromise root cause
steps.desc: Obtain evidence from the partner that the root cause of their credential compromise (phishing, weak secret storage, exposed CI/CD pipeline) has been remediated before re-issuing access.
steps.outcome: Partner remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If the partner cannot demonstrate remediation, escalate to leadership to consider suspending the integration pending further assurance.

steps.title: Re-establish the integration with new credentials and notify affected customers
steps.desc: Issue new OAuth credentials/service account access under verified remediation and complete required notifications to affected customers.
steps.outcome: Integration restored with no recurrence; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review credential lifecycle management for partner integrations
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish improved credential rotation cadence, scope limitation, and monitoring requirements for partner-held OAuth tokens/service accounts.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved credential lifecycle management improvements.

ITID-51623.def: An intake classification for incidents involving a breach of shared data through a partner integration where the mechanism (API design flaw or compromised credential) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51623.purpose: Captures a confirmed partner integration breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Partner Integration Breach.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed partner integration breach of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
scopeExcludes: Confirmed API design/authorization flaw (Shared API Integration Breach leaf)
Confirmed compromised OAuth/service account (Partner's Compromised OAuth/Service Account leaf)
ITID-51623.severity: High by default, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51623.priority: P1 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51623.escalation: Escalate to application security, legal, and the partner organization jointly; disable the integration as a precaution while triage proceeds if risk warrants it.
indicators: Partner integration anomaly report with insufficient detail to determine root cause
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard partner integration breach intake and triage process
ITID-51623.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51623.response: Rapidly triage jointly with the partner to determine the mechanism and reclassify.
metrics: Number of unclassified partner integration breach incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51623.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Partner Integration Breach leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Partner Integration Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed partner integration breach not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported partner integration breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (shared API breach, compromised partner OAuth/service account) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review API/integration logs and any partner communications to classify the incident.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected data and integration touchpoints
steps.desc: Determine which data and integration touchpoints with the partner are affected.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected data and touchpoints.

steps.title: Rotate shared credentials/tokens and restrict the integration
steps.desc: Rotate API keys/OAuth tokens shared with the partner and restrict or disable the integration pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Shared credentials rotated; integration access restricted.

steps.title: Coordinate joint incident response with the partner and Legal
steps.desc: Establish joint coordination with the partner organization and engage Legal/Compliance for notification obligation assessment.
steps.outcome: Joint coordination and Legal/Compliance tracking active.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or credential issue responsible for the breach once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify partner has remediated the confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Obtain and review evidence from the partner organization confirming remediation of the root cause before restoring the integration.
steps.outcome: Partner remediation verified and documented.
steps.abort: If the partner cannot demonstrate remediation, escalate to leadership regarding the integration.

steps.title: Restore the integration and notify affected customers
steps.desc: Restore the partner integration under corrected controls and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Integration restored; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update partner integration governance
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements for partner integrations.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51631.def: An incident in which a software dependency or package (e.g., a public package registry component) used by the organization's software is compromised, maliciously modified, or typosquatted, and results in exposure of organizational or customer data.
ITID-51631.purpose: Captures data breaches resulting from a compromised open-source or third-party software dependency/package pulled into the organization's software supply chain.
scopeIncludes: Malicious code injected into a legitimate open-source package the organization depends on
Typosquatted package mimicking a legitimate dependency, installed inadvertently
Compromised maintainer account used to publish a malicious package version
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the organization's own software build/release pipeline (Compromised Software Update Mechanism leaf)
A library deliberately backdoored by its original author/maintainer over time as opposed to a single compromise event (Backdoored Third-Party Library leaf)
ITID-51631.severity: High; a compromised dependency can affect every system and every customer of the software built with it.
ITID-51631.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a compromised dependency was present in a data-handling code path.
ITID-51631.escalation: Escalate to application security, engineering leadership, and legal immediately; determine the blast radius across all systems using the affected dependency version.
indicators: Software composition analysis (SCA) tooling flagging a known-malicious package version
Unexpected outbound network activity originating from a build or runtime environment traced to a specific dependency
Public security advisory naming a package the organization depends on
vectors: Malicious code published in a new version of a legitimate, widely used package
Typosquatting a popular package name to trick developers into installing it
Compromised maintainer credentials used to publish a malicious update
rootCauses: Lack of software composition analysis / dependency vulnerability scanning
No pinning or verification of dependency versions/checksums
Insufficient review process for adding new third-party dependencies
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Software composition analysis (SCA) scanning all dependencies
Dependency version pinning with checksum/signature verification
Review process for new third-party dependency additions
ITID-51631.detection: Moderate to good where SCA tooling and outbound network monitoring from build/runtime environments are in place; detection often lags public disclosure of the compromised package.
ITID-51631.response: Remove or pin back the compromised dependency immediately across all affected systems, assess what data may have been exposed, and rebuild/redeploy affected software.
metrics: Number of compromised dependency incidents per period
Time from public disclosure to internal remediation
Percentage of dependencies under active SCA scanning
sops: Software Supply Chain Compromise Response SOP
ITID-51631.notes: T1195.002 per the Supply Chain Data Breach MITRE mapping guidance.

playbook.name: Data Breach via Compromised Software Dependency/Package Response
playbook.description: A malicious or compromised open-source/commercial software dependency introduces a backdoor or exfiltration mechanism, resulting in a data breach.

steps.title: Confirm the compromised dependency and its exfiltration mechanism
steps.desc: Validate the identity of the compromised software dependency/package (via vendor advisory, security researcher disclosure, or internal detection) and confirm the specific exfiltration or backdoor mechanism it introduced.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the affected package name/version against your software bill of materials (SBOM) and dependency inventory.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromised dependency with mechanism of data exfiltration documented.
steps.abort: If the flagged dependency is not present in the environment, close as not applicable.

steps.title: Identify all systems/applications using the compromised dependency
steps.desc: Use the software bill of materials (SBOM) and dependency scanning to identify every application/service in the environment that includes the compromised package, directly or transitively.
steps.guidance: Check transitive dependencies as well as direct ones — many supply chain compromises propagate through nested dependencies.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of affected systems/applications.

steps.title: Determine what data was actually exfiltrated
steps.desc: Analyze logs and network traffic from affected systems to determine what data, if any, was actually exfiltrated via the compromised dependency's mechanism.
steps.guidance: Review outbound network connections matching known indicators of compromise (IOCs) published for the compromised package.
steps.outcome: Documented determination of actual data exfiltration scope.

steps.title: Remove or pin the compromised dependency across all affected systems
steps.desc: Immediately remove or downgrade to a known-safe pinned version of the compromised dependency across all identified affected systems.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with development teams to deploy emergency patches/rebuilds using the SBOM-derived list of affected systems.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed no longer using the compromised dependency version.

steps.title: Block known malicious indicators at the network layer
steps.desc: Block any known-malicious C2 domains/IPs associated with the compromised dependency's exfiltration mechanism at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: Malicious indicators blocked; no further exfiltration observed.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed data exfiltration scope to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking notification obligations as applicable.

steps.title: Perform SBOM-wide review and implement dependency-pinning/verification hardening
steps.desc: Conduct a comprehensive SBOM review across the organization to identify any other unverified or unpinned dependencies with similar risk, and implement dependency pinning, checksum/signature verification, and a vetting process for future dependency updates.
steps.guidance: Consider adopting a private package registry with vetted/mirrored packages and requiring cryptographic signature verification for all dependency updates.
steps.outcome: Dependency-pinning and verification controls implemented and verified across affected build pipelines.
steps.tool: SBOM management platform / private package registry

steps.title: Redeploy affected systems with verified-clean dependencies and notify as required
steps.desc: Redeploy all affected applications with the verified-clean dependency versions and complete any required notifications to affected customers.
steps.outcome: All affected systems redeployed and verified clean; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review software supply chain security program maturity
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive maturity improvements in SBOM coverage, dependency vetting, and supply-chain threat monitoring across the SDLC.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved supply-chain security program improvements.

ITID-51632.def: An incident in which the mechanism used to build, sign, or distribute software updates (CI/CD pipeline, build server, or update distribution channel) is compromised, resulting in malicious code being delivered to production systems and exposing data.
ITID-51632.purpose: Captures data breaches resulting from compromise of an organization's or vendor's software update/distribution mechanism, distinct from a compromised dependency pulled in during development.
scopeIncludes: Compromised CI/CD pipeline injecting malicious code into a build before release
Compromised code-signing infrastructure used to sign a malicious update as legitimate
Compromised update distribution server pushing a malicious update to endpoints
scopeExcludes: Compromise of a third-party open-source dependency the organization consumes (Compromised Software Dependency/Package leaf)

A vendor's software the organization uses being backdoored by the vendor's own compromise upstream (Backdoored Third-Party Library leaf, if the compromise is in a consumed library rather than the organization's own build pipeline)
ITID-51632.severity: High; a compromised build/update mechanism can affect every deployment of the affected software, often with a trusted, signed appearance that evades typical detection.
ITID-51632.priority: P1 upon confirmation that the build or update pipeline was compromised.
ITID-51632.escalation: Escalate to engineering leadership, application security, and legal immediately; halt further deployments/updates until the pipeline is confirmed clean.
indicators: Build artifact hash mismatch against expected/known-good values
Unauthorized modification to CI/CD pipeline configuration or build scripts
Code-signing certificate used in a manner inconsistent with normal release cadence
vectors: Compromised CI/CD credentials or build server access
Malicious commit/merge into the build pipeline configuration
Compromised code-signing key or certificate authority trust
rootCauses: Insufficient access control and monitoring on CI/CD infrastructure
Lack of build artifact integrity verification (reproducible builds, hash validation)
Code-signing keys not adequately protected (e.g., hardware security module)
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: CI/CD pipeline access control and change monitoring
Build artifact integrity verification (reproducible builds, signed hashes)
Hardware-protected code-signing key management
ITID-51632.detection: Requires dedicated build/release pipeline integrity monitoring, which many organizations under-invest in relative to production system monitoring.
ITID-51632.response: Halt deployments immediately, rebuild the pipeline from a known-good state, revoke and reissue signing keys if compromised, and assess the scope of affected deployments.
metrics: Number of build/update pipeline compromise incidents per period
Deployments affected before detection
Time from compromise to pipeline remediation
sops: Software Supply Chain Compromise Response SOP
ITID-51632.notes: Differentiated from the dependency-compromise leaf by location: this leaf covers compromise of the organization's/vendor's own build and distribution mechanism, not an upstream open-source package.

playbook.name: Data Breach via Compromised Software Update Mechanism Response
playbook.description: An attacker compromises a legitimate software update mechanism (build server, code-signing process, or update distribution channel) to push a malicious update that exfiltrates data.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of the update mechanism and malicious update delivery
steps.desc: Validate evidence (vendor advisory, anomalous build artifact, unexpected code-signing certificate use) confirming the software update mechanism was compromised and a malicious update was distributed.
steps.guidance: Review build server logs, code-signing audit logs, and update distribution logs for anomalies.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise with the malicious update version/artifact identified.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify all systems that received the malicious update
steps.desc: Determine which internal or customer-facing systems installed the malicious update via the compromised distribution channel.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference update deployment logs/telemetry against the identified malicious version.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of systems that received the malicious update.

steps.title: Determine what data was exfiltrated via the malicious update
steps.desc: Analyze the malicious update's behavior and affected system logs/network traffic to determine what data was accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Perform reverse engineering/malware analysis on the malicious update artifact if feasible.
steps.outcome: Documented data exfiltration scope.
steps.tool: Malware analysis sandbox / network traffic analysis

steps.title: Halt distribution of the malicious update and revoke compromised signing certificates
steps.desc: Immediately halt further distribution of the malicious update and revoke any compromised code-signing certificates used to sign it.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the CA/certificate provider on certificate revocation and reissuance.
steps.outcome: Malicious update distribution stopped; compromised certificates revoked.

steps.title: Push an emergency rollback/clean update to affected systems
steps.desc: Distribute an emergency, verified-clean update or rollback to all systems that received the malicious version.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed rolled back or updated to a clean version.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for breach-notification and customer communication
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed data exfiltration scope to assess breach-notification obligations, including obligations to affected customers if the update mechanism serves external customers.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking notification obligations.

steps.title: Harden the build/signing/distribution pipeline
steps.desc: Implement hardened controls for the build server, code-signing process, and update distribution channel (isolated build environments, hardware security module-backed signing keys, mandatory code review, artifact integrity verification).
steps.guidance: Conduct a full forensic rebuild of the build/signing infrastructure rather than trusting incremental cleanup.
steps.outcome: Hardened pipeline verified secure via independent review before resuming normal update releases.

steps.title: Resume normal update releases and notify affected customers
steps.desc: Resume normal software update releases under the hardened pipeline and complete required notifications to affected customers.
steps.outcome: Update releases resumed with no recurrence; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review software supply chain build/signing security program
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive comprehensive improvements to build pipeline security, code-signing key protection, and update integrity verification for customers.
steps.guidance: Consider implementing update signature verification and transparency logs (e.g., Sigstore-style) that customers can independently verify.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved build/signing security program improvements.

ITID-51633.def: An incident in which a third-party software library or component in active use contains a deliberately embedded backdoor, allowing an adversary sustained, ongoing unauthorized access or data exfiltration capability over time.
ITID-51633.purpose: Captures data breaches resulting from a third-party library that has been deliberately and persistently backdoored, distinct from a one-time dependency or build-pipeline compromise event.
scopeIncludes: Library found to contain a long-standing, deliberately obfuscated backdoor rather than a single tainted release
Backdoor discovered in a widely deployed commercial or open-source component after extended use
Data exfiltration capability built into a library by a malicious contributor or nation-state-linked developer
scopeExcludes: A single compromised package version/release event (Compromised Software Dependency/Package leaf)
Compromise of the organization's own build/update pipeline (Compromised Software Update Mechanism leaf)
ITID-51633.severity: High; backdoored libraries can provide sustained, undetected access over long periods before discovery, compounding total data exposure.
ITID-51633.priority: P1 upon confirmation of an active backdoor in a deployed library, given the likely extended dwell time.
ITID-51633.escalation: Escalate to application security, engineering leadership, and legal immediately; conduct a full historical review of data access/exfiltration during the library's entire deployment period.
indicators: Security research disclosure or CVE describing a deliberate backdoor in a specific library version range
Reverse engineering/code audit uncovering obfuscated command-and-control or exfiltration logic
Long-running unexplained outbound network activity traced to the library's runtime behavior
vectors: Malicious code deliberately embedded by a compromised or malicious original maintainer/contributor
Long-dormant backdoor activated remotely by the adversary at a chosen time
Obfuscated exfiltration logic disguised as legitimate telemetry/analytics functionality
rootCauses: Lack of code-level security review for third-party libraries prior to and during use
Insufficient monitoring for anomalous long-running network behavior from library-dependent components
Overreliance on a library's reputation without ongoing security auditing
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Ongoing security auditing of critical third-party libraries
Behavioral network monitoring for anomalous long-running outbound activity
Software bill of materials (SBOM) tracking to identify affected deployments quickly upon disclosure
ITID-51633.detection: Weak by nature of the attack (deliberately obfuscated and long-dwelling); discovery is typically driven by external security research rather than internal detection.
ITID-51633.response: Remove or patch the backdoored library across all deployments immediately upon disclosure, conduct a full historical data exposure review, and rotate any credentials/secrets the library may have had access to.
metrics: Number of backdoored library incidents per period
Estimated dwell time before discovery
Percentage of software inventory covered by an accurate SBOM
sops: Software Supply Chain Compromise Response SOP
detections: SBOM-driven rapid impact assessment upon disclosure
ITID-51633.notes: Differentiated from the other two Software Supply Chain Attack leaves by persistence and intent: this is a long-lived, deliberately embedded backdoor rather than a discrete compromise event.

playbook.name: Data Breach via Backdoored Third-Party Library Response
playbook.description: A third-party software library used by the company is discovered to contain an intentionally embedded backdoor, resulting in data exposure.

steps.title: Confirm the backdoored library and its malicious functionality
steps.desc: Validate the identity of the backdoored library (via security researcher disclosure, vendor advisory, or internal reverse engineering) and confirm the specific malicious functionality it contains.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the affected library name/version against your software bill of materials (SBOM) and dependency inventory; review published analysis of the backdoor's behavior.
steps.outcome: Confirmed backdoored library with malicious functionality documented.
steps.abort: If the flagged library is not present in the environment, close as not applicable.

steps.title: Identify all systems using the backdoored library and assess exploitation history
steps.desc: Use the SBOM to identify all systems/applications including the backdoored library, and analyze logs/network traffic to determine whether the backdoor was actually exploited and what data was accessed.
steps.guidance: Since a backdoor may lie dormant, absence of current activity does not rule out prior exploitation — review historical logs as far back as the library's introduction date.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of affected systems and a documented exploitation history assessment.

steps.title: Remove the backdoored library from all affected systems
steps.desc: Immediately remove or replace the backdoored library with a verified-clean version or alternative across all identified affected systems.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with development teams for emergency patches/rebuilds using the SBOM-derived list of affected systems.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed no longer using the backdoored library.

steps.title: Block known backdoor command-and-control indicators
steps.desc: Block any known-malicious C2 domains/IPs associated with the backdoor's communication mechanism at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: Malicious indicators blocked; no further backdoor communication observed.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed exploitation history and data exposure scope to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking notification obligations as applicable.

steps.title: Conduct SBOM-wide review and implement dependency verification hardening
steps.desc: Conduct an organization-wide SBOM review to identify any other libraries from the same maintainer/source with similar risk, and implement checksum/signature verification and a maintainer-vetting process for future library adoption.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring reproducible builds or third-party security audits for critical dependencies going forward.
steps.outcome: Dependency verification controls implemented and verified.

steps.title: Redeploy affected systems with verified-clean libraries and notify as required
steps.desc: Redeploy all affected applications with the verified-clean library versions and complete any required notifications to affected customers.
steps.outcome: All affected systems redeployed and verified clean; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Review third-party library vetting and supply chain risk program
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive maturity improvements in third-party library vetting, SBOM coverage, and ongoing supply-chain threat monitoring.
steps.outcome: After-action report with approved supply-chain security program improvements.

ITID-51634.def: An intake classification for incidents involving data exposure via a software supply chain compromise where the mechanism (compromised dependency, compromised build/update pipeline, or backdoored library) has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51634.purpose: Captures a confirmed software supply chain data breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Software Supply Chain Attack.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed software supply chain-related data breach of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
scopeExcludes: Confirmed compromised dependency/package (Compromised Software Dependency/Package leaf)
Confirmed compromised build/update mechanism (Compromised Software Update Mechanism leaf)
Confirmed backdoored library (Backdoored Third-Party Library leaf)
ITID-51634.severity: High by default given the typically broad blast radius of software supply chain compromises, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51634.priority: P1 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-51634.escalation: Escalate to application security and engineering leadership immediately; begin blast-radius assessment before reclassification is complete.
indicators: Software supply chain compromise report with insufficient detail to determine mechanism
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Standard software supply chain breach intake and triage process
ITID-51634.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51634.response: Rapidly triage to determine the mechanism and reclassify; begin blast-radius assessment in parallel regardless of classification status.
metrics: Number of unclassified software supply chain breach incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
sops: Software Supply Chain Compromise Response SOP
ITID-51634.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Software Supply Chain Attack leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Software Supply Chain Data Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed software supply chain data breach not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported software supply chain data breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (compromised dependency, compromised update mechanism, backdoored library) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review the SBOM, build logs, and available threat intelligence to classify the incident.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope affected systems and data using the SBOM
steps.desc: Use the software bill of materials to identify all systems potentially affected and assess what data those systems process.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected systems and data.

steps.title: Isolate or patch affected systems pending investigation
steps.desc: Apply protective isolation or emergency patching to affected systems as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance for notification assessment
steps.desc: Provide Legal/Compliance with confirmed scope to assess breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance actively tracking the matter.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause and review SBOM/dependency hardening
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability, dependency, or pipeline issue responsible for the breach once confirmed, and review SBOM/dependency-pinning practices for gaps.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Review SBOM coverage for related dependencies or pipeline gaps
steps.desc: Once the specific root cause is confirmed, review the software bill of materials (SBOM) and build pipeline for related gaps that could allow a similar compromise.
steps.outcome: SBOM/pipeline gap review completed with any findings remediated.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and notify affected individuals
steps.desc: Restore normal operations under corrected controls and complete required notifications.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed as required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update supply chain security controls
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements for software supply chain security.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51641.def: An incident in which a shipping, tracking, or delivery management system (whether the organization's own or a logistics partner's) is compromised or misconfigured, exposing customer delivery information such as addresses, delivery windows, and order contents.
ITID-51641.purpose: Captures breaches of shipping and tracking systems that expose customer delivery information, a logistics-specific PII exposure pathway.
scopeIncludes: Compromised shipping/tracking portal exposing customer delivery details in bulk
Misconfigured logistics API exposing tracking data beyond intended access scope
Logistics partner breach exposing shared delivery/customer address data
scopeExcludes: Inventory management system breach not involving customer delivery data (Inventory Management System Breach leaf)
General customer PII exposure unrelated to shipping/logistics systems (PII Exposure category leaves)
ITID-51641.severity: Medium-High; exposed delivery data (home addresses, delivery patterns, order contents) creates both privacy and physical safety risk for customers.
ITID-51641.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the exposure includes home addresses at scale or delivery-timing data usable for targeting (e.g., burglary risk).
ITID-51641.escalation: Escalate to legal/privacy and logistics/operations leadership; consider customer safety communications if delivery-timing/address data creates a physical risk.
indicators: Shipping/tracking portal access logs showing bulk or anomalous queries
External researcher or customer report of exposed tracking data
Logistics partner breach notification referencing shared delivery data
vectors: Predictable/sequential tracking number enumeration exposing other customers' shipment details
Compromised logistics portal credentials
Misconfigured API exposing tracking data without proper authorization checks
rootCauses: Lack of authorization checks preventing enumeration of tracking/shipment records
Insufficient access control on logistics/shipping systems
Third-party logistics integration lacking adequate data minimization
controls: Authorization checks preventing tracking number/shipment enumeration
Access control review on shipping/logistics systems
Data minimization in logistics partner integrations
ITID-51641.detection: Moderate; depends on whether logistics/shipping systems are included in the organization's standard access and anomaly monitoring, which is often treated as lower priority than core customer systems.
ITID-51641.response: Restrict the exposed access point immediately, determine scope of customer delivery data exposed, and assess physical safety and privacy notification obligations.
metrics: Number of shipping/tracking data breach incidents per period
Customer records exposed per incident
Time from exposure to detection
ITID-51641.notes: Differentiated from Inventory Management System Breach by data type: this leaf concerns customer-facing delivery/PII data rather than internal stock/inventory records.

playbook.name: Shipping/Tracking Data Breach Exposing Customer Delivery Information Response
playbook.description: A breach of shipping/logistics systems exposes customer delivery information such as addresses, tracking numbers, and delivery schedules.

steps.title: Confirm the shipping/tracking data exposure
steps.desc: Validate the alert or report confirming that customer delivery information (addresses, tracking numbers, delivery windows) was accessed or exfiltrated from shipping/logistics systems.
steps.guidance: Review logistics platform access logs and any DLP alerts for the affected system.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of exposed shipping/tracking records.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, close as false positive.

steps.title: Assess whether exposed data includes any additional PII beyond delivery details
steps.desc: Determine whether the exposed data set includes any additional customer PII (payment details, order contents) beyond basic shipping/tracking information, since this affects notification thresholds.
steps.outcome: Documented data sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected logistics system
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the affected shipping/logistics system as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Assess customer-notification need given lower sensitivity of delivery data
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to assess whether customer notification is warranted; while shipping/tracking data is generally lower-sensitivity than financial/health data, exposure of home addresses and delivery patterns can still carry safety and privacy implications warranting notification.
steps.guidance: Consider the specific risk of exposed delivery schedules (e.g., revealing when a customer's home will be unoccupied) as a factor in the notification decision.
steps.outcome: Documented notification decision with Legal/Compliance sign-off.
steps.abort: If Legal/Compliance determines notification is not warranted, document the risk-based rationale.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed root-cause vulnerability
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or access issue responsible for the exposure once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to shipping/tracking data remains
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access remains against the affected shipping/logistics system after the primary remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Restore normal logistics operations and notify customers if warranted
steps.desc: Restore normal shipping/logistics operations under corrected controls and complete customer notifications if Legal/Compliance determined they were warranted.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed if required.

steps.title: Review logistics data protection controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and recommend improvements to access controls and data minimization practices for shipping/logistics systems.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51642.def: An incident in which an inventory management system (stock levels, warehouse records, supplier order data) is breached or exposed, revealing internal operational and supply chain data rather than customer-identifying information.
ITID-51642.purpose: Captures breaches of internal inventory management systems, distinct from customer-facing shipping/tracking data by its operational (non-PII) content.
scopeIncludes: Compromised inventory management system exposing stock levels, SKUs, and warehouse locations
Exposed supplier order/purchasing data within the inventory system
Unauthorized access to inventory forecasting or supply chain planning data
scopeExcludes: Shipping/tracking data breaches involving customer delivery information (Shipping/Tracking Data Breach leaf)
General database dump incidents not specific to inventory/logistics systems (Database Dump leaves under Operational Data Breach)
ITID-51642.severity: Medium; primarily a competitive/operational risk (revealing supply chain strategy, supplier relationships, stock positions) rather than a direct customer privacy risk.
ITID-51642.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if exposed data reveals sensitive supplier contract terms or enables supply chain disruption targeting.
ITID-51642.escalation: Escalate to supply chain/operations leadership and legal if supplier contract or pricing data is exposed, given potential competitive and contractual implications.
indicators: Inventory system access logs showing anomalous bulk queries or exports
Inventory/supplier data found circulating externally or with a competitor
Unusual access to inventory system from an unrecognized account or location
vectors: Compromised credentials for the inventory management system
Misconfigured access controls on inventory/warehouse management software
Insider exfiltration of inventory/supplier data
rootCauses: Insufficient access control on inventory management systems
Lack of monitoring for anomalous bulk export activity
Inventory systems treated as lower-sensitivity and under-monitored relative to customer-facing systems
controls: Access control review on inventory management systems
Anomalous bulk export monitoring on inventory/supply chain systems
Classification of supplier/pricing data with appropriate handling controls
ITID-51642.detection: Moderate; inventory systems often receive less security monitoring investment than customer-facing systems, creating a coverage gap.
ITID-51642.response: Restrict access immediately, determine scope of exposed operational and supplier data, and assess competitive/contractual impact with supply chain leadership.
metrics: Number of inventory system breach incidents per period
Records/SKUs exposed per incident
Inventory systems under active access monitoring
ITID-51642.notes: Differentiated from the shipping/tracking leaf by data type: internal operational/supplier data here versus customer-identifying delivery data there.

playbook.name: Inventory Management System Breach Response
playbook.description: A breach of the inventory management system exposes stock levels, SKU data, supplier information, and potentially linked customer order data.

steps.title: Confirm the inventory management system breach
steps.desc: Validate the alert or report confirming unauthorized access to the inventory management system and identify what data (stock levels, SKU/pricing data, supplier details, linked order data) was accessed.
steps.guidance: Review inventory system access and application logs for anomalous activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed breach with data scope documented.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine whether customer PII or order data was linked and exposed
steps.desc: Assess whether the inventory system breach also exposed linked customer order records containing PII, since inventory data alone is typically low-sensitivity but often connects to order/customer tables.
steps.guidance: Review the data model/schema to determine what customer-linked data, if any, was within the accessed scope.
steps.outcome: Documented determination of whether customer PII was exposed alongside inventory data.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected inventory system
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the affected inventory management system as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Assess customer-notification need if linked PII was exposed
