steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to assess whether customer notification is warranted, particularly if linked order/PII data was confirmed exposed alongside the inventory data.
steps.outcome: Documented notification decision with Legal/Compliance sign-off.
steps.abort: If Legal/Compliance determines notification is not warranted because only non-PII inventory/supplier data was exposed, document the risk-based rationale.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed root-cause vulnerability
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or access issue responsible for the breach once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to the inventory system remains
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access remains against the affected inventory management system after the primary remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Restore normal inventory operations and notify customers if warranted
steps.desc: Restore normal inventory management operations under corrected controls and complete customer notifications if warranted.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed if required.

steps.title: Review data segmentation between inventory and customer PII systems
steps.desc: Document the incident and recommend improvements to data segmentation/access boundaries between inventory data and customer PII to limit future blast radius.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51643.def: An intake classification for incidents involving exposure of logistics, shipping, tracking, or inventory data where the specific system or data type has not yet been, or cannot be, determined.
ITID-51643.purpose: Captures a confirmed logistics or inventory data breach that does not cleanly match a more specific leaf under Logistics and Inventory Data Breach.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed logistics/inventory data breach of unclear or mixed origin pending triage
scopeExcludes: Confirmed shipping/tracking data breach (Shipping/Tracking Data Breach leaf)
Confirmed inventory management system breach (Inventory Management System Breach leaf)
ITID-51643.severity: Medium-High by default, pending reclassification and refined severity assessment.
ITID-51643.priority: P2 pending triage; reclassify to a specific leaf and reassess priority once the affected system/data type is confirmed.
ITID-51643.escalation: Escalate to supply chain/operations leadership and legal/privacy for an initial impact assessment while triage proceeds.
indicators: Report of exposed logistics/inventory data with insufficient detail to determine the specific system
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Unknown pending investigation
controls: Standard logistics/inventory breach intake and triage process
ITID-51643.detection: Varies entirely by eventual root cause; this leaf exists to hold incidents during the triage window.
ITID-51643.response: Rapidly triage to determine the affected system/data type and reclassify.
metrics: Number of unclassified logistics/inventory breach incidents pending reclassification
Time to reclassification
ITID-51643.notes: This is an intake/catch-all leaf; incidents should be reclassified into a specific Logistics and Inventory Data Breach leaf as soon as the affected system/data type is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Logistics and Inventory Data Breach Response
playbook.description: Suspected or confirmed logistics or inventory data breach not fitting a more specific sub-category, requiring triage.

steps.title: Triage the reported logistics/inventory data breach
steps.desc: Gather initial details of the suspected breach and determine whether it fits a known sub-category (shipping/tracking data, inventory management system) or is a general/mixed case.
steps.guidance: Review relevant system logs to classify the incident.
steps.outcome: Incident classified and re-routed to a specific playbook if applicable, or confirmed general case.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after reasonable investigation, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Determine data sensitivity and whether customer PII is involved
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the exposed data, specifically whether any customer PII (delivery addresses, order details) is included beyond low-sensitivity operational data.
steps.outcome: Documented sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected system
steps.desc: Apply protective access restrictions to the affected logistics/inventory system as the top-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure halted or significantly reduced.

steps.title: Assess customer-notification need with Legal/Compliance
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to assess whether customer notification is warranted based on the confirmed data sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Documented notification decision with Legal/Compliance sign-off.

steps.title: Remediate confirmed root cause
steps.desc: Fix the specific vulnerability or access issue responsible for the breach once confirmed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access to the affected system remains
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up review to confirm no residual unauthorized access remains against the affected logistics/inventory system after the primary remediation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized access exists.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and notify customers if warranted
steps.desc: Restore normal operations under corrected controls and complete customer notifications if warranted.
steps.outcome: Operations normalized; notifications completed if required.

steps.title: Document classification gaps and update logistics data protection controls
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend detection/control improvements for logistics and inventory systems.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed with recommendations.

ITID-51711.def: An insider with legitimate access deliberately exfiltrates company data with the intent to sell it to a competitor, broker, or on the dark web for personal financial gain.
ITID-51711.purpose: Classifies insider data theft motivated by direct financial gain through sale of data, distinguishing the profit motive from revenge or external coercion.
scopeIncludes: Employee/contractor exfiltration of customer, financial, or proprietary data for sale
Evidence of negotiation or transaction with a buyer (competitor, broker, dark web marketplace)
scopeExcludes: Data theft motivated by grievance/retaliation rather than profit (ITID-51712)
Insider acting under external recruitment/coercion rather than self-initiated profit motive (ITID-51713)
ITID-51711.severity: High. Motivated, deliberate insider action against data with a ready buyer typically means rapid onward disclosure.
ITID-51711.priority: P1 upon confirmation of intent to sell or evidence of a completed transaction.
ITID-51711.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, HR, and law enforcement given the criminal nature of data sale; preserve evidence for potential prosecution.
indicators: Unusual bulk data access/export by an employee outside normal job duties
Communications referencing sale, price negotiation, or a buyer for company data
Employee financial distress or sudden unexplained income
vectors: Bulk export to removable media or personal cloud storage ahead of resignation
Direct upload to a dark web marketplace or broker
rootCauses: Insufficient DLP monitoring of high-privilege user data access
Lack of departing-employee access review and offboarding controls
controls: DLP monitoring on bulk data export
User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) for anomalous access patterns
Departing-employee heightened monitoring and access revocation
ITID-51711.detection: DLP and UEBA provide strong technical detection surface for the exfiltration itself, though motive/buyer evidence typically requires HR/legal investigation.
ITID-51711.response: Immediately revoke access, preserve forensic evidence, and coordinate with legal and law enforcement on prosecution and data recovery.
metrics: Volume/sensitivity of data exfiltrated
Time from anomalous access to detection
ITID-51711.notes: Differentiated from sibling insider leaves by motive: financial gain via sale, evidenced by buyer/transaction activity, rather than grievance or coercion.

playbook.name: Insider Steals Data for Financial Gain (Sale to Competitor/Dark Web)
playbook.description: An employee or contractor deliberately exfiltrated company data intending to sell it to a competitor or on the dark web for personal financial gain.

steps.title: Detect anomalous data access/exfiltration by the insider
steps.desc: Identify unusual bulk data access, download, or transfer activity by the individual (e.g. to personal cloud storage, USB, personal email) via DLP, UEBA, or CASB alerts.
steps.guidance: Look for behavioral precursors: recent resignation notice, upcoming departure, or contact with competitors, which often correlate with financially-motivated insider theft.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous exfiltration activity attributable to the individual.
steps.abort: If activity is explained by authorized business need, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before any account or personnel action
steps.desc: Forensically preserve logs, device images, and access records related to the individual's activity before taking any action that could alert them or destroy evidence.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal on timing — evidence preservation must occur before termination or account changes tip off the insider.
steps.outcome: A forensically sound evidence record established for potential legal/HR action.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR and Legal on account restriction and personnel action
steps.desc: Jointly with HR and Legal, plan and execute simultaneous account suspension/access revocation and any personnel action (suspension, termination) to prevent further exfiltration while preserving legal standing.
steps.guidance: Timing account revocation to coincide with personnel action prevents the insider from retaliating or destroying further evidence upon notice.
steps.outcome: The insider's access is fully revoked with HR/Legal alignment on next steps.

steps.title: Recover or disable access to exfiltrated data where possible
steps.desc: Attempt to remotely wipe/revoke access to company data on personal devices or cloud accounts where technically and legally feasible (e.g. via MDM for company-managed personal devices).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on the legality of remote actions against personal devices/accounts before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Reduced further exposure of the exfiltrated data where legally and technically possible.
steps.abort: If no legal/technical means exist to act on personal devices, document and proceed to legal remedies.

steps.title: Close the access gap that enabled the exfiltration
steps.desc: Remediate the access control or monitoring gap that allowed the bulk exfiltration to occur undetected for as long as it did.
steps.outcome: The specific exfiltration channel/technique is closed for other users.

steps.title: Implement enhanced monitoring for departing/high-risk employees
steps.desc: Deploy heightened UEBA monitoring thresholds for employees who have submitted resignation notice or are otherwise flagged as elevated departure risk.
steps.outcome: Future financially-motivated insider exfiltration attempts are detected earlier.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies and monitor for data sale/use
steps.desc: Legal pursues appropriate remedies (civil action, law enforcement referral) and the organization monitors dark web/competitor activity for signs the data was sold or used.
steps.outcome: Legal action initiated where warranted and monitoring established.

steps.title: Review insider threat detection program and departure procedures
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to UEBA detection rules, off-boarding/departure monitoring, and cross-functional insider-threat response coordination.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked program improvements.

ITID-51712.def: An insider with legitimate access deliberately exfiltrates or discloses company data as an act of retaliation following a perceived grievance, such as termination, demotion, or a disciplinary action.
ITID-51712.purpose: Classifies insider data theft motivated by revenge or retaliation following a workplace grievance, distinguishing the retaliatory motive from profit-driven or coerced insider theft.
scopeIncludes: Data theft or public disclosure occurring in close temporal proximity to a termination, disciplinary action, or negative performance review
Deliberate destructive or embarrassing disclosure intended to harm the company rather than for financial gain
scopeExcludes: Data theft primarily for financial gain via sale (ITID-51711)
Insider acting under external recruitment/coercion (ITID-51713)
ITID-51712.severity: High. Retaliatory actors are often willing to disclose data publicly regardless of consequence, maximizing reputational harm.
ITID-51712.priority: P1, particularly when the insider retains active access following a known grievance trigger event.
ITID-51712.escalation: Escalate immediately to HR and legal; prioritize rapid access revocation for any employee with a recent adverse HR action.
indicators: Data access or export activity spiking immediately after a termination notice, demotion, or disciplinary meeting
Threatening or grievance-laden communications preceding the incident
Public or semi-public disclosure (e.g. social media, forums) rather than a quiet sale
vectors: Bulk export or deletion of data during a notice/garden-leave period
Public posting of sensitive internal documents
rootCauses: Delayed access revocation following termination or adverse HR action
Lack of coordination between HR and IT security on offboarding triggers
controls: Immediate access revocation triggered by HR adverse-action workflows
Heightened monitoring during notice/garden-leave periods
DLP alerting on bulk export or mass deletion activity
ITID-51712.detection: Correlating HR event triggers with access/export monitoring provides strong detection coverage for this specific pattern.
ITID-51712.response: Revoke access immediately upon any adverse HR action trigger, and investigate all activity in the preceding and following window.
metrics: Time from HR adverse-action trigger to access revocation
Number of retaliation-pattern incidents per year
detections: DLP mass-export/deletion alerting correlated with HR events
ITID-51712.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51711 by motive and disclosure pattern: retaliatory/public harm rather than a discreet sale for profit.

playbook.name: Insider Steals Data for Revenge/Retaliation Following Grievance
playbook.description: An aggrieved employee or contractor deliberately exfiltrated or destroyed company data as an act of retaliation following a workplace grievance.

steps.title: Detect anomalous data access/exfiltration or destruction correlated with a known grievance
steps.desc: Identify unusual data access, exfiltration, or deletion activity by the individual, using DLP/UEBA alerts and correlating with HR-known grievance events (disciplinary action, denied promotion, termination notice).
steps.guidance: HR-flagged high-risk terminations/grievances should trigger proactive monitoring; treat this as a priority correlation source.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous activity attributable to the individual, with grievance context noted.
steps.abort: If activity is explained by authorized business need, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before any account or personnel action
steps.desc: Forensically preserve logs, device images, and access/deletion records related to the individual's activity before further action.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with HR and Legal given the retaliatory/emotional context, which may also carry workplace-safety considerations.
steps.outcome: A forensically sound evidence record established.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR and Legal on immediate account restriction
steps.desc: Jointly with HR and Legal, immediately suspend the individual's access given the elevated risk of further retaliatory action (data destruction, sabotage) once a grievance is identified.
steps.guidance: Assess whether workplace-safety/security measures (badge deactivation, physical security notification) are also warranted given the retaliatory motive.
steps.outcome: The insider's access is fully revoked with HR/Legal/security alignment.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any data destruction or sabotage
steps.desc: Determine whether the individual deleted, corrupted, or sabotaged data/systems, and restore from backup or repair as needed.
steps.outcome: Any destructive impact is identified and remediated.

steps.title: Close the access gap that enabled the retaliatory action
steps.desc: Remediate the access control or monitoring gap that allowed the exfiltration or destruction to occur.
steps.outcome: The specific technique is closed for other users.

steps.title: Implement enhanced monitoring following HR-flagged grievance events
steps.desc: Deploy a formal process to trigger heightened security monitoring automatically when HR records a significant grievance, disciplinary action, or termination notice.
steps.outcome: Future retaliation-motivated insider incidents are detected earlier.

steps.title: Pursue appropriate personnel/legal action and restore normal operations
steps.desc: HR/Legal complete appropriate personnel and legal action, and affected systems/data are confirmed restored to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Incident formally closed with appropriate action taken.

steps.title: Review grievance-to-security-monitoring escalation process
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive formalized coordination between HR grievance processes and security monitoring to enable proactive risk flagging for future cases.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with a tracked HR-security coordination process improvement.

ITID-51713.def: An insider with legitimate access is recruited (via payment or ideological appeal) or coerced (via blackmail or threat) by an external threat actor to exfiltrate company data on that actor's behalf.
ITID-51713.purpose: Classifies insider data theft where the insider was recruited or coerced by an external threat actor, distinguishing externally-directed insider action from self-initiated profit or revenge motives.
scopeIncludes: Evidence of external contact, recruitment, or coercion (e.g. by a nation-state actor, organized crime group, or competitor agent) directing the insider's actions
Insider acting as a proxy for an identified or suspected external adversary
scopeExcludes: Self-initiated data theft for personal sale without external direction (ITID-51711)
Retaliation-driven theft without external involvement (ITID-51712)
ITID-51713.severity: Critical. External-actor direction implies a more sophisticated, sustained, and potentially state-sponsored threat.
ITID-51713.priority: P1, with counterintelligence/law-enforcement engagement given the external-actor dimension.
ITID-51713.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, HR, and law enforcement/counterintelligence contacts; treat as a potential espionage matter.
indicators: Communications with an external party requesting specific data categories
Insider behavior consistent with coercion (e.g. financial distress paired with foreign contact)
Data exfiltrated matching interests known to a specific external threat actor
vectors: Recruitment via professional networking platforms or approach by a foreign intelligence service
Blackmail using compromising personal information to coerce data access
rootCauses: Insufficient insider-threat/counterintelligence awareness training for high-access personnel
Lack of proactive vetting/monitoring for personnel with access to high-value data
controls: Insider-threat program with behavioral and travel/contact risk indicators
Enhanced vetting and periodic re-screening for high-access roles
DLP and UEBA monitoring tuned to high-value data categories
ITID-51713.detection: Technical DLP/UEBA detects the exfiltration; identifying the external-recruitment dimension typically requires HR, legal, and counterintelligence investigation.
ITID-51713.response: Coordinate with law enforcement/counterintelligence, preserve all evidence of external contact, and assess broader compromise of the same external campaign against other personnel.
metrics: Number of suspected externally-directed insider cases per year
Time to identify external-actor involvement
ITID-51713.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51711/51712 by the presence of an external directing actor; overlaps conceptually with APT-driven breach leaves (ITID-518xx) when the external actor is a sophisticated persistent adversary — cross-reference accordingly.

playbook.name: Insider Recruited/Coerced by External Threat Actor
playbook.description: An employee or contractor was recruited or coerced by an external threat actor (criminal group or nation-state) to exfiltrate company data on the actor's behalf.

steps.title: Detect anomalous data access/exfiltration with indicators of external coordination
steps.desc: Identify unusual data access/exfiltration activity by the individual, and look for corroborating indicators of external contact or coordination (unusual communications, financial windfalls, contact with known threat-actor infrastructure).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with counter-intelligence/insider-threat program resources where available, given the potential nation-state or organized-crime nexus.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous exfiltration with indicators suggesting external recruitment or coercion.
steps.abort: If no external-coordination indicators are found, treat as a standard malicious-insider case instead.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before any account or personnel action
steps.desc: Forensically preserve logs, device images, communications records, and access data before any action that could alert the insider or their external handler.
steps.guidance: Given potential law-enforcement/counter-intelligence interest, preserve evidence to forensic standards suitable for a criminal investigation.
steps.outcome: A forensically sound evidence record suitable for law-enforcement handoff.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal, HR, and law enforcement/counter-intelligence before acting
steps.desc: Engage Legal, HR, and, given the external threat-actor nexus, law enforcement or counter-intelligence contacts (e.g. FBI, relevant national security liaison) before taking overt containment action, since premature action could compromise an active investigation.
steps.guidance: Law enforcement may request a delay in overt action to preserve their own investigation — this decision must be made jointly, not unilaterally by IT/Security.
steps.outcome: A coordinated containment plan agreed with Legal, HR, and law enforcement.

steps.title: Revoke access per the coordinated plan
steps.desc: Execute the agreed account suspension/access revocation and any personnel action in coordination with law enforcement's timing requirements.
steps.outcome: The insider's access is revoked at the agreed time without compromising any parallel investigation.

steps.title: Close the access gap and assess broader compromise from the external actor
steps.desc: Remediate the access control gap exploited, and assess whether the external threat actor established any other footholds via the recruited insider (e.g. backdoors, other compromised accounts).
steps.outcome: The specific technique is closed and no additional actor footholds remain.

steps.title: Implement counter-recruitment awareness and reporting channels
steps.desc: Roll out insider-threat awareness training on recognizing and reporting recruitment/coercion attempts, and establish confidential reporting channels for employees approached by external actors.
steps.outcome: Employees are better equipped to recognize and report recruitment attempts, and future cases can potentially be caught before data loss occurs.

steps.title: Support ongoing law enforcement investigation and restore operations
steps.desc: Continue cooperating with law enforcement/counter-intelligence as needed, and confirm affected systems have returned to normal secure operation.
steps.outcome: Investigation support ongoing as needed and operations restored.

steps.title: Review insider threat program for external-recruitment risk indicators
steps.desc: Document the incident (within the constraints of any ongoing investigation) and drive improvements to insider-threat monitoring for external-recruitment risk factors.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked program improvements, redacted as required by any active investigation.

ITID-51714.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed malicious insider data breaches where the specific motive (financial gain, revenge/retaliation, or external recruitment/coercion) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51714.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for malicious insider data breaches not yet attributed to a specific motive.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of deliberate insider data theft pending motive determination
Confirmed intentional insider action where investigation into motive is still underway
scopeExcludes: Confirmed financial-gain motive (ITID-51711)
Confirmed revenge/retaliation motive (ITID-51712)
Confirmed external recruitment/coercion (ITID-51713)
Accidental/non-deliberate insider exposure (ITID-517xx Accidental Insider Breach group)
ITID-51714.severity: High by default until motive and scope are determined.
ITID-51714.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, and security immediately upon confirmation of deliberate insider action; re-triage once motive is established.
indicators: Confirmed deliberate data exfiltration by an insider with motive not yet established
Anomalous access flagged by DLP/UEBA pending investigative interview
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard insider-threat detection controls pending scoping
ITID-51714.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature beyond general insider-threat tooling.
ITID-51714.response: Preserve evidence, conduct HR/legal investigation to establish motive, and re-classify to the specific leaf once determined.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to motive-specific classification
detections: DLP and UEBA general anomaly alerting
ITID-51714.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51711, -51712, or -51713 as soon as motive is established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malicious Insider Data Breach
playbook.description: An employee or contractor deliberately exfiltrated, exposed, or misused company data for a motive not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Detect anomalous data access/exfiltration by the insider
steps.desc: Identify unusual bulk data access, download, or transfer activity by the individual via DLP, UEBA, or CASB alerts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous activity attributable to the individual.
steps.abort: If activity is explained by authorized business need, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before any account or personnel action
steps.desc: Forensically preserve logs, device images, and access records related to the individual's activity before taking action that could alert them.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal on timing.
steps.outcome: A forensically sound evidence record established.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR and Legal on account restriction and personnel action
steps.desc: Jointly with HR and Legal, plan and execute account suspension/access revocation and any personnel action to prevent further data loss while preserving legal standing.
steps.outcome: The insider's access is fully revoked with HR/Legal alignment.

steps.title: Assess scope of data accessed, exfiltrated, or exposed
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of what data was affected and its sensitivity/business impact.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of impact to inform legal and notification decisions.

steps.title: Close the access gap that enabled the breach
steps.desc: Remediate the access control or monitoring gap that allowed the activity to occur undetected.
steps.outcome: The specific channel/technique is closed for other users.

steps.title: Implement enhanced UEBA monitoring thresholds for high-risk activity patterns
steps.desc: Deploy or tune UEBA detection rules for bulk-access and exfiltration patterns similar to those observed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Future malicious insider activity of this kind is detected earlier.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies as warranted and restore normal operations
steps.desc: Legal pursues appropriate remedies where warranted, and affected systems/data are confirmed restored.
steps.outcome: Incident formally closed with appropriate action taken.

steps.title: Review insider threat detection and response program
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to UEBA detection rules and cross-functional insider-threat response coordination.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked program improvements.

ITID-51721.def: Sensitive company or customer data is unintentionally sent to an unintended recipient or distribution list due to human error, with no malicious intent by the sender.
ITID-51721.purpose: Classifies accidental data exposure caused by misdirected sharing (wrong email recipient, wrong distribution list), a common and purely human-error breach pattern.
scopeIncludes: Email or file sent to the wrong individual due to autocomplete or address-list error
Data sent to an outdated or overly broad distribution list
scopeExcludes: Data made publicly accessible via a misapplied sharing/permission setting (ITID-51722)
Data uploaded to an unauthorized personal platform (ITID-51723)
ITID-51721.severity: Medium, scaling with data sensitivity and recipient count/nature.
ITID-51721.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the recipient is external or the data is highly sensitive (e.g. health, financial, or large-scale PII).
ITID-51721.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal for notification assessment as soon as the misdirected recipient is confirmed unable/unwilling to delete the data.
indicators: Sender self-report of a misdirected email/file
Recipient report of receiving data not intended for them
Email DLP alert on sensitive-data pattern sent to an unexpected external domain
vectors: Human error, not an adversary technique
rootCauses: Autocomplete address selection errors
Outdated or improperly scoped distribution lists
Lack of send-time DLP warnings for sensitive content
controls: Outbound email DLP with sensitive-content warnings/holds
Distribution list governance and periodic review
Delayed-send/recall capability on email
ITID-51721.detection: Outbound DLP scanning provides moderate detection coverage; many cases are only caught via self-report or recipient report.
ITID-51721.response: Request deletion/confirmation of non-disclosure from the recipient, assess data sensitivity, and notify affected individuals if required.
metrics: Number of misdirected-data incidents per quarter
Percentage caught by DLP before send completion
ITID-51721.notes: Human error, not an adversary technique. No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies; classification and remediation focus on process/tooling controls rather than adversary defense.

playbook.name: Sensitive Data Accidentally Shared with Wrong Recipient/Distribution List
playbook.description: An employee unintentionally sent sensitive company or customer data to an incorrect individual or distribution list.

steps.title: Confirm the misdirected share and identify content and recipient(s)
steps.desc: Validate the report (typically self-reported or flagged by DLP) and determine exactly what data was shared, via what channel, and to whom.
steps.guidance: Self-reported accidental shares should be encouraged and treated non-punitively to preserve a culture of prompt disclosure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed content, channel, and unintended recipient(s).
steps.abort: If the recipient is confirmed to be authorized, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine sensitivity and scope of the shared data
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the data shared (PII, financial, confidential business data) and how many individuals/records were involved.
steps.outcome: A defined scope for risk assessment and any required notification.

steps.title: Attempt message recall and request destruction/non-disclosure from the recipient
steps.desc: Recall the message where technically possible, and directly contact the unintended recipient(s) to request deletion/destruction and confirm no further sharing.
steps.guidance: Document the recipient's response, as this is a mitigating factor in any downstream risk/breach assessment.
steps.outcome: Message recalled where possible and recipient cooperation confirmed or documented.
steps.abort: If recall fails and the recipient is unresponsive, document for the risk assessment and proceed to broader containment if warranted.

steps.title: Confirm no further propagation of the data
steps.desc: Verify the shared data was not forwarded, downloaded, or further distributed by the unintended recipient or any secondary parties.
steps.outcome: Confirmed containment with no further spread of the data.

steps.title: Correct the underlying cause (autocomplete error, outdated list, permission gap)
steps.desc: Identify and fix the specific cause of the misdirection — e.g. remove a stale distribution-list entry, adjust email autocomplete/warning settings, or add a send-confirmation step for sensitive data.
steps.outcome: The specific misdirection cause cannot recur.

steps.title: Deploy outbound DLP rules targeting the specific data type involved
steps.desc: Configure DLP policies to flag or block outbound transmission of the specific sensitive data type involved when sent to unexpected external recipients.
steps.outcome: Future accidental shares of this data type are caught before or immediately after transmission.

steps.title: Notify affected parties if required and close out the assessment
steps.desc: Complete any required notification based on data sensitivity and scope, and close the incident record.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations (if any) fulfilled and incident closed.

steps.title: Reinforce non-punitive reporting culture and outbound data-loss controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive process improvements (outbound DLP rules, send-confirmation prompts, distribution-list hygiene) while reinforcing that prompt self-reporting is valued, not penalized.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked process improvements.

ITID-51722.def: Sensitive company or customer data becomes accessible to unintended parties (public internet, all-company, or an overly broad group) due to a misapplied sharing, visibility, or permission setting on a file, repository, or cloud resource.
ITID-51722.purpose: Classifies accidental data exposure caused by a misconfigured or over-permissive sharing setting, distinguishing exposure via configuration from misdirected point-to-point sharing.
scopeIncludes: Cloud storage bucket or file-share link set to 'anyone with the link' or public when it should be restricted
Collaboration platform document/folder permission accidentally broadened beyond intended audience
scopeExcludes: Point-to-point misdirected email/recipient error (ITID-51721)
Data uploaded to an unauthorized personal/external platform (ITID-51723)
ITID-51722.severity: Medium-High, scaling with how long the resource was publicly accessible and its data sensitivity.
ITID-51722.priority: P1 if actively indexed/accessed by external parties; P2 if caught before external access is confirmed.
ITID-51722.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal immediately upon confirming external accessibility, especially if search-engine indexing or external access logs show retrieval.
indicators: Cloud security posture management (CSPM) alert on a public storage resource
External access logged against a resource believed to be internal-only
Discovery via search-engine indexing of an internal document
vectors: Human error, not an adversary technique
rootCauses: Default-public sharing settings on cloud storage/collaboration platforms
Lack of automated scanning for public-facing sensitive-data exposures
Insufficient training on platform sharing-setting implications
controls: CSPM/DSPM continuous scanning for publicly exposed sensitive data
Default-private sharing policy enforcement
Periodic access/permission review on collaboration platforms
ITID-51722.detection: CSPM/DSPM tooling provides strong, proactive detection coverage for this specific exposure pattern.
ITID-51722.response: Immediately restrict access, determine whether the resource was accessed externally during exposure, and notify affected parties if confirmed.
metrics: Duration of public exposure before remediation
Number of publicly exposed resources identified per scan cycle
ITID-51722.notes: Human error, not an adversary technique. No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies; the differentiator from ITID-51721 is a configuration/permission failure rather than a point-to-point sending mistake.

playbook.name: Sensitive Data Accidentally Made Publicly Visible via Misapplied Sharing Setting
playbook.description: Sensitive company or customer data was unintentionally exposed to the public internet due to an incorrectly applied sharing or access setting.

steps.title: Confirm the public exposure and identify the affected resource
steps.desc: Validate the report (self-reported, DLP, or external researcher notification) and identify the specific file, folder, bucket, or system that was publicly accessible.
steps.guidance: Encourage non-punitive self-reporting; external security-researcher reports should be triaged quickly and courteously.
steps.outcome: Confirmed publicly exposed resource and its content.
steps.abort: If the resource was not actually publicly accessible, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine how long the resource was public and whether it was accessed
steps.desc: Establish the exposure window from configuration-change logs and check access logs for any evidence of actual external access (not just theoretical exposure).
steps.guidance: Access-log evidence of actual retrieval significantly changes the risk/notification calculus versus a theoretical, unaccessed exposure.
steps.outcome: A defined exposure window and evidence of whether the data was actually accessed.

steps.title: Correct the sharing/access setting immediately
steps.desc: Restrict the resource's access setting to the intended, authorized scope, removing public/anonymous access.
steps.outcome: The resource is no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Assess whether the data was indexed or cached externally
steps.desc: Check search-engine caches, web archives, and third-party crawler logs to determine if the exposed data was indexed or copied elsewhere, and request removal where found.
steps.outcome: Identified and requested removal of any external copies/caches of the exposed data.
steps.abort: If no evidence of indexing/caching is found, document and proceed.

steps.title: Implement guardrails to prevent recurrence of the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Deploy automated cloud security posture management (CSPM) rules or default-deny sharing policies to detect or prevent similar public-exposure misconfigurations across the environment.
steps.guidance: Sweep for other resources with the same misconfiguration pattern.
steps.outcome: The specific misconfiguration class is prevented or automatically flagged going forward.

steps.title: Set default-private sharing policies across the affected platform
steps.desc: Change default sharing settings on the affected platform/service to private-by-default, requiring explicit action to make any resource public.
steps.outcome: Future accidental public exposure via default settings is prevented.

steps.title: Notify affected parties if required based on access evidence
steps.desc: Determine and execute any required notification based on data sensitivity and evidence of actual access, in coordination with Legal/Compliance if PII was involved.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations (if any) fulfilled.

steps.title: Reinforce non-punitive reporting and sharing-configuration training
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive process improvements (default-private sharing settings, periodic exposure audits, staff training) while reinforcing a non-punitive reporting culture.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked process improvements.

ITID-51723.def: An employee unintentionally exposes sensitive company data by uploading, syncing, or storing it on a personal or unauthorized third-party platform (personal cloud storage, personal email, unsanctioned SaaS tool) outside company control.
ITID-51723.purpose: Classifies accidental data exposure caused by an employee uploading sensitive data to an unauthorized personal or third-party platform, distinguishing shadow-IT exposure from misdirection or misconfiguration.
scopeIncludes: Sensitive files synced to a personal cloud storage account for convenience (e.g. working from home)
Company data pasted into an unsanctioned AI/SaaS tool without malicious intent
Data emailed to a personal account for after-hours work
scopeExcludes: Deliberate exfiltration to a personal platform for sale or retaliation (ITID-51711/ITID-51712)
Misdirected recipient email (ITID-51721)
Public cloud misconfiguration (ITID-51722)
ITID-51723.severity: Medium, scaling with data sensitivity and the security posture of the platform involved.
ITID-51723.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the platform is confirmed to have its own weak security or the data volume is large.
ITID-51723.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal if the platform's terms of service or security posture create meaningful ongoing exposure risk.
indicators: CASB/DLP alert on sensitive data upload to an unsanctioned SaaS or personal cloud domain
Employee self-report of using a personal tool for convenience
Data discovered on a personal device or account during an unrelated investigation
vectors: Human error, not an adversary technique
rootCauses: Lack of sanctioned, convenient tools for remote/after-hours work, driving shadow-IT use
Insufficient CASB coverage of unsanctioned SaaS destinations
Inadequate policy awareness on personal-device/account data handling
controls: CASB monitoring and blocking of unsanctioned SaaS uploads
Provisioning of secure, convenient sanctioned remote-work tooling
Policy and awareness training on personal-account data handling
ITID-51723.detection: CASB/DLP tooling provides good detection coverage for known unsanctioned destinations; personal-account use via unmanaged devices is harder to detect.
ITID-51723.response: Request deletion from the unauthorized platform, confirm no further propagation, and address the underlying tooling gap that drove the behavior.
metrics: Number of shadow-IT data exposure incidents per quarter
Percentage caught by CASB before manual report
ITID-51723.notes: Human error, not an adversary technique. No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies; differentiated from siblings by the shadow-IT/personal-platform destination rather than misdirected recipient or public misconfiguration.

playbook.name: Sensitive Data Accidentally Uploaded to Unauthorized/Personal Platform
playbook.description: An employee unintentionally uploaded sensitive company or customer data to an unauthorized third-party or personal platform (e.g. personal cloud storage, a public code repository, an AI/LLM tool).

steps.title: Confirm the upload and identify the destination platform and content
steps.desc: Validate the report (self-reported or flagged via CASB/DLP) and determine exactly what data was uploaded and to which unauthorized/personal platform.
steps.guidance: Encourage non-punitive self-reporting, particularly given the rise of well-intentioned but risky uploads to AI/LLM tools for legitimate work tasks.
steps.outcome: Confirmed uploaded content and destination platform.
steps.abort: If the platform is confirmed authorized/sanctioned, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine sensitivity of the data and the platform's data-retention/exposure risk
steps.desc: Assess data sensitivity and research the destination platform's data handling (e.g. whether an AI tool retains/trains on submitted data, whether a code repository is public).
steps.outcome: A defined risk assessment informing containment options.

steps.title: Request deletion from the platform and remove any public exposure
steps.desc: Delete the uploaded content from the platform where the employee has access, and submit a formal deletion/takedown request to the platform provider if needed (e.g. for a public repository or third-party service).
steps.guidance: For AI tools, check whether an opt-out/deletion request to the vendor is required to prevent the data being used in model training.
steps.outcome: The data is removed from the unauthorized platform or a formal removal request is filed.
steps.abort: If the platform cannot guarantee deletion (e.g. already used in training), document this limitation for the risk assessment.

steps.title: Block the unauthorized platform if not already restricted
steps.desc: Add the platform to the organization's blocked-services list (via CASB/web proxy) if it is not an approved tool, to prevent recurrence org-wide.
steps.outcome: The unauthorized platform is blocked or flagged for future use attempts.

steps.title: Provide or expand an approved alternative for the underlying business need
steps.desc: Identify why the employee used the unauthorized platform (e.g. no sanctioned AI tool, cumbersome approved file-sharing) and provide a sanctioned, secure alternative to reduce recurrence.
steps.guidance: Shadow IT/AI usage is often driven by unmet legitimate needs — address the root cause, not just the block.
steps.outcome: A sanctioned alternative is available, reducing incentive to use unauthorized platforms.

steps.title: Deploy CASB policy enforcement for the platform category involved
steps.desc: Configure CASB rules to detect or block future uploads of sensitive data to the same category of unauthorized platform.
steps.outcome: Future uploads of sensitive data to unauthorized platforms of this type are caught or blocked.

steps.title: Notify affected parties if required and close out the assessment
steps.desc: Complete any required notification based on data sensitivity and platform exposure, and close the incident record.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations (if any) fulfilled and incident closed.

steps.title: Update acceptable-use policy and training on approved platforms
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive policy/training updates on approved data-handling platforms, including specific guidance on AI/LLM tool usage with sensitive data.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked policy and training updates.

ITID-51724.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed accidental (non-malicious) insider data breaches where the specific mechanism (misdirected recipient, misconfigured sharing, or unauthorized platform upload) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51724.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for accidental insider breaches not yet attributed to a specific sub-category.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of accidental data exposure pending mechanism determination
Confirmed non-malicious insider exposure where the specific pathway is still under investigation
scopeExcludes: Confirmed misdirected recipient (ITID-51721)
Confirmed misconfigured sharing setting (ITID-51722)
Confirmed unauthorized platform upload (ITID-51723)
Any deliberate/malicious insider action (ITID-517xx Malicious Insider group)
ITID-51724.severity: Medium by default until scope is determined.
ITID-51724.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal for notification assessment while the specific mechanism is being confirmed.
indicators: Unconfirmed reports of accidental data exposure
Preliminary DLP/CASB alert pending root-cause determination
vectors: Human error, not an adversary technique
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard DLP/CASB controls pending scoping
ITID-51724.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51724.response: Rapidly determine the specific mechanism of accidental exposure and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to specific classification
ITID-51724.notes: Human error, not an adversary technique. Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51721, -51722, or -51723 as soon as scope permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Accidental Insider Breach
playbook.description: An employee unintentionally exposed or mishandled sensitive company or customer data through an error not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the accidental exposure and identify the cause
steps.desc: Validate the report (typically self-reported) and determine what data was exposed and through what specific error or process failure.
steps.guidance: Encourage non-punitive self-reporting to preserve a culture of prompt disclosure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure and identified cause.
steps.abort: If no actual exposure occurred, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Determine scope and sensitivity of the exposed data
steps.desc: Assess how much data, and of what sensitivity, was affected, and the exposure time window.
steps.outcome: A defined scope for risk assessment and any required notification.

steps.title: Stop further exposure and recall/contain the data where possible
steps.desc: Take the appropriate action given the specific error — recall a message, revoke a link, correct a permission — to halt further exposure.
steps.outcome: No further unauthorized exposure of the data is occurring.

steps.title: Confirm no further propagation of the data
steps.desc: Verify the exposed data was not further accessed, copied, or distributed beyond the initial incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed containment with no further spread.

steps.title: Correct the underlying process or control gap
steps.desc: Fix the specific process, configuration, or training gap that allowed the accidental exposure to occur.
steps.outcome: The specific cause cannot recur.

steps.title: Deploy targeted DLP/CASB controls addressing the specific error pattern
steps.desc: Configure DLP or CASB rules specifically addressing the error pattern identified in this incident to catch similar mistakes going forward.
steps.outcome: Future accidental exposures of the same pattern are caught earlier.

steps.title: Notify affected parties if required and close out the assessment
steps.desc: Complete any required notification based on data sensitivity and scope, and close the incident record.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations (if any) fulfilled and incident closed.

steps.title: Reinforce non-punitive reporting culture and relevant process controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive process/training improvements while reinforcing that prompt self-reporting is valued, not penalized.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked process improvements.

ITID-51731.def: A privileged user (administrator, executive assistant, database administrator, etc.) accesses or discloses data beyond their legitimate business need, resulting in a data breach, where the specific motive or mechanism does not warrant a dedicated sibling leaf.
ITID-51731.purpose: Serves as the intake/general classification for privileged-access-misuse data breaches within the insider-driven category, capturing cases where a privileged user's excessive or misused access resulted in data exposure.
scopeIncludes: Privileged user browsing or extracting data unrelated to their job function
Use of elevated access to view/export data outside an assigned investigation or task
Cases where privileged-access misuse is confirmed but does not clearly fit financial-gain, retaliation, or accidental-exposure patterns
scopeExcludes: Privileged misuse clearly motivated by financial gain (ITID-51711)
Privileged misuse clearly motivated by retaliation (ITID-51712)
Accidental exposure by a privileged user with no misuse of the privilege itself (ITID-5172x Accidental Insider Breach group)
ITID-51731.severity: High, given that privileged access typically grants exposure to the most sensitive data categories.
ITID-51731.priority: P1 given the scope of data typically accessible to privileged accounts.
ITID-51731.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, and security leadership immediately; privileged-access misuse often has outsized data-exposure potential.
indicators: Privileged account access to records with no corresponding ticket, case, or business justification
UEBA anomaly flagging access pattern inconsistent with role
Audit log review revealing curiosity-driven browsing of sensitive records
vectors: Use of standing administrative access to browse unrelated sensitive records
Abuse of break-glass or emergency access outside its intended scope
rootCauses: Excessive standing privileged access not scoped to least privilege
Lack of just-in-time access and mandatory business-justification logging for sensitive data access
Insufficient audit review of privileged access logs
controls: Just-in-time/least-privilege access provisioning
Mandatory business-justification logging for sensitive data queries
Regular privileged-access audit review
ITID-51731.detection: UEBA and privileged-access audit logging provide reasonably strong detection coverage when tuned to role-based access baselines.
ITID-51731.response: Revoke or scope down the misused privilege, determine the extent of data viewed/exported, and pursue disciplinary/legal action as warranted.
metrics: Number of privileged-access misuse cases identified per audit cycle
Percentage of privileged accounts under just-in-time access
ITID-51731.notes: This leaf is currently the sole child of its Tier-4 group and functions as both the general classification and the intake point for privileged-access-misuse breaches; re-triage to ITID-51711/51712 if a clear financial-gain or retaliation motive is later established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Privileged Access Misuse (Insider-Driven Breach Context)
playbook.description: An employee or contractor with elevated/privileged access used that access beyond its authorized purpose to view, exfiltrate, or expose sensitive data.

steps.title: Detect anomalous use of privileged access
steps.desc: Identify privileged-account activity inconsistent with the individual's role or job-required scope (e.g. an admin browsing unrelated executive records, a DBA exporting production data without a change ticket) via PAM session recording or audit logs.
steps.guidance: Correlate the activity against an approved change/access-request record; absence of a corresponding ticket is a strong signal of misuse.
steps.outcome: Confirmed misuse event with the specific privileged action(s) identified.
steps.abort: If the activity is tied to an approved change or legitimate task, close as non-incident.

steps.title: Assess severity and scope of the misuse
steps.desc: Determine what data was accessed/exposed, whether it was a one-time lapse or a pattern, and the apparent motive (curiosity, personal gain, malice) to calibrate the response.
steps.guidance: Severity assessment should directly drive how evidence-preserving vs. corrective the subsequent containment approach is.
steps.outcome: A calibrated severity assessment guiding proportionate response.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and restrict privileged access proportionate to severity
steps.desc: Preserve session recordings/logs, and restrict or suspend the individual's privileged access — full revocation for high-severity/malicious cases, or scoped restriction pending review for lower-severity lapses.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR on the appropriate level of access action; avoid over-punitive responses to genuinely low-severity, non-malicious lapses while still preserving evidence.
steps.outcome: Further misuse is prevented and evidence is preserved regardless of ultimate severity finding.

steps.title: Escalate to HR/Legal if severity indicates malicious intent or material harm
steps.desc: Where the assessed severity suggests malicious intent or material data exposure, engage HR and Legal per insider-threat procedures; for low-severity lapses, route to the individual's manager for corrective action.
steps.outcome: Response track (formal insider-threat process vs. managerial correction) matched to actual severity.

steps.title: Tighten privileged access controls and just-in-time access enforcement
steps.desc: Reduce standing privileged access in favor of just-in-time, ticket-linked elevation, and implement or tune PAM session recording/alerting for the access pattern exploited.
steps.outcome: Standing privileged access is reduced and misuse of the same kind would be both harder and faster to detect.

steps.title: Implement mandatory dual-approval for high-sensitivity privileged actions
steps.desc: Require a second-approver workflow for privileged actions touching highly sensitive data categories, reducing the ability of a single privileged user to act unilaterally.
steps.outcome: Future misuse of privileged access requires collusion rather than a single actor, raising the barrier to recurrence.

steps.title: Restore appropriate access levels and confirm normal operations
steps.desc: Following the review outcome, restore the individual's access to an appropriate scope (or confirm permanent revocation) and confirm affected systems/data are unaffected.
steps.outcome: Access levels finalized appropriately and operations confirmed normal.

steps.title: Review privileged access model and monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of least-privilege/JIT access models and improved PAM monitoring coverage across privileged account types.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked access-model improvements.

ITID-51811.def: An advanced persistent threat maintains covert access to company systems over a period of years, periodically returning to collect data in discrete episodes rather than continuously exfiltrating.
ITID-51811.purpose: Classifies APT breaches characterized by sustained, multi-year unauthorized access with periodic (not continuous) data collection, distinguishing sustained human-operated persistence from an automated harvesting script.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed multi-year dwell time with evidence of the actor returning at intervals to collect specific data
Human-operated, deliberately paced collection activity consistent with a patient, well-resourced adversary
scopeExcludes: Automated harvesting scripts running continuously and unattended (ITID-51812)
Single-episode or short-duration breaches regardless of severity
ITID-51811.severity: Critical. Multi-year dwell time implies extensive cumulative data exposure and deep adversary familiarity with the environment.
ITID-51811.priority: P1 upon confirmation of multi-year persistence.
ITID-51811.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and consider engaging external incident-response/threat-intelligence support given the sophistication implied.
indicators: Log retention gaps or evidence of long-dormant backdoors reactivated periodically
Forensic timeline showing distinct collection episodes spaced months or years apart
Persistence mechanisms (scheduled tasks, web shells) with creation timestamps years prior to discovery
vectors: Long-lived web shells or backdoors maintained across infrastructure changes
Periodic re-use of previously established access via valid credentials or persistence mechanisms
rootCauses: Insufficient log retention preventing full historical reconstruction
Lack of periodic threat hunting to detect dormant persistence mechanisms
Inadequate credential rotation allowing long-term reuse of compromised access
controls: Extended log retention supporting multi-year forensic reconstruction
Regular proactive threat hunting for dormant persistence
Credential and certificate rotation policies
ITID-51811.detection: Detection is difficult by design; threat hunting and anomaly detection on long-dormant accounts/mechanisms provide the primary opportunity for discovery.
ITID-51811.response: Full forensic reconstruction of the entire dwell period, comprehensive eviction across all persistence mechanisms, and assumption of maximal data exposure pending scoping.
metrics: Total dwell time from initial compromise to eviction
Number of distinct collection episodes identified
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
detections: Threat hunting for dormant persistence mechanisms
ITID-51811.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51812 by the human-operated, episodic collection pattern versus a continuously running automated script.

playbook.name: Multi-Year Persistent Access with Periodic Data Collection
playbook.description: An advanced threat actor maintained undetected persistent access to the environment for multiple years, periodically collecting and exfiltrating data.

steps.title: Confirm the persistent access and establish an initial timeline hypothesis
steps.desc: Validate the discovered indicator (e.g. unusual long-lived credential, backdoor, unexplained scheduled task) and begin constructing an initial hypothesis of how long the actor has had access.
steps.guidance: Given the likely long dwell time, assume available logs cover only a fraction of the true intrusion period — plan retention-limited log gaps into the investigation from the start.
steps.outcome: Confirmed persistent access with an initial (likely incomplete) timeline hypothesis.
steps.abort: If the indicator does not corroborate genuine persistent access, close as false positive.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full multi-year timeline and data collection scope through deep forensics
steps.desc: Conduct extended forensic analysis across all available log sources, backups, and artifacts to reconstruct the actor's full access history, persistence mechanisms, and each period of data collection/exfiltration.
steps.guidance: Engage an external incident-response/forensics firm with APT experience given the scale and sophistication typically involved; expect this scoping phase to take considerably longer than a standard incident.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive, multi-year timeline of access and data collection events, acknowledging residual uncertainty where logs no longer exist.

steps.title: Contain all identified persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal/blocking of all identified backdoors, scheduled tasks, credentials, and access paths to prevent the actor from re-establishing access via an undiscovered secondary foothold.
steps.guidance: Acting on discovered mechanisms one at a time risks tipping off the actor to re-establish access elsewhere — plan for coordinated, simultaneous action.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms are severed at the same time.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for a full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Given the scale and duration, escalate immediately to executive leadership and Legal to authorize a full external IR engagement, breach-notification assessment, and potential law-enforcement/regulator engagement.
steps.outcome: Executive sponsorship and Legal oversight established for the full response effort.

steps.title: Rebuild or fully re-credential affected systems and accounts
steps.desc: Given multi-year access, treat affected systems and credentials as fully compromised — rebuild critical systems from known-clean sources and rotate all potentially exposed credentials, keys, and certificates.
steps.guidance: A full domain/enterprise credential reset (including service accounts, certificates, and the krbtgt account where AD is implicated) is typically warranted at this scale.
steps.outcome: No trust is placed in any potentially-touched system or credential without rebuild/rotation.

steps.title: Extend log retention and deploy threat-hunting for similar long-dwell TTPs
steps.desc: Increase log retention periods and establish a recurring threat-hunting program specifically looking for the TTPs and persistence techniques used by this actor.
steps.outcome: Future long-dwell intrusions of similar sophistication are more likely to be detected sooner.

steps.title: Validate environment integrity through extended monitoring before declaring recovery
steps.desc: Implement heightened monitoring for an extended period post-eradication to confirm the actor has not retained or re-established access via an undiscovered mechanism.
steps.guidance: Given the actor's demonstrated persistence capability, a standard short monitoring window is insufficient — extend validation monitoring accordingly.
steps.outcome: Sustained absence of actor activity confirms successful eradication.

steps.title: Conduct comprehensive post-incident review and long-dwell detection improvement
steps.desc: Document the full timeline, root causes, and remediation for executive/board reporting, and drive investment in detection capabilities specifically aimed at reducing long-dwell-time blind spots (log retention, threat hunting cadence).
steps.outcome: Formal report with tracked long-term detection and architecture improvements.

ITID-51812.def: An advanced persistent threat deploys an automated script, tool, or malware that continuously collects and stages company data over an extended period without requiring ongoing manual operator interaction, remaining undetected until discovery.
ITID-51812.purpose: Classifies APT breaches involving an automated data-harvesting script or tool left running continuously and undetected, distinguishing automated persistence from human-operated periodic collection.
scopeIncludes: Malware or scripts configured to continuously harvest and stage data (e.g. scheduled database queries, file system scanners) over months or years
Automated exfiltration pipelines running with minimal or no operator interaction between initial deployment and discovery
scopeExcludes: Human-operated, periodic manual collection episodes (ITID-51811)
Short-lived automated tooling used in a single-episode breach
ITID-51812.severity: Critical. Continuous automated collection over an extended period implies the largest possible cumulative data exposure.
ITID-51812.priority: P1 upon discovery of a long-running automated harvesting mechanism.
ITID-51812.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal immediately; treat all data accessible to the script's execution context as potentially exfiltrated.
indicators: Scheduled task or cron job with an unexplained long creation-to-discovery gap
Consistent, low-and-slow outbound traffic pattern over an extended period
Staged data archives found in an unexpected location with a long history of file modification timestamps
vectors: Malicious scheduled tasks or cron jobs performing recurring data queries/exports
Malware configured for automated, low-and-slow beaconing and exfiltration
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of scheduled task/cron job creation and modification
Lack of network traffic baselining to catch low-and-slow exfiltration
Inadequate endpoint detection for long-running unauthorized processes
controls: Scheduled task/cron job creation monitoring and alerting
Network traffic baselining for low-and-slow exfiltration detection
Endpoint detection for long-running unauthorized processes
ITID-51812.detection: Network traffic baselining and scheduled-task monitoring provide the primary detection opportunity for this quiet, automated pattern.
ITID-51812.response: Isolate and terminate the harvesting mechanism, assess the full scope of data it had access to over its runtime, and remediate the persistence pathway that allowed it to run undetected.
metrics: Total runtime of the harvesting mechanism before discovery
Volume of data collected/staged over the runtime period
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
ITID-51812.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51811 by the automated, unattended nature of the collection mechanism rather than periodic human operator activity.

playbook.name: Automated Long-Term Data Harvesting Script Left Running Undetected
playbook.description: An attacker-deployed automated script continuously or periodically harvested data from company systems over an extended period without detection.

steps.title: Discover and confirm the harvesting script and its execution history
steps.desc: Confirm the script's presence (via EDR alert, anomalous scheduled task/cron discovery, or unusual recurring outbound traffic pattern) and determine how long it has been running.
steps.guidance: Recurring low-and-slow outbound traffic at regular intervals is a key indicator distinguishing automated harvesting from a one-time exfiltration event.
steps.outcome: Confirmed script with an established execution timeline.
steps.abort: If the process is legitimate automation, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine total volume and scope of data harvested over the script's lifetime
steps.desc: Reconstruct what data sources the script accessed and estimate the cumulative volume of data harvested across its entire undetected runtime.
steps.guidance: Use the script's own logic/configuration (if recovered) to determine exactly what it was targeting, rather than assuming scope from network volume alone.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of harvested data across the full undetected period.

steps.title: Terminate the script and remove its persistence mechanism
steps.desc: Kill the running process/script and remove its scheduled task, cron entry, or service registration to stop further harvesting.
steps.guidance: Preserve a copy of the script and its configuration before removal for forensic analysis.
steps.outcome: The harvesting script is no longer running or able to restart.

steps.title: Block the script's exfiltration destination and revoke any credentials it used
steps.desc: Block the command-and-control or exfiltration endpoint the script communicated with, and revoke/rotate any credentials embedded in or used by the script.
steps.outcome: No further exfiltration is possible even if a copy of the script exists elsewhere.

steps.title: Remediate the initial access vector and sweep for related artifacts
steps.desc: Identify and close how the script was originally deployed, and sweep the environment for other instances or related tooling from the same actor.
steps.outcome: The deployment vector is closed and no related artifacts remain elsewhere in the environment.

steps.title: Implement scheduled-task/cron auditing and baseline-deviation alerting
steps.desc: Deploy monitoring that audits and alerts on new or modified scheduled tasks, cron entries, and services across the environment, tuned to catch similar unauthorized automation.
steps.outcome: Future unauthorized automated scripts are detected significantly faster.

steps.title: Validate system integrity and monitor for redeployment attempts
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems are clean and implement monitoring for any attempt to redeploy similar harvesting tooling.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean environment with monitoring in place.

steps.title: Improve detection for long-running unauthorized automation
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive detection improvements for scheduled-task/cron auditing and baseline-deviation alerting on recurring low-volume outbound traffic.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection improvements.

ITID-51813.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed long-term APT data collection where the specific mechanism (periodic manual collection or automated harvesting) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51813.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for long-term data collection incidents not yet attributed to a periodic human-operated or automated pattern.
scopeIncludes: Initial discovery of long-dwell-time access pending mechanism determination
Confirmed extended unauthorized access where the collection pattern is still under forensic investigation
scopeExcludes: Confirmed periodic human-operated collection (ITID-51811)
Confirmed automated harvesting script (ITID-51812)
ITID-51813.severity: Critical by default given the long-term-access context.
ITID-51813.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal immediately; re-triage once the collection mechanism is forensically established.
indicators: Evidence of long dwell time without yet-determined collection pattern
Preliminary forensic findings pending full timeline reconstruction
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard APT detection and threat hunting controls pending scoping
ITID-51813.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51813.response: Rapidly determine whether the collection pattern was periodic/manual or automated and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to specific classification
ITID-51813.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51811 or ITID-51812 as soon as scope permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Long-Term Data Collection
playbook.description: A threat actor maintained undetected access over an extended period, collecting data through a mechanism not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the long-term access and establish an initial timeline hypothesis
steps.desc: Validate the discovered indicator of long-term unauthorized access and begin constructing an initial hypothesis of the intrusion's duration and mechanism.
steps.guidance: Assume available logs may only cover part of the true intrusion period given retention limits.
steps.outcome: Confirmed long-term access with an initial timeline hypothesis.
steps.abort: If the indicator does not corroborate genuine long-term access, close as false positive.

steps.title: Reconstruct the collection timeline and data scope through extended forensics
steps.desc: Conduct forensic analysis across available log sources and artifacts to reconstruct the full history of access and each period of data collection.
steps.guidance: Engage external IR/forensics support if internal capability or log retention is insufficient for the apparent scale.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive timeline of access and data collection events.

steps.title: Contain all identified persistence and access mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal/blocking of all identified access mechanisms to prevent the actor from re-establishing access via an undiscovered secondary foothold.
steps.outcome: All known access mechanisms are severed at the same time.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal to authorize the scope of response needed, including breach-notification assessment where warranted.
steps.outcome: Executive sponsorship and Legal oversight established.

steps.title: Rebuild or re-credential affected systems and accounts
steps.desc: Treat affected systems and credentials as compromised given the extended access period — rebuild from known-clean sources and rotate exposed credentials.
steps.outcome: No trust is placed in any potentially-touched system or credential without rebuild/rotation.

steps.title: Extend log retention and deploy threat-hunting for similar long-dwell activity
steps.desc: Increase log retention periods and establish recurring threat-hunting specifically looking for the persistence and collection techniques used in this incident.
steps.outcome: Future long-dwell data collection is more likely to be detected sooner.

steps.title: Validate environment integrity through extended monitoring
steps.desc: Implement heightened monitoring post-eradication to confirm the actor has not retained or re-established access.
steps.outcome: Sustained absence of actor activity confirms successful eradication.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and long-dwell detection improvement
steps.desc: Document the timeline, root causes, and remediation, and drive investment in detection capabilities aimed at reducing long-dwell-time blind spots.
steps.outcome: Formal report with tracked detection and architecture improvements.

ITID-51821.def: A sophisticated, sustained intrusion attributed (or reasonably suspected to be attributable) to a nation-state-sponsored threat actor, specifically targeting the company's trade secrets, proprietary research, or strategic intellectual property.
ITID-51821.purpose: Classifies APT breaches attributed to nation-state-sponsored actors targeting trade secrets and intellectual property, distinguishing state-sponsored espionage from competitor-driven espionage.
scopeIncludes: Intrusions with tactics, techniques, and infrastructure consistent with known nation-state APT groups
Targeted theft of R&D, proprietary formulas, source code, or strategic business intelligence
scopeExcludes: Espionage attributed to a business competitor rather than a nation-state (ITID-51822)
General/unattributed espionage (ITID-51823)
ITID-51821.severity: Critical. Nation-state involvement implies advanced capability, strategic intent, and typically severe long-term competitive/national-security impact.
ITID-51821.priority: P1, with mandatory engagement of executive leadership, legal, and government/law-enforcement liaison channels.
ITID-51821.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and relevant government cybersecurity agencies; nation-state attribution often carries reporting obligations.
indicators: Threat intelligence attribution linking observed TTPs/infrastructure to a known nation-state APT group
Targeting pattern focused specifically on R&D, proprietary technology, or strategic data rather than broad financial data
Highly sophisticated evasion and living-off-the-land techniques
vectors: Spear-phishing targeting R&D or executive personnel
Supply-chain compromise of a technology vendor
Exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation isolating high-value R&D data from general corporate networks
Inadequate threat intelligence integration for nation-state indicator detection
controls: Network segmentation isolating high-value intellectual property
Threat intelligence feeds tuned to known nation-state indicators
Enhanced monitoring on R&D and executive systems
ITID-51821.detection: Threat intelligence-informed hunting provides the strongest detection opportunity given the sophistication of nation-state tradecraft.
ITID-51821.response: Engage specialized incident response and government liaison, conduct full forensic scoping of R&D/IP data accessed, and assess long-term strategic impact.
metrics: Volume/sensitivity of intellectual property confirmed accessed
Time from threat intelligence attribution to containment
