ITID-51821.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51822 by attribution: nation-state sponsorship rather than a business competitor.

playbook.name: Nation-State-Sponsored Corporate Espionage Targeting Trade Secrets
playbook.description: A nation-state-affiliated threat actor conducted a targeted campaign to steal the organization's trade secrets for strategic or economic advantage.

steps.title: Confirm nation-state attribution indicators and targeted trade secret access
steps.desc: Analyze TTPs, infrastructure, and malware against known nation-state threat-actor intelligence to assess attribution confidence, while confirming specific access to trade-secret-designated systems/data.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence resources (internal or a specialized vendor) for attribution assessment; attribution confidence should inform but not delay containment urgency.
steps.outcome: An attribution confidence assessment and confirmed access to trade secret material.
steps.abort: If access to trade secret material cannot be confirmed despite the actor's presence, scope the response to general intrusion handling instead.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full campaign timeline and determine exactly what was accessed/exfiltrated
steps.desc: Conduct deep forensic investigation to establish the actor's full dwell time, lateral movement path, and precisely which trade secret data was accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Nation-state actors typically employ sophisticated anti-forensic techniques — engage specialized external IR support experienced with nation-state intrusions.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive campaign timeline and defined scope of trade secret exposure.

steps.title: Coordinate simultaneous, comprehensive containment across all identified footholds
steps.desc: Given nation-state actors' typical redundant persistence, plan and execute simultaneous containment across every identified access point to prevent the actor pivoting to an undiscovered foothold.
steps.outcome: All known footholds are severed simultaneously.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Legal, and relevant government/CISA partners
steps.desc: Escalate immediately to executive leadership and Legal, and engage relevant government partners (e.g. CISA, sector-specific ISAC, or national security liaison) given the nation-state nexus and potential national-security implications.
steps.guidance: Nation-state espionage of trade secrets may trigger government interest independent of the organization's own reporting obligations.
steps.outcome: Government partners engaged and executive/Legal oversight established.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems and rotate all potentially exposed credentials
steps.desc: Treat all touched systems and credentials as compromised given the sophistication of the actor — rebuild from known-clean sources and rotate exposed credentials, keys, and certificates.
steps.outcome: No residual trust placed in potentially compromised infrastructure or credentials.

steps.title: Deploy threat-intel-informed detection for the attributed actor's known TTPs
steps.desc: Ingest and operationalize threat-intelligence indicators specific to the attributed nation-state actor into detection tooling to catch reuse of similar infrastructure or techniques.
steps.outcome: Future activity from the same or affiliated actor is detected faster.

steps.title: Validate environment integrity via extended, specialized monitoring
steps.desc: Implement extended monitoring, ideally informed by threat-intel indicators specific to the attributed actor, to confirm eradication before declaring recovery complete.
steps.outcome: Sustained absence of actor activity confirms successful eradication.

steps.title: Conduct executive/board-level post-incident review and strategic hardening
steps.desc: Document the campaign, attribution assessment, and remediation for executive/board reporting, and drive strategic investment in trade-secret protection and nation-state threat detection capability.
steps.outcome: Formal report with tracked strategic security investments.

ITID-51822.def: A sophisticated, sustained intrusion attributed (or reasonably suspected to be attributable) to a business competitor or an actor acting on a competitor's behalf, targeting proprietary business information for commercial advantage.
ITID-51822.purpose: Classifies APT-style breaches attributed to a business competitor rather than a nation-state, distinguishing commercially-motivated espionage from state-sponsored activity.
scopeIncludes: Intrusions where evidence (targeting pattern, timing relative to competitive bids, or direct attribution) points to a competitor
Theft of pricing strategy, customer lists, bid information, or product roadmaps of clear commercial value to a specific competitor
scopeExcludes: Espionage attributed to a nation-state actor (ITID-51821)
General/unattributed espionage (ITID-51823)
ITID-51822.severity: High-Critical, scaling with the commercial sensitivity of the data and competitive market impact.
ITID-51822.priority: P1 given direct competitive harm and likely legal/civil litigation implications.
ITID-51822.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal immediately; competitor attribution often supports civil litigation or trade-secret misappropriation claims.
indicators: Targeting pattern focused specifically on data of clear value to a known competitor (bids, pricing, customer lists)
Timing correlation between the intrusion and competitive business events (bid deadlines, product launches)
Forensic or legal evidence directly implicating a competitor or its agent
vectors: Spear-phishing targeting sales, product, or strategy personnel
Insider recruitment by a competitor (cross-reference ITID-51713)
Compromise of a shared vendor or partner with access to competitive data
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls on commercially sensitive data (pricing, bids, customer lists)
Inadequate monitoring for access patterns correlated with competitive events
controls: Access controls and DLP on commercially sensitive business data
Legal preservation processes for suspected competitor-driven incidents
Monitoring for access-pattern correlation with competitive milestones
ITID-51822.detection: Detection often relies on correlating data-access anomalies with competitive business timing, alongside standard DLP/UEBA tooling.
ITID-51822.response: Preserve forensic evidence to support potential trade-secret misappropriation litigation, assess commercial impact, and coordinate with legal on competitor-directed response options.
metrics: Commercial value/sensitivity of data confirmed accessed
Time from suspected competitor targeting to attribution confidence
detections: UEBA access-pattern correlation with competitive events
ITID-51822.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51821 by attribution: a business competitor rather than a nation-state; cross-reference ITID-51713 (Insider Recruited/Coerced by External Threat Actor) when a competitor's espionage is insider-facilitated.

playbook.name: Competitor-Sponsored Corporate Espionage
playbook.description: A threat actor operating on behalf of, or hired by, a business competitor conducted a targeted campaign to steal the organization's confidential business information.

steps.title: Confirm targeted access and gather indicators suggesting competitor sponsorship
steps.desc: Confirm the targeted intrusion and access to competitively sensitive data, and gather any indicators (targeting pattern focused narrowly on competitive intelligence, prior business disputes, timing correlated with competitive events) suggesting competitor involvement.
steps.guidance: Competitor attribution is often circumstantial — document indicators carefully for potential legal action rather than asserting attribution prematurely.
steps.outcome: Confirmed targeted access with documented attribution indicators.
steps.abort: If access to competitively sensitive data cannot be confirmed, scope response to general intrusion handling instead.

steps.title: Determine exactly what competitive/business data was accessed or exfiltrated
steps.desc: Reconstruct the intrusion timeline and precisely identify which business-sensitive data (bids, pricing, customer lists, strategic plans) was accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Engage the affected business unit to assess competitive impact of the specific data exposed.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of exposure with clear competitive-impact assessment.

steps.title: Contain all identified access points
steps.desc: Remove or block all identified footholds and revoke any compromised credentials used in the intrusion.
steps.outcome: The actor's access is fully severed.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for evidence preservation and potential litigation
steps.desc: Engage executive leadership and Legal to preserve evidence to a litigation-ready standard and assess potential civil action against the competitor if attribution can be substantiated.
steps.guidance: Preserve all attribution-relevant evidence carefully given the potential for future legal proceedings.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and Legal has opened an assessment of potential action.

steps.title: Remediate the exploited vulnerability and rotate exposed credentials
steps.desc: Close the vulnerability or weakness exploited for initial access and rotate any credentials, keys, or certificates the actor may have obtained.
steps.outcome: The specific access path cannot be reused.

steps.title: Strengthen protection around the categories of business data targeted
steps.desc: Apply additional access controls, DLP, and monitoring specifically to the categories of competitively sensitive data targeted in this campaign (bids, pricing, customer lists).
steps.outcome: The targeted data categories are better protected against repeat targeting.

steps.title: Validate environment integrity and monitor for repeat targeting
steps.desc: Confirm the environment is clean and establish monitoring for further targeting attempts consistent with the same actor's pattern.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean environment with targeted monitoring in place.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and strengthen competitive-intelligence protection
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improved protection (access controls, DLP, monitoring) around the categories of business data targeted.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked protection improvements.

ITID-51823.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed targeted corporate espionage breaches where the sponsoring actor (nation-state or business competitor) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51823.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for targeted corporate espionage incidents not yet attributed to a nation-state or competitor.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of targeted IP/trade-secret theft pending attribution
Confirmed espionage-pattern breaches where attribution investigation is still underway
scopeExcludes: Confirmed nation-state sponsorship (ITID-51821)
Confirmed competitor sponsorship (ITID-51822)
ITID-51823.severity: High-Critical by default given the targeted-espionage context.
ITID-51823.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal immediately; re-triage once attribution is established.
indicators: Targeted theft of intellectual property or strategic data with attribution not yet determined
Preliminary threat intelligence findings pending confirmation
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard IP-protection and DLP controls pending scoping
ITID-51823.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51823.response: Rapidly pursue attribution to determine whether the sponsor is a nation-state or competitor and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to attribution-specific classification
ITID-51823.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51821 or ITID-51822 as soon as attribution permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Targeted Corporate Espionage
playbook.description: A threat actor conducted a targeted campaign to steal the organization's confidential business information for a sponsor or purpose not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm targeted access to sensitive business data
steps.desc: Confirm the targeted nature of the intrusion and access to competitively or strategically sensitive data.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence resources to assess actor sophistication and possible motive/sponsor.
steps.outcome: Confirmed targeted access with an initial assessment of actor sophistication.
steps.abort: If access to sensitive business data cannot be confirmed, scope response to general intrusion handling instead.

steps.title: Reconstruct the campaign timeline and determine what was accessed or exfiltrated
steps.desc: Conduct forensic investigation to establish dwell time, lateral movement, and precisely which business-sensitive data was accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: A defined campaign timeline and scope of exposure.

steps.title: Contain all identified access points
steps.desc: Remove or block all identified footholds and revoke any compromised credentials used in the intrusion.
steps.outcome: The actor's access is fully severed.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal
steps.desc: Engage executive leadership and Legal to assess response scope, evidence preservation needs, and potential regulatory/law-enforcement engagement.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established for the response.

steps.title: Remediate the exploited vulnerability and rotate exposed credentials
steps.desc: Close the vulnerability or weakness exploited for access and rotate any credentials, keys, or certificates the actor may have obtained.
steps.outcome: The specific access path cannot be reused.

steps.title: Strengthen protection around the categories of business data targeted
steps.desc: Apply additional access controls, DLP, and monitoring specifically to the categories of business-sensitive data targeted in this campaign.
steps.outcome: The targeted data categories are better protected against repeat targeting.

steps.title: Validate environment integrity and monitor for repeat targeting
steps.desc: Confirm the environment is clean and establish monitoring for further targeting attempts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean environment with targeted monitoring in place.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and strengthen protection of targeted data
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improved protection around the categories of business data targeted.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked protection improvements.

ITID-51831.def: A sophisticated breach in which the threat actor combines phishing (for initial access or credential theft) with vulnerability exploitation (for privilege escalation, lateral movement, or an alternate access path) across the kill chain, rather than relying on a single vector.
ITID-51831.purpose: Classifies APT breaches achieved through a combination of phishing-based initial access and separate exploit-based techniques, distinguishing purely technical multi-vector attacks from those blending insider and external elements.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed use of both phishing and exploit-based techniques within the same intrusion campaign
Multi-stage attacks where an initial phishing foothold is combined with exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability for escalation
scopeExcludes: Single-vector phishing-only breaches (classified under Credential Theft, ITID-511xx)
Combined insider-and-external-actor breaches (ITID-51832)
ITID-51831.severity: Critical. Multi-vector attacks indicate a well-resourced, adaptable adversary with multiple footholds.
ITID-51831.priority: P1 given the increased difficulty of full eviction across multiple entry vectors.
ITID-51831.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and specialized incident response; assume multiple persistence mechanisms until proven otherwise.
indicators: Forensic timeline showing both a phishing-derived credential compromise and separate exploit-based access in the same campaign
Multiple distinct initial-access artifacts (malicious email plus exploited vulnerability logs)
vectors: Spear-phishing for initial credential access combined with exploitation of an unpatched internet-facing vulnerability
Phishing-derived access used to pivot to exploitation of internal systems
rootCauses: Delayed patching creating an available exploit path alongside phishing susceptibility
Insufficient network segmentation allowing a single foothold to expand via exploitation
controls: Timely vulnerability patching to close exploit paths
Phishing-resistant MFA to blunt credential-based footholds
Network segmentation limiting lateral spread from either vector
ITID-51831.detection: Requires correlated detection across email security, vulnerability management, and network monitoring to see the full multi-vector picture.
ITID-51831.response: Full forensic scoping across both vectors, comprehensive eviction, and validation that no additional foothold remains before closure.
metrics: Number of distinct vectors confirmed in the campaign
Time to full eviction across all vectors
detections: Correlated email security and vulnerability exploitation alerting
ITID-51831.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51832 by scope: this leaf is purely technical (phishing plus exploitation), not combined with an insider component.

playbook.name: Combined Phishing and Exploit-Based Multi-Vector Breach
playbook.description: An attacker combined a phishing campaign with exploitation of a technical vulnerability across multiple vectors to achieve a data breach.

steps.title: Identify and correlate all distinct attack vectors used
steps.desc: Investigate the initial phishing-related alert and any concurrent/related exploit-based alerts to confirm both vectors are part of a single coordinated campaign rather than unrelated events.
steps.guidance: Multi-vector attacks are often initially triaged as separate, lower-severity incidents — actively look for correlation across seemingly unrelated alerts before scoping down.
steps.outcome: Confirmed multi-vector campaign with each vector identified.
steps.abort: If the events are confirmed unrelated, handle as separate, smaller incidents instead.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full attack chain and determine data accessed via each vector
steps.desc: Map how the phishing and exploit vectors were combined (e.g. phishing for initial credential access, then exploit for privilege escalation/lateral movement) and determine what data was accessed or exfiltrated at each stage.
steps.outcome: A complete attack-chain reconstruction with defined data-exposure scope.

steps.title: Contain both vectors simultaneously
steps.desc: Revoke phished credentials/sessions and patch or isolate systems affected by the exploited vulnerability at the same time, to prevent the actor pivoting from one vector to sustain access via the other.
steps.outcome: Both vectors are neutralized without leaving a residual access path.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal given the breach's scale and complexity
steps.desc: Engage executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations and oversee the broader response given the multi-vector complexity.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Patch the exploited vulnerability and harden phishing defenses
steps.desc: Apply the vulnerability patch/configuration fix, and implement or strengthen phishing-resistant authentication and email security controls to close both vectors permanently.
steps.outcome: Neither vector remains available to the actor or a similar future attacker.

steps.title: Tune SIEM correlation rules to link phishing and exploit-stage alerts
steps.desc: Build or refine SIEM correlation logic to automatically flag when phishing-related alerts and exploit/vulnerability alerts occur against the same user or system within a short window.
steps.outcome: Future multi-vector campaigns combining these two techniques are recognized as a single incident sooner.

steps.title: Validate full environment integrity before declaring recovery
steps.desc: Confirm no residual access remains via either vector and that affected systems/accounts are restored to normal secure operation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean environment across both attack vectors.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review of cross-vector detection and correlation capability
steps.desc: Document the full attack chain and drive improvements to SIEM correlation rules so future multi-vector campaigns are recognized as a single incident earlier.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection-correlation improvements.

ITID-51832.def: A sophisticated breach in which an external threat actor's intrusion is combined with the involvement of a company insider (witting or coerced), such that both an internal and external actor jointly enable the data breach.
ITID-51832.purpose: Classifies APT breaches combining an insider component with external attacker activity, distinguishing hybrid insider/external campaigns from purely technical multi-vector attacks.
scopeIncludes: External APT campaign that recruits or coerces an insider mid-campaign to facilitate deeper access or bypass controls
Insider provides credentials, access, or internal reconnaissance that is then leveraged by an external technical intrusion
scopeExcludes: Purely technical multi-vector breaches with no insider involvement (ITID-51831)
Insider-only breaches with no external actor involvement (classified under Insider-Driven Data Breach, ITID-517xx)
ITID-51832.severity: Critical. The combination of insider access and external technical capability typically defeats perimeter and access controls simultaneously.
ITID-51832.priority: P1 given the compounded difficulty of detection and containment.
ITID-51832.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, HR, and law enforcement given both the external-intrusion and insider dimensions.
indicators: External intrusion artifacts correlated with anomalous insider access facilitating the campaign
Insider communications with an external party matching intrusion timing
Access patterns showing internal reconnaissance handed off to external technical exploitation
vectors: Insider providing VPN/credential access later leveraged by an external actor
External actor recruiting an insider mid-campaign for internal reconnaissance support
rootCauses: Insufficient insider-threat monitoring alongside external intrusion detection
Lack of correlation between HR risk indicators and security telemetry
controls: Correlated insider-threat and external-intrusion monitoring programs
Enhanced vetting/monitoring for personnel with access to high-value systems
Segmentation limiting the blast radius of a single insider-facilitated foothold
ITID-51832.detection: Requires joint insider-threat and network/endpoint detection correlation; neither alone reliably surfaces the hybrid pattern.
ITID-51832.response: Coordinate technical eviction with HR/legal action against the insider, and pursue law enforcement engagement given the coordinated nature of the attack.
metrics: Time to identify the insider-facilitation component
Scope of data accessed via the combined vector
detections: Correlated insider-threat and network intrusion detection
ITID-51832.notes: Differentiated from ITID-51831 by the presence of a genuine insider-facilitation component; cross-reference ITID-51713 (Insider Recruited/Coerced by External Threat Actor) when the insider action itself is the primary classification focus.

playbook.name: Combined Insider and External Attacker Multi-Vector Breach
playbook.description: An insider collaborated with, or was leveraged by, an external attacker to achieve a data breach combining insider access with external attack techniques.

steps.title: Identify indicators of both insider involvement and external attacker activity
steps.desc: Investigate alerts suggesting both an internal account acting outside its normal pattern and evidence of external attacker infrastructure/tooling, and assess whether they are connected.
steps.guidance: Look for correlation such as an insider's credentials being used from an external attacker's infrastructure, or an insider disabling controls to facilitate external access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed connection between insider activity and external attacker involvement.
steps.abort: If no connection is found, handle as separate insider and external incidents.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and reconstruct the full collaboration timeline
steps.desc: Forensically preserve evidence of the insider's actions and the external actor's activity before taking action, and reconstruct how the two combined to achieve the breach and what data was accessed.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal given the insider dimension — evidence preservation should meet standards suitable for potential personnel action and criminal referral.
steps.outcome: A forensically sound, complete timeline of the combined attack.

steps.title: Coordinate simultaneous containment of insider access and external attacker infrastructure
steps.desc: Jointly with HR/Legal, suspend the insider's access while simultaneously blocking the external attacker's identified infrastructure/access points, to prevent either party from independently sustaining the breach.
steps.guidance: Timing must be coordinated to prevent the insider from alerting the external party or vice versa.
steps.outcome: Both the insider and external attacker access paths are severed at the same time.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Legal, HR, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Given the combined insider-external nature, escalate to executive leadership, Legal, HR, and consider law-enforcement referral given the potential criminal conspiracy involved.
steps.outcome: Full cross-functional oversight established including potential law-enforcement engagement.

steps.title: Close the access gap the insider exploited or enabled
steps.desc: Remediate the specific access control or process gap that allowed the insider to facilitate or enable external attacker access.
steps.outcome: The specific insider-enabled vector is closed.

steps.title: Tune detection to correlate insider behavioral anomalies with external threat indicators
steps.desc: Build or refine detection logic linking UEBA-flagged insider anomalies with threat-intelligence indicators of known external attacker infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Future insider-external collusion is recognized as a single coordinated incident sooner.

steps.title: Complete personnel/legal action and validate environment integrity
steps.desc: HR/Legal complete appropriate personnel and legal action against the insider, and confirm the environment is free of any residual external attacker access.
steps.outcome: Incident formally closed with appropriate action taken and environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Review insider-external collusion detection capability
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to detection correlating insider behavioral anomalies with external threat intelligence indicators.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection improvements.

ITID-51833.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed multi-vector APT-style data breaches where the composition of vectors (technical-only versus insider-facilitated) has not yet been determined.
ITID-51833.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for multi-vector data breaches not yet attributed to a purely technical or insider-facilitated pattern.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of a multi-vector breach pending vector-composition determination
Confirmed complex breaches where forensic investigation into the specific vector mix is ongoing
scopeExcludes: Confirmed purely technical phishing-plus-exploit combination (ITID-51831)
Confirmed insider-facilitated combination (ITID-51832)
ITID-51833.severity: Critical by default given the multi-vector context.
ITID-51833.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal immediately; re-triage once the vector composition is forensically established.
indicators: Evidence of multiple attack vectors with composition not yet determined
Preliminary forensic findings pending full investigation
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard APT detection controls pending scoping
ITID-51833.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51833.response: Rapidly determine whether the breach was purely technical or insider-facilitated and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to vector-specific classification
detections: General intrusion detection and threat hunting
ITID-51833.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51831 or ITID-51832 as soon as scope permits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Multi-Vector Data Breach
playbook.description: An attacker combined multiple distinct attack vectors not otherwise classified to achieve a data breach.

steps.title: Identify and correlate all distinct attack vectors used
steps.desc: Investigate related alerts across different vectors to confirm they are part of a single coordinated campaign rather than unrelated events.
steps.guidance: Actively look for correlation across seemingly unrelated alerts before scoping the incident down to a single vector.
steps.outcome: Confirmed multi-vector campaign with each vector identified.
steps.abort: If the events are confirmed unrelated, handle as separate, smaller incidents.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full attack chain and determine data accessed via each vector
steps.desc: Map how each vector was used and combined, and determine what data was accessed or exfiltrated at each stage.
steps.outcome: A complete attack-chain reconstruction with defined data-exposure scope.

steps.title: Contain all identified vectors simultaneously
steps.desc: Neutralize each identified vector at the same time to prevent the actor pivoting from one to sustain access via another.
steps.outcome: All vectors are neutralized without leaving a residual access path.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal given the breach's scale and complexity
steps.desc: Engage executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations and oversee the broader response.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Remediate each vector's root cause
steps.desc: Apply the necessary fixes across each vector used, closing them permanently.
steps.outcome: None of the vectors remain available to the actor or a similar future attacker.

steps.title: Tune SIEM correlation rules to link alerts across the vectors observed
steps.desc: Build or refine SIEM correlation logic to automatically flag when alerts across the specific vectors observed in this campaign occur against the same user or system within a short window.
steps.outcome: Future multi-vector campaigns of this kind are recognized as a single incident sooner.

steps.title: Validate full environment integrity before declaring recovery
steps.desc: Confirm no residual access remains via any vector and that affected systems/accounts are restored to normal secure operation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean environment across all attack vectors.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review of cross-vector detection and correlation capability
steps.desc: Document the full attack chain and drive improvements to detection correlation so future multi-vector campaigns are recognized as a single incident earlier.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection-correlation improvements.

ITID-51841.def: A data breach that went undetected by internal security monitoring for its entire duration and was only discovered because a third party (customer, partner, law enforcement, researcher, or the threat actor itself) notified the company.
ITID-51841.purpose: Classifies undetected data breaches where discovery came only via notification from a third party, distinguishing external-first discovery from internal audit or dark web monitoring discovery.
scopeIncludes: Breach disclosed to the company via a customer, partner, security researcher, or law enforcement report
Extortion contact from the threat actor serving as the first indication of the breach
scopeExcludes: Discovery via the company's own unrelated security audit/assessment (ITID-51842)
Discovery via the company's own dark web monitoring program (ITID-51843)
ITID-51841.severity: Critical. Third-party-first discovery indicates a complete internal detection failure and typically means the exposure window is unknown and potentially extensive.
ITID-51841.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership and legal; the credibility and completeness of the third-party report must be assessed with urgency.
indicators: Inbound report from a customer, partner, researcher, or law enforcement describing a breach the company had no prior awareness of
Direct extortion contact referencing exfiltrated data
vectors: Any prior intrusion technique that evaded internal detection entirely; the vector is determined only during post-notification forensic investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient internal detection/logging coverage across the environment
Lack of a means for external researchers to responsibly disclose findings, delaying awareness
controls: Comprehensive logging and detection coverage across all critical systems
A published responsible-disclosure/bug-bounty channel to accelerate external reporting
Post-incident detection-gap review and remediation program
ITID-51841.detection: By definition, internal detection coverage failed for this incident; response focuses on rapid post-notification forensic reconstruction.
ITID-51841.response: Validate and scope the third-party report immediately, conduct full retrospective forensic investigation, and remediate the detection gap that allowed the breach to go unnoticed.
metrics: Estimated undetected dwell time prior to third-party notification
Time from notification to full scope determination
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
detections: N/A — detection failure is the defining characteristic of this leaf
ITID-51841.notes: Differentiated from siblings by discovery channel: an external party, rather than the company's own audit or monitoring program, first surfaced the breach.

playbook.name: Data Breach Discovered Only via Third-Party Notification
playbook.description: The organization first learned of a data breach through notification from a third party (customer, partner, security researcher, or law enforcement) rather than its own detection.

steps.title: Validate the third-party notification and establish initial credibility
steps.desc: Assess the credibility and specificity of the third-party report, and attempt to independently corroborate the claim against internal logs and systems.
steps.guidance: Treat third-party notifications seriously even when initial corroboration is difficult — the organization's own visibility gap is precisely why external notification occurred.
steps.outcome: An initial credibility assessment and any available corroborating internal evidence.
steps.abort: If the claim is thoroughly investigated and found to have no basis, document and close, but retain the record given reputational sensitivity.

steps.title: Reconstruct the undetected timeline and determine true scope from a position of incomplete visibility
steps.desc: Conduct forensic investigation starting from the third party's evidence, working backward and forward to reconstruct how long the breach existed, how it occurred, and its true scope — explicitly acknowledging that internal detection failed to catch it.
steps.guidance: Since internal telemetry did not catch this, do not assume internal logs give a complete picture; supplement with the third party's evidence, external threat intelligence, and where necessary an external forensics firm with experience reconstructing breaches from limited internal visibility.
steps.outcome: A best-available timeline and scope determination, with documented confidence levels and acknowledged gaps.

steps.title: Contain the identified breach mechanism immediately
steps.desc: Once the mechanism is identified from the reconstructed timeline, immediately contain it (revoke access, patch vulnerability, isolate systems) even while broader scoping continues.
steps.outcome: The known active exposure is stopped without waiting for full scope completion.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal, and engage the notifying third party for full detail-sharing
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal given the reputational and regulatory implications of external-first discovery, and formally engage the notifying third party to obtain all available evidence they hold.
steps.guidance: Discovery via external notification often draws additional regulatory scrutiny regarding the organization's own detection capability — factor this into the response posture.
steps.outcome: Full evidence exchange with the third party and executive/Legal oversight established.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause and close the detection gap that allowed it to go unnoticed
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability or misconfiguration, and specifically address why internal detection failed to catch the breach.
steps.outcome: The root cause is closed and the specific detection blind spot is addressed.

steps.title: Establish or expand a formal external vulnerability disclosure/reporting channel
steps.desc: Set up or improve a clear channel for external parties (customers, researchers, partners) to report suspected security issues, reducing time-to-notification for any future external discovery.
steps.outcome: Future external reports reach the security team faster and with clearer initial detail.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and validate environment integrity
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required (factoring in the delayed-discovery timeline for notification-clock purposes) and confirm the environment is clean.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on how delayed discovery affects notification-clock calculations under applicable law.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Conduct a detection-capability gap review
steps.desc: Document why internal detection missed the breach and drive concrete investment in the monitoring, logging, or alerting capability that would have caught it.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection-capability investments.

ITID-51842.def: A data breach that went undetected by real-time security monitoring and was instead uncovered as a byproduct of an unrelated internal security audit, penetration test, or compliance assessment.
ITID-51842.purpose: Classifies undetected data breaches discovered incidentally during an unrelated internal security audit or assessment, distinguishing internal-incidental discovery from external notification or proactive dark web monitoring.
scopeIncludes: Breach evidence found during a routine penetration test, compliance audit, or unrelated forensic review
Historical compromise indicators surfaced while investigating a separate, smaller incident
scopeExcludes: Discovery via third-party notification (ITID-51841)
Discovery via dedicated dark web monitoring (ITID-51843)
ITID-51842.severity: High-Critical, scaling with the dwell time revealed by the audit findings.
ITID-51842.priority: P1 upon confirmation that audit findings represent an actual historical breach rather than a benign misconfiguration.
ITID-51842.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal as soon as audit findings are confirmed to represent a genuine prior compromise.
indicators: Penetration test or audit uncovering evidence of prior unauthorized access (backdoors, unexplained accounts, anomalous historical logs)
Compliance assessment surfacing data-access patterns inconsistent with authorized activity
vectors: Any prior intrusion technique that evaded real-time detection; determined via forensic investigation following the audit finding
rootCauses: Insufficient real-time detection coverage relative to periodic audit depth
Infrequent security assessments allowing long undetected dwell time between audits
controls: Regular, sufficiently deep security audits and penetration testing
Real-time detection coverage improvements to close the gap audits currently fill
Historical log analysis capability supporting retrospective investigation
ITID-51842.detection: Real-time detection failed; periodic audit/assessment served as the effective (if delayed) detection mechanism.
ITID-51842.response: Treat the audit finding as a full incident: conduct retrospective forensic investigation, determine breach scope and duration, and remediate the real-time detection gap.
metrics: Estimated dwell time prior to audit discovery
Time between security audits/assessments
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
detections: N/A — real-time detection failure is the defining characteristic of this leaf
ITID-51842.notes: Differentiated from siblings by discovery channel: an internal, unrelated audit or assessment rather than an external party or dedicated dark web monitoring.

playbook.name: Data Breach Discovered During Unrelated Security Audit/Assessment
playbook.description: A data breach was discovered incidentally during an unrelated security audit, penetration test, or compliance assessment rather than through active monitoring.

steps.title: Validate the audit finding and separate it from the audit's original scope
steps.desc: Confirm the auditor's/assessor's finding represents an actual historical or ongoing breach, distinct from a theoretical vulnerability finding, and formally hand off from the audit process to incident response.
steps.guidance: Ensure a clean handoff — audit teams often are not equipped to run incident response, so transition ownership to IR promptly once a real breach is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed breach finding formally handed to the incident response process.
steps.abort: If the finding is a theoretical vulnerability with no evidence of actual exploitation, handle as a standard vulnerability-remediation item instead.

steps.title: Reconstruct the undetected timeline and determine true scope from a position of incomplete visibility
steps.desc: Conduct forensic investigation starting from the audit's finding to reconstruct how long the breach existed, how it occurred, and its true scope, since routine monitoring did not previously catch it.
steps.guidance: Do not assume the audit uncovered the full extent — use the finding as a starting point for a broader forensic sweep of related systems.
steps.outcome: A best-available timeline and scope determination, with documented confidence levels and acknowledged gaps.

steps.title: Contain the identified breach mechanism immediately
steps.desc: Once the mechanism is identified, immediately contain it (revoke access, patch vulnerability, isolate systems) even while broader scoping continues.
steps.outcome: The known active exposure is stopped without waiting for full scope completion.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations, factoring in that discovery occurred well after the likely breach start date.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause and close the monitoring gap that allowed it to go unnoticed
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability or misconfiguration, and specifically address why routine monitoring failed to catch the breach before this audit did.
steps.outcome: The root cause is closed and the specific monitoring blind spot is addressed.

steps.title: Increase frequency and scope of proactive security assessments
steps.desc: Expand the cadence and scope of internal/external security audits and penetration tests to reduce the window during which similar issues could go undetected.
steps.outcome: Future latent breaches are more likely to be caught sooner through proactive assessment.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and validate environment integrity
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required, factoring in the delayed-discovery timeline, and confirm the environment is clean.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Conduct a detection-capability gap review and expand ongoing assessment cadence
steps.desc: Document why routine monitoring missed the breach and drive investment in continuous monitoring/detection capability plus a more frequent proactive audit/assessment cadence going forward.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection and assessment-cadence improvements.

ITID-51843.def: A data breach that went undetected by internal security monitoring and was instead discovered when the company's dark web monitoring program identified company data being sold, dumped, or referenced on dark web forums or marketplaces.
ITID-51843.purpose: Classifies undetected data breaches discovered via the company's own dark web monitoring program, distinguishing proactive threat-intelligence-driven discovery from third-party notification or audit findings.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of company data listings via a dedicated dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring service
Analyst-driven dark web forum research surfacing evidence of a prior undetected breach
scopeExcludes: Discovery via direct third-party notification (ITID-51841)
Discovery via unrelated internal audit (ITID-51842)
Classification of the dark web listing itself as a post-breach monetization event (ITID-519xx Dark Web Data Dump group — cross-reference once the listing is confirmed)
ITID-51843.severity: Critical. Dark web discovery typically means the data has already begun circulating among threat actors.
ITID-51843.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed dark web listing of company data.
ITID-51843.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership and legal; assess whether the listing indicates active ongoing sale versus a one-time historical dump.
indicators: Dark web monitoring alert matching company domain, employee, or customer data patterns
Forum or marketplace listing referencing the company by name or a matching dataset sample
vectors: Any prior intrusion technique that evaded real-time detection; determined via forensic investigation following the dark web finding
rootCauses: Insufficient real-time detection coverage relative to the eventual dark web exposure
Reliance on dark web monitoring as a backstop rather than proactive detection
controls: Ongoing dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring service
Real-time detection improvements to close the gap dark web monitoring currently fills as a backstop
Rapid validation process for dark web data-listing alerts
ITID-51843.detection: Real-time internal detection failed; dark web monitoring served as the effective (if delayed) detection mechanism.
ITID-51843.response: Validate the authenticity and scope of the dark web listing, conduct retrospective forensic investigation into the original breach source, and initiate notification obligations.
metrics: Time from data theft (estimated) to dark web listing discovery
Number of breaches first discovered via dark web monitoring per year
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
ITID-51843.notes: Differentiated from siblings by discovery channel: proactive dark web monitoring rather than third-party notification or an unrelated audit. This leaf classifies the undetected-breach angle; the Dark Web Data Dump group (ITID-519xx) separately classifies the disclosure/monetization event once confirmed.

playbook.name: Data Breach Discovered via Dark Web Monitoring After the Fact
playbook.description: The organization discovered a historical data breach after its own data was found posted on dark web forums or marketplaces via a dark web monitoring service.

steps.title: Validate the dark web finding and assess data authenticity
steps.desc: Confirm the dark web monitoring alert reflects genuine, current company data rather than stale, recycled, or fabricated data from an unrelated source (a common tactic to inflate a listing's perceived value).
steps.guidance: Verify authenticity by sampling a subset of records against internal systems (e.g. confirming a handful of customer/employee records genuinely exist and match) without downloading or interacting with the full dataset from the dark web source itself.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity assessment of the posted data.
steps.abort: If the data is determined to be fabricated or unrelated to the organization, document and close, retaining the record for reference.

steps.title: Reconstruct the undetected source breach timeline and determine true scope
steps.desc: Working backward from the authenticated dark web data, conduct forensic investigation to identify the original source breach, how it occurred, when, and its full scope, since it went undetected until this after-the-fact discovery.
steps.guidance: The dataset's own contents/fields often reveal which internal system it originated from — use this to focus the forensic investigation rather than searching the entire environment.
steps.outcome: A best-available reconstruction of the source breach with documented confidence levels and acknowledged gaps.

steps.title: Contain the identified source vulnerability if still active
steps.desc: If the source breach's vulnerability or access path is determined to still be active/exploitable, contain it immediately (revoke access, patch, isolate) even while broader scoping continues.
steps.outcome: Any still-active exposure is stopped without waiting for full scope completion.
steps.abort: If forensic evidence indicates the source vulnerability was already closed through unrelated prior remediation, document this and proceed to scope/notification steps.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations, factoring in the significant delay between the likely breach date and this after-the-fact discovery.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Confirm remediation of the source vulnerability (not removal of the dark web dump)
steps.desc: Confirm the source vulnerability or access path is fully remediated; recognize that removing the data from the dark web marketplace itself is not a realistic eradication goal since takedown requests are rarely successful there.
steps.guidance: Focus eradication effort on preventing recurrence at the source rather than pursuing marketplace takedown, though a takedown/reporting request may still be filed opportunistically.
steps.outcome: The source vulnerability is confirmed closed, with the dark web posting acknowledged as outside the organization's ability to remove.

steps.title: Formalize dark web monitoring as an ongoing standing control
steps.desc: Establish or expand dark web monitoring coverage as a permanent, continuously operating control rather than an ad hoc capability, with defined alert-triage procedures.
steps.outcome: Future exposures are identified sooner through consistent, ongoing monitoring.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and monitor for exploitation of the exposed data
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required, and establish monitoring for fraud or further exploitation attempts using the exposed data (e.g. credential stuffing if credentials were included).
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and downstream-exploitation monitoring established.

steps.title: Conduct a detection-capability gap review and formalize dark web monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Document why the source breach went undetected until dark web discovery, and drive investment in internal detection plus ongoing dark web monitoring as a standing control.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection-capability investments.

ITID-51844.def: A catch-all classification for suspected or confirmed undetected data breaches where the discovery channel (third-party notification, internal audit, or dark web monitoring) has not yet been determined or does not cleanly fit a sibling category.
ITID-51844.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for undetected data breaches not yet attributed to a specific discovery channel.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of a previously undetected breach pending discovery-channel attribution
Breaches discovered via a channel not covered by the existing sibling leaves
scopeExcludes: Confirmed third-party notification discovery (ITID-51841)
Confirmed internal audit discovery (ITID-51842)
Confirmed dark web monitoring discovery (ITID-51843)
ITID-51844.severity: Critical by default given the undetected-breach context.
ITID-51844.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership and legal immediately; re-triage once the discovery channel is established.
indicators: Evidence of a previously undetected breach with discovery channel not yet determined
vectors: Unconfirmed at time of intake
rootCauses: To be determined during investigation
controls: Standard detection-gap remediation controls pending scoping
ITID-51844.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual specific category; this leaf itself has no dedicated detection signature.
ITID-51844.response: Rapidly determine the discovery channel and re-classify accordingly.
metrics: Time to re-triage from intake to discovery-channel-specific classification
sops: Critical Data Breach Crisis Management SOP
ITID-51844.notes: Intake/unclassified bucket only; every incident logged here should be re-triaged to ITID-51841, -51842, or -51843 as soon as the discovery channel is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Undetected Data Breach
playbook.description: A data breach was discovered through a delayed-discovery mechanism not otherwise classified, well after the underlying compromise occurred.

steps.title: Validate the discovery and establish initial credibility
steps.desc: Assess the credibility and specificity of the discovery, and attempt to corroborate the claim against internal logs and systems where available.
steps.guidance: Take the discovery seriously even where internal corroboration is initially difficult, given the discovery mechanism's inherent delay from the actual breach.
steps.outcome: An initial credibility assessment and any available corroborating internal evidence.
steps.abort: If thoroughly investigated and found to have no basis, document and close.

steps.title: Reconstruct the undetected timeline and determine true scope from a position of incomplete visibility
steps.desc: Conduct forensic investigation to reconstruct how long the breach existed, how it occurred, and its true scope, explicitly acknowledging that routine detection did not catch it.
steps.guidance: Engage external forensics support if internal capability or log retention is insufficient for the apparent scale and age of the breach.
steps.outcome: A best-available timeline and scope determination, with documented confidence levels and acknowledged gaps.

steps.title: Contain the identified breach mechanism immediately
steps.desc: Once the mechanism is identified, immediately contain it even while broader scoping continues.
steps.outcome: The known active exposure is stopped without waiting for full scope completion.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations, factoring in the delayed-discovery timeline.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause and close the detection gap that allowed it to go unnoticed
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability or misconfiguration, and specifically address why detection failed to catch the breach earlier.
steps.outcome: The root cause is closed and the specific detection blind spot is addressed.

steps.title: Increase frequency and scope of proactive security assessments
steps.desc: Expand the cadence and scope of internal/external security audits and penetration tests to reduce the window during which similar breaches could go undetected.
steps.outcome: Future latent breaches are more likely to be caught sooner through proactive assessment.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and validate environment integrity
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required, factoring in the delayed-discovery timeline, and confirm the environment is clean.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Conduct a detection-capability gap review
steps.desc: Document why detection missed the breach and drive concrete investment in the monitoring, logging, or alerting capability that would have caught it sooner.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked detection-capability investments.

ITID-51911.def: The identification of company or customer data being listed for sale (fixed-price or negotiated) on a dark web forum, marketplace, or broker channel, following a prior (possibly separately classified) data breach.
ITID-51911.purpose: Captures the discovery and classification of previously breached company data being actively offered for sale on a dark web forum or marketplace, as a post-breach monetization event distinct from the original intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a for-sale listing referencing company data on a known dark web marketplace or forum
Direct or indirect contact from a seller/broker offering company data for purchase
scopeExcludes: The underlying breach mechanism that produced the data (classify separately under the appropriate Credential Theft, Financial Data Breach, Insider-Driven, or APT-Driven leaf)
Free/no-cost public data dumps (ITID-51921)
Auction-format listings (ITID-51931)
Bundled credential-reuse packages (ITID-51941)
ITID-51911.severity: High. An active for-sale listing indicates the data is being actively marketed to potentially multiple buyers.
ITID-51911.priority: P1 upon confirmed identification of a for-sale listing containing verified company data.
ITID-51911.escalation: Escalate to legal, communications, and executive leadership; a confirmed listing typically accelerates notification and law-enforcement engagement.
indicators: Dark web monitoring alert identifying a listing with a company-matching data sample
Threat intelligence vendor report of a for-sale listing referencing the company
vectors: Prior confirmed or unconfirmed data breach later surfacing as a for-sale listing on a dark web marketplace
Data broker or reseller monetizing previously stolen records with no new intrusion
Insider-sourced data package offered for sale by a threat actor
rootCauses: Underlying breach that produced the dataset was never fully identified or remediated
Lack of ongoing dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring to detect listings promptly
Absence of a defined process for validating and responding to third-party data-for-sale claims
controls: Dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring for company-data listings
Rapid listing validation and takedown-request process where applicable
Coordinated legal/law-enforcement engagement upon confirmed listing
ITID-51911.detection: Dark web monitoring services provide the primary and often only detection surface for this classification.
ITID-51911.response: Validate the listing's authenticity and scope, initiate or accelerate breach notification if not already underway, and pursue takedown/law-enforcement action where feasible.
metrics: Number of confirmed for-sale listings identified per year
Time from listing discovery to notification action
ITID-51911.notes: This ITID and its sibling Dark Web Data Dump leaves classify the post-breach monetization/disclosure stage, not the underlying intrusion technique — mapped_mitre is intentionally empty. Always cross-reference the breach-mechanism leaf (e.g. ITID-511xx, -514xx, -517xx, or -518xx) responsible for the original theft.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Data-for-Sale Listing (Dark Web Dump Context)
playbook.description: The organization's data was discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace or forum.

steps.title: Triage the dark web monitoring alert and verify data authenticity
steps.desc: Review the dark web monitoring service alert for the listing and verify the sample data's authenticity against internal systems without engaging further with the seller.
steps.guidance: Verify authenticity by sampling a subset of records against internal systems; sellers commonly pad or fabricate listings to appear more valuable.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity assessment of the listed data.
steps.abort: If the data is determined to be fabricated or unrelated to the organization, document and close.

steps.title: Determine data scope, record count, and identify the source breach if not already known
steps.desc: Assess how many records and which data fields are included in the listing, and if the source breach is not already known/tracked, investigate to identify it using clues from the listing's content and metadata.
steps.guidance: The listing's field structure often matches a specific internal system's schema — use this to narrow the source investigation.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of listed data and, where possible, an identified or hypothesized source breach.

steps.title: Confirm or contain the source vulnerability if not already remediated
steps.desc: If the source breach is newly identified and its vulnerability is still active, contain it immediately (revoke access, patch, isolate).
steps.outcome: Any still-active source exposure is stopped.
steps.abort: If the source was already remediated through prior, unrelated action, document this and proceed.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations to affected customers/individuals and regulators based on the listing's scope.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Confirm source vulnerability remediation (not marketplace takedown)
steps.desc: Confirm the source vulnerability is fully remediated; recognize takedown requests against dark web marketplaces are usually unsuccessful and should not be relied upon as the primary remediation path.
steps.guidance: A takedown/reporting request may still be filed opportunistically where a reporting mechanism exists, but eradication focus should be on the source.
steps.outcome: The source vulnerability is confirmed closed.

steps.title: File takedown/reporting requests where a marketplace mechanism exists
steps.desc: Submit a takedown or abuse-reporting request through any available marketplace or hosting-provider mechanism, while treating the source-vulnerability remediation as the primary control.
steps.guidance: Expect a low success rate but pursue opportunistically as a low-cost secondary action.
steps.outcome: A takedown request is filed and tracked, with expectations set appropriately.
steps.abort: If no reporting mechanism exists for the marketplace, document this and skip.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and monitor for downstream exploitation
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required, and establish monitoring for fraud or further exploitation using the listed data (e.g. credential stuffing, identity theft).
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and downstream-exploitation monitoring established.

steps.title: Review dark web monitoring coverage and source-breach detection capability
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to dark web monitoring scope and the internal detection capability that should have caught the source breach.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked monitoring and detection improvements.

ITID-51921.def: The identification of company or customer data being publicly released at no cost on a dark web forum, paste site, or public dump repository, following a prior (possibly separately classified) data breach.
ITID-51921.purpose: Captures the discovery and classification of previously breached company data being released for free on the dark web or public dump sites, as a post-breach disclosure event distinct from the original intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a free public dump referencing company data on a forum, paste site, or dump repository
Data released as a reputational/retaliatory act rather than for financial gain
scopeExcludes: The underlying breach mechanism that produced the data (classify separately)
Data offered for sale (ITID-51911)
Auction-format listings (ITID-51931)
Bundled credential-reuse packages (ITID-51941)
ITID-51921.severity: Critical. Free public release maximizes exposure since no purchase barrier limits access to the data.
ITID-51921.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed identification of a free public dump containing company data.
ITID-51921.escalation: Escalate to legal, communications, and executive leadership immediately; free public dumps require the fastest possible notification given unrestricted access.
indicators: Dark web/paste-site monitoring alert identifying a free dump matching company data
Media or researcher report of a publicly released company dataset
vectors: Threat actor publicly releasing stolen data at no cost to maximize reputational damage or pressure a victim
Hacktivist-motivated free dump following a breach or defacement campaign
Failed extortion attempt resulting in the dataset being dumped rather than sold
rootCauses: Underlying breach that produced the dataset was never fully identified or remediated
Lack of ongoing dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring to detect free dumps promptly
Absence of a defined process for validating and responding to public data dump claims
controls: Dark web/paste-site monitoring for free public dumps referencing company data
Rapid takedown-request process for identified paste sites/repositories
Accelerated breach notification workflow for confirmed public dumps
ITID-51921.detection: Dark web and paste-site monitoring services provide the primary detection surface for this classification.
ITID-51921.response: Validate the dump's authenticity and scope, initiate immediate breach notification given unrestricted public access, and pursue takedown where feasible.
metrics: Number of confirmed free public dumps identified per year
Time from dump discovery to notification action
ITID-51921.notes: This ITID classifies the post-breach monetization/disclosure stage, not the underlying intrusion technique — mapped_mitre is intentionally empty. Always cross-reference the breach-mechanism leaf responsible for the original theft. Differentiated from ITID-51911 by the absence of a sale transaction — data is released freely, often for reputational or retaliatory reasons.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Free Data Dump (Dark Web Dump Context)
playbook.description: The organization's data was discovered posted for free on a dark web forum or paste site, rather than offered for sale.

steps.title: Triage the dark web monitoring alert and verify data authenticity
steps.desc: Review the dark web monitoring service alert for the free dump and verify the data's authenticity against internal systems.
steps.guidance: Free dumps are sometimes released by an actor after failing to sell the data, or as a reputational/retaliatory act — note any accompanying message from the poster as it may indicate motive.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity assessment of the dumped data.
steps.abort: If the data is determined to be fabricated or unrelated to the organization, document and close.

steps.title: Determine data scope, record count, and identify the source breach if not already known
steps.desc: Assess how many records and which data fields are included, and if the source breach is not already known/tracked, investigate to identify it using clues from the dump's content and metadata.
steps.guidance: A free dump often exposes the full dataset rather than a sample, giving a clearer picture of true scope than a for-sale listing's teaser sample.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of dumped data and, where possible, an identified or hypothesized source breach.

steps.title: Confirm or contain the source vulnerability if not already remediated
steps.desc: If the source breach is newly identified and its vulnerability is still active, contain it immediately.
steps.outcome: Any still-active source exposure is stopped.
steps.abort: If the source was already remediated, document and proceed.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations, noting that a free public dump generally increases urgency given immediate widespread accessibility.
steps.guidance: A freely posted dump is immediately accessible to a wide audience, which typically accelerates notification urgency compared to a paywalled for-sale listing.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked, expedited notification assessment.

steps.title: Confirm source vulnerability remediation (not removal of the public dump)
steps.desc: Confirm the source vulnerability is fully remediated; recognize that removing a freely posted dump from forums/paste sites is unlikely to succeed given its ease of mirroring, and should not be relied upon.
steps.guidance: File takedown/reporting requests with hosting platforms opportunistically, but treat source remediation as the true eradication goal.
steps.outcome: The source vulnerability is confirmed closed.

steps.title: File takedown/reporting requests with hosting platforms where possible
steps.desc: Submit takedown or abuse-reporting requests to the hosting platform/paste site where the dump was posted, while treating source-vulnerability remediation as the primary control.
steps.guidance: Expect the dump to be mirrored elsewhere regardless; pursue takedown as a low-cost secondary action.
steps.outcome: A takedown request is filed and tracked, with expectations set appropriately.
steps.abort: If no reporting mechanism exists, document this and skip.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and monitor for downstream exploitation
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required, and establish monitoring for fraud or exploitation given the data's free, wide accessibility.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and downstream-exploitation monitoring established.

steps.title: Review dark web monitoring coverage and source-breach detection capability
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to dark web/paste-site monitoring scope and the internal detection capability that should have caught the source breach.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked monitoring and detection improvements.

ITID-51931.def: The identification of company or customer data being offered via a competitive auction (bidding process, reserve price, deadline) on a dark web forum or marketplace, following a prior (possibly separately classified) data breach.
ITID-51931.purpose: Captures the discovery and classification of previously breached company data being offered via a dark web auction format, as a post-breach monetization event distinct from a fixed-price sale or free dump.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of an auction-format listing (bidding, reserve price, or deadline-based sale) referencing company data
Threat actor communications indicating an auction process is underway or planned for company data
scopeExcludes: The underlying breach mechanism that produced the data (classify separately)
Fixed-price for-sale listings (ITID-51911)
Free public dumps (ITID-51921)
Bundled credential-reuse packages (ITID-51941)
ITID-51931.severity: Critical. Auction dynamics can drive rapid escalation and multiple simultaneous prospective buyers, and often indicate the actor believes the data has high value.
ITID-51931.priority: P1 upon confirmed identification of an auction listing, with urgency tied to the auction deadline.
ITID-51931.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, executive leadership, and communications; the auction deadline creates a hard timeline for response decisions.
indicators: Dark web monitoring alert identifying an auction-format listing with a company-matching data sample
Threat actor communication referencing bid amounts, a reserve price, or an auction close date
vectors: Threat actor placing stolen dataset up for private auction to the highest bidder among criminal buyers
Time-limited auction listing used to create urgency and drive up sale price
Rebrokered dataset auctioned by a party distinct from the original intruder
rootCauses: Underlying breach that produced the dataset was never fully identified or remediated
Lack of ongoing dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring to detect auction listings promptly
Absence of a defined process for validating and responding to third-party data auction claims
controls: Dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring for auction-format listings
Pre-established extortion/ransom decision-making process to respond within the auction timeline
Coordinated legal/law-enforcement engagement upon confirmed listing
ITID-51931.detection: Dark web monitoring services provide the primary detection surface; auction deadlines demand rapid validation once found.
ITID-51931.response: Validate the listing and data sample authenticity urgently given the auction deadline, initiate or accelerate breach notification, and engage law enforcement regarding the extortion dynamic.
metrics: Number of confirmed auction listings identified per year
Time from listing discovery to notification/decision action
ITID-51931.notes: This ITID classifies the post-breach monetization/disclosure stage, not the underlying intrusion technique — mapped_mitre is intentionally empty. Always cross-reference the breach-mechanism leaf responsible for the original theft. Differentiated from ITID-51911 by the competitive bidding/deadline structure rather than a straightforward fixed-price sale.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Auctioned Data Listing (Dark Web Dump Context)
playbook.description: The organization's data was discovered listed in an auction format on a dark web marketplace, with the seller soliciting competing bids.

steps.title: Triage the dark web monitoring alert and verify data authenticity
steps.desc: Review the dark web monitoring service alert for the auction listing and verify the sample/teaser data's authenticity against internal systems.
steps.guidance: Auction listings often include a countdown or bidding deadline — note this timing as it may indicate urgency for a buyer to act, which can inform response prioritization.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity assessment of the auctioned data.
steps.abort: If the data is determined to be fabricated or unrelated to the organization, document and close.

steps.title: Determine data scope, record count, and identify the source breach if not already known
steps.desc: Assess how many records and which data fields are included in the auction listing, and if the source breach is not already known/tracked, investigate to identify it using clues from the listing's content and metadata.
steps.outcome: A defined scope of listed data and, where possible, an identified or hypothesized source breach.

steps.title: Confirm or contain the source vulnerability if not already remediated
steps.desc: If the source breach is newly identified and its vulnerability is still active, contain it immediately.
steps.outcome: Any still-active source exposure is stopped.
steps.abort: If the source was already remediated, document and proceed.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal for breach-notification assessment
steps.desc: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal/Compliance to assess breach-notification obligations, treating the auction's bidding deadline as a factor accelerating internal response urgency.
steps.outcome: Executive and Legal oversight established with a tracked notification assessment.

steps.title: Confirm source vulnerability remediation (not marketplace takedown)
steps.desc: Confirm the source vulnerability is fully remediated; recognize takedown requests against the auction marketplace are usually unsuccessful and should not be relied upon as the primary remediation path.
steps.guidance: A takedown/reporting request may still be filed opportunistically, but eradication focus should be on the source.
steps.outcome: The source vulnerability is confirmed closed.

steps.title: File takedown/reporting requests where a marketplace mechanism exists
steps.desc: Submit a takedown or abuse-reporting request through any available marketplace mechanism, while treating source-vulnerability remediation as the primary control.
steps.guidance: Expect a low success rate but pursue opportunistically before the auction concludes if possible.
steps.outcome: A takedown request is filed and tracked, with expectations set appropriately.
steps.abort: If no reporting mechanism exists, document this and skip.

steps.title: Execute required notifications and monitor for a winning bidder's exploitation
steps.desc: Complete regulatory/customer notifications as required, and establish monitoring for fraud or exploitation attempts once the auction concludes and a buyer obtains the data.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations met and downstream-exploitation monitoring established.

steps.title: Review dark web monitoring coverage and source-breach detection capability
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive improvements to dark web monitoring scope and the internal detection capability that should have caught the source breach.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked monitoring and detection improvements.

ITID-51941.def: The identification of company employee or customer credential pairs bundled into a combo list or credential-reuse package and distributed (sold or freely shared) on the dark web, following a prior (possibly separately classified) credential theft.
ITID-51941.purpose: Captures the discovery and classification of previously breached company-associated credentials being bundled and distributed as reusable credential packages (combo lists), as a post-breach monetization event distinct from the original credential theft.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a combo list / credential-reuse package containing company-domain email addresses paired with passwords
