Bundled credential packages assembled from this breach alongside data from unrelated third-party breaches
scopeExcludes: The underlying credential theft mechanism that produced the data (classify separately under the appropriate ITID-511xx Credential Theft leaf)
Fixed-price for-sale listings of non-credential data (ITID-51911)
Free public dumps of non-credential data (ITID-51921)
Auction-format listings (ITID-51931)
ITID-51941.severity: Critical. Credential-reuse packages directly enable follow-on credential-stuffing attacks against the company and other services.
ITID-51941.priority: P1 upon confirmed identification of a combo list containing company-domain credentials.
ITID-51941.escalation: Escalate to identity security and legal immediately; treat as an active threat to all accounts using the exposed credential pairs, including reused passwords elsewhere.
indicators: Dark web/combo-list monitoring alert identifying company-domain email addresses in a credential package
Spike in credential-stuffing attempts against company systems following a known combo-list release
vectors: Combolist or credential-stuffing package compiled from prior breaches offered for resale
Aggregated username/password dump repackaged from multiple historical sources
Credential package advertised specifically for use in automated credential-stuffing attacks against other services
rootCauses: Underlying breach(es) that produced the credentials were never fully identified or remediated
Widespread password reuse across services amplifying the value and impact of the package
Lack of ongoing dark web/threat-intelligence monitoring to detect credential package listings promptly
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Dark web/combo-list monitoring for company-domain credential exposure
Automated forced-reset workflow triggered by confirmed combo-list identification
Breached-password screening at login to block reuse of listed credentials
ITID-51941.detection: Dark web/combo-list monitoring services provide the primary detection surface; authentication-anomaly monitoring provides a secondary signal once the package circulates.
ITID-51941.response: Force password resets for all affected accounts, enforce MFA, and monitor for a subsequent spike in credential-stuffing attempts referencing the package.
metrics: Number of company-domain credentials identified in combo lists per year
Time from combo-list discovery to forced reset completion
ITID-51941.notes: This ITID classifies the post-breach monetization/disclosure stage, not the underlying intrusion technique — mapped_mitre is intentionally empty. Always cross-reference the breach-mechanism leaf responsible for the original credential theft (e.g. ITID-51111, -51121, -51131, -51141).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Credentials Reuse Package Listing (Dark Web Dump Context)
playbook.description: The organization's user credentials were discovered packaged and listed on a dark web marketplace or forum, typically compiled from credential-stuffing-ready combo lists.

steps.title: Triage the dark web monitoring alert and verify credential authenticity
steps.desc: Review the dark web monitoring alert for the credentials package and verify a sample of the listed username/password (or hash) pairs against internal systems.
steps.guidance: Combo lists are frequently aggregated from multiple unrelated breaches (credential recycling) — verify these are genuinely the organization's current, valid credentials rather than old, already-rotated, or third-party-sourced entries.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticity assessment of the listed credentials.
steps.abort: If the credentials are determined to be stale/already-rotated or unrelated to the organization, document and close.

steps.title: Determine the number of valid, still-active accounts and identify the source if not already known
steps.desc: Cross-reference the listed credentials against active accounts to determine how many remain valid, and if the source breach is not already known/tracked, investigate using clues from the package's content and metadata.
steps.outcome: A defined list of currently valid, exposed accounts and, where possible, an identified or hypothesized source.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions for all valid exposed accounts
steps.desc: Immediately reset credentials and terminate active sessions for every account confirmed still valid within the listed package.
steps.outcome: The listed credentials can no longer be used to access the affected accounts.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal/Compliance for notification assessment and enforce MFA on affected accounts
steps.desc: Escalate to Legal/Compliance to assess notification obligations, and enforce MFA on affected accounts to prevent any residual or future stuffing attempts using the same credentials from succeeding.
steps.outcome: Notification assessment underway and MFA enforced on affected accounts.

steps.title: Confirm or investigate the source of the credential compilation
steps.desc: If the source of the credential exposure is identified as a still-active internal vulnerability, remediate it; recognize takedown requests against the marketplace listing are usually unsuccessful.
steps.guidance: If the credentials appear recycled from a known third-party breach unrelated to the organization's own systems, document this and focus remediation on breach-password-blocklisting rather than searching for a nonexistent internal source.
steps.outcome: Either the internal source is closed, or the credentials are confirmed as externally-sourced reuse with appropriate blocklisting deployed.

steps.title: Deploy continuous credential-exposure monitoring against breach-compilation feeds
steps.desc: Subscribe to or expand automated monitoring of breach-compilation and combo-list feeds to catch future exposure of company credentials faster.
steps.outcome: Future credential exposure in dark web packages is detected sooner.

steps.title: Notify affected users and monitor for stuffing attempts using the package
steps.desc: Notify affected users to encourage unique password practices going forward, and monitor authentication logs for stuffing attempts using the listed credential package.
steps.outcome: Users notified and monitoring established for exploitation attempts.

steps.title: Review credential hygiene enforcement and dark web monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of breach-password blocklisting, mandatory MFA, and continued dark web credential-monitoring coverage.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with tracked credential-hygiene and monitoring improvements.

ITID-52111.def: A form of insider espionage in which an individual applies for and obtains legitimate employment as a deliberate placement by a competitor, criminal group, or state actor, with the intent of using their resulting access to collect or exfiltrate information over time.
ITID-52111.purpose: Captures the discovery that an employee was placed inside the organization by an external party specifically to gain insider access, before that person was ever hired.
scopeIncludes: An employee later confirmed to have been directed or sponsored by an external organization prior to applying
A hire whose background, references, or prior employment history is found to have been fabricated to secure the role
Discovery of pre-employment contact with a handler or sponsoring organization tied to the hiring decision
scopeExcludes: An existing, legitimately hired employee who is recruited or turned after the fact (ITID-52112)
Ordinary resume embellishment with no espionage intent
ITID-52111.severity: High to Critical, reflecting that the individual's access was designed from the outset for exfiltration and may have been in place long enough to reach broad systems.
ITID-52111.priority: P1. Treat as an active, sustained compromise of trust rather than a single event.
ITID-52111.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk, HR, legal, and executive leadership; involve law enforcement and counter-intelligence contacts where a state actor or organized criminal sponsor is suspected. Preserve access logs before any account action is taken.
indicators: Background-check inconsistencies discovered after hire
Access patterns inconsistent with the employee's stated role from very early in tenure
Unexplained contact with a known competitor or foreign entity discovered during an unrelated investigation
vectors: Fabricated resume/references used to pass hiring screening
Targeted application to a role known to carry sensitive access
rootCauses: Insufficient background verification for sensitive-access roles
No ongoing re-verification of employee-provided credentials after hire
controls: Enhanced background screening for sensitive-access roles
Staged/least-privilege access provisioning for new hires with review checkpoints
ITID-52111.detection: Human-intelligence and pre-employment placement activity has no technical detection signature; discovery typically comes from HR investigation, insider-risk behavioral analytics, or counter-intelligence referral rather than SOC tooling.
ITID-52111.response: Investigate the full scope of access and data touched since hire date before any containment action; coordinate account/access actions with HR and legal to avoid tipping off a sponsoring organization.
metrics: Time from suspicion to confirmed determination
Scope of data/systems accessed during tenure
detections: Insider risk behavioral analytics baseline deviation
ITID-52111.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels.

playbook.name: Insider Planted by External Organization Prior to Hire
playbook.description: An employee is discovered to have been deliberately placed into the organization by an external competitor, nation-state, or criminal actor prior to being hired, for the purpose of long-term intelligence access.

steps.title: Corroborate the pre-employment placement indicator
steps.desc: Security and HR jointly review the triggering indicator (e.g., inconsistent employment history, undisclosed prior affiliation, handler contact, or a tip from law enforcement/partner agency) that suggests the individual was placed rather than organically hired.
steps.guidance: Do not rely on a single data point. Cross-check background-check records, references, and any discrepancies in the original application against current findings. Loop in Legal before any employee-facing action.
steps.outcome: A documented, evidence-based assessment of whether the placement indicator is credible enough to warrant a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If the indicator cannot be corroborated with at least two independent sources, downgrade to monitoring rather than opening a full investigation.
steps.tool: HR background-check archive; case management system

steps.title: Scope systems and data accessed by the individual
steps.desc: Determine every system, repository, and dataset the employee has accessed since hire, with emphasis on access outside their normal job function.
steps.guidance: Pull identity and access management (IAM) logs, VPN logs, and data loss prevention (DLP) alerts for the full tenure of employment, not just recent activity.
steps.outcome: A timeline of access showing what may already have been exposed to the external organization.

steps.title: Coordinate covert monitoring before any overt action
steps.desc: Legal, HR, and Security decide whether to quietly restrict access while preserving the appearance of normalcy, to avoid alerting the individual or their handler before evidence-gathering and, where applicable, law-enforcement coordination is complete.
steps.guidance: Premature overt action can destroy evidentiary value and tip off the sponsoring organization. Weigh counter-intelligence value of continued discreet observation against ongoing exposure risk.
steps.outcome: An agreed containment posture (covert restriction vs. immediate lockout) approved by Legal and executive leadership.
steps.abort: If active, ongoing exfiltration of highly sensitive data is detected, escalate immediately to overt containment regardless of counter-intelligence value.

steps.title: Restrict access to sensitive systems and data
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege restrictions or silent access revocation to the highest-sensitivity systems the individual can reach, using change-management cover stories where a covert approach was chosen.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with IT to avoid raising suspicion; use routine-looking access reviews as cover where possible.
steps.outcome: Sensitive systems are no longer reachable by the individual without detection.

steps.title: Coordinate law-enforcement and Legal-led termination process
steps.desc: Legal, HR, and (where applicable) law enforcement or national counter-intelligence authorities determine the process for separating the individual, including timing that preserves any ongoing investigation.
steps.guidance: Follow legal counsel on any criminal referral. Preserve all evidence via approved chain-of-custody procedures before termination.
steps.outcome: A coordinated separation plan that does not compromise a parallel law-enforcement investigation.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Reassess and harden pre-employment screening controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen background-check depth, reference verification, and onboarding data-access provisioning tied to role sensitivity.
steps.guidance: Focus on roles with access to strategic, competitive, or classified data.
steps.outcome: Updated screening standards reducing the likelihood of a repeat placement.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Conduct after-action review with Security, HR, Legal, and executive leadership
steps.desc: Document the full timeline, indicators missed, and control gaps, and brief executive leadership and the board (or audit committee) as appropriate given the counter-intelligence sensitivity.
steps.guidance: Restrict distribution of the after-action report to a need-to-know list given the sensitivity of counter-intelligence findings.
steps.outcome: A documented, access-restricted after-action report with concrete control improvements.

ITID-52112.def: A form of insider espionage in which an existing employee, with no prior placement intent, is recruited, turned, or otherwise brought under the direction of an external handler during the course of their employment.
ITID-52112.purpose: Captures the case of a legitimately hired, previously trustworthy employee who is later recruited or coerced by an external party into acting as an insider source.
scopeIncludes: An employee confirmed to be providing information to an external party they were not sponsored by at hire
A long-tenured employee whose behavior changes coincide with contact from a competitor, foreign entity, or intermediary
scopeExcludes: An employee planted by an external organization before hire (ITID-52111)
An employee acting purely out of personal grievance with no external handler (see Disgruntled Insider Leaks, ITID-5263x)
ITID-52112.severity: High to Critical, scaled to the sensitivity of the data the employee could access and the length of time the recruitment is believed to have been active.
ITID-52112.priority: P1 once recruitment is confirmed or strongly suspected.
ITID-52112.escalation: Escalate to insider risk, HR, legal, and executive leadership; involve law enforcement or counter-intelligence contacts where a state or organized-crime handler is suspected. Coordinate timing of any access change to avoid alerting the employee before evidence is preserved.
indicators: Sudden change in an employee's data access patterns or working hours with no role change
Unexplained financial improvement
Contact with a known competitor, broker, or foreign entity revealed through other investigative means
vectors: Approach via professional networking, industry events, or personal relationships
Financial or ideological inducement offered over time
rootCauses: Lack of ongoing insider-risk monitoring for privileged users after initial onboarding
No periodic re-affirmation of confidentiality/conflict-of-interest obligations
controls: Continuous insider-risk monitoring for privileged/sensitive-access roles
Periodic conflict-of-interest and outside-relationship attestations
ITID-52112.detection: No direct technical detection signature for the recruitment itself; detection relies on behavioral analytics flagging anomalous data access alongside HR/insider-risk referral.
ITID-52112.response: Establish full scope of data exposure across the suspected recruitment period; involve legal before confronting or removing the employee's access.
metrics: Number of confirmed recruitment cases per year
Mean time to detect from recruitment onset
detections: User behavior analytics anomalous access alerting
ITID-52112.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels.

playbook.name: Existing Employee Recruited/Turned by External Handler
playbook.description: A previously trusted employee is found to have been recruited or 'turned' by an external handler after hire, and is providing ongoing access or information to that outside party.

steps.title: Assess the turning indicator
steps.desc: Review the behavioral, technical, or human-source indicator suggesting the employee has been recruited (e.g., anomalous data access, unexplained financial change, suspicious travel, or a colleague report).
steps.guidance: Combine HR, Legal, and Security perspectives before treating the indicator as credible; avoid acting on a single anomalous event.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of whether a formal covert investigation is warranted.
steps.abort: If insufficient, place the employee under a low-key monitoring watchlist rather than opening a full case.

steps.title: Establish a discreet monitoring baseline
steps.desc: With Legal approval, establish enhanced but covert monitoring of the employee's account and data-access activity to characterize the scope of compromise.
steps.guidance: Ensure monitoring complies with employment law and any works-council/union requirements in the relevant jurisdiction.
steps.outcome: A clear picture of what data or access has been or is being provided to the handler.

steps.title: Coordinate with Legal and law enforcement before any overt action
steps.desc: Determine whether to pursue a quiet, evidence-preserving containment (restricting access without alerting the employee) or immediate access revocation, weighing investigative and prosecutorial value.
steps.guidance: A premature lockout can destroy the opportunity to identify the handler or the full scope of compromise; consult Legal and, where a criminal referral is likely, law enforcement before acting.
steps.outcome: An approved containment strategy balancing exposure risk against investigative value.

steps.title: Limit further data exposure
steps.desc: Restrict or silently revoke the employee's access to the most sensitive systems and data identified in the scoping step.
steps.guidance: Use routine access-review cover stories to avoid tipping off the employee where a covert approach is chosen.
steps.outcome: Material reduction in the employee's ability to exfiltrate further data.

steps.title: Execute coordinated separation and evidence preservation
steps.desc: Legal and HR execute termination or suspension in coordination with any law-enforcement process, preserving forensic evidence under chain of custody.
steps.guidance: Follow Legal's direction on timing to avoid prejudicing any criminal case.
steps.outcome: Employee separated with all evidence preserved and access fully revoked.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Review and remediate exposed data and relationships
steps.desc: Assess what information was compromised and notify affected internal stakeholders, partners, or customers as legally required.
steps.guidance: Coordinate notification timing and content with Legal and Communications.
steps.outcome: Affected parties are notified where required and exposure is documented for risk assessment.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Conduct restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Document indicators, response timeline, and control gaps in a distribution-limited report to executive leadership and the board/audit committee as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Actionable recommendations to reduce insider-recruitment risk (e.g., financial-stress monitoring programs, enhanced periodic reinvestigation for sensitive roles).

ITID-52113.def: An insider espionage case distinguished by the specific communication method used to transfer information to a handler: a dead-drop, steganographic channel, or other covert communication mechanism designed to avoid detection, rather than direct or obvious contact.
ITID-52113.purpose: Captures an insider's use of covert communication tradecraft — digital or physical dead-drops — to pass information to an external handler while evading normal monitoring.
scopeIncludes: Use of a public web service, forum post, or shared document as a covert message/dead-drop resolver
Use of a personal or anonymous account to relay data outside normal, monitored channels
Physical dead-drop combined with digital tasking or acknowledgment
scopeExcludes: Insider recruitment/placement without a confirmed covert-communication method (ITID-52111/52112)
Ordinary personal email/cloud-storage use with no evidence of handler tasking
ITID-52113.severity: Critical. The use of tradecraft-grade covert communication indicates a sophisticated, likely externally-directed operation.
ITID-52113.priority: P1, with immediate involvement of counter-intelligence-capable resources.
ITID-52113.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk, legal, and law enforcement/counter-intelligence liaison; preserve network and endpoint evidence of the communication channel before any user notification or access change.
indicators: Recurring visits to an obscure or unrelated public web page/service with no business justification
Use of steganography or encoded content in otherwise innocuous-looking posts or files
Pattern of access immediately preceding or following visits to the covert channel
vectors: Dead-drop resolver via a public web service (e.g., pastebin-style site, social media post, cloud document) used to signal or relay tasking
Encoded/steganographic content embedded in innocuous files or images
rootCauses: Limited monitoring of outbound web traffic to low-reputation or single-purpose destinations
No content-based detection for anomalous data embedded in outbound files
mitreTechniques: T1102.001 Web Service: Dead Drop Resolver
controls: Web proxy/DNS monitoring for anomalous or single-purpose destinations
DLP inspection of outbound content for encoded/steganographic payloads
ITID-52113.detection: The covert-communication mechanism itself is a genuine technical detection surface, unlike most insider-recruitment activity; network and content-inspection telemetry can surface it.
ITID-52113.response: Map the full communication history through the covert channel before acting; coordinate with legal/law enforcement on evidence handling given likely criminal proceedings.
metrics: Number of covert-channel indicators identified per investigation
Time from first covert-channel indicator to confirmed case
ITID-52113.notes: Unlike most leaves in this Tier-4 group, the covert-communication method itself gives the SOC a real technical detection surface (T1102.001); the underlying recruitment/handling relationship remains a human-intelligence matter.

playbook.name: Insider Espionage Using Dead-Drop/Covert Communication with Handler
playbook.description: An insider is found to be using covert, non-standard communication methods (dead drops, encrypted side-channels, steganographic messages) to relay information to an external handler, avoiding normal monitored channels.

steps.title: Identify the covert communication channel
steps.desc: Investigate the technical or physical indicator of covert communication (e.g., unexplained physical meetings, unusual encrypted traffic, anomalous file metadata suggesting steganography, or use of unsanctioned messaging apps).
steps.guidance: Involve digital forensics and, if physical dead drops are suspected, physical security/executive-protection teams.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of the covert channel type and a preliminary sense of its duration and content.
steps.abort: If the channel cannot be confirmed, maintain passive monitoring rather than escalate.

steps.title: Map the scope of information likely transmitted
steps.desc: Reconstruct, from available access and file logs, what information the insider had access to during the period the covert channel was active.
steps.guidance: Correlate access timestamps with observed communication events to bound the scope of likely compromise.
steps.outcome: A defensible estimate of what has been exposed to the handler.

steps.title: Coordinate covert surveillance with Legal and law enforcement
steps.desc: Because dead-drop/handler tradecraft strongly suggests a sophisticated, potentially foreign-directed operation, decide jointly with Legal and law enforcement whether to continue quiet observation to identify the handler network before acting overtly.
steps.guidance: This is high-value counter-intelligence territory; premature action can burn a law-enforcement opportunity to identify a broader network.
steps.outcome: A documented, jointly approved surveillance and containment plan.
steps.abort: Escalate to immediate overt containment if evidence indicates imminent, high-impact data loss (e.g., pending release of highly classified or safety-critical material).

steps.title: Limit the insider's ongoing access footprint
steps.desc: Silently narrow the insider's access to reduce further exposure while preserving normal appearance of their role.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT to avoid detectable changes that could alert the insider or handler.
steps.outcome: Reduced access footprint with no detectable change from the insider's perspective.

steps.title: Execute coordinated takedown with law enforcement
steps.desc: Once the investigation and any law-enforcement process are ready, execute a coordinated separation and evidence-seizure action.
steps.guidance: Follow the law-enforcement/Legal timeline precisely; do not act unilaterally ahead of an agreed operation.
steps.outcome: Insider separated, devices and evidence secured under chain of custody, handler network exposure assessed.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Assess and remediate compromised information and relationships
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of exposed data and notify affected business units, partners, or government authorities as required.
steps.outcome: Documented exposure assessment and required notifications completed.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Conduct restricted counter-intelligence after-action review
steps.desc: Produce a tightly access-controlled report covering tradecraft observed, detection gaps, and recommended monitoring improvements for covert-channel detection.
steps.outcome: Improved detection capability for covert/dead-drop-style insider communication.

ITID-52114.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of insider espionage — an internal actor suspected of providing information to an external party — pending sufficient investigation to determine whether it was a pre-employment plant, an in-tenure recruitment, or uses covert tradecraft.
ITID-52114.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected insider espionage that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial insider-espionage suspicion prior to determining the recruitment method
Cases where evidence is inconclusive on whether the insider was planted or turned
scopeExcludes: Any case where the recruitment timing or communication method has already been established (ITID-52111/52112/52113)
ITID-52114.severity: High pending triage; re-assess once the specific mechanism is established.
ITID-52114.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify to a specific leaf as facts develop.
ITID-52114.escalation: Escalate to insider risk and legal on initial suspicion; do not wait for full classification before preserving evidence.
indicators: General insider-risk referral naming suspected external data disclosure
Anomalous access flagged by behavioral analytics with an as-yet-unclear external nexus
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Insider risk case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52114.detection: None specific; this leaf exists to route suspected cases for investigation before technical or human-intelligence detection surfaces are known.
ITID-52114.response: Open a formal insider-threat investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf as soon as the recruitment mechanism is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
detections: Insider risk behavioral analytics baseline deviation
ITID-52114.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Insider Espionage group; reclassify promptly once the recruitment mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Insider Espionage
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of insider espionage, where an employee is suspected of providing internal information or access to an external party for reasons not yet attributed to a specific method.

steps.title: Validate the initial insider-espionage indicator
steps.desc: Security and HR review the triggering report or anomaly (e.g., DLP alert, tip, unusual access pattern) to determine if it plausibly indicates espionage rather than routine policy violation.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal early given the sensitivity and potential for criminal referral.
steps.outcome: A documented decision to open a formal insider-threat investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, close as a routine policy matter with HR follow-up.

steps.title: Scope access and behavior of the individual
steps.desc: Review the employee's system access, data movement, and behavioral history to characterize what may have been exposed and to whom.
steps.guidance: Pull IAM, DLP, and email/communication logs for a reasonable historical window.
steps.outcome: A working hypothesis of scope and possible recipient/motive.

steps.title: Decide covert vs. overt containment approach
steps.desc: Legal and Security determine whether quiet access restriction or immediate suspension best preserves both evidence and business interests.
steps.outcome: An approved containment approach.

steps.title: Restrict access to sensitive systems
steps.desc: Apply access restrictions to the systems and data at risk, using discreet methods if a covert approach was chosen.
steps.outcome: Further data exposure is materially reduced.

steps.title: Execute separation and evidence preservation
steps.desc: HR and Legal execute the appropriate personnel action while preserving forensic evidence under chain of custody.
steps.outcome: Individual separated or otherwise addressed with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and notify affected parties
steps.desc: Determine what data was exposed and complete any required internal or external notifications.
steps.outcome: Exposure documented and notifications completed where required.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Complete after-action review
steps.desc: Document findings, response timeline, and control improvements in a distribution-limited report.
steps.outcome: Actionable recommendations to reduce future insider-espionage risk.

ITID-52121.def: A form of corporate espionage in which a competitor engages an external operative — a contractor, private investigator, or intermediary — to obtain proprietary or confidential information, rather than acting through its own personnel.
ITID-52121.purpose: Captures competitor-directed espionage carried out through a third party hired specifically to obtain the target's confidential information.
scopeIncludes: A confirmed or suspected contractor/consultant engagement whose true purpose was intelligence collection for a competitor
Use of an intermediary to approach current or former employees on a competitor's behalf
scopeExcludes: A competitor's own employee acting directly (see Poached Employee, ITID-52122)
Lawful competitive intelligence gathering using only public information (see OSINT Exploitation, ITID-5253x)
ITID-52121.severity: High. Third-party operatives are often used precisely because they provide the sponsoring competitor with deniability, complicating attribution and response.
ITID-52121.priority: P1 upon confirmation of a hired-operative arrangement.
ITID-52121.escalation: Escalate to legal (trade secret/competitive tort exposure), executive leadership, and law enforcement where the conduct is criminal (e.g., unauthorized access, bribery of an employee).
indicators: An individual with no legitimate business relationship persistently seeking access to specific proprietary information
A departing/former employee approached by an unfamiliar consultant or 'recruiter' asking pointed technical questions
Contract engagement whose scope does not match the actual activity observed
vectors: Sham consulting/vendor engagement used as pretext for access
Direct approach to current employees by an operative posing as a recruiter or journalist
rootCauses: Insufficient vetting of third-party contractors granted facility or system access
No process to validate the legitimacy of unsolicited 'consulting' or 'research' inquiries
controls: Third-party/contractor vetting and access-scoping standard
Employee awareness training on pretexting and unsolicited approaches
ITID-52121.detection: Primarily a legal and physical/personnel-security detection surface; no reliable technical signal unless the operative also attempts a technical intrusion, which would be tracked under the relevant technical ITID leaf.
ITID-52121.response: Document the full pattern of contact and requests; involve legal early to preserve options for civil or criminal action against the sponsoring competitor.
metrics: Number of suspicious third-party engagements identified per year
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52121.notes: Engagement of an external human operative is primarily a personnel-security and legal matter; no single ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies at this classification level — technical follow-through by the operative, if any, is tracked under the specific technical ITID leaf involved.

playbook.name: Competitor-Directed Corporate Espionage via Hired Third-Party Operative
playbook.description: A competitor is found to have hired a third-party operative (private investigator, contractor, or intermediary firm) to obtain confidential competitive information about the organization.

steps.title: Corroborate the third-party operative indicator
steps.desc: Investigate the initial signal (suspicious contact attempts, an approach to an employee, or a discovered contractor with undisclosed competitor ties) with Security and Legal.
steps.guidance: Third-party operative cases often surface through an employee reporting a suspicious approach; treat employee reports as a primary source and protect the reporting employee's confidentiality.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of whether a competitor-directed operation is underway.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, log and monitor rather than escalate.

steps.title: Identify targeted individuals, data, and access vectors
steps.desc: Determine which employees, systems, or facilities the operative targeted or attempted to access.
steps.guidance: Interview any employees who were approached, with HR/Legal support, and review physical/badge and IT logs for related anomalies.
steps.outcome: A clear picture of the operative's targeting scope.

steps.title: Alert and protect targeted employees
steps.desc: Notify and brief employees who were or may be targeted, providing guidance on how to handle further contact and reporting channels.
steps.guidance: Coordinate messaging with Legal to avoid tipping off the operative prematurely if a law-enforcement or civil action is contemplated.
steps.outcome: Targeted employees are aware, protected, and cooperating with the investigation.

steps.title: Restrict exposure of at-risk information
steps.desc: Tighten access controls or physical security around the specific data or facilities the operative appears to be targeting.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of successful further collection.

steps.title: Pursue legal action against the operative and sponsoring competitor
steps.desc: Legal evaluates civil (trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference) and/or criminal referral options against the operative and, where evidence supports it, the competitor.
steps.guidance: Preserve all evidence of the approach and any related communications under legal hold.
steps.outcome: A determined legal course of action, including possible cease-and-desist or litigation.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Reinforce protections for at-risk personnel and information
steps.desc: Implement longer-term protective measures for employees in externally visible or high-exposure roles, and reassess information classification for the targeted data.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of repeat targeting.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Brief leadership and update employee awareness training
steps.desc: Document the incident and update security-awareness training to help employees recognize and report competitor-directed approaches.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational resilience to future third-party operative attempts.

ITID-52122.def: A form of corporate espionage in which an employee, in the course of leaving to join a competitor, copies or retains confidential or proprietary information for the new employer's benefit.
ITID-52122.purpose: Captures the case of a departing employee who takes proprietary information to a competitor upon joining them.
scopeIncludes: Bulk download or transfer of proprietary files by an employee shortly before resignation
Confirmed use of retained former-employer material by the new (competitor) employer
scopeExcludes: A competitor's use of a hired external operative with no employment relationship (ITID-52121)
Ordinary departure with no evidence of data retention or transfer
ITID-52122.severity: High, reflecting direct trade-secret loss to a named competitor with clear commercial harm.
ITID-52122.priority: P1 during the departure window; time-sensitive given the risk of immediate use by the competitor.
ITID-52122.escalation: Escalate to legal immediately — this is frequently addressed through civil trade-secret litigation and injunctive relief, which depends on rapid evidence preservation.
indicators: Spike in downloads, printing, or cloud-sync activity in the weeks before resignation
Access to files unrelated to the employee's current project shortly before departure
External storage device or personal cloud account used near the resignation date
vectors: Mass download to USB or personal cloud storage before resignation
Emailing files to a personal account under the guise of 'personal records'
rootCauses: No offboarding-triggered review of pre-departure data activity
DLP not tuned to flag bulk exfiltration in the pre-resignation window
mitreTechniques: T1074.001 Data Staged: Local Data Staging
controls: Departure/offboarding-triggered DLP review
Egress monitoring for personal cloud storage and webmail
ITID-52122.detection: Strong technical detection surface: DLP, endpoint, and cloud-access logs typically capture the bulk-download and exfiltration activity directly.
ITID-52122.response: Preserve forensic evidence of pre-departure activity before the employee's last day where possible; coordinate with legal on cease-and-desist or injunction options against the new employer.
metrics: Number of departure-window exfiltration cases per quarter
Percentage of departures with a completed pre-departure DLP review
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52122.notes: This is a lone-child-adjacent, technically observable leaf; cross-reference the fuller IP-theft treatments of departing-employee data theft in the Data Breaches domain (ITID-51311/51321/51331 series) within this same ITID-50000 Tier-1 for detection detail that is not duplicated here.

playbook.name: Competitor Espionage via Poached Employee Bringing Stolen IP
playbook.description: A departing employee is discovered to have taken confidential or proprietary information with them to a competitor, or a newly hired employee is discovered to have brought a competitor's stolen IP into the organization.

steps.title: Confirm data exfiltration by the departing/incoming employee
steps.desc: Review offboarding or onboarding forensic triggers (e.g., mass file downloads before resignation, USB transfers, personal cloud uploads, or discovery of competitor files on company systems) to confirm data movement occurred.
steps.guidance: Standard offboarding forensic review (last 30-90 days of activity) is the primary detection point; ensure this is a routine, consistently applied practice, not selective.
steps.outcome: Confirmed evidence of data taken or brought in, with a defined scope.
steps.abort: If no evidence is found, close the case but retain findings per data-retention policy.

steps.title: Classify the sensitivity and ownership of the data involved
steps.desc: Work with the relevant business unit and Legal to determine whether the data is a protectable trade secret and quantify its competitive value.
steps.outcome: A documented classification supporting subsequent legal action.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
steps.desc: Immediately image relevant devices/accounts and issue a legal hold to prevent further data movement or destruction.
steps.guidance: Act quickly — trade-secret cases often turn on evidence preserved in the first 24-48 hours.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved and admissible.

steps.title: Revoke access and secure returned/incoming devices
steps.desc: Revoke all system access for a departing employee immediately upon confirmation, or quarantine devices/media brought in by an incoming employee pending review.
steps.outcome: No further data can move in or out via the individual's access.

steps.title: Pursue cease-and-desist and/or litigation against employee and competitor
steps.desc: Legal sends a cease-and-desist to the employee and, where warranted, the competitor, and evaluates trade-secret litigation or injunctive relief.
steps.outcome: Formal legal action initiated to recover or destroy the stolen IP and prevent its use.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Verify destruction/return of stolen data and reassess exposure
steps.desc: Confirm, where legally achievable, that stolen data has been returned or destroyed, and assess ongoing competitive exposure.
steps.outcome: Documented resolution of the data-exposure risk.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Strengthen offboarding/onboarding IP-protection controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and improve standard offboarding forensic review and onboarding IP-attestation processes.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of repeat IP leakage through personnel movement.

ITID-52123.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of competitor-directed espionage pending determination of whether it was carried out via a hired third-party operative or a poached employee.
ITID-52123.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected competitor espionage that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial competitor-espionage suspicion prior to identifying the specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any case where the mechanism has already been established (ITID-52121/52122)
ITID-52123.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52123.escalation: Escalate to legal on initial suspicion of competitor involvement.
indicators: General report or referral naming a competitor without a clear mechanism yet established
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52123.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52123.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52123.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Competitor Espionage group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Competitor Espionage
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case in which a competitor is suspected of obtaining confidential business information through unspecified means.

steps.title: Validate the competitor-espionage indicator
steps.desc: Security and Legal assess the triggering signal (e.g., competitor product/pricing moves that closely mirror unreleased internal plans, or a specific tip) to determine plausibility.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Identify the likely access vector
steps.desc: Investigate plausible vectors — a current or former employee, a vendor/partner, or technical intrusion — using available logs and interviews.
steps.outcome: A narrowed hypothesis on how the information reached the competitor.

steps.title: Restrict further exposure of the affected information
steps.desc: Tighten access to the specific data or business unit implicated, pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of continued leakage.

steps.title: Preserve relevant evidence
steps.desc: Issue a legal hold and preserve logs, communications, and device data relevant to the suspected vector.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for potential legal action.

steps.title: Address the confirmed vector and pursue legal options
steps.desc: Take appropriate personnel, contractual, or legal action against the confirmed source, in coordination with Legal.
steps.outcome: The confirmed leakage vector is closed.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Reassess competitive-information protection controls
steps.desc: Review classification and access controls for strategic/competitive information across the implicated business unit.
steps.outcome: Strengthened controls around sensitive competitive information.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Document findings and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report summarizing findings and recommended control improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership is informed and improvements are tracked to completion.

ITID-52131.def: Human-intelligence-style collection in which an adversary uses a false pretext — posing as a peer, journalist, recruiter, or attendee — at an industry event to elicit confidential or proprietary information from employees.
ITID-52131.purpose: Captures information gathering conducted through in-person social engineering at conferences, trade shows, and other industry events.
scopeIncludes: Pretext conversations at conferences/trade shows aimed at eliciting technical or strategic details
Use of a fake persona/business card to build rapport for future elicitation
scopeExcludes: Purely passive observation of publicly presented material at an event (see OSINT Exploitation, ITID-5253x)
Remote phone-based pretext calls (ITID-52521)
ITID-52131.severity: Medium-High, depending on the sensitivity of information discussed and whether repeat targeting is identified.
ITID-52131.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the employee disclosed sensitive information or if the same actor is linked to prior targeting.
ITID-52131.escalation: Escalate to security awareness/insider risk teams for employee debrief; escalate to legal/counter-intelligence liaison if a pattern suggests organized, repeat targeting.
indicators: Employee report of an unusually probing conversation with an unfamiliar 'peer' at an event
Pattern of the same individual or organization approaching multiple employees across events
Follow-up contact after an event referencing details only shared in a probing conversation
vectors: False persona/pretext used to build rapport and elicit detail at industry events
Fake surveys, interviews, or 'networking' requests used as elicitation cover
rootCauses: Insufficient employee training on elicitation and pretexting risks before travel/conference attendance
No standard guidance on what information is appropriate to discuss externally
controls: Pre-travel/pre-conference security awareness briefing
Post-event debrief process for reporting suspicious contacts
ITID-52131.detection: Minimal technical detection; ATT&CK's reconnaissance techniques are written primarily with digital collection in mind, so the mapping here is an honest approximation of an in-person analog rather than an exact fit. Detection relies almost entirely on employee reporting.
ITID-52131.response: Debrief the employee to determine what was disclosed; log the actor/organization for pattern tracking across events.
metrics: Number of suspicious-contact reports per year
Number of repeat-actor patterns identified
ITID-52131.notes: Primarily a human-intelligence detection surface; the ATT&CK reconnaissance mapping is approximate since Enterprise ATT&CK is written for digital-medium collection.

playbook.name: Human Intelligence (HUMINT) Collection via Social Engineering at Industry Events
playbook.description: An individual is identified as having used social engineering tactics at a conference, trade show, or industry event to elicit confidential information from company employees.

steps.title: Debrief the employee(s) approached and confirm the elicitation attempt
steps.desc: Security interviews the employee(s) who report the suspicious contact to reconstruct what was asked, what may have been disclosed, and any identifying details about the collector.
steps.guidance: This is typically identified retrospectively via employee self-report; make reporting easy and non-punitive to encourage disclosure.
steps.outcome: A documented account of the elicitation attempt and what information may have been disclosed.

steps.title: Correlate with other recent contacts or targeting patterns
steps.desc: Check whether other employees have reported similar approaches, at this or recent events, to determine if this is part of a broader collection campaign.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against travel and event-attendance records for a pattern of targeting specific roles or projects.
steps.outcome: A determination of whether this is an isolated incident or part of a coordinated collection effort.

steps.title: Brief and heighten protective posture for affected/upcoming-event employees
steps.desc: Provide targeted guidance to the affected employee(s) and to employees planning to attend related upcoming events about the observed tactics and how to respond to similar approaches.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of further successful elicitation at upcoming events.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Human Intelligence (HUMINT) Collection via Social Engineering at Industry Events" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Assess and limit exposure of disclosed information
steps.desc: Determine whether any disclosed information requires business changes (e.g., accelerating a patent filing, adjusting a go-to-market timeline) to limit competitive harm.
steps.guidance: Involve the relevant business unit and Legal/IP counsel where applicable.
steps.outcome: Any necessary defensive business actions are identified and initiated.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Update pre-event briefing and conference security-awareness materials
steps.desc: Incorporate the observed tactics into standard pre-travel/pre-event security briefings for employees attending industry events.
steps.outcome: Improved employee resilience to social-engineering elicitation at future events.

steps.title: Document the tactic and share within trusted industry security-sharing channels where appropriate
steps.desc: Record the elicitation tactic observed and, where appropriate and legally permissible, share indicators with trusted industry ISAC or peer-security channels.
steps.outcome: Broader situational awareness of the tactic across the industry sharing community.

ITID-52132.def: Signals-intelligence-style collection in which an adversary intercepts corporate voice, data, or network communications — through network-level interception, rogue wireless infrastructure, or radio/cellular interception — to obtain confidential information in transit.
ITID-52132.purpose: Captures the technical interception of corporate communications by an adversary seeking strategic or competitive intelligence.
scopeIncludes: Network traffic sniffing or adversary-in-the-middle interception of corporate communications
Use of rogue Wi-Fi access points or cellular interception equipment near corporate facilities to capture communications
scopeExcludes: Interception of an individual executive's personal communications specifically (see Executive Communications Surveillance, ITID-52143)
Interception achieved via a compromised insider (ITID-5211x)
ITID-52132.severity: High, given the breadth of information potentially exposed and the sophistication implied by dedicated interception capability.
ITID-52132.priority: P1 upon confirmation of active interception.
ITID-52132.escalation: Escalate to network security, legal, and — where radio/cellular interception near a facility is suspected — physical security and counter-surveillance resources, since this component falls outside standard SOC telemetry.
indicators: Unrecognized wireless access points or cellular equipment detected near corporate facilities
Certificate warnings or unexpected TLS interception indicators on corporate network segments
Anomalous ARP/DNS behavior consistent with on-path interception
vectors: Rogue access point or adversary-in-the-middle positioning on corporate network segments
Network sniffing of unencrypted or weakly encrypted traffic
rootCauses: Unencrypted internal traffic on sensitive network segments
Lack of wireless intrusion detection coverage at facility perimeters
controls: Wireless intrusion detection at facility perimeters
End-to-end encryption for sensitive internal communications
ITID-52132.detection: Network-based interception has a real technical detection surface; radio/cellular-band interception (e.g., IMSI catchers) falls outside ATT&CK Enterprise's scope and standard SOC telemetry, requiring dedicated RF/counter-surveillance detection instead.
ITID-52132.response: Identify and remove any rogue interception infrastructure; assess scope of communications likely exposed and notify affected parties per policy.
metrics: Number of rogue wireless devices detected per quarter
Time to remediate confirmed interception infrastructure
ITID-52132.notes: Network-layer interception is technically detectable; RF/cellular-band interception is outside ATT&CK Enterprise's scope and requires physical/counter-surveillance coordination.

playbook.name: Signals Intelligence (SIGINT)-Style Interception of Corporate Communications
playbook.description: Evidence indicates an external party intercepted corporate communications (calls, radio, wireless traffic, or unencrypted data links) using signals-intelligence-style techniques.

steps.title: Confirm the interception indicator
steps.desc: Technical Security investigates the indicator (e.g., rogue cell-site/IMSI-catcher detection, unencrypted call/data-link exposure, or a tip about intercepted communications) to confirm plausibility.
steps.guidance: Engage RF/technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) specialists if a physical interception device is suspected.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of whether an interception capability was present and its likely scope.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, monitor and reassess.

steps.title: Determine which communications and personnel were exposed
steps.desc: Identify which calls, meetings, or data links were within range/scope of the interception and what sensitivity level of information was discussed.
steps.outcome: A bounded assessment of exposed communications content.

steps.title: Eliminate the interception vector
steps.desc: Remove or neutralize the technical vulnerability (e.g., migrate to encrypted communication channels, remove a detected rogue device, patch a wireless vulnerability).
steps.outcome: The interception capability is no longer effective.

steps.title: Shift sensitive discussions to secure channels
steps.desc: Direct affected teams to use vetted, encrypted communication channels for sensitive discussions until the interception vector is fully remediated.
steps.outcome: Ongoing sensitive communications are protected during remediation.

steps.title: Coordinate with law enforcement if unlawful interception is confirmed
steps.desc: Legal assesses whether the interception constitutes a criminal offense (e.g., wiretapping laws) and coordinates with law enforcement as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal/law-enforcement engagement initiated where warranted.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Harden communications infrastructure
steps.desc: Implement longer-term hardening (encrypted voice/data by default, periodic TSCM sweeps of sensitive facilities) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Reduced susceptibility to future SIGINT-style interception.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership on communications-security posture
steps.desc: Report findings and remediation to leadership and update the communications-security standard accordingly.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational communications-security baseline.

ITID-52133.def: Collection in which an adversary compiles and cross-references publicly available information — organizational, personal, technical, or financial — to construct a profile supporting a subsequent espionage operation.
ITID-52133.purpose: Captures the systematic aggregation of publicly available information specifically to build a targeting or intelligence profile for espionage purposes.
scopeIncludes: Systematic collection and correlation of public records, social media, filings, and technical publications about the organization or its employees
Aggregation activity later found to precede a targeted approach or intrusion
scopeExcludes: General OSINT exploitation not tied to a subsequent espionage operation (see Surveillance and Reconnaissance, ITID-5253x)
One-off, non-systematic public searches
ITID-52133.severity: Medium, escalating to High when correlated with a subsequent targeted approach, phishing campaign, or intrusion attempt.
ITID-52133.priority: P2, escalating to P1 when aggregation is confirmed as precursor activity to an active campaign.
ITID-52133.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence for correlation with active campaigns; escalate to legal/HR if targeted individuals need to be advised.
indicators: Coordinated, high-volume access to employee LinkedIn/social profiles from a small set of accounts
Systematic scraping of the corporate website, filings, or job postings
A subsequent phishing or approach campaign referencing detail only available through aggregated OSINT
vectors: Automated or manual scraping of social media, public filings, and job postings
Cross-referencing multiple public sources to build individual or organizational profiles
rootCauses: Excessive organizational detail in public job postings and social media presence
No monitoring for automated scraping of corporate public-facing assets
controls: Public-facing information minimization standard
Threat intelligence monitoring for organizational OSINT exposure
ITID-52133.detection: Limited direct detection since the activity occurs largely outside owned infrastructure; best detected via threat intelligence monitoring and by correlating downstream campaigns back to likely OSINT precursors.
ITID-52133.response: Correlate aggregation activity with any subsequent targeted campaign; reduce public exposure of the specific detail exploited.
metrics: Number of OSINT-precursor correlations made per quarter
ITID-52133.notes: Cross-reference against the dedicated OSINT Exploitation Tier-4 group (ITID-5253x) under Surveillance and Reconnaissance, which covers the underlying techniques in more depth; this leaf is scoped to aggregation confirmed or suspected as espionage precursor activity.

playbook.name: Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) Aggregation for Targeted Espionage
playbook.description: An external actor is found to have aggregated large volumes of publicly available information about the company and its personnel to build a targeting profile in support of an espionage operation.

steps.title: Identify the OSINT aggregation activity
steps.desc: Security investigates the indicator (e.g., a discovered dossier, unusual scraping of company/employee public profiles, or a tip from a partner or law enforcement) suggesting systematic OSINT aggregation.
steps.guidance: This is frequently identified retrospectively, after a related targeting attempt (phishing, approach, or physical contact) surfaces evidence of prior reconnaissance.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that OSINT aggregation occurred and an initial sense of its target scope.
steps.tool: OSINT monitoring tools; case management system

steps.title: Determine which individuals and information categories were targeted
steps.desc: Catalog which employees, roles, or public-facing information (org charts, press releases, patent filings, social media) were aggregated.
steps.outcome: A prioritized list of individuals/information likely at heightened risk of follow-on targeting.

steps.title: Correlate with and heighten posture against follow-on targeting
steps.desc: Brief identified at-risk individuals and heighten monitoring for phishing, pretexting, or physical approaches that may follow the reconnaissance.
steps.guidance: OSINT aggregation is typically a precursor step; treat this as an early-warning trigger rather than a standalone closed incident.
steps.outcome: Affected individuals are aware and monitoring is heightened for follow-on activity.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) Aggregation for Targeted Espionage" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Reduce the organization's public attack surface where feasible
steps.desc: Work with Communications, HR, and affected individuals to reduce unnecessary public exposure of sensitive organizational or personal details (e.g., overly detailed org charts, executive travel details).
steps.outcome: Reduced material available for future OSINT-based targeting.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Update employee digital-footprint guidance
steps.desc: Provide guidance to affected and at-risk employees on managing their public digital footprint and privacy settings.
steps.outcome: Reduced future OSINT exposure for at-risk personnel.

steps.title: Document findings and update reconnaissance-detection playbook triggers
steps.desc: Record the aggregation pattern observed and use it to refine detection triggers for future reconnaissance activity.
steps.outcome: Improved early detection of future OSINT-based targeting campaigns.

ITID-52134.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of covert intelligence collection pending determination of whether it was HUMINT, SIGINT-style interception, or OSINT aggregation.
ITID-52134.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected covert intelligence collection that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of covert collection activity prior to identifying the specific method
scopeExcludes: Any case where the collection method has already been established (ITID-52131/52132/52133)
ITID-52134.priority: P2 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52134.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence and insider risk for initial triage.
indicators: General report of suspicious information-gathering activity without a confirmed method
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52134.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52134.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the method is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52134.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Covert Intelligence Collection group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Covert Intelligence Collection
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of covert intelligence collection directed against the organization by an external actor using unspecified tradecraft.

steps.title: Validate the covert-collection indicator
steps.desc: Security and Legal assess the triggering signal to determine whether it plausibly reflects a deliberate covert intelligence-collection effort.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Characterize the collection method and targets
steps.desc: Investigate available evidence to determine the likely collection method (human, technical, or open-source) and which individuals or information were targeted.
steps.outcome: A working hypothesis of method and scope.

steps.title: Protect targeted individuals and information
steps.desc: Brief affected personnel and restrict access to or increase monitoring around the targeted information.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of continued or successful collection.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Unclassified / General Covert Intelligence Collection" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Close the identified collection vector
steps.desc: Take appropriate technical, physical, or personnel action to eliminate the confirmed collection method.
steps.outcome: The collection vector is no longer viable.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Reassess protective controls for sensitive information and personnel
steps.desc: Review classification, access, and physical-security controls relevant to the exposed information.
steps.outcome: Strengthened controls reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report summarizing findings and recommended improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52141.def: Espionage targeting a corporate executive during business travel, exploiting the reduced physical and network security typical of hotels, transit, and foreign venues to tamper with devices or intercept communications.
ITID-52141.purpose: Captures espionage activity targeting an executive's devices or physical security specifically during travel.
scopeIncludes: Suspected or confirmed tampering with an executive's device left unattended in a hotel room or venue
Adversary-in-the-middle attacks against an executive's device via hotel or venue Wi-Fi
Targeted rogue-charging-station or cable ('juice jacking'-style) compromise attempts
scopeExcludes: Compromise of an executive's personal device unrelated to travel (ITID-52142)
Interception of executive communications not tied to a travel event (ITID-52143)
ITID-52141.severity: High to Critical given the strategic value of executive access and the difficulty of securing travel environments.
ITID-52141.priority: P1, treated as time-sensitive given the executive is often still traveling when discovered.
ITID-52141.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive protection, IT security, and legal; consider device replacement rather than remediation-in-place for high-confidence tampering.
indicators: Physical evidence of device tampering (open casing, unfamiliar cable/adapter)
Unexpected certificate warnings or forced Wi-Fi captive-portal behavior while traveling
Device state (settings, installed profiles) inconsistent with pre-travel baseline upon return
vectors: Physical tampering with a device left unattended in a hotel room ('evil maid')
Rogue or spoofed Wi-Fi access point at a travel venue
Compromised public charging infrastructure
rootCauses: Executives traveling with devices containing sensitive data rather than travel-hardened loaner devices
No mandatory VPN/travel security briefing before high-risk-destination trips
controls: Executive travel security program (loaner devices, VPN mandate, pre/post-travel device checks)
Mobile threat defense on executive devices
ITID-52141.detection: Network-layer AiTM and device-state changes are technically detectable; physical tampering itself (the 'evil maid' component) is a physical-security matter outside ATT&CK Enterprise's telemetry.
ITID-52141.response: Treat any suspected tampering as a full compromise: image and replace the device rather than clean it, and assess what data/credentials it had access to during the travel window.
metrics: Number of executive travel security incidents per year
Percentage of high-risk trips completed with pre/post-travel device checks
detections: VPN/certificate anomaly detection during travel windows
ITID-52141.notes: The device-tampering component is a physical-security matter with no ATT&CK Enterprise technique; the network-interception component maps to real techniques.

playbook.name: Executive Device/Travel-Targeted Espionage
playbook.description: An executive's device or travel itinerary is targeted for espionage purposes, such as device compromise during international travel or interception tied to travel patterns.

steps.title: Confirm the device/travel-targeting indicator
steps.desc: Security investigates the indicator (e.g., anomalous device behavior after travel, evidence of physical tampering, or a border/customs device-seizure event) in coordination with the executive-protection team.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with the executive and their assistant, who often provide the earliest signal.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of whether the device or the executive was targeted, and by what likely means.

steps.title: Forensically examine the affected device(s)
steps.desc: Conduct a forensic examination of the executive's device(s) to determine whether compromise occurred and what data may have been accessed.
steps.outcome: A documented forensic finding on compromise and data exposure.
steps.abort: If no evidence of compromise, close with recommended hardening measures.

steps.title: Isolate and replace the compromised device
steps.desc: Remove the device from use, revoke associated credentials/tokens, and issue a clean replacement device.
steps.outcome: The executive is operating on a known-clean device with rotated credentials.

steps.title: Review and adjust executive travel security protocols
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive-protection and Security to review travel-related device-handling protocols (e.g., loaner devices for high-risk travel, Faraday bags).
steps.outcome: Updated travel-security protocol reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Assess and remediate downstream account/data exposure
steps.desc: Rotate credentials and review access for any accounts or systems the compromised device could reach.
steps.outcome: No residual access remains via the compromised device.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Brief the executive and implement enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Brief the executive on findings and implement enhanced monitoring of their accounts and devices going forward.
steps.outcome: Executive is informed and under heightened protective monitoring.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Update executive travel-security policy
steps.desc: Document findings and update the organization's executive travel-security policy and briefing materials.
steps.outcome: Improved protection for executives on future high-risk travel.

ITID-52142.def: Espionage in which an adversary compromises an executive's personal phone, tablet, or home computer — typically less protected than corporate assets — as a pivot point to access corporate email, credentials, or strategic information.
ITID-52142.purpose: Captures the compromise of an executive's personal (non-corporate) device specifically to gain a path into corporate intelligence.
