scopeIncludes: Spearphishing or spyware delivered to an executive's personal device
Use of personal-device access (e.g., synced credentials, forwarded email) to reach corporate systems
scopeExcludes: Compromise occurring specifically during travel (ITID-52141)
Interception of communications rather than device compromise (ITID-52143)
ITID-52142.severity: High to Critical given the likely pivot to corporate systems and the reduced visibility the SOC has into personal devices.
ITID-52142.escalation: Escalate to executive protection, IT security, and legal; extend incident scope to any corporate account or system the personal device had access to.
indicators: Executive reports unusual behavior on a personal device (battery drain, unfamiliar apps, unexpected messages)
Corporate account access from an unrecognized personal device or location
Phishing targeting the executive's personal email/phone number referencing corporate detail
vectors: Spearphishing sent to a personal email or messaging account
Commercial spyware/stalkerware-class tooling installed on a personal device
Credential reuse between personal and corporate accounts
rootCauses: No corporate security program extended to executive personal devices
Executives using personal devices/accounts for corporate business without MDM or MFA enforcement
controls: Executive personal-device security program (mobile threat defense enrollment, offered on a voluntary basis)
MFA enforcement on all corporate access regardless of originating device
ITID-52142.detection: Limited visibility into personal devices constrains direct detection; corporate-side detection relies on anomalous authentication and email-forwarding-rule monitoring for the executive's account.
ITID-52142.response: Assume corporate credential exposure until proven otherwise; force credential reset and review forwarding rules/OAuth grants on the executive's corporate account.
metrics: Number of executive personal-device compromises identified per year
detections: Anomalous authentication detection on executive accounts
ITID-52142.notes: Personal-device compromise itself has limited corporate telemetry; response focuses on the corporate-side blast radius once the pivot is confirmed.

playbook.name: Executive Personal Device Compromise for Corporate Intelligence Access
playbook.description: An executive's personal (non-corporate-managed) device is compromised and used as a pivot point to access corporate intelligence, exploiting the weaker security posture of personal devices.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of the personal device
steps.desc: With the executive's consent, Security investigates the indicator (e.g., anomalous corporate account access from an unrecognized device, malware alert, or executive-reported suspicious activity).
steps.guidance: Personal-device investigations require explicit executive consent and careful handling of personal privacy alongside the corporate security interest.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of compromise and the corporate access the device could reach.
steps.abort: If the executive declines forensic access to the personal device, focus on corporate-side containment (credential revocation) instead.

steps.title: Determine what corporate data or access was reachable from the device
steps.desc: Review which corporate accounts, email, or systems were accessible from the compromised personal device (e.g., via mobile email, SSO session, or synced credentials).
steps.outcome: A bounded list of corporate exposure via the personal device.

steps.title: Revoke corporate access from the compromised device
steps.desc: Immediately revoke corporate sessions, tokens, and mobile-email access associated with the personal device.
steps.outcome: The compromised device can no longer reach corporate systems.

steps.title: Rotate the executive's corporate credentials
steps.desc: Force password and MFA-token resets for all corporate accounts accessible from the device.
steps.outcome: Corporate credentials are no longer valid to any residual attacker foothold.

steps.title: Assist with or recommend remediation of the personal device
steps.desc: Advise the executive on remediating or replacing the personal device, and offer corporate-provided secure device alternatives.
steps.outcome: The personal device is no longer a viable pivot point, or is replaced.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Implement a bring-your-own-device policy review for executives
steps.desc: Review and, if needed, tighten policy on personal-device access to corporate systems for executives and other high-value targets.
steps.outcome: Reduced future exposure via personal-device pivoting.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership on BYOD risk
steps.desc: Report findings and recommended policy changes to leadership.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational posture on executive personal-device risk.

ITID-52143.def: Espionage focused on intercepting or collecting an executive's calls, email, calendar, or messaging content to obtain strategically valuable, time-sensitive information, distinct from device compromise for general access.
ITID-52143.purpose: Captures the targeted surveillance of an executive's communications to obtain strategic intelligence such as deal terms, board discussions, or negotiating positions.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized mailbox rule/forwarding configured to silently copy an executive's email
Compromise of an executive's calendar or conferencing account to monitor upcoming discussions
Interception of an executive's calls or messages during a specific negotiation or event
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the underlying device without evidence of targeted communications monitoring (ITID-52142)
Broad network-level interception not specific to an executive (ITID-52132)
ITID-52143.severity: Critical when tied to an active, time-sensitive negotiation, deal, or board matter; High otherwise.
ITID-52143.priority: P1, treated as time-critical given the perishable value of the intelligence to the adversary.
ITID-52143.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal and the board/executive team when active deal or litigation communications may be exposed; consider out-of-band communication for sensitive matters until the compromise is contained.
indicators: Unrecognized inbox rule or forwarding address on an executive mailbox
Unfamiliar delegate/calendar-sharing permission on an executive account
Evidence that a counterparty appears to have advance knowledge of the executive's private position
vectors: Hidden mailbox forwarding rule or OAuth grant on the executive's account
Compromised conferencing/calendar credentials used to monitor scheduled discussions
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of mailbox rule and OAuth grant changes on executive accounts
No dedicated protective monitoring tier for executive communications
controls: Executive account protective monitoring program
Automated alerting on mailbox rule and OAuth grant changes for executive accounts
ITID-52143.detection: Strong technical detection surface for the digital-collection component (mail rules, OAuth grants); real-time call/room interception is outside standard SOC telemetry and requires facilities/counter-surveillance sweeps.
ITID-52143.response: Immediately remove unauthorized forwarding/delegation, assess what content was exposed and to whom, and advise legal on any deal or litigation impact.
metrics: Time to detect unauthorized mailbox rule on executive accounts
Number of executive communication surveillance incidents per year
detections: Mailbox rule/OAuth grant change alerting on VIP accounts
ITID-52143.notes: Digital collection is well covered by mail-security telemetry; in-room/verbal interception requires physical/counter-surveillance coordination and is outside SOC visibility.

playbook.name: Executive Communications Surveillance for Strategic Intelligence
playbook.description: An executive's communications (email, calendar, calls, messaging) are found to be under unauthorized surveillance for the purpose of extracting strategic business intelligence.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized access to executive communications
steps.desc: Investigate the indicator (e.g., anomalous mailbox access, forwarding rule discovered, or leaked information tracing back to executive communications) to confirm unauthorized surveillance.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of unauthorized access and its duration.

steps.title: Scope the communications and information exposed
steps.desc: Determine which mailboxes, calendars, or channels were accessed and what strategic information (deals, plans, negotiations) was likely exposed.
steps.outcome: A bounded assessment of exposed strategic information.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized access and forwarding mechanisms
steps.desc: Remove any discovered mail-forwarding rules, delegate permissions, or unauthorized integrations, and rotate credentials.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access to the executive's communications is eliminated.

steps.title: Move sensitive strategic discussions to secure channels temporarily
steps.desc: Direct the executive and relevant team to use a vetted secure channel for highly sensitive discussions until the investigation concludes.
steps.outcome: Ongoing sensitive discussions are protected during remediation.

steps.title: Investigate the source of unauthorized access
steps.desc: Determine whether the surveillance originated from an external compromise, a third-party vendor, or an insider, and address the root cause accordingly.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal if an insider or vendor is implicated.
steps.outcome: Root cause identified and addressed.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Assess business impact and notify affected counterparties if needed
steps.desc: Determine whether exposed strategic information (e.g., deal terms) requires notifying counterparties, legal counsel, or adjusting business strategy.
steps.outcome: Appropriate business and legal actions taken to limit impact.

steps.title: Brief affected business stakeholders on residual risk
steps.desc: Brief the business unit(s) affected by the incident on residual competitive or strategic risk and any recommended business-level mitigations.
steps.outcome: Business stakeholders are informed and able to adjust plans in light of residual risk.

steps.title: Harden executive communications security
steps.desc: Document findings and implement enhanced monitoring and access controls for executive communications going forward.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of future executive communications surveillance.

ITID-52144.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of espionage targeting an executive pending determination of whether it involved travel-based targeting, personal-device compromise, or communications surveillance.
ITID-52144.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected executive-targeted espionage that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of executive targeting prior to identifying the specific vector
scopeExcludes: Any case where the vector has already been established (ITID-52141/52142/52143)
ITID-52144.severity: High pending triage, given the strategic sensitivity of executive access.
ITID-52144.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52144.escalation: Escalate to executive protection and legal on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of unusual activity involving an executive's accounts, devices, or communications
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52144.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52144.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the vector is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52144.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Executive Targeting group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Executive Targeting Espionage
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case in which an executive is suspected of being targeted for espionage purposes by unspecified means.

steps.title: Validate the executive-targeting indicator
steps.desc: Security, in coordination with executive-protection, assesses the triggering signal to determine plausibility of deliberate espionage targeting.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Characterize the likely targeting vector
steps.desc: Investigate available evidence across devices, communications, and physical/travel patterns to determine the likely vector.
steps.outcome: A working hypothesis of vector and scope.

steps.title: Protect the executive and limit further exposure
steps.desc: Take immediate protective action appropriate to the vector (credential rotation, device isolation, physical-security adjustment).
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of continued targeting success.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Unclassified / General Executive Targeting Espionage" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Close the confirmed vector
steps.desc: Take appropriate technical, physical, or personnel action to eliminate the confirmed targeting vector.
steps.outcome: The vector is no longer viable.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or information flow remains
steps.desc: Confirm, through a follow-up review, that all identified access paths and information-flow channels related to the incident have been fully closed.
steps.outcome: Independently verified confirmation that the exposure has been fully eradicated.

steps.title: Implement enhanced ongoing protective monitoring
steps.desc: Establish heightened monitoring for the executive's accounts, devices, and physical security going forward.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of repeat targeting.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report summarizing findings and recommended improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52211.def: A sustained, technically sophisticated intrusion campaign attributed — through infrastructure, tooling, or intelligence-community reporting — to a specific state-sponsored APT group, aimed at long-term covert access and intelligence collection.
ITID-52211.purpose: Captures a cyber espionage campaign formally attributed to a known nation-state advanced persistent threat (APT) group.
scopeIncludes: Intrusion activity matching known TTPs, infrastructure, or malware of a tracked APT group
Campaigns confirmed via threat intelligence attribution reporting or government notification
scopeExcludes: Activity by a contracted cyber-mercenary/PSOA group acting on a state's behalf (ITID-52212)
Suspected but unattributed nation-state-style activity (ITID-52213)
ITID-52211.severity: Critical. Attributed APT activity implies a well-resourced, persistent adversary with strategic intent.
ITID-52211.priority: P1, with executive and board-level visibility given the geopolitical and reputational dimensions.
ITID-52211.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and, where required by sector regulation, government/sector-ISAC notification channels; engage external incident response and threat intelligence support.
indicators: Malware, infrastructure, or tooling matching a tracked APT group's known signature
Long-dwell-time persistence mechanisms discovered during investigation
Government or threat-intelligence-vendor notification of targeting
vectors: Spearphishing with APT-associated malware or infrastructure
Exploitation of known or zero-day vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems
Supply-chain compromise as an initial access vector
rootCauses: Unpatched internet-facing systems
Insufficient network segmentation limiting lateral movement
Gaps in long-dwell-time detection (e.g., logging retention, EDR coverage)
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1560.001 Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
controls: Threat-intelligence-driven detection engineering for tracked APT TTPs
Network segmentation and egress filtering
Extended log retention supporting long-dwell-time investigation
ITID-52211.detection: Strong technical detection surface across the intrusion lifecycle; the primary challenge is dwell time and attribution confidence rather than raw signal availability.
ITID-52211.response: Run a full-scope forensic investigation assuming long dwell time; coordinate remediation timing carefully to avoid tipping off a persistent adversary before full eviction is possible.
metrics: Dwell time from initial access to detection
Number of attributed APT campaigns detected per year
ITID-52211.notes: Represents the fullest technical APT framing in the Nation-State Espionage group; the technique list above is illustrative of a typical campaign, not exhaustive of any one actor's TTPs.

playbook.name: Nation-State APT Group Attributed Espionage Campaign
playbook.description: A confirmed advanced persistent threat (APT) group with attributed nation-state sponsorship is found conducting a targeted espionage campaign against the organization.

steps.title: Confirm and attribute the campaign
steps.desc: The incident response and threat-intelligence teams confirm technical indicators of compromise and correlate tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) against known APT group profiles to support attribution.
steps.guidance: Engage external threat-intelligence partners or government cyber agencies to corroborate attribution before making external statements.
steps.outcome: A documented, evidence-based attribution assessment and confirmed scope of compromise.

steps.title: Determine dwell time and full scope of access
steps.desc: Reconstruct the intrusion timeline across all affected systems to determine how long the actor has had access and what was accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Nation-state campaigns often have long dwell times; assume broader compromise than initially observed and expand scope conservatively.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive timeline and scope of compromise.

steps.title: Notify executive leadership, Legal, and government liaison channels
steps.desc: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, Legal, and, given nation-state attribution, the relevant national cyber/counter-intelligence authority (e.g., FBI, CISA, or national equivalent).
steps.guidance: Nation-state campaigns typically carry mandatory or strongly advised government notification obligations distinct from standard breach notification.
steps.outcome: Leadership and appropriate government authorities are informed and coordinating.

steps.title: Contain the intrusion without alerting the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate with law enforcement/government liaison on containment sequencing to avoid tipping off a sophisticated actor before evidence-gathering is complete, where investigative value justifies a measured approach.
steps.guidance: Balance ongoing exposure risk against intelligence value of continued observation; government liaison partners often have a view on sequencing.
steps.outcome: An approved, coordinated containment plan.
steps.abort: Escalate to immediate isolation if active, high-impact exfiltration or destructive activity is detected.

steps.title: Eradicate all identified persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors, implants, and persistence mechanisms across the environment in a coordinated eradication event.
steps.guidance: Coordinate a single, comprehensive eradication event across all affected systems to prevent the actor from re-establishing access via missed footholds.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms are removed.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Rebuild and validate affected systems
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-good sources, rotate all potentially exposed credentials, and validate system integrity before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Affected systems are restored and verified clean.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Conduct a comprehensive after-action review with government partners
steps.desc: Produce a detailed after-action report, share indicators of compromise with appropriate government and industry partners, and brief the board on strategic implications.
steps.outcome: Improved detection capability and strengthened government-liaison relationships for future campaigns.

ITID-52212.def: A cyber espionage campaign in which a state sponsor uses a commercial surveillance/exploitation vendor or contracted hacking group to conduct intrusion and collection activity on its behalf, providing the sponsor a layer of deniability.
ITID-52212.purpose: Captures state-sponsored espionage carried out through a commercial cyber-mercenary group or private-sector offensive actor (PSOA) rather than a state's own internal APT unit.
scopeIncludes: Intrusion activity using commercial spyware or exploit tooling sold/leased by a known PSOA
Attribution evidence linking contracted operator infrastructure to a state client
scopeExcludes: Direct activity by a state's own internal APT unit (ITID-52211)
Commercially-motivated (non-state) mercenary hacking-for-hire (see relevant Data Breaches domain leaf)
ITID-52212.severity: Critical, given state sponsorship and the advanced tooling typically available to commercial vendors.
ITID-52212.priority: P1, with the same executive/board visibility as direct APT activity.
ITID-52212.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and government/sector notification channels; engage external threat intelligence with visibility into the specific PSOA's tooling.
indicators: Malware or exploit chains matching known commercial spyware/PSOA tooling
Infrastructure previously linked to a known PSOA's customer base
Targeting pattern consistent with a specific state's known interests despite commercial tooling
vectors: Zero-click or one-click exploit chains associated with commercial spyware vendors
Spearphishing using PSOA-supplied malware
Exploitation acquired/obtained through a commercial capability broker
rootCauses: Unpatched zero-day exposure exploited by well-funded commercial tooling
Limited detection engineering specific to known PSOA toolkits
controls: Threat-intel monitoring for known PSOA infrastructure/tooling indicators
Rapid patching program for high-risk internet/mobile-facing vulnerabilities
ITID-52212.detection: Detection depends heavily on threat-intelligence visibility into the specific vendor's tooling, which is often more limited than for well-documented state APT groups.
ITID-52212.response: Treat as a full nation-state-grade incident despite the commercial-vendor layer; pursue attribution to the sponsoring state where possible for legal and diplomatic response options.
metrics: Number of PSOA-attributed incidents per year
ITID-52212.notes: The commercial-vendor layer complicates attribution but does not reduce the technical severity; response should proceed as for direct state APT activity.

playbook.name: State-Sponsored Espionage via Contracted Cyber Mercenary Group
playbook.description: A nation-state is found to have contracted a commercial cyber-mercenary or 'hack-for-hire' group to conduct espionage against the organization, providing plausible deniability to the sponsoring state.

steps.title: Confirm mercenary-group attribution
steps.desc: Threat intelligence correlates observed TTPs and infrastructure with known commercial hack-for-hire group signatures, distinguishing this from a directly state-operated campaign.
steps.guidance: Engage external threat-intelligence vendors specializing in mercenary-group tracking; attribution to the sponsoring state may be indirect or unconfirmed.
steps.outcome: A documented attribution assessment noting confidence level.

steps.title: Determine scope of compromise and likely client/sponsor motive
steps.desc: Assess what was accessed or exfiltrated and evaluate what business or strategic interest a sponsor might have in the targeted data.
steps.outcome: A scoped assessment of compromise and a hypothesis on sponsor motive.

steps.title: Escalate to leadership, Legal, and government liaison
steps.desc: Notify executive leadership, Legal, and relevant government cyber authorities given the state-sponsorship dimension, even where attribution confidence is moderate.
steps.outcome: Leadership and authorities informed and coordinating on response.

steps.title: Contain the intrusion
steps.desc: Isolate affected systems and revoke compromised credentials, coordinating timing with any parallel law-enforcement interest.
steps.outcome: The intrusion is contained without prejudicing any parallel investigation.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence and remediate the initial access vector
steps.desc: Remove all identified footholds and remediate the initial access vector used by the mercenary group.
steps.outcome: The environment is free of known persistence mechanisms.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Restore and validate affected systems
steps.desc: Rebuild affected systems and rotate exposed credentials, validating integrity before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and verified clean.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Brief leadership and share indicators with government/industry partners
steps.desc: Document findings, share threat indicators through appropriate channels, and brief leadership on the implications of state-sponsored contracted threats.
steps.outcome: Improved detection and strengthened partner coordination.

ITID-52213.def: A general or not-yet-attributed case of suspected nation-state sponsored cyber espionage, pending determination of whether it involves a known APT group or a contracted cyber-mercenary group.
ITID-52213.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected nation-state sponsored activity pending formal attribution.
scopeIncludes: Intrusion activity bearing hallmarks of nation-state sophistication without confirmed attribution
scopeExcludes: Any case with confirmed attribution to a specific APT group or PSOA (ITID-52211/52212)
ITID-52213.severity: Critical pending triage, given that nation-state-style sophistication is itself a high-severity signal even before attribution.
ITID-52213.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as attribution develops.
ITID-52213.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and threat intelligence immediately on initial suspicion; do not wait for attribution to begin full-scope response.
indicators: Intrusion sophistication (custom tooling, careful operational security, long dwell time) suggestive of well-resourced sponsorship without a confirmed match to known groups
vectors: Varies by underlying campaign; not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Varies by underlying campaign; not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
Threat intelligence attribution engagement
ITID-52213.detection: Varies by the underlying campaign; see the attributed leaves (ITID-52211/52212) once classification is complete.
ITID-52213.response: Treat as a full-scope, high-severity incident from first suspicion; reclassify once attribution is established rather than waiting to begin response.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 90 days
ITID-52213.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Nation-State Sponsored Attacks group; technique mapping intentionally left general since it varies by the eventual attributed campaign.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Nation-State Sponsored Attack
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case suspected to involve a nation-state sponsored actor conducting espionage against the organization, with attribution not yet confirmed.

steps.title: Assess indicators for potential nation-state involvement
steps.desc: Threat intelligence and incident response review technical indicators for characteristics (sophistication, targeting, infrastructure) suggestive of nation-state involvement.
steps.guidance: Treat nation-state suspicion as a trigger for elevated handling even before attribution is confirmed.
steps.outcome: A documented preliminary assessment and elevated handling designation if warranted.

steps.title: Scope the compromise
steps.desc: Determine the full extent of systems accessed and data potentially exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive scope assessment.

steps.title: Escalate to leadership, Legal, and government liaison as warranted
steps.desc: Notify executive leadership and Legal, and engage government cyber authorities if the preliminary assessment supports nation-state suspicion.
steps.outcome: Appropriate stakeholders informed based on assessed likelihood of state involvement.

steps.title: Contain the intrusion
steps.desc: Isolate affected systems and revoke compromised credentials.
steps.outcome: The intrusion is contained.

steps.title: Eradicate identified persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Remove all confirmed backdoors and persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: The environment is free of known persistence.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Restore and validate affected systems
steps.desc: Rebuild systems and rotate credentials, validating integrity before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and verified clean.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Document findings and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and recommended improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52221.def: Cyber or human espionage targeting a defense contractor's classified, controlled unclassified information (CUI), or export-controlled program data, sponsored by or benefiting a foreign state.
ITID-52221.purpose: Captures nation-state theft of classified or controlled defense program data from a defense contractor or its supply chain.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected exfiltration of classified/CUI program data from a defense contractor environment
Targeting of a defense-program subcontractor as an access path to the prime contractor's data
scopeExcludes: Theft of military technology/weapons system design specifically (ITID-52222)
Non-defense-sector industrial espionage (ITID-5223x)
ITID-52221.severity: Critical without exception. Classified and export-controlled program data carries national security implications beyond commercial harm.
ITID-52221.priority: P1, with mandatory government notification per defense-industrial-base regulatory obligations.
ITID-52221.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, facility security officer/FSO, and the relevant government program office/agency per contractual and regulatory reporting obligations; engage government incident response support.
indicators: Access to classified/CUI enclaves from an unauthorized account or location
Exfiltration of files tagged with program classification or export-control markings
Targeting pattern consistent with known state interest in the specific defense program
vectors: Spearphishing targeting program personnel with cleared access
Exploitation of a smaller subcontractor with weaker security as a pivot to the prime contractor
Insider access by a cleared employee under external direction
rootCauses: Inconsistent security controls across the defense supply chain
Insufficient monitoring of access to classified/CUI enclaves
controls: CMMC/NIST 800-171-aligned controls for CUI environments
Supply-chain security assessment for subcontractors with program access
ITID-52221.detection: Strong where CUI/classified-enclave monitoring is mature; supply-chain pivot points through smaller subcontractors are the most common detection gap.
ITID-52221.response: Follow contractual/regulatory incident reporting timelines exactly; scope the investigation across the full program supply chain, not just the immediately affected entity.
metrics: Time to regulatory notification from confirmed compromise
Number of supply-chain-originated incidents per year
sops: Defense Industrial Base Incident Reporting SOP
ITID-52221.notes: Regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., DFARS-aligned) are typically time-critical and independent of the technical investigation timeline.

playbook.name: Defense Contractor Classified Program Data Theft
playbook.description: As a defense contractor, the organization discovers that data related to a classified program has been accessed or exfiltrated by an unauthorized party.

steps.title: Confirm classified-data exposure and classification level
steps.desc: Facility Security Officer (FSO) and incident response jointly confirm whether the accessed/exfiltrated data is classified, and at what level, using program classification guides.
steps.guidance: Involve the program's assigned government security representative immediately given mandatory reporting obligations for classified spillage or compromise.
steps.outcome: A confirmed classification determination and documented scope of the exposed data.
steps.tool: Classified system audit logs; program classification guide

steps.title: Determine the access vector and affected systems
steps.desc: Investigate how the unauthorized access occurred (insider, technical intrusion, spillage) and which classified or controlled systems were involved.
steps.outcome: A documented access-vector determination and system scope.

steps.title: Notify the government contracting officer and cognizant security authority
steps.desc: Immediately notify the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) or equivalent cognizant security authority, the government contracting officer, and program security officer per contractual and regulatory reporting timelines.
steps.guidance: Classified-program incidents typically carry strict, time-bound government reporting requirements distinct from standard breach notification — do not delay pending full internal investigation.
steps.outcome: Required government notifications completed within mandated timeframes.

steps.title: Isolate affected classified systems and revoke access
steps.desc: Isolate the affected classified or controlled systems and revoke access for any implicated individuals pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Follow government-approved incident-handling procedures specific to classified information systems.
steps.outcome: Further exposure of classified data is halted.

steps.title: Conduct government-coordinated damage assessment
steps.desc: Support the government's classification/damage assessment process, providing all requested forensic evidence and access records.
steps.guidance: The government authority, not the contractor alone, determines final damage classification for a classified-program compromise.
steps.outcome: A completed, government-validated damage assessment.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Remediate systems and restore accreditation status
steps.desc: Remediate affected systems per government-approved procedures and work with the cognizant security authority to restore any suspended accreditation or facility clearance status.
steps.outcome: Systems remediated and program security accreditation restored.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Complete formal after-action report for government review
steps.desc: Produce a formal after-action report meeting government contractual requirements, with distribution restricted per classification handling rules.
steps.outcome: A compliant, appropriately restricted after-action report accepted by the government authority.

ITID-52222.def: Cyber or human espionage targeting the technical design, specifications, or performance data of a military technology or weapons system, sponsored by or benefiting a foreign state.
ITID-52222.purpose: Captures nation-state theft of specific military technology or weapons system design information.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of weapons system CAD/engineering data, specifications, or test results
Theft of source code or firmware for a military technology platform
scopeExcludes: Theft of broader classified program administrative/contractual data without specific technical design content (ITID-52221)
ITID-52222.priority: P1, with mandatory government notification per defense-industrial-base regulatory obligations.
ITID-52222.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, facility security officer/FSO, and the relevant government program office; engage government incident response support given the national security sensitivity of the specific technology.
indicators: Targeted access to engineering/CAD repositories for a specific weapons platform
Exfiltration of firmware or source code tied to a military system
Targeting pattern consistent with a known state's technology-acquisition priorities
vectors: Spearphishing or intrusion targeting engineering teams with access to weapons-system design data
Insider access by a cleared engineer under external direction
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation between general engineering environments and the most sensitive weapons-design repositories
Overly broad access to design repositories beyond the specific engineers who need it
controls: Least-privilege access segmentation for weapons-system design repositories
Data loss prevention tuned to engineering CAD/source formats
ITID-52222.detection: Detection is strongest where design repositories are segmented and monitored distinctly from general engineering environments; broad, flat access materially weakens it.
ITID-52222.response: Follow contractual/regulatory incident reporting timelines exactly; assess the specific technical capability exposed for national-security impact, not just data volume.
metrics: Time to regulatory notification from confirmed compromise
sops: Defense Industrial Base Incident Reporting SOP
ITID-52222.notes: Distinguished from ITID-52221 by its focus on specific technical design/performance data rather than broader classified program information.

playbook.name: Military Technology/Weapons System Design Theft
playbook.description: Design data for a military technology or weapons system is discovered to have been stolen or exfiltrated by an external actor.

steps.title: Confirm theft and identify the specific design data exposed
steps.desc: Incident response, in coordination with the program security office, confirms which weapons-system design files or specifications were accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against export-control (ITAR/EAR or equivalent) classification of the affected technical data.
steps.outcome: A confirmed inventory of exposed design data with export-control classification noted.
steps.tool: PLM/CAD system audit logs; export-control classification registry

steps.title: Determine the exfiltration vector and likely recipient
steps.desc: Investigate technical logs and threat intelligence to determine how the data left the environment and to whom it may have been directed.
steps.outcome: A documented exfiltration-vector and attribution hypothesis.

steps.title: Notify government export-control and defense security authorities
steps.desc: Notify the relevant government authorities (e.g., Directorate of Defense Trade Controls, DCSA, or national equivalent) given the export-control and national-security implications.
steps.guidance: Unauthorized export of controlled technical data may itself trigger separate regulatory reporting obligations regardless of the theft investigation's status.
steps.outcome: Required government notifications completed.

steps.title: Isolate the exfiltration vector and revoke access
steps.desc: Isolate affected systems, revoke access for implicated accounts, and close the technical exfiltration path.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration is prevented.

steps.title: Support government damage assessment and law-enforcement investigation
steps.desc: Provide full cooperation and evidence to law enforcement and government damage-assessment teams.
steps.outcome: Completed government/law-enforcement damage assessment.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Remediate technical vulnerabilities and restore secure operations
steps.desc: Remediate the exploited vulnerability, rotate credentials, and validate system integrity before resuming normal program operations.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and verified secure.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Complete restricted after-action report and update export-control safeguards
steps.desc: Document findings in a classification-appropriate report and strengthen technical safeguards around export-controlled data.
steps.outcome: Improved protection of controlled technical data.

ITID-52223.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected nation-state espionage against a defense contractor or defense-related asset, pending determination of scope.
ITID-52223.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected military and defense espionage that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of defense-sector espionage prior to confirming the specific data targeted
scopeExcludes: Any case where the target (classified program data vs. weapons technology) has already been established (ITID-52221/52222)
ITID-52223.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52223.escalation: Escalate to legal and the facility security officer on initial suspicion; regulatory notification clocks may start before full classification is complete.
indicators: General suspicious-access report within a defense-program environment
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52223.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52223.response: Begin regulatory-notification-clock assessment immediately even before full classification; reclassify once scope is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
sops: Defense Industrial Base Incident Reporting SOP
ITID-52223.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Military and Defense Espionage group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Military and Defense Espionage
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected espionage targeting military or defense-related information held by the organization.

steps.title: Validate the indicator and determine program sensitivity
steps.desc: Incident response and the program security office jointly assess the triggering indicator and determine whether classified or controlled defense information may be involved.
steps.outcome: A documented sensitivity determination guiding subsequent notification requirements.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Scope the affected systems and data
steps.desc: Determine which systems, programs, and data categories are implicated.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of investigation.

steps.title: Notify government security authorities as warranted
steps.desc: Escalate to the cognizant government security authority if the scoping step indicates classified or export-controlled exposure.
steps.outcome: Appropriate government notification completed where warranted.

steps.title: Contain the exposure
steps.desc: Isolate affected systems and revoke relevant access.
steps.outcome: Further exposure is halted.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed vector
steps.desc: Address the confirmed technical, physical, or personnel vector responsible for the exposure.
steps.outcome: The vector is closed.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Restore secure operations
steps.desc: Validate system integrity and restore normal operations, including any required accreditation steps.
steps.outcome: Operations restored securely.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership and government partners as appropriate
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report with distribution appropriate to the sensitivity involved.
steps.outcome: Leadership and relevant partners informed.

ITID-52231.def: State-sponsored espionage targeting proprietary manufacturing processes, industrial formulas, or production methods, typically to accelerate a foreign state's domestic industrial capability.
ITID-52231.purpose: Captures nation-state theft of manufacturing or industrial process know-how for the sponsor's economic or industrial benefit.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of proprietary manufacturing process documentation, recipes, or production-line configuration data
Targeting pattern consistent with a state's declared industrial development priorities
scopeExcludes: Theft of a specific product's design/patent rather than the manufacturing process itself (see IP Theft leaves, ITID-5231x/5232x)
Critical infrastructure operational technology targeting (ITID-52232)
ITID-52231.severity: High to Critical depending on the strategic value of the process and the scale of loss.
ITID-52231.priority: P1 upon confirmation of state sponsorship or targeting pattern.
ITID-52231.escalation: Escalate to legal, executive leadership, and government/sector notification channels where applicable.
indicators: Exfiltration of manufacturing execution system (MES) or process-control documentation
Intrusion pattern consistent with known state industrial-espionage campaigns
Targeting concentrated on a specific process rather than broad data collection
vectors: Spearphishing or intrusion targeting process engineers and plant IT/OT staff
Supply-chain compromise via an equipment vendor with access to process configuration
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation between IT and OT/process-control networks
Broad access to process documentation beyond the engineers who require it
controls: IT/OT network segmentation
Access controls on process-control documentation repositories
ITID-52231.detection: Adequate on the IT side; detection within OT/process-control environments is typically weaker and should be treated as a coverage gap to close.
ITID-52231.response: Scope the investigation across both IT and OT environments; assess competitive/strategic impact alongside technical remediation.
metrics: Number of industrial espionage incidents per year
OT/process-control detection coverage percentage
ITID-52231.notes: Distinguished from product-IP theft leaves by its focus on the manufacturing process itself rather than the end-product design.

playbook.name: State-Sponsored Theft of Manufacturing/Industrial Process Secrets
playbook.description: A nation-state actor is found to have targeted and stolen proprietary manufacturing or industrial process information from the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the theft and attribute state sponsorship
steps.desc: Incident response and threat intelligence confirm the exfiltration of process data and assess indicators supporting state-sponsored attribution.
steps.guidance: Engage external threat-intelligence and, where warranted, government cyber authorities to corroborate attribution.
steps.outcome: A confirmed scope of exfiltration and a documented attribution assessment.

steps.title: Determine the competitive/strategic value of the stolen process data
steps.desc: Work with engineering/operations leadership to quantify the strategic and competitive significance of the stolen manufacturing process information.
steps.outcome: A documented business-impact assessment.

steps.title: Escalate to leadership, Legal, and government cyber authorities
steps.desc: Notify executive leadership, Legal, and the relevant national cyber/counter-intelligence authority given the state-sponsored attribution.
steps.outcome: Leadership and government authorities informed and coordinating.

steps.title: Isolate affected industrial control and engineering systems
steps.desc: Isolate affected systems (including any operational technology/industrial control system touchpoints) and revoke compromised access.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with OT/engineering teams to avoid disrupting live manufacturing operations during containment.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration is halted without disrupting production safety.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence and remediate the access vector
steps.desc: Remove identified persistence mechanisms and remediate the initial access vector across IT and, if applicable, OT environments.
steps.outcome: The environment is free of known persistence.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Restore systems and reassess process-data protection
steps.desc: Restore affected systems and implement enhanced protections (segmentation, DLP) around manufacturing process data.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with strengthened protections in place.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Conduct after-action review with government/industry partners
steps.desc: Document findings, share indicators with appropriate government and industry partners, and brief leadership.
steps.outcome: Improved detection and stronger partner coordination.

ITID-52232.def: State-sponsored espionage targeting an operator of critical infrastructure (energy, water, transportation, healthcare, financial systems, etc.) to collect intelligence on operations or to pre-position for potential future disruption.
ITID-52232.purpose: Captures nation-state espionage specifically targeting a critical infrastructure operator's systems for intelligence or pre-positioning purposes.
scopeIncludes: Intrusion into critical infrastructure IT or OT environments attributed to or consistent with state sponsorship
Reconnaissance or access consistent with pre-positioning rather than immediate disruption
scopeExcludes: State-sponsored theft of manufacturing process know-how at a non-critical-infrastructure manufacturer (ITID-52231)
Active disruptive/destructive attacks on infrastructure (tracked under the relevant attack-availability domain, not espionage)
ITID-52232.severity: Critical without exception, given the potential for pre-positioned access to be leveraged for future disruption of essential services.
ITID-52232.priority: P1, with mandatory government/sector (e.g., CISA, sector-ISAC) notification.
ITID-52232.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, government cybersecurity agencies, and sector-ISAC channels; treat any OT access as a potential safety issue requiring engineering involvement.
indicators: Unattributed persistent access discovered in OT or industrial control system environments
Reconnaissance activity mapping control-system architecture with no immediate disruptive action
Living-off-the-land technique use within OT-adjacent IT systems
vectors: Initial access via IT environment with lateral movement toward OT/ICS boundary
Compromise of a vendor or remote-access solution used to service OT equipment
rootCauses: Weak segmentation between corporate IT and OT/ICS networks
Remote access solutions for OT maintenance lacking strong authentication and monitoring
controls: IT/OT network segmentation and monitored boundary
Strong authentication and session monitoring on OT remote-access solutions
ITID-52232.detection: Detection at the IT/OT boundary is the most reliable technical signal; detection within legacy OT/ICS protocols themselves is often limited and should be treated as a known gap requiring specialized ICS monitoring.
ITID-52232.response: Coordinate closely with engineering/operations before any containment action in OT environments to avoid safety impact; notify government/sector channels per critical-infrastructure obligations.
metrics: Dwell time in OT-adjacent environments before detection
Time to government/sector notification
ITID-52232.notes: OT/ICS-specific detection is a known gap relative to IT-side telemetry and should be prioritized for this leaf.

playbook.name: Critical Infrastructure Operator Targeted for Industrial Espionage
playbook.description: The organization, as a critical infrastructure operator, is targeted by an actor conducting industrial espionage against its operational or engineering data.

steps.title: Confirm targeting and assess critical-infrastructure sector reporting obligations
steps.desc: Incident response confirms the scope of targeting and determines applicable sector-specific regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., to a national critical-infrastructure cyber authority).
steps.guidance: Critical-infrastructure operators typically have mandatory incident-reporting timelines distinct from general commercial breach rules.
steps.outcome: A confirmed scope and documented regulatory reporting determination.

steps.title: Assess safety and operational-continuity implications
steps.desc: Jointly with OT/engineering, assess whether the espionage activity has touched or risks touching operational/safety systems, distinct from pure data theft.
steps.outcome: A documented safety and operational-impact assessment.

steps.title: Notify the sector regulator and government cyber authority
steps.desc: Complete required notifications to the sector regulator and national critical-infrastructure cyber authority.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed within mandated timeframes.

steps.title: Contain the intrusion while preserving safe operations
steps.desc: Isolate affected IT systems, coordinating carefully with OT operations to avoid any disruption to safety-critical infrastructure functions.
steps.outcome: The intrusion is contained without operational disruption.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence and remediate the access vector
steps.desc: Remove identified footholds and remediate the vulnerability that enabled access.
steps.outcome: The environment is free of known persistence.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Restore systems and validate operational integrity
steps.desc: Restore affected systems and validate that OT/engineering system integrity is intact before resuming full operations.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and operational integrity confirmed.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Conduct after-action review with regulators and industry ISAC
steps.desc: Document findings and share appropriate indicators with the sector regulator and industry information-sharing organization.
steps.outcome: Improved sector-wide situational awareness and internal control improvements.

ITID-52233.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected state-sponsored industrial espionage pending determination of whether the target is a manufacturing process or critical infrastructure operations.
ITID-52233.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected state-sponsored industrial espionage that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of state-sponsored industrial targeting prior to confirming the specific target type
scopeExcludes: Any case where the target has already been established (ITID-52231/52232)
ITID-52233.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52233.escalation: Escalate to legal and government notification channels on initial suspicion given the potential critical-infrastructure nexus.
indicators: General suspicious-access report in an industrial or manufacturing environment without confirmed classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52233.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52233.response: Begin critical-infrastructure notification assessment immediately even before full classification; reclassify once scope is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52233.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Industrial Espionage group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Industrial Espionage
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected nation-state industrial espionage targeting the organization's operational or engineering data.

steps.title: Validate the indicator
steps.desc: Incident response assesses the triggering signal to determine whether it plausibly indicates state-directed industrial espionage.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Scope affected systems and data
steps.desc: Determine which systems and industrial/process data are implicated.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of investigation.

steps.title: Escalate to leadership and relevant authorities as warranted
steps.desc: Notify leadership, Legal, and government cyber authorities if evidence supports state involvement.
steps.outcome: Appropriate stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Contain the exposure
steps.desc: Isolate affected systems and revoke compromised access.
steps.outcome: Further exposure is halted.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed vector
steps.desc: Address the confirmed vector responsible for the exposure.
steps.outcome: The vector is closed.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Restore systems and strengthen protections
steps.desc: Restore affected systems and implement enhanced protections around industrial process data.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with strengthened protections.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52241.def: Espionage targeting diplomatic communications infrastructure — embassy networks, foreign ministry correspondence, or diplomatic cable/messaging systems — to obtain foreign-policy or diplomatic intelligence.
ITID-52241.purpose: Captures state interception of foreign ministry or embassy communications for diplomatic intelligence purposes, where the organization operates or hosts such communications infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: Intrusion or interception targeting an embassy's or foreign ministry's network or communications systems hosted or serviced by the organization
Compromise of a diplomatic messaging or correspondence system
scopeExcludes: Trade negotiation intelligence theft specifically (ITID-52242)
Non-diplomatic government-sector targeting
ITID-52241.severity: Critical without exception, given the diplomatic and international-relations sensitivity.
ITID-52241.priority: P1, with immediate government and diplomatic-channel notification.
ITID-52241.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, executive leadership, and the relevant government/diplomatic liaison; handle notification with particular discretion given international sensitivities.
indicators: Intrusion into networks or systems known to host diplomatic communications
Targeting pattern consistent with known state interest in a specific diplomatic relationship or negotiation
vectors: Spearphishing targeting diplomatic or foreign-ministry personnel
Compromise of a managed service provider hosting diplomatic communications infrastructure
rootCauses: Insufficient isolation of diplomatic communications infrastructure from general hosting environments
Weak vendor/MSP security oversight for diplomatically sensitive systems
controls: Isolation of diplomatically sensitive hosting environments
Enhanced vendor oversight for government/diplomatic clients
ITID-52241.detection: Standard intrusion-detection techniques apply, but the diplomatic sensitivity of any finding requires unusually careful, discreet handling regardless of technical severity.
ITID-52241.response: Coordinate response timing and disclosure carefully with government/diplomatic counterparts; preserve evidence to the standard required for potential international-relations consequences.
metrics: Time to government/diplomatic notification
ITID-52241.notes: Applies primarily to organizations that host, service, or otherwise touch diplomatic communications infrastructure as part of their business.

playbook.name: Foreign Ministry/Embassy Communications Interception
playbook.description: The organization's communications with a foreign ministry or embassy contact are found to have been intercepted, suggesting diplomatic-espionage targeting.

steps.title: Confirm the interception and diplomatic sensitivity
steps.desc: Incident response, together with Legal and Government Affairs, confirms that communications with the foreign ministry/embassy contact were intercepted and assesses the diplomatic sensitivity involved.
steps.guidance: Engage Government Affairs/international counsel early given potential diplomatic implications beyond a standard commercial breach.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of interception and a documented sensitivity assessment.

steps.title: Determine content and parties exposed
steps.desc: Identify the specific communications, participants, and topics exposed by the interception.
steps.outcome: A bounded exposure assessment.

steps.title: Notify Legal, Government Affairs, and relevant national authorities
steps.desc: Escalate to Legal, Government Affairs, and the appropriate national counter-intelligence or diplomatic-security authority given the cross-border and diplomatic dimensions.
steps.outcome: Appropriate internal and government stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Shift to secure communication channels
steps.desc: Migrate ongoing communications with the affected foreign-government contact to vetted, secure channels.
steps.outcome: Ongoing communications are protected.

steps.title: Remediate the interception vector
steps.desc: Identify and close the technical or procedural vector that allowed interception.
steps.outcome: The interception vector is eliminated.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Reassess diplomatic-communications security practices
steps.desc: Review and strengthen practices for handling communications with government and diplomatic contacts going forward.
steps.outcome: Improved security posture for diplomatic communications.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership and Government Affairs
steps.desc: Produce a distribution-appropriate after-action report and brief relevant leadership.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52242.def: Espionage aimed at obtaining an organization's or government's confidential trade negotiation strategy, positions, or fallback terms, typically to benefit a foreign state's negotiating position.
ITID-52242.purpose: Captures state or state-sponsored theft of intelligence on trade negotiation positions to gain diplomatic or economic advantage.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of trade negotiation strategy documents, position papers, or internal deliberation records
Targeting concentrated in the period immediately before or during active trade negotiations
scopeExcludes: Interception of general diplomatic communications infrastructure without a specific trade-negotiation nexus (ITID-52241)
ITID-52242.severity: Critical during an active negotiation window; High otherwise given the ongoing strategic value of negotiation methodology.
ITID-52242.priority: P1, treated as time-critical given the perishable value of negotiation-position intelligence.
ITID-52242.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, executive leadership, and the relevant government trade or diplomatic office; treat timing as urgent given active negotiations may be directly affected.
indicators: Targeted access to files or accounts belonging to the negotiation team
Intrusion timing tightly correlated with negotiation milestones
Counterparty behavior suggesting advance knowledge of the organization's position
vectors: Spearphishing targeting negotiation team members
Compromise of a shared document repository used for negotiation preparation
rootCauses: Negotiation materials stored without heightened access restriction relative to their sensitivity
Insufficient operational security awareness among negotiation team members
controls: Heightened access restriction and monitoring for active negotiation materials
Operational security briefing for negotiation team members
ITID-52242.detection: Reasonable technical detection surface where negotiation materials are held in monitored repositories; risk is highest when materials are handled informally outside monitored systems.
ITID-52242.response: Notify the negotiation team and relevant government office immediately given the time-sensitivity; assess whether negotiation strategy needs to be adjusted in light of the exposure.
metrics: Time to detection relative to negotiation milestones
ITID-52242.notes: Time-sensitivity relative to negotiation milestones is the key differentiator from general diplomatic communications interception.

playbook.name: Trade Negotiation Position Intelligence Theft
playbook.description: Confidential information about the organization's trade negotiation position is discovered to have been stolen, likely to benefit a foreign government or competing party in ongoing negotiations.

steps.title: Confirm theft of negotiation-position information
steps.desc: Incident response, Legal, and the negotiation team confirm what specific negotiation-strategy information was accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Time sensitivity is critical here — negotiation positions lose protective value quickly once exposed, so expedite confirmation.
steps.outcome: A confirmed, time-stamped scope of exposed negotiation information.

steps.title: Assess the access vector and likely beneficiary
steps.desc: Determine how the information was accessed and who is likely to benefit (a specific foreign government, competing bidder, or counterparty).
steps.outcome: A documented vector and beneficiary hypothesis.

steps.title: Notify Legal, executive leadership, and the negotiation team immediately
steps.desc: Alert Legal, executive leadership, and the negotiation team so the negotiation strategy can be adjusted before further exposure causes harm.
steps.guidance: Speed matters more than completeness here; give the negotiation team an initial alert even before the full investigation concludes.
steps.outcome: The negotiation team is able to adapt strategy in light of the compromise.

steps.title: Close the access vector
steps.desc: Revoke access and remediate the vulnerability or account that enabled the theft.
steps.outcome: No further negotiation information can be exfiltrated via the same vector.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and pursue legal options where warranted
steps.desc: Complete the investigation into how the theft occurred and, with Legal, evaluate options including diplomatic protest, contractual remedies, or law-enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Root cause addressed and appropriate legal/diplomatic options pursued.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Reassess protections for future negotiation materials
steps.desc: Implement enhanced access controls, need-to-know restrictions, and secure-room/communication practices for future sensitive negotiations.
steps.outcome: Strengthened protections for future negotiation-sensitive information.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce a restricted after-action report and brief executive leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52243.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected state-sponsored diplomatic espionage pending determination of whether it targets diplomatic communications infrastructure or trade negotiation intelligence.
ITID-52243.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected diplomatic espionage that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of diplomatic-espionage targeting prior to confirming the specific target
scopeExcludes: Any case where the target has already been established (ITID-52241/52242)
ITID-52243.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52243.escalation: Escalate to legal and government/diplomatic liaison channels on initial suspicion.
indicators: General suspicious-access report involving diplomatic or trade-related systems without confirmed classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52243.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52243.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the target is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52243.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Diplomatic Espionage group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Diplomatic Espionage
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected diplomatic espionage involving the organization's interactions with a foreign government entity.

steps.title: Validate the indicator
steps.desc: Incident response, with Legal and Government Affairs, assesses the triggering signal to determine plausibility of diplomatic-espionage targeting.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Scope the affected communications or data
steps.desc: Determine which communications, data, or relationships are implicated.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of investigation.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal, Government Affairs, and relevant authorities
steps.desc: Notify Legal, Government Affairs, and government counter-intelligence authorities as warranted by the scope.
steps.outcome: Appropriate stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Contain the exposure
steps.desc: Close the identified access vector and shift sensitive communications to secure channels.
steps.outcome: Further exposure is halted.

steps.title: Remediate the confirmed vector
steps.desc: Address the confirmed technical or procedural vector responsible for the exposure.
steps.outcome: The vector is closed.

steps.title: Validate eradication with threat-intelligence partners
steps.desc: Confirm with threat-intelligence and, where engaged, government partners that no further indicators of the actor's presence remain in the environment.
steps.outcome: Independently corroborated confirmation of eradication.

steps.title: Strengthen diplomatic-communications protections
steps.desc: Review and improve practices for handling sensitive communications with government/diplomatic contacts.
steps.outcome: Improved protective posture.

steps.title: Conduct a phased return-to-operations validation
steps.desc: Phase the return of affected systems to full operation, validating security monitoring coverage at each phase before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Systems are returned to operation with validated monitoring at each phase.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52311.def: Theft of unfiled patent material, research findings, or R&D output carried out as part of a broader espionage operation, as distinct from opportunistic data-breach-driven theft of the same material.
ITID-52311.purpose: Provides the espionage-context classification for theft of patent-pending inventions or R&D output, for use when the taxonomy needs to distinguish an espionage-motivated actor from an ordinary data-breach actor.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of R&D/patent-pending material confirmed or suspected to be directed by a competitor or state sponsor
R&D theft occurring alongside other espionage indicators (e.g., a recruited insider or nation-state intrusion)
scopeExcludes: Opportunistic, non-espionage-motivated R&D or trade-secret theft, which is tracked in the Data Breaches domain's IP theft leaves (ITID-51331 R&D Theft, ITID-51321 Trade Secret Exposure)
Theft of source code specifically (ITID-52321)
ITID-52311.severity: High to Critical depending on the strategic value of the R&D and the sophistication of the sponsoring actor.
ITID-52311.priority: P1 once an espionage nexus (competitor or state sponsor) is confirmed or strongly suspected.
ITID-52311.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership on confirmation of an espionage nexus; coordinate with the parallel Data Breaches domain investigation if both classifications are in play for the same incident.
indicators: Targeted, selective exfiltration of specific R&D projects rather than broad data collection
Corroborating espionage indicators such as a recruited insider or attributed intrusion
