vectors: Insider exfiltration of R&D repositories
Targeted intrusion into R&D file shares or lab systems
rootCauses: Insufficient access segmentation for high-value, unfiled R&D material
No monitoring tuned to detect selective, targeted exfiltration patterns
controls: Access segmentation for unfiled patent/R&D repositories
DLP tuned to detect selective/targeted exfiltration patterns
ITID-52311.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category at the espionage-context classification level; the fuller technical detection detail lives with the parallel Data Breaches domain leaves for the same underlying activity.
ITID-52311.response: Coordinate investigation scope with the Data Breaches domain team to avoid duplicated or conflicting incident handling for the same underlying facts.
metrics: Number of R&D theft cases with a confirmed espionage nexus per year
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52311.notes: Lone-child stub for this Tier-4 group, following the same pattern as ITID-51311 in the Data Breaches domain: cross-reference ITID-51321 (Trade Secret Exposure) and ITID-51331 (R&D Theft) in the parallel Data Breaches leaves under this same ITID-50000 Tier-1 for the fuller technical treatment; this leaf exists to flag the espionage-motive distinction.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Patent and R&D Theft (Espionage Context)
playbook.description: Patent-pending or unpublished research and development information is discovered to have been stolen for use by an external, espionage-motivated party.

steps.title: Confirm theft and scope the R&D materials exposed
steps.desc: Incident response, with the R&D and IP-counsel teams, confirms which patent applications, lab notebooks, or research data were accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: Engage IP counsel immediately — unpublished patent material carries statutory novelty/priority implications if disclosed.
steps.outcome: A confirmed inventory of exposed R&D/patent material.
steps.tool: Document management system audit logs; DLP

steps.title: Determine the access vector and likely recipient
steps.desc: Investigate how the material was accessed and assess whether a competitor, foreign entity, or other party is the likely beneficiary.
steps.outcome: A documented vector and beneficiary hypothesis.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve relevant systems, logs, and communications under legal hold to support potential trade-secret litigation.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and admissible.

steps.title: Close the access vector
steps.desc: Revoke access and remediate the vulnerability or account responsible for the exposure.
steps.outcome: No further R&D material can be exfiltrated via the same vector.

steps.title: Coordinate with IP counsel on protective filings and legal action
steps.desc: IP counsel evaluates accelerating patent filing timelines, pursuing trade-secret litigation, or other protective legal measures.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal protective action initiated.

steps.title: Confirm removal of exposed material from external reach
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, confirm that the exposed intellectual property has been removed from or is no longer reachable by the external party (e.g., takedown request, injunction compliance check).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction or removal of the external party's continued access to the stolen material.

steps.title: Strengthen R&D data protection controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced access controls, watermarking, and DLP around unpublished patent and R&D materials.
steps.outcome: Strengthened protections reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Reassess classification and labeling of related intellectual property
steps.desc: Review the classification and access-labeling of related, not-yet-exposed intellectual property to ensure consistent protection standards are applied.
steps.outcome: Consistent classification and protection applied to related IP assets.

steps.title: Document and brief R&D and Legal leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief R&D and Legal leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52321.def: Theft of proprietary source code carried out as part of a broader espionage operation, as distinct from opportunistic data-breach-driven source code theft.
ITID-52321.purpose: Provides the espionage-context classification for theft of proprietary source code, for use when the taxonomy needs to distinguish an espionage-motivated actor from an ordinary data-breach actor.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of source code confirmed or suspected to be directed by a competitor or state sponsor
Source code theft occurring alongside other espionage indicators
scopeExcludes: Opportunistic, non-espionage-motivated source code theft, tracked in the Data Breaches domain (ITID-51311 Source Code Theft)
ITID-52321.severity: High to Critical depending on the strategic value of the code and the sophistication of the sponsoring actor.
ITID-52321.priority: P1 once an espionage nexus is confirmed or strongly suspected.
ITID-52321.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership on confirmation of an espionage nexus; coordinate with the parallel Data Breaches domain investigation.
indicators: Targeted, selective exfiltration of a specific repository rather than broad code access
Corroborating espionage indicators such as a recruited insider or attributed intrusion
vectors: Insider exfiltration of source code repositories
Targeted intrusion into version control or CI/CD systems
rootCauses: Insufficient repository access segmentation
No monitoring tuned to detect selective, targeted repository exfiltration
controls: Repository access segmentation and monitoring
DLP for source-code file types and repository exports
ITID-52321.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category at the espionage-context classification level; the fuller technical detection detail lives with the parallel Data Breaches domain leaf for the same underlying activity.
ITID-52321.response: Coordinate investigation scope with the Data Breaches domain team to avoid duplicated or conflicting incident handling for the same underlying facts.
metrics: Number of source code theft cases with a confirmed espionage nexus per year
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52321.notes: Lone-child stub following the same pattern as ITID-51311 in the Data Breaches domain — cross-reference ITID-51311 (Unclassified/General Source Code Theft, IP Theft Context) in the parallel leaves under this same ITID-50000 Tier-1 for the fuller technical treatment.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Source Code Theft (Espionage Context)
playbook.description: Proprietary source code is discovered to have been stolen by an external, espionage-motivated actor for competitive or strategic advantage.

steps.title: Confirm theft and scope the repositories/code exposed
steps.desc: Incident response confirms which source-code repositories were accessed or cloned and by whom, using version-control and access logs.
steps.outcome: A confirmed inventory of exposed code repositories and commits.

steps.title: Assess the sensitivity and competitive value of the exposed code
steps.desc: Work with engineering leadership to determine the strategic sensitivity of the exposed codebase (e.g., core algorithms vs. non-sensitive utilities).
steps.outcome: A documented business-impact assessment.

steps.title: Revoke access and rotate credentials/keys
steps.desc: Revoke compromised access, rotate API keys/secrets embedded in the exposed code, and close the access vector.
steps.guidance: Treat any credentials or secrets embedded in the exposed code as compromised even if the code itself is the primary concern.
steps.outcome: No further code exposure and all embedded secrets invalidated.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve relevant logs and system images under legal hold for potential trade-secret litigation.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and admissible.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and pursue legal remedies
steps.desc: Complete the investigation and, with Legal, evaluate cease-and-desist, injunctive relief, or criminal referral options.
steps.outcome: Root cause addressed and appropriate legal action pursued.

steps.title: Confirm removal of exposed material from external reach
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, confirm that the exposed intellectual property has been removed from or is no longer reachable by the external party (e.g., takedown request, injunction compliance check).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction or removal of the external party's continued access to the stolen material.

steps.title: Strengthen source-code access controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced repository access controls, code-watermarking, and anomaly detection for bulk code access/downloads.
steps.outcome: Strengthened protections reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Reassess classification and labeling of related intellectual property
steps.desc: Review the classification and access-labeling of related, not-yet-exposed intellectual property to ensure consistent protection standards are applied.
steps.outcome: Consistent classification and protection applied to related IP assets.

steps.title: Document and brief engineering and Legal leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52331.def: Theft of proprietary manufacturing process, formula, or production-method information carried out as part of a broader espionage operation by a competitor, contracted operative, or state sponsor.
ITID-52331.purpose: Provides the espionage-context classification for theft of manufacturing process know-how, for use when the taxonomy needs to distinguish an espionage-motivated (including but not limited to state-sponsored) actor from an ordinary data-breach actor.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of manufacturing process documentation confirmed or suspected to be directed by a competitor or state sponsor
Process theft occurring alongside other espionage indicators
scopeExcludes: State-sponsored manufacturing process theft specifically attributed to a nation-state actor (ITID-52231, which carries the fuller nation-state technical treatment)
Opportunistic, non-espionage-motivated process theft (tracked in the Data Breaches domain)
ITID-52331.severity: High to Critical depending on the strategic value of the process.
ITID-52331.priority: P1 once an espionage nexus is confirmed or strongly suspected.
ITID-52331.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership on confirmation of an espionage nexus.
indicators: Targeted, selective exfiltration of specific process documentation
Corroborating espionage indicators such as a recruited insider or a competitor/state nexus
vectors: Insider exfiltration of manufacturing execution system (MES) or process documentation
Targeted intrusion into process-engineering file shares
rootCauses: Insufficient access segmentation for process documentation
No monitoring tuned to detect selective, targeted exfiltration
controls: Access segmentation for process documentation repositories
DLP tuned to targeted exfiltration patterns
ITID-52331.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; where the sponsor is confirmed as a nation-state, reclassify to ITID-52231 for the fuller technical treatment.
ITID-52331.response: Determine whether the sponsor is a competitor or a state actor early, as this determines which leaf and reporting track applies.
metrics: Number of manufacturing process theft cases with a confirmed espionage nexus per year
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52331.notes: Cross-reference ITID-52231 (state-sponsored manufacturing process theft, Nation-State Espionage) when a state sponsor is confirmed; this leaf covers the broader espionage-context case including competitor sponsorship.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Manufacturing Process Espionage
playbook.description: Proprietary manufacturing process information is discovered to have been stolen by an external, espionage-motivated actor.

steps.title: Confirm theft and scope the process data exposed
steps.desc: Incident response confirms which manufacturing process documentation, formulas, or specifications were accessed or exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: A confirmed inventory of exposed process data.
steps.tool: Document management system audit logs; DLP

steps.title: Assess access vector, including OT/engineering systems
steps.desc: Determine how the data was accessed, including whether operational technology or engineering systems were involved.
steps.outcome: A documented access-vector determination.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and close the access vector
steps.desc: Issue a legal hold, revoke compromised access, and remediate the exploited vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and further exposure halted.

steps.title: Coordinate with operations to protect ongoing manufacturing integrity
steps.desc: Confirm with operations/engineering that containment actions have not disrupted safety-critical manufacturing processes.
steps.outcome: Containment completed without operational disruption.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies
steps.desc: Legal evaluates trade-secret litigation or other remedies against the identified party.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal action pursued.

steps.title: Confirm removal of exposed material from external reach
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, confirm that the exposed intellectual property has been removed from or is no longer reachable by the external party (e.g., takedown request, injunction compliance check).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction or removal of the external party's continued access to the stolen material.

steps.title: Strengthen protections for manufacturing process data
steps.desc: Implement enhanced access controls and monitoring around process documentation and OT systems.
steps.outcome: Strengthened protections reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Reassess classification and labeling of related intellectual property
steps.desc: Review the classification and access-labeling of related, not-yet-exposed intellectual property to ensure consistent protection standards are applied.
steps.outcome: Consistent classification and protection applied to related IP assets.

steps.title: Document and brief operations and Legal leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52341.def: Espionage-motivated exfiltration of a trained machine learning model's weights, architecture definition, or checkpoint artifacts, enabling a competitor or foreign actor to replicate or fine-tune the model without the underlying investment.
ITID-52341.purpose: Captures theft of a proprietary machine learning model's weights, architecture, or checkpoint files.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of model weight/checkpoint files from a training or model-registry environment
Theft of model architecture/configuration files revealing proprietary design choices
scopeExcludes: Theft of the training dataset rather than the trained model itself (ITID-52342)
Reconstruction of model behavior via API querying rather than direct file theft (ITID-52343)
ITID-52341.severity: High to Critical, reflecting the substantial R&D investment typically embodied in a production-grade model.
ITID-52341.priority: P1 upon confirmation of model artifact exfiltration.
ITID-52341.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; assess competitive impact given that model theft can eliminate a competitor's development lead time.
indicators: Unusual access to or download from a model registry or training-environment storage bucket
Bulk transfer of checkpoint files inconsistent with the accessing user's normal workflow
Departing employee with recent access to model artifacts
vectors: Insider exfiltration of model registry contents
Intrusion into ML training infrastructure or object storage housing checkpoints
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls on model registries and training storage
No DLP coverage for large binary model-artifact file types
controls: Access controls and audit logging on model registries
DLP coverage for model-artifact file types and storage locations
ITID-52341.detection: Reasonable technical detection surface where model registries and training storage are centrally logged and monitored; coverage weakens significantly for ad hoc or unmanaged ML infrastructure.
ITID-52341.response: Identify the specific model version and training data lineage exposed; assess whether the model can be retired/rotated to reduce the competitive value of the stolen artifact.
metrics: Number of model artifact theft cases per year
Percentage of model registries with access audit logging enabled
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
detections: Large binary artifact egress DLP alerting
ITID-52341.notes: Differentiated from its siblings by targeting the trained model artifact itself rather than the training data or externally-observed model behavior.

steps.title: Confirm theft and identify the specific model artifacts exposed
steps.desc: Incident response and the ML engineering team confirm which model weight files, checkpoints, or architecture definitions were accessed or exfiltrated.

steps.title: Assess the competitive value and training investment represented

steps.outcome: A documented business-impact assessment.

steps.title: Revoke access and rotate model-registry credentials
steps.desc: Revoke compromised access to the model registry/artifact store and rotate associated credentials and API keys.
steps.outcome: No further model artifacts can be exfiltrated via the same access.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve relevant logs and system state under legal hold for potential trade-secret litigation.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and admissible.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and pursue legal remedies
steps.desc: Complete the investigation and, with Legal, evaluate trade-secret litigation or other remedies against the identified party.
steps.outcome: Root cause addressed and appropriate legal action pursued.

steps.title: Confirm removal of exposed material from external reach

steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction or removal of the external party's continued access to the stolen material.

steps.title: Strengthen model-artifact access controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced access controls, encryption at rest, and anomaly detection for bulk model-artifact downloads.
steps.outcome: Strengthened protections reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Reassess classification and labeling of related intellectual property
steps.desc: Review the classification and access-labeling of related, not-yet-exposed intellectual property to ensure consistent protection standards are applied.
steps.outcome: Consistent classification and protection applied to related IP assets.

steps.title: Document and brief ML/product and Legal leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52342.def: Espionage-motivated exfiltration of a curated, proprietary training dataset — including labeled data, feedback/reinforcement data, or a proprietary data pipeline's output — to accelerate a competitor's or foreign actor's own model development.
ITID-52342.purpose: Captures theft of a proprietary training dataset for use in a competitor's own AI development.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration of curated/labeled training datasets from data lakes or annotation platforms
Theft of proprietary data-collection or labeling pipeline output
scopeExcludes: Theft of the trained model itself rather than its training data (ITID-52341)
ITID-52342.severity: High to Critical, reflecting the significant cost and time typically invested in data curation and labeling.
ITID-52342.priority: P1 upon confirmation of training dataset exfiltration.
ITID-52342.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; assess whether the dataset includes regulated personal data, which would trigger parallel data-protection incident handling.
indicators: Unusual bulk access to a data lake, labeling platform, or annotation tool export function
Departing employee with recent access to curated dataset exports
vectors: Insider exfiltration of dataset exports
Intrusion into data lake or annotation platform infrastructure
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls on curated dataset repositories
No monitoring of bulk export activity from annotation/labeling platforms
controls: Access controls and export logging on data lakes and annotation platforms
DLP coverage for structured dataset export formats
ITID-52342.detection: Reasonable technical detection surface where dataset exports are centrally logged; weaker where researchers routinely move data locally for experimentation.

sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
detections: Data lake/annotation platform bulk export anomaly detection
ITID-52342.notes: Differentiated from ITID-52341 by targeting the input data rather than the trained model artifact.

steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52343.def: Espionage-motivated collection in which an adversary submits a large, systematically designed volume of queries to a model's public or partner-facing API in order to reverse-engineer its decision boundaries, extract approximate parameters, or replicate its functional behavior in a competing model.
ITID-52343.purpose: Captures the reconstruction of a proprietary model's behavior or parameters by systematically querying its public-facing API, without any direct file theft.
scopeIncludes: High-volume, systematically structured querying of a model API consistent with extraction rather than normal usage
Confirmed downstream appearance of a competing model with closely matching behavior following such querying
scopeExcludes: Direct theft of model weight/architecture files (ITID-52341)
ITID-52343.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where a competing product with matching behavior subsequently appears.
ITID-52343.priority: P2, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a resulting competing product.
ITID-52343.escalation: Escalate to legal for terms-of-service/contractual enforcement options and to the ML platform team for rate-limiting and access-policy changes.
indicators: Anomalous query volume or query-pattern diversity from a single account/API key inconsistent with normal usage
Query patterns systematically probing decision boundaries (e.g., minimally-varied input pairs)
Emergence of a competing model with unusually close behavioral similarity
vectors: Automated high-volume querying via a legitimate or trial API account
Distributed querying across multiple accounts to evade rate limits
rootCauses: Insufficient rate limiting and anomaly detection on model API usage
No query-pattern analysis to distinguish extraction attempts from normal usage
controls: API rate limiting and query-pattern anomaly detection
Terms of service prohibiting extraction/reverse-engineering with enforcement mechanisms
ITID-52343.detection: Model extraction via API querying is a novel technique class without an exact ATT&CK Enterprise identifier; T1213 is used here only as the closest collection-stage analog, and this mapping should be treated as an honest approximation rather than a precise fit. Detection relies on API usage analytics rather than traditional intrusion telemetry.
ITID-52343.response: Apply rate limiting/account suspension to the offending account(s); coordinate with legal on contractual enforcement; consider model-level defenses (e.g., output perturbation) for future protection.
metrics: Number of suspected extraction campaigns detected per year
Time to detect anomalous query patterns
sops: Trade Secret Misappropriation Legal Response SOP
ITID-52343.notes: This is a novel technique class not well represented in ATT&CK Enterprise; the T1213 mapping is a closest-analog approximation, not an exact match, and should be reviewed as ATT&CK coverage of AI/ML-specific techniques matures.

playbook.name: Model Extraction via API Query-Based Reverse Engineering
playbook.description: An external actor is found to be systematically querying the organization's AI model API to reconstruct or approximate the underlying proprietary model through model-extraction techniques.

steps.title: Detect anomalous query-pattern activity via API rate/pattern monitoring
steps.desc: API security monitoring flags anomalous usage patterns (high query volume, systematic input-space sweeping, or account behavior consistent with known model-extraction techniques) distinct from normal customer usage.
steps.guidance: This is the key technical identification signature for this leaf, distinguishing it from other AI-theft leaves: rate-limiting alerts, query-pattern-anomaly detection, and per-account usage-baseline deviation are the primary detection tools.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination that the observed API usage pattern is consistent with a model-extraction attempt rather than legitimate heavy usage.
steps.abort: If the pattern is more consistent with legitimate high-volume use, close as a false positive and tune detection thresholds.

steps.title: Identify the account(s) and scope of queries involved
steps.desc: Determine which API account(s), keys, or IP ranges are conducting the extraction attempt and the volume/scope of queries made to date.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of the extraction attempt.

steps.title: Throttle, rate-limit, or suspend the implicated account(s)
steps.desc: Apply aggressive rate-limiting or suspend the API key(s)/account(s) associated with the extraction pattern.
steps.outcome: The extraction attempt is halted or significantly slowed.

steps.title: Review terms-of-service violation and evidence for legal action
steps.desc: Legal reviews the API terms of service for the applicable violation and preserves logs as evidence.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and terms-of-service basis for action documented.

steps.title: Pursue account termination and legal remedies
steps.desc: Terminate the offending account(s) permanently and, with Legal, evaluate further remedies (cease-and-desist, litigation) against the identified party.
steps.outcome: The account is terminated and appropriate legal action pursued.

steps.title: Confirm removal of exposed material from external reach
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, confirm that the exposed intellectual property has been removed from or is no longer reachable by the external party (e.g., takedown request, injunction compliance check).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction or removal of the external party's continued access to the stolen material.

steps.title: Strengthen API rate-limiting and query-pattern defenses
steps.desc: Implement or tune rate-limiting, output perturbation, and query-pattern-anomaly detection to reduce susceptibility to future extraction attempts.
steps.outcome: Strengthened API defenses against model-extraction techniques.

steps.title: Reassess classification and labeling of related intellectual property
steps.desc: Review the classification and access-labeling of related, not-yet-exposed intellectual property to ensure consistent protection standards are applied.
steps.outcome: Consistent classification and protection applied to related IP assets.

steps.title: Document and brief ML/API platform leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and update detection thresholds and playbook triggers for future extraction attempts.
steps.outcome: Improved detection capability for future model-extraction attempts.

ITID-52344.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected theft of proprietary AI/ML assets, pending determination of whether it involves model weights, training data, or API-based model extraction.
ITID-52344.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected AI/algorithm theft that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of AI/algorithm theft prior to identifying the specific asset targeted
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific asset targeted has already been established (ITID-52341/52342/52343)
ITID-52344.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52344.escalation: Escalate to legal and the ML platform team on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of unusual access to ML infrastructure or unusual API usage without a confirmed classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52344.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52344.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the targeted asset is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52344.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the AI and Algorithm Theft group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General AI and Algorithm Theft
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected theft of proprietary AI models, algorithms, or related intellectual property.

steps.title: Validate the theft indicator
steps.desc: Incident response assesses the triggering signal to determine whether it plausibly indicates theft of AI/algorithm intellectual property.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Scope the affected AI assets
steps.desc: Determine which models, algorithms, or related artifacts are implicated and their competitive significance.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of investigation.

steps.title: Revoke access and close the exposure vector
steps.desc: Revoke compromised access and remediate the vulnerability or misconfiguration responsible.
steps.outcome: Further exposure is halted.

steps.title: Preserve evidence
steps.desc: Issue a legal hold and preserve relevant logs and system state.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for potential legal action.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies
steps.desc: Legal evaluates appropriate remedies against the identified party.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal action pursued.

steps.title: Confirm removal of exposed material from external reach
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, confirm that the exposed intellectual property has been removed from or is no longer reachable by the external party (e.g., takedown request, injunction compliance check).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction or removal of the external party's continued access to the stolen material.

steps.title: Strengthen AI-asset protection controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced access controls and monitoring around AI models and algorithms.
steps.outcome: Strengthened protections reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Reassess classification and labeling of related intellectual property
steps.desc: Review the classification and access-labeling of related, not-yet-exposed intellectual property to ensure consistent protection standards are applied.
steps.outcome: Consistent classification and protection applied to related IP assets.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52411.def: A multi-stage, persistent intrusion campaign exhibiting advanced-persistent-threat tradecraft — careful operational security, long dwell time, and deliberate, targeted collection — used to classify cyber espionage activity within this Tier-3 category independent of whether the sponsor has been formally attributed to a specific state (see ITID-5221x for attributed nation-state cases).
ITID-52411.purpose: Captures a sustained, technically sophisticated intrusion operated for long-term covert intelligence collection, classified under Cyber Espionage Operations regardless of confirmed nation-state attribution.
scopeIncludes: Multi-stage intrusions exhibiting long-dwell, low-noise operational tradecraft aimed at covert collection
Campaigns not yet attributed to a specific tracked actor but exhibiting clear APT-grade sophistication
scopeExcludes: Campaigns formally attributed to a specific tracked nation-state APT group (ITID-52211) or contracted cyber-mercenary group (ITID-52212)
Opportunistic, low-sophistication intrusions
ITID-52411.severity: Critical, reflecting the sophistication and persistence implied by APT-grade tradecraft.
ITID-52411.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and threat intelligence; engage external incident response support for full-scope investigation.
indicators: Custom or rarely-seen tooling with careful anti-forensic behavior
Long dwell time discovered upon investigation
Deliberate, selective collection rather than broad opportunistic access
vectors: Spearphishing with custom malware
Exploitation of internet-facing vulnerabilities followed by careful, low-noise lateral movement
Living-off-the-land technique use to minimize detection footprint
rootCauses: Insufficient long-dwell-time detection capability (log retention, behavioral analytics)
Gaps in lateral-movement detection across network segments
controls: Extended log retention for long-dwell investigation
Behavioral/EDR detection tuned for low-noise lateral movement
ITID-52411.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; strong technical detection surface exists across the intrusion lifecycle, with dwell time being the primary challenge rather than raw signal availability.
ITID-52411.response: Run a full-scope forensic investigation assuming long dwell time; reclassify to ITID-52211/52212 if attribution is later confirmed.
metrics: Dwell time from initial access to detection
ITID-52411.notes: Distinguished from ITID-52211/52212 by the absence of confirmed attribution; reclassify once attribution is established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General APT Cyber Espionage Operation
playbook.description: An advanced persistent threat actor is discovered conducting a cyber espionage operation against the organization, not yet formally attributed to a specific nation-state.

steps.title: Confirm APT activity and establish dwell time
steps.desc: Incident response and threat intelligence confirm indicators of a sophisticated, persistent intrusion and reconstruct dwell time across the environment.
steps.guidance: Assume broader compromise than initially observed; APT operations frequently maintain multiple footholds.
steps.outcome: A confirmed scope of compromise and dwell-time assessment.

steps.title: Determine data and systems accessed
steps.desc: Reconstruct what data was accessed, staged, or exfiltrated across the compromised environment.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive exposure assessment.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and Legal
steps.desc: Notify executive leadership and Legal given the sophistication and potential business impact of an APT operation.
steps.outcome: Leadership and Legal informed and coordinating.

steps.title: Coordinate containment sequencing to avoid tipping off the actor
steps.desc: Plan a coordinated containment action across all identified footholds simultaneously to prevent the actor from re-establishing access via a missed foothold.
steps.outcome: An approved, coordinated containment plan.
steps.abort: Escalate to immediate isolation if active, high-impact exfiltration is detected.

steps.title: Eradicate all identified persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors, implants, and persistence mechanisms in a coordinated eradication event.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms are removed.

steps.title: Conduct a full-environment sweep for missed indicators of compromise
steps.desc: Run a comprehensive, environment-wide sweep using updated indicators of compromise to confirm no additional footholds remain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of additional footholds across the environment.

steps.title: Rebuild and validate affected systems
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-good sources, rotate all potentially exposed credentials, and validate integrity before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Affected systems restored and verified clean.

steps.title: Validate monitoring coverage before full restoration
steps.desc: Validate that detection and monitoring coverage for the affected systems is fully operational before returning them to normal production use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed monitoring coverage prior to full restoration.

steps.title: Conduct a comprehensive after-action review
steps.desc: Produce a detailed after-action report, share indicators of compromise with appropriate partners, and brief leadership on strategic implications.
steps.outcome: Improved detection capability for future APT activity.

ITID-52421.def: The deliberate, low-noise exfiltration of collected data through covert channels — encrypted C2 tunnels, alternative protocols, or staged small-volume transfers — designed to evade data-loss-prevention and network-monitoring controls.
ITID-52421.purpose: Captures the covert channel and method used to move collected data out of the environment during a cyber espionage operation, as distinct from the collection activity itself.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration over an established command-and-control channel rather than a legitimate business data-transfer path
Use of alternative or non-standard protocols/ports to move data out undetected
Deliberately staged, low-and-slow exfiltration to avoid volume-based detection thresholds
scopeExcludes: Exfiltration specifically using steganographic encoding (ITID-52441)
The initial collection/staging of data prior to exfiltration, tracked as part of the broader campaign leaf (ITID-52411)
ITID-52421.severity: Critical, since successful covert exfiltration typically confirms that sensitive data has already left the environment.
ITID-52421.priority: P1 upon detection of the exfiltration channel.
ITID-52421.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal and executive leadership; treat data as compromised even if the destination or recipient is not yet identified.
indicators: Outbound traffic to C2 infrastructure carrying encrypted or encoded payloads
Low-and-slow outbound transfer patterns evading volume-based DLP thresholds
Use of non-standard ports or protocols for outbound data transfer
vectors: Exfiltration over an existing C2 channel
Exfiltration over an alternative protocol not typically monitored for data loss
rootCauses: DLP tuned only for high-volume transfers, missing low-and-slow patterns
Insufficient egress monitoring for non-standard protocols/ports
controls: Egress monitoring for non-standard protocols and low-and-slow transfer patterns
DLP thresholds tuned for both high-volume and low-and-slow exfiltration
ITID-52421.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; network egress monitoring is the primary technical detection surface, with low-and-slow patterns being the most common coverage gap.
ITID-52421.response: Assume any data reaching the exfiltration channel has left the environment; determine content and scope for breach notification assessment.
metrics: Volume of data confirmed exfiltrated per incident
Time from exfiltration onset to detection
ITID-52421.notes: Scoped narrowly to the exfiltration channel/mechanism itself, distinct from the broader campaign classification (ITID-52411) and from steganographic exfiltration (ITID-52441).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Covert Data Exfiltration (Cyber Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have covertly exfiltrated data from the organization's environment using techniques designed to evade standard detection.

steps.title: Confirm covert exfiltration activity
steps.desc: Incident response identifies and confirms indicators of covert data exfiltration (e.g., unusual outbound traffic patterns, use of covert channels, or DLP anomalies).
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination that covert exfiltration occurred.

steps.title: Determine data exfiltrated and destination
steps.desc: Identify what data was exfiltrated and, where possible, the destination or likely recipient of the data.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Block the exfiltration channel
steps.desc: Block the identified exfiltration channel (network destination, protocol, or covert mechanism) at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via the identified channel is halted.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems and revoke compromised access
steps.desc: Isolate the systems involved in the exfiltration and revoke any compromised credentials or access.
steps.outcome: The compromised systems no longer pose an exfiltration risk.

steps.title: Eradicate the exfiltration mechanism and any persistence
steps.desc: Remove the technical mechanism used for exfiltration and any associated persistence or backdoor.
steps.outcome: The exfiltration mechanism is fully removed.

steps.title: Conduct a full-environment sweep for missed indicators of compromise
steps.desc: Run a comprehensive, environment-wide sweep using updated indicators of compromise to confirm no additional footholds remain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of additional footholds across the environment.

steps.title: Restore systems and enhance exfiltration-detection controls
steps.desc: Restore affected systems and implement enhanced DLP and network-monitoring controls to detect similar covert exfiltration in the future.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with strengthened detection capability.

steps.title: Validate monitoring coverage before full restoration
steps.desc: Validate that detection and monitoring coverage for the affected systems is fully operational before returning them to normal production use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed monitoring coverage prior to full restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52431.def: Espionage in which an adversary compromises a supplier, software vendor, or service provider trusted by the target organization, using that trust relationship as the initial access vector into the target's environment.
ITID-52431.purpose: Captures cyber espionage carried out by compromising a trusted vendor, supplier, or software dependency to reach the actual target organization.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of a software update mechanism or vendor-distributed component subsequently used to access the target
Compromise of a managed service provider or vendor with privileged access to the target's environment
scopeExcludes: Direct intrusion into the target's own environment with no supply-chain intermediary
ITID-52431.severity: Critical, given that supply-chain compromise typically bypasses perimeter controls and can affect many downstream organizations simultaneously.
ITID-52431.priority: P1 upon confirmation of a supply-chain vector.
ITID-52431.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and the affected vendor immediately; coordinate disclosure carefully given potential impact to other downstream customers of the same vendor.
indicators: Malicious code introduced via a vendor software update or component
Unusual activity originating from a vendor/MSP account or connection
Indicators shared by threat intelligence linking the vendor to a broader supply-chain campaign
vectors: Compromised software update or build pipeline at a trusted vendor
Compromised MSP/vendor remote-access credentials used to pivot into the target
rootCauses: Insufficient vetting and monitoring of vendor/MSP access
No integrity verification for third-party software updates
controls: Vendor/MSP access review and least-privilege scoping
Software supply-chain integrity verification (code signing, SBOM review)
ITID-52431.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; detection depends heavily on monitoring vendor/MSP access paths specifically, which is frequently a coverage gap relative to direct-access monitoring.
ITID-52431.response: Assess and, if necessary, suspend the vendor/MSP access path while investigating; coordinate with the vendor on joint remediation.
metrics: Number of supply-chain-vector incidents per year
Percentage of critical vendors with access reviewed in the past 12 months
ITID-52431.notes: Cross-reference the organization's broader third-party/vendor risk program, since supply-chain espionage incidents frequently surface through vendor risk monitoring rather than internal SOC telemetry alone.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Espionage
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have compromised a supplier, vendor, or software dependency in the organization's supply chain as a vector for espionage against the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the supply-chain compromise and affected component
steps.desc: Incident response, in coordination with the vendor and third-party risk team, confirms which supplier, software component, or vendor relationship was compromised and used as an entry vector.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the vendor's own security team; supply-chain incidents often require joint investigation across organizational boundaries.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the compromised component and how it connects to the organization's environment.
steps.tool: SIEM; software composition analysis; vendor incident reports

steps.title: Scope internal exposure resulting from the compromised component
steps.desc: Determine which internal systems, data, or processes were exposed as a result of the compromised supply-chain component.
steps.outcome: A documented internal exposure assessment.

steps.title: Isolate or disable the compromised component/vendor connection
steps.desc: Isolate, disable, or restrict the compromised software component, integration, or vendor network connection pending remediation.
steps.outcome: The supply-chain vector is no longer usable for further access.
steps.tool: Network segmentation controls; vendor access management

steps.title: Notify affected internal stakeholders and coordinate with the vendor
steps.desc: Notify internal stakeholders reliant on the affected component and coordinate remediation timing and disclosure with the vendor.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed and vendor coordination underway.

steps.title: Remediate or replace the compromised component
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's patch, replace the compromised component, or terminate the vendor relationship if remediation is insufficient.
steps.outcome: The compromised component is fully remediated or removed.

steps.title: Conduct a full-environment sweep for missed indicators of compromise
steps.desc: Run a comprehensive, environment-wide sweep using updated indicators of compromise to confirm no additional footholds remain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of additional footholds across the environment.

steps.title: Reassess third-party risk management controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen third-party/vendor security assessment and monitoring practices for similarly positioned suppliers.
steps.outcome: Strengthened supply-chain risk management posture.

steps.title: Validate monitoring coverage before full restoration
steps.desc: Validate that detection and monitoring coverage for the affected systems is fully operational before returning them to normal production use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed monitoring coverage prior to full restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership and procurement/vendor-management teams
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership and procurement teams on findings and control improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52441.def: Exfiltration in which stolen data is embedded within seemingly innocuous carrier files (images, documents, media) using steganographic or other data-obfuscation techniques, specifically to evade content-inspection and DLP controls.
ITID-52441.purpose: Captures the use of steganography or other data-hiding techniques to conceal stolen data within innocuous-looking files during a cyber espionage operation.
scopeIncludes: Data embedded within image, audio, or document files using steganographic techniques prior to exfiltration
Use of obfuscation/encoding specifically intended to defeat content-based DLP inspection
scopeExcludes: Exfiltration over a covert network channel without steganographic content encoding (ITID-52421)
ITID-52441.severity: Critical, since the deliberate use of steganography indicates a sophisticated actor specifically evading standard DLP controls.
ITID-52441.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; treat data as compromised and reassess DLP content-inspection capability given the demonstrated evasion.
indicators: Outbound files with anomalous entropy or size inconsistent with their apparent content type
Detection tooling flagging statistical anomalies consistent with steganographic encoding
Correlation with other espionage campaign indicators (e.g., attributed APT activity)
vectors: Steganographic embedding of data within image or media files transferred via normal-looking channels
Use of alternate data streams or file-format metadata fields to hide data
rootCauses: DLP content inspection limited to plaintext/pattern matching, missing encoded or embedded content
No entropy-based or statistical anomaly detection on outbound files
controls: Entropy/statistical anomaly detection on outbound file transfers
Advanced DLP with steganography-aware content inspection
ITID-52441.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; this is a genuinely difficult technical detection problem, and most organizations should treat entropy-based anomaly detection as a maturing rather than fully solved capability.
ITID-52441.response: Attempt to recover and decode the carrier files to determine what data was exfiltrated; reassess DLP capability given the demonstrated evasion technique.
metrics: Number of steganographic exfiltration cases detected per year
ITID-52441.notes: This is a genuinely difficult detection surface; be honest in reporting about the maturity gap in steganography-aware DLP rather than overstating coverage.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Steganographic Data Theft (Cyber Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An actor is discovered to be exfiltrating data by embedding it within seemingly innocuous files or media (steganography) to evade detection.

steps.title: Confirm steganographic exfiltration technique
steps.desc: Digital forensics analyzes suspected carrier files (images, audio, documents) to confirm the presence of hidden embedded data, using steganalysis techniques.
steps.guidance: Standard DLP content inspection typically misses steganographic payloads; specialized steganalysis tools are usually required to confirm this technique.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination that steganography was used and identification of the carrier file type/pattern.
steps.abort: If steganalysis is inconclusive, treat as a suspected covert exfiltration and continue investigation via other means.

steps.title: Determine the scope of data hidden and exfiltrated
steps.desc: Extract and analyze the hidden payload where possible to determine what data was exfiltrated via this method.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Block the exfiltration channel and carrier-file pathway
steps.desc: Block the outbound channel (email, cloud upload, messaging platform) used to move the carrier files, and restrict the responsible account's access.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via the identified channel is halted.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the carrier files and related system/account evidence under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and admissible.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and pursue appropriate action
steps.desc: Determine whether the actor was an insider or external intruder and take appropriate personnel or legal action.
steps.outcome: Root cause addressed.

steps.title: Conduct a full-environment sweep for missed indicators of compromise
steps.desc: Run a comprehensive, environment-wide sweep using updated indicators of compromise to confirm no additional footholds remain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of additional footholds across the environment.

steps.title: Enhance content-inspection and steganalysis detection capability
steps.desc: Implement or enhance DLP/content-inspection controls with steganalysis capability for high-risk file types and channels.
steps.outcome: Improved future detection capability for steganographic exfiltration.

steps.title: Validate monitoring coverage before full restoration
steps.desc: Validate that detection and monitoring coverage for the affected systems is fully operational before returning them to normal production use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed monitoring coverage prior to full restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52511.def: The development, customization, or acquisition of keylogging software or hardware intended for use in an espionage operation, classified at the development/tooling stage rather than the deployment/collection stage.
ITID-52511.purpose: Captures the development or acquisition of custom keylogging capability specifically to support an espionage operation, as distinct from its deployment.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of custom keylogger source code or build artifacts associated with the organization or a known actor targeting it
Procurement or development activity for keylogging capability tied to a suspected espionage operation
scopeExcludes: Active deployment and use of a keylogger against a specific target, which is tracked under the relevant deployed-malware/insider-threat leaf elsewhere in the taxonomy
ITID-52511.severity: Medium at the development stage, escalating sharply once evidence of intended or actual deployment emerges.
ITID-52511.priority: P2 at the development-detection stage; escalate to P1 immediately upon any evidence of deployment.
ITID-52511.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence and legal upon discovery; treat as a precursor requiring proactive threat hunting for deployment, not just documentation.
indicators: Discovery of custom keylogger code in a threat actor's toolkit via threat intelligence
Suspicious development activity on an endpoint (e.g., a compromised developer workstation) producing input-capture code with no legitimate business purpose
vectors: Custom malware development incorporating input-capture functionality
Modification of legitimate remote-access or monitoring software to add covert keylogging
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring for anomalous development activity on endpoints with elevated privileges
Reliance on signature-based detection that custom tooling is designed to evade
controls: Threat hunting for input-capture behavior on endpoints
Behavioral EDR detection for keystroke-hooking activity
ITID-52511.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; the development stage itself has limited SOC visibility and is most often surfaced via threat intelligence, while the deployment stage (tracked elsewhere) has stronger EDR-based detection coverage.
ITID-52511.response: Treat discovery as a signal to proactively threat-hunt for deployment; do not close the case on documentation of development alone.
metrics: Time from development-stage discovery to deployment threat hunt completion
ITID-52511.notes: The T1056.001 mapping applies to the development/tooling context described by this leaf; deployed keylogger use against a specific victim is tracked under the applicable deployed-malware leaf elsewhere in the taxonomy.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Keylogger Development for Espionage
playbook.description: Evidence indicates an actor developed or deployed a keylogging tool against organizational systems or personnel as a precursor to a broader espionage effort.

steps.title: Confirm keylogger presence and scope
steps.desc: Endpoint security confirms the presence of a keylogging tool on affected system(s) and determines how long it may have been active.
steps.guidance: Keyloggers are often discovered incidentally during unrelated endpoint investigation; treat discovery as a trigger to investigate what was captured and correlate with any subsequent targeting.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of keylogger presence, type, and active duration.

steps.title: Determine what credentials or information may have been captured
steps.desc: Assess what accounts, credentials, or sensitive information the affected user(s) typed during the keylogger's active period.
steps.outcome: A bounded assessment of likely captured information.

steps.title: Remove the keylogger and isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the affected endpoint from the network and remove the keylogging tool.
steps.outcome: The keylogger is no longer capturing data.

steps.title: Rotate all potentially captured credentials
steps.desc: Force password resets and MFA re-enrollment for all accounts the affected user accessed during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: No captured credential remains valid.

steps.title: Determine and remediate the infection vector
steps.desc: Investigate how the keylogger was installed (phishing, physical access, insider) and remediate the root cause.
steps.outcome: The infection vector is closed.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting and heighten protective posture
steps.desc: Review whether the affected individual has experienced or is likely to experience follow-on targeting using the captured information, and heighten monitoring accordingly.
steps.guidance: Treat keylogger discovery as a precursor indicator warranting elevated protective posture for the affected individual, not just a closed technical incident.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place for the affected individual and accounts.

steps.title: Extend awareness briefing to adjacent teams
steps.desc: Extend the awareness briefing beyond the immediately affected individual(s) to adjacent teams or roles who may face similar targeting.
steps.outcome: Broader organizational awareness of the observed reconnaissance tactic.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings and improvements to endpoint detection.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52521.def: Social-engineering reconnaissance in which an adversary places a phone call using a false pretext — vendor, recruiter, journalist, or internal-sounding caller — to elicit organizational structure, reporting lines, or process detail from an employee.
ITID-52521.purpose: Captures a phone-based pretext call used to elicit information about the organization's structure, personnel, or processes.
scopeIncludes: A phone call using a fabricated identity/purpose to extract organizational or process information
A pattern of similar calls across multiple employees consistent with a coordinated reconnaissance effort
scopeExcludes: In-person pretexting at an industry event (ITID-52131)

A pretext call that also attempts to obtain credentials or immediate account access, which should additionally be tracked as a vishing/social-engineering intrusion attempt in the relevant Data Breaches or Fraud domain leaf
ITID-52521.severity: Medium, escalating to High where the elicited information appears to support a subsequent, more serious operation.
ITID-52521.priority: P2, escalating to P1 upon evidence of a coordinated, repeated campaign.
ITID-52521.escalation: Escalate to security awareness/insider risk for employee debrief and organization-wide alerting; escalate to threat intelligence to check for related campaign indicators.
indicators: Employee report of an unusual call asking pointed questions about org structure, reporting lines, or internal processes
Caller ID spoofing or a caller unable to substantiate their claimed organization when challenged
Multiple employees receiving similar calls in a short window
vectors: Vishing (voice phishing) call using a fabricated pretext to elicit organizational information
Caller ID spoofing to appear as an internal or trusted external number
rootCauses: Insufficient employee training on verifying caller identity before disclosing organizational information
No centralized reporting channel for suspicious calls, limiting pattern detection
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Employee awareness training on caller verification and vishing
Centralized suspicious-contact reporting channel
ITID-52521.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; reliant on employee reporting and pattern correlation across reports.
ITID-52521.response: Debrief the employee on what was disclosed; log the call for pattern tracking and alert other employees if a coordinated campaign is suspected.
metrics: Number of suspicious-call reports per quarter
ITID-52521.notes: Differentiated from its siblings by the phone/voice channel specifically; escalate to the appropriate fraud/intrusion leaf if the call also attempts credential or account access.

playbook.name: Pretext Phone Call for Organizational Structure Reconnaissance
playbook.description: An employee reports receiving a suspicious pretext phone call attempting to elicit information about organizational structure, reporting lines, or personnel, consistent with reconnaissance for a later espionage or social-engineering operation.

steps.title: Debrief the employee and document the pretext call
steps.desc: Security interviews the reporting employee to capture the caller's pretext, questions asked, and any identifying details (phone number, claimed affiliation, voice characteristics).
steps.guidance: This is identified retrospectively via employee self-report; make reporting easy and non-punitive.
steps.outcome: A documented record of the pretext call and information sought.

steps.title: Correlate with other reports for a targeting pattern
steps.desc: Check whether other employees have received similar pretext calls, to determine whether this is an isolated event or a broader reconnaissance campaign.
steps.outcome: A determination of whether a pattern exists across multiple employees or departments.

steps.title: Alert potentially targeted departments and heighten vigilance
steps.desc: Notify the department(s) or roles likely to be targeted next based on the information sought, and provide guidance on handling similar calls.
steps.outcome: Increased vigilance and reduced likelihood of further successful elicitation.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Pretext Phone Call for Organizational Structure Reconnaissance" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Block or flag the identified contact information where feasible
steps.desc: Where the caller's number or claimed affiliation is identified, flag it in relevant systems and consider notifying phone-system administrators.
steps.outcome: Reduced ability for the same actor to repeat the pretext call successfully.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor for any follow-on targeting (phishing, physical approach, further pretext contact) directed at the individuals or department involved.
steps.guidance: Treat this as a precursor indicator warranting a period of heightened monitoring, not a standalone closed incident.
steps.outcome: Any follow-on targeting is detected earlier due to the established correlation.

steps.title: Update social-engineering awareness training
steps.desc: Incorporate the pretext tactic observed into employee security-awareness training, particularly for front-line and administrative staff.
steps.outcome: Improved employee resilience to future pretext-calling attempts.

ITID-52522.def: Social-engineering reconnaissance in which an adversary poses as a legitimate researcher, journalist, or industry analyst conducting a survey or interview, using the pretext to elicit strategic, technical, or organizational information from employees.
ITID-52522.purpose: Captures the use of a fabricated industry survey, research study, or interview request as a pretext for eliciting sensitive information.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated survey/interview request targeting employees for strategic or technical detail
Use of a fake research organization, publication, or analyst persona to add legitimacy to the request
scopeExcludes: A pretext delivered by phone specifically without a survey/interview framing (ITID-52521)
In-person pretexting at an industry event (ITID-52131)
ITID-52522.severity: Medium, escalating to High where the survey elicited genuinely sensitive strategic or technical detail.
ITID-52522.priority: P2, escalating to P1 upon evidence of a coordinated, repeated campaign.
ITID-52522.escalation: Escalate to security awareness/insider risk for employee debrief and organization-wide alerting.
indicators: Employee report of a survey/interview request seeking unusually specific technical or strategic detail
Requesting organization or publication that cannot be verified as legitimate
Similar requests received by multiple employees, especially in technical or strategic roles
vectors: Unsolicited survey or interview request via email or professional networking platform
Fabricated research organization or publication used to lend credibility
rootCauses: Insufficient employee training on verifying external research/media requests before participating
No policy requiring communications/PR sign-off before employees engage with external researchers or journalists
mitreTechniques: T1591.002 Gather Victim Org Information: Business Relationships
controls: Policy requiring communications/PR review before employee participation in external research or media requests
Employee awareness training on pretexting via survey/interview requests
ITID-52522.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; reliant on employee reporting and verification of the requesting organization.
ITID-52522.response: Verify the legitimacy of the requesting organization; debrief the employee on what was disclosed if participation already occurred.
metrics: Number of suspicious survey/interview requests reported per quarter
ITID-52522.notes: Differentiated from its siblings by the survey/interview pretext specifically, which often targets technical or strategic roles more precisely than a general cold call.

playbook.name: Fake Industry Survey/Interview for Intelligence Gathering
playbook.description: An employee is targeted with a fabricated industry survey, research study, or media interview request designed to elicit confidential business information under a plausible pretext.

steps.title: Debrief the employee and evaluate the survey/interview legitimacy
steps.desc: Security and Communications review the survey or interview request, verifying the purported organization's legitimacy and the nature of questions asked.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Communications, since legitimate media/analyst inquiries pass through official channels; deviation from those channels is a red flag.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of whether the survey/interview was a pretext for intelligence gathering.
steps.abort: If it is determined legitimate, close with no further action.

steps.title: Assess what information may have already been disclosed
steps.desc: Review what the employee shared, if anything, before recognizing the pretext.
steps.outcome: A bounded assessment of any disclosed information.

steps.title: Brief affected employee and relevant department
steps.desc: Brief the targeted employee and their department on the tactic observed and appropriate response for future similar requests.
steps.outcome: Increased awareness and reduced likelihood of further disclosure.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Fake Industry Survey/Interview for Intelligence Gathering" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Route future inquiries through official channels
steps.desc: Reinforce policy that all media, survey, and analyst inquiries be routed through Communications/Investor Relations before any response.
steps.outcome: Reduced future risk of similar pretext-based elicitation.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor for follow-on targeting of the same employee or department using information potentially obtained.
steps.outcome: Any follow-on targeting is detected earlier.

steps.title: Update security-awareness training on pretext inquiries
steps.desc: Incorporate the observed tactic into training materials on handling unsolicited survey/interview/research requests.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational resilience to future pretext-based inquiries.

ITID-52523.def: Social-engineering reconnaissance in which an adversary creates or uses professional networking (e.g., LinkedIn-style) profiles to systematically connect with an organization's employees, building a map of personnel, roles, and relationships to support later targeting.
ITID-52523.purpose: Captures the systematic use of fake or opportunistic professional-network connections to map an organization's employees and reporting structure.
scopeIncludes: A pattern of connection requests from suspicious or fabricated profiles targeting the organization's employees
Use of harvested connection data to build an organizational target map
scopeExcludes: Passive review of already-public professional profiles without an active connection/farming campaign (ITID-52532 Social Media Profile Aggregation)
ITID-52523.severity: Medium, escalating to High when correlated with a subsequent targeted campaign.
ITID-52523.priority: P2, escalating to P1 when the mapping is confirmed as precursor activity to an active campaign.
ITID-52523.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence for correlation with active campaigns; advise affected employees on the specific fabricated profiles identified.
indicators: A cluster of connection requests from newly-created or sparse profiles targeting employees in specific, sensitive roles
Fabricated profile details (employer, credentials) that do not withstand verification
Reports from multiple employees of the same or similar suspicious profile
vectors: Fabricated professional-network profile used to connect broadly with employees
Automated or semi-automated connection farming targeting specific roles or departments
rootCauses: Insufficient employee awareness of connection-farming reconnaissance
No process to report and track suspicious professional-network contact
mitreTechniques: T1593.001 Search Open Websites/Domains: Social Media
T1591.004 Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
controls: Employee awareness training on connection-farming reconnaissance
Suspicious professional-network contact reporting channel
ITID-52523.detection: Minimal direct technical detection since the activity occurs on third-party platforms; detection relies on employee reporting and, where available, threat intelligence monitoring of professional-network abuse patterns.
ITID-52523.response: Report fabricated profiles to the hosting platform; correlate with any subsequent targeted campaign.
metrics: Number of suspicious connection-farming reports per quarter
ITID-52523.notes: Differentiated from ITID-52532 by its active, connection-based data-gathering method rather than passive aggregation of already-public profile data.

playbook.name: LinkedIn/Social Network Connection Farming for Target Mapping
playbook.description: An actor is discovered to be systematically farming professional social-network connections with employees to map organizational structure and identify high-value targets for a future espionage operation.

steps.title: Identify and assess the connection-farming pattern
steps.desc: Security reviews reported suspicious connection requests or profiles (e.g., fake recruiter profiles, minimal history, mass connection requests to employees in sensitive roles) to determine if this reflects deliberate target mapping.
steps.guidance: Often surfaces through an employee report or a security-awareness team's periodic social-media exposure review.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of whether a connection-farming campaign is underway and its apparent targeting focus.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Identify targeted employees and roles
steps.desc: Determine which employees or roles have been targeted by the suspicious profile(s), noting any pattern (e.g., focus on engineering, executive assistants, or a specific project team).
steps.outcome: A prioritized list of targeted individuals/roles.

steps.title: Brief targeted employees and recommend they disconnect/report the profile
steps.desc: Advise targeted employees to avoid engaging further, disconnect if already connected, and report the profile to the platform.
steps.outcome: Reduced ongoing engagement with the suspicious profile(s).

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "LinkedIn/Social Network Connection Farming for Target Mapping" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Report the profile(s) to the social-network platform
steps.desc: Report the fraudulent or suspicious profile(s) to the platform's trust-and-safety team for takedown.
steps.outcome: The profile is reported and, where the platform acts, removed.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor targeted employees for follow-on contact attempts (phishing, job offers, in-person approaches) that may build on the connection-mapping effort.
steps.guidance: Treat this as a precursor indicator warranting heightened protective posture.
steps.outcome: Improved early detection of follow-on targeting.

steps.title: Update social-media security-awareness guidance
steps.desc: Update employee guidance on evaluating and responding to unsolicited professional-network connection requests, particularly for employees in sensitive or externally visible roles.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational resilience to future connection-farming campaigns.

ITID-52524.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected social engineering reconnaissance pending determination of the specific method used (phone pretext, survey/interview, or connection farming).
ITID-52524.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected social engineering reconnaissance that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of social engineering reconnaissance prior to identifying the specific method
scopeExcludes: Any case where the method has already been established (ITID-52521/52522/52523)
ITID-52524.priority: P2 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52524.escalation: Escalate to security awareness/insider risk on initial suspicion.
indicators: General employee report of a suspicious contact without a clear method yet established
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52524.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52524.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the method is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52524.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Social Engineering Reconnaissance group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Social Engineering Reconnaissance
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected social-engineering reconnaissance directed against the organization or its personnel.

steps.title: Validate the reconnaissance indicator
steps.desc: Security assesses the reported or observed indicator to determine whether it plausibly reflects deliberate social-engineering reconnaissance.
steps.guidance: Recognize that identification here is often retrospective, based on employee reports or a pattern of related activity.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Identify targeted individuals and information sought
steps.desc: Determine which employees were targeted and what type of information the reconnaissance effort appeared to be seeking.
steps.outcome: A documented targeting and information-scope assessment.

steps.title: Brief affected individuals and heighten vigilance
steps.desc: Notify targeted employees and any others likely to be approached next, with guidance on responding to further contact.
