steps.outcome: Increased vigilance and reduced likelihood of successful follow-on elicitation.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Unclassified / General Social Engineering Reconnaissance" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Close the identified vector where feasible
steps.desc: Take appropriate action to reduce the effectiveness of the observed reconnaissance vector (e.g., reporting a fake profile, updating a public-facing information source).
steps.outcome: Reduced viability of the observed vector for further use.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor for follow-on targeting activity building on the reconnaissance observed.
steps.outcome: Improved early detection of follow-on targeting.

steps.title: Update security-awareness training
steps.desc: Incorporate observed tactics into employee security-awareness training.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational resilience to future social-engineering reconnaissance.

ITID-52531.def: OSINT reconnaissance in which an adversary systematically collects and analyzes public job postings, employee titles, and organizational structure signals to infer reporting lines, technology stack, and likely high-value targets.
ITID-52531.purpose: Captures the systematic mining of an organization's public job postings and inferred org chart to build a reconnaissance profile.
scopeIncludes: Systematic collection of job postings to infer technology stack, team structure, or upcoming initiatives
Correlation of job postings with employee profiles to build an org chart
scopeExcludes: Aggregation focused on social media profiles specifically (ITID-52532)
One-off review of a single job posting with no systematic collection
ITID-52531.severity: Low-Medium in isolation, escalating to High when correlated with a subsequent targeted campaign.
ITID-52531.priority: P3 for isolated activity; P1 when confirmed as precursor to an active campaign.
ITID-52531.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence for correlation with active campaigns.
indicators: Automated or high-volume scraping of the organization's careers page or job-board postings
A subsequent phishing or approach campaign referencing detail (technology stack, team names) only available through job postings
vectors: Automated scraping of careers pages and job-board listings
Manual correlation of job postings with employee LinkedIn profiles
rootCauses: Job postings disclosing excessive technical or organizational detail
No monitoring for automated scraping of the careers page
mitreTechniques: T1591.004 Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
controls: Job posting content review to minimize technical/organizational detail disclosure
Web scraping detection on public-facing careers pages
ITID-52531.detection: Limited direct detection since the activity occurs largely outside owned infrastructure; best detected via web analytics scraping detection and correlating downstream campaigns back to likely precursors.
ITID-52531.response: Reduce excessive technical detail in job postings; correlate with any subsequent targeted campaign.
metrics: Number of OSINT-precursor correlations made per quarter
ITID-52531.notes: Differentiated from ITID-52532 by its focus on job-posting/org-structure data specifically rather than employee social media content.

playbook.name: Public Job Posting/Org Chart Mining for Reconnaissance
playbook.description: An actor is discovered to be systematically mining the organization's public job postings and inferred organizational structure to build a targeting profile for a future espionage operation.

steps.title: Identify the mining activity and its apparent focus
steps.desc: Security reviews the indicator (e.g., a tip, discovered dossier, or unusual scraping activity against careers pages) to determine the apparent focus of the mining effort (specific teams, technologies, or seniority levels).
steps.guidance: Often surfaces retrospectively, after related targeting (phishing tailored to a specific team, or a suspicious approach) reveals prior reconnaissance.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the mining activity's scope and apparent focus.

steps.title: Assess what sensitive information job postings may have revealed
steps.desc: Review recent job postings for the implicated teams to identify whether overly detailed postings (technology stack, project names, org structure) contributed to the exposure.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of information exposure via job postings.

steps.title: Reduce sensitive detail in public job postings
steps.desc: Work with HR/Talent Acquisition to reduce overly specific technical or organizational detail in public job postings going forward.
steps.outcome: Reduced future exposure of sensitive organizational detail via job postings.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Public Job Posting/Org Chart Mining for Reconnaissance" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Heighten protective posture for identified at-risk teams
steps.desc: Brief the teams identified as the apparent focus of the mining effort and heighten monitoring for follow-on targeting.
steps.outcome: Increased vigilance for the affected teams.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor for follow-on targeting attempts directed at the identified teams or individuals.
steps.outcome: Improved early detection of follow-on targeting.

steps.title: Update job-posting and public-information disclosure guidelines
steps.desc: Update HR and Communications guidelines on the level of organizational detail appropriate for public disclosure.
steps.outcome: Reduced future OSINT exposure via public postings.

ITID-52532.def: OSINT reconnaissance in which an adversary systematically collects and cross-references employees' social media content — posts, photos, connections, location check-ins — to build a targeting profile.
ITID-52532.purpose: Captures the systematic aggregation of employee social media profiles to build a reconnaissance profile of a target individual or the organization.
scopeIncludes: Systematic collection and correlation of employee social media content across multiple platforms
Aggregation activity later found to precede a targeted phishing or physical-surveillance operation
scopeExcludes: Aggregation focused on job postings/org chart data specifically (ITID-52531)
Active connection-farming campaigns, which are tracked separately as a social-engineering reconnaissance method (ITID-52523)
ITID-52532.severity: Low-Medium in isolation, escalating to High when correlated with a subsequent targeted campaign, especially one involving physical surveillance.
ITID-52532.priority: P3 for isolated activity; P1 when confirmed as precursor to an active campaign.
ITID-52532.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence for campaign correlation; escalate to executive protection if a specific individual (especially an executive) appears to be the focus.
indicators: Coordinated, high-volume access to specific employees' social media profiles from a small set of accounts
A subsequent phishing, approach, or physical-surveillance event referencing detail only available through aggregated social media content
vectors: Manual or automated aggregation of public social media content across platforms
Cross-referencing social media detail (location, routine, relationships) to support targeting
rootCauses: Excessive personal detail shared publicly by employees, particularly those in sensitive or executive roles
No employee guidance on social media exposure risk for high-profile roles
mitreTechniques: T1593.001 Search Open Websites/Domains: Social Media
controls: Employee guidance on social media exposure for sensitive/executive roles
Threat intelligence monitoring for targeted OSINT aggregation of key personnel
ITID-52532.detection: Limited direct detection since the activity occurs on third-party platforms outside owned infrastructure; best detected via correlation with downstream targeting events.
ITID-52532.response: Correlate aggregation activity with any subsequent targeted campaign; advise affected individuals on exposure reduction.
metrics: Number of OSINT-precursor correlations made per quarter
ITID-52532.notes: This leaf carries elevated risk when the target is an executive, since aggregated social media content can directly enable physical surveillance (see Physical Surveillance, ITID-5254x).

playbook.name: Social Media Profile Aggregation for Target Reconnaissance
playbook.description: An actor is discovered to have systematically aggregated employees' social media profiles and posts to build detailed targeting profiles in support of a future espionage or social-engineering operation.

steps.title: Identify the aggregation activity and affected employees
steps.desc: Security investigates the indicator (a discovered dossier, employee report, or related targeting attempt referencing personal details) to confirm social-media aggregation occurred and identify affected employees.
steps.guidance: Often identified retrospectively after a phishing or approach attempt reveals unusually detailed personal knowledge.
steps.outcome: A confirmed assessment of the aggregation activity and affected individuals.

steps.title: Assess the sensitivity of aggregated information
steps.desc: Determine what categories of personal and professional information were aggregated and how they might be leveraged for follow-on targeting.
steps.outcome: A documented sensitivity assessment.

steps.title: Brief affected employees and provide privacy-hardening guidance
steps.desc: Notify affected employees and provide guidance on reviewing and tightening their social-media privacy settings.
steps.outcome: Reduced future exposure of personal information.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Social Media Profile Aggregation for Target Reconnaissance" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Heighten monitoring for the affected employees
steps.desc: Place affected employees on a heightened-monitoring watchlist for phishing or other follow-on targeting attempts.
steps.outcome: Improved detection capability for follow-on targeting.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor for follow-on phishing, social-engineering, or approach attempts using the aggregated information.
steps.outcome: Any follow-on targeting is detected earlier.

steps.title: Update employee digital-footprint and privacy training
steps.desc: Update security-awareness training on managing personal digital footprint and privacy settings, particularly for at-risk roles.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational resilience to future OSINT aggregation.

ITID-52533.def: OSINT reconnaissance in which an adversary systematically analyzes public financial filings, regulatory disclosures, and patent databases to infer strategic direction, R&D priorities, or financial position ahead of a targeted operation.
ITID-52533.purpose: Captures the systematic mining of public financial filings and patent databases to extract competitively or strategically valuable intelligence.
scopeIncludes: Systematic cross-referencing of financial filings and patent applications to infer undisclosed strategic direction
Correlation of filing/patent data with other OSINT to refine a targeting or investment thesis
scopeExcludes: Ordinary, lawful competitive or investment analysis with no subsequent targeting or intrusion
General social media or job-posting aggregation (ITID-52531/52532)
ITID-52533.severity: Low-Medium in isolation, escalating to High when correlated with a subsequent targeted campaign, insider trading concern, or competitive intelligence operation.
ITID-52533.priority: P3 for isolated activity; P1 when confirmed as precursor to an active campaign.
ITID-52533.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence and legal for correlation with active campaigns or potential securities-law implications.
indicators: Systematic, automated collection of filings/patent data around specific business units or technologies
A subsequent targeted campaign or approach referencing strategic detail only inferable from aggregated filings
vectors: Automated scraping of regulatory filing and patent databases
Manual cross-referencing of filings with other public sources to infer strategic intent
rootCauses: Standard, unavoidable regulatory disclosure requirements creating an inherent OSINT surface
No monitoring for unusual aggregation activity around the organization's specific filings
controls: Threat intelligence monitoring for targeted OSINT aggregation around sensitive filings/patents
ITID-52533.detection: Minimal direct detection since the underlying data is required to be publicly disclosed; detection relies on correlating downstream campaigns back to likely OSINT precursors.
ITID-52533.response: Correlate aggregation activity with any subsequent targeted campaign; loop in legal where securities-law implications (e.g., pre-announcement trading) are possible.
metrics: Number of OSINT-precursor correlations made per quarter
ITID-52533.notes: Because the underlying filings and patent data are required disclosures, this leaf focuses on the systematic aggregation and its downstream use rather than the (unavoidable) existence of the data itself.

playbook.name: Public Financial Filing/Patent Database Mining for Intelligence
playbook.description: An actor is discovered to have systematically mined public financial filings and patent databases to extract competitively or strategically sensitive intelligence about the organization.

steps.title: Identify the mining activity and information categories accessed
steps.desc: Security and Legal/IP counsel review the indicator (e.g., a tip, discovered analysis referencing non-obvious combinations of filings, or unusual database query patterns) to confirm systematic mining occurred.
steps.guidance: Often surfaces indirectly, e.g., through a competitor's product announcement that closely mirrors patterns only derivable from combining multiple public filings.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the mining activity and information categories involved.

steps.title: Assess the strategic sensitivity of the information derivable
steps.desc: Work with Legal, IP counsel, and Investor Relations to assess how sensitive the derivable intelligence is and whether it reveals more than any single filing intended.
steps.outcome: A documented sensitivity assessment.

steps.title: Review future disclosure practices for aggregation risk
steps.desc: Work with Legal, IP counsel, and Investor Relations to review whether future filings can be structured to reduce unintended aggregation risk while maintaining compliance.
steps.outcome: Reduced future exposure via public-filing aggregation.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Public Financial Filing/Patent Database Mining for Intelligence" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Assess competitive impact and adjust strategy if warranted
steps.desc: Determine whether business or IP strategy (e.g., filing timing, product roadmap communication) should be adjusted in light of the exposure.
steps.outcome: Appropriate business adjustments made where warranted.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with competitor activity for further indicators
steps.desc: Monitor competitor activity for signs that the aggregated intelligence is being acted upon, informing future defensive measures.
steps.outcome: Improved situational awareness of competitor use of the aggregated intelligence.

steps.title: Document and brief Legal, IP, and Investor Relations leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and disclosure-practice improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52534.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected OSINT-based reconnaissance pending determination of the specific source exploited (job postings/org chart, social media, or financial/patent filings).
ITID-52534.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected OSINT exploitation that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of OSINT-based reconnaissance prior to identifying the specific source
scopeExcludes: Any case where the source has already been established (ITID-52531/52532/52533)
ITID-52534.priority: P3 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52534.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of unusual public-data aggregation activity without a confirmed source
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52534.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52534.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the source is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52534.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the OSINT Exploitation group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General OSINT Exploitation
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected open-source intelligence exploitation directed against the organization or its personnel.

steps.title: Validate the OSINT exploitation indicator
steps.desc: Security assesses the reported or observed indicator to determine whether it plausibly reflects deliberate OSINT-based targeting.
steps.guidance: Recognize that identification here is often retrospective.
steps.outcome: A documented decision on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Identify targeted individuals/information and the public sources involved
steps.desc: Determine which individuals or information categories were targeted and what public sources were leveraged.
steps.outcome: A documented targeting and source assessment.

steps.title: Reduce public exposure of the implicated information
steps.desc: Work with relevant teams to reduce unnecessary public exposure of the information category involved.
steps.outcome: Reduced future OSINT exposure.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Unclassified / General OSINT Exploitation" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Brief affected individuals and heighten protective posture
steps.desc: Notify affected individuals and heighten monitoring for follow-on targeting.
steps.outcome: Increased vigilance for affected individuals.

steps.title: Confirm removal or reporting of the reconnaissance artifact
steps.desc: Where a specific artifact enabled the reconnaissance (a fake profile, an overly detailed public posting, a discoverable document), confirm it has been reported, removed, or corrected.
steps.outcome: The specific reconnaissance-enabling artifact is no longer accessible.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeting activity
steps.desc: Monitor for follow-on targeting building on the OSINT exploitation observed.
steps.outcome: Improved early detection of follow-on targeting.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52541.def: Physical surveillance in which an adversary maintains a covert, sustained watch on a corporate facility or an executive's residence to observe patterns of activity, access routines, or presence, in support of a subsequent operation.
ITID-52541.purpose: Captures a sustained physical stakeout of a corporate facility or an executive's residence conducted to gather targeting intelligence.
scopeIncludes: A vehicle or individual observed maintaining a sustained watch on a facility or residence with no legitimate purpose
Repeated presence of the same individual/vehicle at the same location across multiple observation periods
scopeExcludes: Covert photography/video capture specifically (ITID-52542)
Vehicle/license-plate tracking of movement rather than static observation (ITID-52543)
ITID-52541.severity: High to Critical, particularly where an executive residence is involved, given the direct personal-safety dimension.
ITID-52541.priority: P1. Treat any confirmed stakeout as an active personal-safety concern, not solely a corporate-espionage matter.
ITID-52541.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical/executive security and law enforcement; notify the affected individual(s) promptly and discreetly, and coordinate any public-facing response carefully to avoid escalating risk.
indicators: Security or facilities staff, neighbors, or residents reporting an unfamiliar vehicle or individual present for extended or repeated periods
Access-control or camera systems showing the same individual/vehicle at the perimeter on multiple occasions with no legitimate business
Reports from the executive or family members of a recurring unfamiliar presence
vectors: Stationary vehicle surveillance near a facility or residence
Foot surveillance maintaining position near an entrance or routine route
rootCauses: Limited physical security monitoring/patrol coverage of facility perimeters and, where applicable, executive residences
No standing protocol for reporting and investigating unfamiliar recurring presence
controls: Physical security patrol and camera coverage of facility perimeters
Executive residential security assessment for high-risk individuals
ITID-52541.detection: Physical surveillance tradecraft — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection relies entirely on physical security monitoring, facilities/neighbor reporting, and, where warranted, professional counter-surveillance sweeps.
ITID-52541.response: Treat as a personal-safety matter first: notify and support the affected individual, involve law enforcement where warranted, and only then assess the corporate-espionage motive and scope.
metrics: Number of confirmed stakeout incidents per year
Time from first report to law enforcement/security engagement
ITID-52541.notes: Personal-safety response takes precedence over espionage-motive investigation; coordinate discreetly with law enforcement and the affected individual throughout.

playbook.name: Physical Stakeout of Facility/Executive Residence
playbook.description: An employee or security patrol reports a suspected physical stakeout of a company facility or an executive's residence, consistent with reconnaissance for a future espionage, surveillance, or physical-security threat.

steps.title: Confirm the stakeout observation and gather details
steps.desc: Physical/executive-protection security reviews the report (suspicious vehicle, loitering individual, repeated presence) and, where available, camera footage to confirm and characterize the observed activity.
steps.guidance: Coordinate immediately with the physical/executive-protection security team, who own primary response for this leaf.
steps.outcome: A documented, corroborated account of the observed stakeout activity.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated after review, log and continue routine monitoring.
steps.tool: CCTV footage review; physical security incident log

steps.title: Assess personal-safety risk and law-enforcement threshold
steps.desc: Executive-protection security and Legal assess whether the observed activity rises to a level warranting law-enforcement notification given potential personal-safety risk.
steps.guidance: Where personal safety may be at risk, err toward involving law enforcement promptly.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment and law-enforcement engagement decision.

steps.title: Increase protective presence and notify affected individual(s)
steps.desc: Increase security presence at the affected facility or residence and brief the affected executive/employee and their family as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Increased protective posture and informed affected individuals.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement if personal safety is at risk
steps.desc: Where the risk assessment supports it, formally engage local law enforcement to report the suspicious activity and request patrol support.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement is engaged and aware of the situation.
steps.abort: If risk assessment does not support law-enforcement engagement, continue with internal protective measures only.

steps.title: Investigate for connection to broader espionage or targeting activity
steps.desc: Assess whether the stakeout connects to other reconnaissance or espionage indicators involving the same facility, executive, or program.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of whether this is an isolated event or part of a broader campaign.

steps.title: Confirm no residual surveillance capability remains at the location
steps.desc: Physical/executive-protection security conducts a follow-up sweep to confirm no residual surveillance capability (device, vantage point, ongoing presence) remains active.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of residual surveillance capability.

steps.title: Reassess and harden physical-security posture
steps.desc: Review and strengthen physical-security measures (lighting, camera coverage, patrol patterns) at the affected location.
steps.outcome: Strengthened physical-security posture reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Review and update the individual's or facility's protective risk profile
steps.desc: Update the affected individual's or facility's protective risk profile and protection plan to reflect the confirmed threat.
steps.outcome: An updated, documented protective risk profile.

steps.title: Document and brief executive-protection and security leadership
steps.desc: Produce a restricted after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52542.def: Physical surveillance distinguished by the deliberate covert capture of photographic or video evidence of a facility, individual, or location, as distinct from mere observational presence.
ITID-52542.purpose: Captures the covert photography or video recording of a facility, individual, or location as part of a surveillance operation.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a hidden camera or recording device positioned to observe a facility or individual
An individual observed covertly photographing or filming a facility, entrance, or executive
scopeExcludes: Sustained observational presence without confirmed photography/recording (ITID-52541)
Covert photography of internal documents/whiteboards specifically, which is an office-breach leaf (ITID-52942)
ITID-52542.severity: High to Critical, particularly where the subject is an individual (personal-safety dimension) rather than a facility alone.
ITID-52542.priority: P1 upon discovery or confirmed observation.
ITID-52542.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical/executive security and law enforcement; preserve any recovered device or footage as evidence.
indicators: Discovery of a concealed camera or recording device at a facility perimeter or near a residence
An individual observed with recording equipment behaving evasively when noticed
Reports of an unfamiliar person photographing entrances, badges, or personnel
vectors: Concealed camera positioned to observe an entrance, parking area, or executive's routine
Covert use of a phone or dedicated camera at close range to a facility or individual
rootCauses: Limited perimeter sweeps for unauthorized recording devices
No standing protocol for reporting individuals seen photographing facilities or personnel
controls: Periodic physical sweeps for unauthorized recording devices at sensitive locations
Employee guidance on reporting suspected covert photography
ITID-52542.detection: Physical surveillance tradecraft — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection relies on physical security sweeps and employee/facilities reporting.
ITID-52542.response: Preserve any recovered device/footage; notify and support any individual who was the specific subject; involve law enforcement for device forensics.
metrics: Number of covert recording devices discovered per year
ITID-52542.notes: Distinguished from ITID-52541 by the presence of confirmed recording capability/intent rather than observational presence alone.

playbook.name: Covert Photography/Video Surveillance of Target Location
playbook.description: Evidence is discovered of covert photography or video surveillance of a company facility, meeting location, or individual, consistent with espionage-related reconnaissance.

steps.title: Confirm the covert surveillance and identify the equipment/vantage point
steps.desc: Physical security investigates the report or discovered evidence (a hidden camera, a discovered device, or observed photography) to confirm covert surveillance occurred and identify the method used.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) specialists if a hidden device is suspected.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the surveillance method and vantage point.
steps.tool: TSCM sweep equipment; CCTV footage review

steps.title: Determine what was likely captured
steps.desc: Assess what activities, individuals, or sensitive material (e.g., visible whiteboards, badge holders, visitors) may have been captured from the identified vantage point.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Remove or neutralize the surveillance capability
steps.desc: Remove any discovered device and, if a physical vantage point (e.g., a parked vehicle or rented space) is involved, restrict access to it where within the organization's control.
steps.outcome: The surveillance capability is no longer active.

steps.title: Brief affected individuals and adjust exposed activity
steps.desc: Notify individuals who may have been captured and adjust practices (e.g., relocate sensitive meetings, cover whiteboards) to prevent continued exposure while the investigation continues.
steps.outcome: Reduced ongoing exposure risk for affected individuals and activities.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement where warranted
steps.desc: Legal and Security assess whether the covert surveillance constitutes a criminal offense and engage law enforcement accordingly.
steps.outcome: Appropriate law-enforcement engagement completed where warranted.

steps.title: Confirm no residual surveillance capability remains at the location
steps.desc: Physical/executive-protection security conducts a follow-up sweep to confirm no residual surveillance capability (device, vantage point, ongoing presence) remains active.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of residual surveillance capability.

steps.title: Harden physical security and conduct routine TSCM sweeps
steps.desc: Implement or increase the frequency of TSCM sweeps and physical-security hardening at the affected location.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of future covert surveillance going undetected.

steps.title: Review and update the individual's or facility's protective risk profile
steps.desc: Update the affected individual's or facility's protective risk profile and protection plan to reflect the confirmed threat.
steps.outcome: An updated, documented protective risk profile.

steps.title: Document and brief physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52543.def: Physical surveillance in which an adversary tracks a target's vehicle — through direct following, license-plate reader data, or a covertly installed tracking device — to build a profile of routine routes, schedules, and locations.
ITID-52543.purpose: Captures the tracking of a target's vehicle or license plate to build a pattern-of-life profile of their movements.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a covert GPS or tracking device attached to a target's vehicle
Confirmed or suspected vehicle-following behavior consistent with pattern-of-life mapping
Misuse of license-plate-reader data to track a specific individual's movements
scopeExcludes: Static observation of a facility or residence without vehicle tracking (ITID-52541)
ITID-52543.severity: High to Critical, given the direct personal-safety and predictability risk that movement tracking creates.
ITID-52543.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical/executive security and law enforcement; advise the affected individual to vary routines until the device/threat is resolved.
indicators: Discovery of an unfamiliar tracking device on a vehicle during routine inspection
The target reporting a pattern of being followed on routine routes
Unexplained knowledge by a third party of the target's routine schedule or locations
vectors: Covert GPS tracker physically attached to a vehicle
Direct vehicle-following surveillance
Unauthorized access to or misuse of license-plate-reader systems
rootCauses: No routine vehicle inspection program for high-risk individuals
Insufficient access controls/audit logging on license-plate-reader data where the organization operates such systems
controls: Routine vehicle inspection for tracking devices for high-risk individuals
Access controls and audit logging on any organization-operated license-plate-reader systems
ITID-52543.detection: Physical surveillance tradecraft — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection relies on physical inspection, the target's own pattern-recognition reporting, and, where relevant, audit of internal license-plate-reader system access.
ITID-52543.response: Preserve any discovered device as evidence; advise the affected individual on route variation and increased vigilance; involve law enforcement for device tracing.
metrics: Number of tracking devices discovered per year
ITID-52543.notes: Personal-safety response (route variation, notification, support) takes precedence over the espionage-motive investigation.

playbook.name: Vehicle/License Plate Tracking for Movement Pattern Analysis
playbook.description: Evidence indicates an actor is tracking an executive's or facility's vehicle/license plate to analyze movement patterns in support of a future physical or espionage-related operation.

steps.title: Confirm the vehicle-tracking observation
steps.desc: Executive-protection security reviews the report (a repeatedly observed vehicle, a suspicious GPS tracker discovery, or a pattern noted by the executive/driver) to confirm tracking activity.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with a professional vehicle-sweep service if a physical tracking device is suspected.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of tracking activity and method.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, log and continue monitoring.

steps.title: Assess personal-safety risk
steps.desc: Executive-protection security and Legal assess whether the tracking activity poses an elevated personal-safety risk warranting law-enforcement engagement.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment.

steps.title: Remove any tracking device and vary travel patterns
steps.desc: Remove any discovered tracking device from the vehicle and vary travel routes and schedules as an interim protective measure.
steps.outcome: The tracking capability is neutralized and predictability is reduced.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement if personal safety is at risk
steps.desc: Where the risk assessment supports it, engage local law enforcement to report the tracking activity.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement is engaged and aware of the situation.
steps.abort: If risk assessment does not support engagement, proceed with internal protective measures only.

steps.title: Investigate for connection to broader targeting activity
steps.desc: Assess whether this connects to other surveillance or espionage indicators involving the same executive or facility.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of isolated vs. broader campaign.

steps.title: Confirm no residual surveillance capability remains at the location
steps.desc: Physical/executive-protection security conducts a follow-up sweep to confirm no residual surveillance capability (device, vantage point, ongoing presence) remains active.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of residual surveillance capability.

steps.title: Implement enhanced vehicle-security protocols
steps.desc: Establish routine vehicle sweeps and enhanced protective-driving protocols for at-risk executives.
steps.outcome: Reduced future vulnerability to vehicle tracking.

steps.title: Review and update the individual's or facility's protective risk profile
steps.desc: Update the affected individual's or facility's protective risk profile and protection plan to reflect the confirmed threat.
steps.outcome: An updated, documented protective risk profile.

steps.title: Document and brief executive-protection leadership
steps.desc: Produce a restricted after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52544.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected physical surveillance pending determination of the specific method (stakeout, covert photography, or vehicle tracking).
ITID-52544.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected physical surveillance that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of physical surveillance prior to identifying the specific method
scopeExcludes: Any case where the method has already been established (ITID-52541/52542/52543)
ITID-52544.severity: High pending triage, given the personal-safety dimension inherent to any physical surveillance suspicion.
ITID-52544.priority: P1 for initial investigation regardless of eventual classification.
ITID-52544.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical/executive security on initial suspicion; do not wait for full classification given the personal-safety stakes.
indicators: General report of feeling watched or followed, or an unfamiliar recurring presence, without a confirmed method
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow with immediate physical security engagement
ITID-52544.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification, though physical security should engage immediately regardless of classification status.
ITID-52544.response: Treat every report seriously and engage physical security immediately; reclassify to a specific leaf once the method is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 14 days
ITID-52544.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Physical Surveillance group; given the personal-safety stakes, initial response should not wait on classification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Physical Surveillance
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected physical surveillance directed against the organization, its facilities, or its personnel.

steps.title: Confirm the physical surveillance indicator
steps.desc: Physical security investigates the reported or observed indicator to confirm whether deliberate physical surveillance is occurring.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical/executive-protection security, which owns primary response for this category.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of surveillance activity and its apparent target.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, log and continue monitoring.
steps.tool: CCTV footage review; physical security incident log

steps.title: Assess personal-safety and business-impact risk
steps.desc: Assess whether the surveillance activity poses a personal-safety risk to specific individuals or a business-impact risk to facilities/operations.
steps.guidance: Where personal safety may be at risk, involve law enforcement promptly.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment guiding response scale.

steps.title: Increase protective measures and brief affected individuals
steps.desc: Increase security presence or monitoring at the affected location and brief any affected individuals.
steps.outcome: Increased protective posture.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement where personal safety is at risk
steps.desc: Engage local law enforcement where the risk assessment supports it.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement engaged where warranted.

steps.title: Investigate for connection to broader targeting activity
steps.desc: Assess whether the surveillance connects to other reconnaissance or espionage indicators.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of isolated vs. broader campaign.

steps.title: Confirm no residual surveillance capability remains at the location
steps.desc: Physical/executive-protection security conducts a follow-up sweep to confirm no residual surveillance capability (device, vantage point, ongoing presence) remains active.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence of residual surveillance capability.

steps.title: Harden physical-security posture
steps.desc: Review and strengthen physical-security measures at the affected location.
steps.outcome: Strengthened physical-security posture.

steps.title: Review and update the individual's or facility's protective risk profile
steps.desc: Update the affected individual's or facility's protective risk profile and protection plan to reflect the confirmed threat.
steps.outcome: An updated, documented protective risk profile.

steps.title: Document and brief physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52611.def: Coercion of an employee into acting as an insider source through the threat of disclosing compromising personal information (kompromat) — financial, relational, or reputational — obtained or fabricated by the coercing party.
ITID-52611.purpose: Captures the use of compromising personal information to blackmail an employee into providing insider access or data on behalf of an external party.
scopeIncludes: An employee reporting or confirmed to be under threat of disclosure of compromising personal material in exchange for information or access
Discovery of kompromat-style material being used as leverage against an employee, whether the material is genuine or fabricated
scopeExcludes: Coercion via threats to physical safety of the employee or family (ITID-52612)
Coercion leveraging the employee's own prior illegal act specifically (ITID-52613)
ITID-52611.severity: Critical. This is treated as both a security incident and a duty-of-care matter for the affected employee, independent of how much data may have already been disclosed.
ITID-52611.priority: P1, with immediate joint HR/legal/security handling.
ITID-52611.escalation: Escalate immediately and discreetly to HR, legal, and security leadership; involve law enforcement promptly where the coercion includes extortion or where the employee's safety may be at risk. Handle contact with the affected employee with particular care and confidentiality.
indicators: An employee disclosing to a manager, HR, or the security team that they are being pressured or blackmailed
Sudden, unexplained change in an employee's data access behavior alongside signs of personal distress
Direct evidence of an extortion attempt referencing personal material
vectors: Approach via a compromised or fabricated personal relationship used to obtain or manufacture compromising material
Direct extortion contact referencing genuine or fabricated compromising content
rootCauses: No confidential, well-publicized channel for employees to report coercion attempts without fear of professional consequence
Insufficient awareness among employees in sensitive-access roles of coercion/kompromat tactics
controls: Confidential employee reporting channel for coercion/extortion attempts
Insider-risk awareness training addressing coercion tactics for sensitive-access roles
ITID-52611.detection: No technical detection signature; discovery depends almost entirely on the employee coming forward, a concerned colleague or manager reporting a change in behavior, or investigative referral.
ITID-52611.response: Prioritize the affected employee's safety and well-being alongside the investigation: offer support resources, avoid actions that could be perceived as punitive toward the victim, and scope the extent of any actual data compromise separately from the employee's culpability.
metrics: Number of coercion cases reported through the confidential channel per year
Time from disclosure to HR/legal engagement
ITID-52611.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels. Response should center on supporting the affected employee safely while investigating the scope of compromise.

playbook.name: Blackmail Using Compromising Personal Information (Kompromat)
playbook.description: An employee discloses, or is otherwise found to be, providing organizational information or access under duress after being blackmailed with compromising personal information (kompromat) by an external party.

steps.title: Receive the disclosure through a confidential channel and confirm coercion is occurring
steps.desc: Security, HR, and Legal jointly and confidentially receive and assess the report — whether from the affected employee coming forward voluntarily or from another indicator — to confirm that coercion via kompromat is occurring.
steps.guidance: Treat the employee as a victim of blackmail requiring protection and support, not primarily as a security threat. Use a confidential reporting channel and involve Legal immediately to establish attorney-client privilege over the investigation given the potential for criminal referral against the blackmailer.
steps.outcome: A confirmed, confidentially-handled understanding of the coercion and what has been demanded or provided.
steps.tool: Confidential reporting channel; case management system (access-restricted)

steps.title: Scope what information or access has already been compromised
steps.desc: Working discreetly with the employee, determine what organizational information or access has already been provided to the blackmailer.
steps.guidance: Conduct this scoping with sensitivity and without judgment toward the employee, recognizing they are acting under duress.
steps.outcome: A documented, confidential scope of compromise.

steps.title: Provide protective and support measures for the employee and family
steps.desc: Legal and HR arrange protective measures (safety planning, if needed law-enforcement coordination for the employee's personal safety, confidential leave options) and support resources for the employee and, if relevant, their family.
steps.guidance: This step should be prioritized alongside — not after — the security containment steps, reflecting the victim-support framing required for this leaf.
steps.outcome: The employee and family have access to support and protection appropriate to the threat.

steps.title: Contain the security exposure without punitive action against the coerced employee
steps.desc: Quietly restrict or monitor the employee's access to sensitive systems as needed to limit further exposure, while adopting a non-punitive posture toward the employee given their voluntary disclosure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with Legal and, where a criminal referral against the blackmailer is contemplated, law enforcement, before taking any containment action that could tip off the blackmailer.
steps.outcome: Security exposure is limited without punishing the coerced employee for coming forward.

steps.title: Pursue legal action against the blackmailer with law enforcement
steps.desc: Legal, in coordination with law enforcement, pursues criminal referral or other legal action against the blackmailing party, with the employee's safety as a primary consideration in timing and sequencing.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal/law-enforcement action taken against the blackmailer.

steps.title: Confirm the coercion has ceased and no further demands are being made
steps.desc: Working confidentially with the employee and Legal, confirm that the coercive contact has ceased following the legal/law-enforcement action, and establish a plan should contact resume.
steps.guidance: Maintain the confidential, victim-centered posture established earlier in this investigation.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that active coercion has ceased, with a contingency plan in place.

steps.title: Support the employee's continued employment and reintegration
steps.desc: Where appropriate, HR and Legal support the employee's continued, protected employment, adjusting role or access as needed for their safety and the organization's security.
steps.outcome: A documented, supportive resolution for the employee where feasible.

steps.title: Offer continued confidential support resources to the employee
steps.desc: Continue to make confidential counseling, legal, and safety-support resources available to the employee for as long as needed.
steps.outcome: The employee has ongoing access to support resources beyond the immediate incident response.

steps.title: Conduct a tightly restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Document the incident in a highly access-restricted, privileged report, and use lessons learned to improve confidential reporting channels and support resources — without identifying the employee beyond the need-to-know circle.
steps.outcome: Improved confidential-reporting and victim-support processes for future coercion cases.

ITID-52612.def: Coercion of an employee into providing insider access or information through explicit or implied threats of physical harm to the employee or their family members.
ITID-52612.purpose: Captures the coercion of an employee into insider activity through threats made against their physical safety or that of their family.
scopeIncludes: An employee reporting a direct or implied threat of physical harm tied to a demand for information or access
Evidence that an employee's insider activity coincided with a documented threat to personal safety
scopeExcludes: Coercion using compromising personal information without a physical-safety threat (ITID-52611)
ITID-52612.severity: Critical without exception. This is treated first and foremost as a physical-safety emergency.
ITID-52612.priority: P1, with immediate law enforcement involvement.
ITID-52612.escalation: Escalate immediately to law enforcement, physical/executive security, HR, and legal; prioritize protective measures for the employee and family before any investigative or access-control action.
indicators: An employee disclosing a direct threat of physical harm tied to a demand
Sudden, unexplained fear-driven behavior change in an employee with sensitive access
Corroborating evidence of contact with the employee's family consistent with a coercion attempt
vectors: Direct or implied threat of violence communicated to the employee
Threatening contact made with a family member to pressure the employee
rootCauses: No confidential, rapid-response channel for employees to report safety threats tied to coercion
Insufficient coordination protocol between security, HR, and law enforcement for safety-threat scenarios
controls: Rapid-response protocol linking security, HR, and law enforcement for safety-threat disclosures
Confidential employee reporting channel for coercion/threat attempts
ITID-52612.detection: No technical detection signature; discovery depends on the employee or a concerned party coming forward, or investigative referral following unusual insider activity.
ITID-52612.response: Treat protective action for the employee and family as the immediate priority, ahead of investigative or access-control steps; coordinate closely and continuously with law enforcement.
metrics: Time from disclosure to law enforcement/protective engagement
sops: Workplace Violence and Threat Response SOP
ITID-52612.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels, with physical safety response taking precedence over all other considerations.

playbook.name: Coercion Through Threats to Family/Personal Safety
playbook.description: An employee is found to be providing organizational information or access under duress after an external party threatened harm to the employee's family or personal safety.

steps.title: Receive the disclosure through a confidential channel and assess the immediate safety threat
steps.desc: Security, HR, and Legal jointly and confidentially assess the report, treating any threat to family or personal safety as the most urgent priority, ahead of the security-exposure assessment.
steps.guidance: An active safety threat may warrant immediate law-enforcement involvement before any other step in this playbook.
steps.outcome: A confirmed understanding of the coercion and the current level of safety threat.

steps.title: Scope what information or access has already been compromised
steps.desc: Working discreetly and sensitively with the employee, determine what organizational information or access has already been provided under duress.
steps.outcome: A documented, confidential scope of compromise.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement for personal-safety protection
steps.desc: With the employee's involvement and consent where possible, engage law enforcement to assess and respond to the safety threat against the employee and family.
steps.guidance: Personal-safety threats to family members typically warrant law-enforcement engagement regardless of the security-investigation timeline.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement is engaged and protective measures are underway.

steps.title: Contain the security exposure with a non-punitive posture toward the employee
steps.desc: Quietly restrict or monitor the employee's access as needed to limit further exposure, without treating the employee punitively given the coercion.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with Legal and law enforcement to avoid escalating the safety threat.
steps.outcome: Security exposure limited without compounding the employee's distress.

steps.title: Pursue legal/law-enforcement action against the coercing party
steps.desc: Legal and law enforcement pursue action against the party making the threats, prioritizing continued family/employee safety throughout.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal/law-enforcement action taken.

steps.title: Confirm the coercion has ceased and no further demands are being made
steps.desc: Working confidentially with the employee and Legal, confirm that the coercive contact has ceased following the legal/law-enforcement action, and establish a plan should contact resume.
steps.guidance: Maintain the confidential, victim-centered posture established earlier in this investigation.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that active coercion has ceased, with a contingency plan in place.

steps.title: Provide ongoing protective and support resources
steps.desc: Continue protective measures and support resources (counseling, security assistance) for the employee and family as needed.
steps.outcome: The employee and family have ongoing access to support and protection.

steps.title: Offer continued confidential support resources to the employee
steps.desc: Continue to make confidential counseling, legal, and safety-support resources available to the employee for as long as needed.
steps.outcome: The employee has ongoing access to support resources beyond the immediate incident response.

steps.title: Conduct a tightly restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Document the incident in a highly access-restricted, privileged report focused on improving confidential-reporting and rapid safety-response processes.
steps.outcome: Improved processes for future safety-threat coercion cases.

ITID-52613.def: Coercion of an employee into providing insider access or information through threats to expose an illegal act or serious misconduct the employee previously committed, whether or not related to their employment.
ITID-52613.purpose: Captures the coercion of an employee into insider activity by leveraging knowledge of the employee's own prior illegal or seriously compromising conduct.
scopeIncludes: An employee reporting or confirmed to be pressured using knowledge of a prior illegal act as leverage
Discovery that an employee's insider activity was preceded by a threat to report them to authorities or the employer for a prior act
scopeExcludes: Coercion using fabricated or unrelated compromising personal material (ITID-52611)
Coercion via physical-safety threats without leverage tied to a prior illegal act (ITID-52612)
ITID-52613.severity: Critical. Requires careful, coordinated handling given the overlapping legal exposure of the employee alongside the security incident.
ITID-52613.priority: P1, with immediate joint HR/legal handling given the legal complexity.
ITID-52613.escalation: Escalate immediately and discreetly to legal and HR before any law-enforcement engagement, given the employee's own potential legal exposure; involve law enforcement as legal counsel advises, and maintain confidentiality throughout.
indicators: An employee disclosing that they are being pressured using knowledge of a past act
Unexplained insider activity discovered alongside evidence of an external party possessing leverage over the employee
vectors: Direct threat to report a prior illegal act to law enforcement or the employer unless the employee cooperates
Approach by an external party who obtained knowledge of the prior act through investigation or coincidence
rootCauses: No confidential channel allowing an employee to disclose coercion without fear of automatic termination or reporting
Insufficient legal/HR coordination protocol for cases involving an employee's own legal exposure
controls: Confidential employee reporting channel for coercion attempts, paired with clear legal/HR handling guidance
Legal counsel engagement protocol for coercion cases involving employee legal exposure
ITID-52613.detection: No technical detection signature; discovery depends almost entirely on the employee coming forward or investigative referral.
ITID-52613.response: Involve legal counsel before taking any action that could affect the employee's legal standing; balance the organization's investigative needs with a fair and measured approach to the employee's own conduct.
metrics: Number of coercion cases reported through the confidential channel per year
ITID-52613.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels. Legal exposure of the employee themselves requires especially careful, counsel-guided handling.

playbook.name: Coercion Leveraging Employee's Own Prior Illegal Act
playbook.description: An employee is found to be providing organizational information or access under duress after an external party threatened to expose the employee's own prior illegal act.

steps.title: Receive the disclosure through a confidential, privileged channel
steps.desc: Legal, with Security and HR, confidentially receives and assesses the report, establishing attorney-client privilege over the investigation given both the coercion and the underlying prior illegal act.
steps.guidance: Legal counsel should lead this intake given the dual sensitivity — the coercion itself and the employee's own prior act — to preserve privilege and give the employee appropriate legal guidance.
steps.outcome: A confidentially and legally managed understanding of the coercion and its basis.

steps.title: Scope what information or access has already been compromised
steps.desc: Working with Legal and the employee, determine what organizational information or access has already been provided under this duress.
steps.outcome: A documented, confidential scope of compromise.

steps.title: Advise the employee on legal options and protections
steps.desc: Legal counsel advises the employee on their legal options, including cooperation with any law-enforcement referral regarding the coercing party and potential considerations regarding the employee's own prior act.
steps.guidance: Handle with careful, legally-guided sensitivity; a voluntary, cooperative disclosure by the employee may be viewed favorably in any subsequent proceeding, and this should be communicated to encourage continued cooperation.
steps.outcome: The employee is informed of their options and legal posture going forward.

steps.title: Contain the security exposure
steps.desc: Quietly restrict or monitor the employee's access as needed to limit further security exposure, coordinated with Legal to avoid prejudicing any parallel legal process.
steps.outcome: Security exposure is limited in a legally coordinated manner.

steps.title: Pursue legal action against the coercing party with law enforcement
steps.desc: Legal and law enforcement pursue action against the party leveraging the coercion, in a manner that accounts for the employee's cooperation and legal circumstances.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal/law-enforcement action taken against the coercing party.

steps.title: Confirm the coercion has ceased and no further demands are being made
steps.desc: Working confidentially with the employee and Legal, confirm that the coercive contact has ceased following the legal/law-enforcement action, and establish a plan should contact resume.
steps.guidance: Maintain the confidential, victim-centered posture established earlier in this investigation.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that active coercion has ceased, with a contingency plan in place.

steps.title: Determine appropriate employment resolution with Legal and HR guidance
steps.desc: Legal and HR jointly determine an appropriate resolution regarding the employee's continued employment, informed by legal counsel and the circumstances of cooperation.
steps.outcome: A legally-guided, documented resolution.

steps.title: Offer continued confidential support resources to the employee
steps.desc: Continue to make confidential counseling, legal, and safety-support resources available to the employee for as long as needed.
steps.outcome: The employee has ongoing access to support resources beyond the immediate incident response.

steps.title: Conduct a tightly restricted, privileged after-action review
steps.desc: Document the incident under privilege, in a highly access-restricted report focused on improving confidential-reporting processes for this especially sensitive coercion pattern.
steps.outcome: Improved processes for future cases of this nature.

ITID-52614.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected employee coercion pending determination of the specific leverage used (compromising personal information, physical-safety threats, or a prior illegal act).
ITID-52614.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected employee coercion that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of employee coercion prior to identifying the specific leverage used
scopeExcludes: Any case where the leverage type has already been established (ITID-52611/52612/52613)
ITID-52614.severity: Critical pending triage, given the duty-of-care stakes inherent to any coercion suspicion.
ITID-52614.priority: P1 for initial investigation regardless of eventual classification.
ITID-52614.escalation: Escalate immediately and discreetly to HR, legal, and security on initial suspicion; do not wait for full classification to begin supporting the affected employee.
indicators: General report or behavioral signal suggesting an employee may be under pressure, without a confirmed leverage type
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow with immediate HR/legal engagement
ITID-52614.detection: No technical detection signature; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52614.response: Prioritize the affected employee's safety and well-being from the first report; reclassify to a specific leaf once the leverage type is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 14 days
ITID-52614.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Employee Coercion group; human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies. Given the duty-of-care stakes, initial support should not wait on classification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Employee Coercion
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case in which an employee is suspected of providing organizational information or access under some form of coercion by an external party.

steps.title: Receive the disclosure through a confidential channel and confirm coercion
steps.desc: Security, HR, and Legal jointly and confidentially assess the report to confirm that some form of coercion, rather than voluntary insider action, is occurring.
steps.guidance: Treat the employee as a potential victim requiring protection and support until the facts indicate otherwise; use a confidential reporting channel and involve Legal to establish privilege given the potential for criminal referral against the coercing party.
steps.outcome: A confidentially-handled understanding of the coercion.

steps.title: Scope what information or access has already been compromised
steps.desc: Working discreetly with the employee, determine what has already been provided to the coercing party.
steps.outcome: A documented, confidential scope of compromise.

steps.title: Provide protective and support measures for the employee
steps.desc: Legal and HR arrange appropriate protective and support measures for the employee given the nature of the coercion.
steps.outcome: The employee has access to appropriate support and protection.

steps.title: Contain the security exposure with a non-punitive posture
steps.desc: Quietly restrict or monitor access as needed to limit further exposure, adopting a non-punitive posture toward the coerced employee.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal and, where warranted, law enforcement before acting.
steps.outcome: Security exposure limited without punishing the coerced employee.

steps.title: Pursue legal action against the coercing party
steps.desc: Legal and, where warranted, law enforcement pursue action against the coercing party.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal/law-enforcement action taken.

steps.title: Confirm the coercion has ceased and no further demands are being made
steps.desc: Working confidentially with the employee and Legal, confirm that the coercive contact has ceased following the legal/law-enforcement action, and establish a plan should contact resume.
steps.guidance: Maintain the confidential, victim-centered posture established earlier in this investigation.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that active coercion has ceased, with a contingency plan in place.

steps.title: Support the employee's resolution and reintegration
steps.desc: HR and Legal determine an appropriate, supportive resolution for the employee where feasible.
steps.outcome: A documented, supportive resolution.

steps.title: Offer continued confidential support resources to the employee
steps.desc: Continue to make confidential counseling, legal, and safety-support resources available to the employee for as long as needed.
steps.outcome: The employee has ongoing access to support resources beyond the immediate incident response.

steps.title: Conduct a tightly restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Document the incident in a highly access-restricted report focused on improving confidential-reporting and support processes.
steps.outcome: Improved processes for future coercion cases.

ITID-52621.def: Insider recruitment in which an employee is offered and accepts a direct cash payment from an external party in exchange for providing information or access, without the more elaborate structuring of a job offer or contract arrangement.
ITID-52621.purpose: Captures the recruitment of an insider through a direct, straightforward cash payment in exchange for data or system access.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or strongly suspected direct cash payment made to an employee in exchange for data or access
Evidence of a proposed cash payment even where the employee is believed to have declined
scopeExcludes: Payment structured as a job offer or consulting contract (ITID-52622)
Payment made via cryptocurrency specifically to obscure the transaction (ITID-52623)
ITID-52621.severity: High to Critical depending on the sensitivity of the data/access exchanged.
ITID-52621.escalation: Escalate to insider risk, HR, legal, and law enforcement; preserve financial evidence promptly, as it is often the most concrete evidence available in bribery cases.
indicators: Unexplained cash deposits or lifestyle changes inconsistent with an employee's known income
Direct report of a payment offer from a colleague or the employee themselves
Financial records or communications referencing a payment tied to specific data or access
vectors: Direct approach offering cash in exchange for specific information or access
Use of an intermediary to deliver payment and obscure the direct relationship
rootCauses: Insufficient financial-disclosure or conflict-of-interest monitoring for employees in sensitive-access roles
No confidential channel for employees to report bribery approaches
controls: Conflict-of-interest and outside-payment attestation program
Confidential bribery-approach reporting channel
ITID-52621.detection: No technical detection signature; discovery relies on financial anomaly review, employee reporting, or investigative referral.
ITID-52621.response: Preserve financial evidence promptly; coordinate with legal and law enforcement given the likely criminal nature of the conduct.
metrics: Number of confirmed bribery cases per year
ITID-52621.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels.

playbook.name: Direct Cash Payment for Data Access
playbook.description: An employee is discovered to have accepted direct cash payment from an external party in exchange for providing organizational data or system access.

steps.title: Confirm the bribery indicator
steps.desc: HR, Legal, and Security jointly review the triggering indicator (e.g., unexplained cash deposits flagged by financial-crimes monitoring, a tip, or unusual data access correlated with financial anomalies) to confirm bribery is plausible.
steps.guidance: Involve Legal/Compliance early given the potential for criminal referral (bribery/commercial corruption statutes).
steps.outcome: A documented determination on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.

steps.title: Scope the data/access provided and the payment trail
steps.desc: Investigate what data or access was provided and trace the payment where possible (bank records, cryptocurrency, or other financial evidence).
steps.outcome: A documented scope of compromise and financial trail.

steps.title: Restrict access pending investigation
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the employee's access to the implicated systems and data pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Further data exposure via this employee is halted.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve relevant logs, communications, and financial records under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for potential criminal referral.

steps.title: Complete HR/Legal/Compliance investigation and determine personnel action
steps.desc: HR, Legal, and Compliance complete the investigation and determine appropriate personnel action, coordinating with law enforcement for potential criminal referral.
steps.outcome: Personnel action taken and criminal referral pursued where warranted.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any related conflict-of-interest or process gaps
steps.desc: Review whether the bribery exposes broader gaps in conflict-of-interest disclosure, procurement, or approval processes, and remediate as needed.
steps.outcome: Related process gaps identified and remediated.

steps.title: Reassess data-access and financial-anomaly monitoring controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen controls for detecting anomalous data access correlated with financial indicators of bribery.
steps.outcome: Strengthened detection controls.

steps.title: Communicate outcome to relevant business unit leadership
steps.desc: Brief the relevant business unit leadership on the outcome and any process changes, consistent with confidentiality and legal requirements.
steps.outcome: Business unit leadership informed appropriately.

steps.title: Document and brief HR, Legal, and Compliance leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52622.def: Insider recruitment in which an employee is offered a highly favorable future job or consulting arrangement with a competitor or sponsoring organization, structured to appear as a legitimate career opportunity, in exchange for information or access.
ITID-52622.purpose: Captures the recruitment of an insider through the offer of a lucrative future job or consulting contract with the sponsoring organization.
scopeIncludes: An offer of employment or consulting work whose terms are disproportionate to the stated role and coincide with a request for information or access
Post-departure consulting arrangements found to have been contingent on data provided while still employed
scopeExcludes: A simple, direct cash payment with no job/contract structuring (ITID-52621)
ITID-52622.severity: High to Critical, and often harder to detect than direct cash payment because the arrangement can appear as legitimate recruitment.
ITID-52622.escalation: Escalate to insider risk, HR, legal, and law enforcement; involve legal early given the potential for a formal-looking contract to complicate the investigation.
indicators: An employee receiving an unusually favorable offer from a competitor shortly before or after a period of anomalous data access
A consulting arrangement with terms disproportionate to the actual work described
Data access patterns that shift immediately after the employee accepts an external offer
vectors: A structured job or consulting offer used as cover for a bribery arrangement
A post-employment consulting contract contingent on data delivered while still employed
rootCauses: No policy requiring disclosure of outside job offers or consulting arrangements for employees in sensitive-access roles
Insufficient post-departure monitoring for a pattern connecting departure timing to a new external role
controls: Outside-offer/consulting-arrangement disclosure policy for sensitive-access roles
Post-departure monitoring for suspicious data-access-to-new-role correlation
ITID-52622.detection: No technical detection signature; discovery relies on disclosure requirements, HR review of departures, or investigative referral.
ITID-52622.response: Investigate the full data-access history leading up to the offer; coordinate with legal given the contractual/employment-law dimensions.
metrics: Number of confirmed bribery-via-offer cases per year
ITID-52622.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels.

playbook.name: Bribery via Lucrative Job Offer/Consulting Contract
playbook.description: An employee is discovered to have been offered, and to have accepted, a lucrative future job offer or consulting contract from an external party in exchange for providing organizational data or access.

steps.title: Confirm the bribery indicator
steps.desc: HR, Legal, and Security review the triggering indicator (e.g., undisclosed outside employment/consulting relationship discovered, conflict-of-interest disclosure gap, or unusual data access) to confirm plausibility.
steps.guidance: Cross-check against conflict-of-interest disclosure records and outside-employment policy compliance.
steps.outcome: A documented determination on whether to open a formal investigation.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.
steps.tool: HR conflict-of-interest disclosure records; case management system

steps.title: Scope the data/access provided and the relationship with the external party
steps.desc: Investigate what data or access was provided and characterize the nature and timing of the job offer/consulting arrangement relative to the data disclosure.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of compromise and relationship timeline.

steps.title: Restrict access pending investigation
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the employee's access to implicated systems and data pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Further data exposure via this employee is halted.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
