steps.desc: Preserve relevant logs, communications, and outside-employment records under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for potential criminal referral.

steps.title: Complete HR/Legal/Compliance investigation and determine personnel action
steps.desc: HR, Legal, and Compliance complete the investigation and determine appropriate personnel action, coordinating with law enforcement for potential criminal referral where warranted.
steps.outcome: Personnel action taken and criminal referral pursued where warranted.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any related conflict-of-interest or process gaps
steps.desc: Review whether the bribery exposes broader gaps in conflict-of-interest disclosure, procurement, or approval processes, and remediate as needed.
steps.outcome: Related process gaps identified and remediated.

steps.title: Strengthen conflict-of-interest disclosure and enforcement processes
steps.desc: Review and strengthen outside-employment/conflict-of-interest disclosure requirements and enforcement.
steps.outcome: Strengthened controls reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Communicate outcome to relevant business unit leadership
steps.desc: Brief the relevant business unit leadership on the outcome and any process changes, consistent with confidentiality and legal requirements.
steps.outcome: Business unit leadership informed appropriately.

steps.title: Document and brief HR, Legal, and Compliance leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52623.def: Insider recruitment involving bribery payment made in cryptocurrency, distinguished from other bribery leaves by the deliberate use of a payment method chosen to evade financial-crime monitoring and complicate attribution.
ITID-52623.purpose: Captures insider recruitment where payment is made via cryptocurrency specifically to obscure the financial relationship between the insider and the sponsoring party.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected cryptocurrency payment made to an employee in exchange for data or access
Evidence of a proposed cryptocurrency payment even where the employee is believed to have declined
scopeExcludes: Payment via traditional cash, wire, or job/contract structuring (ITID-52621/52622)
ITID-52623.severity: High to Critical, with the payment method itself signaling a more sophisticated, deliberately evasive sponsor.
ITID-52623.escalation: Escalate to insider risk, HR, legal, and law enforcement; involve financial-crime/blockchain-analysis resources early given the tracing challenges cryptocurrency presents.
indicators: Evidence of a cryptocurrency wallet or exchange account inconsistent with the employee's known financial profile
Communications referencing a cryptocurrency payment tied to specific data or access
Blockchain analysis linking a wallet to the employee following an insider-risk referral
vectors: Direct approach offering cryptocurrency payment specifically to avoid traditional financial-monitoring trails
Use of a mixing service or intermediary wallet to further obscure the payment
rootCauses: Financial-disclosure programs not extended to cover cryptocurrency holdings for sensitive-access roles
Limited internal capability to trace cryptocurrency payments without external blockchain-analysis support
controls: Financial-disclosure program extended to cryptocurrency holdings for sensitive-access roles
Established relationship with a blockchain-analysis provider for financial-crime investigations
ITID-52623.detection: No technical detection signature within corporate telemetry; discovery relies on employee reporting, investigative referral, or external blockchain-analysis tracing once a suspicion exists.
ITID-52623.response: Engage blockchain-analysis support promptly to trace payment flows; coordinate closely with law enforcement given the cross-jurisdictional nature typical of cryptocurrency-facilitated bribery.
metrics: Number of confirmed cryptocurrency-facilitated bribery cases per year
ITID-52623.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via insider-risk and HR/legal coordination channels. The cryptocurrency payment mechanism itself may benefit from financial-crime/blockchain-analysis support outside standard SOC tooling.

playbook.name: Bribery via Cryptocurrency Payment for Anonymity
playbook.description: An employee is discovered to have accepted cryptocurrency payment, chosen specifically for its anonymity properties, from an external party in exchange for providing organizational data or access.

steps.title: Confirm the bribery indicator and initiate blockchain-transaction tracing
steps.desc: HR, Legal, and Security review the triggering indicator and, where evidence of cryptocurrency payment exists, engage blockchain forensic analysis to trace the transaction.
steps.guidance: Engage specialized blockchain-forensics support (internal or external) given the technical complexity of tracing cryptocurrency payments.
steps.outcome: A documented determination on investigation scope, including any traceable transaction evidence.
steps.abort: If not credible, log and monitor.
steps.tool: Blockchain forensic analysis tooling; case management system

steps.title: Scope the data/access provided
steps.desc: Investigate what data or access was provided in connection with the payment.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of compromise.

steps.title: Restrict access pending investigation
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the employee's access to implicated systems and data pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Further data exposure via this employee is halted.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and issue legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve relevant logs, communications, and any blockchain-transaction evidence under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for potential criminal referral.

steps.title: Complete HR/Legal/Compliance investigation and coordinate with law enforcement
steps.desc: HR, Legal, and Compliance complete the investigation and coordinate with law enforcement, who may have additional resources for tracing cryptocurrency payments to their source.
steps.outcome: Personnel action taken and criminal referral pursued where warranted.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any related conflict-of-interest or process gaps
steps.desc: Review whether the bribery exposes broader gaps in conflict-of-interest disclosure, procurement, or approval processes, and remediate as needed.
steps.outcome: Related process gaps identified and remediated.

steps.title: Strengthen financial-anomaly and data-access correlation monitoring
steps.desc: Review and strengthen controls for detecting anomalous data access, recognizing that traditional financial monitoring may not catch cryptocurrency-based bribery.
steps.outcome: Strengthened detection controls.

steps.title: Communicate outcome to relevant business unit leadership
steps.desc: Brief the relevant business unit leadership on the outcome and any process changes, consistent with confidentiality and legal requirements.
steps.outcome: Business unit leadership informed appropriately.

steps.title: Document and brief HR, Legal, and Compliance leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52624.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of suspected insider bribery pending determination of the specific payment method used.
ITID-52624.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected bribery and corruption that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of bribery prior to identifying the specific payment method
scopeExcludes: Any case where the payment method has already been established (ITID-52621/52622/52623)
ITID-52624.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52624.escalation: Escalate to insider risk and legal on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of a suspected bribery arrangement without a confirmed payment method
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52624.detection: No technical detection signature; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52624.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the payment method is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52624.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Bribery and Corruption group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Bribery and Corruption

steps.title: Confirm the bribery indicator

steps.desc: Review whether the bribery exposes broader gaps in conflict-of-interest disclosure, procurement, or approval processes, and remediate as needed.

steps.title: Strengthen anti-bribery and corruption monitoring controls

steps.title: Communicate outcome to relevant business unit leadership

ITID-52631.def: Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by an employee acting alone out of grievance following a denied promotion or raise, with no evidence of an external handler or payment.
ITID-52631.purpose: Captures a data leak by an employee whose motivation traces to a denied promotion or compensation increase, rather than external recruitment or payment.
scopeIncludes: A leak confirmed to have followed, and to be motivated by, a specific denied promotion or compensation decision
Communications or statements by the employee tying the leak to the denied decision
scopeExcludes: A leak involving payment or direction from an external party (see Bribery and Corruption, ITID-5262x, or Insider Espionage, ITID-5211x)
A leak following termination/layoff specifically (ITID-52632)
ITID-52631.severity: Medium to High depending on the sensitivity and scope of the data disclosed.
ITID-52631.priority: P2, escalating to P1 based on data sensitivity or public/media disclosure.
ITID-52631.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal; coordinate messaging carefully where the disclosure has reputational or media dimensions.
indicators: Data access or disclosure activity closely following a documented denial of promotion or raise
Employee statements, internal or external, expressing grievance tied to the compensation decision
Disclosure targeted at information relevant to the employee's grievance (e.g., compensation data, management decisions)
vectors: Direct disclosure to media, a regulator, or a public forum
Internal forwarding of confidential material to unauthorized recipients
rootCauses: No structured, trusted internal channel for employees to raise compensation grievances
Insufficient monitoring of data access following adverse HR decisions
controls: HR-triggered data-access review following adverse compensation decisions
Accessible internal grievance/appeals channel
ITID-52631.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies to the underlying human motivation; the specific exfiltration method used, if any, may have a technical signature tracked under the corresponding leaf in the Data Breaches domain.
ITID-52631.response: Assess scope of disclosure and legal exposure; consider whether the underlying grievance reflects a legitimate process gap requiring remediation, separate from the disciplinary/legal response to the leak itself.
metrics: Number of leaks correlated with adverse compensation decisions per year
ITID-52631.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment-adjacent activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies to the motivation itself; tracked via insider-risk and HR coordination channels. Cross-reference the Data Breaches domain for the specific exfiltration method if a technical vector was used.

playbook.name: Leak Following Denied Promotion/Raise
playbook.description: An employee who was recently denied a promotion or raise is discovered to have leaked confidential organizational information, apparently in retaliation.

steps.title: Confirm the leak and correlate with the employment grievance
steps.desc: Security and HR jointly confirm the data leak occurred and correlate the timing with the employee's recent denied promotion/raise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with HR, who will have context on the underlying employment decision and any documented performance/compensation history.
steps.outcome: A confirmed leak with a documented correlation to the employment grievance.

steps.title: Scope the information leaked and its recipient
steps.desc: Determine what information was leaked and to whom (media, competitor, social media, regulator).
steps.outcome: A documented scope of leaked information and recipient.

steps.title: Restrict further access and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Restrict the employee's access to sensitive systems and preserve relevant logs and communications under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Further leakage is halted and evidence is preserved.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Leak Following Denied Promotion/Raise" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Determine personnel action with HR and Legal
steps.desc: HR and Legal determine appropriate personnel action regarding the leak itself.
steps.outcome: Personnel action taken regarding the leak.

steps.title: Confirm no further copies of the leaked information remain accessible
steps.desc: Where feasible, confirm that further copies or republications of the leaked information have been addressed (e.g., takedown request to a publisher or platform).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction in the leaked information's continued availability, where achievable.

steps.title: Flag the underlying compensation/promotion grievance for independent HR review
steps.desc: HR conducts an independent review of the underlying promotion/compensation decision and process, separate from the security investigation, to assess whether the grievance itself warrants attention.
steps.guidance: This review should proceed on its own track regardless of the outcome of the security investigation — an employee's leak does not retroactively validate or invalidate the fairness of the original decision.
steps.outcome: A documented, independent HR assessment of the underlying grievance.

steps.title: Document and brief HR and Legal leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report addressing both the security incident and any HR process findings, and brief relevant leadership.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked on both fronts.

ITID-52632.def: Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by an employee acting alone out of grievance following notice of layoff or termination, with no evidence of an external handler or payment.
ITID-52632.purpose: Captures a data leak by an employee whose motivation traces to a layoff or termination notice, rather than external recruitment or payment.
scopeIncludes: A leak confirmed to have followed, and to be motivated by, a layoff or termination notice
Disclosure occurring during the notice/transition period before the employee's final day
scopeExcludes: A leak motivated by a denied promotion/raise rather than a layoff/termination (ITID-52631)
A leak involving payment or direction from an external party (see Bribery and Corruption, ITID-5262x)
ITID-52632.severity: Medium to High depending on the sensitivity and scope of the data disclosed.
ITID-52632.priority: P2, escalating to P1 based on data sensitivity, and treated as time-sensitive given the employee's imminent departure.
ITID-52632.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal promptly given the narrow window before the employee's access is removed.
indicators: Data access or disclosure activity closely following a layoff/termination notice
Bulk access or download activity concentrated in the notice period
Disclosure targeted at information relevant to the layoff decision or affecting the organization's reputation
vectors: Bulk download or forwarding of confidential material during the notice period
Direct disclosure to media, a regulator, or a public forum timed to the departure
rootCauses: No offboarding-triggered access restriction or monitoring effective immediately upon notice
Standard access retained through the full notice period regardless of role sensitivity
controls: Immediate access restriction/monitoring upon layoff or termination notice for sensitive-access roles
Departure-triggered DLP review
ITID-52632.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies to the underlying human motivation; the specific exfiltration method used, if any, may have a technical signature tracked under the corresponding leaf in the Data Breaches domain.
ITID-52632.response: Move quickly given the compressed notice-period timeline; assess scope of disclosure and legal exposure.
metrics: Number of leaks correlated with layoff/termination notices per year
Percentage of layoffs with immediate access restriction applied
ITID-52632.notes: Human-intelligence/insider-recruitment-adjacent activity — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies to the motivation itself; cross-reference the Data Breaches domain for the specific exfiltration method if a technical vector was used.

playbook.name: Leak Following Layoff/Termination Notice
playbook.description: An employee who recently received a layoff or termination notice is discovered to have leaked confidential organizational information, apparently in retaliation.

steps.title: Confirm the leak and correlate with the termination notice
steps.desc: Security and HR jointly confirm the data leak occurred and correlate the timing with the employee's layoff/termination notice.
steps.guidance: Standard offboarding forensic review is often the point of detection; ensure this review is applied consistently to all departing employees, not just those under suspicion.
steps.outcome: A confirmed leak with a documented correlation to the termination event.

steps.title: Scope the information leaked and its recipient
steps.desc: Determine what information was leaked and to whom.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of leaked information and recipient.

steps.title: Immediately revoke access and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Immediately revoke all system access for the employee if not already offboarded, and preserve relevant logs and device data under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Further leakage is halted and evidence is preserved.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Leak Following Layoff/Termination Notice" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Determine legal action regarding the leak
steps.desc: Legal evaluates appropriate action regarding the leak, including any severance-agreement or confidentiality-obligation implications.
steps.outcome: Appropriate legal action taken regarding the leak.

steps.title: Confirm no further copies of the leaked information remain accessible
steps.desc: Where feasible, confirm that further copies or republications of the leaked information have been addressed (e.g., takedown request to a publisher or platform).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction in the leaked information's continued availability, where achievable.

steps.title: Flag the underlying layoff process for independent HR review if warranted
steps.desc: Where the leak suggests a broader grievance about the layoff process, HR conducts an independent review of that process separate from the security investigation.
steps.outcome: A documented, independent HR assessment where warranted.
steps.abort: If no broader grievance pattern is indicated, this review may be limited in scope.

steps.title: Strengthen offboarding forensic review process
steps.desc: Document the incident and strengthen the standard offboarding forensic review process applied to all departing employees.
steps.outcome: Improved detection of future departure-related leaks.

ITID-52633.def: Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by an employee who believes the disclosure exposes unethical, unsafe, or unlawful conduct by the organization, acting alone and without external payment or direction.
ITID-52633.purpose: Captures a data leak by an employee acting on a perceived ethical violation by the employer, distinguishing this motive from other disgruntled-insider grievances.
scopeIncludes: A leak accompanied by the employee's stated belief that they were exposing wrongdoing
Disclosure to a regulator, media outlet, or public forum framed around an alleged ethical violation
scopeExcludes: A leak motivated by personal compensation grievance (ITID-52631) or job loss (ITID-52632) with no ethical-violation claim
A leak made through the organization's protected internal or regulatory whistleblower channel, which should be handled under the applicable whistleblower policy rather than as a security incident
ITID-52633.severity: Medium to High depending on data sensitivity; assess independently of whether the underlying ethical claim has merit.
ITID-52633.priority: P2, escalating to P1 based on data sensitivity or public/media/regulatory disclosure.
ITID-52633.escalation: Escalate to legal and compliance in parallel with, not instead of, HR and security; determine promptly whether the disclosure qualifies for protected-whistleblower treatment before pursuing a purely disciplinary or investigative response.
indicators: Disclosure accompanied by a stated ethical or legal concern about organizational conduct
Disclosure routed to a regulator, journalist, or public forum rather than an internal channel
Prior internal complaints or concerns raised by the same employee on a related topic
vectors: Direct disclosure to a regulator or journalist of documents believed to evidence wrongdoing
Internal forwarding of material to a colleague or external advocate believed sympathetic to the concern
rootCauses: Perceived absence of a credible, safe internal channel for raising ethical concerns
Employee perception that a prior internal complaint on the same topic was not taken seriously
controls: Well-publicized, trusted internal ethics/compliance reporting channel
Legal/compliance review process to determine whistleblower-protection applicability early in any investigation
ITID-52633.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies to the underlying human motivation; the specific exfiltration method used, if any, may have a technical signature tracked under the corresponding leaf in the Data Breaches domain.
ITID-52633.response: Determine whistleblower-protection status before pursuing disciplinary action against the employee; separately assess the validity of the underlying ethical concern through the compliance process.
metrics: Number of leaks correlated with a stated ethical concern per year
ITID-52633.notes: Requires careful legal/compliance coordination to distinguish a security-incident response from a protected-whistleblower disclosure; the two are not mutually exclusive and both tracks may need to proceed in parallel.

playbook.name: Leak Following Perceived Ethical Violation by Employer
playbook.description: An employee is discovered to have leaked confidential organizational information, motivated by a perceived ethical violation on the part of the employer, in what may resemble whistleblowing.

steps.title: Confirm the leak and assess whether whistleblower protections apply
steps.desc: Security and Legal jointly confirm the leak occurred and carefully assess, with Legal's guidance, whether the disclosure may qualify for whistleblower legal protections given its motivation.
steps.guidance: This determination materially changes the appropriate response; involve Legal early and handle with particular care, since a mischaracterized retaliatory response to a protected disclosure carries significant legal risk.
steps.outcome: A confirmed leak with a documented legal assessment of whistleblower-protection applicability.

steps.title: Assess the underlying ethical concern raised
steps.desc: Independently and in parallel, assess the substance of the ethical concern the employee raised, regardless of the propriety of the leak method.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the underlying concern's validity.

steps.title: Limit further unauthorized disclosure while preserving lawful channels
steps.desc: Take measured action to limit further unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information, while ensuring the employee retains access to any lawful/protected reporting channels (e.g., regulator, ethics hotline).
steps.outcome: Security exposure is managed without infringing on protected reporting rights.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Leak Following Perceived Ethical Violation by Employer" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Determine appropriate resolution with Legal guidance
steps.desc: Legal and HR jointly determine an appropriate resolution regarding both the leak and the underlying ethical concern, ensuring no retaliatory action is taken if whistleblower protections apply.
steps.outcome: A legally-guided, documented resolution.

steps.title: Confirm no further copies of the leaked information remain accessible
steps.desc: Where feasible, confirm that further copies or republications of the leaked information have been addressed (e.g., takedown request to a publisher or platform).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction in the leaked information's continued availability, where achievable.

steps.title: Address the underlying ethical concern through appropriate channels
steps.desc: Route the substantive ethical concern to Compliance, Internal Audit, or the Ethics function for proper investigation and resolution, independent of the security response.
steps.outcome: The underlying concern is addressed through appropriate governance channels.

steps.title: Document and brief Legal, Compliance, and Ethics leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report covering both the security handling and the ethical-concern resolution, with careful attention to legal sensitivities, and brief relevant leadership.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked on both fronts.

ITID-52634.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of a suspected disgruntled-insider leak pending determination of the specific motivating grievance.
ITID-52634.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected disgruntled-insider leaks that do not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of a disgruntled-insider leak prior to identifying the specific motivation
scopeExcludes: Any case where the motivation has already been established (ITID-52631/52632/52633)
ITID-52634.priority: P2 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52634.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of a suspected internally-motivated leak without a confirmed grievance
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52634.detection: No technical detection signature; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52634.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the motivation is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52634.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Disgruntled Insider Leaks group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Disgruntled Insider Leak
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case in which a disgruntled employee is suspected of leaking confidential organizational information.

steps.title: Confirm the leak and assess the underlying grievance
steps.desc: Security and HR jointly confirm the leak occurred and assess what grievance, if any, may have motivated it.
steps.outcome: A confirmed leak with a documented grievance assessment.

steps.title: Scope the information leaked and its recipient
steps.desc: Determine what information was leaked and to whom.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of leaked information.

steps.title: Restrict access and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Restrict the employee's access to sensitive systems and preserve relevant logs under legal hold.
steps.outcome: Further leakage is halted and evidence preserved.

steps.title: Coordinate with additional stakeholders as needed
steps.desc: Confirm all relevant internal stakeholders (Legal, HR, affected business unit) have been looped in appropriately for "Unclassified / General Disgruntled Insider Leak" before proceeding to eradication.
steps.outcome: All relevant stakeholders confirmed as informed and coordinated.

steps.title: Determine personnel action with HR and Legal
steps.desc: HR and Legal determine appropriate personnel action regarding the leak.
steps.outcome: Personnel action taken.

steps.title: Confirm no further copies of the leaked information remain accessible
steps.desc: Where feasible, confirm that further copies or republications of the leaked information have been addressed (e.g., takedown request to a publisher or platform).
steps.outcome: Confirmed reduction in the leaked information's continued availability, where achievable.

steps.title: Flag the underlying grievance for independent HR review
steps.desc: HR reviews whether the underlying grievance warrants attention independent of the security response.
steps.outcome: A documented, independent HR assessment.

steps.title: Document and brief HR and Legal leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52641.def: A long-term insider agent maintained in a dormant, low-activity state by a handler for an extended period — often years — using only their ordinary, valid account access to preserve cover, until a decision is made to activate them for a specific collection task.
ITID-52641.purpose: Captures the discovery of an insider recruited or placed long before any activity was required of them, maintained in a dormant state until activated.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed long-term insider relationship with an extended dormant period prior to any detected activity
Evidence that the individual maintained only ordinary access patterns for years before an activation event
scopeExcludes: An insider agent under active, ongoing tasking throughout the relationship rather than a dormant period (ITID-52642)
ITID-52641.severity: Critical. A confirmed sleeper arrangement implies a well-resourced, patient sponsor and a potentially very broad historical window of risk.
ITID-52641.priority: P1 upon confirmation or strong suspicion.
ITID-52641.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk, legal, and law enforcement/counter-intelligence liaison; scope the investigation across the individual's entire tenure, not just the recent activation period.
indicators: A sudden, marked change in an otherwise long-stable employee's access or behavior with no role change to explain it
Historical access review revealing the individual was positioned in a role with strategic access far earlier than any apparent need
Corroborating counter-intelligence intelligence identifying a dormant asset
vectors: Long-term maintenance of ordinary valid-account access with no anomalous activity until activation
Activation event triggering a sudden, targeted collection task
rootCauses: No periodic re-baselining of long-tenured employees' access relative to evolving role sensitivity
Insufficient historical log retention to support investigation of a multi-year dormant period
controls: Periodic re-baselining of long-tenured privileged users' access
Extended log retention supporting multi-year historical investigation
ITID-52641.detection: The dormant period itself is a human-intelligence matter with no technical detection signature; the activation event, when it occurs, uses the insider's ordinary valid accounts, giving the SOC a genuine (if narrow) technical signal via anomaly detection on an otherwise-stable access pattern.
ITID-52641.response: Scope the investigation across the individual's full tenure; coordinate closely with legal and law enforcement given the likely long timeline and evidentiary complexity.
metrics: Time between activation event and detection
Number of long-term insider agent cases confirmed per year
ITID-52641.notes: Unlike most leaves in the broader Insider Recruitment Tier-3, the activation event here can be tracked as anomalous use of valid accounts (T1078); the underlying recruitment and dormancy remain a human-intelligence matter with no ATT&CK Enterprise technique.

playbook.name: Multi-Year Sleeper Agent Awaiting Activation
playbook.description: An employee is identified, through counter-intelligence indicators, as a likely long-term 'sleeper' agent placed years earlier and awaiting activation by an external handler.

steps.title: Corroborate the sleeper-agent indicator without alerting the individual
steps.desc: Security, Legal, and (given the nature of the case) law enforcement/counter-intelligence authorities jointly and covertly assess the indicator suggesting a long-dormant placement, using historical background and access records.
steps.guidance: This is the most sensitive leaf in the taxonomy. Absolute discretion is required — any premature inquiry, access change, or conversation with the individual's manager or colleagues risks tipping off the individual and losing years of potential counter-intelligence value. Engage law enforcement/national counter-intelligence authorities before taking any action.
steps.outcome: A documented, tightly access-restricted assessment of the indicator's credibility, made without alerting the individual.
steps.abort: If insufficient corroboration exists, maintain silent, long-term observation rather than escalate.
steps.tool: Historical HR/background records (accessed discreetly); case management system (access-restricted to a minimal need-to-know group)

steps.title: Establish long-term, covert monitoring in coordination with law enforcement
steps.desc: With law-enforcement/Legal guidance, establish carefully designed covert monitoring of the individual's access and behavior over an extended period to build an evidentiary record.
steps.guidance: Monitoring design and legal authorization should be led by law enforcement/counter-intelligence partners given the specialized nature of this investigation.
steps.outcome: A documented, evidentiary record of the individual's activity, built without detection.
steps.tool: UEBA; SIEM (access restricted to minimal need-to-know group)

steps.title: Defer containment action until law enforcement's evidence-gathering objectives are met
steps.desc: Legal and law enforcement jointly determine the point at which continued observation is no longer more valuable than containment, weighing the multi-year evidentiary and network-mapping value of a careful, coordinated takedown against ongoing exposure risk.
steps.guidance: Do not act unilaterally; any containment step must be sequenced with law enforcement's investigation and, potentially, a broader operation against the handler network.
steps.outcome: A jointly agreed timeline and trigger conditions for eventual containment.
steps.abort: Escalate immediately if evidence indicates imminent, high-impact harm (e.g., pending sabotage or safety-critical data compromise) that outweighs continued observation value.

steps.title: Silently limit access to the highest-sensitivity systems if risk escalates
steps.desc: If risk escalates before the coordinated takedown point, quietly and minimally restrict access to the most sensitive systems using routine-looking cover (e.g., a standard access review).
steps.outcome: Reduced immediate risk without alerting the individual.

steps.title: Execute the coordinated takedown with law enforcement
steps.desc: At the agreed trigger point, execute a coordinated separation and evidence-seizure action jointly planned with law enforcement/counter-intelligence authorities.
steps.guidance: Follow the law-enforcement operational plan precisely; this is a joint operation, not a unilateral HR/security action.
steps.outcome: The individual is separated and evidence secured under chain of custody, with any broader handler network exposure assessed.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any broader network exposed by the operation
steps.desc: With law enforcement, assess whether the coordinated takedown revealed a broader handler network or additional compromised individuals requiring further action.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of broader network exposure and any follow-on action required.

steps.title: Conduct a comprehensive, multi-year exposure assessment
steps.desc: Assess the full scope of information likely compromised over the individual's entire tenure, informed by the evidentiary record built during the investigation.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive, documented exposure assessment spanning the individual's full tenure.

steps.title: Conduct a phased, need-to-know restoration of affected systems
steps.desc: Restore affected systems and access in a phased manner, validated at each step, given the extended duration of the compromise.
steps.outcome: Systems restored in a controlled, validated manner.

steps.title: Conduct an executive- and board-level restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Produce a tightly access-restricted after-action report and brief executive leadership and the board (or audit committee) given the strategic counter-intelligence significance.
steps.outcome: A documented, appropriately restricted report with strengthened long-term insider-threat detection recommendations.

ITID-52642.def: A long-term insider agent who maintains an active, recurring relationship with an external handler over an extended period, receiving periodic tasking and providing information on an ongoing basis using their valid, ordinary access and, frequently, a covert communication channel.
ITID-52642.purpose: Captures an insider agent who receives ongoing, recurring tasking from a handler over an extended period, as distinct from a one-time recruitment or a dormant sleeper arrangement.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed long-term insider relationship characterized by recurring tasking and delivery over months or years
Use of a covert communication channel to receive tasking or deliver information on an ongoing basis
scopeExcludes: A dormant sleeper arrangement with no ongoing tasking until a single activation event (ITID-52641)
ITID-52642.severity: Critical. Ongoing tasking implies a sustained, active operational relationship with the broadest cumulative data exposure among the insider-recruitment leaves.
ITID-52642.priority: P1 upon confirmation or strong suspicion.
ITID-52642.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk, legal, and law enforcement/counter-intelligence liaison; preserve evidence of the communication channel and full history of access.
indicators: Recurring, periodic pattern of anomalous access or data movement over an extended period
Recurring use of a covert communication channel (see ITID-52113) correlating with access spikes
Financial or behavioral indicators consistent with sustained, ongoing compensation from a handler
vectors: Recurring use of valid account access to collect tasked information
Recurring use of a dead-drop or covert digital channel to receive tasking and deliver collected data
rootCauses: Insufficient longitudinal behavioral analytics capable of detecting a recurring, low-and-slow pattern rather than a single spike
No correlation between covert-channel indicators and account access patterns
mitreTechniques: T1102.001 Web Service: Dead Drop Resolver
controls: Longitudinal behavioral analytics tuned for recurring, low-and-slow insider patterns
Correlation between covert-channel and account-access telemetry
ITID-52642.detection: Stronger than most insider-recruitment leaves: the recurring tasking relationship gives the SOC a genuine technical signal both through ordinary valid-account usage patterns and through any covert digital communication channel used for tasking.
ITID-52642.response: Map the full multi-year history of access and communication before any containment action; coordinate closely with legal and law enforcement given the likely criminal proceedings.
metrics: Duration of the tasking relationship before detection
Number of long-term insider agent cases confirmed per year
ITID-52642.notes: Distinguished from ITID-52641 by the presence of ongoing, recurring tasking rather than a single dormant-to-activation transition; carries the same technical follow-through exception (T1078, and T1102.001 where a covert digital channel is used) as ITID-52113.

playbook.name: Insider Agent Receiving Ongoing Handler Tasking Over Extended Period
playbook.description: An employee is discovered to be an active insider agent, receiving ongoing tasking from an external handler and providing information or access over an extended period.

steps.title: Corroborate the ongoing-tasking indicator discreetly
steps.desc: Security, Legal, and law enforcement/counter-intelligence authorities jointly and discreetly assess the indicator suggesting ongoing handler tasking.
steps.guidance: As with sleeper-agent cases, discretion is paramount — premature action risks tipping off the individual and losing the opportunity to identify the handler and tasking pattern.
steps.outcome: A documented, access-restricted assessment of the indicator's credibility.
steps.abort: If insufficient, maintain quiet, long-term observation rather than escalate.

steps.title: Characterize the tasking pattern and handler relationship
steps.desc: With law-enforcement guidance, establish covert monitoring to characterize the recurring tasking pattern, communication method, and apparent handler relationship.
steps.outcome: A documented understanding of the tasking cadence and handler relationship, built without detection.

steps.title: Coordinate containment timing with law enforcement before any action
steps.desc: Legal and law enforcement jointly determine the appropriate point to move from observation to containment, weighing the ongoing evidence-gathering value against continued exposure.
steps.guidance: Do not act unilaterally; sequence with any broader law-enforcement operation against the handler.
steps.outcome: A jointly agreed containment timeline and trigger conditions.
steps.abort: Escalate immediately if evidence indicates imminent, high-impact harm.

steps.title: Silently limit access if risk escalates before the planned takedown
steps.desc: If needed before the coordinated takedown point, quietly and minimally restrict access using routine-looking cover.
steps.outcome: Reduced immediate risk without alerting the individual.

steps.title: Execute the coordinated takedown with law enforcement
steps.desc: At the agreed trigger point, execute a coordinated separation and evidence-seizure action jointly planned with law enforcement/counter-intelligence authorities.
steps.outcome: The individual is separated and evidence secured under chain of custody.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any broader network exposed by the operation
steps.desc: With law enforcement, assess whether the coordinated takedown revealed a broader handler network or additional compromised individuals requiring further action.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of broader network exposure and any follow-on action required.

steps.title: Conduct a comprehensive exposure assessment across the tasking period
steps.desc: Assess the full scope of information compromised across the entire period of active tasking.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive, documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Conduct a phased, need-to-know restoration of affected systems
steps.desc: Restore affected systems and access in a phased manner, validated at each step, given the extended duration of the compromise.
steps.outcome: Systems restored in a controlled, validated manner.

steps.title: Conduct an executive- and board-level restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Produce a tightly access-restricted after-action report and brief executive leadership and the board given the counter-intelligence significance.
steps.outcome: A documented, appropriately restricted report with strengthened detection recommendations.

ITID-52643.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of a suspected long-term insider agent relationship, pending determination of whether it involves a dormant sleeper arrangement or ongoing recurring tasking.
ITID-52643.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected long-term insider agent activity that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of a long-term insider relationship prior to determining its operational pattern
scopeExcludes: Any case where the pattern has already been established (ITID-52641/52642)
ITID-52643.priority: P1 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52643.escalation: Escalate to insider risk and law enforcement/counter-intelligence liaison on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of a suspected sustained insider relationship without a confirmed operational pattern
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow
ITID-52643.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52643.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the operational pattern is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52643.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Long-Term Insider Agents group.

playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case in which an employee is suspected of acting as a long-term insider agent for an external party.

steps.title: Establish covert monitoring to characterize the activity

steps.title: Coordinate containment timing with law enforcement

steps.guidance: Do not act unilaterally.
steps.outcome: A jointly agreed containment timeline.

steps.title: Conduct a restricted after-action review
steps.desc: Produce a tightly access-restricted after-action report and brief executive leadership.
steps.outcome: A documented, appropriately restricted report with strengthened detection recommendations.

ITID-52711.def: Espionage in which an adversary — an external intruder or a directed insider — systematically collects data from cloud storage or file-sharing platforms (object storage, cloud drives, shared workspaces) rather than from on-premises systems.
ITID-52711.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated harvesting of data directly from cloud storage or file-sharing platforms.
scopeIncludes: Bulk or selective download from cloud storage/file-sharing platforms consistent with espionage-motivated collection
Use of compromised or insider cloud credentials to browse and harvest shared workspace content
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a specific SaaS application's business logic or features beyond basic storage access (ITID-52721)
Abuse of cloud provider APIs specifically to automate collection at scale (ITID-52731)
ITID-52711.severity: High to Critical depending on the volume and sensitivity of data harvested.
ITID-52711.priority: P1 upon confirmation of espionage-motivated cloud data collection.
ITID-52711.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; determine whether the access originated from a compromised credential or a directed insider, as this materially changes the investigation path.
indicators: Anomalous bulk download or access volume from cloud storage inconsistent with the account's normal usage
Access to shared workspaces or folders outside the accessing user's normal scope of work
Access from an unfamiliar location or device to cloud storage holding sensitive material
vectors: Compromised cloud account credentials used to browse and download shared storage
Insider use of legitimate cloud access to harvest broader shared content than their role requires
rootCauses: Overly broad sharing permissions on cloud storage and workspaces
Insufficient monitoring of bulk download/access volume from cloud storage
controls: Least-privilege sharing permissions on cloud storage and workspaces
Cloud access security broker (CASB) or native cloud DLP monitoring bulk download volume
ITID-52711.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; cloud audit logging and CASB/DLP tooling provide a reasonably strong technical detection surface where enabled and tuned.
ITID-52711.response: Revoke and rotate the credential/session used; assess scope of data accessed via cloud audit logs.
metrics: Number of cloud data harvesting incidents per year
Percentage of cloud storage with least-privilege sharing enforced
ITID-52711.notes: Lone-child stub for this Tier-4 group; captures the general cloud-storage collection case, distinct from SaaS-application-specific and API-abuse leaves in this same Tier-3.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud Data Harvesting (Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have systematically harvested data from the organization's cloud environment, motivated by intelligence-gathering rather than financial gain.

steps.title: Confirm cloud data harvesting and its scope
steps.desc: Cloud security reviews audit logs to confirm systematic data access/download activity consistent with harvesting, and identifies the accounts and resources involved.
steps.guidance: Review cloud audit logs (e.g., CloudTrail-equivalent) for bulk data access, unusual API call volume, or cross-region replication anomalies.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of harvesting activity and its scope.

steps.title: Assess whether the targeted data has strategic or competitive value
steps.desc: Review the specific data harvested for strategic, competitive, or intelligence value, distinct from a standard financial/PII-focused breach assessment.
steps.guidance: Given the espionage motive, prioritize identifying data with strategic or competitive significance, not only regulated personal data.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the strategic significance of the harvested data.

steps.title: Revoke compromised credentials and API access
steps.desc: Revoke or rotate compromised cloud credentials, API keys, and access tokens associated with the harvesting activity.
steps.outcome: Further harvesting via the identified access is halted.

steps.title: Review and tighten cloud access-control configurations
steps.desc: Review the cloud resource permissions and configurations that enabled the harvesting and tighten them to least privilege.
steps.outcome: Reduced attack surface for future harvesting attempts.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and remediate the initial access vector
steps.desc: Determine how the initial access was obtained (misconfigured bucket, compromised credential, third-party integration) and remediate it.
steps.outcome: The initial access vector is closed.

steps.title: Audit related cloud resources for similar misconfiguration or exposure
steps.desc: Audit other cloud resources, accounts, or SaaS integrations for the same class of misconfiguration or exposure that enabled this incident.
steps.outcome: Related exposures identified and remediated proactively.

steps.title: Restore secure configuration and enhance monitoring
steps.desc: Validate that cloud configurations are restored to a secure baseline and implement enhanced monitoring for anomalous data-access patterns.
steps.outcome: Strengthened cloud monitoring and configuration posture.

steps.title: Validate least-privilege posture before restoring full access
steps.desc: Validate that restored or reinstated access follows least-privilege principles before returning to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed least-privilege access posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief cloud security and leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52721.def: Espionage in which an adversary exploits the specific features of a SaaS application (e.g., collaboration suites, CRM, HR platforms) — search, export, sharing, or integration functionality — to collect intelligence at a scale or scope beyond simple file access.
ITID-52721.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated exploitation of a specific SaaS application's features or business logic — beyond basic storage access — to collect intelligence.
scopeIncludes: Use of a SaaS application's native search/export functionality to systematically collect data beyond normal usage
Abuse of SaaS-native sharing or integration features to establish a persistent collection channel
scopeExcludes: Basic bulk download from cloud storage without exploiting application-specific features (ITID-52711)
Automated collection specifically via the platform's API (ITID-52731)
ITID-52721.severity: High to Critical depending on the SaaS platform's data sensitivity and the scope of the exploitation.
ITID-52721.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; involve the SaaS vendor's security team where the exploitation involves a platform-level feature or misconfiguration.
indicators: Anomalous use of a SaaS application's export or bulk-search functionality
Unusual configuration of sharing or integration features enabling persistent external access
Access pattern inconsistent with the user's normal role within the SaaS platform
vectors: Abuse of native export functionality (e.g., a CRM contact export or document management system search-and-export)
Establishment of a persistent external share or integration to enable ongoing collection
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of SaaS-native export and sharing feature usage
Overly permissive default configuration of SaaS integration/sharing features
mitreTechniques: T1213.002 Data from Information Repositories: Sharepoint
controls: SaaS security posture management (SSPM) monitoring export/sharing feature usage
Regular review of SaaS integration and sharing configurations
ITID-52721.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; detection depends on SaaS-native audit logging and SSPM tooling, and coverage varies significantly by platform.
ITID-52721.response: Disable the exploited feature/integration; assess scope of data exposed through SaaS-native audit logs.
metrics: Number of SaaS exploitation incidents per year
ITID-52721.notes: The T1213.002 mapping (SharePoint) is illustrative of one common SaaS platform; treat the actual mapped technique as platform-dependent for any specific case.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General SaaS Exploitation for Espionage
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have exploited a SaaS application used by the organization for intelligence-gathering purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the SaaS exploitation and affected application
steps.desc: Security reviews SaaS application audit logs and any vendor security advisories to confirm exploitation and identify the affected application and accounts.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the SaaS vendor's security team, since much of the relevant telemetry resides in the vendor's environment.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of exploitation and affected scope.
steps.tool: SaaS application audit logs; CASB tooling

steps.title: Assess whether the targeted data has strategic or competitive value
steps.desc: Review the specific data accessible via the exploited application for strategic or competitive significance.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the strategic significance of the exposed data.

steps.title: Revoke compromised sessions and credentials
steps.desc: Revoke compromised sessions, API tokens, and OAuth grants associated with the affected SaaS application.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation via the identified access is halted.

steps.title: Coordinate remediation with the SaaS vendor
steps.desc: Work with the SaaS vendor to apply any available patch or configuration fix and confirm the vulnerability is closed.
steps.outcome: The vulnerability is remediated by the vendor or via configuration change.

steps.title: Review and tighten SaaS application permissions and integrations
steps.desc: Review third-party integrations and permission scopes for the affected SaaS application and tighten to least privilege.
steps.outcome: Reduced attack surface for future exploitation.

steps.title: Audit related cloud resources for similar misconfiguration or exposure
steps.desc: Audit other cloud resources, accounts, or SaaS integrations for the same class of misconfiguration or exposure that enabled this incident.
steps.outcome: Related exposures identified and remediated proactively.

steps.title: Enhance SaaS security monitoring
steps.desc: Implement or enhance monitoring for anomalous SaaS application usage and access patterns.
steps.outcome: Strengthened SaaS monitoring posture.

steps.title: Validate least-privilege posture before restoring full access
steps.desc: Validate that restored or reinstated access follows least-privilege principles before returning to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed least-privilege access posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52731.def: Espionage in which an adversary uses a cloud or SaaS platform's programmatic API — often via a stolen API key, OAuth token, or service-account credential — to automate large-scale or persistent data collection outside the normal user interface.
ITID-52731.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated abuse of cloud provider or SaaS platform APIs to automate collection at scale, typically using stolen tokens or credentials.
scopeIncludes: Use of a stolen or abused API key/token to programmatically enumerate and extract data
Establishment of a persistent OAuth grant or service-account credential enabling ongoing automated collection
scopeExcludes: Manual, UI-driven exploitation of a SaaS application's features (ITID-52721)
ITID-52731.severity: High to Critical, given that API-based collection can operate at much greater speed and scale than manual access.
ITID-52731.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; revoke the abused credential/token immediately given the scale-up risk inherent to API-driven collection.
indicators: Anomalous API call volume or pattern inconsistent with normal application usage
An OAuth grant or service-account credential with broader scope than its stated purpose
API access from an unfamiliar IP range or at a time inconsistent with normal business usage
vectors: Stolen API key or OAuth token used to programmatically enumerate and extract data
Malicious or over-permissioned third-party application granted OAuth access
rootCauses: Insufficient scoping and review of OAuth grants and API keys
No API-call-volume anomaly detection on cloud/SaaS platforms
controls: OAuth grant and API key review/scoping program
API call-volume and pattern anomaly detection
ITID-52731.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; API-level audit logging, where enabled, provides a strong technical detection surface for volume and pattern anomalies.
ITID-52731.response: Revoke the abused API key/OAuth grant immediately; assess the full scope of data accessible through the compromised credential's scope.
metrics: Number of API abuse incidents per year
Percentage of OAuth grants reviewed in the past 12 months
ITID-52731.notes: Cross-reference the fuller credential-theft treatments elsewhere in the taxonomy for how the underlying API key/token was likely obtained.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud API Abuse (Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have abused the organization's cloud API access for intelligence-gathering purposes.

steps.title: Confirm API abuse and identify the affected API/account
steps.desc: Cloud/API security reviews API gateway and cloud audit logs to confirm abuse and identify the affected API endpoints and calling accounts.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of abuse and affected scope.
steps.tool: API gateway logs; cloud audit logs

steps.title: Assess whether the targeted data has strategic or competitive value
steps.desc: Review the specific data accessible via the abused API for strategic or competitive significance.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the strategic significance of the exposed data.

steps.title: Revoke compromised API keys/tokens and rate-limit the source
steps.desc: Revoke the compromised API keys or tokens and apply rate-limiting or blocking to the source of the abuse.
steps.outcome: Further abuse via the identified access is halted.
steps.tool: API gateway admin console; cloud IAM console

steps.title: Review and tighten API permission scopes
steps.desc: Review the permission scopes granted to the abused API access and tighten to least privilege.
steps.outcome: Reduced attack surface for future abuse.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and remediate the initial access vector
steps.desc: Determine how the initial API access was obtained and remediate the root cause.
steps.outcome: The initial access vector is closed.

steps.title: Audit related cloud resources for similar misconfiguration or exposure
steps.desc: Audit other cloud resources, accounts, or SaaS integrations for the same class of misconfiguration or exposure that enabled this incident.
steps.outcome: Related exposures identified and remediated proactively.

steps.title: Enhance API monitoring and anomaly detection
steps.desc: Implement or enhance monitoring for anomalous API usage patterns.
steps.outcome: Strengthened API monitoring posture.

steps.title: Validate least-privilege posture before restoring full access
steps.desc: Validate that restored or reinstated access follows least-privilege principles before returning to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed least-privilege access posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52741.def: Espionage in which an adversary reaches the target organization's cloud or SaaS environment through a trusted cross-tenant relationship — a shared parent/partner tenant, a multi-tenant platform misconfiguration, or a compromised partner organization's access — rather than direct intrusion.
ITID-52741.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated abuse of a trusted cross-tenant relationship — a shared cloud tenant, partner integration, or multi-tenant SaaS misconfiguration — to reach the target organization's data.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of a partner or affiliated organization's tenant subsequently used to access the target's data via a trust relationship
Exploitation of a multi-tenant SaaS platform misconfiguration allowing cross-tenant data access
scopeExcludes: Direct compromise of the target's own tenant with no cross-tenant trust relationship involved
ITID-52741.severity: Critical, given that cross-tenant compromise can bypass the target's own perimeter and access controls entirely.
ITID-52741.priority: P1 upon confirmation of a cross-tenant vector.
ITID-52741.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership immediately; coordinate with the affected partner organization and, where a platform-level misconfiguration is involved, the SaaS/cloud provider.
indicators: Access to the organization's tenant originating from an unexpected partner/affiliated tenant
Evidence of a platform-level cross-tenant data-isolation failure reported by the provider or discovered through investigation
Anomalous activity in a partner-facing integration or shared workspace
vectors: Compromise of a partner organization's tenant used to pivot into the target via an established trust relationship
Exploitation of a multi-tenant platform's data-isolation flaw
rootCauses: Overly broad or insufficiently reviewed cross-tenant trust relationships
Reliance on the SaaS/cloud provider's tenant-isolation guarantees without independent verification
controls: Periodic review and least-privilege scoping of cross-tenant trust relationships
Independent monitoring of cross-tenant access patterns rather than relying solely on provider isolation guarantees
ITID-52741.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; detection depends on monitoring cross-tenant access patterns specifically, which is frequently a coverage gap since most logging assumes single-tenant boundaries.
ITID-52741.response: Coordinate the investigation with the partner organization and/or platform provider; assess and, if necessary, suspend the cross-tenant trust relationship while investigating.
metrics: Number of cross-tenant incidents per year
Percentage of cross-tenant trust relationships reviewed in the past 12 months
ITID-52741.notes: Lone-child stub for this Tier-4 group; cross-reference the organization's broader third-party/vendor risk program.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cross-Tenant Attack (Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have exploited a cross-tenant vulnerability in a shared cloud/SaaS platform to access the organization's data for intelligence-gathering purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the cross-tenant exposure and affected platform
steps.desc: Security, in coordination with the cloud/SaaS provider, confirms whether a cross-tenant isolation failure occurred and what organizational data was exposed.
steps.guidance: Cross-tenant incidents require close coordination with the platform provider, who controls the underlying isolation mechanism and typically leads the technical root-cause investigation.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the cross-tenant exposure and its scope.
steps.tool: Provider incident report; cloud audit logs

steps.title: Assess whether the exposed data has strategic or competitive value
steps.desc: Review the specific data exposed via the cross-tenant issue for strategic or competitive significance.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the strategic significance of the exposed data.

steps.title: Coordinate with the provider to close the isolation failure
steps.desc: Work with the platform provider to confirm the isolation failure has been remediated and no further cross-tenant access is possible.
steps.outcome: The provider confirms remediation of the isolation failure.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and review access as a precaution
steps.desc: As a precaution, rotate credentials and review access logs for the affected tenant environment.
steps.outcome: Reduced residual risk from the exposure window.

steps.title: Validate the provider's remediation and request an independent assessment if warranted
steps.desc: Request evidence or an independent assessment of the provider's remediation, particularly if the exposed data was highly sensitive.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated remediation of the underlying platform vulnerability.

steps.title: Audit related cloud resources for similar misconfiguration or exposure
steps.desc: Audit other cloud resources, accounts, or SaaS integrations for the same class of misconfiguration or exposure that enabled this incident.
steps.outcome: Related exposures identified and remediated proactively.

steps.title: Reassess reliance on the affected platform for sensitive data
steps.desc: Review whether continued use of the platform for sensitive data is appropriate given the incident, and adjust data-placement policy if needed.
steps.outcome: A documented risk-based decision on continued platform use.

steps.title: Validate least-privilege posture before restoring full access
steps.desc: Validate that restored or reinstated access follows least-privilege principles before returning to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed least-privilege access posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership on third-party platform risk
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief leadership on findings, including third-party/vendor risk implications.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52811.def: Theft or harvesting of employee credentials — via phishing, brute force, or credential-stuffing — carried out in service of a broader espionage operation, as distinct from opportunistic, non-espionage-motivated credential theft.
ITID-52811.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated harvesting of employee credentials specifically as a precursor to intelligence-gathering access.
scopeIncludes: Credential harvesting confirmed or suspected to be directed by a competitor or state sponsor as part of a targeted operation
Credential harvesting occurring alongside other espionage indicators (e.g., targeted spearphishing of specific roles with strategic access)
scopeExcludes: Opportunistic, non-espionage-motivated credential theft, tracked in the Data Breaches domain's credential-theft leaves
Session hijacking after a credential has already granted access (ITID-52821)
ITID-52811.severity: High to Critical depending on the privilege level of the harvested credential and the sponsor's sophistication.
ITID-52811.priority: P1 once an espionage nexus is confirmed or strongly suspected.
ITID-52811.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership on confirmation of an espionage nexus; force credential reset and review all activity performed under the compromised credential.
indicators: Targeted spearphishing of specific roles with strategic data access rather than broad opportunistic phishing
Credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts concentrated on accounts with known strategic value
Corroborating espionage indicators such as attributed intrusion infrastructure
vectors: Targeted spearphishing designed to harvest credentials from specific high-value roles
Brute-force or credential-stuffing against accounts identified through prior reconnaissance
rootCauses: Insufficient MFA enforcement on accounts with strategic data access
Reconnaissance-derived targeting not correlated with subsequent phishing/brute-force detection
controls: Universal MFA enforcement, prioritized for strategic-access accounts
Phishing-resistant authentication (e.g., FIDO2) for high-value roles
ITID-52811.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; standard credential-access detection techniques apply and are covered in fuller depth by the parallel credential-theft treatments elsewhere in the taxonomy — this leaf exists to flag the espionage-motive distinction.
ITID-52811.response: Force credential reset and review all activity performed under the compromised credential; correlate with threat intelligence to assess sponsor attribution.
metrics: Number of espionage-motivated credential harvesting cases per year
ITID-52811.notes: Lone-child stub for this Tier-4 group; cross-reference the fuller credential-theft treatments in the Data Breaches domain for detection detail not duplicated here — this leaf is scoped to the espionage-motive distinction.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Credential Harvesting for Espionage
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have harvested employee credentials with the intent of using them to gain intelligence-gathering access to organizational systems.

steps.title: Confirm credential harvesting and identify affected accounts
steps.desc: Security reviews phishing reports, dark-web credential-monitoring alerts, or authentication anomalies to confirm harvesting occurred and identify affected accounts.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of harvesting and affected account scope.
steps.tool: Email security gateway; dark-web monitoring; SIEM

steps.title: Assess whether harvested accounts have access to strategically valuable data
steps.desc: Determine whether the affected accounts have access to data of strategic or competitive value, given the espionage motive, not only financial/PII exposure.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of strategic exposure risk.

steps.title: Force credential resets and MFA re-enrollment
steps.desc: Force password resets and MFA re-enrollment for all affected accounts immediately.
steps.outcome: Harvested credentials are no longer valid.

steps.title: Review affected accounts for signs of prior unauthorized use
steps.desc: Review authentication and access logs for the affected accounts to determine whether the harvested credentials were already used for unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of whether unauthorized access already occurred.

steps.title: Remediate the harvesting vector
steps.desc: Address the root cause of the harvesting (e.g., phishing campaign, credential-stuffing exposure) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: The harvesting vector is closed.

steps.title: Audit for other accounts affected by the same technique
steps.desc: Audit the broader account population for exposure to the same credential or identity-compromise technique observed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Any additional exposed accounts are identified and remediated.

steps.title: Strengthen credential-hardening measures
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen phishing-resistant MFA and credential-monitoring controls for at-risk accounts.
steps.outcome: Strengthened credential-security posture.

steps.title: Validate hardened authentication controls before restoring normal access
steps.desc: Validate that hardened authentication controls are functioning correctly before returning the affected account(s) to normal access levels.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated hardened authentication posture.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52821.def: Theft and reuse of an active session token, cookie, or authentication artifact — bypassing the need for a username/password or even MFA — carried out in service of a broader espionage operation.
ITID-52821.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated hijacking of an already-authenticated session — via stolen session tokens or cookies — to gain intelligence access without needing the underlying credential.
scopeIncludes: Theft and reuse of a session cookie or token to access an account without re-authenticating
Use of an adversary-in-the-middle or malware-based technique to capture a live session artifact
scopeExcludes: Initial credential harvesting that precedes, but does not itself involve, session hijacking (ITID-52811)
ITID-52821.severity: High to Critical, since session hijacking typically bypasses MFA entirely, giving the adversary access equivalent to the legitimate user without needing to defeat the second factor.
ITID-52821.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; invalidate all active sessions for the affected account immediately, not just the specific hijacked session.
indicators: Session activity from an impossible or highly anomalous location relative to the legitimate user's last known session
Session token reuse detected after the token's expected device/IP fingerprint changes
Malware or adversary-in-the-middle indicators on the endpoint consistent with session-cookie theft
vectors: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing kit capturing session cookies in real time
Malware harvesting browser session tokens from an infected endpoint
rootCauses: Session tokens with excessively long validity periods and no device-binding
Insufficient anomaly detection on session continuity (impossible travel, device fingerprint change)
mitreTechniques: T1550.001 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
controls: Device-bound or short-lived session tokens
Session continuity anomaly detection (impossible travel, device fingerprint change)
ITID-52821.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; session-anomaly detection provides a real technical signal, though it is less mature at most organizations than credential-based detection.
ITID-52821.response: Invalidate all active sessions for the affected account, not just the identified hijacked session; assess what was accessed during the session window.
metrics: Number of session hijacking incidents per year
ITID-52821.notes: Cross-reference the fuller credential/session-theft treatments elsewhere in the taxonomy for how the underlying session artifact was likely obtained.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Session Hijacking for Intelligence Access
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have hijacked an active user session to gain intelligence-gathering access to organizational systems.

steps.title: Confirm session hijacking and identify the affected session/account
steps.desc: Security reviews authentication and session logs to confirm session hijacking (e.g., token theft, session-cookie replay) occurred and identify the affected account.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of session hijacking and affected account scope.

steps.title: Assess whether the hijacked session accessed strategically valuable data
steps.desc: Determine what data or systems were accessed during the hijacked session, prioritizing identification of strategically or competitively valuable data given the espionage motive.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Invalidate the hijacked session and rotate tokens
steps.desc: Immediately invalidate the hijacked session and rotate any associated authentication tokens.
steps.outcome: The hijacked session is no longer usable.

steps.title: Force credential reset and MFA re-enrollment for the affected account
steps.desc: Force a password reset and MFA re-enrollment for the affected account as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Residual access via the compromised account is eliminated.

steps.title: Remediate the hijacking vector
steps.desc: Determine and remediate the technique used to hijack the session (e.g., cross-site scripting vulnerability, malware-based token theft, insecure session handling).
steps.outcome: The hijacking vector is closed.

steps.title: Audit for other accounts affected by the same technique
steps.desc: Audit the broader account population for exposure to the same credential or identity-compromise technique observed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Any additional exposed accounts are identified and remediated.

steps.title: Strengthen session-security controls
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen session-security controls (short session lifetimes, token binding, anomaly detection for session reuse).
steps.outcome: Strengthened session-security posture.
