steps.title: Validate hardened authentication controls before restoring normal access
steps.desc: Validate that hardened authentication controls are functioning correctly before returning the affected account(s) to normal access levels.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated hardened authentication posture.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52831.def: Circumvention of an account's multi-factor authentication protection — through prompt-bombing/MFA fatigue, SIM-swapping, or exploitation of a weak MFA fallback method — carried out in service of a broader espionage operation.
ITID-52831.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated bypass of multi-factor authentication controls, most commonly via MFA fatigue/prompt-bombing, to gain intelligence access.
scopeIncludes: Repeated MFA push-notification prompting intended to induce accidental approval (MFA fatigue/prompt bombing)
SIM-swap or other interception of an SMS/voice-based MFA fallback
scopeExcludes: Initial credential harvesting that precedes, but does not itself defeat, MFA (ITID-52811)
ITID-52831.severity: High to Critical, since successful MFA bypass indicates the account's strongest available control has already been defeated.
ITID-52831.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; force credential and MFA method reset for the affected account.
indicators: A burst of MFA push notifications in a short period, especially outside the user's normal working hours
User report of unexpected MFA prompts they did not initiate
Evidence of a SIM-swap or carrier-account change preceding an MFA bypass
vectors: Repeated automated MFA push prompting until the user approves out of fatigue or confusion
SIM-swapping to intercept SMS-based MFA codes
rootCauses: Reliance on push-notification MFA without number-matching or phishing-resistant alternatives
SMS/voice-based MFA fallback left enabled for high-value accounts
controls: Number-matching or phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO2) for high-value accounts
Removal of SMS/voice MFA fallback for high-value accounts
ITID-52831.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; MFA-prompt-volume anomaly detection provides a strong, well-understood technical signal for the prompt-bombing variant specifically.
ITID-52831.response: Force credential and MFA method reset immediately; review all activity performed after the bypass.
metrics: Number of MFA bypass incidents per year
Percentage of high-value accounts on phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-52831.notes: Cross-reference the fuller credential-theft treatments elsewhere in the taxonomy for how the underlying credential was likely obtained prior to the MFA bypass attempt.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General MFA Bypass for Espionage
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have bypassed multi-factor authentication controls to gain intelligence-gathering access to organizational systems.

steps.title: Confirm the MFA bypass technique and affected account
steps.desc: Security reviews authentication logs to confirm the specific MFA-bypass technique used (e.g., MFA fatigue/push-bombing, SIM-swap, adversary-in-the-middle proxy) and identify the affected account.
steps.guidance: Identifying the specific bypass technique is important, since remediation differs materially between push-bombing, SIM-swap, and phishing-proxy techniques.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the bypass technique and affected account scope.

steps.title: Assess whether the account accessed strategically valuable data
steps.desc: Determine what data or systems were accessed following the MFA bypass, prioritizing strategically or competitively valuable data.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and force credential/MFA re-enrollment
steps.desc: Revoke all active sessions for the affected account and force password reset and full MFA re-enrollment.
steps.outcome: The compromised access is fully revoked.

steps.title: Apply technique-specific hardening
steps.desc: Apply hardening specific to the confirmed bypass technique (e.g., number-matching MFA to counter push-bombing, carrier-level SIM-swap protection, phishing-resistant FIDO2/WebAuthn to counter proxy-based bypass).
steps.outcome: The specific bypass technique is no longer viable.

steps.title: Investigate root cause and remediate broader exposure
steps.desc: Determine whether other accounts are similarly exposed to the same bypass technique and remediate broadly.
steps.outcome: The bypass technique is closed organization-wide, not just for the affected account.

steps.title: Audit for other accounts affected by the same technique
steps.desc: Audit the broader account population for exposure to the same credential or identity-compromise technique observed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Any additional exposed accounts are identified and remediated.

steps.title: Roll out phishing-resistant MFA more broadly if warranted
steps.desc: Where the incident reveals a systemic MFA weakness, evaluate and roll out phishing-resistant MFA methods to at-risk populations.
steps.outcome: Strengthened MFA posture across the organization.

steps.title: Validate hardened authentication controls before restoring normal access
steps.desc: Validate that hardened authentication controls are functioning correctly before returning the affected account(s) to normal access levels.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated hardened authentication posture.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52841.def: Impersonation of a legitimate employee, executive, or trusted third party — via synthetic media (deepfake video/audio), fabricated identification, or fraudulent credential presentation — carried out to gain access or extract information as part of a broader espionage operation.
ITID-52841.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated impersonation of a legitimate individual's identity — through deepfake, voice cloning, or fabricated credentials — to gain access or extract information.
scopeIncludes: Use of synthetic voice or video to impersonate an executive or employee for access or information requests
Presentation of fabricated identification or credentials to gain physical or logical access
scopeExcludes: Non-synthetic, low-tech pretexting (e.g., a simple phone pretext call) with no impersonation of a specific real individual's identity, which is tracked under Social Engineering Reconnaissance (ITID-5252x)
ITID-52841.severity: High to Critical, particularly where synthetic media is used to impersonate a specific executive, given the difficulty of detection and the trust typically placed in such communications.
ITID-52841.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership; where the impersonated individual is an executive, notify them and their team directly and quickly.
indicators: A request from a purported executive or trusted party that is unusual in nature, urgency, or channel
Audio/video artifacts inconsistent with genuine recordings (subtle synchronization or quality anomalies)
The purported individual denying having made the request when verified out-of-band
vectors: Synthetic voice call impersonating an executive to request sensitive information or urgent action
Fabricated video/audio used to authenticate a request through a channel that trusts audio/visual confirmation
rootCauses: No out-of-band verification requirement for unusual or urgent requests purportedly from executives
Employee unfamiliarity with the growing realism and accessibility of synthetic media tools
controls: Mandatory out-of-band verification for unusual or urgent executive requests
Employee awareness training on synthetic media/deepfake impersonation risk
ITID-52841.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; synthetic media detection technology remains immature, so out-of-band verification process controls are currently more reliable than technical detection.
ITID-52841.response: Verify the request out-of-band immediately upon suspicion; notify the impersonated individual and reinforce verification procedures organization-wide.
metrics: Number of suspected impersonation attempts reported per year
ITID-52841.notes: Given the current immaturity of technical synthetic-media detection, process controls (mandatory out-of-band verification) are the primary defense for this leaf.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Identity Spoofing (Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An external actor is discovered to have spoofed the identity of a trusted individual or system to gain intelligence-gathering access to organizational systems or information.

steps.title: Confirm the identity-spoofing technique and scope
steps.desc: Security investigates the reported or detected indicator (e.g., spoofed email domain, impersonated executive, forged credentials) to confirm spoofing occurred and characterize the technique.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the spoofing technique and scope.

steps.title: Assess what information or access was obtained through the spoofing
steps.desc: Determine what information, access, or actions (e.g., a fraudulent request approved based on the spoofed identity) resulted from the spoofing.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Block the spoofed identity/channel
steps.desc: Block the spoofed sender domain, phone number, or account, and alert affected individuals or teams that may still be targeted.
steps.outcome: Further use of the spoofed identity is blocked.

steps.title: Verify and, if needed, reverse any actions taken based on the spoofed identity
steps.desc: Review and, where possible, reverse or halt any organizational actions taken in reliance on the spoofed identity (e.g., a data-sharing request or access grant).
steps.outcome: Any erroneous actions based on the spoofing are identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen identity-verification procedures for high-risk requests
steps.desc: Implement or reinforce out-of-band identity-verification procedures for high-risk requests (e.g., data access, wire transfers, credential resets).
steps.outcome: Reduced susceptibility to future identity-spoofing attempts.

steps.title: Audit for other accounts affected by the same technique
steps.desc: Audit the broader account population for exposure to the same credential or identity-compromise technique observed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Any additional exposed accounts are identified and remediated.

steps.title: Brief affected teams and update awareness training
steps.desc: Brief affected teams on the observed spoofing technique and update security-awareness training accordingly.
steps.outcome: Improved organizational resilience to future spoofing attempts.

steps.title: Validate hardened authentication controls before restoring normal access
steps.desc: Validate that hardened authentication controls are functioning correctly before returning the affected account(s) to normal access levels.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated hardened authentication posture.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52911.def: Espionage carried out through a covertly installed hardware device — a hardware keylogger, network implant, or malicious peripheral — added to a system or network to intercept data, independent of any software-based compromise.
ITID-52911.purpose: Captures the discovery of a covert hardware device physically installed to intercept data or communications for espionage purposes.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of an unauthorized hardware device attached to a workstation, network port, or peripheral

A device intercepted and modified during shipping prior to reaching its destination (cross-reference the Devices domain's interdiction leaf, ITID-61431, if the interdiction itself is the primary finding)
scopeExcludes: A purely software-based implant with no physical hardware component (tracked under the relevant cyber espionage leaf)
A rogue network device specifically positioned to intercept network traffic at the network layer (ITID-52931)
ITID-52911.severity: Critical. Physical hardware implants indicate an adversary with direct physical access to the environment, which is itself a serious security failure independent of the data at risk.
ITID-52911.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and legal; preserve the device as evidence and do not power it down or disturb it without forensic guidance where possible.
indicators: Physical inspection revealing an unfamiliar device attached to a workstation, keyboard cable, or network port
Unexplained device or peripheral appearing in an asset inventory reconciliation
Anomalous network or endpoint behavior later traced to a physical device rather than software
vectors: Covert hardware keylogger installed inline on a keyboard cable
Malicious USB or peripheral device left for an employee to plug in, or covertly installed by an insider or intruder with physical access
rootCauses: Insufficient physical access controls to workstations and network infrastructure
No routine physical inspection program for hardware tampering
controls: Physical access controls to workstations, server rooms, and network infrastructure
Routine physical inspection/asset reconciliation program for hardware tampering
ITID-52911.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; T1200 is a genuine ATT&CK Enterprise technique, but detection is fundamentally a physical-security matter — technical telemetry alone rarely surfaces a purely passive hardware implant.
ITID-52911.response: Preserve the device for forensic analysis; determine how physical access was obtained and close that specific gap.
metrics: Number of hardware implants discovered per year
ITID-52911.notes: Cross-reference ITID-61431 (Hardware Interdiction During Shipping) and ITID-34334 (Unclassified/General Hardware Implant Exfiltration) elsewhere in the taxonomy, which cover related but distinct hardware-implant scenarios; this leaf is scoped to the physical-espionage context of a device discovered already in place.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Hardware Implant (Physical Espionage Context)
playbook.description: A covert hardware implant (e.g., a rogue chip, malicious peripheral, or modified device component) is discovered on organizational equipment, apparently intended for espionage purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the hardware implant through physical inspection and hardware forensics
steps.desc: IT security and hardware forensics specialists physically inspect and analyze the suspected device to confirm the presence and function of an implant.
steps.guidance: Engage specialized hardware-forensics support given the technical complexity of confirming and characterizing a hardware implant.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the implant's presence and function.
steps.abort: If inspection does not confirm an implant, close with a documented finding.

steps.title: Determine how and when the implant was introduced
steps.desc: Investigate the equipment's supply chain, physical access history, and badge/camera records to determine how and when the implant was likely introduced.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security for facility access-log and camera-footage review.
steps.outcome: A documented hypothesis on the implant's introduction point and timing.
steps.tool: Badge access logs; CCTV footage review

steps.title: Isolate and remove the affected equipment
steps.desc: Immediately isolate the affected equipment from the network and physically remove it from service.
steps.outcome: The implant is no longer able to capture or transmit data.

steps.title: Inspect similarly sourced equipment for related implants
steps.desc: Inspect other equipment from the same supplier, batch, or physical-access window for similar implants.
steps.outcome: Any additional compromised equipment is identified.

steps.title: Coordinate with the supplier and, where warranted, law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify the equipment supplier and, if evidence suggests deliberate supply-chain tampering, engage law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Supplier notified and law enforcement engaged where warranted.

steps.title: Inspect the broader environment for similar hardware exposure
steps.desc: Inspect other equipment, locations, or supply-chain batches for similar hardware-based exposure.
steps.outcome: Any additional affected equipment is identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen hardware supply-chain and physical-security controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen hardware supply-chain vetting and physical-access controls for sensitive equipment.
steps.outcome: Strengthened controls reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Validate remediation before returning equipment to service
steps.desc: Validate that remediation is complete and the equipment or environment is safe before returning it to normal service.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated remediation prior to restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief IT and physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52921.def: Espionage in which data is copied onto a removable storage device (USB drive, external hard drive, memory card) for physical removal from the premises, bypassing network-based DLP and egress monitoring entirely.
ITID-52921.purpose: Captures espionage-motivated data theft carried out by physically copying data onto removable media rather than through a network-based exfiltration channel.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected copying of sensitive data to an unauthorized removable storage device
Physical removal of a removable device known or suspected to contain sensitive data
scopeExcludes: Network-based exfiltration with no removable-media component (tracked under the relevant cyber espionage leaf)
ITID-52921.severity: High to Critical depending on the volume and sensitivity of data copied.
ITID-52921.escalation: Escalate to legal and physical security; time-sensitivity is high if the device and the individual who removed it are still on-site or reachable.
indicators: Endpoint logs showing a large file transfer to a removable storage device shortly before the device is disconnected
Removable-media usage from an account/endpoint with no legitimate business need for such transfers
Physical security or facilities reporting an individual observed with unfamiliar storage media near sensitive areas
vectors: Direct copy of sensitive files to a USB drive using standard operating system file operations
Use of an unmanaged personal device connected briefly to copy data
rootCauses: Removable media usage not restricted or logged on endpoints with access to sensitive data
No DLP policy blocking or alerting on large transfers to removable storage
controls: Removable media restriction/allowlisting policy for sensitive-data endpoints
DLP alerting on large transfers to removable storage
ITID-52921.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; endpoint DLP and removable-media logging provide a strong technical detection surface where enabled, though the physical removal of the device itself remains outside network telemetry.
ITID-52921.response: Attempt to recover the device promptly if the individual is still reachable; assess the full scope of data copied via endpoint logs.
metrics: Number of removable-media exfiltration incidents per year
Percentage of sensitive-data endpoints with removable media restricted
ITID-52921.notes: Lone-child stub for this Tier-4 group; the exfiltration technique itself is well covered by endpoint DLP, distinguishing this leaf's detection maturity from most others in the Physical and Hardware-Based Espionage Tier-3.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Data Theft via Removable Media (Physical Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An individual is discovered to have used removable media (USB drive, external storage) to copy and remove sensitive organizational data, apparently for espionage purposes.

steps.title: Confirm removable-media data transfer and identify the device/user
steps.desc: Endpoint security reviews device-control and DLP logs to confirm removable-media data transfer occurred and identify the responsible user and device.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the transfer and responsible party.

steps.title: Scope the data copied and assess its sensitivity
steps.desc: Determine what specific data was copied to the removable media and assess its sensitivity and strategic value.
steps.outcome: A documented scope of exposure.

steps.title: Recover or secure the removable media if possible
steps.desc: Where feasible and legally appropriate, recover the physical removable media (e.g., during offboarding or with employee cooperation).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/HR on the appropriate legal basis for requesting or requiring the return or inspection of the device.
steps.outcome: The media is recovered or its contents are otherwise accounted for.
steps.abort: If the media cannot be recovered, proceed with legal and containment options based on the confirmed scope.

steps.title: Restrict the individual's access pending investigation
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the individual's access to sensitive systems and data pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Further data exposure via this individual is halted.

steps.title: Determine personnel and legal action
steps.desc: HR and Legal determine appropriate personnel action and evaluate legal remedies, including potential criminal referral.
steps.outcome: Appropriate personnel and legal action taken.

steps.title: Inspect the broader environment for similar hardware exposure
steps.desc: Inspect other equipment, locations, or supply-chain batches for similar hardware-based exposure.
steps.outcome: Any additional affected equipment is identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen removable-media controls
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen device-control policies restricting or monitoring removable-media use for sensitive systems.
steps.outcome: Strengthened controls reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Validate remediation before returning equipment to service
steps.desc: Validate that remediation is complete and the equipment or environment is safe before returning it to normal service.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated remediation prior to restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52931.def: Espionage carried out through a rogue network device — an unauthorized switch, access point, network tap, or single-board computer — physically connected to the corporate network to intercept traffic or provide a persistent covert access point.
ITID-52931.purpose: Captures the discovery of an unauthorized network device covertly connected to the corporate network to intercept or exfiltrate data at the network layer.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of an unauthorized device connected to a network port or wiring closet
Discovery of a rogue wireless access point bridged into the corporate network
scopeExcludes: A hardware implant attached directly to an individual workstation or peripheral rather than the network infrastructure itself (ITID-52911)
ITID-52931.severity: Critical. A rogue network device implies physical access to network infrastructure and can provide the adversary a durable, hard-to-detect foothold.
ITID-52931.escalation: Escalate immediately to network security and physical security; preserve the device for forensic analysis and assess how physical access to network infrastructure was obtained.
indicators: Network asset inventory reconciliation revealing an unrecognized device MAC address or port usage
Physical inspection of wiring closets or network infrastructure revealing an unfamiliar device
Unexplained network traffic pattern traced to a physical port not associated with a known asset
vectors: Covert network tap or switch installed in a wiring closet or under-desk network port
Rogue wireless access point bridged into the wired network to extend covert remote access
rootCauses: Insufficient physical access controls to network infrastructure (wiring closets, patch panels)
No network access control (802.1X) or port-level device authentication
controls: Network access control (802.1X) restricting unauthorized device connection
Physical access controls and routine inspection of network infrastructure locations
ITID-52931.detection: This is a lone-leaf stub covering the whole Tier-4 category; network access control and asset-inventory reconciliation provide a genuine technical detection surface, though purely passive taps can evade detection for extended periods without physical inspection.
ITID-52931.response: Preserve the device for forensic analysis; determine how physical access was obtained and close that specific gap; assess what traffic may have been intercepted.
metrics: Number of rogue network devices discovered per year
Percentage of network ports with 802.1X enforcement
detections: Network access control (802.1X) unauthorized device alerting
ITID-52931.notes: Lone-child stub for this Tier-4 group; shares the T1200 mapping with ITID-52911 but is distinguished by targeting network infrastructure rather than an individual endpoint.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Rogue Network Device (Physical Espionage Context)
playbook.description: An unauthorized, rogue network device (e.g., a network tap, rogue access point, or hidden network interception hardware) is discovered connected to the organization's network, apparently for espionage purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the rogue device and its network position
steps.desc: Network security and physical security jointly confirm the presence, location, and network position of the rogue device.
steps.guidance: Coordinate physical facility inspection with network-scanning tools to locate and physically confirm the device.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the device's presence, location, and network access.
steps.tool: Network access control (NAC) scanning; physical facility inspection

steps.title: Assess what network traffic or data was exposed
steps.desc: Determine what network segments, traffic, or data the rogue device had visibility into and for how long.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Physically remove the rogue device and isolate the affected network segment
steps.desc: Physically remove the device and isolate or reset the affected network segment.
steps.outcome: The rogue device is no longer able to intercept network traffic.

steps.title: Review facility access records for introduction of the device
steps.desc: Review badge access and camera footage to determine how and when the device was physically introduced.
steps.outcome: A documented hypothesis on the device's introduction point and timing.
steps.tool: Badge access logs; CCTV footage review

steps.title: Engage law enforcement where warranted
steps.desc: Legal and Security assess whether the rogue device installation constitutes a criminal offense and engage law enforcement accordingly.
steps.outcome: Appropriate law-enforcement engagement completed where warranted.

steps.title: Inspect the broader environment for similar hardware exposure
steps.desc: Inspect other equipment, locations, or supply-chain batches for similar hardware-based exposure.
steps.outcome: Any additional affected equipment is identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen network access control and physical-security monitoring
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen network access control (802.1X or equivalent) and physical-security monitoring of network infrastructure locations.
steps.outcome: Strengthened controls reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Validate remediation before returning equipment to service
steps.desc: Validate that remediation is complete and the equipment or environment is safe before returning it to normal service.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated remediation prior to restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief network and physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52941.def: Physical intrusion in which an adversary with unauthorized or pretextual access to a facility covertly searches an employee's unattended desk, workstation, or nearby storage for sensitive documents, credentials, or devices, without removing anything or causing obvious disturbance.
ITID-52941.purpose: Captures the covert physical search of an employee's unattended workstation or desk to locate sensitive information.
scopeIncludes: Discovery that a desk or workstation area was searched, disturbed, or accessed while the employee was away with no legitimate reason
An individual observed lingering at or searching another employee's workstation without authorization
scopeExcludes: Covert photography of documents/whiteboards specifically (ITID-52942)
After-hours access resulting in actual theft of documents or devices (ITID-52943)
ITID-52941.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where sensitive credentials or documents (e.g., written passwords) are confirmed to have been exposed.
ITID-52941.priority: P2, escalating to P1 where credentials or highly sensitive material were exposed.
ITID-52941.escalation: Escalate to physical security immediately; coordinate with the affected employee to assess what was exposed on or near their desk.
indicators: Employee reporting that items on their desk appear disturbed or rearranged
Access-control or camera footage showing an unfamiliar individual at the desk with no legitimate purpose
Colleague reporting having observed someone unfamiliar near a workstation while its occupant was away
vectors: Opportunistic search of an unattended desk by someone already inside the facility under a legitimate or pretextual reason for being there
Coordinated timing of a search with a known meeting or break period
rootCauses: Clean-desk policy not consistently enforced for sensitive material and written credentials
Insufficient visitor/contractor escort policy allowing unsupervised movement near employee workstations
controls: Clean-desk policy enforcement for sensitive material and credentials
Visitor/contractor escort policy for areas with employee workstations
ITID-52941.detection: Physical intrusion — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection relies on employee observation, camera footage review, and physical security coordination.
ITID-52941.response: Coordinate with physical security to review access logs/footage for the relevant window; assess and remediate any credential or sensitive-material exposure with the affected employee.
metrics: Number of unattended-workstation search incidents reported per year
ITID-52941.notes: Physical intrusion tradecraft — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; coordinate with physical security for investigation and remediation.

playbook.name: Covert Physical Search of Unattended Workstation/Desk
playbook.description: Evidence indicates an unauthorized individual covertly searched an employee's unattended workstation or desk, apparently seeking sensitive documents or information.

steps.title: Confirm the covert search and identify the affected workstation/desk
steps.desc: Physical security reviews the report (disturbed items, a suspicious individual observed, or camera footage) to confirm an unauthorized search occurred.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities/physical security and review available camera footage for the relevant time window.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination that an unauthorized search occurred.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, log and continue monitoring.
steps.tool: CCTV footage review; physical security incident log

steps.title: Assess what sensitive information may have been accessible
steps.desc: Determine what documents, devices, or information were present and potentially accessible at the workstation/desk during the search.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Review badge access records for the relevant time window
steps.desc: Review badge access logs for the affected area during the relevant time window to identify who had physical access.
steps.outcome: A narrowed list of individuals with access during the relevant window.

steps.title: Advise the affected employee and reinforce clean-desk practices
steps.desc: Notify the affected employee and reinforce clean-desk and document-security practices for the affected area.
steps.outcome: Reduced future exposure at the affected workstation.

steps.title: Investigate for connection to broader targeting activity
steps.desc: Assess whether the search connects to other reconnaissance or espionage indicators involving the same employee, team, or project.
steps.outcome: A documented determination of isolated vs. broader campaign.

steps.title: Conduct a facility-wide physical-security review
steps.desc: Conduct a broader physical-security review of the facility to identify any other exploitable gaps beyond the one used in this incident.
steps.outcome: Additional physical-security gaps identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen physical-access controls and clean-desk policy enforcement
steps.desc: Review and strengthen physical-access controls for the affected area and reinforce clean-desk policy enforcement organization-wide.
steps.outcome: Strengthened physical-security posture reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Validate restored physical-security controls before normal operations resume
steps.desc: Validate that restored or enhanced physical-security controls are functioning correctly before the facility returns to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated physical-security posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52942.def: Physical intrusion in which an adversary with unauthorized or pretextual facility access covertly photographs sensitive documents, whiteboards, or displayed screens, leaving no physical trace of the visit.
ITID-52942.purpose: Captures the covert photography of sensitive physical documents or whiteboards to capture confidential information without removing anything.
scopeIncludes: Discovery that whiteboard content, printed documents, or displayed screens were photographed without authorization
An individual observed photographing meeting-room whiteboards or workstation screens without a legitimate business reason
scopeExcludes: A general covert search of a workstation without confirmed photography (ITID-52941)
ITID-52942.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where the photographed content included strategic, technical, or otherwise highly sensitive information.
ITID-52942.priority: P2, escalating to P1 where highly sensitive content is confirmed to have been photographed.
ITID-52942.escalation: Escalate to physical security immediately; assess and, where necessary, treat the photographed content as compromised for planning purposes (e.g., changing a strategy discussed on a photographed whiteboard).
indicators: Camera/photography sound or visible phone positioning observed by an employee near a whiteboard or screen
Security camera footage showing an individual photographing meeting-room content
Unexplained knowledge by a third party of content that was only ever displayed on an internal whiteboard or screen
vectors: Covert use of a phone camera to photograph a whiteboard or screen during or after a meeting
Photography of printed documents left visible on a desk or in a common area
rootCauses: No clean-whiteboard policy requiring sensitive content to be erased after meetings
Meeting rooms and sensitive display areas visible to visitors or non-employees without adequate physical barriers
controls: Clean-whiteboard policy for meeting rooms used for sensitive discussions
Physical layout/visibility review for meeting rooms and display areas accessible to visitors
ITID-52942.detection: Physical intrusion — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection relies on employee observation and camera footage review.
ITID-52942.response: Assess what content was likely photographed based on the timing and location; treat sensitive strategic content as potentially compromised for planning purposes.
metrics: Number of covert document/whiteboard photography incidents reported per year
ITID-52942.notes: Physical intrusion tradecraft — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; coordinate with physical security for investigation.

playbook.name: Covert Photography of Sensitive Physical Documents/Whiteboards
playbook.description: An unauthorized individual is discovered to have covertly photographed sensitive physical documents or whiteboards containing confidential organizational information.

steps.title: Confirm the covert photography and identify what was captured
steps.desc: Physical security investigates the report (a witness account, camera footage, or a discovered photograph) to confirm covert photography occurred and identify what was captured.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the photography and its content.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, log and continue monitoring.
steps.tool: CCTV footage review; physical security incident log

steps.title: Identify the individual and their access basis
steps.desc: Determine who took the photograph and under what basis they had access to the location (employee, visitor, vendor, contractor).
steps.outcome: A documented identification of the responsible individual and their access basis.
steps.tool: Badge access logs; visitor management system

steps.title: Restrict the individual's further access pending investigation
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the individual's access to the facility or sensitive areas pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized photography by this individual is prevented.

steps.title: Assess exposure of the captured information
steps.desc: Determine the sensitivity of the captured information and whether any protective business action (e.g., accelerating a decision, notifying a partner) is warranted.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment and any necessary protective action identified.

steps.title: Determine personnel/contractual/legal action
steps.desc: HR, Legal, or vendor management (depending on the individual's relationship to the organization) determine appropriate action.
steps.outcome: Appropriate action taken based on the individual's relationship to the organization.

steps.title: Conduct a facility-wide physical-security review
steps.desc: Conduct a broader physical-security review of the facility to identify any other exploitable gaps beyond the one used in this incident.
steps.outcome: Additional physical-security gaps identified and addressed.

steps.title: Reinforce clean-room/whiteboard-security practices
steps.desc: Reinforce policies on covering or erasing sensitive whiteboard content and securing sensitive documents when not in active use, particularly in visitor-accessible areas.
steps.outcome: Reduced future exposure of sensitive physical information.

steps.title: Validate restored physical-security controls before normal operations resume
steps.desc: Validate that restored or enhanced physical-security controls are functioning correctly before the facility returns to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated physical-security posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52943.def: Physical intrusion into a corporate office outside normal business hours, when fewer witnesses are present, with the specific purpose of stealing physical documents, storage media, or devices.
ITID-52943.purpose: Captures unauthorized after-hours entry to an office specifically to steal physical documents or devices.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected after-hours entry resulting in the theft of documents, devices, or storage media
Evidence of after-hours access-control bypass or tailgating followed by a report of missing items
scopeExcludes: A covert search or photography during after-hours access with nothing physically removed (ITID-52941/52942)
ITID-52943.severity: High to Critical depending on the sensitivity of what was stolen.
ITID-52943.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and law enforcement; preserve access-control and camera evidence promptly before routine retention periods expire.
indicators: Access-control logs showing after-hours entry inconsistent with the employee's normal schedule or role
Missing devices, documents, or storage media discovered the following business day
Signs of forced entry or access-control tampering
vectors: After-hours entry using a stolen or cloned access badge
Tailgating or exploiting an unlocked door during after-hours access
Forced entry bypassing physical access controls
rootCauses: Insufficient after-hours access-control monitoring/alerting
Sensitive documents or devices not secured (locked) when the office is unoccupied
controls: After-hours access-control alerting and review
Secure storage requirement for sensitive documents/devices outside business hours
ITID-52943.detection: Physical intrusion — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection relies on access-control logging, camera footage, and physical security patrol.
ITID-52943.response: Preserve access-control and camera evidence promptly; report to law enforcement; assess and communicate the specific loss.
metrics: Number of after-hours theft incidents per year
Time to preserve evidence following discovery
ITID-52943.notes: Physical intrusion tradecraft — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; coordinate with physical security and law enforcement for investigation.

playbook.name: After-Hours Office Access for Document/Device Theft
playbook.description: An unauthorized individual is discovered to have accessed the office after hours to steal physical documents or devices, apparently for espionage purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the after-hours breach and what was taken
steps.desc: Physical security and IT jointly confirm the after-hours access occurred (via badge logs, alarm records, or physical evidence of entry) and inventory what documents or devices are missing.
steps.guidance: Coordinate immediately with building management/facilities, since after-hours physical breaches often involve shared building security systems beyond the organization's sole control.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the breach and an inventory of missing items.
steps.tool: Badge access logs; alarm system logs; CCTV footage review

steps.title: Assess the sensitivity of stolen documents/devices
steps.desc: Determine the sensitivity of the stolen documents or devices and what organizational information they contained or could access.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Remotely wipe/lock stolen devices and revoke associated credentials
steps.desc: Remotely wipe or lock any stolen devices where technically possible and revoke credentials or tokens accessible from them.
steps.outcome: Stolen devices can no longer be used to access organizational systems.

steps.title: Notify building management and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify building management/facilities and law enforcement given the unauthorized after-hours physical access and theft.
steps.outcome: Building management and law enforcement are informed and coordinating.

steps.title: Review and strengthen after-hours access controls
steps.desc: Review the after-hours access-control gap that allowed entry (e.g., badge system vulnerability, tailgating, unsecured door) and remediate it.
steps.outcome: The access-control gap is closed.

steps.title: Conduct a facility-wide physical-security review
steps.desc: Conduct a broader physical-security review of the facility to identify any other exploitable gaps beyond the one used in this incident.
steps.outcome: Additional physical-security gaps identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen physical-security measures for after-hours periods
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen after-hours security measures (patrols, alarm monitoring, camera coverage) for the affected facility.
steps.outcome: Strengthened physical-security posture reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Validate restored physical-security controls before normal operations resume
steps.desc: Validate that restored or enhanced physical-security controls are functioning correctly before the facility returns to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated physical-security posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief physical-security and building-management leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-52944.def: A general or not-yet-classified case of a suspected corporate office breach pending determination of the specific activity (covert search, covert photography, or after-hours theft).
ITID-52944.purpose: Serves as the intake classification for suspected corporate office breach activity that does not yet fit a more specific leaf in this group.
scopeIncludes: Initial suspicion of a physical office breach prior to identifying the specific activity
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific activity has already been established (ITID-52941/52942/52943)
ITID-52944.priority: P2 for initial investigation; reclassify as facts develop.
ITID-52944.escalation: Escalate to physical security on initial suspicion.
indicators: General report of a suspicious physical presence or disturbance without a confirmed activity type
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Not yet determined at time of intake
controls: Case-intake and triage workflow with physical security engagement
ITID-52944.detection: None specific; routing bucket pending classification.
ITID-52944.response: Open an investigation and reclassify to a specific leaf once the activity is established.
metrics: Number of cases reclassified out of this bucket within 30 days
ITID-52944.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf for the Corporate Office Breach group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Corporate Office Breach
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-fully-characterized case of suspected unauthorized physical intrusion into a corporate office or facility, apparently for espionage purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the breach and scope of unauthorized access
steps.desc: Physical security confirms the unauthorized physical access occurred and determines the areas and time window involved.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with building management/facilities as needed.
steps.outcome: A confirmed determination of the breach and its scope.
steps.tool: Badge access logs; CCTV footage review

steps.title: Assess what was accessed, viewed, or taken
steps.desc: Determine what documents, devices, or areas were accessed, viewed, or taken during the breach.
steps.outcome: A documented exposure assessment.

steps.title: Secure the affected area and revoke any compromised access
steps.desc: Secure the affected area and revoke or reset any physical or system access potentially compromised by the breach.
steps.outcome: The affected area and access are secured.

steps.title: Notify building management and law enforcement as warranted
steps.desc: Notify building management/facilities and, where warranted, law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Appropriate stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Remediate the access-control gap
steps.desc: Identify and remediate the physical-security gap that allowed the breach.
steps.outcome: The access-control gap is closed.

steps.title: Conduct a facility-wide physical-security review
steps.desc: Conduct a broader physical-security review of the facility to identify any other exploitable gaps beyond the one used in this incident.
steps.outcome: Additional physical-security gaps identified and addressed.

steps.title: Strengthen physical-security measures
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen physical-security measures for the affected facility.
steps.outcome: Strengthened physical-security posture reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Validate restored physical-security controls before normal operations resume
steps.desc: Validate that restored or enhanced physical-security controls are functioning correctly before the facility returns to normal operations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed, validated physical-security posture upon restoration.

steps.title: Document and brief physical-security leadership
steps.desc: Produce an after-action report and brief relevant leadership on findings and improvements.
steps.outcome: Leadership informed and improvements tracked.

ITID-53111.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cases where an adversary poses as a CEO, CFO, or other senior executive (via a compromised, spoofed, or lookalike email account) to pressure an employee into making an urgent, unauthorized wire transfer or financial action, and the case has not been further subtyped.
ITID-53111.purpose: Captures the fraud-outcome intake bucket for BEC attacks that impersonate a senior executive to induce a subordinate into an unauthorized wire or payment.
scopeIncludes: An email purporting to be from a senior executive requesting an urgent, confidential wire transfer
Follow-up impersonation via phone or text reinforcing the email request
Cases pending further classification into a more specific executive-impersonation subtype
scopeExcludes: The technical mechanism of the email compromise/spoofing itself, which is classified under ITID-22411 through ITID-22415
Vendor invoice redirection fraud (ITID-53121)
Payroll direct-deposit redirection fraud (ITID-53131)
ITID-53111.severity: High. Executive-impersonation BEC frequently targets high-dollar, time-pressured wire transfers with low recoverability once funds leave the institution.
ITID-53111.priority: P1 if a transfer is in-flight or unconfirmed as stopped; P2 once contained and the matter is in financial-recovery/reporting status.
ITID-53111.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/treasury to attempt a wire recall, to the SOC for the underlying email-account investigation, and to legal/law enforcement (FBI IC3) if funds have left the institution.
indicators: Urgent, secrecy-emphasizing wire request purportedly from an executive
Reply-to address that differs subtly from the executive's real address
Request routed around normal payment-approval workflow
Executive unreachable through verified channels at time of request
vectors: Compromised executive mailbox
Lookalike/spoofed domain impersonating the executive
Display-name spoofing with no domain compromise
rootCauses: No out-of-band verification requirement for wire requests above a threshold
Employees not trained to recognize urgency/secrecy pressure tactics
Lack of DMARC/DKIM/SPF enforcement enabling spoofing
controls: Mandatory out-of-band verification for wire transfers above a defined threshold
DMARC/DKIM/SPF enforcement with quarantine/reject policy
Executive-impersonation-themed phishing awareness training
ITID-53111.detection: Email security gateway and DMARC reporting can surface spoofing attempts; the fraud outcome itself is typically caught by finance-workflow controls, not SOC telemetry.
ITID-53111.response: SOC investigates and contains the email vector (per ITID-22411-22415); finance/fraud team owns wire-recall attempts and law-enforcement reporting; SOC does not own fund recovery.
metrics: Count of executive-impersonation BEC attempts per quarter
Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
Median time to wire-recall initiation
ITID-53111.notes: This leaf covers the fraud/monetization outcome only. For the technical email-compromise/spoofing mechanism, see the fuller BEC treatment at ITID-22411 (compromised mailbox), ITID-22412 (display-name spoofing), ITID-22413 (lookalike domain), and ITID-22414 (compromised vendor account).

playbook.name: Executive Impersonation Fraud (BEC)
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates a senior executive by email (spoofed or lookalike domain, or a compromised mailbox) to pressure an employee into an urgent, unauthorized wire transfer or sensitive-data disclosure.

steps.title: Collect the suspect email and full headers
steps.desc: Obtain the original email (as .eml/.msg, not a forward) from the recipient, including full internet headers.
steps.guidance: Ask the recipient to forward the message as an attachment or export it directly from the mailbox so headers survive. Do not reply to or forward the sender.
steps.outcome: Raw email with headers preserved for header/domain analysis.

steps.title: Analyze sender domain and header authenticity
steps.desc: Check the From/Reply-To domain against the executive's real domain, and review SPF/DKIM/DMARC results and Received-path hops for spoofing or lookalike-domain indicators (e.g. transposed letters, different TLD).
steps.guidance: Compare against known-good domain records; check DMARC alignment failures; look for newly-registered lookalike domains via WHOIS.
steps.outcome: Confirmed spoof/lookalike domain or compromised legitimate mailbox, with supporting header evidence.
steps.abort: If headers show a fully authenticated internal send with no anomaly, escalate as a suspected compromised executive mailbox rather than closing as external spoof.

steps.title: Confirm the out-of-band verification failure
steps.desc: Determine whether the employee attempted or skipped independent verification of the request (e.g. phone call to a known number) before acting.
steps.guidance: Interview the targeted employee; document exactly what was requested, when, and whether any funds/data movement already occurred.
steps.outcome: Clear timeline of the request and any action taken, establishing whether a loss event occurred.

steps.title: Initiate urgent bank recall / SWIFT recall request
steps.desc: If funds were transferred, immediately contact the sending bank's fraud department to request an emergency wire recall or SWIFT MT192 recall — this window is typically only a few hours.
steps.guidance: Provide transaction reference, amount, beneficiary details, and fraud confirmation. Simultaneously notify the receiving bank if known. Involve Finance leadership and Legal immediately given the time pressure.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed with sending bank within the window; receiving bank notified where possible.
steps.abort: If no funds moved, skip recall and proceed to blocking the sender.
steps.tool: Banking fraud hotline / SWIFT recall portal

steps.title: Block sender domain/address and quarantine similar messages
steps.desc: Block the spoofed/lookalike domain and sender address at the email gateway; search and quarantine any other messages from the same source across the organization.
steps.guidance: Use mail gateway threat-intel blocking; search mailbox audit logs for other recipients of the same campaign.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked org-wide; other potential targets identified and warned.

steps.title: Alert Finance/AP to hold related payments
steps.desc: Notify Accounts Payable and Treasury to place a hold on any pending payments referencing the same request, beneficiary, or invoice details.
steps.guidance: Circulate the fraudulent beneficiary account details to Finance and Treasury teams as a payment-block flag.
steps.outcome: No further payments released to the fraudulent beneficiary.

steps.title: Harden DMARC/SPF/DKIM enforcement
steps.desc: Review and tighten the organization's DMARC policy (move toward p=reject where feasible) and confirm SPF/DKIM records are correctly enforced for the executive's domain.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with email/security engineering; review DMARC aggregate reports for gaps exploited by this campaign.
steps.outcome: DMARC/SPF/DKIM configuration closes the spoofing vector used in this incident.

steps.title: Implement mandatory callback verification for executive payment requests
steps.desc: Update the payment-authorization policy to require independent, out-of-band callback verification (using a pre-known number, not one in the email) for any executive-initiated payment or wire request.
steps.guidance: Work with Finance leadership to formalize and communicate the policy; add it to AP procedures.
steps.outcome: Documented callback-verification requirement in place and communicated to relevant staff.

steps.title: Pursue fund recovery and file law-enforcement report
steps.desc: If funds were lost, continue working with the bank and file a report with law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3) and cyber-insurance carrier to pursue recovery.
steps.guidance: Provide the bank's fraud case number and full transaction trail; track recall outcome.
steps.outcome: Recovery case opened with bank/law enforcement; insurance claim filed if applicable.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and staff awareness update
steps.desc: Document the full incident timeline, root cause, and control gaps; brief Finance/AP staff on the specific lure used and reinforce verification procedures.
steps.guidance: Include a redacted example of the fraudulent email in awareness training materials.
steps.outcome: Incident report finalized; targeted awareness communication issued to at-risk staff.

ITID-53121.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cases where an adversary impersonates or compromises a known vendor/supplier's email to submit a fraudulent invoice or change banking details on a legitimate one, diverting payment to an attacker-controlled account, and the case has not been further subtyped.
ITID-53121.purpose: Captures the fraud-outcome intake bucket for BEC attacks that impersonate or hijack a vendor relationship to redirect an invoice payment.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed or compromised vendor email requesting updated banking/remittance details
A fraudulent invoice submitted under a real vendor's identity
Cases pending further classification into a more specific vendor-fraud subtype
scopeExcludes: The technical mechanism of the underlying vendor mailbox compromise, classified under ITID-22414
Executive-impersonation wire fraud (ITID-53111)
Payroll diversion fraud (ITID-53131)
ITID-53121.severity: High. Vendor invoice fraud often targets recurring, large-dollar payments and can go unnoticed until reconciliation.
ITID-53121.priority: P1 while a payment is pending or unconfirmed as stopped; P2 once contained and in financial-recovery status.
ITID-53121.escalation: Escalate to accounts payable/finance to halt payment, to the SOC if a vendor's or the company's own mailbox is compromised, and to legal/law enforcement once funds have moved.
indicators: Vendor email requesting a change to banking/remittance details outside normal channels
Invoice with formatting or amount inconsistent with vendor history
Request to expedite payment or bypass standard AP verification
vectors: Compromised vendor email account
Lookalike domain impersonating the vendor
Interception/monitoring of a genuine AP email thread to inject a fraudulent reply
rootCauses: No callback-verification requirement for vendor banking-detail changes
Lack of vendor master-data change controls in the ERP/AP system
Absence of DMARC enforcement enabling vendor-domain spoofing
controls: Mandatory callback verification (using a known-good number, not one supplied in the email) for any vendor banking-detail change
Vendor master-data change approval workflow
DMARC/DKIM/SPF enforcement
ITID-53121.detection: Email gateway/DMARC telemetry can flag spoofed vendor domains; the fraud itself is usually caught by AP reconciliation rather than SOC detection.
ITID-53121.response: SOC investigates/contains any compromised mailbox involved; AP/finance owns payment-hold and recovery efforts; both coordinate on vendor notification.
metrics: Count of vendor invoice fraud attempts per quarter
Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered/stopped
Percentage caught before payment release
detections: AP anomaly detection on banking-detail changes
ITID-53121.notes: This leaf covers the fraud/monetization outcome only. For the technical compromise of the vendor mailbox itself, see ITID-22414 (BEC via compromised vendor/third-party email account) and the broader BEC set at ITID-22411-22413.

playbook.name: Vendor Invoice Fraud (BEC)
playbook.description: An attacker, posing as a known vendor via a spoofed or compromised email, submits a fraudulent invoice or changes banking details to redirect a legitimate payment to an attacker-controlled account.

steps.title: Collect the fraudulent invoice/bank-change email and headers
steps.desc: Obtain the email and any attached invoice or bank-detail-change notice, preserving full headers.
steps.guidance: Request the .eml export from AP staff; capture the invoice PDF and any linked payment portal.
steps.outcome: Full evidence set preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Analyze sender domain and compare to known vendor contact history
steps.desc: Check whether the sending domain matches the vendor's legitimate domain, or is a lookalike/compromised account, and compare against the vendor's historical invoicing pattern and bank details on file.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference vendor master file bank details against the new request; flag any mismatch as high-confidence fraud.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this is a spoofed domain, a compromised vendor mailbox, or a genuine change.
steps.abort: If bank details match records on file exactly, close as false positive.
steps.tool: AP vendor master file / email analyzer

steps.title: Determine payment status
steps.desc: Confirm whether the fraudulent invoice has already been paid, is scheduled, or is still pending approval.
steps.guidance: Check AP payment run schedules and bank transaction records.
steps.outcome: Clear status of the payment enabling correct containment action.

steps.title: Halt or recall the payment
steps.desc: If payment is pending, place an immediate hold; if already sent, initiate an emergency wire/ACH recall with the bank.
steps.guidance: Engage Treasury/Finance leadership immediately; recall windows are narrow, especially for wire transfers.
steps.outcome: Payment held, or recall request filed with the bank.

steps.title: Verify vendor contact out-of-band and freeze the vendor record
steps.desc: Contact the real vendor using a previously-known phone number (not one from the suspect email) to confirm the fraud, and freeze/flag the vendor master record to block further payments until verified.
steps.guidance: Use the vendor contact on file prior to the incident, not any number supplied in the fraudulent communication.
steps.outcome: Vendor confirms fraud; vendor record locked pending re-verification.

steps.title: Enforce callback-verification-required policy for bank-detail changes
steps.desc: Update AP procedures to require mandatory independent callback verification for any vendor bank-detail change before it is applied in the vendor master file.
steps.guidance: Formalize with AP leadership; ensure the policy is applied retroactively to review other recent vendor changes.
steps.outcome: Documented policy change reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Review and harden email authentication controls
steps.desc: Review SPF/DKIM/DMARC posture on the vendor-facing email path and apply hardening where the spoofing/compromise vector is identified.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with security engineering to close the specific gap exploited.
steps.outcome: Authentication gap closed.

steps.title: Restore legitimate vendor payment and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Process the legitimate invoice payment to the correct account once verified, and pursue recovery of diverted funds via the bank and law enforcement.
steps.guidance: File an IC3 report and notify the cyber-insurance carrier if funds were lost.
steps.outcome: Vendor paid correctly; recovery case opened for lost funds.

steps.title: Document incident and brief AP team
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and root cause, and brief the AP team on this specific fraud pattern to reinforce verification discipline.
steps.guidance: Update AP training materials with a redacted example.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and staff awareness reinforced.

ITID-53131.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cases where an adversary, impersonating an employee (often via a compromised or spoofed personal/corporate email), submits a fraudulent direct-deposit change request to HR/payroll, diverting the employee's next paycheck, and the case has not been further subtyped.
ITID-53131.purpose: Captures the fraud-outcome intake bucket for BEC attacks that redirect an employee's payroll direct deposit to an attacker-controlled account.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed or compromised employee email requesting a direct-deposit banking-detail change
Self-service HR portal changes made using stolen employee credentials for payroll-diversion purposes
Cases pending further classification into a more specific payroll-diversion subtype
scopeExcludes: Executive-impersonation wire fraud (ITID-53111)
Vendor invoice fraud (ITID-53121)
Insider-perpetrated payroll fraud by an employee acting on their own payroll record without impersonation, classified under ITID-53631
ITID-53131.severity: Medium-High. Individual instances are lower-dollar than executive/vendor BEC but can recur across many employees if a shared HR portal credential set is compromised.
ITID-53131.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the same technique is confirmed against multiple employees (indicating a portal-wide credential compromise).
ITID-53131.escalation: Escalate to HR/payroll to reverse the deposit change before the pay run processes, and to the SOC if the HR self-service portal or employee mailbox shows signs of broader credential compromise.
indicators: Direct-deposit change request submitted outside normal employee behavior/location
Email requesting the change sent from an address subtly different from the employee's known address
Multiple employees reporting the same request pattern in a short window
vectors: Phishing for employee HR-portal credentials
Spoofed employee email to HR/payroll
Credential-stuffing against the HR self-service portal
rootCauses: No secondary verification (e.g., call-back or MFA step-up) required for direct-deposit changes
Lack of MFA on the HR/payroll self-service portal
No alerting on payroll banking-detail change velocity
controls: MFA on HR/payroll self-service portal
Secondary verification for direct-deposit banking-detail changes
Alerting on anomalous volume of payroll banking-detail changes
ITID-53131.detection: HR/payroll system audit logs and portal authentication logs provide the primary detection surface; email gateway telemetry supports the email-vector cases.
ITID-53131.response: HR/payroll reverses fraudulent changes and reissues payment; SOC investigates the credential-compromise vector if a portal account is involved.
metrics: Count of payroll diversion attempts per pay cycle
Number of employees affected per incident
Time to detect and reverse fraudulent change
sops: HR Self-Service Portal Account Compromise SOP
ITID-53131.notes: This leaf covers external/impersonation-driven payroll diversion. When an employee redirects their own payroll or a co-worker's without any impersonation or portal compromise, classify under Payroll Fraud By Employees (ITID-53631) instead.

playbook.name: Payroll Diversion Fraud (BEC)
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates an employee (often via a spoofed or compromised personal/work email) to request an unauthorized change to direct-deposit bank details, diverting the employee's payroll to an attacker-controlled account.

steps.title: Collect the direct-deposit change request and headers
steps.desc: Obtain the email or self-service portal request that initiated the bank-detail change, with full headers or portal audit log.
steps.guidance: Pull HRIS/payroll system change logs alongside the email evidence.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled covering both the request and system-level change record.

steps.title: Verify sender authenticity and account-change pattern
steps.desc: Check whether the request came from the employee's genuine, authenticated account or a spoofed/lookalike address, and whether the new bank account is associated with other recent fraudulent changes (a common indicator of a coordinated campaign).
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the new routing/account number against other recent payroll-change requests org-wide for reuse.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent request and identification of any linked cases.
steps.abort: If the employee confirms they made the change themselves, close as false positive.

steps.title: Contact the employee out-of-band to confirm
steps.desc: Reach the actual employee via a known phone number or in person to confirm whether they submitted the change.
steps.guidance: Do not rely on email to confirm — use a verified phone number or manager introduction.
steps.outcome: Definitive confirmation the employee did not authorize the change.

steps.title: Revert bank details and halt the next pay run
steps.desc: Immediately revert the direct-deposit details to the last known-good account and, if the next payroll run has already processed to the fraudulent account, contact the bank/payroll processor for an emergency recall.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with Payroll and the payroll processor; recall windows for ACH are short.
steps.outcome: Payroll details reverted; recall initiated if payment already sent.

steps.title: Flag the fraudulent account and review other employees for the same pattern
steps.desc: Flag the fraudulent destination account across the payroll system and check whether other employees' payroll was redirected to the same or similar accounts.
steps.guidance: Search payroll change history for the same routing/account number.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified; other affected employees remediated.

steps.title: Enforce out-of-band verification for payroll bank-detail changes
steps.desc: Update HR/Payroll procedures to require a secondary verification step (e.g. MFA-protected self-service, or a callback for manually-submitted changes) before any direct-deposit change takes effect.
steps.guidance: Work with HR/Payroll leadership and HRIS administrators to implement.
steps.outcome: Policy and/or system control implemented to prevent unverified changes.

steps.title: Reimburse the employee and pursue recovery of diverted funds
steps.desc: Ensure the affected employee is made whole for any missed pay via off-cycle payment, and pursue recovery of the diverted funds through the bank and, if warranted, law enforcement.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Payroll and Finance for the off-cycle payment; file IC3 report if funds were lost.
steps.outcome: Employee paid correctly; recovery case opened.

steps.title: Document incident and reinforce HR/Payroll awareness
steps.desc: Record the incident timeline and root cause, and brief HR/Payroll staff on the fraud pattern and reinforced verification steps.
steps.guidance: Include this case in HR fraud-awareness training.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53141.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cases where an adversary, impersonating an executive or trusted colleague via spoofed or compromised email, convinces an employee to purchase retail gift cards and send the redemption codes, and the case has not been further subtyped.
ITID-53141.purpose: Captures the fraud-outcome intake bucket for BEC attacks that pressure an employee into purchasing and surrendering gift cards.
scopeIncludes: An email purportedly from an executive requesting the urgent purchase of gift cards for a 'confidential' purpose
Follow-up impersonation via text/phone reinforcing the gift-card request
Cases pending further classification into a more specific gift-card-scam subtype
scopeExcludes: Executive-impersonation wire fraud (ITID-53111)
Vendor invoice fraud (ITID-53121)
Consumer-targeted gift-card scams unrelated to a company impersonation pretext (out of Attacks Against the Company scope)
ITID-53141.severity: Low-Medium. Per-incident dollar loss is typically small (capped by gift-card denominations) and largely unrecoverable once codes are redeemed, but volume can be high.
ITID-53141.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the same pretext is being used against multiple employees simultaneously (indicating an active mass campaign).
ITID-53141.escalation: Escalate to the SOC for email-vector containment and broader-campaign check; typically does not require law-enforcement engagement given the low per-incident value, though aggregate cases may be reported.
indicators: Urgent, informal-toned email requesting gift-card purchase 'as a favor'
Request to photograph and send the card's redemption code
Sender address subtly different from the impersonated executive's real address
vectors: Display-name spoofing of an executive
Compromised or lookalike executive email account
rootCauses: Employees not trained to recognize the gift-card-request BEC pattern
No policy prohibiting gift-card purchases via informal email request
controls: Employee awareness training specifically covering the gift-card BEC pattern
Policy banning gift-card purchases as a company payment method
Email banner flagging external/lookalike-domain senders
ITID-53141.detection: Low technical detection surface; most cases surface through employee self-reporting after the fact rather than SOC telemetry.
ITID-53141.response: SOC investigates the email vector for broader-campaign indicators; finance/HR handles employee reimbursement policy and awareness follow-up.
metrics: Count of gift-card scam attempts reported per quarter
Number of employees who completed a purchase before recognizing the scam
Awareness-training completion rate
sops: Gift Card Scam Employee Reporting SOP
ITID-53141.notes: Lowest-value, highest-volume member of the BEC fraud-outcome group; primarily a training and awareness problem rather than a technical detection one. See ITID-22411-22415 for the underlying email-compromise mechanics.

playbook.name: Gift Card Scam (BEC)
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates an executive or manager via spoofed/lookalike email to pressure an employee into urgently purchasing gift cards and sending the card codes, converting company funds into an untraceable payment instrument.

steps.title: Collect the suspect email and headers
steps.desc: Obtain the request email in full, with headers, from the targeted employee.
steps.guidance: Ask for a direct export/forward-as-attachment; note any gift card codes already sent.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved including any card details already disclosed.

steps.title: Analyze sender domain/display-name spoofing
steps.desc: Check the From address and display name against the impersonated executive's real address; gift card BEC frequently uses display-name spoofing from free webmail rather than domain spoofing.
steps.guidance: Look specifically for a mismatched reply-to address and free-webmail sending domain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed spoofing method used.

steps.title: Determine what was purchased/disclosed and when
steps.desc: Interview the employee to establish exactly which gift cards (retailer, amount, card numbers/PINs) were purchased and disclosed, and the timing.
steps.guidance: Time is critical — gift card codes can be redeemed within minutes of disclosure.
steps.outcome: Full list of card numbers, PINs, amounts, and retailers, with timestamps.

steps.title: Contact retailers immediately to freeze/flag the gift cards
steps.desc: Call each retailer's fraud line immediately with the card numbers to request a freeze or balance check before the codes are redeemed.
steps.guidance: Retailers can sometimes halt redemption if contacted quickly enough; have card numbers, purchase receipts, and PINs ready.
steps.outcome: Retailer fraud teams engaged; any unredeemed balance frozen.
steps.abort: If cards are already fully redeemed, note the loss and proceed to reporting.

steps.title: Block the sender and alert staff org-wide
steps.desc: Block the sending address/domain at the email gateway and send an internal alert warning staff about the active gift-card BEC campaign.
steps.guidance: Search for other recipients of similar messages and notify them proactively.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked; other potential targets warned before falling for the scam.

steps.title: Establish a no-gift-card-purchase policy for executive requests
steps.desc: Formalize a policy that no employee purchases gift cards or similar payment instruments on the basis of an email request, and require callback verification for any unusual purchase request purportedly from leadership.
steps.guidance: Communicate via Finance and executive assistants who are common targets.
steps.outcome: Documented policy reducing recurrence.

steps.title: File retailer and law-enforcement fraud reports
steps.desc: File formal fraud reports with each retailer and with law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3) for any unrecovered funds.
steps.guidance: Retain all purchase receipts and correspondence for the reports.
steps.outcome: Reports filed; any possible reimbursement pursued.

steps.title: Brief at-risk staff and update awareness training
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief roles commonly targeted (executive assistants, office managers, new hires) on this specific scam pattern.
steps.guidance: Add a redacted example to phishing-awareness training.
steps.outcome: Awareness materials updated; incident closed.

ITID-53211.def: Fraudulent redirection of an outgoing wire payment to a legitimate vendor, achieved by an adversary impersonating the vendor (typically via a spoofed or compromised email thread) to request an update to bank routing/account details in accounts payable systems immediately before a scheduled payment.
ITID-53211.purpose: Captures wire fraud losses caused by an adversary tricking a company employee into changing a legitimate vendor's banking details on file, then diverting a routine payment to an attacker-controlled account.
scopeIncludes: Spoofed or compromised vendor email requesting a 'new' bank account for an upcoming invoice payment
AP staff updating vendor banking details based solely on an email request with no out-of-band verification
Wire sent to the new account before the fraud is discovered
Attacker monitoring a compromised vendor or internal mailbox to time the request around a real invoice
scopeExcludes: Wire fraud tied to a real estate/escrow closing (ITID-53212)
Payroll direct-deposit redirection (payroll diversion, ITID-53130 branch)
