Gift card or other non-wire BEC payment requests (ITID-53140 branch)
Wire fraud with no identifiable vendor-detail-change mechanism (ITID-53213)
ITID-53211.severity: High to Critical, scaled to the wire amount and whether recovery/clawback is still possible (the first 24-72 hours are decisive).
ITID-53211.priority: P1 if the wire has been sent within the last 24-72 hours and a recall/hold may still be possible; P2 once the recovery window has closed and the incident shifts to investigation and loss reporting.
ITID-53211.escalation: Escalate immediately to Finance/Treasury and the sending bank for an emergency wire recall, to Legal for law-enforcement (FBI IC3) and insurance notification, and to the SOC for email-compromise triage of the mailbox(es) involved.
indicators: Vendor bank-detail change request arriving by email shortly before a scheduled payment
Slight domain/display-name spoofing or a compromised vendor mailbox sending the request
Urgency or confidentiality language discouraging phone verification
New account at a bank/geography inconsistent with the vendor's known profile
Mailbox rules or forwarding discovered on a compromised internal or vendor account
vectors: Business email compromise of the vendor's mailbox
Look-alike domain spoofing the vendor's email address
Compromise of internal AP staff mailbox to intercept and alter the real invoice thread
rootCauses: No callback/out-of-band verification requirement for vendor banking-detail changes
AP process trusts email as sufficient authorization for payment-detail changes
Lack of email authentication (DMARC/DKIM/SPF) enforcement allowing spoofing to reach the inbox
controls: Mandatory out-of-band (phone, previously-verified number) confirmation for any vendor banking-detail change
Email authentication enforcement (DMARC reject/quarantine)
Positive-pay/dual-approval workflow for new or changed vendor payment instructions
ITID-53211.detection: Weak at the technical layer once the fraudulent detail change is accepted; detection depends primarily on AP process controls and post-hoc bank/vendor reconciliation rather than SOC telemetry, though mailbox compromise (if present) is detectable via login/forwarding-rule monitoring.
ITID-53211.response: Attempt an emergency wire recall with the originating bank immediately, freeze further payments to the vendor pending verification, and if a mailbox compromise is suspected, run standard BEC account-compromise containment (password reset, session revocation, forwarding-rule audit) in parallel.
metrics: Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
Time from wire execution to fraud detection
Number of vendor banking-change requests verified out-of-band vs. bypassed
sops: Vendor Payment Detail Change Verification SOP
ITID-53211.notes: Mechanically overlaps with BEC Vendor Invoice Fraud (ITID-53120 branch); this leaf is scoped specifically to the wire-transfer payment rail and vendor bank-detail-change vector rather than invoice content manipulation generally.

playbook.name: Wire Transfer Fraud via Compromised Vendor Banking Details Change Email
playbook.description: A fraudulent email purporting to be from a known vendor requests a change to banking details, and finance staff execute a wire transfer to the fraudulent account before the deception is discovered.

steps.title: Confirm the fraudulent banking-detail change and affected wire
steps.desc: Validate that a vendor banking-detail change request was received via email/portal and that a wire transfer was executed against the new (fraudulent) account details.
steps.guidance: Pull the originating email headers, compare the requested account/routing numbers against the vendor's on-file banking details, and confirm the wire confirmation number, amount, and destination bank with Treasury/AP.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent wire with exact amount, destination account/routing number, receiving bank, and timestamp documented.
steps.abort: If the banking-detail change was independently verified through an out-of-band callback prior to the wire, this is a false positive — close as a verified legitimate change.
steps.tool: Email header analysis / AP audit trail

steps.title: Identify the compromise vector for the fraudulent email
steps.desc: Determine whether the fraudulent request originated from a compromised vendor mailbox, a spoofed/lookalike domain, or a compromise of internal AP/finance credentials.
steps.guidance: Check SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, sender domain registration date, and reply-to address; check internal mailbox audit logs for AP staff for any signs of BEC compromise on the receiving side.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector identified (vendor-side BEC, domain spoofing, or internal mailbox compromise) to scope containment.

steps.title: Initiate emergency wire recall with originating and receiving banks
steps.desc: Immediately contact Treasury's bank and the receiving bank's fraud department to request a SWIFT recall or hold on the funds; time is critical, typically within 24 hours of transfer for any realistic recovery.
steps.guidance: Use the bank's wire fraud hotline, provide the wire reference number, and simultaneously file an FBI IC3 complaint to trigger the Financial Fraud Kill Chain if funds transferred domestically within the US window.
steps.outcome: Recall request submitted to both banks; kill-chain/FBI complaint filed where the window allows; funds hold status documented.
steps.abort: If funds have already been withdrawn or moved offshore beyond recall, document this and proceed directly to law-enforcement referral and insurance claim.
steps.tool: Bank wire fraud hotline / FBI IC3

steps.title: Lock down the compromised mailbox and freeze further vendor payments
steps.desc: If a mailbox compromise was identified, reset credentials and revoke sessions/tokens; place a company-wide hold on any further payments to the affected vendor pending verification.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT security to reset passwords, revoke OAuth tokens/forwarding rules, and flag the vendor record in the AP system as 'payment hold - suspected fraud'.
steps.outcome: Compromised account secured, forwarding rules removed, and vendor payment hold active in AP system.

steps.title: Remove attacker persistence and malicious forwarding rules
steps.desc: Eliminate any inbox rules, forwarding addresses, or compromised credentials that enabled the fraud, and remove the fraudulent vendor banking details from AP master data.
steps.guidance: Audit mailbox rules for hidden forwarding/deletion rules; purge the fraudulent bank account from the vendor master record and restore verified legitimate details.
steps.outcome: No residual attacker access; vendor master data restored to verified accurate banking details.
steps.tool: Email admin console / ERP vendor master

steps.title: Implement callback verification and dual-approval for banking changes
steps.desc: Institute mandatory out-of-band callback verification (using a known, previously-verified phone number, not one supplied in the change request) for any vendor banking-detail change, plus dual approval before disbursement.
steps.guidance: Update AP procedures to require verbal confirmation from a known vendor contact before any banking-detail change takes effect, and require second-approver sign-off on wires above a defined threshold.
steps.outcome: Updated AP control procedure documented and communicated to Treasury/AP staff.

steps.title: Restore normal vendor payment operations and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Resume normal payments to the verified vendor account and continue pursuing fund recovery through banks, insurance, and law enforcement channels.
steps.guidance: Track the recall/insurance claim status to closure; reconcile AP records to reflect the fraudulent transaction and any recovered funds.
steps.outcome: Vendor payments resumed on verified details; recovery efforts tracked to conclusion.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and update BEC awareness training
steps.desc: Document root cause, financial loss, recovery outcome, and control gaps; update finance-team phishing/BEC awareness training and simulate future callback-verification drills.
steps.guidance: Include timeline, loss amount, recovered amount, and control changes in the after-action report; brief Finance and Treasury leadership.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed and control improvements tracked to implementation.

ITID-53212.def: Fraudulent interception or redirection of a high-value, time-sensitive real estate or escrow wire transfer, typically achieved by compromising the email of a title company, real estate agent, escrow officer, or one of the transacting parties and sending falsified wire instructions to the buyer or another party at the closing.
ITID-53212.purpose: Captures wire fraud targeting real estate or escrow closings, where an adversary intercepts closing-fund wire instructions and redirects buyer, title, or escrow funds to a fraudulent account.
scopeIncludes: Compromised title/escrow/agent mailbox sending 'updated' wire instructions to a home buyer or seller
Spoofed closing-agent email intercepted mid-transaction near closing date
Funds wired to a fraudulent account and discovered only after closing
scopeExcludes: General vendor banking-detail-change wire fraud outside a real estate/escrow context (ITID-53211)
Wire fraud with no real-estate/escrow nexus (ITID-53213)
ITID-53212.severity: Critical — real estate wires are typically large, one-time, and irreversible once received by the fraudulent account, often representing a buyer's entire life savings or the company's transaction proceeds.
ITID-53212.priority: P1, always, given the narrow (often same-day) recovery window characteristic of closing wires.
ITID-53212.escalation: Escalate immediately and in parallel to the sending bank for recall, to the title/escrow company and all transacting parties to halt further disbursement, to Legal, and to law enforcement (FBI IC3 has a dedicated real-estate wire fraud recovery process).
indicators: Last-minute change to wire instructions received close to the scheduled closing date
Email domain subtly altered from the title/escrow company's real domain
Pressure to wire quickly to avoid 'delaying closing'
Company's own escrow/deposit account is the compromised party rather than a counterparty
vectors: Business email compromise of a title company, escrow officer, or real estate agent involved in the transaction
Interception of a legitimate closing-instructions email thread and injection of altered banking details
rootCauses: Real estate/escrow industry's continued reliance on email for wire instructions with no standardized secure verification channel
Absence of a company policy requiring phone verification (using a previously-known number, not one in the email) before wiring closing funds
controls: Mandatory phone verification of wire instructions using an independently sourced number for any real estate/escrow transaction
Use of secure wire-instruction portals rather than email where available
Internal policy requiring dual sign-off before initiating property-transaction wires
ITID-53212.detection: Limited technical detection surface for the fraud itself; SOC visibility is mainly indirect, through detecting compromise of the company's own escrow-related mailboxes if that is the entry point.
ITID-53212.response: Immediately contact the sending and receiving banks to request a wire recall/hold, notify all transaction parties, and preserve the email thread for forensic and law-enforcement review.
metrics: Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
Time from wire execution to fraud detection
Number of real-estate/escrow transactions verified via out-of-band callback
detections: Anomalous lookalike-domain detection for known title/escrow partners
ITID-53212.notes: Distinguished from the general vendor-detail-change leaf (ITID-53211) by transaction context: high-dollar, one-time, deadline-driven property closings where the compromised party is frequently a third-party title/escrow firm outside the company's direct security controls.

playbook.name: Wire Transfer Fraud via Real Estate/Escrow Transaction Interception
playbook.description: An attacker intercepts email communications in a real-estate or escrow transaction and diverts closing funds to a fraudulent account via spoofed wiring instructions.

steps.title: Confirm interception and fraudulent wiring instructions
steps.desc: Validate that wiring instructions received by the company (as buyer, seller, or intermediary) for a real-estate/escrow closing were altered or spoofed, and confirm whether funds were transferred.
steps.guidance: Compare the wiring instructions received against the title/escrow company's originally issued instructions; verify email header authenticity and sender domain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent instruction with exact destination account, amount, and transfer timestamp.
steps.abort: If instructions match originally-verified escrow details, this is a false positive.

steps.title: Determine which party's email was compromised
steps.desc: Identify whether the compromise occurred in the company's own mailbox, the title/escrow company, the realtor, or another transaction party.
steps.guidance: Request incident cooperation from title company/realtor IT; review internal mailbox logs for anomalous access, forwarding rules, or login from unfamiliar geographies.
steps.outcome: Compromise point identified to scope containment and notification obligations.

steps.title: Initiate emergency wire recall within the critical time window
steps.desc: Immediately contact the originating bank's wire fraud department and the receiving bank to request recall/hold; real-estate wire fraud has a very narrow recovery window, often under 24-48 hours.
steps.guidance: File an FBI IC3 complaint requesting Financial Fraud Kill Chain activation if within the window; notify title insurance/escrow company simultaneously.
steps.outcome: Recall requests submitted to both banks and FBI kill-chain filed where applicable; hold status documented.
steps.abort: If beyond recovery window, document and proceed to insurance claim and law-enforcement referral.
steps.tool: Bank wire fraud hotline / FBI IC3

steps.title: Notify and coordinate with all transaction parties
steps.desc: Alert the escrow/title company, realtor, buyer/seller counsel, and any cyber-insurance carrier to halt further disbursements on the transaction and coordinate a unified response.
steps.guidance: Establish a single point of contact among all parties to avoid duplicate or conflicting communications that could tip off the attacker.
steps.outcome: All transaction parties notified and further disbursements on the deal frozen pending investigation.

steps.title: Remove compromised access and secure the affected mailbox
steps.desc: If the compromise was in a company-controlled mailbox, reset credentials, revoke sessions/forwarding rules, and remove any persistence mechanisms.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT security for full mailbox forensic review and credential reset; if compromise was external (title/realtor), confirm their remediation status before resuming communication.
steps.outcome: Compromised mailbox secured with no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Harden wiring-instruction verification procedures for real-estate transactions
steps.desc: Require verbal, out-of-band verification of wiring instructions using a phone number sourced independently (not from the email itself) before any real-estate/escrow related wire is sent.
steps.guidance: Update internal procurement/legal transaction procedures and communicate to any staff involved in real-estate transactions.
steps.outcome: Updated verification procedure documented and adopted.

steps.title: Track recovery and complete the transaction on verified terms
steps.desc: Pursue fund recovery through banks/insurance/law enforcement, and re-execute the transaction using verified wiring instructions once safe to proceed.
steps.guidance: Maintain a recovery tracker and update all transaction parties on status until resolution.
steps.outcome: Recovery status tracked to conclusion; transaction completed on verified instructions if still viable.

steps.title: Document incident and share findings with transaction ecosystem
steps.desc: Complete an after-action report covering root cause, loss/recovery amounts, and control changes; share relevant findings with title/escrow partners to strengthen ecosystem-wide defenses.
steps.guidance: Include timeline, financial impact, and control updates; brief legal and finance leadership.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed and distributed to relevant stakeholders.

ITID-53213.def: An unclassified or general instance of fraudulent wire transfer redirection or interception that does not fit an existing, more specific Wire Transfer Fraud leaf.
ITID-53213.purpose: Intake bucket for wire transfer fraud incidents that do not clearly fit the vendor-banking-detail-change or real-estate/escrow patterns, pending further triage.
scopeIncludes: Wire fraud reported without enough detail yet to determine the specific mechanism or context
Novel or mixed-mechanism wire fraud not covered by the vendor-detail-change or real-estate/escrow leaves
scopeExcludes: Wire fraud via compromised vendor banking-detail-change email (ITID-53211)
Wire fraud tied to real estate/escrow transactions (ITID-53212)
ITID-53213.severity: High to Critical, assessed the same as any wire fraud pending reclassification — do not let taxonomy uncertainty delay recovery action.
ITID-53213.priority: P1 while the wire is still potentially recoverable; reassess and reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53213.escalation: Escalate to Finance/Treasury for an emergency wire recall and to Legal/law enforcement exactly as for any confirmed wire fraud; escalate to the SOC lead to determine the correct sub-classification once details emerge.
indicators: Unauthorized or redirected wire reported by Finance without a clearly identified fraud mechanism
Discrepancy discovered during bank reconciliation with no immediately obvious cause
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause; general weaknesses in wire-authorization verification processes
controls: Standard wire-authorization dual-control and out-of-band verification controls applicable to all wire fraud
ITID-53213.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific technical or non-technical vector.
ITID-53213.response: Apply standard emergency wire-recall response immediately, then investigate to reclassify under a specific Wire Transfer Fraud leaf as soon as the mechanism is known.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
Time to reclassification
ITID-53213.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification; incidents should be reclassified to a specific Wire Transfer Fraud leaf as soon as sufficient detail is available.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Wire Transfer Fraud
playbook.description: A wire transfer fraud incident that does not fit the vendor-banking-change or real-estate/escrow patterns, requiring general fraudulent-wire triage and response.

steps.title: Confirm the fraudulent wire and gather transaction details
steps.desc: Validate that a wire transfer was executed based on fraudulent instructions, impersonation, or unauthorized access, and capture the full transaction detail.
steps.guidance: Obtain the wire confirmation, originating request, requestor identity claims, destination account/routing details, and amount from Treasury/AP records.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent wire with full transaction detail documented.
steps.abort: If the transaction is confirmed as legitimate upon review, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism and entry point
steps.desc: Investigate how the fraudulent instruction was introduced — social engineering, credential compromise, insider action, or vendor/counterparty compromise.
steps.guidance: Review authentication logs, email trails, and approval workflow records to trace the fraud's origin.
steps.outcome: Fraud mechanism and entry point identified to scope containment.

steps.title: Initiate wire recall and bank fraud-department engagement
steps.desc: Contact the originating bank's wire fraud department immediately to request a recall/hold, and engage the receiving bank where possible; file an FBI IC3 complaint for Kill Chain consideration.
steps.guidance: Time is critical — act within hours of discovery to maximize recovery likelihood.
steps.outcome: Recall requests submitted and hold status documented.
steps.abort: If beyond recovery window, document and move to law-enforcement/insurance track.
steps.tool: Bank wire fraud hotline / FBI IC3

steps.title: Suspend the exploited process or access pathway
steps.desc: Freeze the specific payment process, account, or credential pathway that enabled the fraud to prevent repeat exploitation.
steps.guidance: Disable compromised credentials, place holds on affected accounts, and require manual review for any pending wires from the same channel.
steps.outcome: Exploited pathway suspended with no further unauthorized wires possible.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause
steps.desc: Eliminate the specific vulnerability, compromised credential, or process gap that enabled the fraud.
steps.guidance: Reset credentials, patch process gaps, and remove any attacker persistence identified during investigation.
steps.outcome: Root cause eliminated and verified closed.

steps.title: Strengthen payment-authorization controls
steps.desc: Introduce or tighten dual-approval, callback-verification, or transaction-limit controls on the affected payment pathway to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Document the specific control change and the approval workflow update in Treasury/AP procedures.
steps.outcome: Enhanced payment-authorization control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Restore normal payment operations under enhanced controls
steps.desc: Resume the affected payment process under strengthened verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Apply enhanced monitoring/manual review to the affected process for a defined period post-incident.
steps.outcome: Payment process restored with enhanced controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update wire-fraud controls
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial impact, and recovery outcome; update wire-transfer control policy and staff training accordingly.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance/Treasury leadership and track control-improvement action items to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed and control updates implemented.

ITID-53221.def: Unauthorized purchase made using stolen credit/debit card information (card number, expiry, CVV) in an online, phone, or mail-order transaction where the physical card is never presented, typically sourced from a prior data breach, skimming operation, or phishing campaign.
ITID-53221.purpose: Captures fraudulent card-not-present transactions made against the company's payment accounts using stolen card data, without the physical card or cardholder present.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent online purchases charged to a company card using stolen card data
Recurring/subscription charges fraudulently set up using stolen card details
Card-testing activity (small authorization attempts) preceding a larger fraudulent charge
scopeExcludes: Fraud involving a physically cloned or counterfeit card presented in person (ITID-53222)
Charges resulting from a fully taken-over cardholder account/portal (ITID-53223)
ITID-53221.severity: Low to Medium per individual transaction, escalating to Medium-High if part of a larger pattern (card-testing wave, bulk charge fraud) affecting multiple accounts.
ITID-53221.priority: P3 for an isolated disputed charge; P2 if multiple company cards show a coordinated fraud pattern.
ITID-53221.escalation: Escalate to the card issuer/acquiring bank for chargeback and card reissuance, and to Finance for reconciliation; escalate to the SOC only if the stolen card data appears to originate from a breach of company-held cardholder data.
indicators: Unrecognized online merchant charges on a statement
Multiple small 'test' authorizations followed by a larger charge
Charges originating from a geographic location inconsistent with the cardholder
Card issuer fraud-alert flag on the transaction
vectors: Card data obtained from a third-party data breach or dark-web marketplace
Phishing of card details directly from a company employee or system
Card-skimming malware on a compromised e-commerce or payment page
rootCauses: Card data exposed in an unrelated third-party breach
Lack of transaction monitoring/alerting on company card accounts
Weak CVV/AVS enforcement by merchants accepting the fraudulent charge
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Real-time transaction monitoring and fraud-alerting on company card accounts
Virtual/single-use card numbers for online purchasing where feasible
Prompt card reissuance upon suspected exposure
ITID-53221.detection: Primarily a banking/issuer-side fraud-detection function; SOC visibility is limited to cases where the underlying stolen card data can be traced back to a company system breach.
ITID-53221.response: Dispute the charge with the issuer, reissue the affected card, and review whether the stolen data traces back to a company-side exposure requiring a broader breach investigation.
metrics: Number of disputed CNP transactions per period
Dollar amount recovered via chargeback
Time from charge to detection
sops: Card Fraud Dispute and Reissuance SOP
ITID-53221.notes: The mapped MITRE technique is a loose analog (stolen-identity-information framing) rather than a direct technical intrusion mapping — CNP fraud is fundamentally a payment-fraud pattern, not an ATT&CK-modeled intrusion, unless the company itself is the breached source of the card data.

playbook.name: Card-Not-Present (CNP) Fraudulent Transaction
playbook.description: Fraudulent card-not-present transactions (online/phone) are processed against the company's payment systems or corporate cards using stolen card data.

steps.title: Detect anomalous CNP transaction patterns
steps.desc: Identify transactions flagged by payment-processor fraud scoring, chargebacks, or anomaly monitoring (unusual volume, geography, velocity, or mismatched billing/shipping data).
steps.guidance: Review payment gateway fraud alerts, AVS/CVV mismatch logs, and chargeback notifications for the affected merchant account or corporate card program.
steps.outcome: Confirmed set of fraudulent CNP transactions with amounts, timestamps, and card BINs identified.
steps.abort: If flagged transactions are confirmed legitimate customer activity, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope the fraud pattern and affected systems
steps.desc: Determine whether the fraud reflects stolen-card testing/carding against the company's checkout, a compromised corporate card, or a merchant-account-level attack.
steps.guidance: Correlate transaction IP addresses, device fingerprints, and card BIN ranges to identify a coordinated carding attack versus isolated fraud.
steps.outcome: Fraud pattern scoped, distinguishing carding-bot activity from isolated stolen-card use.

steps.title: Engage card network/acquirer fraud department and block the pattern
steps.desc: Notify the acquiring bank/payment processor's fraud team, and if a corporate card is affected, contact the issuing bank to freeze the card immediately.
steps.guidance: Provide the processor with transaction IDs for rapid reversal where possible; request the issuer freeze/reissue any compromised corporate card.
steps.outcome: Processor/issuer engaged; compromised cards frozen; further fraudulent authorizations blocked.
steps.tool: Payment processor fraud hotline / card issuer

steps.title: Apply velocity/geo-blocking rules to stop the ongoing attack
steps.desc: If a carding attack is in progress against checkout, apply temporary rate-limiting, CAPTCHA, or geo/IP blocking to stop further fraudulent authorization attempts.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the e-commerce platform team to deploy WAF rules or fraud-filter tightening without unduly blocking legitimate customers.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent transaction attempts drop to baseline levels.

steps.title: Reverse fraudulent charges and reissue compromised credentials
steps.desc: Process chargebacks/reversals for confirmed fraudulent transactions and reissue any compromised corporate card numbers.
steps.guidance: Work with the processor on dispute filings and confirm new card numbers are activated with updated recurring-payment details.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent charges reversed and compromised cards reissued.

steps.title: Implement stronger authentication for checkout/payment flows
steps.desc: Adopt or tighten 3-D Secure, AVS/CVV enforcement, or tokenization on the checkout flow to reduce future CNP fraud exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the payment processor and e-commerce platform team to enable the additional verification layer.
steps.outcome: Stronger authentication control implemented and verified in the checkout flow.

steps.title: Restore normal checkout operations and monitor closely
steps.desc: Lift temporary blocking rules once the attack subsides and monitor transaction patterns closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Maintain heightened fraud-score thresholds for a defined monitoring period.
steps.outcome: Checkout operations restored to normal with continued heightened monitoring.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen CNP fraud controls
steps.desc: Record loss amount, chargeback outcomes, and root cause; evaluate additional controls such as 3-D Secure, AVS/CVV enforcement, or tokenization.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance and e-commerce leadership; track control improvements to implementation.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53222.def: Unauthorized in-person transaction made using a counterfeit or cloned physical payment card, created by copying magnetic-stripe or (less commonly) chip data obtained through skimming devices, POS malware at a third-party merchant, or other physical/point-of-sale compromise, and presented at a card terminal or ATM.
ITID-53222.purpose: Captures fraud losses from a physically cloned or counterfeit card presented in person, distinguishing purely physical card-fraud mechanisms from remote/online fraud.
scopeIncludes: Physical counterfeit card manufactured from skimmed magnetic-stripe data
In-person fraudulent purchase or ATM withdrawal using a cloned card
Skimming device discovered on a company-operated payment terminal or ATM
scopeExcludes: Remote/online card-not-present fraud (ITID-53221)
Fraud driven by a compromised online account rather than a physical card (ITID-53223)
ITID-53222.severity: Low to Medium per incident, escalating to Medium-High if the company's own point-of-sale or ATM equipment is found to be compromised (indicating an ongoing skimming operation affecting many cardholders).
ITID-53222.priority: P3 for a single fraudulent charge; P1-P2 if a skimming device or POS compromise is discovered on company-operated equipment.
ITID-53222.escalation: Escalate to the card issuer for dispute/reissuance for isolated fraud; escalate immediately to physical security, the SOC, and the payment processor if a skimmer or compromised terminal is found on company premises.
indicators: In-person charge or ATM withdrawal the cardholder did not make
Physical skimming device or hidden camera found on a card terminal/ATM
Cluster of fraud reports traceable to a single merchant or terminal ('common point of purchase')
vectors: Skimming device installed on a card reader or ATM
POS malware harvesting card data from a compromised terminal
Card data cloned from a prior breach and encoded onto a blank card
rootCauses: Physical tampering with unattended or poorly monitored payment terminals
Lack of EMV chip enforcement allowing magnetic-stripe fallback transactions
Insufficient physical inspection routines for company-operated card terminals/ATMs
controls: Routine physical inspection of card terminals and ATMs for tampering
EMV chip enforcement and magnetic-stripe fallback restriction
Point-to-point encryption on POS payment terminals
ITID-53222.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise mapping — the counterfeit-card mechanism itself is a physical fraud method, not a network/endpoint intrusion; detection relies on physical inspection, issuer fraud analytics, and common-point-of-purchase analysis rather than SOC telemetry, except where POS malware is the skimming vector.
ITID-53222.response: For isolated fraud, dispute and reissue via the card issuer; for a discovered skimmer or compromised terminal, secure the device for law enforcement, notify the payment processor and affected cardholders, and if POS malware is involved, run standard endpoint compromise containment.
metrics: Number of skimming devices found during physical inspections
Number of disputed cloned-card transactions
Time from discovery to terminal remediation
sops: Card Fraud Dispute and Reissuance SOP
ITID-53222.notes: Mapped MITRE is intentionally empty for the physical cloning/counterfeiting mechanism itself — there is no ATT&CK Enterprise technique for physical card cloning; if POS malware is the data-harvesting source, that malware compromise should also be logged under the relevant ITID-30000 malware leaf.

playbook.name: Cloned/Counterfeit Physical Card Fraud
playbook.description: A physical corporate or company-issued payment card is cloned/counterfeited using skimmed data and used for unauthorized in-person purchases.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized physical-card transactions
steps.desc: Validate reported unauthorized in-person (card-present) transactions against the cardholder's actual location and activity to confirm cloning/counterfeiting rather than legitimate use.
steps.guidance: Compare transaction locations/timestamps against the cardholder's travel/expense records and confirm the physical card was in the cardholder's possession at the time.
steps.outcome: Confirmed cloned-card fraud with transaction list, amounts, and merchant locations documented.
steps.abort: If transactions match legitimate cardholder activity, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify the likely skimming point of compromise
steps.desc: Trace the cardholder's recent legitimate card-present transactions to identify a common merchant, ATM, or terminal that may have been compromised by a skimmer.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference multiple affected cardholders (if any) against shared merchant locations or terminals to identify a skimming point.
steps.outcome: Likely point of compromise identified or ruled out.

steps.title: Freeze the compromised card and issuing account immediately
steps.desc: Contact the card issuer's fraud department to freeze/cancel the cloned card and place a hold on further authorizations.
steps.guidance: Request expedited card cancellation and confirm no further authorizations post through the freeze.
steps.outcome: Card frozen/cancelled with no further fraudulent authorizations.

steps.title: Alert other cardholders if a common compromise point is identified
steps.desc: If a shared skimming point was identified, notify other employees/cardholders who used that merchant/terminal to review their own statements.
steps.guidance: Send a targeted advisory to affected cardholder population with guidance to monitor statements and report anomalies.
steps.outcome: Affected cardholder population notified and monitoring their accounts.

steps.title: Reissue the compromised card and dispute fraudulent charges
steps.desc: Reissue a new card number to the affected cardholder and file disputes for all confirmed fraudulent transactions.
steps.guidance: Confirm new card activation and update any recurring payments tied to the old card number.
steps.outcome: New card issued and activated; fraudulent charges disputed with the issuer.

steps.title: Report the compromised terminal/merchant for remediation
steps.desc: If a specific skimming point was identified, report the compromised terminal/ATM/merchant to the card network and relevant authorities for remediation.
steps.guidance: File a report with the card network's fraud unit and, where a public terminal is involved, notify the merchant/ATM operator.
steps.outcome: Compromised terminal reported and remediation confirmed or in progress.

steps.title: Confirm reimbursement and resume normal card use
steps.desc: Track the dispute/chargeback outcome to confirm reimbursement and resume normal use of the reissued card.
steps.guidance: Reconcile expense records once the dispute resolves.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent charges reversed/reimbursed and reissued card in normal use.

steps.title: Document incident and advise on card-security practices
steps.desc: Record findings including the suspected skimming point, and update employee guidance on physical card security (chip-preferred transactions, contactless use, monitoring statements).
steps.guidance: Brief Finance leadership and update the corporate card-use policy if warranted.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed and employee guidance updated.

ITID-53223.def: Unauthorized card charges made possible by an adversary gaining control of a cardholder's online banking, card-issuer, or digital-wallet account (via credential theft, brute force, or MFA-fatigue), then adding a payment method, changing account controls, or directly authorizing fraudulent transactions from within the compromised account.
ITID-53223.purpose: Captures credit/debit card fraud that results from a full takeover of the cardholder's online account or payment profile, rather than from stolen card numbers alone.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent charges made after an adversary logs into the cardholder's card-issuer portal or digital wallet using stolen credentials
Adversary adding a new authorized card or shipping address after taking over the account
MFA-fatigue or brute-force attack against a card/bank account login preceding fraudulent charges
scopeExcludes: Fraud using only stolen card numbers with no account login involved (ITID-53221)
Fraud from a physically cloned card (ITID-53222)
ITID-53223.severity: Medium to High, since account takeover typically grants the adversary broader control (statement access, PII exposure, ability to change contact details) beyond a single fraudulent charge.
ITID-53223.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the takeover is confirmed to extend to primary banking credentials shared with other sensitive accounts.
ITID-53223.escalation: Escalate to Finance and the card issuer to lock the account and reverse fraudulent charges, and to the SOC for standard account-compromise response (credential reset, session revocation) if the takeover involved a company-managed identity.
indicators: Login to a card/banking portal from an unrecognized device or geography immediately followed by profile changes
Password or contact-detail change on the account not initiated by the legitimate holder
Sudden addition of a new payee, authorized user, or shipping address
Repeated failed login or MFA-push attempts preceding the takeover
vectors: Credential phishing targeting the card/bank portal login
Credential stuffing using passwords reused from an unrelated breach
MFA fatigue (repeated push notifications) to obtain approval
rootCauses: Password reuse across the banking/card portal and other services
Absence of phishing-resistant MFA on the financial account
No anomaly alerting on login-then-profile-change sequences
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA on financial account portals
Anomaly alerting on login-then-payment-method-change sequences
Employee password-reuse prevention/monitoring
ITID-53223.detection: Account-level login and change-event logging on the card/banking portal (where available to the company) provides a real technical signal; internal SOC visibility depends on whether the compromised credential is also a company-managed identity.
ITID-53223.response: Lock the compromised account, reverse fraudulent charges through the issuer, force a credential reset, and review for credential reuse across other company systems.
metrics: Number of account-takeover-driven card fraud cases per period
Time from takeover to detection
Percentage of cases involving reused/phished credentials
sops: Card Fraud Dispute and Reissuance SOP
ITID-53223.notes: Differentiated from the other Credit Card Fraud siblings by mechanism: this leaf is account-takeover-driven (a genuine identity/authentication compromise) rather than stolen-card-data or physical-cloning fraud, which is why it carries real ATT&CK technique mappings.

playbook.name: Account Takeover Leading to Unauthorized Card Charges
playbook.description: An attacker takes over a company payment-account or cardholder online profile and uses it to make unauthorized charges or add fraudulent payment methods.

steps.title: Confirm account takeover and unauthorized charges
steps.desc: Validate that the payment account/cardholder profile was accessed without authorization and used to generate unauthorized charges or add new payees/cards.
steps.guidance: Review account login history, password/contact-detail change events, and transaction history for the account in question.
steps.outcome: Confirmed account takeover with unauthorized login events and transaction list documented.
steps.abort: If access was authorized (e.g., legitimate password reset by the account owner), close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify how account credentials were compromised
steps.desc: Determine the takeover vector — phishing, credential stuffing, SIM-swap, or malware — to scope the containment response.
steps.guidance: Check login IPs/geolocation against normal patterns, review for MFA bypass or SIM-swap indicators, and check for known credential-stuffing lists containing the account.
steps.outcome: Takeover vector identified.

steps.title: Lock the account and reverse unauthorized changes
steps.desc: Immediately lock/suspend the compromised account, revoke active sessions, and reverse any unauthorized changes to contact details or added payment methods.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the payment provider/bank to freeze the account and roll back attacker-added payees or forwarding changes.
steps.outcome: Account locked, sessions revoked, unauthorized changes reversed.

steps.title: Engage card network/bank fraud department for charge reversal
steps.desc: Notify the card issuer or payment provider's fraud team to freeze further authorizations and initiate dispute/reversal of unauthorized charges.
steps.guidance: Provide transaction IDs and the confirmed takeover timeline to expedite reversal.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized charges blocked; disputes filed for confirmed fraudulent transactions.

steps.title: Reset credentials and enforce MFA on the recovered account
steps.desc: Force a full credential reset, enable/strengthen multi-factor authentication, and remove any attacker-added recovery methods or trusted devices.
steps.guidance: Verify no attacker-controlled recovery email/phone remains attached to the account before restoring access.
steps.outcome: Account secured with fresh credentials, MFA enforced, and no attacker persistence remaining.

steps.title: Remove all attacker-added payees and recovery artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm removal of any attacker-added payees, linked accounts, forwarding rules, or app authorizations left behind on the compromised account.
steps.guidance: Run a full account-settings review to confirm nothing attacker-controlled remains before returning the account to normal use.
steps.outcome: Account settings verified clean with no residual attacker artifacts.

steps.title: Restore account access and confirm reimbursement
steps.desc: Restore legitimate account access to the rightful user/department and track reimbursement of disputed charges to completion.
steps.guidance: Reconcile financial records once disputes resolve.
steps.outcome: Account access restored and reimbursement confirmed.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen account-security controls
steps.desc: Record the takeover vector, financial impact, and remediation; evaluate broader MFA/identity-verification improvements across similar accounts.
steps.guidance: Brief IT security and Finance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53224.def: An unclassified or general instance of fraudulent card activity that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Credit Card Fraud leaf.
ITID-53224.purpose: Intake bucket for credit card fraud that does not yet fit the card-not-present, cloned-card, or account-takeover patterns.
scopeIncludes: Disputed card charges reported without enough detail to determine CNP, cloning, or account-takeover origin
Novel or mixed-mechanism card fraud
scopeExcludes: Card-not-present fraud with a confirmed stolen-data mechanism (ITID-53221)
Confirmed cloned/counterfeit physical card fraud (ITID-53222)
Confirmed account-takeover-driven card fraud (ITID-53223)
ITID-53224.severity: Low to Medium, consistent with other card-fraud leaves, pending reclassification.
ITID-53224.priority: P3, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed and the incident is reclassified.
ITID-53224.escalation: Escalate to Finance/the card issuer for standard dispute handling; escalate to the SOC only if investigation reveals an account-takeover or company-side data-exposure component.
indicators: Disputed charge reported by a cardholder or flagged by the issuer with mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard card-dispute and monitoring controls applicable to all card fraud
ITID-53224.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53224.response: Dispute the charge through standard issuer processes and investigate to reclassify under the correct Credit Card Fraud leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
sops: Card Fraud Dispute and Reissuance SOP
ITID-53224.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify to a specific Credit Card Fraud leaf as soon as the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Credit Card Fraud
playbook.description: A credit card fraud incident that does not fit the CNP, cloned-card, or account-takeover patterns, requiring general fraudulent-charge triage and response.

steps.title: Confirm fraudulent card charges and gather transaction detail
steps.desc: Validate reported fraudulent charges against the cardholder's known activity and capture full transaction detail.
steps.guidance: Pull the card issuer's transaction history, timestamps, merchant details, and amounts for all disputed charges.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent charges documented with full transaction detail.
steps.abort: If charges are confirmed legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism
steps.desc: Investigate how the card data or account was compromised to enable the fraudulent charges.
steps.guidance: Review for phishing, data breach exposure, skimming, or insider misuse as potential sources.
steps.outcome: Fraud mechanism identified or narrowed to a set of likely causes.

steps.title: Freeze the card and engage issuer fraud department
steps.desc: Contact the card issuer immediately to freeze the affected card and block further unauthorized authorizations.
steps.guidance: Request expedited freeze and confirm no further charges post after the freeze is applied.
steps.outcome: Card frozen with no further fraudulent charges.

steps.title: Suspend related payment credentials pending review
steps.desc: Suspend any linked digital wallet tokens, recurring-billing authorizations, or related payment credentials that could be affected by the same compromise.
steps.guidance: Check for tokenized card copies in mobile wallets or saved-payment vaults and revoke as needed.
steps.outcome: Related payment credentials suspended with no further exposure.

steps.title: Reissue card and dispute fraudulent transactions
steps.desc: Reissue a new card number and file disputes for all confirmed fraudulent charges.
steps.guidance: Update any recurring payments tied to the old card and confirm dispute filings with the issuer.
steps.outcome: New card issued and disputes filed for all confirmed fraudulent transactions.

steps.title: Determine and close the specific fraud entry point
steps.desc: Based on the identified fraud mechanism, close the specific gap that enabled it (e.g., patch a data-exposure source, revoke a compromised credential, address an insider-misuse finding).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT security or HR as appropriate to the identified root cause.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified.

steps.title: Confirm reimbursement and resume normal card use
steps.desc: Track dispute resolution to confirm reimbursement and resume normal use of the reissued card.
steps.guidance: Reconcile expense/financial records once disputes resolve.
steps.outcome: Reimbursement confirmed and reissued card in normal use.

steps.title: Document incident and update card-fraud response guidance
steps.desc: Record root cause, loss amount, and recovery outcome; update relevant fraud-monitoring and cardholder-guidance materials.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance leadership and track any control improvements.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed.

ITID-53231.def: Chemical or mechanical alteration ('washing') of a legitimate check's payee name and/or dollar amount after it has been written and often after it has been intercepted from mail or a physical drop point, enabling the altered check to be deposited by a party other than the intended payee or for a larger amount.
ITID-53231.purpose: Captures fraud in which a legitimate paper check is physically altered (payee name and/or amount) after issuance to redirect or inflate funds.
scopeIncludes: Check stolen from outgoing or incoming mail and chemically altered before deposit
Payee name changed on a legitimate company check
Dollar amount altered upward on a legitimate check
scopeExcludes: A wholly fabricated counterfeit check (ITID-53232)
Fraud involving duplicate remote-deposit-capture submission of a genuine, unaltered check (ITID-53233)
ITID-53231.severity: Medium, scaled to the altered dollar amount and how many checks in a batch may have been intercepted.
ITID-53231.priority: P2 upon discovery, given the narrow window to place a stop-payment or fraud hold with the bank.
ITID-53231.escalation: Escalate immediately to Finance/Treasury for stop-payment and to the issuing bank's fraud department; escalate to the SOC only if the interception point is a compromised internal mail or business process rather than external mail theft.
indicators: Bank reconciliation discrepancy between the issued check amount/payee and the cleared amount/payee
Payee report of a check never received (indicating interception)
Visible signs of chemical alteration on a returned canceled check
vectors: Physical mail theft (outgoing check pickup or mailbox theft)
Chemical washing of ink to erase and rewrite payee/amount
rootCauses: Reliance on physical mail for check distribution with no tracking
Lack of positive-pay matching between issued and presented checks
Use of check stock/ink without tamper-evident/erasure-resistant properties
controls: Positive-pay check-matching service with the issuing bank
Tamper-resistant check stock and ink
Electronic payment migration to reduce paper check volume
ITID-53231.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — check washing/alteration is a physical, non-technical fraud method; detection runs through bank positive-pay matching and reconciliation, not SOC telemetry.
ITID-53231.response: Place a stop-payment/fraud hold with the bank immediately, reissue the legitimate payment through a verified channel, and report to law enforcement (mail theft may trigger USPS/Postal Inspection involvement).
metrics: Number of altered checks caught by positive pay vs. cleared fraudulently
Dollar amount recovered via stop-payment/bank fraud claim
ITID-53231.notes: Check fraud/forgery — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations and banking-partner coordination rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Check Washing/Alteration Fraud
playbook.description: A company-issued check is intercepted and chemically or physically altered (washed) to change the payee and/or amount before being cashed.

steps.title: Confirm the altered check and discrepancy
steps.desc: Validate that a company check was altered by comparing the cashed check image against the original issuance record (payee, amount, date).
steps.guidance: Obtain the cashed-check image from the bank and compare against the AP disbursement register for the original payee and amount.
steps.outcome: Confirmed alteration with original vs. altered details documented.
steps.abort: If the check matches original issuance, close as false positive.

steps.title: Trace the point of interception
steps.desc: Determine where in the mail/delivery chain the check was intercepted — outgoing mail, intended recipient's mailbox, or internal handling.
steps.guidance: Interview AP staff on check mailing procedures and confirm with the intended payee whether they ever received the original check.
steps.outcome: Likely interception point identified.

steps.title: Place a stop-payment and notify the bank's fraud department
steps.desc: Immediately request a stop-payment/hold on the check with the issuing bank and report the altered-check fraud to the bank's fraud department for reimbursement processing under check-fraud protections.
steps.guidance: Most banks require notification of altered/forged checks within a defined statutory window (commonly 30-60 days) to preserve reimbursement rights — act promptly.
steps.outcome: Stop-payment placed and fraud claim opened with the bank.
steps.abort: If the check has already cleared and the claim window has passed, document and pursue alternative recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Freeze the affected check-issuance account pending review
steps.desc: Temporarily halt further check issuances from the affected account until the scope of exposure is understood, particularly if multiple checks may be affected.
steps.guidance: Review recent outstanding checks from the same account/batch for similar alteration risk.
steps.outcome: Check issuance from the affected account paused or under heightened review.

steps.title: Reissue the legitimate payment and close out the fraudulent instrument
steps.desc: Issue proper payment to the correct payee (via check or ACH) and ensure the fraudulent check is voided/reversed with the bank.
steps.guidance: Confirm with the bank that the fraudulent check will not be honored again and that funds are credited back per the fraud claim outcome.
steps.outcome: Legitimate payee paid; fraudulent check voided and reimbursement processed.

steps.title: Enroll the account in positive-pay/payee-match protection
steps.desc: Enable or verify positive-pay and payee-name-match services on the affected disbursement account to catch future altered checks before they clear.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury and the bank to activate the service and confirm daily exception-review responsibility is assigned.
steps.outcome: Positive-pay/payee-match protection active and an owner assigned for daily exception review.

steps.title: Transition to more secure payment methods where feasible
steps.desc: Evaluate shifting recurring or high-value payments from paper check to ACH/positive-pay controlled disbursement to reduce future exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury on enabling positive pay/payee-match services with the bank.
steps.outcome: Reduced reliance on paper checks for high-risk payment types.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen check-handling controls
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial impact, and reimbursement outcome; update check-mailing and positive-pay control procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance/Treasury leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53232.def: Deposit or negotiation of a check that was entirely fabricated (fake account/routing numbers, forged signature, counterfeit check stock) rather than altered from a legitimately issued instrument, typically drawn against the company's real account and routing numbers obtained from a previously handled genuine check.
ITID-53232.purpose: Captures fraud involving a wholly fabricated check — printed or forged from scratch rather than altered from a genuine instrument — presented against or on behalf of the company.
scopeIncludes: Counterfeit check drawn on the company's account using routing/account numbers copied from a legitimate check the payee previously received
Forged signature on a fabricated check presented for payment
Fraudulent check received by the company from a customer/vendor and deposited before being identified as counterfeit
scopeExcludes: Alteration of a genuinely issued check (ITID-53231)
Fraud from duplicate deposit of a real, unaltered check via RDC (ITID-53233)
ITID-53232.severity: Medium, scaled to the dollar amount and whether multiple counterfeit checks against the same account are in circulation.
ITID-53232.priority: P2 upon discovery, given the limited window for a fraud hold before funds clear or are withdrawn.
ITID-53232.escalation: Escalate to Finance/Treasury and the bank's fraud department immediately; if the company's own account/routing numbers were exposed to make the counterfeit possible, review how those numbers were obtained (e.g., a prior mailed check) and tighten distribution.
indicators: Bank fraud alert on a check presented against the company account that Treasury did not issue
Customer/vendor reporting the company deposited a check that was later returned as counterfeit
Check stock, signature, or printing quality inconsistent with genuine company checks
vectors: Counterfeit check production using account/routing numbers copied from a legitimately received check
Forged authorized-signer signature
rootCauses: Company account/routing numbers exposed via mailed checks with no fraud monitoring
Insufficient funds-availability hold policy on deposited checks before they are treated as cleared
controls: Positive-pay matching with the issuing bank to reject unauthorized checks
Standard funds-availability hold periods on deposited third-party checks
Bank account/routing number exposure minimization
ITID-53232.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — counterfeit check fraud is a physical/financial-instrument crime; detection runs through positive pay and bank fraud-review processes, not SOC telemetry.
ITID-53232.response: Reject/return the counterfeit item through the bank's positive-pay or fraud-review process, notify affected counterparties, and file a report with the bank's fraud department and law enforcement as appropriate.
metrics: Number of counterfeit checks rejected via positive pay vs. cleared fraudulently
Dollar amount recovered
ITID-53232.notes: Check fraud/forgery — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations and banking-partner coordination.

playbook.name: Counterfeit Check Fraud
playbook.description: A counterfeit check bearing the company's account and routing information is fraudulently created and deposited/cashed by an unauthorized party.

steps.title: Confirm the counterfeit check and unauthorized debit
steps.desc: Validate that a check drawn on the company's account was not issued by the company (no matching entry in the AP disbursement register) and confirm the resulting unauthorized debit.
steps.guidance: Obtain the check image from the bank and compare against the AP register; verify signature and check-stock authenticity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed counterfeit check with debit amount and date documented.
steps.abort: If the check matches a legitimate issuance, close as false positive.

steps.title: Assess scope of exposure for the account/routing number
steps.desc: Determine whether the company's account/routing number has been exposed more broadly (e.g., leaked check stock, prior mail theft) that could enable further counterfeit checks.
steps.guidance: Review for other suspicious items presented against the same account in recent bank statements.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposure assessed, including any other suspicious items identified.

steps.title: Report the counterfeit check to the bank and request account protection
steps.desc: Immediately report the counterfeit item to the bank's fraud department and request activation of positive-pay/account-protection controls to reject further unauthorized items.
steps.guidance: Request the bank return the counterfeit item and place enhanced monitoring on the account.
steps.outcome: Bank fraud claim opened and enhanced account protection activated.

steps.title: Consider closing and reopening the account if exposure is broad
steps.desc: If account/routing details appear broadly compromised (multiple counterfeit items or leaked check stock), evaluate closing the account and moving to a new account number.
steps.guidance: Weigh the operational disruption of an account change against ongoing counterfeit-check risk; consult Treasury and the bank's fraud specialist.
steps.outcome: Decision made and documented on whether to migrate to a new account.
steps.abort: If exposure is limited to a single isolated item, account migration may not be warranted.

steps.title: Confirm reimbursement and secure check stock
steps.desc: Confirm the bank reimburses the unauthorized debit under check-fraud protections and review physical/digital check-stock security to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Audit check-stock storage, printing access controls, and any third-party check-printing vendor security.
steps.outcome: Funds reimbursed and check-stock security gaps closed.

steps.title: Activate positive-pay protection on the account
steps.desc: Enable positive-pay/payee-match services on the account (new or existing) to reject future counterfeit items before they clear.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury and the bank to activate the service and assign daily exception-review ownership.
steps.outcome: Positive-pay protection active with an assigned exception-review owner.

steps.title: Resume normal account operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal disbursement operations (on the existing or newly-issued account) with positive-pay and enhanced monitoring active.
steps.guidance: Confirm all recurring payees/ACH originators are updated if the account number changed.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced fraud controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update account-protection controls
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial impact, and reimbursement outcome; formalize positive-pay adoption and check-stock security policy.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance/Treasury leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53233.def: Fraudulent duplicate negotiation of a single genuine check achieved by depositing it via remote deposit capture (photographing/scanning the check through a banking app) and then also depositing or cashing the physical check a second time — at a different bank, branch, or via a second RDC submission — before the first deposit clears and the physical item is flagged as already negotiated.
ITID-53233.purpose: Captures fraud in which the same genuine check is deposited more than once by exploiting remote deposit capture (mobile/scan deposit) alongside physical deposit or a second RDC submission.
scopeIncludes: Same check deposited via mobile RDC and then also cashed/deposited physically
Same check submitted via RDC at two different financial institutions before either flags the duplicate
Employee or customer intentionally exploiting the RDC clearing-time gap for double value
scopeExcludes: Alteration of a check's payee/amount (ITID-53231)
A wholly counterfeit/fabricated check (ITID-53232)
ITID-53233.severity: Low to Medium per instance, scaled by dollar amount and whether the pattern recurs across multiple checks (indicating deliberate, repeated exploitation rather than a one-off).
ITID-53233.priority: P3 for an isolated instance; P2 if a pattern of repeated duplicate-deposit attempts is identified against the same account or by the same depositor.
ITID-53233.escalation: Escalate to Finance/Treasury for reconciliation and reversal, and to the bank's fraud/duplicate-detection team; escalate to HR/Legal if the depositor is an employee engaging in deliberate double-deposit fraud.
indicators: Same check number/amount posted twice across the company's bank statement
RDC duplicate-detection alert from the bank (image/MICR-line matching)
Depositor pattern of check amounts just under duplicate-detection review thresholds
vectors: Exploiting the time gap between RDC image capture and physical-check clearing
Depositing the same check at two separate institutions before duplicate-detection systems cross-reference
rootCauses: Insufficient duplicate-image detection on the RDC platform
No policy requiring immediate destruction/marking of a check once deposited via RDC
Lack of reconciliation cross-check between RDC deposits and physical deposits
controls: Bank-side RDC duplicate-image (MICR-line) detection
Policy requiring physical checks be voided/marked immediately after RDC deposit
Reconciliation review flagging duplicate check numbers/amounts
ITID-53233.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — this is a banking-process fraud exploiting settlement timing, not a technical intrusion; detection is a reconciliation and bank fraud-system function.
ITID-53233.response: Reverse the duplicate deposit through the bank, recover funds from the depositor if applicable, and if a company employee or customer is the depositor, coordinate with HR/Legal on further action.
metrics: Number of duplicate-deposit attempts caught vs. cleared
Dollar amount recovered via reversal
ITID-53233.notes: Check fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, reconciliation, and banking-partner coordination.

playbook.name: Remote Deposit Capture (RDC) Duplicate Deposit Fraud
playbook.description: A check is fraudulently deposited multiple times using remote deposit capture (photo deposit) and physical presentment, resulting in duplicate credits against the company's account.

steps.title: Confirm the duplicate deposit and reconcile affected items
steps.desc: Validate that a single check was deposited more than once (via RDC and/or physical presentment) resulting in a duplicate or fraudulent credit, and identify which deposit is illegitimate.
steps.guidance: Reconcile bank deposit records against AR/cash-application records to identify the duplicate item and confirm which deposit channel and depositor account received the improper credit.
steps.outcome: Confirmed duplicate deposit with original vs. duplicate transaction detail documented.
steps.abort: If deposits reconcile as legitimate separate items, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine whether this reflects a customer/counterparty scheme or an internal control gap
steps.desc: Assess whether the duplicate deposit was perpetrated by an external party (customer double-depositing a refund/rebate check) or reflects an internal RDC control weakness.
steps.guidance: Review RDC duplicate-detection settings and depositor account ownership on the improper duplicate deposit.
steps.outcome: Root actor and control gap identified.

steps.title: Report the duplicate item to the bank and request reversal
steps.desc: Notify the depositing bank's fraud/deposit-operations team of the duplicate presentment and request reversal/chargeback of the improper duplicate credit.
steps.guidance: Provide both deposit images/reference numbers to substantiate the duplicate claim.
steps.outcome: Reversal request submitted and acknowledged by the bank.

steps.title: Flag the responsible account/customer pending investigation
steps.desc: Place a hold or enhanced review flag on the depositor account or customer relationship involved in the duplicate deposit pending resolution.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AR/Collections if a customer account is involved to avoid further improper credits or refunds.
steps.outcome: Responsible account flagged with no further improper transactions processed.

steps.title: Correct the ledger and recover duplicated funds
steps.desc: Reverse the duplicate credit in the accounting system once confirmed by the bank, and pursue recovery of any funds already disbursed based on the erroneous duplicate credit.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AR/GL teams to correct the ledger entries and document recovery status.
steps.outcome: Ledger corrected and duplicated funds recovered or recovery in progress.

steps.title: Address the responsible party per findings
steps.desc: If the duplicate deposit was a deliberate customer/counterparty scheme, refer the matter to Collections/Legal for recovery action and account-relationship review; if internal control gap, close the process gap.
steps.guidance: Document the disposition and any account-relationship consequences (e.g., suspension of RDC privileges).
steps.outcome: Responsible party addressed and process gap closed.

steps.title: Tighten RDC duplicate-detection controls
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen the bank's RDC duplicate-detection thresholds and internal cash-application matching to catch future duplicate presentments.
steps.guidance: Confirm with the bank that duplicate-item detection is active on the RDC service and review internal reconciliation frequency.
steps.outcome: Enhanced duplicate-detection controls active and verified.

steps.title: Document incident and update deposit-reconciliation procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial impact, and recovery outcome; update deposit-reconciliation frequency and RDC control policy.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance/Treasury leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53234.def: An unclassified or general instance of check fraud affecting the company that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Check Fraud leaf.
ITID-53234.purpose: Intake bucket for check fraud that does not yet fit the washing/alteration, counterfeit, or RDC duplicate-deposit patterns.
scopeIncludes: Check fraud reported without enough detail to determine alteration, counterfeit, or duplicate-deposit origin
Novel or mixed-mechanism check fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed check washing/alteration (ITID-53231)
Confirmed counterfeit check fraud (ITID-53232)
Confirmed RDC duplicate-deposit fraud (ITID-53233)
ITID-53234.severity: Medium, pending reclassification once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53234.priority: P2 upon discovery, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed and the incident is reclassified.
ITID-53234.escalation: Escalate to Finance/Treasury and the bank's fraud department for standard check-fraud handling regardless of final classification.
indicators: Bank reconciliation discrepancy or fraud alert on a check with mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard positive-pay and reconciliation controls applicable to all check fraud
ITID-53234.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies to check fraud generally; treat mechanism as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53234.response: Apply standard stop-payment/fraud-hold response immediately, then investigate to reclassify under a specific Check Fraud leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53234.notes: Check fraud/forgery — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations and banking-partner coordination. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Check Fraud
playbook.description: A check fraud incident that does not fit the washing/alteration, counterfeit, or RDC-duplicate-deposit patterns, requiring general fraudulent-check triage and response.

steps.title: Confirm the fraudulent check and gather item detail
steps.desc: Validate the reported check fraud against bank records and internal disbursement/receipt registers, and capture the check image, amount, and payee/depositor detail.
steps.guidance: Obtain the check image from the bank and reconcile against AP/AR records to confirm the fraud.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent check with full transaction detail documented.
steps.abort: If the item reconciles as legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism
steps.desc: Investigate how the fraud was perpetrated — forgery, identity misuse, insider action, or another mechanism not covered by more specific playbooks.
steps.guidance: Interview relevant staff and review the chain of custody for the check/item in question.
steps.outcome: Fraud mechanism identified.

steps.title: Notify the bank's fraud department and request a hold/stop-payment
steps.desc: Contact the bank immediately to place a stop-payment or fraud hold on the affected item and open a fraud claim.
steps.guidance: Provide the check image and transaction reference number; confirm the claim window requirements with the bank.
steps.outcome: Stop-payment/hold placed and fraud claim opened.
steps.abort: If the item has already cleared and the claim window has passed, document and pursue alternative recovery.

steps.title: Restrict further check activity on the affected account pending review
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict further check issuance/deposit on the affected account until the scope of the fraud is understood.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury to determine whether other checks may be affected by the same scheme.
steps.outcome: Further check activity restricted with no additional fraudulent items processed.

steps.title: Correct financial records and pursue reimbursement
steps.desc: Correct the ledger for the fraudulent item and pursue reimbursement through the bank's fraud claim process.
steps.guidance: Track the claim to resolution and reconcile once funds are credited back.
steps.outcome: Ledger corrected and reimbursement obtained or in progress.

steps.title: Strengthen check-handling and verification controls
steps.desc: Evaluate and implement positive-pay, dual-signature, or check-stock security controls appropriate to the identified fraud mechanism.
steps.guidance: Document the specific control update in Treasury/AP procedures.
steps.outcome: Updated control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal check operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Lift the restriction on check activity once controls are verified and monitor closely for a defined period.
steps.guidance: Maintain heightened reconciliation frequency for the affected account post-incident.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active.

steps.title: Document incident and update check-fraud response procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial impact, and recovery outcome; update the general check-fraud response procedure and staff guidance.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance/Treasury leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53241.def: Unauthorized execution of cryptocurrency-mining JavaScript within a user's web browser, triggered by visiting a compromised legitimate site or a malicious page (a 'drive-by' delivery), consuming device compute resources for the duration of the browser session without installing persistent malware.
ITID-53241.purpose: Captures cryptocurrency-mining scripts silently run in a visitor's browser via a compromised or malicious website, stealing CPU/GPU cycles for the attacker's financial benefit.
scopeIncludes: In-browser mining script (e.g., Coinhive-style) injected into a compromised website visited by company users
Malicious ad (malvertising) delivering a mining script
Browser extension bundling a hidden mining script
scopeExcludes: Persistent cryptojacking malware installed on cloud compute instances (ITID-53242)
Self-propagating cryptojacking worm activity across the internal network (ITID-53243)
ITID-53241.severity: Low to Medium — impact is typically limited to session-duration CPU/GPU consumption, battery drain, and device slowdown, without persistence or data compromise.
ITID-53241.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the source is an internally hosted/controlled site that has been compromised (indicating a broader web-compromise incident).
ITID-53241.escalation: Escalate to the SOC for endpoint/browser investigation and to web/content teams if a company-owned site is the delivery source; no executive or legal escalation typically required unless the compromised site is customer-facing.
indicators: Sudden, sustained high CPU/GPU utilization tied to browser activity with no corresponding user action
Browser network connections to known mining-pool domains/IPs
Fan noise/thermal alerts and battery drain reported by end users
Web/proxy logs showing injected mining-script domains on a visited page
vectors: Compromise of a legitimate website to inject a mining script
Malvertising network serving a mining payload
Malicious or trojanized browser extension
rootCauses: Unpatched CMS/plugin vulnerabilities on a compromised website
Lack of web-content filtering/blocking for known mining-pool domains
Absence of browser extension allowlisting
controls: Web/proxy filtering blocking known mining-pool domains and scripts
Browser extension allowlisting
Endpoint CPU-usage anomaly monitoring
ITID-53241.detection: Strong — mining-pool domain connections and sustained anomalous CPU usage tied to browser processes are readily detectable via web proxy logs and endpoint monitoring.
ITID-53241.response: Block the mining-pool domain/script at the web proxy, notify affected users to close the browser tab/session, and if a company-owned site is the source, remediate the underlying website compromise.
metrics: Number of drive-by mining events blocked at the proxy
Mean time to detect and remediate a compromised hosting site
ITID-53241.notes: Fully technical leaf with a direct ATT&CK mapping (T1189 for delivery, T1496 for the resource-theft impact); distinguished from the cloud-instance and worm-propagation siblings by its transient, browser-session-scoped nature with no persistence mechanism.

playbook.name: Browser-Based Cryptojacking Script (Drive-By Mining)
playbook.description: A malicious script embedded in a compromised or malicious website silently hijacks visitors' browser CPU resources on company workstations to mine cryptocurrency.

steps.title: Detect abnormal CPU/browser resource consumption
