steps.desc: Identify endpoints exhibiting sustained high CPU usage tied to browser processes, fan noise/thermal complaints, or EDR alerts for known cryptomining JavaScript signatures.
steps.guidance: Review EDR/endpoint telemetry for browser processes with sustained near-100% CPU utilization and correlate with recently visited URLs.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints and the responsible malicious site/script identified.
steps.abort: If high CPU usage is attributable to legitimate workload, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify the malicious site/domain and scope affected users
steps.desc: Determine the malicious or compromised website serving the mining script and identify all users/endpoints that visited it during the exposure window.
steps.guidance: Use proxy/web-gateway logs to identify all visitors to the malicious URL within the relevant time window.
steps.outcome: Full list of affected endpoints/users and the malicious domain documented.

steps.title: Block the malicious domain at the web gateway/DNS layer
steps.desc: Immediately block the identified malicious domain and any associated mining-pool endpoints at the proxy/DNS/firewall layer to stop the script from executing.
steps.guidance: Add the domain and associated mining-pool IPs to the web gateway and DNS-sinkhole blocklists.
steps.outcome: Malicious domain blocked; no further script execution from affected endpoints.

steps.title: Close affected browser sessions/tabs on impacted endpoints
steps.desc: Direct affected users (or remotely terminate) the browser tab/process running the mining script to immediately stop resource consumption.
steps.guidance: Provide simple end-user instructions or push a remote command via endpoint-management tooling to close the offending process.
steps.outcome: CPU utilization on affected endpoints returns to baseline.

steps.title: Clear browser cache/extensions and verify no persistence
steps.desc: Clear the browser cache and review installed extensions on affected endpoints for any malicious browser extension that may re-inject the mining script.
steps.guidance: Scan for and remove any unauthorized browser extensions; run a full endpoint malware scan to rule out a dropped persistent payload.
steps.outcome: Browser state clean with no malicious extensions or persistence confirmed.

steps.title: Deploy browser-level mining-script blocking fleet-wide
steps.desc: Deploy a browser extension policy or ad/script-blocking rule fleet-wide to prevent cryptomining scripts from executing on other endpoints.
steps.guidance: Push a managed browser policy (e.g., extension allowlist, script-blocking list) via endpoint management.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide browser-level mining-script protection deployed.

steps.title: Restore normal browsing and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Confirm affected endpoints are back to normal performance and monitor web-gateway logs for renewed attempts to reach the malicious domain or related infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Maintain the domain block and monitor for a defined period post-incident.
steps.outcome: Endpoints operating normally with no renewed contact to malicious infrastructure.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen web-filtering controls
steps.desc: Record the malicious domain, affected user count, and remediation; evaluate broader web-filtering/ad-blocking policy and cryptomining-script detection signatures.
steps.guidance: Brief IT security leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53242.def: Deployment of persistent cryptocurrency-mining software onto company-owned cloud compute instances (VMs, containers, serverless functions) by an adversary who obtained access via stolen cloud API keys/credentials, exposed management consoles, or misconfigured resources, generating unauthorized compute cost and potentially degrading legitimate workloads.
ITID-53242.purpose: Captures cryptomining malware deployed onto compromised cloud compute resources, typically enabled by stolen or exposed cloud credentials, resulting in direct billing/cost impact to the company.
scopeIncludes: Mining malware installed on a compromised cloud VM or container using stolen/leaked cloud credentials
Adversary spinning up new, attacker-controlled cloud instances under the company's account specifically to mine
Exposed cloud API keys (e.g., committed to a public code repository) leading to mining deployment
scopeExcludes: Transient browser-based mining scripts (ITID-53241)
Self-propagating mining worm spreading across the internal network (ITID-53243)
ITID-53242.severity: Medium to High — direct, often substantial, unplanned cloud billing impact, and the underlying credential compromise may indicate broader cloud environment exposure beyond just mining.
ITID-53242.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the compromised credentials also have access to production data or broader account-level control (billing admin, IAM management).
ITID-53242.escalation: Escalate to Cloud/Platform engineering to revoke compromised credentials and terminate rogue instances immediately, and to Finance regarding unexpected billing spikes; escalate to the SOC for full credential-compromise investigation.
indicators: Sudden, unexplained spike in cloud compute billing/usage
New, unrecognized compute instances or regions active in the cloud account
Outbound connections from cloud instances to known mining-pool domains
Leaked cloud API key or access key found in a public repository or logs
vectors: Cloud credentials leaked in source code, config files, or public repositories
Exploitation of an exposed/misconfigured cloud management console or API
Compromise of a CI/CD pipeline with cloud deployment permissions
rootCauses: Cloud credentials hard-coded or committed to source control
Overly permissive IAM roles allowing instance creation with no anomaly alerting
No billing-anomaly alerting configured on the cloud account
controls: Cloud billing-anomaly alerting
Secrets-scanning on source repositories to catch leaked cloud credentials
Least-privilege IAM policies restricting instance-creation permissions
Cloud-native workload protection detecting mining processes
ITID-53242.detection: Strong — cloud billing anomalies, unrecognized instance creation, and outbound mining-pool connections are all readily detectable via cloud-provider monitoring and CSPM/CWPP tooling.
ITID-53242.response: Revoke the compromised credentials immediately, terminate rogue instances, rotate all potentially exposed secrets, and investigate the credential-leak source to prevent recurrence.
metrics: Unauthorized cloud compute cost incurred
Time from instance creation to detection/termination
Number of leaked-credential incidents identified via secrets scanning
ITID-53242.notes: Distinguished from the browser-based leaf by persistence and financial-impact mechanism (direct cloud billing cost) and by requiring a genuine credential-compromise access vector, hence the added T1078 mapping alongside T1496.

playbook.name: Cryptojacking Malware Deployed on Compromised Cloud Compute Instances
playbook.description: An attacker who has gained unauthorized access to cloud compute instances deploys cryptomining malware, driving up cloud compute costs and consuming resources.

steps.title: Detect abnormal cloud compute usage and billing anomalies
steps.desc: Identify unexpected spikes in cloud compute/GPU usage, billing-alert triggers, or unusual outbound connections to known mining-pool endpoints.
steps.guidance: Review cloud cost-anomaly alerts, CPU/GPU utilization dashboards, and network flow logs for connections to known mining-pool IPs/ports.
steps.outcome: Affected cloud instances identified with confirmed cryptomining activity and cost impact quantified.
steps.abort: If usage is attributable to legitimate workload scaling, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the initial access vector into the cloud environment
steps.desc: Investigate how the attacker gained access to deploy the mining malware — exposed credentials, misconfigured security group, vulnerable exposed service, or compromised CI/CD pipeline.
steps.guidance: Review cloud provider access logs (e.g., CloudTrail/Activity Log), IAM key usage, and recent configuration changes to the affected instances.
steps.outcome: Initial access vector identified to guide eradication.

steps.title: Isolate or terminate the compromised instances
steps.desc: Immediately isolate affected instances via security-group/network-ACL restriction or terminate/snapshot them to stop further resource consumption and lateral movement.
steps.guidance: Snapshot the instance disk for forensic preservation before termination where feasible; isolate rather than destroy if investigation requires live analysis.
steps.outcome: Compromised instances isolated or terminated with mining activity stopped.

steps.title: Revoke compromised credentials and rotate cloud access keys
steps.desc: Revoke and rotate any IAM credentials, API keys, or service-account tokens implicated in the initial access, and disable any attacker-created IAM users/roles.
steps.guidance: Audit for attacker-persistence artifacts such as newly created IAM users, access keys, or privilege-escalation grants.
steps.outcome: Compromised credentials revoked and attacker-created access removed.

steps.title: Rebuild affected instances from known-good images
steps.desc: Rebuild/redeploy affected compute instances from a clean, verified image rather than attempting to clean an infected running instance.
steps.guidance: Use infrastructure-as-code pipelines to redeploy from a trusted base image and confirm no malicious startup scripts or scheduled tasks persist.
steps.outcome: Affected workloads restored on clean, verified instances.

steps.title: Close the exploited misconfiguration or vulnerability
steps.desc: Remediate the specific misconfiguration, exposed credential, or vulnerability that enabled initial access.
steps.guidance: Apply security-group hardening, patch vulnerable services, and enforce least-privilege IAM policy changes as indicated by the investigation.
steps.outcome: Root-cause vulnerability closed and verified via re-scan.

steps.title: Validate cloud billing normalization and dispute excess charges
steps.desc: Confirm cloud compute usage/billing returns to baseline and pursue a billing credit/dispute with the cloud provider for the fraud-driven cost spike.
steps.guidance: Provide the provider's fraud/abuse team with the incident timeline and affected resource IDs to support a billing adjustment request.
steps.outcome: Billing normalized and credit/dispute request submitted or resolved.

steps.title: Document incident and harden cloud security posture
steps.desc: Record root cause, cost impact, and remediation; implement cloud-spend anomaly alerting and periodic IAM/security-group configuration reviews.
steps.guidance: Brief IT security and Finance/cloud-operations leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53243.def: Cryptomining malware engineered to self-propagate across internal network hosts by exploiting remotely accessible service vulnerabilities or weak authentication (e.g., exposed RDP/SMB, unpatched remote services), infecting successive machines automatically without further attacker interaction and deploying a mining payload on each.
ITID-53243.purpose: Captures self-propagating cryptomining malware that spreads laterally across the internal network by exploiting vulnerable or exposed services, distinguishing worm-driven spread from a single-host or cloud-instance compromise.
scopeIncludes: Mining worm exploiting an unpatched remote-service vulnerability to spread host-to-host
Mining payload dropped automatically following successful lateral exploitation
Rapid, multi-host infection pattern consistent with automated propagation rather than manual deployment
scopeExcludes: Single-host or single-cloud-instance mining deployment without self-propagation (ITID-53242)
Transient browser-based mining with no host infection (ITID-53241)
ITID-53243.severity: High — self-propagating malware on the internal network poses containment and scale risk beyond the direct resource-theft/billing impact, and the exploited vulnerability may also be usable for more damaging payloads.
ITID-53243.priority: P1 given the active-spread nature of a worm; treat as an ongoing outbreak requiring network segmentation response, not just a single-host cleanup.
ITID-53243.escalation: Escalate immediately to the SOC incident response team and network engineering for segmentation/isolation of affected network segments; escalate to leadership if the exploited vulnerability affects a large portion of the environment or a critical service.
indicators: Rapid, sequential infection of multiple hosts on the same network segment
Exploitation traffic against a known remote-service vulnerability (e.g., SMB, RDP) immediately preceding each new infection
High CPU utilization consistent with mining appearing across many hosts in a short window
Outbound connections to mining-pool domains from numerous internal hosts simultaneously
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched remote-service vulnerability (e.g., EternalBlue-class SMB flaws) for lateral spread
Weak or default credentials on exposed remote-access services enabling automated lateral movement
rootCauses: Unpatched, internet- or internally-exposed remote services
Flat internal network with insufficient segmentation limiting worm spread
Lack of egress filtering allowing mining-pool connections from arbitrary internal hosts
controls: Timely patching of internet- and internally-exposed remote services
Network segmentation limiting lateral spread between host groups
Egress filtering blocking mining-pool domains/IPs at the network boundary
EDR detection of mining-process behavior
ITID-53243.detection: Strong — the propagation pattern (rapid multi-host exploitation traffic followed by mining-pool connections) is well-suited to network IDS/IPS, EDR, and NDR detection.
ITID-53243.response: Isolate affected network segments to halt propagation, patch the exploited vulnerability across the environment, remove the mining payload from infected hosts, and validate no residual persistence remains before reconnecting segments.
metrics: Number of hosts infected during the outbreak
Time from first infection to containment
Patch compliance rate for the exploited vulnerability post-incident
ITID-53243.notes: Distinguished from the other cryptojacking siblings by its self-propagating, multi-host outbreak character, warranting a network-containment response rather than single-asset remediation.

playbook.name: Cryptojacking Worm Propagating Across Internal Network
playbook.description: Self-propagating cryptomining malware spreads laterally across internal network hosts, exploiting weak credentials or unpatched vulnerabilities to install miners fleet-wide.

steps.title: Detect the propagation pattern and scope affected hosts
steps.desc: Identify multiple hosts across the network exhibiting sustained high CPU/GPU usage and connections to mining-pool infrastructure, indicating worm-style propagation rather than an isolated infection.
steps.guidance: Correlate EDR alerts, network flow data, and SIEM detections across the environment to build a full list of infected hosts and the propagation timeline.
steps.outcome: Full scope of infected hosts and propagation vector (e.g., SMB exploit, weak RDP credentials, exposed service) documented.

steps.title: Identify the exploited vulnerability or credential weakness enabling spread
steps.desc: Determine the specific vulnerability, misconfiguration, or weak/default credential the worm exploits to move laterally.
steps.guidance: Analyze malware samples/IOCs and correlate against known exploited CVEs or credential-based lateral-movement techniques (e.g., pass-the-hash, weak RDP/SMB credentials).
steps.outcome: Exploited vulnerability/credential weakness identified with an IOC list for detection.

steps.title: Segment/isolate affected network segments to halt propagation
steps.desc: Immediately isolate infected hosts and, if propagation is active and widespread, apply network segmentation or disable the exploited service/port fleet-wide to halt further spread.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with network operations to apply emergency ACLs/segmentation; consider temporarily disabling SMB/RDP fleet-wide if that is the propagation vector.
steps.outcome: Worm propagation halted with no new infections after containment measures are applied.

steps.title: Force credential resets for exploited accounts fleet-wide
steps.desc: Reset passwords/credentials for any accounts identified as exploited or at risk of exploitation by the worm's credential-based propagation.
steps.guidance: Prioritize privileged and service accounts; enforce complexity requirements to prevent immediate re-exploitation.
steps.outcome: Exploited credentials reset with no further unauthorized lateral movement observed.

steps.title: Remove the miner and worm components from all infected hosts
steps.desc: Run EDR-driven remediation or reimage each confirmed-infected host to remove the mining payload, worm propagation module, and any persistence mechanisms.
steps.guidance: Prioritize reimaging over in-place cleanup for hosts with confirmed rootkit-level persistence; verify via EDR that removal is complete on each host.
steps.outcome: All infected hosts confirmed clean with no residual mining or worm processes.

steps.title: Patch the exploited vulnerability fleet-wide
steps.desc: Deploy the relevant security patch or configuration hardening across the fleet to close the vulnerability the worm exploited, preventing reinfection.
steps.guidance: Coordinate an emergency patch cycle and validate patch deployment via vulnerability re-scan.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability patched fleet-wide and confirmed via re-scan.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and monitor fleet-wide for recurrence
steps.desc: Lift emergency network segmentation once remediation is confirmed, restore normal host operations, and maintain heightened monitoring across the fleet for a defined period.
steps.guidance: Run a follow-up fleet-wide scan after a set interval to confirm no reinfection.
steps.outcome: Normal operations restored with confirmed absence of reinfection.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen network-hardening controls
steps.desc: Record the propagation vector, affected host count, and remediation; evaluate broader network segmentation, patch-cadence, and credential-hygiene improvements to prevent future worm-style spread.
steps.guidance: Brief IT security leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53244.def: An unclassified or general instance of unauthorized cryptocurrency-mining activity on company resources that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Cryptojacking leaf.
ITID-53244.purpose: Intake bucket for cryptojacking activity that does not yet fit the browser-based, cloud-instance, or worm-propagation patterns.
scopeIncludes: Mining activity detected without enough detail yet to determine browser-based, cloud, or worm-propagation origin
Novel or mixed-mechanism cryptojacking
scopeExcludes: Confirmed browser-based drive-by mining (ITID-53241)
Confirmed cloud-instance mining malware (ITID-53242)
Confirmed self-propagating mining worm (ITID-53243)
ITID-53244.severity: Medium, pending reclassification once the delivery/persistence mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53244.priority: P2 upon detection of anomalous resource usage, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53244.escalation: Escalate to the SOC for standard resource-hijacking triage regardless of final classification; escalate further per the confirmed mechanism once known.
indicators: Anomalous CPU/GPU utilization or mining-pool network connections with delivery mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial detection
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Mining-pool domain/IP blocklisting
Endpoint and cloud resource-usage anomaly monitoring
ITID-53244.detection: Resource-hijacking impact (T1496) is detectable regardless of delivery vector; treat delivery mechanism as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53244.response: Isolate the affected asset and block mining-pool connections immediately, then investigate to reclassify under a specific Cryptojacking leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53244.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; the T1496 mapping applies universally to cryptojacking regardless of delivery vector, so it is retained here pending more specific classification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cryptojacking
playbook.description: A cryptomining resource-abuse incident that does not fit the browser-based, cloud-instance, or network-worm patterns, requiring general cryptojacking triage and response.

steps.title: Detect abnormal resource consumption indicative of cryptomining
steps.desc: Identify the affected system(s) exhibiting sustained abnormal CPU/GPU usage or connections to known mining-pool infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Correlate EDR/endpoint telemetry and network flow logs for mining-pool connection signatures.
steps.outcome: Affected system(s) and cryptomining activity confirmed.
steps.abort: If usage is attributable to legitimate workload, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the deployment vector
steps.desc: Investigate how the mining payload was introduced onto the affected system(s) — malicious download, exploited service, insider action, or another vector.
steps.guidance: Review process-creation logs, recent downloads, and access logs for the affected system.
steps.outcome: Deployment vector identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected system and block mining-pool traffic
steps.desc: Isolate the affected host/instance from the network and block outbound traffic to identified mining-pool endpoints.
steps.guidance: Apply network isolation via EDR or firewall and add mining-pool IPs/domains to the blocklist.
steps.outcome: Affected system isolated with no further mining traffic.

steps.title: Suspend or restrict the exploited access pathway
steps.desc: Suspend the compromised credential, service, or access pathway that enabled the mining payload's deployment.
steps.guidance: Disable the specific account/service until the root cause is remediated.
steps.outcome: Exploited pathway suspended with no further unauthorized deployment possible.

steps.title: Remove the mining payload and confirm system integrity
steps.desc: Remove the cryptomining malware/script and any associated persistence mechanisms; reimage the system if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.guidance: Run a full malware scan and verify no residual mining processes or scheduled tasks remain.
steps.outcome: System confirmed clean of mining payload and persistence.

steps.title: Close the exploited deployment vector
steps.desc: Remediate the specific vulnerability, exposed credential, or process gap identified as the deployment vector to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Apply the appropriate patch, credential reset, or access-control tightening based on the identified vector.
steps.outcome: Deployment vector closed and verified.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Return the affected system to normal operation and monitor closely for renewed mining activity.
steps.guidance: Maintain heightened monitoring for a defined post-incident period.
steps.outcome: System restored to normal operation with no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document incident and update resource-abuse detection controls
steps.desc: Record root cause, resource/cost impact, and remediation; evaluate broader cryptomining-detection signature and monitoring improvements.
steps.guidance: Brief IT security leadership and track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53251.def: Unauthorized access to and control of an online banking account, obtained by an adversary through phishing (credential-harvesting) of the account holder's login credentials, followed by unauthorized transfers, bill payments, or account-control changes made directly through the compromised online banking session.
ITID-53251.purpose: Captures takeover of an online banking account resulting from stolen login credentials obtained via phishing, enabling unauthorized fund transfers or account changes.
scopeIncludes: Phished online-banking credentials used to log in and initiate unauthorized transfers or payments
Adversary adding a new payee or changing account notification settings after login
Credential-harvesting page impersonating the bank's login portal
scopeExcludes: Brokerage/investment account takeover (ITID-53252)
Card-only fraud not involving a full online banking account login (ITID-53221/53223)
ITID-53251.severity: High, given direct access to funds-transfer capability and potential exposure of full account/transaction history.
ITID-53251.priority: P1 while unauthorized transfers may still be in-flight or recoverable; P2 once the account is secured and losses are being quantified.
ITID-53251.escalation: Escalate immediately to the bank's fraud department to freeze the account and reverse transfers, and to the SOC for credential-compromise containment if the phished credentials are also used for or reused across company systems.
indicators: Login to online banking from an unrecognized device/location immediately followed by a transfer or payee addition
User report of receiving a bank-impersonating phishing email or SMS shortly before the fraud
Bank fraud-detection alert on the session/transaction
vectors: Phishing email or SMS (smishing) directing the victim to a fake bank login page
Man-in-the-middle phishing kit capturing credentials and MFA codes in real time
rootCauses: Lack of phishing-resistant MFA on the online banking account
User unable to distinguish a spoofed bank login page from the legitimate one
Password reuse enabling credential-stuffing follow-through
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO2/hardware token) on banking accounts
User security awareness training on banking-phishing patterns
Bank-side anomaly detection on login-then-transfer sequences
ITID-53251.detection: Moderate — the phishing delivery is detectable via email/SMS security tooling and user reporting; the account-takeover itself is primarily visible through the bank's own fraud-detection systems rather than internal SOC telemetry, unless the phished credential is company-managed.
ITID-53251.response: Freeze the account and reverse fraudulent transfers with the bank immediately, reset the compromised credential, and if the same password/MFA method is used elsewhere, force resets on those systems too.
metrics: Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
Time from phishing delivery to account compromise detection
Number of phishing-driven banking-takeover attempts reported by users
ITID-53251.notes: Differentiated from brokerage/investment account takeover by the target account type and typical fraud objective (immediate transfer-out vs. trade manipulation or slower-drain withdrawal).

playbook.name: Online Banking Account Takeover via Phished Credentials
playbook.description: An attacker uses credentials obtained through phishing to take over the company's online banking portal access and attempt unauthorized transactions.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized online banking access
steps.desc: Validate that the company's online banking portal was accessed by an unauthorized party using phished credentials, and identify any resulting unauthorized transactions or configuration changes.
steps.guidance: Review the bank's login history/audit trail for the corporate banking portal, cross-referenced against known legitimate user locations/devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access with login timeline and any resulting transaction/configuration-change detail documented.
steps.abort: If access matches legitimate authorized use, close as false positive.

steps.title: Trace the phishing vector and identify the compromised user
steps.desc: Identify the phishing email/site that harvested the credentials and confirm which employee(s) were compromised.
steps.guidance: Review email security gateway logs and interview the affected employee(s) to reconstruct the phishing timeline.
steps.outcome: Phishing vector and compromised employee(s) identified.

steps.title: Lock the banking portal account and notify the bank's fraud department
steps.desc: Immediately contact the bank to lock/suspend the compromised online banking credentials and notify their fraud department of the takeover.
steps.guidance: Request the bank freeze any pending transactions initiated during the unauthorized session and place enhanced monitoring on the account.
steps.outcome: Banking portal access locked and bank fraud team engaged.

steps.title: Reset the compromised employee's credentials and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Force a password reset and session revocation for the compromised employee's accounts (email and banking portal), and review for any other systems using the same credentials.
steps.guidance: Check for password reuse across other business-critical systems and reset those as well.
steps.outcome: Compromised credentials reset across all affected systems with no active attacker sessions.

steps.title: Reverse any unauthorized transactions and restore account configuration
steps.desc: Work with the bank to reverse any unauthorized transactions initiated during the compromise and restore legitimate account/payee configuration.
steps.guidance: Confirm with Treasury that all payees/settings match pre-incident authorized configuration.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized transactions reversed and account configuration restored.

steps.title: Enforce hardware-token or app-based MFA on banking portal access
steps.desc: Require strong, phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (hardware security key or authenticator app, not SMS) for all corporate banking portal users.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the bank to enable stronger MFA options and update the internal banking-access policy.
steps.outcome: Phishing-resistant MFA enforced for all banking portal users.

steps.title: Restore normal banking operations and confirm balance integrity
steps.desc: Confirm the account balance and configuration are fully restored and resume normal banking operations under the enhanced authentication controls.
steps.guidance: Reconcile Treasury records against the bank statement post-incident.
steps.outcome: Normal banking operations resumed with confirmed balance/configuration integrity.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen phishing-defense training
steps.desc: Record the phishing vector, financial impact, and remediation; update phishing-awareness training and simulate future phishing campaigns targeting Treasury/Finance staff.
steps.guidance: Brief IT security and Finance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53252.def: Unauthorized access to and control of a brokerage or investment account, obtained through credential theft, brute force, or MFA-fatigue attacks, enabling the adversary to liquidate holdings, execute unauthorized trades (including pump-and-dump-style manipulation using the victim's capital), or redirect withdrawal proceeds to an attacker-controlled account.
ITID-53252.purpose: Captures takeover of a brokerage or investment account, distinguishing the trade-manipulation and slower-liquidation fraud objectives typical of this account type from direct bank-transfer fraud.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized liquidation of securities holdings followed by withdrawal to an attacker-controlled bank account
Unauthorized trades placed to manipulate a thinly traded security's price using the compromised account's buying power
Credential-stuffing or brute-force attack against a brokerage account login
MFA-fatigue attack used to approve a withdrawal or account-change request
scopeExcludes: Online/retail banking account takeover (ITID-53251)
Securities/stock manipulation carried out by an insider using their own legitimate access and material non-public information (ITID-53441 branch, a distinct non-technical securities-fraud pattern)
ITID-53252.severity: High, given the potential for both direct fund loss and market-manipulation exposure using the victim's trading capacity.
ITID-53252.priority: P1 while a withdrawal or trade may still be reversible; P2 once the account is secured and the firm/broker is handling loss recovery.
ITID-53252.escalation: Escalate immediately to the brokerage's fraud/security team to freeze the account and halt pending withdrawals or trades, and to the SOC for credential-compromise containment if the account credential is shared with or derived from company-managed identities.
indicators: Login to the brokerage account from an unrecognized device/location followed by unusual trading activity or a withdrawal request
Repeated failed login or MFA-push attempts preceding the takeover
Trades placed in securities inconsistent with the account holder's normal investment pattern
Withdrawal request to a newly added, unfamiliar bank account
vectors: Credential stuffing using passwords reused from an unrelated breach
Brute-force login attempts against the brokerage portal
MFA-fatigue (repeated push notifications) to obtain approval for a withdrawal or account change
rootCauses: Password reuse across the brokerage account and other services
Absence of phishing-resistant MFA or a withdrawal-cooldown period on the brokerage account
No anomaly alerting on login-then-large-withdrawal sequences
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA and withdrawal-cooldown periods on brokerage accounts
Number-matching MFA to reduce fatigue-attack effectiveness
Anomaly alerting on login-then-large-withdrawal or unusual-trade sequences
ITID-53252.detection: Moderate — brute-force and MFA-fatigue patterns are detectable via authentication logging where the company has visibility; broader account-takeover monitoring is largely a brokerage-side fraud-detection function.
ITID-53252.response: Freeze the account and halt pending trades/withdrawals with the brokerage immediately, reset the compromised credential, and review for credential reuse across other systems.
metrics: Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
Time from compromise to detection
Number of MFA-fatigue attempts observed against relevant accounts
ITID-53252.notes: Distinguished from online banking takeover by the fraud objective (trade manipulation/liquidation vs. direct transfer) and carries the added T1621 mapping reflecting MFA-fatigue as a common brokerage-account takeover vector.

playbook.name: Brokerage/Investment Account Takeover
playbook.description: An attacker gains unauthorized access to the company's brokerage or investment account and attempts unauthorized trades, transfers, or withdrawals.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized brokerage account access
steps.desc: Validate that the company's brokerage/investment account was accessed without authorization and identify any resulting unauthorized trades, wire transfers, or withdrawal requests.
steps.guidance: Review the brokerage platform's login/audit history and cross-reference against known authorized users' locations and devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access with a documented timeline of any unauthorized trades/transfers.
steps.abort: If access matches authorized use, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the takeover vector
steps.desc: Identify how account access was compromised — phishing, credential stuffing, SIM-swap, or malware on the authorized user's device.
steps.guidance: Review login anomalies, MFA-bypass indicators, and check for known credential-exposure sources.
steps.outcome: Takeover vector identified.

steps.title: Lock the account and notify the brokerage's fraud department
steps.desc: Immediately contact the brokerage firm to freeze the account and notify their fraud/security team of the unauthorized access.
steps.guidance: Request the brokerage halt any pending trades/transfers and place a temporary hold on withdrawal capability.
steps.outcome: Account frozen and brokerage fraud team engaged.

steps.title: Reset compromised credentials and revoke active sessions
steps.desc: Force a credential reset and revoke all active sessions for the compromised account, checking for password reuse on other financial platforms.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT security to reset credentials across any systems sharing the compromised password.
steps.outcome: Compromised credentials reset with no active unauthorized sessions.

steps.title: Reverse unauthorized trades/transfers and restore holdings
steps.desc: Work with the brokerage firm to reverse or unwind any unauthorized trades and recover any transferred/withdrawn funds where possible.
steps.guidance: File a formal dispute with the brokerage's fraud department detailing each unauthorized transaction.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized trades reversed and holdings restored to pre-incident state where recoverable.

steps.title: Enforce strong MFA and withdrawal-verification controls
steps.desc: Require phishing-resistant MFA and a callback-verification step for any withdrawal or external transfer request on the account.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the brokerage to enable available account-protection features (e.g., trusted-device requirements, transfer delays).
steps.outcome: Enhanced authentication and withdrawal-verification controls active.

steps.title: Restore normal account operations and confirm holdings integrity
steps.desc: Confirm account holdings and configuration are fully restored and resume normal operations under enhanced controls.
steps.guidance: Reconcile investment records against the brokerage statement post-incident.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with confirmed holdings integrity.

steps.title: Document incident and update financial-account security policy
steps.desc: Record the takeover vector, financial impact, and remediation; update policy on brokerage/investment account access controls and monitoring.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance and IT security leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53253.def: An unclassified or general instance of financial account takeover that has not yet been attributed to a specific account type or mechanism covered by another Financial Account Takeover leaf.
ITID-53253.purpose: Intake bucket for financial account takeover incidents that do not yet fit the online-banking or brokerage/investment patterns.
scopeIncludes: Account takeover reported without enough detail to determine banking vs. brokerage account type or entry mechanism
Takeover of a financial account type not otherwise covered (e.g., digital wallet, payment app)
scopeExcludes: Confirmed online banking account takeover via phished credentials (ITID-53251)
Confirmed brokerage/investment account takeover (ITID-53252)
ITID-53253.severity: High, consistent with other account-takeover leaves, pending reclassification.
ITID-53253.priority: P1 while funds/assets may still be recoverable, reassessed once the account type and mechanism are confirmed.
ITID-53253.escalation: Escalate to the relevant financial institution's fraud team immediately, and to the SOC for standard account-compromise containment if company-managed credentials are involved.
indicators: Unauthorized login and financial activity reported on an account without a clearly identified type or entry mechanism
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard account-takeover containment controls (credential reset, MFA enforcement) applicable to all financial accounts
ITID-53253.detection: Varies by underlying account type and entry mechanism; treat as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53253.response: Apply standard account-freeze and credential-reset response immediately, then investigate to reclassify under a specific Financial Account Takeover leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53253.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify to a specific Financial Account Takeover leaf as soon as sufficient detail is available.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Financial Account Takeover
playbook.description: A financial account takeover incident that does not fit the online-banking or brokerage-specific patterns, requiring general account-takeover triage and response.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized access to the financial account
steps.desc: Validate that the affected financial account was accessed without authorization and identify any resulting unauthorized transactions or configuration changes.
steps.guidance: Review the account provider's login/audit history and cross-reference against known authorized users' patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access with documented transaction/configuration-change detail.
steps.abort: If access matches authorized use, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the takeover vector
steps.desc: Identify how the account was compromised — phishing, credential stuffing, malware, or another mechanism.
steps.guidance: Review login anomalies and available authentication logs for the affected account.
steps.outcome: Takeover vector identified.

steps.title: Lock the account and notify the provider's fraud department
steps.desc: Immediately contact the financial institution/provider to freeze the account and notify their fraud team of the unauthorized access.
steps.guidance: Request the provider halt any pending transactions and place enhanced monitoring on the account.
steps.outcome: Account frozen and provider fraud team engaged.

steps.title: Reset compromised credentials and revoke active sessions
steps.desc: Force a credential reset and revoke all active sessions for the compromised account.
steps.guidance: Check for password reuse across other systems and reset as needed.
steps.outcome: Compromised credentials reset with no active unauthorized sessions.

steps.title: Reverse unauthorized transactions and restore account configuration
steps.desc: Work with the provider to reverse unauthorized transactions and restore legitimate account configuration.
steps.guidance: File formal disputes for each unauthorized transaction identified.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized transactions reversed and configuration restored.

steps.title: Enforce strong MFA on the recovered account
steps.desc: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication and review recovery-method settings on the account before returning it to normal use.
steps.guidance: Confirm no attacker-controlled recovery email/phone remains attached to the account.
steps.outcome: Strong MFA enforced and recovery settings verified clean.

steps.title: Restore normal account operations under enhanced controls
steps.desc: Confirm account integrity is restored and resume normal operations under enhanced authentication controls.
steps.guidance: Reconcile financial records against the provider's statement post-incident.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with confirmed account integrity.

steps.title: Document incident and update account-takeover response procedures
steps.desc: Record the takeover vector, financial impact, and remediation; update the general financial-account-takeover response procedure.
steps.guidance: Brief Finance and IT security leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53311.def: Establishment of a fake or fictitious vendor record within the company's procurement or accounts-payable system — often by a colluding or malicious insider, or through inadequate vendor-vetting — used to generate and approve payments for goods or services that were never actually provided.
ITID-53311.purpose: Captures fraud in which a fictitious vendor is set up in the procurement/accounts-payable system to enable fraudulent payments, framed as a process/vetting control failure rather than an email-compromise incident.
scopeIncludes: Insider (AP clerk, procurement staff) creating a fake vendor record to divert payments to a controlled account
Fictitious vendor onboarded due to inadequate due diligence, later found to have no legitimate business operations
Collusion between an employee and an external party to establish and pay a fake vendor
scopeExcludes: Vendor fraud where the deception is delivered specifically via a compromised or spoofed vendor email thread (a BEC mechanism covered under the Vendor Invoice Fraud branch, ITID-53120, and Fraudulent Disbursement, ITID-53622)
Shell vendor created specifically to enable invoice padding/overbilling by an otherwise legitimate vendor relationship (ITID-53323)
ITID-53311.severity: Medium to High, scaled by the cumulative dollar value paid to the fake vendor before detection and whether an insider with approval authority is involved.
ITID-53311.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if an employee with financial-approval authority is confirmed complicit.
ITID-53311.escalation: Escalate to Internal Audit and Finance leadership for a full vendor-master review, and to HR/Legal if employee collusion is suspected; SOC involvement is typically limited to supporting evidence preservation (system access logs) rather than technical containment.
indicators: Vendor record with missing/inconsistent business registration, tax ID, or address details
Vendor bank account matching an employee's personal account details
Payments approved by the same individual who created the vendor record with no independent review
No verifiable deliverable, service, or physical presence associated with the vendor
vectors: Insider abuse of vendor-master-file creation privileges
Inadequate or bypassed vendor-vetting/due-diligence process
Collusion between an internal approver and an external accomplice
rootCauses: Lack of segregation of duties between vendor creation and payment approval
No periodic vendor-master-file audit for duplicate/matching bank details against employee records
Insufficient vendor onboarding due diligence
controls: Segregation of duties between vendor creation, invoice approval, and payment disbursement
Periodic vendor-master-file audit cross-referencing vendor bank details against employee payroll bank details
Vendor onboarding due-diligence verification (business registration, tax ID, site visit for high-value vendors)
ITID-53311.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — this is an internal-controls and fraud-operations pattern; detection relies on internal audit, vendor-master analytics, and AP reconciliation rather than SOC technical monitoring, unless collusion is later found to involve a BEC-style email compromise, in which case that separate compromise should also be logged under the appropriate BEC leaf.
ITID-53311.response: Suspend payments to the vendor immediately, engage Internal Audit for a full review of all payments made, and refer to HR/Legal for any confirmed insider involvement.
metrics: Number of fake-vendor records identified per audit cycle
Cumulative dollar amount paid before detection
Time from vendor onboarding to fraud detection
ITID-53311.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls. This leaf is scoped to non-email-compromise fake-vendor setup (insider/vetting-failure mechanism); genuinely BEC-driven fake-vendor payment fraud is covered by the dedicated Vendor Invoice Fraud (ITID-53120) and Fraudulent Disbursement (ITID-53622) leaves to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Fake Vendor Fraud (Procurement Context)
playbook.description: A fictitious vendor is set up in the procurement system — either by an external actor or a complicit/rogue employee — and paid for goods or services never actually delivered.

steps.title: Flag the suspect vendor and pull its full transaction history
steps.desc: Identify the vendor record in question and export all associated purchase orders, invoices, and payments from the ERP/procurement system.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit before taking any visible action that could alert an internal party.
steps.outcome: Complete transaction history assembled for review.

steps.title: Verify vendor legitimacy
steps.desc: Check the vendor's registered business existence (business registry, tax ID, physical address, phone number) and compare its bank account and address against employee records for overlap.
steps.guidance: A shared address/bank account/phone number with an employee is a strong indicator of a fictitious or self-controlled vendor.
steps.outcome: Determined whether the vendor is fictitious, and whether any employee is linked to it.
steps.abort: If the vendor is verified legitimate with a documented service history, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before any confrontation
steps.desc: Work with Internal Audit/Legal to preserve system logs, approval records, and communications related to the vendor before any internal party is confronted, to avoid evidence destruction.
steps.guidance: Follow the organization's evidence-preservation protocol for suspected internal fraud; restrict system access changes until evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved in a defensible, chain-of-custody manner.

steps.title: Suspend the vendor record and hold pending payments
steps.desc: Place the vendor record on payment hold in the ERP system and suspend any pending or scheduled payments.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AP leadership; make the hold as quiet as possible if an internal actor may still have system access.
steps.outcome: No further payments issued to the fraudulent vendor.

steps.title: Restrict system access for implicated employee(s)
steps.desc: If an employee is implicated in creating or approving the fake vendor, coordinate with HR/Legal/IT to restrict their procurement-system access pending investigation, without tipping off other potential co-conspirators prematurely.
steps.guidance: This must be coordinated with HR and Legal — do not act unilaterally on access removal for a potential personnel case.
steps.outcome: Access restricted appropriately without compromising the investigation.

steps.title: Conduct forensic accounting review and quantify loss
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting (internal or external) to quantify total losses and confirm the full scope of fraudulent transactions.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit and Legal on scope and methodology.
steps.outcome: Documented loss quantification supporting recovery and any legal action.

steps.title: Harden vendor-onboarding verification controls
steps.desc: Update vendor-onboarding procedures to require independent verification of business registration, tax ID, and bank details, and to screen for address/bank overlap with employee records.
steps.guidance: Work with Procurement leadership to implement segregation of duties between vendor creation and approval.
steps.outcome: Documented control improvements reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Pursue recovery and determine referral for criminal/civil action
steps.desc: Work with Legal to pursue recovery of misappropriated funds and determine whether the matter warrants law-enforcement or civil referral.
steps.guidance: Legal and HR to jointly decide on employee disciplinary action and any external referral.
steps.outcome: Recovery and referral path determined and initiated.

steps.title: Document findings and update procurement controls
steps.desc: Finalize the investigation report with Internal Audit and Legal, and communicate control improvements to Procurement and Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Investigation closed with documented findings and control updates.

ITID-53321.def: Overbilling by an otherwise legitimate, real vendor who submits invoices reflecting inflated quantities of goods delivered, hours worked, or units of service performed relative to what was actually provided, resulting in the company paying for work or materials it did not receive.
ITID-53321.purpose: Captures fraud by a legitimate vendor who inflates billed quantities, hours, or units beyond what was actually delivered or performed.
scopeIncludes: Contractor invoicing more labor hours than were actually worked
Vendor invoicing for a greater quantity of goods than actually delivered
Time-and-materials billing inflated relative to project scope/completion evidence
scopeExcludes: Submission of the same invoice more than once (ITID-53322)
Billing from an entirely fictitious vendor/shell company (ITID-53323)
ITID-53321.severity: Medium, scaled by the cumulative overbilled amount and whether the pattern is isolated or systemic across multiple invoices/projects.
ITID-53321.priority: P3 for an isolated discrepancy; P2 if a sustained pattern across multiple invoices from the same vendor is identified.
ITID-53321.escalation: Escalate to Procurement/Finance for invoice-vs-delivery reconciliation and vendor dispute, and to Internal Audit if the pattern suggests systemic or long-running overbilling.
indicators: Invoiced quantities/hours exceeding delivery receipts, timesheets, or purchase-order terms
Recurring rounding-up patterns in billed hours across multiple invoices
Discrepancy between vendor-reported and internally tracked project completion status
vectors: Vendor unilaterally inflating invoiced quantities/hours with no independent verification
Collusion between the vendor and an internal approver to accept inflated invoices without scrutiny
rootCauses: No three-way match (purchase order, receipt/delivery confirmation, invoice) before payment
Insufficient independent verification of contractor hours/deliverables
Approval authority concentrated with no secondary review for high-value invoices
controls: Three-way match (PO, goods receipt, invoice) enforcement before payment
Independent verification of contractor hours against timesheets/project logs
Periodic vendor billing audit
ITID-53321.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection relies on internal audit and finance controls (three-way matching, billing audits) rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53321.response: Withhold payment pending reconciliation, dispute the overbilled amount with the vendor, and refer to Internal Audit if a systemic pattern is found.
metrics: Cumulative overbilled dollar amount identified per audit cycle
Number of invoices failing three-way match review
ITID-53321.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls.

playbook.name: Vendor Overbilling via Inflated Quantities/Hours
playbook.description: A vendor (potentially in collusion with an internal employee who approves the invoices) systematically inflates billed quantities, hours, or units above what was actually delivered.

steps.title: Pull invoice history and compare against delivery/time records
steps.desc: Export the vendor's invoice history alongside receiving records, timesheets, or delivery confirmations for the same period.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit; involve the business owner who receives the goods/services if not implicated.
steps.outcome: Dataset assembled for quantitative comparison of billed vs. delivered amounts.

steps.title: Quantify the discrepancy pattern
steps.desc: Analyze the data for a consistent pattern of overbilling (e.g. hours billed exceeding badge/timesheet records, quantities exceeding receiving confirmations).
steps.guidance: Use forensic-accounting or data-analytics support to identify statistically significant discrepancy patterns rather than isolated errors.
steps.outcome: Documented pattern and estimated financial impact.
steps.abort: If discrepancies are isolated and explainable as clerical error, close as non-fraud with a note to the vendor.

steps.title: Identify any internal approver involvement
steps.desc: Review who approved the inflated invoices and whether there is any indication of collusion (e.g. unusually fast approvals, lack of scrutiny, personal relationship with the vendor).
steps.guidance: Preserve approval-workflow logs before any confrontation.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this is vendor-only fraud or involves internal collusion.

steps.title: Hold future payments and require re-verification of pending invoices
steps.desc: Place the vendor's pending and future invoices on hold pending independent re-verification of quantities/hours against source records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AP and the receiving department for re-verification.
steps.outcome: No further inflated invoices paid without verification.

steps.title: Restrict implicated approver's authority pending review
steps.desc: If internal collusion is suspected, coordinate with HR/Legal to temporarily limit the implicated employee's invoice-approval authority.
steps.guidance: Do this discreetly and only with HR/Legal sign-off to avoid prejudicing an ongoing investigation.
steps.outcome: Approval authority restricted without tipping off the implicated employee prematurely.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting quantification of overbilled amounts
steps.desc: Finalize the forensic review to quantify total overbilled amounts across the full vendor relationship history.
steps.outcome: Documented, defensible loss figure for recovery/legal purposes.

steps.title: Enforce three-way-match and independent quantity verification
steps.desc: Implement or tighten three-way-match controls (PO, receipt, invoice) and require independent quantity/hours verification against source records before invoice approval.
steps.guidance: Work with Procurement and AP leadership to close the control gap.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Recover overpayments and determine vendor/employee action
steps.desc: Work with Legal to recover overpaid amounts from the vendor (credit, refund, or legal action) and determine appropriate action against any implicated employee.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued; personnel/vendor action determined.

steps.title: Document findings and communicate control changes
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate the strengthened three-way-match controls to Procurement, AP, and receiving teams.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented control updates.

ITID-53322.def: Submission of the same invoice — or an invoice with only superficial changes such as a slightly altered invoice number or date — more than once for payment, resulting in the company paying twice for a single delivered good or service.
ITID-53322.purpose: Captures fraud from a vendor (or an internal accomplice) submitting the same invoice multiple times, or with only minor cosmetic changes, to obtain duplicate payment.
scopeIncludes: Identical invoice resubmitted under a different invoice number
Duplicate invoice submitted to two different approvers or departments to bypass duplicate-detection controls
Internal AP staff intentionally reprocessing a legitimate invoice for a second payment to a colluding vendor
scopeExcludes: Invoices inflating quantities/hours for a single legitimate delivery (ITID-53321)
Billing from a wholly fictitious vendor (ITID-53323)
ITID-53322.severity: Low to Medium per instance, escalating to Medium-High if duplicate payments recur systemically across many vendors (indicating a control failure rather than an isolated error/fraud).
ITID-53322.priority: P3 for an isolated duplicate payment; P2 if a recurring pattern across multiple vendors or invoices is identified.
ITID-53322.escalation: Escalate to Finance/AP for recovery of the duplicate payment and to Internal Audit if the pattern suggests deliberate fraud rather than a system error.
indicators: Duplicate invoice-number or duplicate-amount alert from the AP system
Same vendor, amount, and date range paid twice within a short window
Invoice resubmitted with a cosmetically altered invoice number but identical line items
vectors: Deliberate resubmission of a paid invoice with a superficial change to bypass duplicate-detection matching
Collusion between a vendor and internal AP staff to reprocess a payment
rootCauses: Weak or absent duplicate-invoice detection logic in the AP system
Manual invoice processing without automated cross-referencing against payment history
Lack of segregation of duties allowing one individual to both submit and approve a resubmission
controls: Automated duplicate-invoice detection (vendor, amount, date, line-item matching) in the AP system
Segregation of duties between invoice entry and payment approval
Periodic duplicate-payment audit
ITID-53322.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection is an AP-system and internal-audit function based on duplicate-matching analytics.
ITID-53322.response: Recover the duplicate payment from the vendor or reverse the internal entry, and if intentional fraud is confirmed, refer to Internal Audit/Legal.
metrics: Number and dollar value of duplicate payments identified and recovered per period
Duplicate-detection system catch rate
ITID-53322.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls.

playbook.name: Duplicate Invoice Submission Fraud
playbook.description: A vendor, or an internal employee manipulating the AP system, submits the same invoice more than once (with minor alterations to invoice numbers or dates) to obtain duplicate payment.

steps.title: Run duplicate-payment detection analysis
steps.desc: Run a data-analytics query across AP records to identify invoices with matching amounts, vendors, and near-duplicate invoice numbers/dates.
steps.guidance: Use fuzzy matching to catch minor invoice-number alterations designed to evade exact-duplicate checks.
steps.outcome: List of candidate duplicate-payment transactions.

steps.title: Confirm duplicate payments and identify responsible party
steps.desc: Manually verify each candidate to confirm actual duplicate payment occurred, and review who submitted/approved each instance for signs of intentional manipulation vs. system error.
steps.guidance: Check for a pattern of the same submitter/approver across multiple duplicates as an indicator of intent.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of fraudulent duplicate payments with responsible parties identified.
steps.abort: If duplicates are attributable to a system/process error with no intent, close as a control-gap finding rather than fraud.

steps.title: Freeze the vendor account and hold related pending invoices
steps.desc: Place a payment hold on the implicated vendor account and any pending invoices matching the pattern.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AP leadership.
steps.outcome: No further duplicate payments processed.

steps.title: Restrict implicated employee's AP system access if internal
steps.desc: If an internal employee intentionally engineered the duplicates, coordinate with HR/Legal to restrict their AP system access pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Access restricted without disrupting legitimate AP operations.

steps.title: Implement system-enforced duplicate-invoice controls
steps.desc: Configure the AP system to flag or block near-duplicate invoices (same vendor/amount within a date range) rather than relying on exact invoice-number matching.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT/ERP administrators to tune duplicate-detection logic.
steps.outcome: System control in place to catch this pattern automatically going forward.

steps.title: Run org-wide retrospective duplicate-payment sweep
steps.desc: Run the enhanced duplicate-detection logic retrospectively across all vendors and prior periods to identify any other undetected duplicate payments.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit to scope the retrospective sweep.
steps.outcome: Any additional duplicate payments identified and queued for recovery.

steps.title: Recover duplicate payments
steps.desc: Recover the duplicate payment amounts from the vendor (offset against future invoices or direct refund) and, if internal, coordinate with HR/Legal on repayment and disciplinary action.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered; disciplinary/legal path determined.

steps.title: Document findings and update AP procedures
steps.desc: Document the investigation and communicate the enhanced duplicate-detection control to AP staff.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented control update.

ITID-53323.def: Establishment of a shell vendor entity — a business with no real operations, employees, or delivered goods/services — within the vendor master file for the sole purpose of submitting and collecting payment on fictitious invoices, typically perpetrated or enabled by an employee with vendor-management or approval authority.
ITID-53323.purpose: Captures fraud in which a shell company with no genuine goods or services is created and inserted into the vendor master specifically to generate and collect fictitious billing.
scopeIncludes: Vendor entity with no verifiable business operations submitting invoices for goods/services never delivered
Employee-created or employee-controlled shell company used to funnel company funds
Invoices from a shell vendor approved by an employee with no independent verification of delivery
scopeExcludes: A legitimate, operating vendor that overbills quantities/hours for real delivered work (ITID-53321)
General fake-vendor setup covered as a broader procurement-fraud catch-all leaf (ITID-53311) where the vendor is not necessarily a fully fabricated shell but a vetting-failure case
ITID-53323.severity: High, given the total loss is typically the full invoiced amount with zero legitimate value received, and shell-vendor schemes often run undetected for extended periods.
ITID-53323.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if an employee with significant approval authority is confirmed as the perpetrator or beneficiary.
ITID-53323.escalation: Escalate immediately to Internal Audit and Legal for a full investigation and potential law-enforcement referral, and to HR for personnel action against any confirmed employee involvement.
indicators: Vendor with no verifiable physical address, website, employees, or business registration
Vendor bank account traceable to an employee or their associate
Invoices with vague or generic service descriptions and no supporting deliverables
Single-approver control over both vendor onboarding and invoice approval for this vendor
vectors: Insider creating and controlling a shell company to bill the employer
Collusion between an employee approver and an external accomplice operating the shell entity
rootCauses: Lack of segregation of duties between vendor onboarding, invoice approval, and payment disbursement
No periodic vendor-master audit for shell-company red flags (address, registration, bank-account matching)
Insufficient scrutiny of vague service-description invoices
controls: Segregation of duties across vendor onboarding, approval, and payment
Vendor-master audit for shell-company indicators (registration, address, bank-account cross-matching against employees)
Independent verification of deliverables before payment approval
ITID-53323.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection is an internal-audit and fraud-operations function.
ITID-53323.response: Suspend all payments to the vendor immediately, conduct a full historical payment review with Internal Audit, and refer confirmed cases to Legal and law enforcement.
metrics: Cumulative dollar amount paid to shell vendors before detection
Number of shell-vendor schemes identified per audit cycle
ITID-53323.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls. Distinguished from ITID-53311 by the total fabrication of the vendor entity rather than a vetting-failure on an otherwise real party.

playbook.name: Shell Vendor Created for Fictitious Billing
playbook.description: An internal employee creates a wholly fictitious vendor (a shell company, often with a bank account they control) in the procurement system and generates invoices for goods or services that were never delivered.

steps.title: Identify the suspect vendor and preserve system records
steps.desc: Identify the vendor record and immediately preserve all related system logs (creation, edits, approvals) and communications before any internal party is aware of the review.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit and Legal from the outset given the likelihood of a personnel/criminal case.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Verify the vendor's non-existence and trace to the creating employee
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has no legitimate business registration, and trace who created and approved the vendor record and its invoices in the system.
steps.guidance: Check for shared bank account, address, phone number, or IP address between the vendor record and any employee.
steps.outcome: Confirmed shell vendor and identified the employee(s) who created/benefited from it.
steps.tool: Business registry lookup / ERP audit trail

steps.title: Engage forensic accounting for full scope assessment
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting to determine the full scope and duration of fictitious billing and total funds diverted.
steps.outcome: Documented scope and loss estimate.

steps.title: Suspend vendor record and freeze implicated employee's system access
steps.desc: Suspend the vendor record to block further payments, and coordinate with HR/Legal/IT to freeze the implicated employee's relevant system access without alerting them prematurely if the investigation is ongoing.
steps.guidance: Sequence access removal carefully with HR/Legal/Security to preserve evidence and avoid tipping off the individual before interview.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent payments; access frozen at the appropriate investigative moment.

steps.title: Notify Legal and consider law-enforcement coordination
steps.desc: Notify Legal to assess criminal referral and evidentiary requirements before any employee confrontation or termination action.
steps.outcome: Legal-approved investigation and containment plan.

steps.title: Close out the shell vendor and reconcile financials
steps.desc: Formally deactivate the shell vendor record and reconcile all financial statements affected by the fictitious billing.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance on any restatement needs.
steps.outcome: Vendor deactivated; financial records reconciled.

steps.title: Implement segregation of duties for vendor creation and approval
steps.desc: Establish segregation of duties so no single employee can both create a vendor and approve its invoices, and require independent verification of new vendor legitimacy.
steps.guidance: Work with Procurement and Internal Audit on control redesign.
steps.outcome: Documented control redesign closing the gap exploited.

steps.title: Pursue recovery, disciplinary action, and criminal referral
steps.desc: Work with Legal and HR to pursue recovery of diverted funds, determine disciplinary action, and refer to law enforcement/prosecutors as warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery and referral actions initiated.

steps.title: Document investigation and brief leadership on control changes
steps.desc: Finalize the investigation report and brief Finance/Procurement/Internal Audit leadership on the segregation-of-duties changes implemented.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and control updates.

ITID-53324.def: An unclassified or general instance of vendor overbilling or invoice-padding fraud that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Overbilling and Padding leaf.
ITID-53324.purpose: Intake bucket for overbilling/invoice-padding fraud that does not yet fit the inflated-quantity, duplicate-invoice, or shell-vendor patterns.
scopeIncludes: Overbilling reported without enough detail to determine inflated-quantity, duplicate, or shell-vendor origin
Novel or mixed-mechanism vendor billing fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed inflated quantity/hours overbilling (ITID-53321)
Confirmed duplicate invoice submission (ITID-53322)
Confirmed shell-vendor fictitious billing (ITID-53323)
ITID-53324.severity: Medium, pending reclassification once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53324.priority: P3, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed and the incident is reclassified.
ITID-53324.escalation: Escalate to Finance/Procurement and Internal Audit for standard billing-discrepancy investigation regardless of final classification.
indicators: Billing discrepancy identified during reconciliation with mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard three-way match and vendor-master audit controls applicable to all overbilling fraud
ITID-53324.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; treat mechanism as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53324.response: Withhold payment pending reconciliation and investigate to reclassify under a specific Overbilling and Padding leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53324.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Overbilling and Padding
playbook.description: A vendor or complicit internal employee inflates invoiced amounts through unspecified or mixed padding methods not otherwise captured by a more specific overbilling scenario.

steps.title: Pull the vendor's full billing and payment history
steps.desc: Export the vendor's complete invoice and payment history for review, alongside relevant contracts and PO terms.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit and the business owner of the vendor relationship.
steps.outcome: Dataset assembled for comprehensive review.

steps.title: Identify the specific padding mechanism and quantify impact
steps.desc: Determine the specific method of overbilling used (e.g. rate manipulation, unauthorized fees, scope creep without approval) and quantify the financial impact.
steps.guidance: Use forensic-accounting support as needed for complex billing structures.
steps.outcome: Documented mechanism and financial impact.
steps.abort: If findings show a contractual/pricing misunderstanding rather than intentional padding, close as a contract-dispute referral to Legal/Procurement rather than fraud.

steps.title: Hold pending payments to the vendor
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending and future payments to the vendor pending resolution of the review.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AP.
steps.outcome: No further padded invoices paid.

steps.title: Review and restrict any internal approver collusion
steps.desc: If internal collusion is suspected, coordinate with HR/Legal to restrict the implicated approver's authority pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Access/authority restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Renegotiate or terminate the vendor relationship as warranted
steps.desc: Based on findings, renegotiate contract terms, demand credits, or terminate the vendor relationship as appropriate.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal and Procurement leadership.
steps.outcome: Vendor relationship resolved per findings.

steps.title: Strengthen invoice-review and approval-threshold controls
steps.desc: Tighten invoice-review procedures and approval thresholds to catch similar padding patterns earlier.
steps.guidance: Work with Procurement/AP leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Recover overpaid amounts
steps.desc: Pursue recovery of overpaid amounts via credit, refund, or legal action as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or offset.

steps.title: Document findings and communicate control updates
steps.desc: Finalize documentation and communicate strengthened controls to relevant teams.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53331.def: Submission of an employee expense report containing fabricated expenses (never actually incurred) or inflated amounts (exceeding the actual cost paid), supported by altered, fabricated, or mismatched receipts, to obtain reimbursement in excess of legitimate business costs.
ITID-53331.purpose: Captures fraud by an employee who fabricates or inflates expense report line items to obtain reimbursement for costs not actually, or not fully, incurred.
scopeIncludes: Receipt altered to show a higher amount than actually paid
Expense claimed for a trip, meal, or purchase that never occurred
Reused or borrowed receipt submitted as one's own expense
scopeExcludes: The same legitimate expense claimed for reimbursement more than once (ITID-53332)
A genuinely personal purchase submitted as if it were a business expense (ITID-53333)
ITID-53331.severity: Low to Medium per instance, escalating to Medium-High if the employee has a sustained pattern across many expense reports or holds a position of financial trust.
ITID-53331.priority: P3 for an isolated discrepancy; P2 if a pattern across multiple reports or a senior employee is involved.
ITID-53331.escalation: Escalate to HR and Internal Audit for investigation and disciplinary action; escalate to Legal if the cumulative amount is significant or law-enforcement referral is warranted.
indicators: Receipt image showing signs of digital alteration
Expense amount inconsistent with the merchant's typical pricing or the receipt's visible total
Claimed expense with no corresponding calendar/travel record supporting the trip or meeting
vectors: Manual alteration of a scanned/photographed receipt before submission
Fabrication of a receipt using a template or another transaction's details
rootCauses: Manual expense-review process with no automated receipt/amount validation
Infrequent or superficial audit sampling of expense reports
Lack of policy limits or itemization requirements for common expense categories
controls: Automated receipt-matching/OCR validation in the expense system
Risk-based sampling and audit of submitted expense reports
Clear expense-policy limits with required itemization for high-risk categories
ITID-53331.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection relies on expense-system analytics and internal audit sampling rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53331.response: Recover the fraudulently claimed amount, refer the case to HR for disciplinary action, and escalate to Legal for cases involving significant dollar amounts or repeat behavior.
metrics: Number and dollar value of fabricated/inflated expense claims identified per audit cycle
