Percentage of expense reports flagged in risk-based sampling
ITID-53331.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls.

playbook.name: Fabricated/Inflated Expense Report Submission
playbook.description: An employee submits an expense report containing fabricated receipts or inflated amounts for reimbursement of expenses never actually incurred at the stated value.

steps.title: Flag the suspect expense report and pull submission history
steps.desc: Identify the specific expense report(s) in question and pull the employee's full expense-submission history for pattern review.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit/Finance before contacting the employee.
steps.outcome: Full expense history assembled for review.

steps.title: Verify receipts against third-party records
steps.desc: Cross-check submitted receipts against merchant records, corporate card statements, or third-party confirmation (e.g. hotel/airline booking systems) to confirm fabrication or inflation.
steps.guidance: Look for altered totals, mismatched dates/vendors, or receipts inconsistent with the employee's known travel/location.
steps.outcome: Confirmed evidence of fabrication or inflation with supporting documentation.
steps.abort: If receipts are verified genuine and amounts are accurate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before employee confrontation
steps.desc: Work with Internal Audit/HR/Legal to preserve the original submission records and supporting communications before confronting the employee.
steps.guidance: Follow the organization's internal-investigation evidence protocol.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Hold pending reimbursement and freeze further expense submissions
steps.desc: Place a hold on the pending reimbursement and any further expense submissions from the employee until the review concludes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/AP.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent reimbursement issued.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR on employee notification and interview
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR/Legal on the timing and approach for notifying and interviewing the employee, consistent with disciplinary/investigation procedures.
steps.guidance: HR leads the interview process; IR/Audit provides supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted per HR protocol; employee response documented.

steps.title: Quantify total fraudulent reimbursement across history
steps.desc: Complete a review of the employee's full expense history to quantify total fraudulent reimbursement obtained.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accounting for larger or long-running cases.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Strengthen expense-report receipt-verification controls
steps.desc: Implement stronger receipt-verification controls (e.g. mandatory itemized receipts, spot audits, automated duplicate/anomaly detection) in the expense system.
steps.guidance: Work with Finance leadership to implement.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Recover funds and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to recover the fraudulently obtained funds (payroll deduction, direct repayment, or legal action) and determine disciplinary outcome.
steps.outcome: Recovery and disciplinary path determined.

steps.title: Document findings and update expense policy communication
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate updated expense-verification requirements to staff.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53332.def: Submission of a claim for reimbursement of the same expense (same receipt, transaction, or cost) more than once, whether via duplicate submission within the same expense system, across multiple systems (e.g., corporate card auto-reconciliation plus a manual claim), or by resubmitting a previously reimbursed item with minor cosmetic changes.
ITID-53332.purpose: Captures fraud where an employee submits the same legitimate expense for reimbursement more than once, whether through separate expense systems, currencies, or resubmission after correction.
scopeIncludes: Same receipt submitted twice in separate expense reports
Expense already paid directly by a corporate card also claimed for personal-reimbursement
Previously reimbursed expense resubmitted after a date or description change
scopeExcludes: A fabricated or inflated expense not actually incurred (ITID-53331)
A personal purchase misrepresented as a business expense (ITID-53333)
ITID-53332.severity: Low per instance, escalating to Medium if a pattern of repeated duplicate claims by the same employee is identified.
ITID-53332.priority: P3 for an isolated duplicate; P2 if a recurring pattern is confirmed.
ITID-53332.escalation: Escalate to Finance/AP for recovery via payroll deduction or direct repayment, and to HR if the pattern indicates intentional, repeated fraud rather than a one-off error.
indicators: Duplicate-receipt-image or duplicate-amount alert from the expense system
Same merchant, date, and amount claimed in two separate reports
Corporate-card transaction also appearing as a separate cash-reimbursement claim
vectors: Deliberate resubmission of a previously reimbursed receipt
Exploiting a lack of cross-checking between corporate-card reconciliation and manual reimbursement claims
rootCauses: No automated duplicate-receipt detection in the expense system
Lack of reconciliation between corporate-card statements and manual expense claims
Infrequent audit review of reimbursement history per employee
controls: Automated duplicate-receipt/amount detection in the expense system
Reconciliation between corporate-card transactions and manual reimbursement claims
Periodic per-employee reimbursement-history audit
ITID-53332.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection is an expense-system analytics and internal-audit function.
ITID-53332.response: Recover the duplicate reimbursement, and if intentional and repeated, refer to HR for disciplinary action.
metrics: Number and dollar value of duplicate reimbursements identified and recovered per period
ITID-53332.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls.

playbook.name: Duplicate Expense Reimbursement Claim
playbook.description: An employee submits the same expense for reimbursement more than once — via separate expense reports, or in combination with a direct corporate card charge — to obtain duplicate payment.

steps.title: Run duplicate-claim detection analysis
steps.desc: Run a query across the expense system for matching amounts, dates, and vendors submitted by the same employee across multiple reports, and cross-check against corporate card charges for the same expense.
steps.guidance: Use fuzzy matching to catch near-duplicate entries with minor date/amount alterations.
steps.outcome: List of candidate duplicate claims.

steps.title: Confirm duplication and pattern of intent
steps.desc: Manually verify each candidate and assess whether the pattern indicates intentional duplication versus an isolated clerical mistake.
steps.guidance: Check frequency and whether the employee corrected/disclosed the duplicate voluntarily.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of intentional duplicate claims.
steps.abort: If it is a single isolated instance with no prior pattern and the employee self-reports, handle as a training/coaching matter rather than a fraud case.

steps.title: Review prior reporting periods for the same pattern
steps.desc: Extend the duplicate-claim analysis to prior reporting periods to determine whether this is a first occurrence or a recurring pattern.
steps.guidance: A recurring pattern across multiple periods strengthens the case for intentional fraud rather than error.
steps.outcome: Documented history of occurrences, if any.

steps.title: Hold pending reimbursements
steps.desc: Place a hold on any pending reimbursement claims from the employee until the review concludes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/AP.
steps.outcome: No further duplicate payments issued.

steps.title: Notify HR and initiate employee interview
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR to notify and interview the employee per disciplinary procedures.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted; employee response documented.

steps.title: Implement automated duplicate-claim detection
steps.desc: Configure the expense system to automatically flag near-duplicate submissions and cross-reference against corporate card feed data.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance systems administrators.
steps.outcome: System control in place to catch this pattern going forward.

steps.title: Recover duplicate reimbursement and determine disciplinary action
steps.desc: Recover the duplicate amount via payroll deduction or direct repayment, and determine appropriate disciplinary action with HR.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered; disciplinary outcome determined.

steps.title: Document findings and communicate control update
steps.desc: Document the investigation and communicate the enhanced duplicate-detection control to Finance/expense-approval staff.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53333.def: Submission of an expense claim for a purchase that was, in fact, personal in nature (with no legitimate business purpose), misrepresented through a false description, category, or context on the expense report to make it appear business-related and therefore reimbursable.
ITID-53333.purpose: Captures fraud where an employee submits a genuinely personal purchase, disguised through mischaracterization, for reimbursement as a legitimate business expense.
scopeIncludes: Personal meal, entertainment, or retail purchase claimed under a business-related expense category
Personal travel expense claimed as if incurred during a business trip
Gift or item for personal use claimed as a client-entertainment or business-supply expense
scopeExcludes: A fabricated expense with no underlying transaction at all (ITID-53331)
The same expense claimed for reimbursement more than once (ITID-53332)
ITID-53333.severity: Low to Medium per instance, escalating to Medium-High if the pattern is sustained or the employee holds a position of financial trust.
ITID-53333.priority: P3 for an isolated instance; P2 if a recurring pattern across multiple reports is identified.
ITID-53333.escalation: Escalate to HR and Internal Audit for investigation and disciplinary action; escalate to Legal for cases involving significant cumulative amounts.
indicators: Expense description inconsistent with the merchant type shown on the receipt
Personal-pattern purchases (e.g., recurring personal retail merchants) claimed under generic business categories
Business justification lacking supporting context (no corresponding meeting, client, or project reference)
vectors: Mischaracterization of a personal purchase's category or description on submission
Reliance on generic or vague expense categories that reduce scrutiny
rootCauses: Vague or overly broad expense-category definitions
Insufficient business-justification documentation requirements
Infrequent audit sampling of expense claims against merchant type
controls: Required business-justification documentation for discretionary expense categories
Merchant-category-code cross-checking against claimed expense type
Risk-based audit sampling of expense reports
ITID-53333.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection relies on expense-system merchant-category analytics and internal audit.
ITID-53333.response: Recover the fraudulently claimed amount, refer to HR for disciplinary action, and escalate to Legal for significant or repeated cases.
metrics: Number and dollar value of personal-purchase misclassifications identified per audit cycle
ITID-53333.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls.

playbook.name: Personal Purchase Disguised as Business Expense
playbook.description: An employee submits a personal purchase (e.g. personal travel, retail goods, entertainment) as a legitimate business expense for reimbursement or via corporate card, misrepresenting its business purpose.

steps.title: Flag the suspect claim and gather supporting documentation
steps.desc: Identify the specific claim(s) and gather receipts, itemized statements, and any stated business justification.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit/Finance before contacting the employee.
steps.outcome: Documentation assembled for review.

steps.title: Verify the business purpose and itemized contents
steps.desc: Review itemized receipts against the stated business purpose and any calendar/meeting records to determine whether the purchase was genuinely business-related.
steps.guidance: Look for mismatches such as personal retail items, family members included in travel, or dates not aligned with any business activity.
steps.outcome: Determined whether the purchase was personal and misrepresented.
steps.abort: If a legitimate business justification is confirmed, close as false positive.

steps.title: Hold pending reimbursement/deny the claim
steps.desc: Deny or hold the pending reimbursement and flag the employee's expense account for enhanced review.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/AP.
steps.outcome: No reimbursement issued for the personal expense.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR on interview and any card suspension
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR to interview the employee and, if a corporate card was used, consider a temporary suspension pending outcome.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted; card suspended if warranted.

steps.title: Review the employee's full expense history for the same pattern
steps.desc: Review the employee's historical claims for other instances of personal expenses disguised as business, quantifying total impact.
steps.outcome: Full scope and financial impact quantified.

steps.title: Reinforce expense-policy training and spot-audit program
steps.desc: Reinforce expense-policy training for the team and expand the spot-audit sampling rate for high-risk expense categories.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Recover any paid amounts and determine disciplinary action
steps.desc: Recover any amounts already reimbursed and determine disciplinary action with HR.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered; disciplinary outcome determined.

steps.title: Document findings and update policy communication
steps.desc: Document the investigation and communicate the reinforced expense-policy expectations to staff.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53334.def: An unclassified or general instance of employee expense reimbursement fraud that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Employee Reimbursement Fraud leaf.
ITID-53334.purpose: Intake bucket for employee reimbursement fraud that does not yet fit the fabricated/inflated, duplicate, or disguised-personal-purchase patterns.
scopeIncludes: Reimbursement fraud reported without enough detail to determine fabrication, duplication, or disguised-personal-purchase origin
Novel or mixed-mechanism reimbursement fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed fabricated/inflated expense claims (ITID-53331)
Confirmed duplicate reimbursement claims (ITID-53332)
Confirmed disguised personal purchases (ITID-53333)
ITID-53334.severity: Low to Medium, pending reclassification once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53334.priority: P3, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed and the incident is reclassified.
ITID-53334.escalation: Escalate to HR and Internal Audit for standard reimbursement-discrepancy investigation regardless of final classification.
indicators: Reimbursement discrepancy identified during audit with mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard expense-report audit and receipt-validation controls applicable to all reimbursement fraud
ITID-53334.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; treat mechanism as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53334.response: Withhold or claw back the reimbursement pending investigation and reclassify under a specific Employee Reimbursement Fraud leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53334.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Employee Reimbursement Fraud
playbook.description: An employee submits fraudulent expense claims through methods not otherwise captured by a more specific reimbursement-fraud scenario, resulting in unwarranted reimbursement.

steps.title: Flag the suspect claims and pull expense history
steps.desc: Identify the specific claim(s) in question and pull the employee's full expense-submission history.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit/Finance.
steps.outcome: Expense history assembled for review.

steps.title: Determine the specific fraud mechanism and quantify impact
steps.desc: Analyze the claims to determine the specific fraud mechanism used and quantify the financial impact.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accounting for complex or long-running patterns.
steps.outcome: Documented mechanism and financial impact.
steps.abort: If findings are explainable by legitimate expense variance, close as false positive.

steps.title: Hold pending reimbursements
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending reimbursements from the employee pending review outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/AP.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent reimbursement issued.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR on interview
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR to interview the employee per disciplinary procedure.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted; response documented.

steps.title: Strengthen relevant expense-control gap
steps.desc: Identify and close the specific control gap that enabled the fraud mechanism identified.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Expand spot-audit coverage for expense submissions
steps.desc: Expand random spot-audit sampling of expense submissions across the department to detect any similar undetected patterns.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit on sampling methodology.
steps.outcome: Broader detection coverage established.

steps.title: Recover funds and determine disciplinary action
steps.desc: Recover fraudulently obtained funds and determine disciplinary action with HR.
steps.outcome: Recovery and disciplinary outcome determined.

steps.title: Document findings and communicate control update
steps.desc: Finalize documentation and communicate the control update to relevant staff.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53341.def: Use of a company-issued procurement or purchasing card by an employee to buy goods or services for personal benefit, with no legitimate business justification, in violation of the card's authorized-use policy.
ITID-53341.purpose: Captures misuse of a company procurement card (P-card) for unauthorized personal purchases unrelated to any business purpose.
scopeIncludes: P-card used to purchase personal retail items, groceries, or entertainment
P-card used for personal travel unrelated to business
Cardholder claiming a personal purchase was business-related after the fact when challenged
scopeExcludes: A legitimate purchase intentionally split into multiple transactions to stay under an approval threshold (ITID-53342)
ITID-53341.severity: Low to Medium per instance, escalating to Medium-High if the pattern is sustained or the cumulative amount is significant.
ITID-53341.priority: P3 for an isolated purchase; P2 if a recurring pattern is identified during statement review.
ITID-53341.escalation: Escalate to the cardholder's manager and HR for a policy-violation review, and to Internal Audit if the amount is material or the pattern is repeated.
indicators: Statement line item at a merchant category inconsistent with the cardholder's role or department
Missing or implausible business justification for a flagged transaction
Cardholder unable to produce a receipt or explain the purchase during statement reconciliation
vectors: Direct unauthorized personal use of an issued P-card with no attempt at concealment
Personal purchase claimed retroactively as a business expense when questioned
rootCauses: Infrequent or superficial P-card statement review
Lack of merchant-category restrictions on the card
Insufficient cardholder training on acceptable-use policy
controls: Merchant-category-code (MCC) restrictions on P-cards
Monthly statement review and reconciliation by a supervisor
Cardholder acceptable-use policy acknowledgment
ITID-53341.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection relies on statement reconciliation and internal audit rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53341.response: Recover the amount from the employee (payroll deduction or direct repayment), and refer to HR for disciplinary action per policy.
metrics: Number and dollar value of unauthorized personal purchases identified per statement cycle
Percentage of P-card statements reviewed on time
ITID-53341.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls.

playbook.name: P-Card Used for Unauthorized Personal Purchases
playbook.description: An employee uses their company-issued procurement card (P-Card) to make personal purchases outside authorized business use.

steps.title: Pull P-Card transaction statement for review
steps.desc: Pull the employee's full P-Card transaction statement and any submitted reconciliation/receipt documentation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Internal Audit before contacting the employee.
steps.outcome: Full transaction history assembled.

steps.title: Identify and verify suspect personal transactions
steps.desc: Review flagged transactions against merchant category codes and receipts to confirm personal (non-business) use.
steps.guidance: Look for merchant categories inconsistent with the employee's role (e.g. retail, entertainment, personal travel).
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of unauthorized personal transactions.
steps.abort: If the employee provides a valid business justification, close as false positive.

steps.title: Suspend the P-Card
steps.desc: Suspend or cancel the employee's P-Card immediately to prevent further unauthorized use.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the card issuer/Finance to process the suspension.
steps.outcome: Card suspended; no further unauthorized transactions possible.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR on interview and disciplinary process
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR to interview the employee and initiate the disciplinary process per policy.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted; response documented.

steps.title: Quantify total unauthorized spend
steps.desc: Review the full card history (and prior cards if reissued) to quantify total unauthorized personal spend.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Tighten P-Card spend-limit and merchant-category restrictions
steps.desc: Review and tighten spend limits and merchant-category-code (MCC) restrictions on P-Cards to prevent similar unauthorized purchases.
steps.guidance: Work with Finance/card-program administrators.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Recover unauthorized amounts and determine disciplinary action
steps.desc: Recover unauthorized amounts via payroll deduction or direct repayment, and determine disciplinary action with HR.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered; disciplinary outcome determined.

steps.title: Document findings and communicate policy reinforcement
steps.desc: Document the investigation and reinforce P-Card usage policy training for cardholders.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53342.def: Intentional division of what should be a single purchase into two or more separate P-card transactions, each kept below the dollar threshold that would otherwise require additional approval or a competitive-bid process, in order to circumvent that control.
ITID-53342.purpose: Captures deliberate splitting of a single purchase into multiple smaller P-card transactions to evade a spending-approval threshold.
scopeIncludes: Single vendor invoice split into multiple same-day or near-same-day P-card charges each under the approval threshold
Same item purchased in smaller increments across consecutive days to avoid triggering review
Coordinated splitting across multiple cardholders for a single larger purchase
scopeExcludes: A single unauthorized personal purchase with no threshold-evasion intent (ITID-53341)
ITID-53342.severity: Medium — this specifically defeats a designed spend-control threshold, indicating deliberate circumvention rather than simple misuse.
ITID-53342.priority: P2, given the deliberate control-circumvention intent, even if the underlying purchase itself was for a legitimate business need.
ITID-53342.escalation: Escalate to Procurement leadership and Internal Audit for review of the cardholder's transaction history and any related approver.
indicators: Multiple same-vendor P-card transactions from one cardholder within a short window, each just under the approval threshold
Sequential charges summing to an amount that would have required additional approval as a single transaction
Pattern recurring across multiple purchase cycles from the same cardholder
vectors: Cardholder deliberately dividing a purchase across multiple transactions or dates
Coordination between multiple cardholders to split a single purchase across their individual cards
rootCauses: Approval-threshold control based solely on single-transaction amount with no aggregation logic
Lack of automated detection for same-vendor, same-period transaction clustering
Insufficient cardholder understanding of why threshold controls exist
controls: Automated transaction-clustering analytics (same vendor/cardholder within a rolling window) to flag potential threshold splitting
Approval-threshold logic aggregated across related transactions, not evaluated per-transaction alone
Cardholder training on threshold-splitting policy violations
ITID-53342.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; detection relies on transaction-clustering analytics within the P-card program, not SOC telemetry.
ITID-53342.response: Require retroactive approval review for the split transactions, and refer to Procurement/Internal Audit for policy-violation action against the cardholder.
metrics: Number of threshold-splitting patterns identified per audit cycle
Cumulative dollar value of split transactions
ITID-53342.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls. Differentiated from ITID-53341 by the deliberate control-circumvention mechanism rather than the underlying legitimacy of the purchase itself.

playbook.name: P-Card Transaction Split to Avoid Approval Threshold
playbook.description: An employee deliberately splits a single purchase into multiple smaller P-Card transactions to stay under a mandatory approval or review threshold.

steps.title: Identify split-transaction pattern
steps.desc: Run an analysis of P-Card transactions for the same merchant, same day/short window, from the same cardholder, with amounts summing above the approval threshold.
steps.guidance: Use data analytics to flag multiple same-merchant transactions just under the threshold.
steps.outcome: List of candidate split-transaction instances.

steps.title: Confirm intentional splitting versus legitimate separate purchases
steps.desc: Review receipts/itemization to determine whether the transactions represent a single order deliberately split, or genuinely separate purchases.
steps.guidance: Check order/invoice numbers and timing for evidence of intentional splitting.
steps.outcome: Confirmed intentional threshold evasion or ruled out as legitimate.
steps.abort: If transactions are confirmed as genuinely separate legitimate purchases, close as false positive.

steps.title: Review cardholder's full transaction history for prior splitting
steps.desc: Review the cardholder's full P-Card history over a longer lookback period to determine whether this is an isolated incident or a recurring practice.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit on the lookback scope.
steps.outcome: Documented history of occurrences, if any.

steps.title: Flag the cardholder for enhanced review and hold further approvals
steps.desc: Flag the cardholder's account for enhanced transaction review and place pending high-value purchases on hold for manual approval.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/card-program administrators.
steps.outcome: Further threshold evasion prevented while review continues.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR/manager on interview
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR and the cardholder's manager to interview the employee regarding the pattern.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted; response documented.

steps.title: Implement system-level split-transaction detection
steps.desc: Configure the P-Card monitoring system to automatically flag same-merchant/same-day transactions that cumulatively exceed the approval threshold.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT/Finance systems administrators.
steps.outcome: Automated detection control in place going forward.

steps.title: Determine appropriate corrective/disciplinary action
steps.desc: Determine whether corrective coaching or formal disciplinary action is warranted with HR, based on severity and intent.
steps.outcome: Disciplinary/corrective outcome determined.

steps.title: Document findings and reinforce approval-threshold policy
steps.desc: Document the investigation and reinforce training on approval-threshold policy for cardholders and approvers.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53343.def: An unclassified or general instance of procurement card (P-card) misuse that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Procurement Card Misuse leaf.
ITID-53343.purpose: Intake bucket for procurement card misuse that does not yet fit the unauthorized-personal-purchase or threshold-splitting patterns.
scopeIncludes: P-card misuse reported without enough detail to determine personal-purchase or threshold-splitting mechanism
Novel or mixed-mechanism P-card misuse
scopeExcludes: Confirmed unauthorized personal purchases (ITID-53341)
Confirmed transaction splitting to avoid approval thresholds (ITID-53342)
ITID-53343.severity: Low to Medium, pending reclassification once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53343.priority: P3, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed and the incident is reclassified.
ITID-53343.escalation: Escalate to Procurement/Finance and HR for standard statement-review investigation regardless of final classification.
indicators: Flagged P-card transaction with mechanism not yet determined during statement review
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard P-card statement review and reconciliation controls applicable to all card misuse
ITID-53343.detection: No ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies — procurement/expense-fraud pattern; treat mechanism as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53343.response: Suspend the card pending investigation and reclassify under a specific Procurement Card Misuse leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53343.notes: Procurement/expense-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal audit and finance controls. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Procurement Card Misuse
playbook.description: An employee misuses a company procurement card through methods not otherwise captured by a more specific P-Card misuse scenario.

steps.title: Pull card transaction history for review
steps.desc: Pull the cardholder's full transaction history and reconciliation records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Internal Audit.
steps.outcome: Transaction history assembled for review.

steps.title: Determine specific misuse mechanism and quantify impact
steps.desc: Analyze the transactions to determine the specific misuse mechanism and quantify financial impact.
steps.outcome: Documented mechanism and financial impact.
steps.abort: If a valid business justification is found, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve transaction evidence before employee confrontation
steps.desc: Preserve the transaction records and reconciliation history before the employee is confronted, coordinating with Internal Audit/HR as needed.
steps.guidance: Follow the organization's evidence-preservation protocol for suspected internal fraud.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Suspend or restrict the card
steps.desc: Suspend the card or restrict its spend limits pending review outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/card issuer.
steps.outcome: Further misuse prevented.

steps.title: Coordinate with HR on interview
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR to interview the employee per disciplinary procedure.
steps.outcome: Interview conducted; response documented.

steps.title: Close the identified control gap
steps.desc: Identify and close the specific P-Card control gap that enabled the misuse (spend limit, category restriction, or reconciliation frequency).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/card-program administrators.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Recover funds and determine disciplinary action
steps.desc: Recover misused funds via payroll deduction or repayment, and determine disciplinary action with HR.
steps.outcome: Recovery and disciplinary outcome determined.

steps.title: Document findings and reinforce policy
steps.desc: Document the investigation and reinforce P-Card policy training.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53411.def: Intentional submission of a corporate tax return to a tax authority that misstates income, expenses, or other reportable figures — through underreporting revenue, fabricating expenses, or misrepresenting entity structure — with the purpose of illegally reducing the company's tax liability.
ITID-53411.purpose: Captures the filing of a corporate tax return containing knowingly falsified information to reduce reported tax liability.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate underreporting of taxable revenue on a filed corporate return
Fabricated or non-existent expenses claimed to reduce taxable income
Misrepresentation of corporate structure or income allocation to reduce tax owed
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent claiming of a specific deduction or credit within an otherwise accurate return (ITID-53412)
Use of offshore structures specifically to evade tax obligations (ITID-53413)
ITID-53411.severity: High — corporate tax fraud carries significant legal, regulatory, and reputational exposure, including potential criminal liability for responsible officers.
ITID-53411.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint given regulatory-reporting and statute-of-limitations implications, even though it is not a SOC technical incident.
ITID-53411.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, and the Chief Financial Officer; this is a legal/regulatory matter requiring outside tax counsel and, where required, voluntary disclosure consideration rather than SOC technical response.
indicators: Discrepancy between internal financial records and figures reported on the filed tax return
Whistleblower report alleging falsified tax filings
Tax authority audit flag or inquiry regarding reported figures
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Deliberate management decision to understate tax liability
Inadequate segregation of duties or oversight in tax-return preparation and review
Insufficient internal audit coverage of tax-filing accuracy
controls: Independent internal audit review of tax filings before submission
Segregation of duties between tax preparation and final sign-off
External tax counsel/auditor review for material filings
ITID-53411.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53411.response: Engage outside tax counsel immediately, assess voluntary-disclosure options with the tax authority, and remediate internal controls over tax-return preparation; the SOC's role is limited to preserving relevant electronic records if requested by Legal.
metrics: Number of tax-filing discrepancies identified per audit cycle
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53411.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response are framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response for this entire Tier-3 group.

playbook.name: Falsified Corporate Tax Return Filing
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that a filed corporate tax return contains falsified figures, requiring investigation, litigation hold, and regulator-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the tip/anomaly indicating falsified tax filing
steps.desc: Assess the whistleblower tip, audit finding, or financial-controls anomaly alleging that a filed corporate tax return contains falsified figures, and determine credibility and scope.
steps.guidance: Interview the reporting party (if known), review the specific return and supporting workpapers, and compare filed figures against the general ledger and supporting schedules for discrepancies.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators of falsification documented with the specific tax return, tax year, and discrepant line items identified.
steps.abort: If the discrepancy is explained by a legitimate accounting treatment or timing difference, close with documented rationale.

steps.title: Scope the investigation and engage Legal and forensic accounting
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance and, where warranted, external forensic accountants to formally scope and lead the internal investigation under attorney-client privilege.
steps.guidance: Establish the investigation team, define scope (tax years and entities in question), and determine whether outside counsel should direct the investigation to preserve privilege.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped and led by Legal/Compliance with appropriate privilege protections in place.

steps.title: Halt further filings and issue a litigation/document hold
steps.desc: Pause any pending or upcoming tax filings relying on the same methodology and issue a litigation hold to preserve all relevant financial records, workpapers, and communications.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to Finance, Tax, and any relevant personnel; suspend automated filing processes reliant on the questioned methodology pending review.
steps.outcome: Further filings halted and all relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Restrict access to affected financial systems and records
steps.desc: Restrict or monitor access to the general ledger modules, tax-preparation systems, and workpapers involved to prevent evidence tampering during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT to apply access restrictions or enhanced logging on the relevant systems for the personnel under investigation.
steps.outcome: Access to affected systems restricted/monitored with an auditable trail during the investigation.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting review and determine the accurate tax position
steps.desc: Complete the forensic accounting analysis to quantify the extent of the falsification and determine the correct tax position and any resulting under/over-payment.
steps.guidance: Document all identified discrepancies with supporting evidence sufficient to support an amended filing decision.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented accurate tax position.

steps.title: Legal assessment of voluntary self-disclosure and amended-filing obligations
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel evaluates whether the company has an obligation or business rationale to voluntarily self-disclose to the IRS and file amended returns, and determines next steps.
steps.guidance: Consider IRS voluntary disclosure practice, statute-of-limitations exposure, and materiality; document the legal rationale for the decision reached.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision on self-disclosure/amended filing, with any required filings initiated.
steps.abort: If Legal determines no disclosure obligation exists and the matter is immaterial, document the rationale and close the disclosure question.

steps.title: Address responsible personnel and remediate internal tax controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate HR/disciplinary action against personnel found responsible, and remediate the internal control weakness that allowed the falsification to occur or go undetected.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal on personnel action; implement additional review/approval controls over tax return preparation and filing.
steps.outcome: Responsible personnel addressed and internal tax-control gap remediated.

steps.title: Resume normal tax filing operations under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Lift the filing hold and resume normal tax operations under the strengthened review/approval controls, filing any required amended returns.
steps.guidance: Confirm all required amended filings are submitted and Finance leadership is briefed on resumption.
steps.outcome: Normal tax filing operations resumed with amended filings completed as required.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, disclosure decisions, remediation, and personnel actions; brief the Audit Committee/Board as appropriate.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report and supporting workpapers under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and appropriate governance bodies briefed.

ITID-53412.def: Claiming of a tax deduction, credit, or incentive on a corporate tax filing that the company does not legitimately qualify for, or overstating the amount of a legitimate deduction/credit, in order to unlawfully reduce tax liability.
ITID-53412.purpose: Captures the fraudulent claiming of a specific tax deduction or credit the company is not legitimately entitled to.
scopeIncludes: Claiming a research-and-development or investment tax credit for activity that does not qualify
Overstating a legitimate depreciation or charitable-contribution deduction
Claiming a deduction/credit based on fabricated supporting documentation
scopeExcludes: Broader falsification of overall reported income/expenses across the entire return (ITID-53411)
Use of offshore structures to evade tax (ITID-53413)
ITID-53412.severity: High — improper deduction/credit claims carry legal, regulatory, and financial-restatement exposure and can trigger a broader tax authority audit.
ITID-53412.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint given regulatory-reporting implications.
ITID-53412.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, and Tax leadership; requires outside tax counsel involvement rather than SOC technical response.
indicators: Deduction/credit claim lacking adequate supporting documentation upon internal review
Tax authority inquiry specifically challenging a claimed deduction or credit
Internal audit finding that claimed activity does not meet the credit's qualifying criteria
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Aggressive tax-position interpretation without adequate legal/technical support
Insufficient documentation retention supporting claimed deductions/credits
Lack of independent review of high-value or novel tax positions before filing
controls: Independent legal/tax review of deduction and credit claims before filing
Documentation-retention policy supporting all claimed tax positions
Periodic internal audit of high-value tax positions
ITID-53412.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53412.response: Engage outside tax counsel to assess exposure and disclosure obligations, amend filings where appropriate, and remediate the underlying tax-position review process.
metrics: Number of challenged deduction/credit claims per audit cycle
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53412.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Fraudulent Tax Deduction/Credit Claim
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that the company claimed a fraudulent or unsupportable tax deduction or credit, requiring investigation and regulator-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the flagged deduction/credit claim
steps.desc: Assess an internal audit finding, whistleblower tip, or reconciliation anomaly indicating a tax deduction or credit was claimed without adequate supporting documentation or eligibility.
steps.guidance: Pull the underlying support for the claimed deduction/credit and compare against applicable eligibility requirements and documentation standards.
steps.outcome: Credibility of the finding assessed with the specific deduction/credit, amount, and tax year identified.
steps.abort: If adequate documentation and eligibility are confirmed, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to formally scope the investigation, including whether the issue reflects an isolated error, a pattern, or intentional misrepresentation.
steps.guidance: Determine whether outside tax counsel should be engaged given complexity or privilege considerations.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with an assigned lead and privilege protections established as needed.

steps.title: Halt reliance on the questioned deduction/credit in future filings
steps.desc: Suspend use of the same deduction/credit methodology in any pending or upcoming filings until the review is complete.
steps.guidance: Notify Tax/Finance teams to flag the item for manual review before any further filings rely on it.
steps.outcome: Further reliance on the questioned item halted pending review.

steps.title: Issue a document/litigation hold for supporting records
steps.desc: Preserve all records, correspondence, and workpapers relevant to the deduction/credit claim under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to Tax, Finance, and any business unit that generated the underlying support documentation.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete forensic review and quantify the correct tax position
steps.desc: Complete a detailed review to determine the amount of the deduction/credit that was properly supportable versus improperly claimed.
steps.guidance: Document findings with sufficient support to inform an amended-filing decision.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented correction amount.

steps.title: Legal assessment of amended filing and self-disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel determines whether an amended return and/or voluntary self-disclosure to the IRS is warranted based on materiality and the nature of the error.
steps.guidance: Document the legal rationale for the decision and initiate any required filings.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision with any required amended filings initiated.
steps.abort: If immaterial and attributable to a good-faith documentation gap, document rationale and close.

steps.title: Remediate documentation and approval controls for deduction/credit claims
steps.desc: Strengthen documentation-retention and second-level review requirements for claiming material deductions/credits going forward.
steps.guidance: Update the tax-provision review checklist and assign clear ownership for supporting-documentation retention.
steps.outcome: Updated control documented and adopted by the Tax function.

steps.title: Resume normal tax filing operations under strengthened review
steps.desc: Resume filings involving similar deductions/credits under the strengthened documentation and review controls.
steps.guidance: Confirm any required amended filings are completed and Finance leadership briefed.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief leadership
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, disclosure decisions, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee as appropriate.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and leadership briefed.

ITID-53413.def: Establishment or use of offshore accounts, shell entities, or corporate structures with the primary purpose of concealing income, assets, or beneficial ownership from tax authorities, thereby evading legitimately owed tax obligations.
ITID-53413.purpose: Captures the use of offshore entities, accounts, or structures specifically designed to conceal income or assets from tax authorities.
scopeIncludes: Undisclosed offshore account holding company or executive funds subject to unreported tax
Shell company structure in a low-tax jurisdiction used to shift profits without genuine business substance
Failure to report foreign financial accounts as required by law
scopeExcludes: Domestic falsification of a corporate tax return with no offshore component (ITID-53411)
A specific fraudulent deduction/credit claim with no offshore structure involved (ITID-53412)
ITID-53413.severity: Critical — offshore tax evasion carries severe legal, regulatory, and reputational consequences, including potential criminal prosecution and cross-border regulatory cooperation (e.g., information-sharing treaties).
ITID-53413.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint given the severity of cross-border regulatory and criminal exposure.
ITID-53413.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, the Board (Audit Committee), and outside counsel with international tax expertise; this is a legal/regulatory matter, not a SOC technical incident.
indicators: Undisclosed offshore account or entity discovered during an internal or external audit
Whistleblower report alleging concealed offshore holdings
Regulatory inquiry or leaked-document (e.g., cross-border data leak) exposure naming the company
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Deliberate structuring of offshore entities to conceal beneficial ownership or income
Inadequate internal controls over disclosure of foreign accounts and entities
Insufficient legal/compliance oversight of cross-border corporate structuring
controls: Mandatory disclosure and legal review of all foreign accounts/entities
Independent compliance oversight of international corporate structuring
Beneficial-ownership transparency review
ITID-53413.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53413.response: Engage outside international tax counsel immediately, assess voluntary-disclosure and remediation options with relevant tax authorities, and conduct a full review of all offshore structures.
metrics: Number of undisclosed offshore structures identified and remediated
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53413.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Offshore Tax Evasion Scheme
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that company funds or income were routed through offshore structures to evade tax obligations, requiring investigation and multi-jurisdictional regulator-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage indicators of an offshore evasion structure
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or transaction-pattern anomaly suggesting income or assets were routed through offshore entities/accounts to evade tax obligations.
steps.guidance: Review the offshore entity structure, intercompany transactions, and any tax-haven jurisdiction involvement identified in the tip or finding.
steps.outcome: Credibility assessed with the offshore structure, entities, and estimated tax exposure identified.
steps.abort: If offshore structures are confirmed to have a legitimate business purpose with proper tax reporting (e.g., correctly filed FBAR/FATCA disclosures), close as false positive.
steps.tool: Intercompany transaction records / entity org chart

steps.title: Engage Legal, Tax, and forensic accounting to scope a multi-jurisdictional investigation
steps.desc: Engage outside counsel with international tax expertise given the complexity and multi-jurisdictional regulatory exposure (IRS, and potentially foreign tax authorities).
steps.guidance: Establish privilege protections and define the investigation scope across all implicated jurisdictions and entities.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with appropriate specialist counsel engaged.

steps.title: Halt further transfers through the questioned offshore structure
steps.desc: Suspend further fund transfers or transactions through the offshore entities/accounts under investigation pending review.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury to freeze scheduled transactions involving the questioned structure.
steps.outcome: Further transfers through the offshore structure halted.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold across all implicated entities and jurisdictions
steps.desc: Preserve all records, correspondence, and financial data across every implicated entity and jurisdiction under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Coordinate hold distribution with local counsel/compliance in each relevant jurisdiction.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved across all implicated jurisdictions.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting analysis of the offshore structure
steps.desc: Trace the flow of funds through the offshore structure to quantify unreported income/tax exposure and identify responsible personnel.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accountants with cross-border expertise; document the full transaction trail.
steps.outcome: Forensic analysis completed with quantified exposure and responsible parties identified.

steps.title: Legal assessment of voluntary disclosure to IRS and foreign tax authorities
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel evaluates voluntary self-disclosure obligations to the IRS (e.g., under applicable voluntary disclosure practice) and any foreign tax authorities with jurisdiction.
steps.guidance: Consider FBAR/FATCA compliance history, statute of limitations, and potential criminal exposure; document the legal rationale.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision on multi-jurisdictional disclosure with required filings initiated.

steps.title: Unwind or restructure the offshore arrangement and address responsible personnel
steps.desc: Unwind or restructure the offshore arrangement to achieve tax compliance going forward, and take appropriate action against personnel found responsible for the evasion scheme.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Tax, Legal, and HR on restructuring and personnel actions.
steps.outcome: Offshore arrangement brought into compliance and responsible personnel addressed.

steps.title: Resume compliant international operations under strengthened oversight
steps.desc: Resume international financial operations under strengthened cross-border tax-compliance oversight and reporting controls.
steps.guidance: Establish ongoing monitoring of offshore/intercompany transactions by Tax and Compliance.
steps.outcome: Normal international operations resumed under strengthened compliance oversight.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, multi-jurisdictional disclosure decisions, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the severity.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Board/Audit Committee briefed.

ITID-53414.def: An unclassified or general instance of fraudulent tax filing activity that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Fraudulent Tax Filings leaf.
ITID-53414.purpose: Intake bucket for fraudulent tax filing matters that do not yet fit the falsified-return, deduction/credit, or offshore-evasion patterns.
scopeIncludes: Tax filing irregularity reported without enough detail to determine the specific fraudulent mechanism
Novel or mixed-mechanism tax filing fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed falsified corporate tax return filing (ITID-53411)
Confirmed fraudulent deduction/credit claim (ITID-53412)
Confirmed offshore tax evasion scheme (ITID-53413)
ITID-53414.severity: High, consistent with other tax-fraud leaves, pending reclassification.
ITID-53414.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53414.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, and Tax leadership regardless of final classification.
indicators: Tax filing discrepancy reported without a clearly identified mechanism
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard tax-filing compliance review controls applicable to all tax fraud
ITID-53414.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels.
ITID-53414.response: Engage Legal/Compliance immediately and investigate to reclassify under a specific Fraudulent Tax Filings leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53414.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Fraudulent Tax Filing
playbook.description: A fraudulent tax filing indicator that does not fit the falsified-return, deduction/credit, or offshore-evasion patterns, requiring general Compliance/Legal-led investigation.

steps.title: Triage the tax-filing fraud indicator
steps.desc: Assess the whistleblower tip, audit finding, or anomaly suggesting a fraudulent tax filing that does not fit a more specific pattern, and determine credibility and scope.
steps.guidance: Review the specific filing, tax year, and available supporting documentation for the flagged issue.
steps.outcome: Credibility assessed with the specific filing and discrepancy documented.
steps.abort: If the finding is explained by a legitimate treatment, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to formally scope and lead the investigation, determining whether outside counsel involvement is warranted.
steps.guidance: Define the investigation scope and privilege protections.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with an assigned lead.

steps.title: Halt further filings relying on the questioned position
steps.desc: Suspend reliance on the questioned filing position in any pending or upcoming filings until the review concludes.
steps.guidance: Notify Tax/Finance to flag the item for manual review.
steps.outcome: Further reliance on the questioned position halted.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold for relevant records
steps.desc: Preserve all relevant financial records, workpapers, and communications under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to Tax, Finance, and relevant personnel.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete forensic review and determine the correct tax position
steps.desc: Complete the review to quantify the discrepancy and determine the accurate tax position.
steps.guidance: Document all findings with supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented tax position.

steps.title: Legal assessment of self-disclosure and amended-filing obligations
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel evaluates whether self-disclosure to the IRS and/or an amended filing is warranted based on materiality.
steps.guidance: Document the legal rationale for the decision reached.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision with any required filings initiated.
steps.abort: If immaterial, document rationale and close the disclosure question.

steps.title: Resume normal tax filing operations under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal tax operations under any strengthened review/approval controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Confirm required amended filings are submitted.
steps.outcome: Normal tax filing operations resumed.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update tax-control procedures
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update the general tax-filing review procedure based on findings.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and procedures updated.

ITID-53421.def: Deduction of required payroll taxes (income tax withholding, Social Security/Medicare or equivalent) from employee wages, followed by the company's failure to actually remit the withheld funds to the appropriate tax authority, instead retaining or diverting the funds for other purposes.
ITID-53421.purpose: Captures the practice of withholding payroll taxes from employee wages but failing to remit those withheld amounts to the government.
scopeIncludes: Payroll taxes withheld from employee paychecks but not forwarded to the tax authority
Diversion of withheld payroll tax funds to cover operating cash-flow shortfalls
Consistent pattern of late or missing payroll tax deposits despite funds being withheld
scopeExcludes: Misclassifying employees to avoid payroll tax obligations altogether rather than withholding-and-not-remitting (ITID-53422)
ITID-53421.severity: Critical — this exposes the company and responsible individuals to significant personal criminal liability under trust-fund-recovery-penalty type provisions in most jurisdictions, in addition to corporate penalties.
ITID-53421.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint given the personal-liability and criminal-exposure dimensions.
ITID-53421.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, Finance leadership, and the Board; requires outside tax counsel and urgent remediation given personal liability exposure for responsible officers.
indicators: Tax authority notice of missing or delinquent payroll tax deposits despite withholding shown on pay stubs
Internal audit finding a gap between amounts withheld per payroll records and amounts actually remitted
Employee complaint of tax authority contact regarding unfiled/unremitted withholding
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Deliberate diversion of withheld funds during cash-flow distress
Inadequate segregation of payroll-tax remittance from general operating funds
Insufficient oversight/reconciliation of withheld vs. remitted payroll tax amounts
controls: Segregated payroll-tax trust account separate from general operating funds
Independent reconciliation of amounts withheld against amounts remitted each pay period
Board/Audit Committee oversight of payroll tax compliance status
ITID-53421.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53421.response: Engage outside tax counsel immediately to assess personal and corporate liability, remit all outstanding amounts as soon as possible, and remediate the underlying cash-management controls.
metrics: Dollar amount of withheld-but-unremitted payroll tax identified
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation and remediation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53421.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Employer Withholding Payroll Taxes Without Remitting to Government
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that payroll taxes withheld from employee wages were not remitted to the applicable tax authority, requiring investigation and self-disclosure assessment.

steps.title: Triage the non-remittance indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, agency notice, or reconciliation anomaly indicating payroll taxes withheld from employees were not remitted to the IRS/state tax authority.
steps.guidance: Reconcile payroll withholding records against actual remittance records/confirmations for the periods in question.
steps.outcome: Confirmed non-remittance with the affected periods and dollar amounts documented.
steps.abort: If remittance records confirm timely payment, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to scope the investigation, given the personal-liability exposure payroll tax non-remittance can create for responsible officers (e.g., IRS Trust Fund Recovery Penalty).
steps.guidance: Identify the individuals with control over payroll tax remittance during the affected periods.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with responsible-party identification underway.

steps.title: Halt further diversion and secure current-period withholdings
steps.desc: Immediately ensure current and future payroll tax withholdings are segregated and remitted on schedule, halting any process that allowed diversion or non-remittance.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury/Payroll to confirm current-period withholding funds are held separately and remittance is current going forward.
steps.outcome: Current withholdings secured and remittance current; no further diversion possible.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold for payroll and remittance records
steps.desc: Preserve all payroll, remittance, and related financial records under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to Payroll, Treasury, Finance, and relevant personnel.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Quantify the total unremitted liability and interest/penalties
steps.desc: Complete a forensic accounting reconciliation to determine the full unremitted payroll tax liability, including accrued interest and penalties.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accountants/payroll tax specialists to produce a period-by-period liability schedule.
steps.outcome: Full liability quantified and documented.

steps.title: Legal assessment of voluntary disclosure and remediation plan with tax authorities
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel evaluates voluntary disclosure to the IRS/state authority and negotiates a remediation/payment plan for the unremitted liability.
steps.guidance: Consider Trust Fund Recovery Penalty exposure for responsible individuals and document the legal rationale for the disclosure approach.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision with a remediation/payment plan initiated with the relevant tax authority.

steps.title: Address responsible personnel and remediate payroll-remittance controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate action against personnel responsible for the non-remittance and implement automated, independently-verified remittance controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal on personnel action; implement segregation of duties between payroll processing and remittance authorization.
steps.outcome: Responsible personnel addressed and remittance control gap remediated.

steps.title: Resume normal payroll tax operations under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal payroll tax withholding and remittance operations under the strengthened, independently-verified control process.
steps.guidance: Confirm the remediation/payment plan with tax authorities is being honored on schedule.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened controls and payment plan on track.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, disclosure/remediation plan, and personnel actions; brief the Audit Committee given the personal-liability exposure involved.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee briefed.

ITID-53422.def: Intentional misclassification of workers who function as employees (subject to direction and control consistent with employment) as independent contractors or another exempt category, in order to avoid payroll tax withholding, unemployment insurance contributions, and related employer tax obligations.
ITID-53422.purpose: Captures the deliberate misclassification of employees as independent contractors (or in another lower-obligation category) specifically to avoid payroll tax and related withholding obligations.
scopeIncludes: Worker treated as an independent contractor (issued a 1099-equivalent) despite meeting legal employee criteria
Systematic misclassification across a class of workers to reduce aggregate payroll tax liability
Misclassification persisting despite internal or external challenges to the worker's status
scopeExcludes: Correctly classified employees whose withheld payroll taxes are simply not remitted (ITID-53421)
ITID-53422.severity: High — worker misclassification carries significant back-tax liability, penalties, and potential class-action/regulatory exposure if applied systematically.
ITID-53422.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint given the scale of potential back-tax and penalty exposure.
ITID-53422.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, and HR leadership for a worker-classification review; requires employment and tax counsel involvement rather than SOC technical response.
indicators: Regulatory agency audit or worker complaint challenging contractor classification
Internal review finding contractors subject to employee-level direction, schedules, and control
Pattern of reclassification challenges across multiple similarly situated workers
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Deliberate classification decision to reduce payroll tax and benefits cost
Inadequate legal review of worker-classification criteria at hiring
Lack of periodic audit of contractor relationships against legal employee tests
controls: Periodic legal review of worker classification against applicable employee tests
HR/Legal sign-off required before classifying a new role as independent contractor
Internal audit of contractor population for misclassification risk indicators
ITID-53422.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53422.response: Engage employment and tax counsel to assess back-tax liability, reclassify affected workers, and remit any outstanding payroll tax obligations with the relevant authority.
metrics: Number of workers reclassified per review cycle
Estimated back-tax liability identified and remediated
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53422.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Differentiated from ITID-53421 by mechanism: avoiding the obligation entirely via misclassification, rather than withholding funds and failing to remit them.

playbook.name: Employee Misclassification to Avoid Payroll Tax Obligations
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that workers were intentionally misclassified as independent contractors to avoid payroll tax and benefit obligations, requiring investigation and remediation.

steps.title: Triage the misclassification indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or agency inquiry alleging that workers who function as employees have been intentionally classified as independent contractors to avoid payroll tax and benefits obligations.
steps.guidance: Review the affected worker population's job duties, control/supervision structure, and contractual terms against applicable worker-classification tests (e.g., IRS common-law factors).
steps.outcome: Credibility assessed with the affected worker population and classification basis documented.
steps.abort: If classification is well-supported under applicable tests, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance (and outside employment/tax counsel as warranted) to scope the investigation and quantify the scale of potential misclassification.
steps.guidance: Determine the number of affected workers, duration of misclassification, and estimated payroll-tax exposure.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with exposure estimate underway.

steps.title: Halt further onboarding under the questioned classification
steps.desc: Suspend further worker engagements under the questioned independent-contractor classification pattern pending review.
steps.guidance: Notify HR/Procurement to flag new contractor engagements matching the questioned pattern for legal review before onboarding.
steps.outcome: Further engagements under the questioned classification halted pending review.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold for HR and contractor records
steps.desc: Preserve all HR, contractor agreement, and payroll records relevant to the classification issue under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to HR, Legal, and relevant business unit managers.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Quantify the payroll tax and benefits exposure
steps.desc: Complete a forensic accounting/HR review to quantify unpaid payroll taxes, unremitted withholdings, and any benefits obligations across the affected worker population.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accountants and employment counsel to produce a worker-by-worker exposure schedule.
steps.outcome: Total exposure quantified and documented.

steps.title: Legal assessment of voluntary disclosure and reclassification remediation
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel evaluates voluntary disclosure to the IRS (e.g., Voluntary Classification Settlement Program) and state labor/tax authorities, and determines a reclassification remediation approach.
steps.guidance: Document the legal rationale for the disclosure and remediation approach chosen.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision with any required disclosure/remediation filings initiated.

steps.title: Reclassify affected workers and remediate classification controls
steps.desc: Reclassify affected workers as appropriate and implement a formal worker-classification review process for future engagements.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal on reclassification and update onboarding procedures to require classification-test documentation.
steps.outcome: Affected workers reclassified as appropriate and classification-review control implemented.

steps.title: Resume normal workforce operations under strengthened classification controls
steps.desc: Resume normal contractor engagement processes under the strengthened classification-review control.
steps.guidance: Confirm any required back-payments or remediation filings are on schedule.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened classification controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief leadership
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, disclosure decisions, and remediation; brief HR, Legal, and Finance leadership.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and leadership briefed.

ITID-53423.def: An unclassified or general instance of payroll tax fraud that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Payroll Tax Fraud leaf.
ITID-53423.purpose: Intake bucket for payroll tax fraud matters that do not yet fit the withholding-not-remitted or misclassification patterns.
scopeIncludes: Payroll tax irregularity reported without enough detail to determine the specific fraudulent mechanism
Novel or mixed-mechanism payroll tax fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed withheld-but-unremitted payroll tax (ITID-53421)
Confirmed employee misclassification to avoid payroll tax (ITID-53422)
ITID-53423.severity: High, consistent with other payroll-tax-fraud leaves, pending reclassification.
ITID-53423.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53423.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, and Finance leadership regardless of final classification.
indicators: Payroll tax discrepancy reported without a clearly identified mechanism
