vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard payroll tax compliance review controls applicable to all payroll tax fraud
ITID-53423.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels.
ITID-53423.response: Engage Legal/Compliance immediately and investigate to reclassify under a specific Payroll Tax Fraud leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53423.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Payroll Tax Fraud
playbook.description: A payroll tax fraud indicator that does not fit the non-remittance or worker-misclassification patterns, requiring general Compliance/Legal-led investigation.

steps.title: Triage the payroll tax fraud indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or anomaly suggesting payroll tax fraud that does not fit a more specific pattern, and determine credibility and scope.
steps.guidance: Review the specific payroll tax issue and available supporting documentation.
steps.outcome: Credibility assessed with the specific issue documented.
steps.abort: If the finding is explained by a legitimate treatment, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Compliance to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Compliance to formally scope and lead the investigation.
steps.guidance: Define the investigation scope and identify responsible personnel.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with an assigned lead.

steps.title: Halt the questioned payroll tax practice
steps.desc: Suspend the questioned payroll tax practice pending the outcome of the review.
steps.guidance: Notify Payroll/Finance to flag the practice for manual review.
steps.outcome: Questioned practice halted pending review.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold for payroll records
steps.desc: Preserve all relevant payroll and financial records under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to Payroll, Finance, and relevant personnel.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete forensic review and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Complete the review to quantify the payroll tax exposure and determine the correct position.
steps.guidance: Document all findings with supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented exposure.

steps.title: Legal assessment of disclosure and remediation obligations
steps.desc: Legal/Tax counsel evaluates whether disclosure to the IRS/state authority and remediation are warranted based on materiality.
steps.guidance: Document the legal rationale for the decision reached.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision with any required filings initiated.
steps.abort: If immaterial, document rationale and close the disclosure question.

steps.title: Resume normal payroll tax operations under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal payroll tax operations under any strengthened controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Confirm required remediation is on schedule.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update payroll tax controls
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update the general payroll-tax control procedure based on findings.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and procedures updated.

ITID-53431.def: Deliberate manipulation of the timing or existence of recorded revenue — booking sales that have not actually occurred, or recognizing legitimate revenue prematurely (before the earnings process is complete) — in order to inflate reported revenue and overall financial performance for a period.
ITID-53431.purpose: Captures financial statement fraud arising from recording revenue that is fictitious, or that is real but recognized in the wrong accounting period, to inflate reported financial performance.
scopeIncludes: Recording revenue for a sale with no underlying delivered good or service
Recognizing revenue on a contract before performance obligations are satisfied
Channel-stuffing (shipping excess product to distributors near period-end to inflate recorded sales)
scopeExcludes: Understating expenses rather than manipulating revenue (ITID-53432)
Concealing liabilities off the balance sheet (ITID-53433)
ITID-53431.severity: Critical — revenue recognition fraud is a core financial-statement-fraud pattern with severe regulatory (securities law), audit, and reputational consequences, and often triggers a restatement.
ITID-53431.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint; requires immediate involvement of external auditors and, for public companies, securities counsel.
ITID-53431.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, the Audit Committee, external auditors, and Compliance; for public companies, assess disclosure obligations under securities law without delay.
indicators: Revenue recognized with no corresponding shipment, delivery, or completed service record
Unusual spike in period-end sales followed by high subsequent-period returns (indicating channel stuffing)
Whistleblower report or auditor inquiry regarding revenue recognition timing
Persistent discrepancy between recognized revenue and cash collections
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Management pressure to meet revenue targets or analyst expectations
Inadequate internal controls over revenue recognition policy application
Insufficient independent review of large or unusual period-end transactions
controls: Independent internal audit review of period-end revenue recognition entries
Segregation of duties between sales, revenue recognition, and financial reporting
External auditor scrutiny of unusual revenue patterns near period-end
ITID-53431.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, external audit, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53431.response: Engage the Audit Committee and external auditors immediately, assess the need for a financial restatement, and for public companies evaluate securities-disclosure obligations with outside counsel.
metrics: Dollar value of revenue subject to restatement
Time from discovery to Audit Committee/legal escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53431.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response for this entire Tier-3 group.

playbook.name: Revenue Recognition Fraud (Fictitious/Premature Revenue Booking)
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that revenue was fictitiously or prematurely recognized to inflate reported financial results, requiring investigation and external-auditor/regulator-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the revenue recognition anomaly
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or analytical-review anomaly (e.g., revenue growth outpacing cash collections, unusual quarter-end booking spikes) suggesting fictitious or premature revenue recognition.
steps.guidance: Review the specific transactions/contracts flagged, compare booking dates against contractual delivery/performance-obligation satisfaction, and assess against applicable revenue-recognition standards.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the specific transactions, periods, and estimated overstatement identified.
steps.abort: If the recognition timing is supportable under applicable accounting standards, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Internal Audit, and forensic accounting to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Formally scope the investigation with Legal and Internal Audit leading, engaging forensic accountants given the financial-statement materiality risk.
steps.guidance: Determine the periods and business units in scope; assess whether outside counsel should lead to preserve privilege.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with privilege protections and forensic accounting support engaged.

steps.title: Halt use of the questioned recognition practice and issue a litigation hold
steps.desc: Suspend the questioned revenue-recognition practice for any pending period-end close and issue a formal litigation hold over all relevant records.
steps.guidance: Notify Finance/Accounting to flag transactions matching the questioned pattern for manual review before the next close; distribute the hold notice broadly.
steps.outcome: Questioned practice halted for pending closes and relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected revenue/close processes
steps.desc: Restrict or monitor access to the general ledger and revenue-recognition modules and processes involved to prevent further tampering during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT to apply access restrictions or enhanced logging for personnel under investigation.
steps.outcome: Access to affected systems restricted/monitored with an auditable trail.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting review and quantify the misstatement
steps.desc: Complete the forensic accounting analysis to quantify the extent of the revenue misstatement across all affected periods.
steps.guidance: Document each affected transaction with the correct recognition treatment and resulting adjustment.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented misstatement.

steps.title: Assess need for financial restatement and notify the external auditor
steps.desc: Legal/Finance leadership, in coordination with the Audit Committee, determines whether a financial restatement is required and formally notifies the external auditor of the findings.
steps.guidance: Consider materiality thresholds and SEC reporting implications (e.g., Item 4.02 Form 8-K for a determination that prior financials should no longer be relied upon, if publicly traded).
steps.outcome: Restatement determination documented and external auditor formally notified.
steps.abort: If immaterial and does not require restatement, document the materiality analysis and rationale.

steps.title: Address responsible personnel and remediate revenue-recognition controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate action against personnel found responsible and implement stronger revenue-recognition review/approval controls (e.g., independent contract review, segregation of duties).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal on personnel action; update the revenue-recognition policy and control documentation.
steps.outcome: Responsible personnel addressed and revenue-recognition control gap remediated.

steps.title: Resume normal financial reporting under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal revenue-recognition and close processes under the strengthened controls, completing any required restated filings.
steps.guidance: Confirm restated financials (if required) are filed and the external auditor's concerns are resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal reporting operations resumed with any required restatement completed.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, restatement decision, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the financial-statement impact.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee/Board briefed.

ITID-53432.def: Deliberate manipulation of reported expenses — through improper capitalization of costs that should be expensed, delayed recognition of known expenses, or outright omission of incurred costs — in order to understate total expenses and inflate reported profit for a period.
ITID-53432.purpose: Captures financial statement fraud arising from deliberately understating expenses to inflate reported profit.
scopeIncludes: Improperly capitalizing routine operating expenses as long-term assets to defer their impact on reported profit
Deliberately delaying recognition of a known liability or incurred cost into a later period
Omitting known expenses from the period's financial statements
scopeExcludes: Manipulating the revenue side of the income statement rather than expenses (ITID-53431)
Concealing liabilities entirely off the balance sheet rather than simply timing-shifting an expense (ITID-53433)
ITID-53432.severity: Critical — expense-understatement fraud is a core financial-statement-fraud pattern with severe regulatory, audit, and reputational consequences, often triggering a restatement.
ITID-53432.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint; requires immediate involvement of external auditors and, for public companies, securities counsel.
ITID-53432.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, the Audit Committee, external auditors, and Compliance; for public companies, assess disclosure obligations under securities law without delay.
indicators: Unusual or aggressive capitalization of costs typically expensed as incurred
Known invoices or liabilities not reflected in the period's financial statements
Auditor inquiry or whistleblower report regarding expense recognition timing
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Management pressure to meet profit targets or analyst expectations
Inadequate internal controls over expense recognition and capitalization policy
Insufficient independent review of capitalization decisions and period-end accruals
controls: Independent internal audit review of capitalization decisions and period-end accruals
Segregation of duties between operational spend approval and financial reporting
External auditor scrutiny of unusual expense-recognition patterns
ITID-53432.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, external audit, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53432.response: Engage the Audit Committee and external auditors immediately, assess the need for a financial restatement, and for public companies evaluate securities-disclosure obligations with outside counsel.
metrics: Dollar value of understated expenses subject to restatement
Time from discovery to Audit Committee/legal escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53432.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Expense Understatement to Inflate Reported Profit
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that expenses were intentionally understated, deferred, or misclassified to inflate reported profit, requiring investigation and external-auditor notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the expense-understatement anomaly
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or analytical-review anomaly (e.g., unusual capitalization of operating costs, unexplained accrual reversals) suggesting expenses were intentionally understated or misclassified.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged journal entries/accruals and compare against supporting documentation and applicable accounting policy.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the specific entries, periods, and estimated understatement identified.
steps.abort: If the treatment is supportable under applicable accounting policy, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Internal Audit, and forensic accounting to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Formally scope the investigation with Legal and Internal Audit leading, engaging forensic accountants given the financial-statement materiality risk.
steps.guidance: Determine the periods and business units in scope and whether outside counsel should lead to preserve privilege.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with forensic accounting support engaged.

steps.title: Halt use of the questioned expense treatment and issue a litigation hold
steps.desc: Suspend the questioned expense-classification/deferral practice for pending closes and issue a formal litigation hold over all relevant records.
steps.guidance: Notify Accounting to flag entries matching the questioned pattern for manual review; distribute the hold notice broadly.
steps.outcome: Questioned practice halted for pending closes and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Restrict access to the affected general ledger accounts
steps.desc: Restrict or monitor access to the general ledger accounts and journal-entry processes involved to prevent further tampering during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT to apply access restrictions or enhanced logging for personnel under investigation.
steps.outcome: Access to affected accounts restricted/monitored with an auditable trail.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting review and quantify the misstatement
steps.desc: Complete the forensic accounting analysis to quantify the extent of the profit overstatement across all affected periods.
steps.guidance: Document each affected entry with the correct expense treatment and resulting adjustment.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented misstatement.

steps.title: Assess need for financial restatement and notify the external auditor
steps.desc: Legal/Finance leadership, in coordination with the Audit Committee, determines whether a financial restatement is required and formally notifies the external auditor of the findings.
steps.guidance: Consider materiality thresholds and SEC reporting implications if publicly traded.
steps.outcome: Restatement determination documented and external auditor formally notified.
steps.abort: If immaterial and does not require restatement, document the materiality analysis and rationale.

steps.title: Address responsible personnel and remediate expense-recognition controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate action against personnel found responsible and implement stronger expense-recognition review/approval controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal on personnel action; update the expense-recognition policy and control documentation.
steps.outcome: Responsible personnel addressed and control gap remediated.

steps.title: Resume normal financial reporting under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal expense-recognition and close processes under the strengthened controls, completing any required restated filings.
steps.guidance: Confirm restated financials (if required) are filed and the external auditor's concerns are resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal reporting operations resumed with any required restatement completed.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, restatement decision, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the financial-statement impact.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee/Board briefed.

ITID-53433.def: Deliberate structuring or omission of liabilities — through undisclosed special-purpose entities, unrecorded guarantees, or other off-balance-sheet arrangements — to keep genuine financial obligations out of the company's reported balance sheet and thereby present a misleadingly favorable financial position to investors, lenders, or regulators.
ITID-53433.purpose: Captures financial statement fraud arising from concealing liabilities outside the reported balance sheet to present a misleadingly favorable financial position.
scopeIncludes: Undisclosed special-purpose entity used to hold debt outside the consolidated balance sheet
Unrecorded loan guarantee or contingent liability material to the company's financial position
Off-book side agreement shifting a genuine liability outside standard financial reporting
scopeExcludes: Revenue-side manipulation (ITID-53431)
Expense-timing manipulation on the income statement (ITID-53432)
ITID-53433.severity: Critical — off-balance-sheet liability concealment is among the most severe financial-statement-fraud patterns, with major regulatory, audit, lender, and reputational consequences.
ITID-53433.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint; requires immediate involvement of external auditors, lenders (where covenant-relevant), and, for public companies, securities counsel.
ITID-53433.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, the Audit Committee, external auditors, and Compliance; for public companies, assess disclosure obligations under securities law without delay, and notify lenders if loan covenants are affected.
indicators: Discovery of an undisclosed entity or guarantee during audit or due diligence
Whistleblower report alleging hidden liabilities or off-book arrangements
Lender or auditor inquiry regarding an unexplained financial-position discrepancy
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Deliberate structuring to conceal debt from lenders, investors, or regulators
Inadequate consolidation and disclosure review over related-party and special-purpose entities
Insufficient board/Audit Committee oversight of complex financing structures
controls: Independent review of all special-purpose entities and off-balance-sheet arrangements for consolidation/disclosure requirements
Board/Audit Committee oversight of complex financing structures
External auditor scrutiny of related-party and guarantee disclosures
ITID-53433.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, external audit, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53433.response: Engage the Audit Committee and external auditors immediately, assess the need for a financial restatement and lender notification, and for public companies evaluate securities-disclosure obligations with outside counsel.
metrics: Dollar value of previously undisclosed liabilities identified
Time from discovery to Audit Committee/legal escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53433.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Off-Balance-Sheet Liability Concealment
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance discovers indicators that material liabilities were concealed off the balance sheet through undisclosed arrangements, requiring investigation and external-auditor/regulator-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the concealment indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or third-party disclosure suggesting material liabilities (e.g., guarantees, special-purpose-entity obligations, undisclosed commitments) were kept off the balance sheet.
steps.guidance: Review the arrangement in question against applicable consolidation and disclosure accounting standards to assess whether it was properly reported.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the specific arrangement, counterparty, and estimated undisclosed liability identified.
steps.abort: If the arrangement was properly evaluated and disclosed under applicable standards, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Internal Audit, and forensic accounting to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Formally scope the investigation with Legal and Internal Audit leading, engaging forensic accountants and technical accounting specialists given the complexity and materiality risk.
steps.guidance: Determine all entities/arrangements potentially in scope and whether outside counsel should lead to preserve privilege.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with specialist support engaged.

steps.title: Halt further reliance on the concealment arrangement and issue a litigation hold
steps.desc: Suspend any further transactions relying on the questioned off-balance-sheet arrangement and issue a formal litigation hold over all relevant records.
steps.guidance: Notify Finance/Treasury/Legal to flag transactions with the counterparty/entity for review; distribute the hold notice broadly.
steps.outcome: Further reliance on the arrangement halted and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Restrict access to relevant contract and treasury records
steps.desc: Restrict or monitor access to the contract-management and treasury systems containing records of the arrangement to prevent further tampering.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT to apply access restrictions or enhanced logging for personnel under investigation.
steps.outcome: Access to affected records restricted/monitored with an auditable trail.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting review and quantify the undisclosed liability
steps.desc: Complete the forensic accounting and technical-accounting analysis to quantify the full undisclosed liability and determine the correct accounting treatment.
steps.guidance: Document the arrangement structure, counterparties, and the resulting balance-sheet/disclosure adjustment required.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented liability and correct accounting treatment.

steps.title: Assess need for financial restatement and notify the external auditor
steps.desc: Legal/Finance leadership, in coordination with the Audit Committee, determines whether a financial restatement is required and formally notifies the external auditor of the findings.
steps.guidance: Consider materiality thresholds and SEC reporting implications (e.g., Item 4.02 Form 8-K) if publicly traded.
steps.outcome: Restatement determination documented and external auditor formally notified.
steps.abort: If immaterial, document the materiality analysis and rationale.

steps.title: Unwind or properly disclose the arrangement and address responsible personnel
steps.desc: Unwind or properly account for and disclose the arrangement going forward, and take appropriate action against personnel found responsible for the concealment.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal, Finance, and HR on remediation and personnel actions.
steps.outcome: Arrangement properly accounted for/disclosed and responsible personnel addressed.

steps.title: Resume normal financial reporting under strengthened disclosure controls
steps.desc: Resume normal financial reporting under strengthened controls over the identification and disclosure of off-balance-sheet arrangements.
steps.guidance: Confirm any required restated filings are completed and the external auditor's concerns resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal reporting operations resumed with strengthened disclosure controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, restatement decision, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the financial-statement impact.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee/Board briefed.

ITID-53434.def: An unclassified or general instance of financial misreporting that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Misreporting Financials leaf.
ITID-53434.purpose: Intake bucket for financial misreporting matters that do not yet fit the revenue-recognition, expense-understatement, or off-balance-sheet-concealment patterns.
scopeIncludes: Financial misreporting concern raised without enough detail to determine the specific mechanism
Novel or mixed-mechanism financial statement fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed revenue recognition fraud (ITID-53431)
Confirmed expense understatement (ITID-53432)
Confirmed off-balance-sheet liability concealment (ITID-53433)
ITID-53434.severity: Critical, consistent with other financial-misreporting leaves, pending reclassification.
ITID-53434.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53434.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, the Audit Committee, and external auditors regardless of final classification.
indicators: Financial statement irregularity reported without a clearly identified mechanism
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard Audit Committee and external-audit oversight controls applicable to all financial misreporting
ITID-53434.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels.
ITID-53434.response: Engage the Audit Committee and Legal immediately and investigate to reclassify under a specific Misreporting Financials leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53434.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Financial Misreporting
playbook.description: A financial misreporting indicator that does not fit the revenue-recognition, expense-understatement, or off-balance-sheet patterns, requiring general Compliance/Legal-led investigation.

steps.title: Triage the financial misreporting indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, audit finding, or anomaly suggesting financial misreporting that does not fit a more specific pattern, and determine credibility and scope.
steps.guidance: Review the specific financial statement line item and available supporting documentation for the flagged issue.
steps.outcome: Credibility assessed with the specific issue and estimated impact documented.
steps.abort: If the finding is explained by a legitimate treatment, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/Internal Audit to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal/Internal Audit to formally scope and lead the investigation, engaging forensic accounting support as warranted.
steps.guidance: Define the investigation scope and privilege protections.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with an assigned lead.

steps.title: Halt use of the questioned reporting practice
steps.desc: Suspend the questioned reporting practice for any pending period-end close until the review concludes.
steps.guidance: Notify Finance/Accounting to flag the item for manual review.
steps.outcome: Questioned practice halted pending review.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold for relevant financial records
steps.desc: Preserve all relevant financial records, workpapers, and communications under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice to Finance, Accounting, and relevant personnel.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete forensic review and quantify the misstatement
steps.desc: Complete the review to quantify the financial misstatement and determine the correct accounting treatment.
steps.guidance: Document all findings with supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented misstatement.

steps.title: Assess restatement need and notify the external auditor
steps.desc: Determine whether a financial restatement is required and, if so, formally notify the external auditor of the findings.
steps.guidance: Document the materiality analysis and rationale for the decision reached.
steps.outcome: Restatement determination documented and external auditor notified if required.
steps.abort: If immaterial, document rationale and close the restatement question.

steps.title: Resume normal financial reporting under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal financial reporting under any strengthened controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Confirm any required restated filings are completed.
steps.outcome: Normal reporting operations resumed.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update financial-reporting controls
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update the general financial-reporting control procedure based on findings.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and procedures updated.

ITID-53441.def: Purchase or sale of the company's (or a related company's) securities by an individual in possession of material, non-public information about that company, or the passing ('tipping') of such information to another person who then trades on it, in advance of the information becoming public.
ITID-53441.purpose: Captures trading in company securities by an insider (or a tippee) based on material, non-public information ahead of a public disclosure event.
scopeIncludes: Executive or employee trading company stock ahead of an unannounced earnings result, merger, or other material event
Tipping a family member or associate with material non-public information who then trades
Trading during a company-imposed blackout period around a known material event
scopeExcludes: Manipulating the reported earnings figures themselves rather than trading on genuine undisclosed information (ITID-53443, where manipulation precedes trading)
General stock-price manipulation via promotional/false statements rather than trading on genuine inside knowledge (ITID-53442)
ITID-53441.severity: Critical — insider trading is a serious securities-law violation carrying personal criminal liability for the trader and tipper, plus significant regulatory and reputational exposure for the company.
ITID-53441.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint; requires immediate securities counsel involvement and, in many jurisdictions, regulator notification consideration.
ITID-53441.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, the Audit Committee, and outside securities counsel; do not delay pending internal fact-finding given regulatory reporting timelines.
indicators: Unusual trading volume or timing by an insider immediately before a material public announcement
Trading activity inconsistent with the individual's normal pattern occurring during a blackout period
Regulatory inquiry (e.g., exchange surveillance flag) regarding pre-announcement trading
Whistleblower report of tipping between an insider and an external trader
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Inadequate insider-trading policy enforcement or blackout-period monitoring
Insufficient restriction/pre-clearance requirements for insider trades
Lack of monitoring for information-sharing between insiders and external parties ahead of material events
controls: Trading blackout periods around material events with enforced pre-clearance
Insider list maintenance and periodic reminder of trading restrictions
Trade-surveillance monitoring for insider trading activity in coordination with brokers/exchanges
ITID-53441.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels (often supported by exchange/regulator trade surveillance) rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53441.response: Engage outside securities counsel immediately, assess regulator notification obligations, and take disciplinary/legal action against the individual(s) involved.
metrics: Number of suspected insider-trading incidents identified per period
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53441.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response for this entire Tier-3 group.

playbook.name: Insider Trading Based on Material Non-Public Information
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance/Legal discovers indicators that an employee traded (or tipped others to trade) company securities while in possession of material non-public information, requiring investigation and SEC-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the suspicious trading indicator
steps.desc: Assess a compliance-surveillance alert, whistleblower tip, or trading-blackout-window violation suggesting an employee traded company securities (or tipped others) while in possession of material non-public information (MNPI).
steps.guidance: Review the employee's trading activity against the timing of relevant MNPI events (e.g., earnings, M&A activity) and the company's trading-window/blackout calendar.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the specific trades, timing relative to MNPI, and individual(s) involved identified.
steps.abort: If the trade occurred during an open window with no MNPI access, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/outside securities counsel to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Immediately engage Legal and outside securities counsel to scope and lead the investigation given the criminal/civil securities-law exposure involved.
steps.guidance: Determine the scope of individuals and information involved; establish privilege protections from the outset.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped and led by securities counsel with privilege protections in place.

steps.title: Impose an immediate trading restriction on the individual(s) involved
steps.desc: Immediately restrict the implicated individual(s) from further trading in company securities and review/tighten the broader trading-blackout policy if a systemic gap is identified.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to place an ad hoc trading restriction and notify the broker/transfer agent as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Further trading by implicated individuals halted.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold and preserve communications
steps.desc: Preserve all communications, calendar records, and system access logs relevant to the implicated individual(s) and the MNPI in question under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT to preserve email, messaging, and access logs before any routine retention/deletion cycle runs.
steps.outcome: Relevant records and communications preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and determine trading-policy violations
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to determine the full scope of the trading activity, whether MNPI was in fact possessed and used, and whether any tipping occurred.
steps.guidance: Interview the implicated individual(s) and any downstream trade recipients; document all findings with supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with documented findings on MNPI possession, trading activity, and any tipping.

steps.title: Legal assessment of SEC self-reporting obligations
steps.desc: Securities counsel evaluates whether the company has an obligation or business rationale to self-report the conduct to the SEC and/or refer the matter to the DOJ, and determines next steps.
steps.guidance: Consider the SEC's cooperation-credit framework, materiality, and any parallel obligations (e.g., Section 16 reporting corrections); document the legal rationale.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision on SEC/DOJ referral with any required actions initiated.

steps.title: Take disciplinary action and strengthen insider-trading controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate disciplinary/termination action against the individual(s) involved and strengthen insider-trading surveillance and pre-clearance controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal on personnel action; review and update the insider trading policy, blackout calendar, and pre-clearance process.
steps.outcome: Disciplinary action taken and insider-trading controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal trading-compliance operations under strengthened surveillance
steps.desc: Lift the individual trading restriction as appropriate to the investigation outcome and resume normal trading-compliance operations under strengthened surveillance.
steps.guidance: Confirm any SEC/DOJ engagement is proceeding on schedule and Legal continues to monitor.
steps.outcome: Normal trading-compliance operations resumed with strengthened surveillance active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, SEC/DOJ disclosure decision, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the severity of securities-law exposure.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee/Board briefed.

ITID-53442.def: Coordinated scheme in which false, misleading, or exaggerated statements about the company are used to artificially inflate its stock price ('pump'), after which the individuals orchestrating or aware of the scheme sell their holdings at the inflated price ('dump'), leaving other investors holding devalued shares once the price collapses.
ITID-53442.purpose: Captures a scheme to artificially inflate the company's (or a related security's) stock price through false or misleading promotion, followed by insiders or coordinators selling ('dumping') at the inflated price.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated promotional campaign making false or exaggerated claims about the company to drive up share price
Insider or coordinator selling shares immediately after an artificially induced price spike
Use of social media, forums, or paid promotion to spread misleading information about the stock
scopeExcludes: Trading on genuine material non-public information without an accompanying false-promotion scheme (ITID-53441)
Manipulating underlying earnings figures rather than public statements/promotion (ITID-53443)
ITID-53442.severity: Critical — pump-and-dump schemes are a serious securities-law violation carrying personal criminal liability and severe regulatory and reputational exposure for the company if it or its personnel are implicated.
ITID-53442.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint; requires immediate securities counsel involvement and regulator notification consideration.
ITID-53442.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, Compliance, the Audit Committee, Investor Relations, and outside securities counsel.
indicators: Sudden, unexplained spike in trading volume and price accompanied by unverified promotional claims
Coordinated social-media or forum activity promoting the stock using misleading claims
Insider or coordinator selling a large position immediately following the price spike
Regulatory exchange surveillance flag on unusual trading activity
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector (though the promotional campaign itself may be delivered via social media/online channels, the fraud mechanism is the false statement and coordinated trading, not a technical intrusion)
rootCauses: Absence of monitoring for coordinated false promotional activity involving the company's securities
Inadequate internal controls preventing employees/insiders from participating in or benefiting from promotional schemes
Insufficient Investor Relations oversight of public statements about the company
controls: Monitoring for coordinated false-promotion activity referencing the company's securities
Clear policy prohibiting employee/insider participation in stock-promotion schemes
Rapid public correction/clarification process for false claims about the company
ITID-53442.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, Investor Relations, and regulatory-reporting channels (often supported by exchange trade surveillance) rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53442.response: Engage outside securities counsel immediately, issue a public clarification if the company is being used as the subject of a promotional scheme it did not orchestrate, and assess regulator notification obligations.
metrics: Number of suspected pump-and-dump incidents identified per period
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53442.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Pump-and-Dump Stock Price Manipulation Scheme
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance/Legal discovers indicators that individuals affiliated with the company participated in a pump-and-dump scheme to artificially inflate and then sell company (or related) securities, requiring investigation and SEC-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the market-manipulation indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, unusual promotional-activity report, or trading-surveillance alert suggesting coordinated promotional activity and subsequent selling by insiders or affiliates consistent with a pump-and-dump scheme.
steps.guidance: Review the promotional communications (social media, press releases, investor forums), trading volume/price patterns, and the timing of sales by implicated individuals.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the promotional activity, trading pattern, and individual(s) involved identified.
steps.abort: If the promotional activity and trading are legitimate and unconnected, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/outside securities counsel to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Immediately engage Legal and outside securities counsel to scope and lead the investigation given the criminal/civil securities-law exposure involved.
steps.guidance: Determine the scope of individuals, communications, and trading activity involved.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped and led by securities counsel with privilege protections in place.

steps.title: Halt any ongoing promotional activity and impose trading restrictions
steps.desc: Immediately halt any company-affiliated promotional activity contributing to the scheme and impose trading restrictions on implicated individuals.
steps.guidance: Issue a public correction/clarification if the company's own communications were misused or misrepresented; coordinate with Legal on trading restrictions.
steps.outcome: Promotional activity halted and further trading by implicated individuals restricted.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold and preserve communications/trading records
steps.desc: Preserve all promotional communications, trading records, and related correspondence under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT/Legal to preserve social media posts, emails, and messaging before any routine deletion cycle runs.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify the manipulation impact
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to determine the full scope of the promotional/trading scheme and quantify the price/volume impact and gains realized by implicated individuals.
steps.guidance: Interview implicated individuals and document all findings with supporting evidence, including any external coordination with third-party promoters.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with documented findings on scheme scope and financial impact.

steps.title: Legal assessment of SEC self-reporting obligations
steps.desc: Securities counsel evaluates whether the company has an obligation or business rationale to self-report the conduct to the SEC (and refer to FINRA/DOJ as applicable), and determines next steps.
steps.guidance: Consider the SEC's cooperation-credit framework and any parallel disclosure obligations; document the legal rationale.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision on SEC/FINRA/DOJ referral with any required actions initiated.

steps.title: Take disciplinary action and strengthen communications/trading controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate disciplinary/termination action against individuals involved and strengthen controls over external investor communications and insider trading pre-clearance.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal/Investor Relations on personnel action and communications-control updates.
steps.outcome: Disciplinary action taken and communications/trading controls strengthened.

steps.title: Restore market confidence and resume normal compliance operations
steps.desc: Issue any necessary corrective public disclosure and resume normal trading-compliance and investor-communications operations under strengthened controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Investor Relations and Legal on any public statement needed to correct the market record.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened controls and market confidence addressed.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, SEC/DOJ disclosure decision, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the severity of securities-law exposure.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee/Board briefed.

ITID-53443.def: Deliberate manipulation of reported earnings or other key financial metrics — timed and calibrated specifically to favorably move the stock price — shortly before an insider executes a planned sale of company shares, combining financial-statement fraud with a securities-trading benefit.
ITID-53443.purpose: Captures deliberate manipulation of reported earnings specifically timed to influence the stock price ahead of a planned insider sale.
scopeIncludes: Earnings manipulated upward ahead of a scheduled or planned insider stock sale
Selective or misleading timing of positive disclosures coordinated with an insider's trading window
Pattern of earnings management correlating with insider selling activity across multiple periods
scopeExcludes: Insider trading based on genuine material non-public information with no accompanying earnings manipulation (ITID-53441)
General earnings manipulation not specifically timed to or coordinated with an insider sale (Misreporting Financials, ITID-53431 branch)
ITID-53443.severity: Critical — this combines financial-statement fraud with securities-law violations (insider trading and potentially market manipulation), representing one of the most severe patterns in this category.
ITID-53443.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint; requires immediate securities counsel and Audit Committee involvement.
ITID-53443.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, the Audit Committee, external auditors, Compliance, and outside securities counsel.
indicators: Earnings adjustment or unusual accounting entry occurring shortly before a documented insider trading window opens
Pattern of insider sales consistently following favorable earnings surprises later found to be manipulated
Whistleblower report alleging coordination between earnings management and insider trading timing
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Personal financial incentive for an insider to inflate short-term stock price before a planned sale
Inadequate independent review of earnings adjustments occurring near insider trading windows
Insufficient correlation monitoring between accounting entries and insider trading activity
controls: Independent Audit Committee review of earnings adjustments occurring near insider trading windows
Correlation monitoring between financial-statement changes and insider trading activity
Mandatory pre-clearance and blackout-period enforcement for insider trades
ITID-53443.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, external audit, and regulatory-reporting channels rather than SOC technical monitoring.
ITID-53443.response: Engage the Audit Committee and outside securities counsel immediately, assess restatement and regulator-notification obligations, and pursue disciplinary/legal action against the individual(s) involved.
metrics: Number of suspected earnings-manipulation-ahead-of-sale incidents identified
Time from discovery to legal/compliance escalation
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53443.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Severity and response framed around compliance and legal escalation rather than SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Earnings Manipulation to Influence Stock Price Before Insider Sale
playbook.description: Internal Audit/Compliance/Legal discovers indicators that reported earnings were manipulated to influence the stock price ahead of a planned insider sale, requiring investigation and SEC-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the earnings-manipulation-timing indicator
steps.desc: Assess an audit finding, whistleblower tip, or analytical correlation between an unusual earnings adjustment/beat and a large insider sale shortly after, suggesting deliberate earnings manipulation timed to an insider transaction.
steps.guidance: Review the specific earnings adjustments in question, the timing of the insider's Rule 10b5-1 plan or discretionary sale, and whether a trading plan was adopted or modified suspiciously close to the manipulation.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the specific earnings items, sale timing, and individual(s) involved identified.
steps.abort: If the earnings item is supportable under applicable accounting standards and the sale followed a properly-adopted trading plan, close as false positive.
steps.tool: General ledger / Section 16 filings / trading plan records

steps.title: Engage Legal, Internal Audit, and forensic accounting to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Immediately engage Legal (including outside securities counsel) and forensic accountants to scope and lead the investigation given the combined accounting-fraud and securities-law exposure.
steps.guidance: Determine the periods, earnings items, and individuals in scope; establish privilege protections from the outset.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped and led with appropriate specialist support engaged.

steps.title: Impose a trading restriction on the individual(s) involved
steps.desc: Immediately restrict the implicated individual(s) from further trading pending the investigation outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to place an ad hoc trading restriction and notify the broker/transfer agent as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Further trading by implicated individuals halted.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold and halt further reliance on the questioned earnings figures
steps.desc: Preserve all relevant financial records and communications under a formal litigation hold, and suspend reliance on the questioned earnings figures in any pending filings or guidance.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT/Legal to preserve records; notify Finance/Investor Relations to pause related guidance communications pending review.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved and further reliance on questioned figures halted.

steps.title: Complete forensic accounting review and quantify the earnings misstatement
steps.desc: Complete the forensic accounting analysis to quantify the earnings misstatement and correlate it with the timing and proceeds of the insider sale.
steps.guidance: Document each affected entry with the correct treatment and the resulting adjustment, and quantify the insider's trading gain attributable to the manipulation.
steps.outcome: Forensic review completed with a quantified, documented misstatement and trading-gain analysis.

steps.title: Assess restatement need, notify the external auditor, and evaluate SEC self-reporting
steps.desc: Determine whether a financial restatement is required, notify the external auditor, and have securities counsel evaluate SEC self-reporting obligations and potential disgorgement of insider trading gains.
steps.guidance: Consider Sarbanes-Oxley Section 304 clawback implications for executive incentive compensation tied to the misstated results; document the legal rationale.
steps.outcome: Restatement/disclosure determinations documented with required notifications and filings initiated.

steps.title: Take disciplinary/clawback action and strengthen controls
steps.desc: Take appropriate disciplinary action, pursue compensation clawback where applicable, and strengthen earnings-review and trading pre-clearance controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal/Compensation Committee on personnel and clawback actions.
steps.outcome: Disciplinary/clawback action taken and controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal financial reporting and trading-compliance operations
steps.desc: Resume normal earnings-reporting and trading-compliance operations under the strengthened controls, completing any required restated filings.
steps.guidance: Confirm restated financials (if required) are filed and the external auditor's and SEC's concerns are resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and brief the Audit Committee/Board
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report covering findings, restatement/SEC disclosure decisions, and remediation; brief the Audit Committee/Board given the severity.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and Audit Committee/Board briefed.

ITID-53444.def: An unclassified or general instance of securities or stock manipulation that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Securities and Stock Manipulation leaf.
ITID-53444.purpose: Intake bucket for securities and stock manipulation matters that do not yet fit the insider-trading, pump-and-dump, or earnings-manipulation-before-sale patterns.
scopeIncludes: Securities-manipulation concern raised without enough detail to determine the specific mechanism
Novel or mixed-mechanism securities fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed insider trading on material non-public information (ITID-53441)
Confirmed pump-and-dump scheme (ITID-53442)
Confirmed earnings manipulation ahead of an insider sale (ITID-53443)
ITID-53444.severity: Critical, consistent with other securities-fraud leaves, pending reclassification.
ITID-53444.priority: P1 from a compliance/legal standpoint, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53444.escalation: Escalate immediately to Legal, the Audit Committee, and outside securities counsel regardless of final classification.
indicators: Unusual trading or disclosure activity reported without a clearly identified mechanism
vectors: Not applicable — this is a financial/regulatory-crime pattern, not a technical attack vector
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard insider-trading policy and trade-surveillance controls applicable to all securities fraud
ITID-53444.detection: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; detection and response run through legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels.
ITID-53444.response: Engage Legal and the Audit Committee immediately and investigate to reclassify under a specific Securities and Stock Manipulation leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
sops: Regulatory Disclosure and Legal Escalation SOP
ITID-53444.notes: Tax/regulatory/securities-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, compliance, and regulatory-reporting channels. Intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Securities and Stock Manipulation
playbook.description: A securities/stock manipulation indicator that does not fit the insider-trading, pump-and-dump, or earnings-manipulation-timing patterns, requiring general Compliance/Legal-led investigation and SEC-notification assessment.

steps.title: Triage the securities-manipulation indicator
steps.desc: Assess a whistleblower tip, surveillance alert, or anomaly suggesting securities/stock manipulation that does not fit a more specific pattern, and determine credibility and scope.
steps.guidance: Review the specific trading/communications activity flagged and available supporting documentation.
steps.outcome: Credibility assessed with the specific activity and individual(s) involved documented.
steps.abort: If the activity is legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Engage Legal/outside securities counsel to scope the investigation
steps.desc: Engage Legal and outside securities counsel to formally scope and lead the investigation.
steps.guidance: Define the investigation scope and establish privilege protections.
steps.outcome: Investigation formally scoped with an assigned lead.

steps.title: Impose trading restrictions on individual(s) involved
steps.desc: Restrict the implicated individual(s) from further trading pending the investigation outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to place an ad hoc trading restriction.
steps.outcome: Further trading by implicated individuals halted.

steps.title: Issue a litigation hold for relevant records
steps.desc: Preserve all relevant communications, trading records, and financial records under a formal litigation hold.
steps.guidance: Distribute the hold notice broadly to relevant personnel.
steps.outcome: Relevant records preserved under litigation hold.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify impact
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to determine the full scope of the activity and quantify any financial/market impact.
steps.guidance: Document all findings with supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with documented findings.

steps.title: Legal assessment of SEC self-reporting obligations
steps.desc: Securities counsel evaluates whether self-reporting to the SEC (or referral to FINRA/DOJ) is warranted based on the findings.
steps.guidance: Document the legal rationale for the decision reached.
steps.outcome: Documented legal decision with any required actions initiated.
steps.abort: If immaterial, document rationale and close the disclosure question.

steps.title: Resume normal trading-compliance operations under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Resume normal trading-compliance operations under any strengthened controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Confirm any required remediation or disclosures are on schedule.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with strengthened controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update trading-compliance procedures
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update the general trading-compliance control procedure based on findings.
steps.guidance: Preserve the report under the litigation hold retention schedule.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and procedures updated.

ITID-53511.def: Fraud in which an individual applies for a loan or line of credit under their genuine identity but submits fabricated pay stubs, tax documents, or employer verification to qualify for an amount or terms they would not otherwise receive.
ITID-53511.purpose: Captures loan applications submitted under the applicant's own true identity but supported by falsified income or employment documentation.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated or altered pay stubs, W-2s, or bank statements submitted with a loan application
Fictitious employer or inflated income claims verified through a collusive third party
Self-employed applicants overstating business revenue with falsified records
scopeExcludes: Loan applications using a stolen or synthetic identity (ITID-53512, ITID-53521)
Straw borrower arrangements where the named applicant is not the true beneficiary (ITID-53513)
ITID-53511.severity: Medium. Financial exposure is bounded by the loan amount and is a lending-institution/finance-team concern more than an active SOC incident unless internal systems were manipulated to produce the falsified documents.
ITID-53511.priority: P3 in most cases, routed to fraud/underwriting review rather than SOC triage.
ITID-53511.escalation: Escalate to the fraud investigations/underwriting team for documentation verification; escalate to the SOC only if internal document-generation systems or employee accounts were misused to fabricate the records.
indicators: Pay stub or bank statement with inconsistent formatting, fonts, or metadata versus known-authentic templates
Employer verification call reaching a number not associated with the claimed employer
Income-to-debt ratio inconsistent with other application data
vectors: Use of commercially available document-editing templates to fabricate pay stubs
Collusion with a third party posing as an HR verifier
rootCauses: Insufficient independent verification of income/employment prior to loan approval
Reliance on applicant-supplied documents without cross-checking against payroll-provider databases
controls: Third-party income/employment verification services (e.g., payroll-database cross-checks)
Document forensics review on submitted financial documentation
Underwriting red-flag rules for inconsistent income documentation
ITID-53511.detection: Minimal technical detection surface; caught primarily through underwriting document review and post-funding audit rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-53511.response: Fraud/underwriting team investigates and denies or unwinds the loan; law enforcement referral if the scheme is part of an organized pattern.
metrics: Number of falsified-documentation loan applications caught per quarter
Dollar exposure prevented at underwriting vs. discovered post-funding
detections: Document-forensics anomaly flags on submitted financial paperwork
ITID-53511.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Loan Application Using Falsified Income/Employment Documentation
playbook.description: The company, acting as a lender, detects that a loan applicant submitted falsified income or employment documentation to qualify for a loan, requiring underwriting investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the underwriting documentation anomaly
steps.desc: Identify indicators that submitted income/employment documentation (pay stubs, W-2s, employer verification) is falsified, inconsistent, or fails independent verification.
steps.guidance: Cross-check submitted documents against employer-verification services, tax-transcript data, and document-forensics tools for signs of alteration or fabrication.
steps.outcome: Confirmed documentation discrepancy with the specific falsified elements and application identified.
steps.abort: If verification confirms the documentation is accurate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope the applicant's full application and any related applications
steps.desc: Determine whether the applicant submitted other applications or whether the falsification pattern appears linked to other applicants (e.g., a common preparer or broker).
steps.guidance: Search the loan origination system for related applications sharing the same preparer, employer, address, or contact information.
steps.outcome: Scope of related applications/patterns identified.

steps.title: Halt the application and freeze any disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt further processing of the application, and if funds have already been disbursed, initiate an emergency freeze/recall through Treasury and the receiving institution.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting to place the application on fraud hold and with Treasury to identify and freeze any disbursed funds.
steps.outcome: Application processing halted and any disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds have already been fully drawn and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Flag the applicant and associated identifiers across the origination system
steps.desc: Flag the applicant's identity and any associated preparer/broker in the fraud-prevention system to block further applications pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add the applicant and related identifiers to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: Applicant and associated identifiers flagged with no further applications processed.

steps.title: Complete the fraud investigation and decision the application
steps.desc: Complete the investigation into the falsified documentation and formally decline/void the application, pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and final application disposition for the file.
steps.outcome: Application declined/voided and recovery of disbursed funds pursued.

steps.title: Assess and file a Suspicious Activity Report if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates whether the falsification pattern meets SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria (dollar thresholds, pattern indicators) and document the rationale for filing or not filing.
steps.outcome: SAR filing decision documented and filed with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen income/employment verification controls
steps.desc: Enhance underwriting verification procedures (e.g., mandatory third-party income-verification services, tighter document-forensics screening) to reduce recurrence.
steps.guidance: Update the underwriting policy and communicate the change to Underwriting staff.
steps.outcome: Updated verification control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal loan-origination operations under enhanced verification
steps.desc: Resume normal loan-origination processing under the strengthened verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence of similar fraud patterns.
steps.guidance: Track fraud-flag rates post-implementation to confirm the control change is effective.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced verification controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update underwriting fraud-detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update underwriting fraud-detection training and procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53512.def: Fraud in which an adversary uses a real victim's stolen personally identifiable information (name, SSN, date of birth) to apply for and obtain a loan or credit line without the victim's knowledge, distinct from a wholly fabricated synthetic identity.
ITID-53512.purpose: Captures loan applications submitted using another real person's stolen identity rather than the applicant's own.
scopeIncludes: Loan application filed using a real victim's stolen SSN and identity details
Account takeover of an existing credit profile to originate a new loan in the victim's name
Use of identity information obtained from a prior data breach or phishing campaign
scopeExcludes: Applications supported by falsified documents but using the applicant's own true identity (ITID-53511)
Applications built on a synthetic (part-real, part-fabricated) identity (ITID-53521)
Straw borrower schemes where the named party knowingly participates (ITID-53513)
ITID-53512.severity: Medium-High for the victim and institution; higher when the stolen identity information originated from the company's own customer/employee data.
ITID-53512.priority: P2 if traced back to a company data exposure as the source of the stolen identity; P3 if the identity theft originated externally and the company is only the lender of record.
ITID-53512.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations for loan reversal and victim remediation; escalate to the SOC and privacy/legal teams if the stolen identity data can be traced to a breach of company-held records.
indicators: Loan application details matching a known identity-theft victim report
Application submitted from a device/IP inconsistent with the named applicant's known history
Credit-bureau alert or freeze inconsistency at time of application
vectors: Identity data purchased from breach-data marketplaces
Phishing targeting individuals for SSN/identity details
Insider access to company-held customer PII
rootCauses: Weak identity-proofing at loan origination (knowledge-based authentication alone)
No cross-check against credit-freeze/fraud-alert flags
Prior data exposure of customer PII providing raw material for the fraud
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Multi-factor identity verification at loan origination (beyond knowledge-based authentication)
Cross-check against credit-bureau fraud alerts/freezes
Monitoring for identity data appearing in breach-data marketplaces
ITID-53512.detection: Identity-verification and credit-bureau cross-check controls at origination are the primary detection surface; SOC involvement is limited to tracing whether company-held data was the source.
ITID-53512.response: Fraud investigations reverses the loan and supports victim remediation; SOC investigates only if company data exposure is implicated as the identity source.
metrics: Number of stolen-identity loan applications caught per quarter
Percentage traced to a company data exposure
Victim remediation time
sops: Identity Theft Loan Fraud Response SOP
detections: Breach-data marketplace monitoring for exposed identity data
ITID-53512.notes: Distinguished from synthetic identity fraud (ITID-53521) by the use of a genuine, real victim's identity rather than a fabricated composite. Distinguished from ITID-53511 by the theft of identity rather than falsification of the applicant's own supporting documents.

playbook.name: Loan Application Using Stolen Identity
playbook.description: The company, acting as a lender, detects that a loan application was submitted using a stolen identity (identity theft), requiring victim notification, underwriting investigation, and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the identity-theft indicator
steps.desc: Identify indicators that the application uses a stolen identity — a victim dispute, an identity-verification failure, or a mismatch between application data and the real identity-holder's known information.
steps.guidance: Cross-check the application against identity-verification services, credit-bureau fraud alerts, and any victim-reported identity-theft complaint.
steps.outcome: Confirmed identity theft with the real identity-holder and impersonated application identified.
steps.abort: If the applicant is confirmed to be the legitimate identity-holder, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the source of the stolen identity data
steps.desc: Investigate how the applicant obtained the victim's identity data, where feasible (e.g., prior data breach, phishing, insider misuse), to inform broader risk assessment.
steps.guidance: Review the application's IP/device fingerprint and correlate against known fraud rings or breach-exposed identity data if available through threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: Likely source of the stolen identity data identified or noted as undeterminable.

steps.title: Halt the application and freeze any disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt further processing of the fraudulent application, and if funds have already been disbursed, initiate an emergency freeze/recall.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting to place the application on fraud hold and with Treasury to identify and freeze any disbursed funds.
steps.outcome: Application processing halted and any disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds have already been fully drawn and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Notify the identity-theft victim and place a fraud alert on their file
steps.desc: Notify the actual identity-holder (victim) that a fraudulent application was submitted in their name, and place a fraud alert/flag on their record to prevent further misuse.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's identity-theft victim-notification procedure and provide the victim guidance on credit-bureau fraud alerts/freezes.
steps.outcome: Victim notified and fraud alert placed on their record.

steps.title: Void the fraudulent application and correct victim records
steps.desc: Formally void/decline the fraudulent application and ensure no adverse record (credit inquiry, loan liability) remains attached to the victim's identity.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with credit bureaus to remove any erroneous inquiry/tradeline resulting from the fraudulent application.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent application voided and victim's records corrected.

steps.title: Refer the matter to law enforcement and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Refer the identity-theft fraud to law enforcement and have the Compliance/BSA officer evaluate SAR-filing criteria and file with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale for filing or not filing.
steps.outcome: Law-enforcement referral made and SAR filing decision documented/filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If SAR criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen identity-verification controls
steps.desc: Enhance identity-verification procedures (e.g., knowledge-based authentication, document liveness checks, database cross-referencing) to reduce recurrence.
