steps.guidance: Update the underwriting/KYC policy and communicate the change to Underwriting staff.
steps.outcome: Updated identity-verification control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal loan-origination operations under enhanced identity verification
steps.desc: Resume normal loan-origination processing under the strengthened identity-verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track identity-fraud flag rates post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced identity-verification controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update identity-theft response procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, victim-notification outcome, and SAR/recovery outcome; update identity-theft response training and procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53513.def: Fraud in which a real person (the 'straw borrower'), often paid or coerced, knowingly applies for and obtains a loan using their own genuine, valid identity, while the funds and true benefit go to an undisclosed third party who would not have qualified or wished to be named on the loan.
ITID-53513.purpose: Captures loan fraud schemes in which a real, consenting individual applies as the named borrower on behalf of an undisclosed true beneficiary.
scopeIncludes: A recruited individual with good credit applying for a loan on behalf of an organizer who directs the proceeds
Straw borrower schemes used to obscure the true beneficiary's involvement in a lending relationship
Repeated use of the same straw borrower across multiple loan applications
scopeExcludes: Loan applications using a stolen identity without the named applicant's knowledge (ITID-53512)
Loan applications using a synthetic, fabricated identity (ITID-53521)
ITID-53513.severity: Medium. The institution's identity-verification controls are not defeated (the borrower is real and consenting), but the loan's true purpose and beneficiary are misrepresented.
ITID-53513.priority: P3, routed to fraud investigations for pattern analysis rather than SOC triage.
ITID-53513.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations when a pattern of shared addresses, devices, or organizers across multiple straw-borrower applications is identified; escalate to legal/compliance if it indicates organized lending fraud.
indicators: Multiple unrelated loan applicants sharing a device, IP address, or disbursement account
Borrower with limited financial sophistication applying for an unusually large or complex loan
Loan proceeds immediately transferred out to a third party after disbursement
vectors: Recruitment of financially vulnerable individuals to act as named borrowers
Coordinated applications through a common organizer/broker
rootCauses: No network analysis linking applications by shared device/IP/disbursement-account fingerprints
Insufficient scrutiny of fund disbursement/use-of-proceeds patterns post-funding
controls: Cross-application network/link analysis on device, IP, and disbursement-account fingerprints
Post-funding monitoring of proceeds disbursement patterns
ITID-53513.detection: Detected primarily through fraud-analytics link analysis across applications rather than any SOC technical telemetry.
ITID-53513.response: Fraud investigations unwinds affected loans and refers organized patterns to law enforcement; SOC has no role absent a technical intrusion component.
metrics: Number of straw-borrower schemes identified per quarter
Number of applications linked to a single organizer/network
ITID-53513.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Straw Borrower Loan Fraud
playbook.description: The company, acting as a lender, detects indicators that a loan application uses a straw borrower — a real person recruited to apply on behalf of an ineligible party who receives the loan proceeds/benefit — requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the straw-borrower pattern
steps.desc: Identify indicators that the named borrower is not the true beneficiary of the loan — e.g., mismatched use-of-funds, proceeds routed to a third party, or the borrower's profile inconsistent with the purpose/property involved.
steps.guidance: Review disbursement destination, occupancy/use representations, and any third-party involvement in the application process for straw-borrower red flags.
steps.outcome: Confirmed straw-borrower pattern with the true beneficiary and named borrower identified.
steps.abort: If the arrangement is a legitimate co-borrower/guarantor structure properly disclosed, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify the organizer/recruiter and scope related applications
steps.desc: Determine whether a broker, organizer, or recruiter coordinated multiple straw-borrower applications, and identify all related applications in the scheme.
steps.guidance: Search the loan origination system for applications sharing the same broker, property, or fund-disbursement destination.
steps.outcome: Scope of the scheme and any organizer/recruiter identified.

steps.title: Halt all related applications and freeze disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt processing of all applications identified as part of the scheme, and freeze/recall any disbursed funds where possible.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting and Treasury across all related applications simultaneously to prevent tipping off remaining participants.
steps.outcome: All related applications halted and disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds have already been fully drawn and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Flag all identified participants across the origination system
steps.desc: Flag the straw borrower(s), organizer/recruiter, and true beneficiary in the fraud-prevention system to block further applications pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add all identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: All identified participants flagged with no further applications processed.

steps.title: Complete the scheme investigation and decision all related applications
steps.desc: Complete the investigation into the full straw-borrower scheme and formally decline/void all related applications, pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and disposition for each application in the file.
steps.outcome: All related applications declined/voided and recovery of disbursed funds pursued.

steps.title: Refer to law enforcement and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Refer the scheme to law enforcement given its organized nature and have the Compliance/BSA officer evaluate and file a SAR with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale, noting the coordinated/organized nature of straw-borrower schemes typically warrants filing.
steps.outcome: Law-enforcement referral made and SAR filed as warranted.

steps.title: Strengthen underwriting controls to detect straw-borrower patterns
steps.desc: Enhance underwriting analytics to detect straw-borrower red flags (e.g., disbursement-destination mismatches, broker-clustering analysis).
steps.guidance: Update the underwriting policy and fraud-analytics rule set to flag similar patterns earlier.
steps.outcome: Updated detection control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal loan-origination operations under enhanced pattern detection
steps.desc: Resume normal loan-origination processing under the strengthened straw-borrower detection controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track fraud-flag rates post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced detection controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update straw-borrower detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update fraud-analytics rules and underwriting staff training.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53514.def: An unclassified/general leaf for loan-application fraud that has not been further classified into falsified-documentation (ITID-53511), stolen-identity (ITID-53512), or straw-borrower (ITID-53513) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53514.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for fraudulent loan applications that do not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported loan-application fraud pending triage and subtype classification
Ambiguous cases combining multiple fraud elements not yet disentangled
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53511, ITID-53512, or ITID-53513
Synthetic identity fraud, tracked separately under ITID-53521-53523
ITID-53514.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53514.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once a specific subtype is determined.
ITID-53514.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations for initial triage; reclassify to a specific ITID-535xx leaf as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Loan-application fraud flagged by underwriting but not yet root-caused
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard loan-fraud triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53514.detection: Not applicable until triaged; detection coverage is inherited from whichever specific subtype the case is ultimately classified under.
ITID-53514.response: Fraud investigations triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-535xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Loan Fraud Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53514.notes: Intake bucket only. Cases should be reclassified into ITID-53511, ITID-53512, or ITID-53513 as soon as sufficient information is available; this leaf should not accumulate a stable long-term population.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Fraudulent Loan Application
playbook.description: A fraudulent loan application indicator that does not fit the falsified-documentation, stolen-identity, or straw-borrower patterns, requiring general underwriting-fraud investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the loan-application fraud indicator
steps.desc: Identify indicators that a loan application involves fraud not fitting a more specific pattern, and confirm the anomaly against underwriting verification sources.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged application against available verification data and underwriting fraud-scoring outputs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraud indicator with the specific application and discrepancy documented.
steps.abort: If verification confirms the application is legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism and scope related applications
steps.desc: Investigate how the fraud was perpetrated and whether it is linked to other applications or a broader pattern.
steps.guidance: Search the loan origination system for related applications sharing common identifiers.
steps.outcome: Fraud mechanism identified and scope of related applications determined.

steps.title: Halt the application and freeze any disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt further processing of the application and freeze/recall any disbursed funds where possible.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting and Treasury to place the application on hold and identify any disbursed funds.
steps.outcome: Application processing halted and disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Flag the applicant across the origination system
steps.desc: Flag the applicant and any associated identifiers in the fraud-prevention system to block further applications pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: Applicant flagged with no further applications processed.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and decision the application
steps.desc: Complete the fraud investigation and formally decline/void the application, pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and final application disposition.
steps.outcome: Application declined/voided and recovery pursued.

steps.title: Assess and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates whether the fraud pattern meets SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale.
steps.outcome: SAR filing decision documented and filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Resume normal loan-origination operations under enhanced controls
steps.desc: Resume normal loan-origination processing under any strengthened controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Track fraud-flag rates post-implementation.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update loan-fraud detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update the general loan-fraud detection procedure.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53521.def: Fraud in which an adversary constructs a new identity that does not correspond to any single real person by blending a genuine identifier (typically an SSN) with a fabricated name, date of birth, and address, then uses that composite identity to open financial accounts or apply for credit.
ITID-53521.purpose: Captures the creation of a synthetic identity by combining a real individual's partial identity elements (commonly a child's or deceased person's SSN) with fabricated personal details.
scopeIncludes: Combining a stolen or purchased genuine SSN with a fabricated name/address to create a new credit profile
Use of a minor's or deceased individual's SSN as the genuine component of the composite identity
Initial account-opening activity establishing the synthetic identity's credit file
scopeExcludes: Use of the synthetic identity to build credit history over time in preparation for bust-out fraud (ITID-53522)
Loan applications using a real victim's complete stolen identity (ITID-53512)
ITID-53521.severity: Medium at creation stage, rising as the synthetic identity accumulates credit lines and approaches a bust-out event.
ITID-53521.priority: P3 at initial detection, escalating to P2 if linked to an active bust-out pattern (see ITID-53522).
ITID-53521.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations for credit-file forensics; escalate to law enforcement (often via SAR filing) once a synthetic-identity network is confirmed.
indicators: Credit application with an SSN that does not match the name/date-of-birth combination on file with the issuing authority
SSN belonging to a minor being used on an adult credit application
No prior credit history despite an application implying an established financial history
vectors: Purchase of stolen SSNs (particularly minors' or deceased individuals') from breach-data marketplaces
Fabrication of supporting identity documents to pair with the genuine SSN
rootCauses: Credit-issuance identity verification that does not cross-check SSN-to-name/DOB consistency against authoritative sources
No specific screening for minor/deceased SSN usage
controls: SSN-to-identity consistency verification against authoritative data sources at account opening
Screening for minor and deceased-individual SSN usage
Synthetic-identity detection analytics on new-account applications
ITID-53521.detection: Primarily detected through credit-bureau synthetic-identity analytics and identity-verification mismatches rather than SOC telemetry.
ITID-53521.response: Fraud investigations closes the fraudulent account and files a SAR where required; SOC has no role absent a company data-exposure link.
metrics: Number of synthetic identities detected at creation stage per quarter
Percentage using minor/deceased SSNs
ITID-53521.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Synthetic Identity Built from Combined Real and Fabricated PII
playbook.description: The company, acting as a lender, detects that an applicant's identity is a synthetic identity — combining real (often stolen) and fabricated personally identifiable information — requiring underwriting investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the synthetic-identity indicator
steps.desc: Identify indicators that the applicant's identity combines real and fabricated PII — e.g., an SSN issued before the claimed date of birth, a thin/inconsistent credit file, or identity-verification service flags suggesting a non-existent person.
steps.guidance: Run the application through identity-verification and synthetic-identity-detection analytics comparing SSN issuance data, credit-file depth, and cross-bureau consistency.
steps.outcome: Confirmed synthetic-identity indicator with the specific inconsistencies documented.
steps.abort: If the identity verifies as a legitimate individual, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine whether the real PII component belongs to an identifiable victim
steps.desc: Investigate whether the real component of the synthetic identity (e.g., a stolen SSN) belongs to an identifiable individual, particularly checking for use of a minor's or deceased person's SSN.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the SSN against death-master-file and known-minor indicators where available.
steps.outcome: Real-PII source identified or confirmed as undeterminable; victim-notification need assessed.

steps.title: Halt the application and freeze any disbursed funds/extended credit
steps.desc: Immediately halt further processing of the application, and if credit/funds have already been extended, initiate an emergency freeze/recall and suspend the associated credit line.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting to place the application on fraud hold and with Treasury/Card Operations to freeze any extended credit.
steps.outcome: Application/credit-line processing halted and any extended funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds/credit have already been fully drawn and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Notify the real-PII victim if identifiable and flag the synthetic identity
steps.desc: If a real identifiable victim's PII was used, notify them per the identity-theft victim procedure; flag the synthetic identity across the fraud-prevention system.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's victim-notification procedure and add the synthetic-identity profile to the internal fraud watchlist and applicable industry consortium databases.
steps.outcome: Victim notified where identifiable and synthetic identity flagged to prevent further use.

steps.title: Void the application/credit line and correct any victim records
steps.desc: Formally void/decline the application or close the associated credit line, and correct any erroneous credit-bureau records tied to the real-PII victim.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with credit bureaus to remove any erroneous inquiry/tradeline resulting from the synthetic-identity application.
steps.outcome: Application/credit line voided and victim records corrected where applicable.

steps.title: File a SAR and refer to law enforcement
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria for the synthetic-identity fraud and files with FinCEN if warranted, referring the matter to law enforcement given the fraud-ring risk.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria; synthetic-identity fraud frequently indicates organized fraud-ring activity warranting filing.
steps.outcome: SAR filed as warranted and law-enforcement referral made.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen synthetic-identity detection controls
steps.desc: Enhance identity-verification analytics (e.g., SSN-issuance validation, credit-file-depth scoring, device/behavioral analytics) to catch synthetic identities earlier in underwriting.
steps.guidance: Update the underwriting/KYC policy and fraud-analytics rule set.
steps.outcome: Updated detection control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal underwriting operations under enhanced synthetic-identity detection
steps.desc: Resume normal loan/credit-origination processing under the strengthened synthetic-identity detection controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track synthetic-identity flag rates post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced detection controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update synthetic-identity response procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update synthetic-identity detection training and procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53522.def: Fraud in which an already-established synthetic identity is used responsibly over months or years to build a legitimate-looking credit history and raise credit limits, before the perpetrator maxes out all available credit lines simultaneously ('busts out') with no intent to repay.
ITID-53522.purpose: Captures the credit-building and eventual bust-out phase of a synthetic identity fraud scheme, distinguishing it from the initial identity-creation stage.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate on-time payment behavior on a synthetic identity's accounts to build credit-bureau trust
Coordinated, simultaneous maxing-out of multiple credit lines tied to the same synthetic identity
Sudden cessation of payment activity following a bust-out event
scopeExcludes: Initial construction of the synthetic identity (ITID-53521)
Legitimate credit-building behavior by a real individual with no fabricated identity elements
ITID-53522.severity: High. Bust-out schemes concentrate losses into a single event after a long dormancy period, often across multiple credit lines/institutions simultaneously.
ITID-53522.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the pattern is detected in-progress with additional credit-line increases still pending approval.
ITID-53522.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations immediately upon detection of coordinated credit-limit utilization spikes; escalate to law enforcement/SAR filing once bust-out is confirmed.
indicators: Sudden, near-simultaneous maxing of credit limits across multiple accounts held by the same identity
Cessation of payments immediately following a credit-limit increase
Credit-limit-increase requests clustered shortly before the utilization spike
vectors: Long-dormant synthetic identity accounts activated in a coordinated bust-out event
Requesting multiple credit-limit increases shortly before executing the bust-out
rootCauses: Credit-limit-increase approval processes that do not weight recent behavioral-change signals
No cross-institution data sharing on synthetic-identity utilization patterns
controls: Behavioral analytics flagging sudden utilization spikes following dormancy
Conservative credit-limit-increase review for accounts with limited credit history depth
Industry consortium data-sharing on known synthetic-identity indicators
ITID-53522.detection: Detected through credit-bureau/issuer behavioral analytics on utilization and payment-pattern change; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53522.response: Fraud investigations charges off the loss, files a SAR, and shares indicators with industry consortiums; SOC has no role.
metrics: Dollar loss per confirmed bust-out event
Time from credit-building start to bust-out
Percentage of bust-outs caught pre-execution via behavioral analytics
sops: Bust-Out Fraud Detection and Response SOP
ITID-53522.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Synthetic Identity Used to Build Credit History Before Bust-Out Fraud
playbook.description: The company, acting as a lender, detects that a synthetic identity was cultivated over time to build a legitimate-looking credit history and then abruptly maxed out credit lines with no intent to repay (bust-out), requiring urgent containment and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the bust-out pattern on a previously-performing account
steps.desc: Identify indicators of a bust-out in progress or completed — a previously well-performing account suddenly maxing out available credit, requesting credit-limit increases shortly before default, or a sudden spike in cash-advance/high-risk transactions.
steps.guidance: Review account transaction velocity, recent credit-limit-increase requests, and payment-history change relative to the account's prior performance pattern.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bust-out pattern with the account, exposure amount, and timeline documented.
steps.abort: If the change in usage is explained by legitimate circumstances (e.g., documented income change with continued payments), close as false positive.

steps.title: Confirm the underlying identity as synthetic and scope related accounts
steps.desc: Confirm the account holder's identity is synthetic (built from combined real/fabricated PII) and check for other accounts opened using the same or related synthetic identities.
steps.guidance: Run synthetic-identity detection analytics and search for accounts sharing common application data elements (address, phone, employer).
steps.outcome: Synthetic-identity confirmation and scope of related accounts documented.

steps.title: Immediately freeze the account(s) to stop further credit utilization
steps.desc: Immediately suspend the credit line(s)/account(s) involved to prevent any further drawdown, given bust-out fraud typically proceeds rapidly once initiated.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Card Operations/Credit Risk to place an emergency freeze on all identified related accounts simultaneously.
steps.outcome: Further credit utilization on the account(s) halted.

steps.title: Flag the synthetic identity and related accounts across the fraud-prevention system
steps.desc: Flag the synthetic identity and all related accounts in the fraud-prevention system and applicable industry consortium database to prevent the same identity from opening new accounts elsewhere.
steps.guidance: Submit the confirmed synthetic-identity profile to relevant industry fraud-consortium data-sharing services.
steps.outcome: Synthetic identity and related accounts flagged internally and shared with the industry consortium.

steps.title: Charge off the account(s) and quantify total exposure
steps.desc: Formally charge off the affected account(s) as fraud loss and quantify the total exposure across all related synthetic-identity accounts.
steps.guidance: Document the full loss quantification for the fraud-loss reserve and financial reporting.
steps.outcome: Accounts charged off and total exposure quantified and documented.

steps.title: File a SAR and refer to law enforcement
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria for the bust-out scheme and files with FinCEN, referring the matter to law enforcement given the organized-fraud-ring risk typically associated with bust-out schemes.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria; bust-out schemes frequently warrant filing given the deliberate, organized nature of the fraud.
steps.outcome: SAR filed and law-enforcement referral made.

steps.title: Strengthen account-monitoring controls for bust-out pattern detection
steps.desc: Enhance transaction-monitoring analytics to detect bust-out precursor patterns (credit-limit-increase requests, sudden utilization spikes) earlier.
steps.guidance: Update the fraud-analytics rule set and account-monitoring thresholds.
steps.outcome: Updated detection control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal account operations under enhanced bust-out monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal account-monitoring operations under the strengthened bust-out detection controls and monitor closely for recurrence across the broader portfolio.
steps.guidance: Run a portfolio-wide scan for similar precursor patterns following the incident.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active across the portfolio.

steps.title: Document incident and update synthetic-identity/bust-out response procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update bust-out detection training and procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Credit Risk and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53523.def: An unclassified/general leaf for synthetic identity fraud that has not been further classified into identity-creation (ITID-53521) or credit-building/bust-out (ITID-53522) stages at the time of intake.
ITID-53523.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for synthetic identity fraud that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported synthetic-identity fraud pending stage classification
Cases where the identity's lifecycle stage is not yet determinable from available data
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53521 or ITID-53522
ITID-53523.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible stage pending reclassification.
ITID-53523.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the lifecycle stage is determined.
ITID-53523.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53521 or ITID-53522 as soon as the stage is understood.
indicators: Synthetic-identity flag raised by credit-bureau analytics without further stage detail yet available
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard synthetic-identity fraud triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53523.response: Fraud investigations triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-535xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Synthetic Identity Fraud Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53523.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response. Intake bucket only; should not accumulate a stable long-term population.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Synthetic Identity Fraud
playbook.description: A synthetic identity fraud indicator that does not fit the identity-construction or bust-out patterns, requiring general underwriting-fraud investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the synthetic-identity fraud indicator
steps.desc: Identify indicators of synthetic identity fraud not fitting a more specific pattern, and confirm against identity-verification and fraud-analytics sources.
steps.guidance: Run the flagged identity through synthetic-identity detection analytics.
steps.outcome: Confirmed synthetic-identity indicator with the specific inconsistencies documented.
steps.abort: If the identity verifies as legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope related accounts/applications
steps.desc: Determine whether the synthetic identity is linked to other accounts or applications across the institution.
steps.guidance: Search for accounts sharing common application data elements.
steps.outcome: Scope of related accounts/applications documented.

steps.title: Freeze the affected account(s)/application(s)
steps.desc: Immediately freeze the affected account(s) or halt the application(s) to prevent further exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the relevant business unit to place an emergency freeze/hold.
steps.outcome: Further exposure halted on the affected account(s)/application(s).

steps.title: Flag the synthetic identity across the fraud-prevention system
steps.desc: Flag the synthetic identity in the fraud-prevention system and applicable industry consortium database.
steps.guidance: Submit the confirmed synthetic-identity profile to relevant data-sharing services.
steps.outcome: Synthetic identity flagged internally and shared with the industry consortium.

steps.title: Close out the fraudulent account/application and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Formally close/decline the fraudulent account or application and quantify the total exposure.
steps.guidance: Document the loss quantification for financial reporting.
steps.outcome: Account/application closed and exposure quantified.

steps.title: File a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale.
steps.outcome: SAR filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Resume normal operations under enhanced synthetic-identity detection
steps.desc: Resume normal operations under any strengthened detection controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Track flag rates post-implementation.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced detection controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update synthetic-identity response procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update the general synthetic-identity detection procedure.
steps.guidance: Brief Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53531.def: Fraud in which an individual (often for a fee, arranged through a broker) is added as an authorized user on a stranger's long-standing, well-managed credit card account purely to inherit that account's positive payment history and inflate their own credit score, with no genuine financial relationship or authorization to use the card.
ITID-53531.purpose: Captures schemes that manipulate a credit score by improperly gaining authorized-user status on another person's well-established credit account.
scopeIncludes: Brokered 'tradeline rental' arrangements adding unrelated individuals as authorized users for a fee
Use of an inflated credit score obtained this way to qualify for loans the individual would not otherwise receive
scopeExcludes: Legitimate authorized-user additions between family members with a genuine relationship
Falsifying credit report disputes to remove accurate negative information (ITID-53532)
ITID-53531.severity: Low-Medium from a direct-loss perspective; primarily a downstream enabler of loan/credit fraud rather than a direct loss event itself.
ITID-53531.priority: P3, tracked as a contributing risk factor rather than a standalone high-priority incident.
ITID-53531.escalation: Escalate to underwriting/fraud teams when tradeline-rental patterns are identified as a contributing factor in a subsequent loan-fraud case.
indicators: Sudden, unexplained credit-score improvement shortly before a loan application
Authorized-user relationship added to an account with no apparent personal/family connection to the primary holder
Multiple unrelated authorized users added to the same primary account in a short period
vectors: Brokered tradeline-rental services matching primary account holders with fee-paying authorized users
rootCauses: Credit-scoring models weighting authorized-user tradelines without verifying the underlying relationship
Lack of underwriting scrutiny on recently added authorized-user tradelines
controls: Underwriting review discounting recently added authorized-user tradelines with no apparent relationship
Monitoring for known tradeline-rental broker patterns
ITID-53531.detection: Detected through underwriting-level credit-report review rather than SOC telemetry; largely a scoring-model and policy issue.
ITID-53531.response: Underwriting adjusts scoring weight or denies the application; fraud investigations tracks broker patterns for referral.
metrics: Number of applications flagged for suspicious authorized-user tradelines per quarter
detections: Authorized-user tradeline anomaly flagging in underwriting review
ITID-53531.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Credit Piggybacking/Authorized User Fraud Scheme
playbook.description: The company, acting as a lender/card issuer, detects an organized scheme adding unrelated individuals as authorized users on seasoned accounts to fraudulently inflate their credit profiles ahead of applications.

steps.title: Detect the authorized-user addition anomaly
steps.desc: Identify indicators of coordinated authorized-user additions to seasoned accounts — a spike in authorized-user requests with no apparent familial/household relationship, often for a fee brokered by a third party.
steps.guidance: Review authorized-user addition volume and relationship data on seasoned accounts, correlating with any subsequent credit-profile improvement and application activity by the added users.
steps.outcome: Confirmed piggybacking pattern with the accounts, authorized users, and any organizing broker identified.
steps.abort: If the authorized-user relationships are legitimate (family/household), close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope the full network of accounts and brokered users involved
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of the scheme, including all primary accounts used and all individuals added as authorized users through the same broker/organizer.
steps.guidance: Search account-management records for the identified broker/organizer's pattern across other seasoned accounts.
steps.outcome: Full network of accounts and authorized users documented.

steps.title: Remove the fraudulently-added authorized users
steps.desc: Remove the improperly added authorized users from the affected accounts to prevent further credit-profile manipulation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Account Services to process the authorized-user removals across all identified accounts.
steps.outcome: Fraudulently-added authorized users removed from all affected accounts.

steps.title: Flag the primary accounts and organizer for enhanced review
steps.desc: Flag the primary account holders (if complicit) and any identified organizer/broker in the fraud-prevention system pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: Primary accounts and organizer flagged for enhanced review.

steps.title: Report the manipulation to credit bureaus for tradeline correction
steps.desc: Notify the credit bureaus of the fraudulent authorized-user additions so the resulting tradeline impact can be corrected on affected credit files.
steps.guidance: Submit bureau-fraud-correction requests referencing the confirmed scheme.
steps.outcome: Credit bureaus notified and tradeline corrections initiated.

steps.title: Refer the organizer/broker for law-enforcement action and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria for the organized scheme and refers the organizer/broker to law enforcement if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria; organized brokered schemes typically warrant filing.
steps.outcome: SAR filed as warranted and law-enforcement referral made.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen authorized-user addition controls
steps.desc: Implement verification requirements (e.g., relationship attestation, velocity limits on authorized-user additions) to reduce recurrence.
steps.guidance: Update the account-services policy and communicate the change to relevant staff.
steps.outcome: Updated control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal account-services operations under enhanced controls
steps.desc: Resume normal authorized-user processing under the strengthened verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track authorized-user addition patterns post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update credit-manipulation detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, scope, and SAR/recovery outcome; update fraud-analytics rules and staff training on piggybacking schemes.
steps.guidance: Brief Credit Risk and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53532.def: Fraud in which a credit-repair operator files disputes against accurate, legitimate negative tradelines (e.g., real late payments, real charge-offs) on a client's credit report, exploiting dispute-processing timelines or fabricated identity-theft claims to have the accurate negative information removed rather than legitimately corrected.
ITID-53532.purpose: Captures credit-repair schemes that manipulate a credit score by fraudulently disputing accurate negative information off a credit report.
scopeIncludes: Filing false identity-theft claims to remove accurate negative tradelines
Mass, automated dispute-flooding intended to exceed a credit bureau's investigation-timeline capacity
Credit-repair operators submitting disputes on behalf of clients without a legitimate basis
scopeExcludes: Legitimate consumer disputes of genuinely inaccurate credit-report information
Tradeline-rental/authorized-user credit score manipulation (ITID-53531)
ITID-53532.severity: Low-Medium from the company's direct-loss perspective; relevant primarily where the company is a creditor whose accurate reporting is being fraudulently disputed.
ITID-53532.priority: P3, tracked as a contributing risk factor in subsequent lending decisions based on the artificially cleaned credit report.
ITID-53532.escalation: Escalate to compliance/legal when a pattern of fraudulent disputes against the company's own reported tradelines is identified, for coordinated response with credit bureaus.
indicators: Dispute claiming identity theft on a tradeline the company can verify as genuinely the consumer's
High-volume, template-worded disputes traceable to a common credit-repair operator
Removed negative tradeline reappearing after re-verification
vectors: Mass dispute-flooding through automated credit-repair services
Fabricated identity-theft affidavits submitted with disputes
rootCauses: Credit-bureau dispute-processing timelines that favor removal over verification under volume pressure
Insufficient creditor-side re-verification response capacity
controls: Prompt, evidence-backed re-verification response to disputes on genuinely accurate tradelines
Pattern tracking of disputes traceable to known credit-repair operators
ITID-53532.detection: Detected through the company's own dispute-response/re-verification workflow rather than SOC telemetry.
ITID-53532.response: Compliance/credit-reporting team re-verifies and reinstates accurate tradelines; legal engagement for operators showing a pattern of fraudulent filings.
metrics: Number of fraudulent disputes identified and successfully re-verified per quarter
sops: Credit Report Dispute Fraud Response SOP
detections: Dispute-pattern tracking against known credit-repair operators
ITID-53532.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Credit Repair Scam Falsifying Credit Report Disputes
playbook.description: The company, acting as a creditor/furnisher, detects a pattern of fraudulent credit-report disputes (often via a credit-repair operation) falsely claiming legitimate tradelines are inaccurate in order to have them removed.

steps.title: Detect the fraudulent dispute pattern
steps.desc: Identify indicators of a fraudulent dispute pattern — a spike in disputes using near-identical boilerplate language, disputes filed for accounts with a clear factual payment history, or disputes traced to a known credit-repair operation.
steps.guidance: Review dispute volume, language similarity, and account payment-history accuracy for the flagged disputes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent dispute pattern with the affected accounts and any credit-repair operation identified.
steps.abort: If disputes reflect legitimate reporting errors, close as false positive and process normally.

steps.title: Scope the full volume of disputes tied to the scheme
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of accounts and customers involved in the fraudulent dispute pattern, and identify the credit-repair entity if a common source is evident.
steps.guidance: Search the dispute-management system for the identified pattern/entity across the broader customer base.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected accounts and any identified credit-repair entity documented.

steps.title: Halt processing of the identified fraudulent disputes
steps.desc: Place a hold on further automated processing of disputes matching the identified fraudulent pattern pending manual review.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the dispute-processing team to flag and route matching disputes for manual review rather than automated resolution.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent disputes routed to manual review with no further improper tradeline removals.

steps.title: Flag affected accounts and any identified credit-repair entity
steps.desc: Flag the affected accounts and the identified credit-repair entity (if any) in the fraud-prevention system.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: Affected accounts and entity flagged for ongoing monitoring.

steps.title: Re-verify and restore accurately reported tradelines
steps.desc: Re-verify the accuracy of any tradelines improperly removed based on the fraudulent disputes and restore accurate reporting to the credit bureaus.
steps.guidance: Submit bureau reinsertion requests with documented verification of the tradeline's accuracy per FCRA requirements.
steps.outcome: Accurately reported tradelines restored with the bureaus.

steps.title: Refer the credit-repair operation for regulatory/law-enforcement action and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance evaluates referral of the identified credit-repair operation to the CFPB/FTC (Credit Repair Organizations Act violations) and to law enforcement, and the BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the referral rationale.
steps.outcome: Regulatory/law-enforcement referral made and SAR filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen dispute-verification controls
steps.desc: Enhance dispute-intake analytics to detect boilerplate/mass-dispute patterns and require enhanced verification before tradeline removal.
steps.guidance: Update the dispute-handling policy and fraud-analytics rule set.
steps.outcome: Updated verification control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal dispute-processing operations under enhanced verification
steps.desc: Resume normal dispute processing under the strengthened verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence of similar patterns.
steps.guidance: Track dispute-pattern flags post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced verification controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update dispute-fraud detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, scope, and referral/recovery outcome; update dispute-handling training and procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Compliance and Credit Risk leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53533.def: An unclassified/general leaf for credit score manipulation fraud that has not been further classified into tradeline/authorized-user (ITID-53531) or fraudulent dispute (ITID-53532) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53533.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for credit score manipulation fraud that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported credit-score manipulation pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53531 or ITID-53532
ITID-53533.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53533.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53533.escalation: Escalate to fraud/underwriting for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53531 or ITID-53532 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Credit score manipulation flagged by underwriting review but not yet root-caused
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard credit-score-manipulation triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53533.response: Fraud/underwriting triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-535xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Credit Score Manipulation Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53533.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response. Intake bucket only.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Credit Score Manipulation
playbook.description: A credit score manipulation indicator that does not fit the authorized-user-piggybacking or credit-repair-dispute-scam patterns, requiring general fraud investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the credit score manipulation indicator
steps.desc: Identify indicators of credit score manipulation not fitting a more specific pattern, and confirm against account/fraud-analytics data.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged account/customer activity against available fraud-analytics outputs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed manipulation indicator with the specific activity documented.
steps.abort: If the activity is legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope related accounts/customers involved
steps.desc: Determine whether the manipulation pattern is linked to other accounts or customers.
steps.guidance: Search for accounts sharing common identifiers or patterns with the flagged activity.
steps.outcome: Scope of related accounts/customers documented.

steps.title: Halt the exploited process pending review
steps.desc: Halt the specific process or account activity enabling the manipulation pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the relevant business unit to place a hold on the exploited process.
steps.outcome: Exploited process halted with no further manipulation possible.

steps.title: Flag affected accounts/parties in the fraud-prevention system
steps.desc: Flag affected accounts and any identified responsible parties pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: Affected accounts/parties flagged for ongoing monitoring.

steps.title: Correct affected credit records and quantify impact
steps.desc: Correct any credit-bureau records improperly affected by the manipulation and quantify the scope/impact of the scheme.
steps.guidance: Submit bureau correction requests as needed and document the impact quantification.
steps.outcome: Affected records corrected and impact quantified.

steps.title: File a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale.
steps.outcome: SAR filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Resume normal operations under enhanced detection controls
steps.desc: Resume normal operations under any strengthened detection controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Track flag rates post-implementation.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update credit-manipulation detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, scope, and SAR/recovery outcome; update the general credit-manipulation detection procedure.
steps.guidance: Brief Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53541.def: Fraud in which a mortgage applicant, sometimes with the assistance of a colluding loan officer or broker, submits fabricated or inflated income, employment, or asset documentation to qualify for a mortgage or a larger loan amount than their true financial position supports.
ITID-53541.purpose: Captures mortgage fraud in which a borrower's income or asset documentation is falsified to qualify for financing.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated pay stubs, W-2s, or bank statements submitted with a mortgage application
Inflated asset statements used to satisfy down-payment or reserve requirements
Collusive loan-officer verification of falsified employment
scopeExcludes: Appraisal-value manipulation in a property-flipping scheme (ITID-53542)
Fraudulent transfer of title/deed (ITID-53543)
ITID-53541.severity: Medium-High given the large dollar amounts typical of mortgage lending and the potential for foreclosure-related loss.
ITID-53541.priority: P2, given typical mortgage loan sizes; P3 for lower-value cases caught pre-closing.
ITID-53541.escalation: Escalate to mortgage fraud investigations and, where a loan officer or broker is implicated, to internal compliance/HR for that individual's conduct.
indicators: Income documentation inconsistent with the applicant's stated occupation or industry norms
Asset statement showing a large, unexplained deposit shortly before application
Loan officer with an unusually high rate of applications relying on manually verified (non-automated) income
vectors: Fabricated income/asset documentation
Collusion with a loan officer or mortgage broker to bypass automated verification
rootCauses: Over-reliance on stated-income/reduced-documentation loan products without independent verification
Insufficient audit of loan-officer-level approval patterns
controls: Independent third-party income/asset verification for all mortgage originations
Loan-officer-level approval-pattern auditing
Large-deposit source-of-funds verification
ITID-53541.detection: Detected through underwriting document review and post-funding quality-control audit; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53541.response: Mortgage fraud investigations unwinds or refers the loan; compliance addresses any implicated internal staff.
metrics: Number of falsified-documentation mortgage applications caught per quarter
Percentage involving internal loan-officer collusion
ITID-53541.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Mortgage Application Income/Asset Falsification
playbook.description: The company, acting as a mortgage lender, detects that a borrower falsified income or asset documentation to qualify for a mortgage loan, requiring underwriting investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the income/asset documentation anomaly
steps.desc: Identify indicators that submitted income/asset documentation (pay stubs, bank statements, tax returns) is falsified, inconsistent, or fails independent verification during underwriting or quality-control review.
steps.guidance: Cross-check submitted documents against employer-verification services, IRS transcript data, and bank-statement authenticity checks for signs of alteration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed documentation discrepancy with the specific falsified elements and loan file identified.
steps.abort: If verification confirms the documentation is accurate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope any related applications or common originator involvement
steps.desc: Determine whether the falsification pattern is linked to other applications or a common loan officer/broker involved in origination.
steps.guidance: Search the loan origination system for other applications sharing the same originator, preparer, or documentation source.
steps.outcome: Scope of related applications/patterns identified.

steps.title: Halt the loan closing/funding and freeze any disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt the closing/funding process if not yet complete, or if funds have already been disbursed, initiate an emergency freeze/recall through Treasury and any title/escrow company involved.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting to place the file on fraud hold and with Treasury/Closing to identify and freeze any disbursed funds.
steps.outcome: Closing/funding halted and any disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If the loan has already fully funded and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Flag the borrower and any originator/broker across the origination system
steps.desc: Flag the borrower's identity and any implicated originator/broker in the fraud-prevention system to block further applications pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist and mortgage-industry fraud-reporting databases as applicable.
steps.outcome: Borrower and any implicated originator flagged with no further applications processed.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and decision the loan file
steps.desc: Complete the investigation into the falsified documentation and formally decline/void the application (or pursue loan-repurchase/putback if already sold), pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and final loan disposition for the file, including any investor putback obligations.
steps.outcome: Loan declined/voided (or repurchase pursued) and recovery of disbursed funds pursued.

steps.title: Assess and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates whether the falsification pattern meets SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria (dollar thresholds, pattern indicators) and document the rationale.
steps.outcome: SAR filing decision documented and filed with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen mortgage income/asset verification controls
steps.desc: Enhance underwriting verification procedures (e.g., mandatory IRS transcript pulls, bank-statement authenticity screening, originator-quality scorecards) to reduce recurrence.
steps.guidance: Update the underwriting policy and communicate the change to Underwriting and originator-management staff.
steps.outcome: Updated verification control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal mortgage-origination operations under enhanced verification
steps.desc: Resume normal mortgage-origination processing under the strengthened verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track fraud-flag rates post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced verification controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update mortgage-fraud detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update underwriting fraud-detection training and originator-oversight procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53542.def: Fraud in which a property is purchased at a low price and quickly resold at an artificially inflated price supported by a collusive or fraudulent appraisal, with the difference funded by a mortgage lender who is misled about the property's true value.
ITID-53542.purpose: Captures property-flipping schemes that rely on a fraudulently inflated appraisal to extract value from a rapid resale.
scopeIncludes: Collusion between a flipper and appraiser to inflate a property's assessed value
Use of a fraudulent appraisal to support a resale mortgage far exceeding the property's true value
Rapid, unimproved resale timelines inconsistent with the claimed value increase
scopeExcludes: Income/asset documentation falsification unrelated to appraisal value (ITID-53541)
Title/deed fraud involving fraudulent property transfer without a flip/resale structure (ITID-53543)
ITID-53542.severity: High. Losses crystallize when the inflated-value property is later foreclosed upon and sold at true market value, often well below the fraudulent mortgage balance.
ITID-53542.priority: P2, given the potential for coordinated multi-property schemes involving the same appraiser or flipping ring.
ITID-53542.escalation: Escalate to mortgage fraud investigations and, where an appraiser is repeatedly implicated, to state appraisal licensing boards and law enforcement.
indicators: Property resold within an unusually short window at a large price increase with no material improvements
Same appraiser appearing repeatedly across a cluster of suspiciously flipped properties
Appraisal comparables that do not reasonably support the assessed value
vectors: Collusive appraiser relationships within a flipping ring
Coordinated straw buyers used to establish an inflated comparable sale
rootCauses: Insufficient independent appraisal review/second-appraisal triggers for rapid resales
No cross-transaction pattern analysis linking appraisers to flipping clusters
controls: Independent appraisal review with automated valuation model cross-check
Rapid-resale (flip) pattern flagging with mandatory second appraisal
Appraiser-level pattern auditing across transactions
ITID-53542.detection: Detected through automated valuation model discrepancy checks and appraiser pattern auditing; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53542.response: Mortgage fraud investigations unwinds affected loans and refers appraisers/rings to licensing boards and law enforcement.
metrics: Number of flip-fraud schemes identified per quarter
Dollar loss per confirmed scheme
Number of appraisers referred to licensing boards
sops: Property Flip Appraisal Fraud Investigation SOP
ITID-53542.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Property Flipping Appraisal Fraud Scheme
playbook.description: The company, acting as a mortgage lender, detects an organized property-flipping scheme relying on inflated/fraudulent appraisals to obtain financing far exceeding true property value, requiring underwriting investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the appraisal-inflation pattern
steps.desc: Identify indicators of appraisal fraud — a property that recently sold at a significantly lower price now appraised far above that value, or an appraiser with a pattern of consistently inflated valuations tied to specific originators.
steps.guidance: Compare the current appraisal against recent sale-price history for the property and run appraiser-performance analytics for outlier valuation patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed appraisal-inflation pattern with the property, appraiser, and any organizing party identified.
steps.abort: If the value increase is supportable by legitimate market conditions or documented improvements, close as false positive.
steps.tool: Appraisal review system / property valuation analytics

steps.title: Scope the full flipping network and related transactions
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of the scheme, including all properties, appraisers, and parties (buyer, seller, broker) involved in the flipping network.
steps.guidance: Search transaction records for the identified appraiser/originator pattern across other recent transactions.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the flipping network documented.

steps.title: Halt the loan closing/funding and freeze any disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt the closing/funding process for the affected transaction(s), or if funds have already been disbursed, initiate an emergency freeze/recall.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting and Treasury/Closing to place all identified related transactions on fraud hold simultaneously.
steps.outcome: Closing/funding halted across all related transactions and any disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If loans have already fully funded and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Flag the appraiser and involved parties across the origination system
steps.desc: Flag the implicated appraiser and all identified parties in the fraud-prevention system, and suspend the appraiser from the approved-appraiser panel pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist and remove the appraiser from active assignment rotation.
steps.outcome: Implicated parties flagged and appraiser suspended from panel pending investigation.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and decision all related loan files
steps.desc: Complete the investigation into the full appraisal-fraud scheme and formally decline/void all related applications, pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and disposition for each loan file in the network.
steps.outcome: All related loan files declined/voided and recovery of disbursed funds pursued.

steps.title: Refer to state appraisal board/law enforcement and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Refer the appraiser to the applicable state appraisal licensing board and the scheme to law enforcement; Compliance/BSA officer evaluates and files a SAR with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria, noting organized flipping schemes with inflated appraisals typically warrant filing.
steps.outcome: Regulatory/law-enforcement referrals made and SAR filed as warranted.

steps.title: Strengthen appraisal-review controls
steps.desc: Enhance appraisal-review analytics (e.g., automated valuation model cross-checks, appraiser-performance scorecards, chain-of-title flip-timing flags) to detect similar schemes earlier.
steps.guidance: Update the underwriting policy and appraisal-review rule set.
steps.outcome: Updated detection control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal mortgage-origination operations under enhanced appraisal review
steps.desc: Resume normal mortgage-origination processing under the strengthened appraisal-review controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track appraisal-flag rates post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced review controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update appraisal-fraud detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and referral/SAR outcome; update appraisal-review training and appraiser-oversight procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53543.def: Fraud in which an adversary forges signatures or fabricates documentation to record a fraudulent deed transfer, quitclaim, or title change on a property, allowing the property to be sold, refinanced, or encumbered without the true owner's knowledge or consent.
ITID-53543.purpose: Captures fraud that transfers a property's title or deed away from its rightful owner without valid authorization.
scopeIncludes: Forged quitclaim deeds filed with a county recorder to transfer title away from the true owner
Fraudulent title transfer used to enable an unauthorized refinance or home-equity loan against the property
Impersonation of a property owner (particularly vacant or absentee-owned properties) to execute a fraudulent transfer
scopeExcludes: Appraisal-inflation-based flipping fraud where title genuinely transfers with the true owner's consent (ITID-53542)
Income/asset falsification unrelated to a title transfer (ITID-53541)
ITID-53543.severity: High. Victim owners can face lengthy, costly legal processes to reclaim clear title, and the lender may face a loan secured by a defective title.
ITID-53543.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a fraudulent transfer is used to enable an active drawdown against a home-equity line before recording authorities can intervene.
ITID-53543.escalation: Escalate to fraud investigations, legal (title-insurance claim), and law enforcement immediately upon discovery of a forged transfer; notify the true property owner without delay.
indicators: Deed transfer recorded for a property with no corresponding sale transaction or owner contact
Notarization on a transfer document that fails verification against the notary's actual records
Transfer involving a vacant, absentee-owned, or recently deceased owner's property
vectors: Forged signatures and fabricated notarization on deed-transfer documents
Impersonation of an absentee or deceased property owner
rootCauses: County recording processes with limited real-time identity verification for filed deeds
No automated alerting to property owners when a document is recorded against their property
controls: Title-insurance underwriting checks prior to funding against a recently transferred property
Owner-notification alerting when a document is recorded against a monitored property (where offered)
Notary verification checks against recording authority records
ITID-53543.detection: Detected primarily through title-insurance underwriting review and county-recorder owner-notification services; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53543.response: Legal/title-insurance pursues title correction and claim resolution; fraud investigations and law enforcement pursue the perpetrator.
metrics: Number of fraudulent title/deed transfers identified per quarter
Average time to title correction
ITID-53543.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response. Distinguished from property-flipping fraud (ITID-53542) by the absence of the true owner's consent to any transfer.

playbook.name: Title/Deed Fraud (Fraudulent Property Transfer)
playbook.description: The company, as a mortgage lender or title-related party, detects that a property title/deed was fraudulently transferred (e.g., forged deed, impersonation of the true owner) to facilitate an unauthorized loan or sale, requiring investigation and law-enforcement/SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the fraudulent title/deed transfer
steps.desc: Identify indicators of a fraudulent deed transfer — a recently recorded deed transfer inconsistent with the true owner's knowledge, forged signatures, or a notarization irregularity flagged during title review.
steps.guidance: Compare the recorded deed against prior title history and contact the purported grantor (true owner) to confirm whether the transfer was authorized.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent transfer with the property, true owner, and fraudulent grantee identified.
steps.abort: If the true owner confirms the transfer was authorized, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism and any associated loan application
steps.desc: Investigate how the fraudulent transfer was accomplished (forged deed, notary fraud, identity impersonation of the owner) and whether a loan application or sale is being processed based on the fraudulent transfer.
steps.guidance: Review the notarization records and any associated loan application tied to the fraudulent grantee.
steps.outcome: Fraud mechanism identified and any associated loan/sale transaction documented.

steps.title: Halt any loan closing/funding and freeze disbursed funds tied to the fraudulent transfer
steps.desc: Immediately halt any loan closing or funding relying on the fraudulent title, and if funds have already been disbursed, initiate an emergency freeze/recall.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting, Closing, and Treasury to place the transaction on fraud hold and freeze any disbursed funds.
steps.outcome: Closing/funding halted and any disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds have already fully funded and cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Notify the true property owner and title insurer
steps.desc: Notify the true property owner of the fraudulent transfer and engage the title insurance company to address the defective title and pursue a corrective quiet-title action.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal and the title insurer on next steps to restore clear title to the rightful owner.
steps.outcome: True owner notified and title insurer engaged to address the fraudulent transfer.

steps.title: Pursue corrective title action and decision the loan file
steps.desc: Support the corrective quiet-title action to restore the true owner's clear title, and formally void any loan file relying on the fraudulent transfer, pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and final loan/title disposition for the file.
steps.outcome: Corrective title action pursued and fraudulent loan file voided with recovery pursued.

steps.title: Refer to law enforcement and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Refer the deed-fraud scheme to law enforcement, and the Compliance/BSA officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale.
steps.outcome: Law-enforcement referral made and SAR filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Strengthen title/deed-fraud detection controls
steps.desc: Enhance title-review procedures (e.g., owner-occupancy verification calls, notarization-authenticity checks, deed-recording alert monitoring) to detect similar fraud earlier.
steps.guidance: Update the underwriting/title-review policy and communicate the change to relevant staff.
steps.outcome: Updated detection control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal title/closing operations under enhanced verification
steps.desc: Resume normal title-review and closing operations under the strengthened verification controls once the corrective title action is resolved.
steps.guidance: Confirm clear title has been restored to the rightful owner before closing any related future transaction.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced verification controls active and clear title restored.

steps.title: Document incident and update title-fraud detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and referral/SAR outcome; update title-review training and procedures.
steps.guidance: Brief Legal, Underwriting, and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53544.def: An unclassified/general leaf for mortgage and real estate fraud that has not been further classified into income/asset falsification (ITID-53541), property-flipping appraisal fraud (ITID-53542), or title/deed fraud (ITID-53543) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53544.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for mortgage and real estate fraud that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported mortgage/real estate fraud pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53541, ITID-53542, or ITID-53543
ITID-53544.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53544.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53544.escalation: Escalate to mortgage fraud investigations for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53541, ITID-53542, or ITID-53543 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Mortgage/real estate fraud flagged during underwriting or servicing but not yet root-caused
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard mortgage fraud triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53544.response: Mortgage fraud investigations triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-535xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Mortgage and Real Estate Fraud Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53544.notes: financial/identity-fraud pattern — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via fraud operations, not SOC technical response. Intake bucket only.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Mortgage and Real Estate Fraud
playbook.description: A mortgage/real-estate fraud indicator that does not fit the income-falsification, appraisal-flipping, or title/deed-fraud patterns, requiring general underwriting-fraud investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the mortgage/real-estate fraud indicator
steps.desc: Identify indicators of mortgage/real-estate fraud not fitting a more specific pattern, and confirm against underwriting/title verification sources.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged transaction against available verification data and fraud-analytics outputs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraud indicator with the specific transaction and discrepancy documented.
steps.abort: If verification confirms the transaction is legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism and scope related transactions
steps.desc: Investigate how the fraud was perpetrated and whether it is linked to other transactions or a broader pattern.
steps.guidance: Search the loan origination/title system for related transactions sharing common identifiers.
steps.outcome: Fraud mechanism identified and scope of related transactions determined.

steps.title: Halt the closing/funding and freeze any disbursed funds
steps.desc: Immediately halt the closing/funding process and freeze/recall any disbursed funds where possible.
