steps.guidance: Coordinate with Underwriting and Treasury to place the transaction on fraud hold.
steps.outcome: Closing/funding halted and disbursed funds frozen or recall initiated.
steps.abort: If funds cannot be recalled, document and proceed to recovery/law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Flag involved parties across the origination system
steps.desc: Flag the borrower and any implicated parties in the fraud-prevention system to block further transactions pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Add identified participants to the internal fraud watchlist.
steps.outcome: Involved parties flagged with no further transactions processed.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and decision the transaction
steps.desc: Complete the fraud investigation and formally decline/void the transaction, pursuing recovery of any disbursed funds.
steps.guidance: Document the investigation findings and final transaction disposition.
steps.outcome: Transaction declined/voided and recovery pursued.

steps.title: Assess and file a SAR if warranted
steps.desc: Compliance/BSA officer evaluates whether the fraud pattern meets SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and document the rationale.
steps.outcome: SAR filing decision documented and filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing.

steps.title: Resume normal mortgage/real-estate operations under enhanced controls
steps.desc: Resume normal mortgage-origination/title operations under any strengthened controls identified during the investigation.
steps.guidance: Track fraud-flag rates post-implementation.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced controls active.

steps.title: Document incident and update mortgage/real-estate fraud-detection procedures
steps.desc: Record root cause, financial exposure, and SAR/recovery outcome; update the general mortgage/real-estate fraud-detection procedure.
steps.guidance: Brief Underwriting and Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: After-action report completed with control-improvement plan.

ITID-53611.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cases in which an employee, executive, or other insider trades company (or a business partner's) securities while in possession of material, non-public information obtained through their position, or tips such information to others who trade on it.
ITID-53611.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for insider trading conducted by employees or executives using material non-public information.
scopeIncludes: Trading in company stock ahead of a material non-public announcement (earnings, M&A, regulatory action)
Tipping material non-public information to a friend or family member who then trades
Trading by an insider in a counterparty's or acquisition target's securities based on deal knowledge
scopeExcludes: Embezzlement or diversion of company funds (ITID-53621-53624)
Falsification of financial reports (ITID-53641)
ITID-53611.severity: High. Insider trading carries significant regulatory (SEC/equivalent), reputational, and legal exposure for both the individual and the company.
ITID-53611.priority: P1 upon credible suspicion, given regulatory reporting obligations and potential trading-window/blackout-period violations in progress.
ITID-53611.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal/compliance and, where applicable, to the company's securities counsel; regulatory self-reporting obligations may apply on an expedited timeline.
indicators: Unusual trading volume/timing by an insider shortly before a material public announcement
Trading activity inconsistent with an employee's standing 10b5-1 plan
Communications suggesting information was shared outside authorized channels ahead of an announcement
vectors: Direct trading by an insider with access to material non-public information
Tipping of material non-public information to a third party who trades on it
rootCauses: Insufficient trading-blackout-window enforcement or monitoring
Overly broad access to material non-public information (deal rooms, earnings data) without need-to-know controls
Lack of pre-clearance requirements for insider trades
controls: Trading blackout-window enforcement and monitoring for designated insiders
Pre-clearance requirement for insider trades
Need-to-know access restriction on material non-public information (deal rooms, draft earnings)
ITID-53611.detection: Detected through trading-surveillance systems and compliance monitoring rather than SOC/technical telemetry; insider access-log review can support an investigation once opened.
ITID-53611.response: Legal/compliance leads the investigation and regulatory reporting; SOC may be asked to support with access-log forensics on who viewed the material non-public information and when.
metrics: Number of insider-trading investigations opened per year
Number of confirmed violations referred to regulators
sops: Material Non-Public Information Access Control SOP
detections: Trading-surveillance alerting on insider trades near material events
ITID-53611.notes: securities/financial-crime pattern, not a cyber intrusion technique. SOC's role is typically limited to supporting access-log forensics once legal/compliance opens an investigation.

playbook.name: Insider Trading (Insider Financial Fraud Context)
playbook.description: An employee with access to material non-public information trades company (or a related company's) securities, or tips others to trade, in violation of securities law and company policy.

steps.title: Identify the suspect trade(s) and the material non-public information involved
steps.desc: Identify the specific trade(s), the employee(s) involved, and the material non-public information (MNPI) to which they had access, and the timing relative to public disclosure.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal/Compliance immediately — this is a securities-law matter, not solely an IT/security incident.
steps.outcome: Documented trade details and MNPI access timeline.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under Legal privilege
steps.desc: Work with Legal to preserve all relevant communications, access logs, and trading records under legal hold, ideally under attorney-client privilege given likely regulatory exposure.
steps.guidance: Do not alert the employee or take visible action before Legal has assessed the evidentiary and privilege strategy.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved defensibly under Legal's direction.

steps.title: Assess SEC/regulatory disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Legal and Compliance assess whether the matter triggers SEC reporting or other regulatory disclosure obligations, and the timeline for any required filing.
steps.guidance: Compliance to coordinate with outside securities counsel as needed.
steps.outcome: Documented disclosure-obligation assessment and timeline.

steps.title: Restrict the employee's trading and system access under Legal direction
steps.desc: Under Legal's direction, restrict the employee's ability to trade further (e.g. blackout enforcement) and limit access to MNPI-bearing systems, timed to avoid compromising the investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with HR/Legal/Compliance on sequencing to preserve evidentiary integrity.
steps.outcome: Further trading/access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Notify Board/Audit Committee as appropriate
steps.desc: Legal/Compliance notify the Board or Audit Committee per governance requirements given the severity and regulatory exposure.
steps.outcome: Appropriate governance body notified.

steps.title: Complete forensic/compliance investigation
steps.desc: Complete the forensic investigation into the full scope of trading activity, tipping, and any other employees involved.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with outside counsel/forensic accounting as needed.
steps.outcome: Documented investigation findings.

steps.title: Strengthen insider-trading controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen insider-list management, trading blackout enforcement, and MNPI access controls to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Compliance/Legal.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Coordinate regulatory filing and disgorgement, determine employment action
steps.desc: Complete any required regulatory filings, pursue disgorgement of trading profits where applicable, and determine employment action and potential criminal referral with Legal/HR.
steps.outcome: Regulatory and employment actions completed per Legal direction.

steps.title: Document findings and update Compliance training
steps.desc: Finalize documentation (subject to privilege considerations) and update insider-trading compliance training for at-risk employee populations.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated training.

ITID-53621.def: Fraud in which an employee with access to incoming cash or check payments (e.g., a cashier, collections clerk, or front-office staff) pockets some or all of a receipt before it is recorded in the accounting system, so that no transaction trail is created for the diverted amount.
ITID-53621.purpose: Captures embezzlement in which an employee diverts cash receipts before they are ever entered into the company's financial records.
scopeIncludes: Pocketing cash payments before they are logged in the point-of-sale or accounting system
Voiding or altering a recorded sale after collecting the customer's payment
Diverting a portion of a batch of receipts during counting/deposit preparation
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent disbursement schemes creating a false payee after funds are already recorded (ITID-53622)
Diversion of company funds via authorized wire/transfer access (ITID-53623)
ITID-53621.severity: Low-Medium per incident, but often recurring and cumulative; severity should reflect the aggregate skimmed amount over the scheme's duration, not a single transaction.
ITID-53621.priority: P3 for an isolated, low-dollar case; P2 if the scheme has been ongoing or spans multiple employees/locations.
ITID-53621.escalation: Escalate to internal audit/HR for evidence gathering and employment action; escalate to legal for restitution or law-enforcement referral once the aggregate amount or duration is substantial.
indicators: Revenue/cash-receipt shortfall relative to expected volume at a location or register
Unusual pattern of voided transactions or unrecorded sales at a specific register or by a specific employee
Discrepancy between physical inventory depletion and recorded sales
vectors: Direct pocketing of unrecorded cash payments
Post-transaction voiding after collecting payment
Skimming during batch cash-counting/deposit preparation
rootCauses: Lack of segregation of duties between cash handling and recording
Absence of surprise cash audits or register reconciliation
Weak oversight of void/refund transaction authority
controls: Segregation of duties between cash handling, recording, and deposit
Surprise cash counts and register reconciliation audits
Void/refund transaction review and approval workflow
ITID-53621.detection: Detected through financial/inventory reconciliation and point-of-sale anomaly review; register/POS system audit logs provide the technical signal where such access is system-mediated.
ITID-53621.response: Internal audit quantifies the loss; HR/legal handles employment and restitution action; SOC's role is limited to preserving relevant system audit-log evidence.
metrics: Aggregate dollar amount recovered per confirmed skimming scheme
Average duration of a scheme before detection
ITID-53621.notes: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is applied loosely here to reflect abuse of legitimate system/register access for an unauthorized purpose; the underlying activity is a financial-controls failure, not a technical intrusion, and primary response ownership sits with internal audit/HR rather than the SOC.

playbook.name: Skimming Cash Receipts Before Recording
playbook.description: An employee with access to incoming cash or check payments diverts a portion for personal use before it is recorded in the accounting system, understating recorded revenue.

steps.title: Identify the discrepancy between expected and recorded receipts
steps.desc: Compare expected cash/check receipts (e.g. from sales records, customer statements, or third-party confirmations) against amounts actually recorded and deposited.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit; use customer confirmations to independently verify amounts paid.
steps.outcome: Documented discrepancy pattern between expected and recorded receipts.

steps.title: Trace the discrepancy to the responsible custodian and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Identify which employee(s) had custody of the cash/checks at the point of diversion, and preserve related records (deposit slips, register logs, access logs) before any confrontation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit/Legal on evidence preservation given the likelihood of a personnel case.
steps.outcome: Responsible custodian identified with preserved supporting evidence.
steps.abort: If discrepancy is fully explained by a documented process error, close as non-fraud.

steps.title: Remove cash-handling duties from the implicated employee
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR/Legal to reassign or restrict the implicated employee's cash-handling duties pending investigation, without alerting them prematurely if evidence-gathering is ongoing.
steps.guidance: Sequence carefully with HR/Legal to preserve evidentiary integrity.
steps.outcome: Further diversion prevented.

steps.title: Secure physical and system access to cash-handling points
steps.desc: Secure physical registers, safes, and system access related to the cash-handling function pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Access secured to prevent further tampering.

steps.title: Engage forensic accounting to quantify total skimmed amount
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting to review the full period of the employee's custody and quantify total skimmed funds.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Implement segregation of duties for cash handling and recording
steps.desc: Implement segregation of duties so the same individual cannot both receive/handle cash and record it in the accounting system, and add independent reconciliation controls.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance leadership on control redesign.
steps.outcome: Documented control redesign closing the gap.

steps.title: Pursue recovery, disciplinary action, and criminal referral
steps.desc: Work with Legal/HR to pursue recovery of skimmed funds, determine disciplinary action, and refer to law enforcement/prosecutors as warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery and referral actions initiated.

steps.title: Document investigation and communicate control changes
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate the segregation-of-duties changes to Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and control updates.

ITID-53622.def: Fraud in which an employee with accounts-payable access sets up a fictitious vendor, or alters payment routing on a legitimate vendor record, so that a disbursement intended for a real business expense is instead paid to an account the employee secretly controls.
ITID-53622.purpose: Captures embezzlement in which an employee creates or manipulates a vendor payment so that funds are disbursed to an account the employee controls.
scopeIncludes: Creation of a fictitious vendor in the ERP/AP system followed by invoicing and payment to a self-controlled account
Alteration of a legitimate vendor's banking details to redirect payment to a self-controlled account
Approval of self-submitted or collusive invoices for goods/services never rendered
scopeExcludes: Diversion of already-collected cash receipts before recording (ITID-53621)
Diversion via authorized wire/transfer access to a personal account without a fake-vendor structure (ITID-53623)
ITID-53622.severity: Medium-High. AP-based schemes can run for extended periods before detection and often involve recurring, escalating disbursement amounts.
ITID-53622.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the employee retains active AP system access and further disbursements can still be initiated.
ITID-53622.escalation: Escalate to internal audit, legal, and IT immediately to suspend the employee's AP system access and freeze further payments to the implicated vendor record.
indicators: Vendor record with no verifiable business registration, address, or tax ID
Vendor banking details matching an account associated with the employee or their known associates
Employee with AP access having both vendor-creation and payment-approval authority (no segregation of duties)
vectors: Fictitious vendor creation in the ERP/AP system
Unauthorized alteration of legitimate vendor banking details
Collusive fake-invoice submission and self-approval
rootCauses: Lack of segregation of duties between vendor-master creation, invoice approval, and payment release
No independent verification of new-vendor legitimacy (business registration/tax ID check)
Insufficient monitoring of vendor banking-detail changes
controls: Segregation of duties across vendor creation, invoice approval, and payment release
Independent new-vendor verification (business registration/tax ID check) before first payment
Alerting on vendor banking-detail changes matching employee-associated accounts
ITID-53622.detection: ERP/AP system audit logs provide a real technical signal for vendor-record creation and banking-detail changes; combined with financial reconciliation to surface the fraud.
ITID-53622.response: IT suspends AP system access on suspicion; internal audit quantifies loss; legal pursues restitution/prosecution.
metrics: Aggregate dollar amount disbursed to fraudulent vendors per confirmed scheme
Time from scheme initiation to detection
sops: Vendor Master Data Fraud Response SOP
detections: Segregation-of-duties violation alerting in the AP workflow
ITID-53622.notes: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is applied loosely to reflect abuse of legitimate ERP/AP system access for an unauthorized purpose; response ownership sits primarily with internal audit and legal, with IT/SOC support limited to access suspension and log preservation.

playbook.name: Fraudulent Disbursement via Fake Vendor Payment to Self-Controlled Account
playbook.description: An employee with AP/disbursement authority creates or exploits a vendor record to route company payments to a bank account they secretly control, embezzling company funds.

steps.title: Identify anomalous disbursement pattern and pull records
steps.desc: Identify the suspect disbursement(s), and pull the vendor record, payment history, and approval chain from the ERP/AP system.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit before taking visible action.
steps.outcome: Full disbursement record assembled.

steps.title: Trace the destination account to the employee
steps.desc: Investigate whether the destination bank account, address, or related details link back to the employee (directly or via a relative/associate).
steps.guidance: Use bank account ownership verification, public records, and cross-reference against HR/payroll bank details for a match.
steps.outcome: Confirmed link (or lack thereof) between the employee and the destination account.
steps.abort: If the vendor is verified legitimate and unrelated to the employee, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under Internal Audit/Legal direction
steps.desc: Preserve all system logs, approval records, and communications before any confrontation, coordinating with Internal Audit and Legal given likely criminal referral.
steps.guidance: Follow the organization's internal-investigation evidence protocol.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Suspend the vendor record and freeze the employee's disbursement authority
steps.desc: Suspend the fraudulent vendor record to block further payments, and coordinate with HR/Legal/IT to restrict the employee's disbursement-approval authority and system access at the appropriate investigative moment.
steps.guidance: Sequence carefully with HR/Legal to avoid tipping off the employee before evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent disbursements; access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Notify Legal for criminal-referral assessment
steps.desc: Notify Legal to assess criminal referral, evidentiary requirements, and interview strategy before any employee confrontation.
steps.outcome: Legal-approved investigation and containment plan.

steps.title: Engage forensic accounting to quantify total diverted funds
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting to review the full period of the employee's disbursement authority and quantify total funds diverted.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Implement segregation of duties over vendor creation, approval, and disbursement
steps.desc: Implement segregation of duties so no single employee can create a vendor, approve its invoices, and release its payment, and add independent bank-account-change verification.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Internal Audit on control redesign.
steps.outcome: Documented control redesign closing the gap.

steps.title: Pursue recovery, disciplinary action, and criminal referral
steps.desc: Work with Legal/HR to pursue recovery of diverted funds, determine disciplinary action, and refer to law enforcement/prosecutors as warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery and referral actions initiated.

steps.title: Document investigation and communicate control changes
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate the segregation-of-duties changes to Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and control updates.

ITID-53623.def: Fraud in which an employee with authorized access to initiate or approve wire transfers, ACH payments, or account movements uses that access to move company funds directly into a personal or associate-controlled account, without the intermediate step of a fake vendor or invoice.
ITID-53623.purpose: Captures embezzlement in which an employee with legitimate treasury/transfer access moves company funds directly into an account they personally control.
scopeIncludes: Direct, self-initiated wire or ACH transfer of company funds to a personal account
Abuse of dual-control/approval workflows through collusion with a second authorized approver
Manipulation of intercompany or account-sweep transfers to route funds to a personal account
scopeExcludes: Diversion via a fictitious vendor/invoice structure (ITID-53622)
Diversion of cash receipts before recording (ITID-53621)
ITID-53623.severity: High. Direct treasury-access abuse typically involves larger, faster-moving amounts than AP-based schemes and can be harder to reverse once transferred externally.
ITID-53623.priority: P1 if the employee retains active transfer authority and additional movements can still occur; P2 once access is revoked and the matter is in recovery/investigation.
ITID-53623.escalation: Escalate immediately to treasury/finance leadership, legal, and IT to revoke transfer authority and attempt recall of any in-flight or recent transfers.
indicators: Wire/ACH transfer initiated and approved by the same individual (control bypass)
Transfer to an account with no prior business relationship or intercompany designation
Pattern of transfers just below a dollar threshold requiring additional approval
vectors: Direct abuse of authorized transfer-initiation and approval access
Collusion with a second approver to defeat dual-control requirements
rootCauses: Inadequate dual-control enforcement on wire/ACH initiation and approval
No monitoring for transfers structured just below approval thresholds
Insufficient reconciliation of intercompany/account-sweep activity
controls: Enforced dual control with independent initiator/approver roles for all outbound transfers
Threshold-structuring detection on transfer amounts
Independent reconciliation of intercompany and account-sweep activity
ITID-53623.detection: Treasury/banking-platform audit logs provide a real technical signal for control-bypass patterns and structuring; SOC can support forensic review of system access logs.
ITID-53623.response: Treasury/finance and legal lead recovery and investigation; IT revokes access; SOC supports log preservation and forensic timeline reconstruction on request.
metrics: Aggregate dollar amount diverted per confirmed scheme
Percentage recovered via transfer recall
detections: Dual-control bypass alerting on wire/ACH platforms
ITID-53623.notes: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is applied loosely to reflect abuse of legitimate treasury-system access for an unauthorized purpose; primary response ownership sits with treasury/finance and legal, not the SOC.

playbook.name: Diversion of Company Funds to Personal Account via Authorized Access
playbook.description: An employee with legitimate access to company bank accounts or financial systems (e.g. Treasury, payroll admin) uses that access to directly transfer company funds to a personal account.

steps.title: Identify the anomalous transfer and pull banking/system records
steps.desc: Identify the specific unauthorized transfer(s) and pull banking records, system access logs, and authorization records for the transaction.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit and Treasury before taking visible action.
steps.outcome: Full transaction record assembled.

steps.title: Confirm the destination account belongs to the employee
steps.desc: Verify the destination account ownership and confirm it is not a legitimate authorized transfer (e.g. an approved reimbursement).
steps.guidance: Use bank verification and cross-reference against known employee accounts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized personal diversion.
steps.abort: If the transfer is confirmed as a properly authorized transaction, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under Internal Audit/Legal direction
steps.desc: Preserve system access logs, transaction records, and approval trails before any confrontation, coordinating with Legal given likely criminal referral.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Revoke the employee's system and banking access
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR/Legal/IT to immediately revoke or suspend the employee's access to banking portals and financial systems.
steps.guidance: Sequence with HR/Legal to preserve evidentiary integrity while stopping further loss.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized transfers prevented.
steps.tool: Identity access management / banking portal admin

steps.title: Notify the bank and place account monitoring/holds
steps.desc: Notify the bank of the suspected fraud and request enhanced monitoring or holds on the affected accounts pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Bank alerted; account safeguards in place.

steps.title: Engage forensic accounting to quantify total diverted funds
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting to review all transactions during the employee's period of access and quantify total funds diverted.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Implement dual-authorization controls for fund transfers
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen dual-authorization (maker-checker) controls for outbound fund transfers above a defined threshold.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury/Finance leadership on control redesign.
steps.outcome: Documented control redesign closing the gap.

steps.title: Pursue recovery, disciplinary action, and criminal referral
steps.desc: Work with Legal/HR to pursue recovery of diverted funds, determine disciplinary action, and refer to law enforcement/prosecutors as warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery and referral actions initiated.

steps.title: Document investigation and communicate control changes
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate the dual-authorization control changes to Treasury/Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and control updates.

ITID-53624.def: An unclassified/general leaf for embezzlement that has not been further classified into cash-skimming (ITID-53621), fictitious-vendor disbursement (ITID-53622), or direct treasury-access diversion (ITID-53623) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53624.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for embezzlement that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported embezzlement pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53621, ITID-53622, or ITID-53623
ITID-53624.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53624.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53624.escalation: Escalate to internal audit for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53621, ITID-53622, or ITID-53623 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Suspected fund diversion flagged by audit but not yet root-caused
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard embezzlement triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53624.detection: Not applicable until triaged; detection coverage is inherited from whichever specific subtype the case is ultimately classified under.
ITID-53624.response: Internal audit triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-536xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
ITID-53624.notes: Intake bucket only; T1078 carried provisionally pending reclassification since all three specific embezzlement subtypes involve abuse of legitimate access.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Embezzlement
playbook.description: An employee misappropriates company funds or assets through methods not otherwise captured by a more specific embezzlement scenario.

steps.title: Identify the suspect misappropriation and pull relevant records
steps.desc: Identify the specific misappropriation and pull relevant financial, access, and approval records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit before taking visible action.
steps.outcome: Relevant records assembled for review.

steps.title: Determine the specific misappropriation mechanism and quantify impact
steps.desc: Analyze the records to determine the specific mechanism used and estimate the financial impact.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accounting for complex cases.
steps.outcome: Documented mechanism and estimated impact.
steps.abort: If findings are explainable without fraudulent intent, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under Internal Audit/Legal direction
steps.desc: Preserve relevant records and communications before any confrontation, coordinating with Legal given potential criminal referral.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved defensibly.

steps.title: Restrict the employee's relevant access
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR/Legal/IT to restrict the employee's access to the relevant financial systems/assets pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Sequence with HR/Legal to preserve evidentiary integrity.
steps.outcome: Further misappropriation prevented.

steps.title: Notify Legal for criminal-referral assessment
steps.desc: Notify Legal to assess criminal referral, evidentiary requirements, and interview strategy.
steps.outcome: Legal-approved investigation and containment plan.

steps.title: Engage forensic accounting to quantify total loss
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting to quantify the total loss over the relevant period.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Close the specific control gap exploited
steps.desc: Identify and close the specific control gap (segregation of duties, reconciliation frequency, approval authority) that enabled the misappropriation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Internal Audit leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented control redesign closing the gap.

steps.title: Pursue recovery, disciplinary action, and criminal referral
steps.desc: Work with Legal/HR to pursue recovery of misappropriated funds, determine disciplinary action, and refer to law enforcement/prosecutors as warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery and referral actions initiated.

steps.title: Document investigation and communicate control changes
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate control changes to Finance/Internal Audit leadership.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and control updates.

ITID-53631.def: Fraud in which an employee, typically one with HR/payroll system access or in collusion with such a person, manipulates payroll data (hours, pay rate, deposit destination, or a fictitious/'ghost' employee record) to receive compensation beyond what they are legitimately owed.
ITID-53631.purpose: Captures fraud in which an employee manipulates their own or a colleague's payroll record for unauthorized personal gain, without external impersonation.
scopeIncludes: Creation of a 'ghost employee' record that receives a paycheck with no corresponding real worker
Falsification of hours worked or pay rate in the payroll system by an employee with access
An employee redirecting their own or a colleague's direct deposit for personal gain without any external impersonation
scopeExcludes: Externally impersonation-driven payroll diversion via a spoofed/compromised email to HR (ITID-53131)
Skimming of cash receipts before recording (ITID-53621)
ITID-53631.severity: Medium. Ghost-employee schemes in particular can run for extended periods with recurring losses per pay cycle before detection.
ITID-53631.priority: P2 if the scheme is ongoing and recurring; P3 for a single-instance, already-stopped case.
ITID-53631.escalation: Escalate to internal audit/HR for investigation and to IT to review payroll-system access; escalate to legal for restitution once the aggregate loss is quantified.
indicators: Employee record with no corresponding badge/system-access activity ('ghost employee')
Hours or pay-rate changes made outside normal approval workflow
Payroll system access used outside an employee's normal job function
vectors: Ghost-employee record creation and maintenance in the payroll system
Unauthorized hours/pay-rate manipulation by an employee with payroll access
Collusive approval of falsified timesheets
rootCauses: Lack of segregation of duties between payroll data entry and approval
No periodic reconciliation of active payroll records against HR/badge-access records
Insufficient audit of payroll-system access outside normal job function
controls: Periodic reconciliation of payroll records against HR headcount and badge-access records
Segregation of duties between payroll entry and approval
Auditing of payroll-system access against job function
ITID-53631.detection: Payroll-system audit logs provide a real technical signal for unauthorized changes; ghost-employee schemes are best surfaced through headcount/badge-access reconciliation.
ITID-53631.response: Internal audit/HR investigates and quantifies loss; IT supports access-log review; legal pursues restitution.
metrics: Aggregate dollar amount recovered per confirmed scheme
Number of ghost-employee records identified per audit cycle
ITID-53631.notes: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is applied loosely to reflect abuse of legitimate payroll-system access for an unauthorized purpose; primary response ownership sits with internal audit/HR rather than the SOC.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Payroll Fraud by Employees
playbook.description: An employee manipulates payroll processes or records (e.g. ghost employees, falsified hours/overtime, unauthorized pay-rate changes) to obtain compensation they are not entitled to.

steps.title: Identify the anomalous payroll pattern and pull payroll records
steps.desc: Identify the specific anomaly (e.g. unexplained pay-rate change, duplicate/ghost employee, inflated hours) and pull the relevant payroll and HRIS records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Internal Audit/HR before taking visible action.
steps.outcome: Relevant payroll records assembled for review.

steps.title: Verify legitimacy of the flagged employee/transaction
steps.desc: Verify whether the flagged employee record, hours, or pay-rate change corresponds to a real, active, correctly-compensated employee, cross-referencing HR records, timesheets, and approval trails.
steps.guidance: For suspected ghost employees, confirm the individual actually exists and reports for work (physical/badge verification, manager confirmation).
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent payroll manipulation with supporting evidence.
steps.abort: If the employee/transaction is confirmed legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Preserve payroll system logs and approval records before any confrontation, coordinating with HR/Legal.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved defensibly.

steps.title: Halt the fraudulent payroll payment(s)
steps.desc: Suspend or correct the fraudulent payroll entry (remove the ghost employee, revert the unauthorized pay-rate change, or hold the next pay run) before it is disbursed further.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Payroll leadership on the timing to avoid disrupting legitimate pay.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent payroll payments issued.

steps.title: Restrict the implicated employee's payroll-system access
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR/Legal/IT to restrict the implicated employee's payroll-system access pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Quantify total fraudulent compensation obtained
steps.desc: Engage forensic accounting/Internal Audit to quantify the total fraudulent compensation paid over the relevant period.
steps.outcome: Documented total loss figure.

steps.title: Implement segregation of duties and periodic payroll audits
steps.desc: Implement segregation of duties between payroll setup/changes and approval, and institute periodic independent payroll audits (e.g. headcount reconciliation, pay-rate change review).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Payroll leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented control redesign closing the gap.

steps.title: Recover funds, determine disciplinary action, and consider referral
steps.desc: Work with Legal/HR to recover fraudulently obtained compensation, determine disciplinary action, and refer to law enforcement if warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery and disciplinary/referral path determined.

steps.title: Document investigation and communicate control changes
steps.desc: Finalize investigation documentation and communicate the strengthened payroll controls to HR/Payroll leadership.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and control updates.

ITID-53641.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cases in which an employee or executive with access to financial reporting systems deliberately misstates, alters, or fabricates financial statements, ledgers, or supporting records to misrepresent the company's true financial position.
ITID-53641.purpose: Captures fraud in which an insider knowingly falsifies company financial reports or records.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate misstatement of revenue, expenses, or reserves in financial statements
Alteration of general-ledger entries to conceal a discrepancy or shortfall
Fabrication of supporting documentation to pass an internal or external audit
scopeExcludes: Embezzlement/diversion of funds without accompanying financial-statement falsification (ITID-53621-53623)
Insider trading based on knowledge of the company's true (undisclosed) financial position (ITID-53611)
ITID-53641.severity: High. Financial report falsification carries significant regulatory, audit, investor-relations, and legal exposure, and often conceals or enables other financial fraud.
ITID-53641.priority: P1 upon credible suspicion, given regulatory disclosure obligations and the risk of an uncorrected material misstatement in a public filing.
ITID-53641.escalation: Escalate immediately to the audit committee, legal, and external auditors; regulatory disclosure obligations may apply on an expedited timeline for public companies.
indicators: General-ledger entries made outside normal period-close procedures or by unauthorized personnel
Financial results inconsistent with underlying operational data (e.g., revenue not matching shipment/usage records)
Unusual resistance or obstruction encountered during an internal or external audit
vectors: Manual general-ledger entries bypassing standard controls
Collusive falsification of supporting documentation across multiple roles
Manipulation of financial-close system access to alter reported figures
rootCauses: Insufficient segregation of duties in the financial-close process
Weak change-control/audit-trail logging on general-ledger systems
Pressure to meet financial targets without corresponding integrity controls
controls: Segregation of duties in the financial-close and reporting process
Immutable audit-trail logging on general-ledger and financial-reporting systems
Independent reconciliation of reported financials against underlying operational data
ITID-53641.detection: General-ledger/ERP audit-trail logs provide a real technical signal for unauthorized or out-of-cycle entries; primary detection is through internal/external audit rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-53641.response: Audit committee and legal lead the investigation and any required restatement/disclosure; IT/SOC supports with system access-log forensics on request.
metrics: Number of financial-reporting integrity investigations opened per year
Number resulting in a restatement
ITID-53641.notes: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is applied loosely to reflect abuse of legitimate financial-system access for an unauthorized purpose; this is fundamentally a financial-controls and governance failure, with SOC's role limited to supporting log forensics once audit/legal opens an investigation.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Financial Report Falsification (Insider Context)
playbook.description: An employee, typically in Finance/Accounting leadership, intentionally misstates financial records or reports (e.g. revenue recognition manipulation, expense mischaracterization, reserve manipulation) to misrepresent the company's financial position.

steps.title: Identify the specific misstatement and pull underlying records
steps.desc: Identify the specific account, entry, or disclosure suspected of falsification and pull the underlying transaction records, journal entries, and supporting documentation.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal/Compliance immediately given likely SEC/regulatory exposure.
steps.outcome: Relevant records assembled for review.

steps.title: Assess materiality and confirm intentional misstatement
steps.desc: Assess the materiality of the misstatement and gather evidence distinguishing intentional falsification from a legitimate accounting judgment or error, including review of journal-entry approval trails and communications.
steps.guidance: Engage forensic accounting and external auditors as appropriate given the sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Documented assessment of materiality and intent.
steps.abort: If the item is a legitimate accounting judgment or immaterial error, close as a non-fraud finding referred to normal accounting-policy review.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under Legal privilege and assess disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Work with Legal to preserve all relevant records under legal hold, ideally under privilege, and assess SEC/regulatory and auditor disclosure obligations and timelines.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with outside securities counsel and the Audit Committee as needed.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; disclosure-obligation assessment documented.

steps.title: Restrict the implicated employee's financial-system access under Legal direction
steps.desc: Under Legal's direction, restrict the implicated employee's access to financial reporting systems and journal-entry authority, sequenced to avoid compromising the investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with HR/Legal/Compliance.
steps.outcome: Further manipulation prevented.

steps.title: Notify Audit Committee/Board and external auditors
steps.desc: Notify the Audit Committee/Board and external auditors per governance and audit requirements given the severity and regulatory exposure.
steps.outcome: Appropriate governance bodies and auditors notified.

steps.title: Complete forensic investigation and determine restatement scope
steps.desc: Complete the forensic investigation into the full scope of the falsification and determine whether a financial restatement is required.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with outside counsel, forensic accounting, and external auditors.
steps.outcome: Documented investigation findings and restatement determination.

steps.title: Strengthen financial-reporting controls
steps.desc: Strengthen journal-entry review, segregation of duties, and management-override controls in the financial close process to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Controller/CFO and Internal Audit.
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Complete restatement, regulatory filing, and employment action
steps.desc: Complete any required financial restatement and regulatory filings, and determine employment action and potential criminal referral with Legal/HR/Board.
steps.outcome: Restatement and employment actions completed per Legal/Board direction.

steps.title: Document findings and update internal control framework
steps.desc: Finalize documentation (subject to privilege considerations) and update the internal control framework (e.g. SOX controls) based on lessons learned.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated control framework.

ITID-53711.def: Fraud in which an adversary who has obtained stolen payment card data (via phishing, skimming, or a data breach) enrolls that card into a mobile digital wallet (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay) under their own or an accomplice's device, exploiting weak card-verification steps during the tokenization/provisioning process to make fraudulent tap-to-pay or in-app purchases.
ITID-53711.purpose: Captures fraud in which stolen payment card details are tokenized into a mobile digital wallet to enable fraudulent purchases.
scopeIncludes: Provisioning a stolen card into a digital wallet using weak or bypassed card-verification (e.g., a compromised one-time passcode)
Use of the tokenized card for in-store tap-to-pay or in-app fraudulent purchases
Social-engineering a cardholder's bank/issuer call center to authorize the provisioning
scopeExcludes: Takeover of an existing wallet via SIM swap (ITID-53712)
Theft/immediate cash-out of an existing cryptocurrency wallet (ITID-53713)
ITID-53711.severity: Medium. Losses are typically bounded by card limits and issuer fraud-loss policies, but tokenization abuse can enable rapid, hard-to-trace point-of-sale fraud.
ITID-53711.priority: P2 for the company as card-issuer/merchant; routed primarily to the card network's/issuer's fraud operations.
ITID-53711.escalation: Escalate to card-issuer fraud operations for chargeback/dispute handling; escalate to the SOC only if the source of the stolen card data traces back to a company system compromise.
indicators: Card provisioned to a digital wallet on a device with no prior relationship to the cardholder
Provisioning verification completed via a channel (SMS OTP, call center) inconsistent with the genuine cardholder's known devices
Rapid, geographically dispersed tap-to-pay transactions shortly after provisioning
vectors: Provisioning using stolen card-data plus intercepted or socially engineered OTP
Call-center social engineering to complete card verification
rootCauses: Weak card-verification requirements during digital-wallet provisioning
Insufficient device/behavioral risk scoring at the point of card enrollment
controls: Step-up verification (beyond SMS OTP) for digital-wallet card provisioning
Device and behavioral risk scoring at enrollment
Post-provisioning transaction velocity monitoring
ITID-53711.detection: Detected through card-network/issuer fraud-scoring systems on provisioning and subsequent transactions; no SOC technical telemetry involved unless the stolen card data traces to a company breach.
ITID-53711.response: Card-issuer fraud operations blocks the token and reverses fraudulent charges; SOC investigates only if company-held card data was the exposure source.
metrics: Number of fraudulent tokenization events identified per quarter
Dollar amount of fraudulent transactions blocked vs. completed
sops: Digital Wallet Provisioning Fraud Response SOP
ITID-53711.notes: This is a card-issuer/payment-network fraud typology; no ATT&CK Enterprise technique cleanly applies to the tokenization-abuse mechanism itself. Where the stolen card data traces to a breach of company systems, cross-reference the relevant ITID-51xxx breach leaf for the intrusion technique.

playbook.name: Mobile Payment Wallet (Apple Pay/Google Pay) Tokenization Fraud
playbook.description: An attacker fraudulently provisions a victim's payment card into a mobile wallet on an attacker-controlled device (e.g. via social engineering of the card issuer or phished card details), enabling unauthorized tokenized transactions.

steps.title: Identify unauthorized tokenized transactions
steps.desc: Identify unauthorized transactions on the company card/account and confirm they originated from a mobile-wallet token rather than the physical card.
steps.guidance: Review card issuer transaction data for the token/device identifier used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized wallet-token transactions identified.

steps.title: Determine how the card was provisioned to the attacker's device
steps.desc: Work with the card issuer to determine how the fraudulent wallet provisioning occurred (e.g. phished card details plus social-engineered OTP, compromised issuer verification).
steps.guidance: Request the issuer's provisioning verification log.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the fraudulent provisioning identified.

steps.title: Preserve transaction and provisioning evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the transaction records and wallet-provisioning logs obtained from the issuer for the dispute and any law-enforcement filing.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for dispute/reporting purposes.

steps.title: Remove the fraudulent token and freeze the card
steps.desc: Contact the card issuer immediately to remove/deactivate the fraudulent wallet token and freeze or reissue the underlying card.
steps.guidance: Time-sensitive — the attacker can continue transacting until the token is revoked.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent token revoked; card frozen/reissued.

steps.title: Review other cardholders for similar provisioning attempts
steps.desc: Check whether other company cards experienced similar unauthorized wallet-provisioning attempts around the same time, indicating a broader campaign.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the card issuer's fraud team.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified.

steps.title: Strengthen wallet-provisioning verification with issuer
steps.desc: Work with the card issuer to strengthen the verification requirements for mobile-wallet provisioning (e.g. stronger OTP/step-up authentication).
steps.outcome: Documented verification improvement reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Dispute fraudulent charges and recover funds
steps.desc: File a formal dispute with the card issuer for all fraudulent transactions and pursue reimbursement per the applicable card-fraud liability policy.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent charges reversed/reimbursed.

steps.title: Document incident and update cardholder awareness
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief cardholders on recognizing phishing attempts that lead to fraudulent wallet provisioning.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and awareness update.

ITID-53712.def: Fraud in which an adversary convinces or bribes a mobile carrier (or exploits carrier support processes) to port a victim's phone number onto a SIM the adversary controls, then uses SMS-based authentication tied to that number to take over the victim's digital payment wallets, banking apps, or exchange accounts.
ITID-53712.purpose: Captures fraud in which an adversary takes over a victim's mobile number via SIM swap to seize control of digital wallets and payment accounts tied to that number.
scopeIncludes: Social engineering a mobile carrier's support staff into porting a number to an attacker-controlled SIM
Using the hijacked number to intercept SMS one-time passcodes and reset wallet/banking credentials
Cash-out or fund transfer from the victim's accounts following takeover
scopeExcludes: Tokenization of stolen card data into a digital wallet with no SIM/number takeover involved (ITID-53711)
Theft/cash-out of an already-compromised cryptocurrency wallet via a non-SIM-swap vector (ITID-53713)
ITID-53712.severity: High. SIM swap takeover typically grants the adversary access to every account tied to the victim's phone number, not just a single wallet.
ITID-53712.priority: P1 while the takeover is active and further account resets/transfers are possible; P2 once the number is recovered and accounts are secured.
ITID-53712.escalation: Escalate immediately to the victim's mobile carrier for number recovery, to affected financial institutions to freeze accounts, and to the SOC if a company-issued device/number is involved.
indicators: Sudden, unexplained loss of cellular service on the victim's device
Password-reset or MFA-enrollment activity across multiple accounts within a short window
Carrier account showing a recent, unrecognized SIM-swap or port-out request
vectors: Social engineering of mobile carrier support/retail staff
Bribery or insider collusion with carrier employees
Exploitation of weak carrier identity-verification processes for SIM swaps
rootCauses: Reliance on SMS-based one-time passcodes as the primary/sole MFA factor for high-value accounts
Weak carrier-side identity verification for SIM swap/port requests
No account-level lock or additional PIN requirement on the mobile carrier account
controls: Migration away from SMS-based OTP to app-based or hardware MFA for high-value accounts
Carrier-account PIN/lock enrollment to prevent unauthorized SIM swap
Account-recovery workflows that do not rely solely on SMS verification
ITID-53712.detection: Detected through carrier-side port/SIM-swap alerting and account-level anomalous-authentication monitoring; largely outside SOC's direct technical telemetry.
ITID-53712.response: Carrier and financial-institution fraud teams lead recovery; SOC investigates only where a company-managed device, number, or MFA enrollment is implicated.
metrics: Number of SIM-swap takeover incidents reported per quarter
Percentage of affected accounts using SMS-only MFA at time of incident
sops: SIM Swap Account Takeover Response SOP
detections: Anomalous authentication/MFA-enrollment monitoring across linked accounts
ITID-53712.notes: SIM swap is a mobile-carrier-account-takeover technique that falls outside ATT&CK Enterprise's scope; a comparable mobile-specific technique (T1451-style SIM swap concepts) exists only in the separate ATT&CK Mobile matrix, not Enterprise, so mapped_mitre is left empty here.

playbook.name: Digital Wallet Takeover via SIM Swap
playbook.description: An attacker socially engineers the victim's mobile carrier into porting their phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM, then uses SMS-based authentication to take over the victim's digital payment wallet and initiate unauthorized transactions.

steps.title: Confirm the SIM swap occurred and identify affected accounts
steps.desc: Confirm with the victim and the mobile carrier that an unauthorized SIM swap/port occurred, and identify which digital wallet, banking, or other accounts rely on that phone number for authentication.
steps.guidance: Check for loss of cellular service reported by the victim as the initial indicator.
steps.outcome: Confirmed SIM swap and list of affected accounts.

steps.title: Identify unauthorized transactions across affected accounts
steps.desc: Review transaction history across all accounts tied to the compromised phone number for unauthorized activity following the swap.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with each affected financial institution/wallet provider.
steps.outcome: Full scope of unauthorized transactions identified.

steps.title: Coordinate with the telecom provider to reverse the SIM swap
steps.desc: Contact the mobile carrier's fraud team immediately to reverse the unauthorized port and restore service to the victim's legitimate device.
steps.guidance: Provide identity verification per the carrier's fraud-recovery process; escalate to the carrier's security team if front-line support cannot act quickly.
steps.outcome: Phone number restored to the victim's legitimate device.

steps.title: Freeze affected wallets/accounts and revoke SMS-based sessions
steps.desc: Freeze or lock the affected digital wallet and financial accounts, and revoke any active sessions or SMS-authenticated changes made during the compromise window.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with each wallet/bank provider's fraud team.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized transactions prevented.

steps.title: Move affected accounts off SMS-based authentication
steps.desc: Replace SMS-based two-factor authentication on the affected accounts with app-based authenticator or hardware-key MFA.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the account holder and IT/security if this is a corporate-linked account.
steps.outcome: SMS-based authentication vector eliminated for affected accounts.

steps.title: Add carrier-level port-protection (PIN/lock)
steps.desc: Work with the mobile carrier to add a port-protection PIN or account lock to prevent future unauthorized SIM swaps.
steps.outcome: Carrier-level protection in place.

steps.title: Dispute fraudulent transactions and pursue recovery
steps.desc: File disputes with affected financial institutions/wallet providers for fraudulent transactions and pursue reimbursement.
steps.guidance: File a police report/IC3 report to support disputes.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent transactions disputed; recovery pursued.

steps.title: Document incident and update MFA guidance
steps.desc: Document the incident and update organizational guidance discouraging SMS-based MFA in favor of stronger authentication methods.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated guidance.

ITID-53713.def: Fraud in which an adversary who has already obtained control of a victim's cryptocurrency wallet (by any compromise vector) immediately transfers the wallet's holdings to an attacker-controlled address, prioritizing speed over concealment given cryptocurrency's irreversible transaction model.
ITID-53713.purpose: Captures the monetization step in which funds are moved out of an already-compromised cryptocurrency wallet before the victim or institution can react.
scopeIncludes: Immediate, single-transaction sweep of a compromised wallet's full balance to an attacker address
Rapid sequential transfers across multiple attacker-controlled addresses to outrun freeze/flag attempts
Use of a decentralized exchange for instant swap-and-scatter following wallet compromise
scopeExcludes: The technical compromise of the wallet itself (private-key theft, exchange infrastructure breach, malicious smart-contract approval, seed-phrase phishing), which is classified under ITID-51441 through ITID-51445
Laundering of the stolen funds through a mixer/tumbler after initial transfer-out, classified under ITID-53941
ITID-53713.severity: High. Cryptocurrency transfers are irreversible once confirmed on-chain, making this the point of no return for fund recovery.
ITID-53713.priority: P1 immediately upon detection, given the narrow window (often minutes) in which exchange-side freezing of a destination address may still be possible.
ITID-53713.escalation: Escalate immediately to any exchange whose address received the funds (to request a freeze), to the SOC for the underlying compromise investigation, and to blockchain-analytics/law-enforcement partners for tracing.
indicators: Full-balance outbound transaction immediately following a wallet-access event
Transfer to a newly created address with no prior transaction history
Rapid multi-hop transfers across addresses within minutes of the initial compromise
vectors: Automated sweep scripts triggered immediately upon obtaining wallet access
Use of decentralized exchanges for rapid, less-traceable asset conversion
rootCauses: No transaction-value or velocity alerting on high-value wallets
Absence of a time-delay/withdrawal-limit mechanism on custodial wallet infrastructure
The upstream wallet-compromise vector itself (see ITID-51441-51445) going undetected
controls: Withdrawal time-delay and velocity limits on custodial wallet infrastructure
Real-time blockchain-analytics monitoring for known attacker-address patterns
Rapid exchange-partner coordination protocol for freeze requests
ITID-53713.detection: On-chain transaction monitoring and blockchain-analytics tooling provide real-time visibility into the transfer-out event itself, though the window to act is very short.
ITID-53713.response: SOC/security investigates the upstream compromise per the applicable ITID-514xx leaf; treasury/fraud-operations coordinates exchange freeze requests and law-enforcement/blockchain-analytics engagement for tracing.
metrics: Percentage of stolen funds frozen/recovered vs. fully lost
Median time from compromise to fund transfer-out
detections: Real-time blockchain-analytics alerting on known attacker addresses
ITID-53713.notes: Scoped to the FRAUD/MONETIZATION angle only (the fund transfer-out itself). The BREACH/THEFT angle — how the wallet was compromised in the first place — is covered under ITID-51441 (hot wallet key compromise), ITID-51442 (exchange infrastructure breach), ITID-51443 (malicious smart-contract approval), and ITID-51444 (seed-phrase phishing); this leaf and those are companion records covering the same event from different stages of the kill chain.

playbook.name: Stolen Cryptocurrency Wallet Used for Immediate Fund Transfer Out
playbook.description: An attacker gains access to a company or employee cryptocurrency wallet (via phished credentials, compromised private key, or malware) and immediately transfers funds out to an attacker-controlled wallet, an inherently irreversible transaction.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized wallet access and outbound transaction
steps.desc: Confirm the wallet was accessed without authorization and identify the outbound transaction(s), amount, and destination wallet address(es).
steps.guidance: Review wallet access logs, device logs, and the blockchain explorer for the destination address.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access and transaction details documented.

steps.title: Determine the compromise vector
steps.desc: Determine how the wallet was compromised (phished seed phrase/private key, malware, compromised exchange account, insider access).
steps.guidance: Review endpoint logs, phishing reports, and exchange account activity.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the compromise identified.

steps.title: Freeze remaining funds and revoke access
steps.desc: Move any remaining funds in the compromised wallet to a new, secure wallet immediately, and revoke/rotate any compromised credentials, API keys, or device access.
steps.guidance: Blockchain transactions are irreversible — the priority is preventing further loss, not reversing the theft.
steps.outcome: Remaining funds secured; compromised access revoked.
steps.abort: If all funds were already transferred out, proceed directly to reporting/tracing.

steps.title: Alert exchanges to flag/freeze the destination address
steps.desc: Notify major cryptocurrency exchanges and blockchain analytics/law-enforcement liaison contacts of the destination wallet address in case the attacker attempts to cash out through a regulated exchange.
steps.guidance: Speed matters — exchanges can sometimes freeze funds if alerted before withdrawal to fiat.
steps.outcome: Destination address flagged with exchanges/analytics firms.
steps.tool: Blockchain analytics firm / exchange compliance contact

steps.title: Migrate to hardened wallet custody controls
steps.desc: Migrate remaining/replacement funds to a wallet architecture with stronger custody controls (e.g. multi-signature, hardware wallet, qualified custodian) rather than the single-key setup that was compromised.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury/security engineering.
steps.outcome: Stronger custody model in place.

steps.title: Close the specific compromise vector
steps.desc: Close the specific vector that led to compromise (e.g. remediate the phishing/malware pathway, revoke exposed credentials organization-wide).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with security engineering.
steps.outcome: Documented remediation of the root cause.

steps.title: Engage blockchain forensics and file law-enforcement report
steps.desc: Engage a blockchain forensics firm to trace the stolen funds and file a report with law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3) and, if applicable, the cyber-insurance carrier.
steps.outcome: Tracing engaged; formal reports filed; recovery pursued where possible.

steps.title: Document incident and update crypto-custody policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update the organization's cryptocurrency custody and access-control policy based on lessons learned.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated policy.

ITID-53714.def: An unclassified/general leaf for stolen payment wallet fraud that has not been further classified into mobile-wallet tokenization (ITID-53711), SIM-swap takeover (ITID-53712), or cryptocurrency wallet fund transfer-out (ITID-53713) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53714.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for stolen-payment-wallet fraud that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported stolen-payment-wallet fraud pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53711, ITID-53712, or ITID-53713
ITID-53714.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53714.priority: P2 pending triage given the typically fast-moving nature of payment-wallet fraud; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53714.escalation: Escalate to fraud operations/SOC for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53711, ITID-53712, or ITID-53713 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Stolen-wallet fraud flagged by payment-fraud monitoring but not yet root-caused
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard stolen-payment-wallet fraud triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53714.response: Fraud operations/SOC triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-537xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Stolen Payment Wallet Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53714.notes: Intake bucket only; should not accumulate a stable long-term population.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Stolen Payment Wallet
playbook.description: An attacker gains unauthorized access to a company or employee digital/cryptocurrency payment wallet through methods not otherwise captured by a more specific stolen-wallet scenario, enabling unauthorized transactions.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized wallet access and transactions
steps.desc: Confirm the wallet was accessed without authorization and identify any unauthorized transactions.
steps.guidance: Review wallet provider logs and transaction history.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access and transaction details documented.

steps.title: Determine the compromise vector
steps.desc: Determine how the wallet was compromised.
steps.guidance: Review device, credential, and access logs.
steps.outcome: Root cause identified.
steps.abort: If no unauthorized access is confirmed, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the unauthorized access
steps.desc: Preserve wallet provider logs, access records, and communications documenting the unauthorized access for dispute/reporting purposes.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for recovery and reporting.

steps.title: Freeze the wallet and revoke compromised access
steps.desc: Freeze the wallet/account and revoke or rotate any compromised credentials or device access to prevent further loss.
steps.guidance: Digital/crypto payment transactions are often irreversible once sent — prioritize stopping further loss.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized transactions prevented.

steps.title: Notify the wallet provider's fraud team
steps.desc: Notify the wallet/payment provider's fraud team to request any available freeze, reversal, or investigative support.
steps.outcome: Provider engaged and any available protective action taken.

steps.title: Close the compromise vector and strengthen wallet access controls
steps.desc: Close the specific vector that enabled compromise and strengthen the wallet's authentication/access controls (e.g. stronger MFA, device restrictions).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT/security.
steps.outcome: Documented remediation reducing recurrence risk.

steps.title: Dispute transactions and pursue recovery
steps.desc: File disputes with the wallet provider for unauthorized transactions and pursue recovery, filing a law-enforcement report if warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued to the extent possible.

steps.title: Document incident and update wallet-security guidance
steps.desc: Document the incident and update guidance on securing digital payment wallets.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53721.def: Fraud in which a scammer sends a victim (or has the victim believe they received) a payment via a peer-to-peer app such as Venmo, Cash App, or Zelle that exceeds an agreed amount, then requests the victim refund the difference — after which the original payment is reversed, revoked, or was never genuinely completed, leaving the victim out the refunded amount.
ITID-53721.purpose: Captures scams that trick a victim into sending money via a P2P payment app based on a fraudulent overpayment pretext.
scopeIncludes: Overpayment for a good/service sold by the victim followed by a request to refund the excess
Fraudulent claim of an accidental transfer requesting the victim send money back
Use of a since-reversed or fraudulent funding source for the initial 'overpayment'
scopeExcludes: Transaction-reversal fraud initiated by a fake buyer/seller in a marketplace transaction after genuine goods exchange (ITID-53722)
ITID-53721.severity: Low-Medium per incident, bounded by P2P app transfer limits; primarily relevant where company payroll, expense-reimbursement, or vendor-payment processes route through such apps.
ITID-53721.priority: P3 in most cases, routed to fraud-awareness/employee reporting rather than SOC triage.
ITID-53721.escalation: Escalate to fraud operations for pattern tracking; escalate to the SOC only if the scam is delivered via a company-branded communication channel that has been compromised.
indicators: Payment received via P2P app followed shortly by a request to refund a 'mistaken' excess amount
Original payment shown as pending/reversed only after the refund is sent
Urgency or pressure tactics accompanying the refund request
vectors: Fraudulent or stolen funding source used for the initial overpayment
Social engineering pressure to refund quickly before the original payment settles
rootCauses: P2P app design allowing a payment to appear settled before it has actually cleared
Insufficient employee awareness of the overpayment-scam pattern
controls: Employee awareness training on P2P overpayment scam patterns
Policy requiring confirmed settlement (not just 'pending' status) before any refund is issued via a P2P app
ITID-53721.detection: Minimal technical detection surface; primarily caught through employee self-reporting and P2P-platform-side fraud monitoring.
ITID-53721.response: Fraud operations tracks the pattern and supports employee reimbursement guidance; no SOC technical response typically required.
metrics: Number of overpayment scam attempts reported per quarter
Dollar amount lost to premature refunds
sops: P2P Payment Scam Employee Reporting SOP
ITID-53721.notes: social-engineering/scam pattern executed via legitimate payment-app functionality — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked as fraud, not a technical intrusion.

playbook.name: Peer-to-Peer Payment App Scam (Venmo/Cash App/Zelle Overpayment Scam)
playbook.description: An attacker sends an overpayment (often via a fraudulent/reversible funding source) through a P2P payment app and requests the excess be refunded or forwarded, then reverses the original payment, leaving the company or employee out the refunded amount.

steps.title: Identify the overpayment and refund/forward request
steps.desc: Identify the specific P2P transaction(s) involved — the original overpayment received and any refund or forwarding request made to the attacker.
steps.guidance: Interview the employee/party involved to establish the full transaction sequence and timing.
steps.outcome: Full transaction sequence documented.

steps.title: Confirm the original payment's funding source is fraudulent/reversed
steps.desc: Confirm with the payment app/bank whether the original overpayment was funded by a stolen card, fraudulent bank link, or has been reversed as unauthorized.
steps.guidance: Request the transaction status directly from the P2P platform's fraud/support team.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the funding source was fraudulent or the payment was reversed.
steps.abort: If the original payment is confirmed legitimate and not reversed, close as false positive/billing dispute.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-preservation requirements.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Halt any pending refund/forward payment
steps.desc: If the refund/forward payment has not yet been sent, halt it immediately.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/AP if a business account is involved.
steps.outcome: No further funds sent to the scammer.
steps.abort: If already sent, proceed to reporting and recovery steps.

steps.title: Report the scam to the payment app and freeze the linked account if needed
steps.desc: Report the fraudulent transaction to the P2P platform's fraud team and request a freeze/review of the linked account.
steps.outcome: Platform fraud case opened; account protected from further loss.

steps.title: Establish a no-refund-before-settlement policy for P2P transactions
steps.desc: Establish a policy that no refund or forwarding of funds is made until the original P2P payment has fully and irrevocably settled (accounting for the platform's reversal window).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance leadership on the policy for any business use of P2P payment apps.
steps.outcome: Documented policy reducing recurrence.

steps.title: Pursue recovery through the platform and law enforcement
steps.desc: Pursue recovery of lost funds through the P2P platform's dispute process and file a report with law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3) for the fraudulent funding source.
steps.outcome: Dispute/recovery process initiated.

steps.title: Document incident and brief staff on the overpayment-scam pattern
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief relevant staff on recognizing overpayment scams involving P2P payment apps.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and staff awareness.

ITID-53722.def: Fraud in which a buyer or seller in a peer-to-peer payment app transaction disputes or reverses a completed payment through the app's or an underlying bank's chargeback/reversal mechanism after already receiving the goods, service, or counter-payment, exploiting the reversal process itself as the fraud vector.
ITID-53722.purpose: Captures fraud in which a party to a P2P/marketplace transaction fraudulently reverses a payment after receiving goods, services, or funds.
scopeIncludes: A fraudulent buyer disputing/reversing payment after receiving goods shipped by the victim seller
A fraudulent seller claiming non-receipt of payment to trigger a reversal after already delivering nothing
Abuse of a linked bank account's chargeback rights against a P2P app payment after the counterparty has already released value
scopeExcludes: Overpayment-refund scams where the initial payment was never genuinely settled (ITID-53721)
ITID-53722.severity: Low-Medium per incident; aggregate exposure can be meaningful where the company routes marketplace-style vendor or gig-worker payments through P2P apps.
ITID-53722.priority: P3 in most cases, routed to fraud/finance operations rather than SOC triage.
ITID-53722.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance operations for dispute-resolution and evidence submission (proof of delivery/service); escalate to legal for repeat-offender patterns.
indicators: Payment dispute filed shortly after goods/service delivery is confirmed
Counterparty account with a history of repeated dispute/reversal filings
Dispute claim inconsistent with documented proof of delivery or service completion
vectors: Abuse of bank-level chargeback rights on a linked account after a P2P transaction settles
False non-receipt claims filed with the payment app's dispute process
rootCauses: Insufficient proof-of-delivery/service documentation captured at time of transaction
P2P app or linked-bank dispute processes not designed for commercial-transaction evidence standards
controls: Mandatory proof-of-delivery/service documentation for company transactions conducted via P2P apps
Counterparty dispute-history screening before engaging in repeat P2P transactions
Preference for payment rails with stronger commercial dispute protections for business use
ITID-53722.detection: Minimal technical detection surface; caught through finance-operations dispute tracking rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-53722.response: Finance/fraud operations manages dispute evidence submission and recovery; legal engagement for repeat-offender patterns.
metrics: Number of fraudulent reversal disputes identified per quarter
Dollar amount recovered through evidence-based dispute rebuttal
sops: P2P Transaction Reversal Dispute Response SOP
ITID-53722.notes: social-engineering/scam pattern executed via legitimate payment-app dispute functionality — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked as fraud, not a technical intrusion.

playbook.name: Fake Buyer/Seller Payment App Transaction Reversal Fraud
playbook.description: A counterparty posing as a legitimate buyer or seller completes a P2P payment app transaction and then fraudulently disputes or reverses the payment (e.g. via a false unauthorized-transaction claim) after receiving goods/services or the original funds.

steps.title: Identify the disputed/reversed transaction
