steps.desc: Identify the specific transaction that was reversed or disputed and pull the full transaction and communication history with the counterparty.
steps.guidance: Preserve all chat/communication with the counterparty as evidence.
steps.outcome: Full transaction and communication record assembled.

steps.title: Assess whether the reversal claim is fraudulent
steps.desc: Review the reversal/dispute claim against the actual transaction facts (goods/services delivered, communication record) to determine if the counterparty's claim is false.
steps.guidance: Gather delivery confirmation, shipping tracking, or service-completion evidence to counter a false claim.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence supporting or refuting the fraud determination.
steps.abort: If the dispute is legitimate (e.g. goods not delivered as promised), close as a customer-service/legitimate-dispute matter rather than fraud.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-preservation requirements.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Contest the reversal with the payment platform
steps.desc: Submit a formal contest/appeal to the P2P platform with supporting evidence to prevent or reverse the fraudulent chargeback.
steps.guidance: Act quickly — most platforms have a limited window to contest disputes.
steps.outcome: Contest filed within the platform's window.

steps.title: Suspend further transactions with the counterparty
steps.desc: Block or flag the counterparty from further transactions pending resolution.
steps.outcome: No further exposure to the same counterparty.

steps.title: Require proof-of-delivery for P2P transactions going forward
steps.desc: Implement a requirement to capture proof-of-delivery/service-completion evidence for any business transaction conducted via P2P payment apps, to support future dispute contests.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Sales leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented process improvement.

steps.title: Pursue recovery through platform escalation or small-claims action
steps.desc: If the platform contest is denied, pursue further escalation with the platform or consider small-claims/civil action to recover the loss.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal if the amount warrants formal action.
steps.outcome: Recovery path pursued to the extent economically warranted.

steps.title: Document incident and update transaction-evidence practices
steps.desc: Document the incident and update practices for evidencing P2P transactions to reduce future dispute exposure.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53723.def: An unclassified/general leaf for fraudulent P2P/digital payment app transactions that have not been further classified into overpayment-scam (ITID-53721) or transaction-reversal-fraud (ITID-53722) subtypes at the time of intake.

vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard digital payment app fraud triage workflow prior to subtype classification

sops: Digital Payment App Fraud Intake and Triage SOP

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Fraudulent Digital Payment App Transaction
playbook.description: A fraudulent transaction occurs via a digital payment app through a mechanism not otherwise captured by a more specific P2P fraud scenario, resulting in unauthorized loss of funds.

steps.title: Identify the fraudulent transaction and pull records
steps.desc: Identify the specific transaction(s) and pull the full transaction and account activity history from the payment app.
steps.outcome: Transaction records assembled for review.

steps.title: Determine the fraud mechanism
steps.desc: Analyze the transaction and account activity to determine the specific fraud mechanism used.
steps.outcome: Documented fraud mechanism.
steps.abort: If the transaction is confirmed legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-preservation requirements.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Freeze the account/halt pending transactions
steps.desc: Freeze the affected account or halt any pending related transactions to prevent further loss.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the payment app's fraud team.
steps.outcome: Further loss prevented.

steps.title: Report the fraud to the payment platform
steps.desc: Report the fraudulent transaction to the payment platform's fraud team and request a formal fraud case.
steps.outcome: Platform fraud case opened.

steps.title: Close the identified control gap
steps.desc: Identify and close the specific control gap that enabled the fraud (e.g. account-linking verification, transaction-limit review).
steps.outcome: Documented control enhancement.

steps.title: Pursue recovery and file law-enforcement report
steps.desc: Pursue recovery through the platform's dispute process and file a law-enforcement report if warranted.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued to the extent possible.

steps.title: Document incident and update awareness
steps.desc: Document the incident and update relevant staff awareness on digital-payment-app fraud patterns.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53731.def: Fraud in which the creators of a decentralized finance (DeFi) token or protocol, after attracting investor funds into a liquidity pool, withdraw ('drain') that liquidity for themselves, instantly and permanently collapsing the token's tradeable value and leaving investors unable to sell their holdings.
ITID-53731.purpose: Captures rug pulls in which a DeFi project's creators drain the liquidity pool backing a token, collapsing its value.
scopeIncludes: Removal of pooled liquidity by a project's deployer wallet(s) shortly after a marketing-driven investment surge
Retention of an undisclosed minting/liquidity-control privilege in the token's smart contract enabling the drain
Coordinated promotion (paid influencers, fake community hype) preceding the drain to maximize invested funds
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent NFT project rug pulls (ITID-53732)
Theft of an existing wallet's holdings via a malicious smart-contract approval, which is a breach/theft rather than a project-level scam (ITID-51443)
ITID-53731.severity: High for affected investors/company treasury exposure; total loss is typical once a drain occurs given no recovery mechanism exists on most such tokens.
ITID-53731.priority: P2 for the company if company treasury funds were invested; P3 if the exposure is limited to advisory/awareness for employees or customers.
ITID-53731.escalation: Escalate to legal/compliance and blockchain-analytics/law-enforcement partners for tracing; escalate to finance if company treasury funds are implicated.
indicators: Token contract retaining an unrenounced owner privilege to withdraw pooled liquidity
Sudden, large liquidity-pool withdrawal by the deployer wallet coinciding with a token price collapse
Aggressive, time-pressured promotional campaign preceding the token's launch
vectors: Smart contracts with an undisclosed or unrenounced liquidity-withdrawal privilege
Paid social-media promotion to inflate investment before the drain
rootCauses: Lack of pre-investment smart-contract audit/renounced-ownership verification
No due-diligence process before company or employee-facing exposure to a DeFi token
controls: Mandatory smart-contract audit and renounced-ownership verification before any treasury exposure to a DeFi token
Employee guidance discouraging speculative DeFi investment using company resources
Blockchain-analytics monitoring of any tokens the company holds or has invested in
ITID-53731.detection: On-chain analytics can retrospectively confirm a liquidity drain event; no proactive technical detection prevents the underlying scam.
ITID-53731.response: Finance/legal quantifies exposure and pursues any available recovery/reporting avenues; law-enforcement/blockchain-analytics referral for tracing where losses are material.
metrics: Dollar exposure per confirmed rug pull affecting company or employee funds
Number of DeFi tokens flagged as high-risk pre-investment
detections: On-chain liquidity-pool monitoring for held tokens
ITID-53731.notes: financial fraud/investment scam pattern, not an intrusion technique — no ATT&CK Enterprise mapping applies; tracked as fraud/investment-loss, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Liquidity Pool Drain Rug Pull (DeFi Token Scam)
playbook.description: The company invests in or holds a DeFi token whose developers drain the associated liquidity pool, rendering the token worthless — the company is a victim of an external scam rather than a technical compromise of its own systems.

steps.title: Confirm the liquidity drain and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Confirm via blockchain explorer that the liquidity pool was drained by the project's developers/deployer address, and quantify the company's exposure (token holdings and cost basis).
steps.guidance: Use blockchain explorers and DeFi analytics tools to trace the drain transaction.
steps.outcome: Confirmed rug pull with quantified company exposure.
steps.abort: If the price drop is due to normal market volatility rather than a liquidity drain, close as an investment-loss matter rather than fraud.

steps.title: Review the investment-decision trail
steps.desc: Review how and by whom the investment decision was made, including any due-diligence records, to establish the internal decision-making context.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Treasury and whoever approved the investment.
steps.outcome: Documented investment-decision trail.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-preservation requirements.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Halt further exposure to the token/project
steps.desc: Immediately halt any further planned investment, staking, or transactions involving the drained token/project, and withdraw any remaining recoverable assets.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury.
steps.outcome: No further exposure or loss.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Finance leadership of the loss event
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Finance leadership of the confirmed loss event for financial-reporting and potential-disclosure assessment.
steps.outcome: Leadership notified; financial-reporting impact assessed.

steps.title: Implement enhanced due-diligence-before-investing controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced due-diligence requirements before any future digital-asset investment (e.g. smart-contract audit verification, developer-team KYC, liquidity-lock verification, independent risk review/approval).
steps.guidance: There is no technical vulnerability of the company's own systems to patch here — the control fix is procedural investment governance.
steps.outcome: Documented due-diligence policy for future digital-asset investment decisions.

steps.title: Assess loss for financial reporting and consider regulator/law-enforcement reporting
steps.desc: Finalize the loss assessment for financial statement treatment, and report to law enforcement and/or securities/consumer-protection regulators as appropriate given the scale of the scam.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Finance on materiality and reporting obligations.
steps.outcome: Loss recorded appropriately; regulatory/law-enforcement reporting completed if warranted.

steps.title: Document findings and update investment governance policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update the organization's digital-asset investment governance policy based on lessons learned.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated policy.

ITID-53732.def: Fraud in which the creators of a non-fungible token (NFT) collection collect minting proceeds from buyers based on promised future utility, roadmap features, or community benefits, then abandon the project and disappear with the funds without delivering on those promises.
ITID-53732.purpose: Captures rug pulls in which the creators of an NFT project abandon it and abscond with mint proceeds after promising future development.
scopeIncludes: Collection of mint proceeds followed by the creators disappearing (deleting social media, abandoning the roadmap)
Misrepresentation of the project's utility, team credentials, or partnerships to drive minting activity
Withdrawal of the project's associated treasury/royalty wallet shortly after mint completion
scopeExcludes: Liquidity-pool-based DeFi token rug pulls (ITID-53731)
ITID-53732.severity: High for affected investors/company treasury exposure; loss is typically total and unrecoverable once creators disappear.
ITID-53732.priority: P2 for the company if treasury funds were used to mint/purchase NFTs; P3 if exposure is limited to employee awareness.
ITID-53732.escalation: Escalate to legal/compliance and blockchain-analytics/law-enforcement partners for tracing; escalate to finance if company treasury funds are implicated.
indicators: Project team using pseudonymous identities with no verifiable credentials
Sudden cessation of project communication/development shortly after mint proceeds are collected
Treasury wallet withdrawal inconsistent with any disclosed roadmap spending
vectors: Misrepresented roadmap/utility promises to drive mint volume
Pseudonymous team identity concealing lack of accountability
rootCauses: Lack of pre-purchase due diligence on project-team identity and track record
No policy governing company or employee use of funds for NFT speculation
controls: Due-diligence requirement (verified team identity, track record) before any treasury exposure to an NFT project
Employee guidance discouraging speculative NFT investment using company resources
ITID-53732.detection: On-chain analytics can retrospectively confirm treasury-wallet withdrawal and abandonment; no proactive technical detection prevents the underlying scam.
ITID-53732.response: Finance/legal quantifies exposure and pursues any available recovery/reporting avenues; law-enforcement/blockchain-analytics referral for tracing where losses are material.
metrics: Dollar exposure per confirmed NFT rug pull affecting company or employee funds
Number of NFT projects flagged as high-risk pre-purchase
detections: On-chain treasury-wallet monitoring for held project positions
ITID-53732.notes: financial fraud/investment scam pattern, not an intrusion technique — no ATT&CK Enterprise mapping applies; tracked as fraud/investment-loss, not SOC technical response.

steps.guidance: The eradication focus is procedural investment governance, not a technical vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Documented due-diligence policy.

steps.title: Assess loss for financial reporting and consider regulator/law-enforcement reporting
steps.desc: Finalize loss assessment for financial statement treatment and report to law enforcement and/or relevant regulators as appropriate.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Finance.
steps.outcome: Loss recorded; reporting completed if warranted.

steps.title: Document findings and update investment governance policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update the organization's digital-asset investment governance policy.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated policy.

ITID-53741.def: Fraud in which the operators of a cryptocurrency exchange (which may have appeared legitimate for a period of operation) abruptly halt customer withdrawals, cease communication, and abscond with the funds held on customers' behalf, having typically never fully backed customer balances with real assets.
ITID-53741.purpose: Captures exit scams in which a cryptocurrency exchange's operators halt withdrawals and disappear with customer deposits.
scopeIncludes: An exchange freezing withdrawals while continuing to accept deposits shortly before disappearing
Operators fabricating a security-incident or regulatory pretext to justify a withdrawal freeze before absconding
Exchange operating on a fractional-reserve basis without disclosing the shortfall to customers
scopeExcludes: Insider fraud by exchange staff against a genuinely solvent, ongoing exchange (ITID-53742)
Theft of individual customer wallets via infrastructure compromise (ITID-51442)
ITID-53741.severity: High. Exit scams typically result in total, unrecoverable loss of all funds held on the exchange at the time of the freeze.
ITID-53741.priority: P1 immediately upon signs of a withdrawal freeze if company treasury funds are held on the exchange, to attempt any possible emergency withdrawal; P2 once losses are confirmed and the matter moves to recovery/legal.
ITID-53741.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/treasury and legal if company funds are held on the affected exchange; escalate to law enforcement and industry fraud-intelligence sharing groups regardless.
indicators: Sudden, unexplained withdrawal freeze or processing delays affecting all customers simultaneously
Exchange operators becoming unreachable or deleting official communication channels
Prior reports or audits questioning the exchange's reserve backing
vectors: Operating an exchange on a fractional or non-existent reserve basis
Fabricated technical/regulatory pretexts to justify a withdrawal freeze
rootCauses: Company treasury holding cryptocurrency on an exchange without independent proof-of-reserves verification
No policy limiting the duration/amount of company funds held on third-party exchanges
controls: Independent proof-of-reserves verification before holding material treasury funds on any exchange
Policy limiting duration and amount of company funds held on third-party exchanges
Diversification across exchanges to limit single-point exposure
ITID-53741.detection: No proactive technical detection prevents an exit scam; early warning may come from industry fraud-intelligence sharing and reserve-audit monitoring.
ITID-53741.response: Finance/treasury attempts emergency withdrawal at first sign of freeze; legal pursues claims through bankruptcy/regulatory proceedings where applicable.
metrics: Dollar exposure per confirmed exchange exit scam affecting company funds
Percentage of treasury crypto holdings verified via independent proof-of-reserves
detections: Proof-of-reserves monitoring for exchanges holding company funds
ITID-53741.notes: financial fraud/investment scam pattern, not an intrusion technique — no ATT&CK Enterprise mapping applies; tracked as fraud/counterparty-risk loss, not SOC technical response.

playbook.name: Fake Cryptocurrency Exchange Exit Scam
playbook.description: A cryptocurrency exchange holding company funds suddenly halts withdrawals and disappears with customer/company assets ('exit scam') — the company is a victim of an external scam rather than a compromise of its own systems.

steps.title: Confirm the exit scam and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Confirm the exchange has halted withdrawals, gone offline, or otherwise ceased operations under suspicious circumstances, and quantify the company's held balance/assets at risk.
steps.guidance: Check exchange status pages, regulatory alerts, and community reports for corroboration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exit scam with quantified exposure.
steps.abort: If the exchange resumes normal operations, close as a temporary-outage matter rather than fraud.
steps.tool: Exchange status page / regulatory alert feeds

steps.title: Review the exchange-selection due-diligence trail
steps.desc: Review how and by whom the decision was made to hold company assets on this exchange, including any due-diligence or risk-review records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury/Finance.
steps.outcome: Documented decision trail.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-preservation requirements.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Attempt emergency withdrawal and halt further deposits
steps.desc: Attempt any available emergency withdrawal of remaining assets immediately, and halt all further deposits or transactions with the exchange.
steps.guidance: Act as quickly as possible — exit scams often have a narrow window before all withdrawal functionality is disabled.
steps.outcome: Any recoverable assets withdrawn; no further exposure.
steps.abort: If withdrawals are already fully disabled, proceed to reporting.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Finance leadership of the loss event
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Finance leadership of the confirmed loss for financial-reporting and disclosure assessment.
steps.outcome: Leadership notified; impact assessed.

steps.title: Implement enhanced due-diligence and diversification controls for exchange counterparty risk
steps.desc: Implement enhanced due-diligence requirements for selecting cryptocurrency exchange counterparties (e.g. regulatory licensing verification, proof-of-reserves review, exposure diversification limits, independent risk approval).
steps.guidance: There is no technical vulnerability of company systems to patch — the fix is counterparty-risk governance.
steps.outcome: Documented due-diligence and diversification policy.

steps.title: Join creditor proceedings and report to regulators/law enforcement
steps.desc: Join any bankruptcy/creditor claims process against the exchange, and report to law enforcement and relevant financial regulators given the scale of the scam.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on the claims process and reporting obligations.
steps.outcome: Claims filed where possible; regulatory/law-enforcement reporting completed.

steps.title: Document findings and update counterparty-risk policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update the organization's exchange counterparty-risk and diversification policy.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated policy.

ITID-53742.def: Fraud in which an employee of a cryptocurrency exchange uses their legitimate internal access (to customer accounts, hot-wallet infrastructure, or trading systems) to misappropriate customer or exchange funds, front-run customer trades, or otherwise unlawfully benefit from insider access to the platform.
ITID-53742.purpose: Captures fraud committed by an exchange's own employees abusing their internal access against the exchange or its customers.
scopeIncludes: An exchange employee misappropriating customer funds using internal administrative access
Front-running customer trades using advance knowledge of pending large orders
Insider manipulation of exchange systems to benefit the employee's own trading positions
scopeExcludes: An exit scam orchestrated by the exchange's own leadership/ownership (ITID-53741)
External compromise of exchange infrastructure by a non-employee attacker (ITID-51442)
ITID-53742.severity: High. Insider access at an exchange often extends to hot-wallet or customer-fund infrastructure with limited independent oversight.
ITID-53742.priority: P1 while the employee retains active access; P2 once access is revoked and the matter is in investigation/recovery.
ITID-53742.escalation: Escalate immediately to the exchange's security/compliance team (or, where the company is the exchange operator, to internal audit and legal) to suspend access and preserve evidence.
indicators: Employee account access to customer funds or hot-wallet infrastructure outside their normal job function
Trading pattern by an employee account consistent with advance knowledge of pending customer orders
Unexplained hot-wallet balance discrepancies traceable to a specific employee's access window
vectors: Abuse of legitimate administrative access to customer accounts or hot-wallet systems
Front-running using privileged visibility into pending order flow
rootCauses: Insufficient segregation of duties and least-privilege enforcement on exchange administrative access
Lack of monitoring/alerting on employee access to customer funds or trade data outside job function
controls: Least-privilege and segregation-of-duties enforcement on exchange administrative and hot-wallet access
Monitoring/alerting on employee access to customer funds or order-flow data outside normal job function
Independent audit of hot-wallet balance reconciliation
ITID-53742.detection: Internal access-log and privileged-activity monitoring on exchange administrative systems provides a real technical signal, supplemented by trading-surveillance analytics for front-running patterns.
ITID-53742.response: Security/compliance suspends access and preserves logs; internal audit quantifies loss; legal pursues restitution/prosecution.
metrics: Number of insider-fraud investigations opened per year at exchange-operator level
Dollar amount recovered per confirmed case
detections: Privileged-access anomaly alerting on hot-wallet/customer-fund systems
ITID-53742.notes: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is applied loosely to reflect abuse of legitimate exchange-administrative access for an unauthorized purpose, consistent with how insider financial-fraud leaves elsewhere in this taxonomy are mapped.

steps.title: Review the exchange-selection due-diligence trail

steps.guidance: Coordinate with Treasury/Finance.
steps.outcome: Documented decision trail.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.

steps.outcome: Leadership notified; impact assessed.

steps.title: Implement enhanced due-diligence and counterparty-monitoring controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced ongoing due-diligence and monitoring of exchange counterparties (e.g. periodic proof-of-reserves review, regulatory-standing monitoring, exposure limits) to catch counterparty risk earlier.
steps.guidance: The fix is counterparty-risk governance, not a technical control on company systems.
steps.outcome: Documented due-diligence and monitoring policy.

steps.title: Join creditor/claims proceedings and report to regulators
steps.desc: Join any applicable claims process against the exchange, and report to relevant financial regulators/law enforcement as appropriate.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal.
steps.outcome: Claims filed where possible; reporting completed.

steps.title: Document findings and update counterparty-risk policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update the organization's exchange counterparty-risk policy based on lessons learned.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and updated policy.

ITID-53743.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cryptocurrency exchange fraud that has not been further classified into exit-scam (ITID-53741) or insider-fraud (ITID-53742) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53743.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for crypto exchange fraud that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported crypto exchange fraud pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53741 or ITID-53742
ITID-53743.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53743.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53743.escalation: Escalate to finance/legal (exit-scam angle) or security/compliance (insider angle) for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53741 or ITID-53742 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Exchange-related fraud reported but not yet root-caused as exit-scam vs. insider
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard crypto exchange fraud triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53743.response: Finance/legal/security triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-537xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Crypto Exchange Fraud Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53743.notes: Intake bucket only; should not accumulate a stable long-term population.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Crypto Exchange Fraud
playbook.description: The company suffers a loss from a cryptocurrency exchange counterparty through a fraud mechanism not otherwise captured by a more specific exchange-fraud scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the fraud event and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Confirm the specific exchange fraud mechanism and quantify the company's financial exposure.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference account statements against exchange disclosures.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure with quantified impact.
steps.abort: If not confirmed as fraud, close as a normal market/operational matter.

steps.title: Review the exchange-selection due-diligence trail
steps.desc: Review how and by whom the decision was made to use this exchange, including any due-diligence records.
steps.outcome: Documented decision trail.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the scam and communications
steps.desc: Preserve all transaction records, on-chain data, and communications related to the scam for recovery, insurance, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting purposes.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-preservation requirements.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with defensible chain of custody.

steps.title: Withdraw remaining assets and halt further exposure
steps.desc: Attempt to withdraw remaining company assets and halt further transactions with the exchange.
steps.outcome: Remaining assets secured where possible.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Finance leadership
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Finance leadership of the confirmed exposure for financial-reporting and disclosure assessment.
steps.outcome: Leadership notified; impact assessed.

steps.title: Implement enhanced due-diligence-before-investing controls
steps.desc: Implement enhanced due-diligence and counterparty-risk controls for future exchange relationships.
steps.outcome: Documented due-diligence policy.

steps.title: Pursue claims and report to regulators/law enforcement
steps.desc: Pursue any applicable claims process and report to regulators/law enforcement as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Claims filed where possible; reporting completed.

steps.title: Document findings and update counterparty-risk policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and update the counterparty-risk policy.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53811.def: An unclassified or general instance of executive-impersonation ('CEO fraud') social engineering used to pressure an employee into an urgent, unauthorized financial action — a wire transfer, gift card purchase, or similar — through a spoofed or compromised communication purporting to be from a senior executive.
ITID-53811.purpose: Captures general CEO-fraud-style social engineering outcomes (an attacker impersonating a senior executive to pressure a victim into an urgent, unauthorized financial action) as a lone-child stub, pointing to the dedicated BEC branch for the underlying mechanics.
scopeIncludes: Any instance of executive impersonation pressuring urgent financial action that does not fall cleanly under the dedicated BEC Executive Impersonation Fraud leaf's more specific email-compromise mechanics
General intake for CEO-fraud-style social engineering reports pending classification
scopeExcludes: The detailed, email-compromise-driven executive impersonation mechanics fully documented under the dedicated Business Email Compromise branch (ITID-53110 Executive Impersonation Fraud and ITID-53111)
Vendor payment diversion social engineering, a related but distinct outcome (ITID-53821)
ITID-53811.severity: High, consistent with BEC-adjacent fraud generally, scaled to the amount at risk and how far the requested action progressed before interception.
ITID-53811.priority: P1 while the requested financial action may still be reversible; P2 once contained and the incident moves to investigation.
ITID-53811.escalation: Escalate to Finance for transaction hold/reversal and to the SOC for standard BEC-style email-compromise triage if a compromised mailbox is involved; cross-reference with the BEC Tier-3 branch (ITID-531xx) team to avoid duplicate incident tracking.
indicators: Urgent, confidentiality-emphasizing request purporting to be from an executive, arriving outside normal channels
Pressure to bypass standard approval processes 'because the CEO said so'
Spoofed or lookalike sender address impersonating the executive
vectors: Spoofed or compromised email impersonating a senior executive
Phishing delivering the impersonation message
rootCauses: No secondary verification requirement for urgent executive-originated financial requests
Lack of email authentication enforcement allowing executive-address spoofing
controls: Mandatory out-of-band verification for any urgent, executive-originated financial request
Email authentication enforcement (DMARC reject/quarantine)
ITID-53811.detection: Moderate — phishing delivery is detectable via email security tooling; the social-engineering pressure itself depends on employee reporting and process controls.
ITID-53811.response: Verify the request out-of-band before any funds move, halt payment if already initiated, and run standard BEC triage on any compromised mailbox involved.
metrics: Number of CEO-fraud-style requests reported and intercepted before payment
Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
ITID-53811.notes: This is a lone-child, BEC-adjacent stub deliberately scoped to avoid restating the dedicated Executive Impersonation Fraud mechanics documented under ITID-53110/53111 in the BEC branch; use this leaf only for general social-engineering-outcome framing, and cross-reference rather than duplicate when the mechanism is a clear email compromise.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General CEO Fraud (Social Engineering Context)
playbook.description: An attacker uses social-engineering pressure tactics — impersonating or purporting to act on behalf of the CEO — to manipulate an employee into an urgent, unauthorized payment or disclosure, via phone, text, or messaging platform rather than pure email spoofing.

steps.title: Collect the communication evidence and timeline
steps.desc: Gather all communications (call logs, text messages, voicemail recordings, chat messages) related to the request from the targeted employee.
steps.guidance: Ask the employee to preserve the original messages/recordings rather than deleting them.
steps.outcome: Evidence set preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Recognize the urgency/pressure-tactic pattern
steps.desc: Analyze the request for classic social-engineering pressure indicators — urgency, secrecy, authority pressure, discouraging verification — and identify the impersonation channel (spoofed caller ID, deepfake voice, compromised messaging account).
steps.guidance: Document the specific tactics used for later staff-awareness material.
steps.outcome: Confirmed social-engineering pattern and impersonation method.
steps.abort: If the request is confirmed as a genuine, properly authorized executive instruction, close as false positive.

steps.title: Confirm the out-of-band verification failure
steps.desc: Determine whether the employee attempted independent verification (calling the executive back on a known number) before acting, and whether any funds/data movement already occurred.
steps.guidance: Interview the employee to build a clear timeline.
steps.outcome: Clear timeline established, including loss status.

steps.title: Halt the payment/transaction in progress
steps.desc: Immediately halt any payment or transaction that is still pending; if already sent, initiate an emergency bank recall.
steps.guidance: Engage Finance/Treasury leadership immediately given the narrow recall window.
steps.outcome: Payment halted or recall initiated.

steps.title: Block the impersonation channel and alert staff
steps.desc: Block the fraudulent phone number/messaging account where possible and alert staff org-wide, particularly those with payment authority, about the active campaign.
steps.outcome: Further targeting reduced; other potential targets warned.

steps.title: Implement mandatory callback verification and secondary approval for executive requests
steps.desc: Formalize a policy requiring independent callback verification (using a pre-known number) and secondary approval for any executive-initiated payment or sensitive-data request, regardless of channel.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance leadership and executive assistants.
steps.outcome: Documented policy in place.

steps.title: Pursue fund recovery and file law-enforcement report
steps.desc: If funds were lost, continue working with the bank and file a report with law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3) and the cyber-insurance carrier.
steps.outcome: Recovery case opened.

steps.title: Conduct awareness briefing on the specific tactic used
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief at-risk staff on the specific social-engineering tactic and impersonation channel used.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons and awareness update.

ITID-53821.def: An unclassified or general instance of social engineering used to divert a legitimate vendor payment to an attacker-controlled account, through impersonation or manipulation of the payment-approval process, that does not fall cleanly under a more specific, dedicated leaf.
ITID-53821.purpose: Captures general vendor-payment-diversion social engineering outcomes as a lone-child stub, pointing to the dedicated BEC branch for the underlying mechanics.
scopeIncludes: General intake for vendor-payment-diversion social engineering reports pending classification
Instances where the diversion mechanism is confirmed social-engineering-driven but does not clearly match the dedicated BEC Vendor Invoice Fraud email-compromise mechanics
scopeExcludes: The detailed, email-compromise-driven vendor invoice fraud mechanics fully documented under the dedicated Business Email Compromise branch (ITID-53120 Vendor Invoice Fraud and ITID-53121)
Wire transfer fraud via compromised vendor banking-detail-change email, documented with its own full mechanics under Payment and Banking Fraud (ITID-53211)
Fraudulent disbursement via fake vendor payment to a self-controlled account (ITID-53622)
CEO fraud impersonation targeting the employee directly rather than the vendor payment channel (ITID-53811)
ITID-53821.severity: High, consistent with BEC-adjacent fraud generally, scaled to the amount at risk and how far the diverted payment progressed before interception.
ITID-53821.priority: P1 while the diverted payment may still be reversible; P2 once contained and the incident moves to investigation.
ITID-53821.escalation: Escalate to Finance for transaction hold/reversal and to the SOC for standard BEC-style triage if a compromised mailbox is involved; cross-reference with the BEC Tier-3 branch team (ITID-531xx) and the Wire Transfer Fraud team (ITID-53211/53622) to avoid duplicate incident tracking.
indicators: Payment redirected to an account not previously on file with no verified change process followed
Social-engineering pressure to expedite a vendor payment outside normal approval channels
Report that does not cleanly match an already-documented BEC or wire-fraud leaf's specific mechanism
vectors: Impersonation of a vendor or internal approver to redirect payment
Phishing or pretexting used to manipulate the payment-approval workflow
rootCauses: No secondary verification requirement for vendor payment-channel changes
Gaps in cross-referencing this general leaf against the more specific, already-documented BEC/wire-fraud leaves, risking duplicate or fragmented incident tracking
controls: Mandatory out-of-band verification for any vendor payment-channel change
Incident-tracking cross-reference check against the dedicated BEC and wire-fraud leaves before finalizing classification under this stub
ITID-53821.detection: Moderate — phishing/pretexting delivery is detectable via email security tooling and process-control failures; classify promptly to the more specific BEC or wire-fraud leaf where the mechanism is clear, retaining this leaf for genuinely general cases.
ITID-53821.response: Verify the request out-of-band before any funds move, halt payment if already initiated, and reclassify to the specific BEC/wire-fraud leaf as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Number of vendor-payment-diversion reports reclassified to a more specific leaf
Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
sops: Vendor Payment Detail Change Verification SOP
ITID-53821.notes: This is a lone-child, BEC-adjacent stub deliberately scoped as a general social-engineering-outcome framing; it explicitly cross-references the dedicated BEC Vendor Invoice Fraud leaves (ITID-53120/53121), the Wire Transfer Fraud leaf (ITID-53211), and Fraudulent Disbursement (ITID-53622) rather than restating their mechanics, to avoid near-duplicate documentation across parallel-agent-owned branches.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Payment Diversion (Social Engineering Context)
playbook.description: An attacker uses social-engineering pressure tactics — impersonating a vendor contact via phone, text, or messaging rather than pure email spoofing — to convince an employee to redirect a legitimate vendor payment to an attacker-controlled account.

steps.title: Collect the communication evidence and timeline
steps.desc: Gather all communications (calls, texts, chat messages) related to the payment-detail change request.
steps.guidance: Ask the employee to preserve original messages/recordings.
steps.outcome: Evidence set preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Compare against known vendor contact and payment history
steps.desc: Compare the new bank/payment details against the vendor master file and known vendor contact channels to identify mismatches.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference AP vendor master records.
steps.outcome: Confirmed mismatch or discrepancy indicating fraud.
steps.abort: If details match records on file, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine payment status
steps.desc: Confirm whether the redirected payment has already been sent, is scheduled, or is still pending approval.
steps.guidance: Check AP payment run schedules and bank transaction records.
steps.outcome: Clear payment status enabling correct containment action.

steps.title: Halt the payment/transaction in progress
steps.desc: Halt any pending payment; if already sent, initiate an emergency wire/ACH recall with the bank.
steps.guidance: Engage Treasury/Finance leadership immediately.
steps.outcome: Payment halted or recall initiated.

steps.title: Verify vendor out-of-band and freeze the vendor record
steps.desc: Contact the real vendor using a previously-known phone number to confirm the fraud, and freeze the vendor master record pending re-verification.
steps.guidance: Use the vendor contact on file prior to the incident, not any contact info supplied in the fraudulent communication.
steps.outcome: Vendor confirms fraud; vendor record locked.

steps.title: Enforce mandatory callback verification for payment-detail changes
steps.desc: Formalize a policy requiring independent callback verification for any vendor payment-detail change, regardless of the channel through which the request arrives.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with AP leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented policy in place.

steps.title: Restore legitimate payment and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Process the legitimate payment to the correct account, and pursue recovery of diverted funds via the bank and law enforcement.
steps.guidance: File IC3 report and notify the cyber-insurance carrier if funds were lost.
steps.outcome: Vendor paid correctly; recovery case opened.

steps.title: Document incident and brief AP team
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief the AP team on this specific social-engineering pattern.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53831.def: Social engineering scam in which the perpetrator falsely claims the target (the company or an employee) is subject to an active lawsuit, legal judgment, or imminent legal action, demanding immediate payment — often via wire transfer or gift card — to 'settle' or avoid the fabricated legal consequence.
ITID-53831.purpose: Captures scams in which a fabricated lawsuit or legal threat is used to pressure a target into making an immediate payment to avoid supposed legal consequences.
scopeIncludes: Phone, email, or letter falsely claiming an active lawsuit or judgment requiring immediate payment
Threat of arrest or asset seizure used to pressure urgent payment
Impersonation of a law firm or process server demanding settlement funds
scopeExcludes: Scams specifically impersonating a tax authority (ITID-53832)
Scams specifically impersonating a regulatory body issuing a fine (ITID-53833)
ITID-53831.severity: Low to Medium per instance, scaled by the amount targeted and whether payment was actually made before the scam was identified.
ITID-53831.priority: P3 if identified and stopped before payment; P2 if payment has been made and recovery is being pursued.
ITID-53831.escalation: Escalate to Legal to confirm no genuine legal action exists, and to Finance to halt any pending payment; report to law enforcement if payment was made.
indicators: Urgent demand for payment to resolve a legal matter with no independently verifiable case record
Threat of immediate arrest, asset seizure, or default judgment used to create urgency
Payment demanded via an unusual method (wire, gift card, cryptocurrency) inconsistent with genuine legal settlement processes
vectors: Phishing email or phone call (vishing) impersonating a law firm or legal authority
Fabricated legal documents sent to lend false credibility to the threat
rootCauses: Lack of employee awareness of legitimate legal-notice processes
No verification requirement before acting on an unsolicited legal-payment demand
controls: Employee awareness training on fake legal-threat scam patterns
Mandatory Legal-department verification before any payment is made in response to a legal threat
ITID-53831.detection: Largely non-technical — this is a social-engineering scam pattern; detection depends on employee awareness and Legal-department verification rather than SOC telemetry, unless the scam is delivered through an identifiable technical phishing vector.
ITID-53831.response: Verify with Legal that no genuine action exists, halt any pending payment, and report the scam attempt for awareness tracking.
metrics: Number of fake legal-threat scams reported and intercepted before payment
Dollar amount attempted vs. lost
ITID-53831.notes: Predominantly non-technical social-engineering scam pattern with mapped_mitre left empty; if a specific instance is delivered via a technical phishing vector (e.g., a credential-harvesting link embedded in the fake legal notice), that instance may separately warrant a T1598 Phishing for Information framing, applied consistently with the sibling leaves in this group.

playbook.name: Fake Lawsuit/Legal Threat Demanding Immediate Payment
playbook.description: An attacker poses as an attorney, court official, or debt collector and threatens legal action (lawsuit, garnishment, arrest) unless an urgent payment is made, pressuring the target into paying a fraudulent claim.

steps.title: Collect the notice/communication and pressure-tactic details
steps.desc: Gather the notice (letter, email, call recording, or text) and document the specific threats and urgency tactics used.
steps.guidance: Preserve the original communication and any contact information provided within it.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled.

steps.title: Independently verify with the purported court/law firm
steps.desc: Verify the claim directly with the purported court or law firm using independently-sourced contact information (official court website/bar association listing) — never the phone number or link provided in the notice itself.
steps.guidance: Legal should assist in this verification given the subject matter.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the notice is fraudulent (no such case/claim exists) or, rarely, confirmed as genuine.
steps.abort: If the independent verification confirms a genuine legal matter, route to Legal for normal case handling rather than fraud response.

steps.title: Check for other employees targeted by the same campaign
steps.desc: Search for other employees who may have received the same or a similar fraudulent notice, to determine the scope of the campaign.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the email/security team to search for similar messages org-wide.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified and other targets warned.

steps.title: Halt any payment in progress
steps.desc: Halt any payment that may be in progress in response to the threat.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance if a payment was initiated.
steps.outcome: No payment made to the fraudulent claimant.

steps.title: Block the sender/caller and alert relevant staff
steps.desc: Block the fraudulent sender/caller and alert staff who may be targeted by the same campaign (e.g. AP, executive assistants).
steps.outcome: Further targeting reduced; sender blocked.

steps.title: Establish independent-verification requirement for legal-threat payment demands
steps.desc: Formalize a policy requiring any payment demand tied to a legal threat to be routed to Legal for independent verification before any payment is considered.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal and Finance leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented policy in place.

steps.title: File a fraud report if any payment was made
steps.desc: If a payment was made before detection, file a report with the bank and law enforcement to pursue recovery.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued if applicable.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, skip recovery.

steps.title: Document incident and brief staff on the tactic
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief staff on recognizing fake legal-threat scams and the requirement to verify independently.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53832.def: Social engineering scam in which the perpetrator impersonates a tax authority (e.g., a national revenue service) and falsely claims the target owes back taxes or penalties, demanding immediate payment — often via wire transfer, gift card, or prepaid debit card — to avoid threatened enforcement action such as asset seizure or arrest.
ITID-53832.purpose: Captures scams in which a fabricated tax authority collection notice is used to pressure a target into making an immediate payment to avoid supposed tax enforcement action.
scopeIncludes: Phone call (vishing) impersonating a tax authority demanding immediate payment
Email or letter falsely claiming an outstanding tax debt with threatened enforcement action
Fabricated tax authority notice/document used to lend false credibility
scopeExcludes: Scams claiming a general lawsuit or legal judgment rather than a tax debt (ITID-53831)
Scams impersonating a regulatory body issuing a fine unrelated to tax (ITID-53833)
Genuine internal tax fraud committed by the company itself (Tax and Regulatory Fraud Tier-3 branch, ITID-534xx) — this leaf is the company being targeted by an external scam, not committing fraud
ITID-53832.severity: Low to Medium per instance, scaled by the amount targeted and whether payment was actually made before the scam was identified.
ITID-53832.priority: P3 if identified and stopped before payment; P2 if payment has been made and recovery is being pursued.
ITID-53832.escalation: Escalate to Legal/Tax to confirm no genuine tax action exists, and to Finance to halt any pending payment; report to the relevant fraud-reporting channel of the actual tax authority.
indicators: Urgent demand for tax payment via an unusual method (wire, gift card, cryptocurrency) inconsistent with genuine tax authority payment processes
Threat of immediate arrest or asset seizure for unpaid taxes
Caller ID or sender address spoofing the tax authority's real contact information
vectors: Vishing call impersonating a tax authority representative
Phishing email or fabricated notice impersonating a tax authority
rootCauses: Lack of employee awareness of legitimate tax authority contact and payment processes
No verification requirement before acting on an unsolicited tax-payment demand
controls: Employee awareness training on tax authority impersonation scam patterns
Mandatory Tax/Legal-department verification before any payment is made in response to a tax notice
ITID-53832.detection: Largely non-technical — this is a social-engineering scam pattern; detection depends on employee awareness and internal verification rather than SOC telemetry, unless delivered through an identifiable technical phishing vector.
ITID-53832.response: Verify with Tax/Legal that no genuine debt exists, halt any pending payment, and report the scam attempt for awareness tracking.
metrics: Number of fake tax-authority scams reported and intercepted before payment
Dollar amount attempted vs. lost
ITID-53832.notes: Predominantly non-technical social-engineering scam pattern with mapped_mitre left empty, consistent with sibling leaves in this group; if delivered via a technical phishing vector, T1598 Phishing for Information may apply to that specific instance.

playbook.name: Fake IRS/Tax Authority Collection Notice
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates the IRS or another tax authority, threatening penalties, liens, or arrest, to pressure the company or an employee into an urgent fraudulent payment.

steps.desc: Gather the notice (letter, email, call, or text) and document the specific threats and payment method demanded (e.g. gift cards, wire, cryptocurrency — atypical for real tax authorities).
steps.guidance: Preserve the original communication.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled.

steps.desc: Verify the claim directly with the tax authority using independently-sourced contact information (the authority's official published phone number/website), never the number or link provided in the notice.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Tax department for the verification.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the notice is fraudulent or, rarely, confirmed as a genuine tax matter.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, route to the Tax/Finance department for normal handling rather than fraud response.

steps.title: Check for other employees targeted by the same campaign
steps.desc: Search for other employees who may have received the same or a similar fraudulent notice, to determine the scope of the campaign.

steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified and other targets warned.

steps.title: Halt any payment in progress

steps.title: Block the sender/caller and alert relevant staff
steps.desc: Block the fraudulent sender/caller and alert Finance/Tax staff who may be targeted by the same campaign.
steps.outcome: Further targeting reduced.

steps.title: Establish independent-verification requirement for tax-authority payment demands
steps.desc: Formalize a policy requiring any tax-authority payment demand to be routed to the Tax/Finance department for independent verification before payment.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Tax leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented policy in place.

steps.title: File a fraud report if any payment was made
steps.desc: If a payment was made before detection, file a report with the bank and law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3, and the real IRS's phishing-report channel) to pursue recovery.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued if applicable.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, skip recovery.

steps.title: Document incident and brief staff on the tactic
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief Finance/Tax staff on recognizing fake tax-authority scams and the requirement to verify independently.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53833.def: Social engineering scam in which the perpetrator impersonates a regulatory body (e.g., a licensing board, data-protection authority, or industry regulator) and falsely claims the company owes a fine or penalty for a compliance violation, demanding immediate payment to avoid threatened enforcement action such as license revocation or public sanction.

Sender/caller impersonating a regulator's real contact information

Fabricated regulatory notice sent to lend false credibility
rootCauses: Lack of employee awareness of legitimate regulatory notice and payment processes
No verification requirement before acting on an unsolicited regulatory-fine demand

playbook.name: Fake Regulatory Fine/Penalty Notice
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates a regulatory body (e.g. a financial, safety, or data-protection regulator), threatening a fine or penalty, to pressure the company into an urgent fraudulent payment.

steps.outcome: Confirmed the notice is fraudulent or, rarely, confirmed as a genuine regulatory matter.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, route to Legal/Compliance for normal regulatory handling rather than fraud response.

steps.title: Check for other employees targeted by the same campaign
steps.desc: Search for other employees who may have received the same or a similar fraudulent notice, to determine the scope of the campaign.

steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified and other targets warned.

steps.title: Halt any payment in progress
steps.desc: Halt any payment that may be in progress in response to the fraudulent notice.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Legal.
steps.outcome: No payment made to the fraudulent claimant.

steps.title: Block the sender/caller and alert relevant staff
steps.desc: Block the fraudulent sender/caller and alert Legal/Compliance/Finance staff who may be targeted by the same campaign.
steps.outcome: Further targeting reduced.

steps.title: Establish independent-verification requirement for regulatory payment demands
steps.desc: Formalize a policy requiring any regulatory-fine payment demand to be routed to Legal/Compliance for independent verification before payment.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented policy in place.

steps.title: File a fraud report if any payment was made
steps.desc: If a payment was made before detection, file a report with the bank and law enforcement to pursue recovery.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued if applicable.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, skip recovery.

steps.title: Document incident and brief staff on the tactic
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief Legal/Compliance/Finance staff on recognizing fake regulatory-notice scams and the requirement to verify independently.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53834.def: An unclassified or general instance of a fake legal or government notice scam that has not yet been attributed to a specific impersonated authority type covered by another Fake Legal or Government Notices leaf.
ITID-53834.purpose: Intake bucket for fake legal or government notice scams that do not yet fit the fake-lawsuit, fake-tax-notice, or fake-regulatory-fine patterns.
scopeIncludes: Fake legal/government notice scam reported without enough detail to determine which authority type is being impersonated
Impersonation of a government/legal authority type not otherwise covered (e.g., a licensing agency, immigration authority)
scopeExcludes: Confirmed fake lawsuit/legal threat (ITID-53831)
Confirmed fake tax authority notice (ITID-53832)
Confirmed fake regulatory fine/penalty notice (ITID-53833)
ITID-53834.severity: Low to Medium, consistent with other leaves in this group, pending reclassification.
ITID-53834.priority: P3 if identified and stopped before payment; P2 if payment has been made.
ITID-53834.escalation: Escalate to Legal to confirm no genuine action exists, and to Finance to halt any pending payment, regardless of final classification.
indicators: Urgent payment demand impersonating an unspecified legal or government authority
vectors: Phishing email or phone call impersonating an unspecified legal/government authority
rootCauses: Lack of employee awareness of legitimate legal/government notice processes
controls: Employee awareness training on fake legal/government notice scam patterns
Mandatory Legal-department verification before any payment is made
ITID-53834.detection: Largely non-technical — this is a social-engineering scam pattern; detection depends on employee awareness and internal verification.
ITID-53834.response: Verify with Legal that no genuine action exists, halt any pending payment, and investigate to reclassify under a specific Fake Legal or Government Notices leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53834.notes: Predominantly non-technical social-engineering scam pattern with mapped_mitre left empty, consistent with sibling leaves; intake/catch-all classification pending reclassification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Fake Legal or Government Notice
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates a legal or government authority not otherwise captured by a more specific scenario, using an official-looking notice to pressure the target into an urgent fraudulent payment or disclosure.

steps.title: Collect the notice/communication and pressure-tactic details
steps.desc: Gather the notice and document the specific authority claimed, threat made, and payment/disclosure method demanded.
steps.guidance: Preserve the original communication.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled.

steps.title: Independently verify with the purported authority
steps.desc: Verify the claim directly with the purported authority using independently-sourced contact information, never the number or link provided in the notice itself.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal for the verification.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the notice is fraudulent or, rarely, confirmed as genuine.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, route to Legal for normal handling rather than fraud response.

steps.title: Check for other employees targeted by the same campaign
steps.desc: Search for other employees who may have received the same or a similar fraudulent notice, to determine the scope of the campaign.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the email/security team to search for similar messages org-wide.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified and other targets warned.

steps.title: Halt any payment/disclosure in progress
steps.desc: Halt any payment or data disclosure that may be in progress in response to the fraudulent notice.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Finance/Legal as applicable.
steps.outcome: No payment/disclosure made to the fraudulent claimant.

steps.title: Block the sender/caller and alert relevant staff
steps.desc: Block the fraudulent sender/caller and alert staff who may be targeted by the same campaign.
steps.outcome: Further targeting reduced.

steps.title: Establish independent-verification requirement for authority payment/disclosure demands
steps.desc: Formalize a policy requiring any purported legal/government payment or disclosure demand to be routed to Legal for independent verification before action.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal leadership.
steps.outcome: Documented policy in place.

steps.title: File a fraud report if any payment/disclosure was made
steps.desc: If a payment was made or data was disclosed before detection, file a report with the bank and law enforcement to pursue recovery/remediation.
steps.outcome: Recovery/remediation pursued if applicable.
steps.abort: If no payment/disclosure occurred, skip recovery.

steps.title: Document incident and brief staff on the tactic
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief staff on recognizing fake legal/government-notice scams and the requirement to verify independently.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53841.def: Social engineering scam in which an adversary impersonates an employee (or the pension plan administrator) to submit a fraudulent request for a pension plan distribution, loan, or withdrawal, directing the payout to an attacker-controlled bank account rather than the legitimate participant's account.
ITID-53841.purpose: Captures scams targeting an employee's pension plan by fraudulently requesting a distribution to be redirected to an attacker-controlled account.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent pension distribution/withdrawal request submitted using stolen participant credentials or identity information
Impersonation of the pension plan administrator to redirect a legitimate distribution
Account-takeover of a pension plan participant portal used to change payout banking details
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent redirection of ongoing benefits-enrollment payments rather than a one-time pension distribution (ITID-53842)
ITID-53841.severity: High, given pension distributions are often large, one-time amounts representing significant retirement savings for the affected employee.
ITID-53841.priority: P1 while the distribution may still be held or reversed by the plan administrator; P2 once contained and the incident moves to investigation and employee support.
ITID-53841.escalation: Escalate immediately to HR/Benefits and the pension plan administrator to freeze the distribution, and to the SOC if the fraud involved compromise of the participant's portal credentials.
indicators: Distribution request submitted with a newly added or changed payout bank account
Login to the pension portal from an unrecognized device/location immediately preceding the request
Employee report of receiving a phishing communication referencing their pension plan shortly before the fraud
vectors: Phishing targeting pension plan participant portal credentials
Impersonation of the plan administrator via phone or email to obtain distribution approval
Identity-theft-based submission of a fraudulent distribution request using the participant's personal information
rootCauses: Lack of phishing-resistant MFA on the pension plan participant portal
Insufficient out-of-band verification before processing a payout-detail change or new distribution request
Employee unaware of how to recognize legitimate plan-administrator communications
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA on the pension plan participant portal
Mandatory out-of-band verification for any distribution request involving a new or changed payout account
Employee awareness training on pension-fraud scam patterns
ITID-53841.detection: Moderate — where the fraud is delivered via a technical phishing vector targeting the plan portal, delivery is detectable through email security tooling; portal-side account-activity monitoring depends on the plan administrator's own fraud controls.
ITID-53841.response: Freeze the distribution with the plan administrator immediately, verify the legitimate participant's intent, and support the affected employee through recovery.
metrics: Number of fraudulent pension distribution requests intercepted before payout
Dollar amount attempted vs. recovered
detections: Pension portal anomalous-login alerting (where visibility exists)
ITID-53841.notes: Framed with a T1598 Phishing for Information mapping given this leaf is typically delivered via a technical phishing vector against the plan participant portal, applied consistently with the benefits-enrollment sibling leaf in this group.

playbook.name: Fraudulent Pension Plan Distribution Request
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates an employee or retiree via social engineering to request an unauthorized distribution or withdrawal from their pension plan account, diverting the funds to an attacker-controlled account.

steps.title: Collect the distribution request and system audit trail
steps.desc: Obtain the distribution request (portal submission, email, or phone request) along with the pension administration system's audit log.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the pension plan administrator/HR Benefits team.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled.

steps.title: Verify requester authenticity and account-change pattern
steps.desc: Check whether the request came from the genuine, authenticated participant account, and whether the new bank details are associated with other recent fraudulent changes.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the new account details against other recent pension distribution requests for reuse.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent request and any linked cases identified.
steps.abort: If the participant confirms they made the request themselves, close as false positive.

steps.title: Contact the participant out-of-band to confirm
steps.desc: Reach the actual employee/retiree via a known phone number to confirm whether they submitted the request.
steps.guidance: Do not rely on the contact information provided with the request.
steps.outcome: Definitive confirmation the participant did not authorize the request.

steps.title: Halt the distribution and notify the plan administrator/custodian
steps.desc: Immediately halt the pending distribution or, if already disbursed, notify the plan administrator/custodian and bank to attempt a recall.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with the pension plan administrator and Treasury.
steps.outcome: Distribution halted or recall initiated.
steps.tool: Pension administration system / bank recall request

steps.title: Flag the destination account and review other participants for the same pattern
steps.desc: Flag the fraudulent destination account and check whether other participants' distributions were redirected to the same or similar accounts.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified.

steps.title: Enforce out-of-band verification for distribution requests
steps.desc: Update plan-administration procedures to require independent, out-of-band verification for any pension distribution request or bank-detail change.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR Benefits and the plan administrator.
steps.outcome: Documented policy/control in place.

steps.title: Restore the participant's account and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Ensure the participant's pension account is restored appropriately, and pursue recovery of diverted funds through the bank/plan administrator and, if warranted, law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Participant made whole; recovery case opened.

steps.title: Document incident and reinforce Benefits team awareness
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief HR Benefits/plan administrator staff on the fraud pattern and reinforced verification steps.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53842.def: Social engineering scam in which an adversary submits a fraudulent benefits-enrollment or direct-deposit change (e.g., HSA/FSA reimbursement account, benefits-related payment routing) through the employee self-service or benefits-administration portal, redirecting ongoing payments to an attacker-controlled bank account.
ITID-53842.purpose: Captures scams targeting an employee's benefits enrollment to fraudulently redirect ongoing benefit payments (e.g., HSA/FSA reimbursements, benefits-related direct deposits) to an attacker-controlled account.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent change to HSA/FSA reimbursement bank details via the benefits portal
Account-takeover of an employee self-service benefits portal used to redirect recurring benefit payments
Phishing targeting benefits-portal credentials specifically to enable a payment-routing change
scopeExcludes: A one-time fraudulent pension distribution/withdrawal request (ITID-53841)

General payroll direct-deposit redirection covered under the BEC Payroll Diversion Fraud branch (ITID-53130) if the mechanism is a mailbox-compromise-driven payroll change rather than a benefits-portal-specific change
ITID-53842.severity: Medium to High, scaled by the recurring payment amount and how long the redirection persists before detection.
ITID-53842.priority: P2 upon discovery; P1 if the redirection has been active for multiple pay/reimbursement cycles with significant cumulative loss.
ITID-53842.escalation: Escalate to HR/Benefits and the benefits-administration provider to freeze and reverse the change, and to the SOC if the fraud involved compromise of the employee's benefits-portal or corporate credentials.
indicators: Benefits-portal payment-routing change made from an unrecognized device/location
Employee report that expected reimbursements/benefit payments have stopped or gone to an unfamiliar account
Login to the benefits portal immediately preceding a payment-detail change, inconsistent with the employee's normal access pattern
vectors: Phishing targeting employee self-service benefits-portal credentials
Credential stuffing against the benefits-portal login using reused passwords
rootCauses: Lack of phishing-resistant MFA on the benefits self-service portal
Insufficient out-of-band verification before processing a payment-routing change
No alerting on login-then-payment-detail-change sequences within the benefits portal
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA on the benefits self-service portal
Mandatory out-of-band verification for any benefits payment-routing change
Anomaly alerting on login-then-payment-detail-change sequences
ITID-53842.detection: Moderate — phishing delivery targeting the portal is detectable through email security tooling; portal-side change monitoring depends on the benefits-administration platform's logging and alerting capability.
ITID-53842.response: Reverse the fraudulent payment-routing change immediately, restore payments to the legitimate employee, and reset the compromised credential.
metrics: Number of fraudulent benefits-routing changes detected and reversed
Cumulative dollar amount misdirected before detection
detections: Benefits portal anomalous-login alerting (where visibility exists)
ITID-53842.notes: Framed with a T1598 Phishing for Information mapping consistent with the pension-distribution sibling leaf, since this leaf's typical delivery mechanism is a technical phishing vector against the benefits self-service portal.

playbook.name: Fake Benefits Enrollment Change Redirecting Payments
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates an employee to fraudulently change benefits enrollment details (e.g. HSA/FSA direct-deposit or reimbursement banking details) via the self-service portal or a social-engineered request, redirecting benefit payments to an attacker-controlled account.

steps.title: Collect the enrollment-change request and system audit trail
steps.desc: Obtain the enrollment/banking-change request and the benefits administration system's audit log.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR Benefits.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled.

steps.title: Verify requester authenticity
steps.desc: Check whether the request came from the genuine, authenticated employee account, and compare against the employee's known banking details.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference HR/payroll records for the employee's known bank details.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent request.
steps.abort: If the employee confirms they made the change, close as false positive.

steps.title: Contact the employee out-of-band to confirm
steps.desc: Reach the actual employee via a known phone number to confirm whether they submitted the change.
steps.outcome: Definitive confirmation the employee did not authorize the change.

steps.title: Revert the banking/enrollment details and halt pending payments
steps.desc: Revert the banking/enrollment details to the last known-good state, and halt or recall any pending benefit payment scheduled to the fraudulent account.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR Benefits and the benefits administrator/payroll processor.
steps.outcome: Details reverted; payment halted or recall initiated.

steps.title: Flag the destination account and review other employees for the same pattern
steps.desc: Flag the fraudulent destination account and check whether other employees' benefits payments were redirected similarly.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified.

steps.title: Enforce out-of-band verification for benefits banking changes
steps.desc: Update HR Benefits procedures to require a secondary verification step before any banking-detail change on a benefits account takes effect.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Benefits administrator.
steps.outcome: Documented policy/control in place.

steps.title: Restore employee's correct payment and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Ensure the employee receives the benefit payment correctly, and pursue recovery of diverted funds.
steps.outcome: Employee made whole; recovery case opened.

steps.title: Document incident and reinforce HR Benefits awareness
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief HR Benefits staff on the fraud pattern and reinforced verification steps.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53843.def: An unclassified or general instance of pension or benefits fraud that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism covered by another Pension and Benefits Fraud leaf.
ITID-53843.purpose: Intake bucket for pension and benefits fraud that does not yet fit the fraudulent pension-distribution or benefits-enrollment-redirection patterns.
scopeIncludes: Pension/benefits fraud reported without enough detail to determine distribution-request or enrollment-redirection origin
Novel or mixed-mechanism pension/benefits fraud
scopeExcludes: Confirmed fraudulent pension plan distribution request (ITID-53841)
Confirmed fake benefits enrollment change redirecting payments (ITID-53842)
ITID-53843.severity: Medium to High, pending reclassification once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-53843.priority: P2, reassessed once the mechanism is confirmed and the incident is reclassified.
ITID-53843.escalation: Escalate to HR/Benefits and the relevant plan administrator immediately regardless of final classification.
indicators: Pension/benefits payment irregularity reported without a clearly identified mechanism
vectors: Unknown or unconfirmed at time of initial report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine root cause
controls: Standard out-of-band verification and portal-security controls applicable to all pension/benefits fraud
ITID-53843.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat as unknown until triage narrows it to a specific leaf.
ITID-53843.response: Freeze the affected payment/distribution pending investigation and reclassify under a specific Pension and Benefits Fraud leaf.
metrics: Count of incidents initially logged here and subsequently reclassified
ITID-53843.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify to a specific Pension and Benefits Fraud leaf as soon as sufficient detail is available.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Pension and Benefits Fraud
