playbook.description: An attacker uses social engineering to commit fraud against a company pension or benefits program through a mechanism not otherwise captured by a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Collect the suspect request and system audit trail
steps.desc: Obtain the suspect request and the relevant benefits/pension administration system's audit log.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR Benefits.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled.

steps.title: Verify requester authenticity and determine fraud mechanism
steps.desc: Verify whether the request came from the genuine account holder and determine the specific fraud mechanism used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraudulent request and mechanism.
steps.abort: If the account holder confirms the request, close as false positive.

steps.title: Contact the account holder out-of-band to confirm
steps.desc: Reach the actual employee/retiree via a known phone number to confirm whether they submitted the request.
steps.outcome: Definitive confirmation of unauthorized activity.

steps.title: Halt the fraudulent transaction and notify the administrator
steps.desc: Halt the pending transaction or, if completed, notify the plan/benefits administrator to attempt recall.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR Benefits and Treasury.
steps.outcome: Transaction halted or recall initiated.

steps.title: Review other accounts for the same pattern
steps.desc: Check whether other employees/retirees were targeted by the same pattern.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign identified.

steps.title: Enforce out-of-band verification for account changes
steps.desc: Update procedures to require independent verification for any sensitive change to pension/benefits accounts.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR Benefits/plan administrator.
steps.outcome: Documented policy/control in place.

steps.title: Restore the account and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Restore the affected account appropriately and pursue recovery of any diverted funds.
steps.outcome: Account restored; recovery case opened.

steps.title: Document incident and reinforce awareness
steps.desc: Document the incident and brief relevant staff on the fraud pattern and reinforced verification steps.
steps.outcome: Incident closed with documented lessons.

ITID-53911.def: Financial-crime activity in which an individual or organization establishes multiple interconnected shell companies, often across jurisdictions, and moves funds between them in a series of transactions with no genuine business purpose, solely to break the audit trail between the funds' illicit source and their eventual legitimate-looking destination.
ITID-53911.purpose: Captures money laundering conducted through a deliberately layered network of shell companies designed to obscure the origin and ownership of funds.
scopeIncludes: Funds passed through a chain of shell companies with no genuine commercial activity
Use of nominee directors/owners to obscure the beneficial ownership of the shell network
Cross-jurisdictional shell structures exploiting differing corporate-transparency requirements
scopeExcludes: A single shell company created specifically to receive BEC fraud proceeds (ITID-53912)
Trade-based laundering using invoice manipulation rather than a shell-company network (ITID-53931)
ITID-53911.severity: High. Shell company networks are frequently a component of larger, organized financial-crime schemes with significant aggregate value.
ITID-53911.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the company is found to be an unwitting counterparty (e.g., a customer or vendor) to an active shell network.
ITID-53911.escalation: Escalate to AML/BSA compliance for SAR filing and to legal for counterparty risk assessment; coordinate with law enforcement where the company's own accounts were used as a layering point.
indicators: Business counterparty with no verifiable operations, employees, or physical presence consistent with its transaction volume
Beneficial ownership obscured through nominee directors or complex cross-jurisdictional structures
Transaction patterns with no apparent commercial rationale between related entities
vectors: Registration of shell companies using nominee directors/owners
Cross-jurisdictional layering exploiting weak corporate-transparency regimes
rootCauses: Insufficient beneficial-ownership verification during customer/vendor onboarding (KYC/KYB)
Lack of ongoing transaction-pattern monitoring for counterparties with shell-company characteristics
controls: Beneficial-ownership verification (KYB) at onboarding and periodic re-verification
Transaction-pattern monitoring for shell-company indicators
AML/BSA SAR filing workflow for identified layering activity
ITID-53911.detection: Detected through AML transaction-monitoring systems and KYB due-diligence review rather than SOC technical telemetry.
ITID-53911.response: AML/BSA compliance files required SARs and coordinates with law enforcement; legal manages counterparty relationship risk; SOC has no role absent a technical intrusion component.
metrics: Number of shell-company networks identified per year
Number of SARs filed related to shell-company activity
detections: AML transaction-pattern monitoring for shell-company indicators
ITID-53911.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination.

playbook.name: Layered Shell Company Network for Fund Obfuscation
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects transaction-monitoring alerts indicating funds moving through the company or a customer relationship are being layered through a network of shell companies to obscure the true source or ownership of funds.

steps.title: Triage the transaction-monitoring alert for shell-company red flags
steps.desc: Assess the transaction-monitoring system alert indicating fund movement consistent with shell-company layering — entities with no discernible business purpose, no employees/physical presence, or beneficial-ownership opacity.
steps.guidance: Review the entity's incorporation records, beneficial-ownership disclosures, transaction purpose narratives, and compare against known shell-company red-flag typologies (e.g., nominee directors, registered-agent-only addresses).
steps.outcome: Credible shell-company layering pattern documented with the entity network and transaction flow identified.
steps.abort: If the entity has a documented legitimate business purpose and transparent beneficial ownership, close as false positive.

steps.title: Map the full shell-company network and fund flow
steps.desc: Trace the full network of related shell entities and the flow of funds through them to identify the ultimate source and destination of the layered funds.
steps.guidance: Use link analysis across account-opening data, wire beneficiary/originator information, and public corporate registries to map entity relationships.
steps.outcome: Full entity network and fund-flow diagram documented.
steps.tool: Link analysis / AML case management system

steps.title: Place a transaction hold and restrict the implicated accounts
steps.desc: Immediately place a hold on pending transactions and restrict further activity on all accounts identified in the shell-company network pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Account Operations to apply the hold across all implicated accounts simultaneously to prevent further fund movement or evidence destruction.
steps.outcome: Pending transactions held and further account activity restricted across the network.

steps.title: Issue an internal investigation hold and escalate to the BSA Officer
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and issue an internal hold on records related to the implicated accounts and relationships.
steps.guidance: Ensure the escalation follows the institution's AML case-escalation procedure and that record preservation begins immediately.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence and quantify the laundered fund flow
steps.desc: Complete enhanced due diligence (EDD) on the implicated entities and quantify the total value of funds laundered through the network.
steps.guidance: Document the full EDD findings, including beneficial-ownership verification results and the quantified fund flow, for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with a quantified, documented fund-flow analysis.

steps.title: File a Suspicious Activity Report with FinCEN
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the shell-company layering scheme, consistent with the institution's statutory AML reporting obligations.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline and ensure the narrative includes the entity network, fund flow, and red flags identified.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after EDD, the activity is determined not to meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Exit or restrict the customer relationship and remediate onboarding EDD controls
steps.desc: Determine whether to exit the customer relationship(s) per the institution's risk-appetite policy, and strengthen beneficial-ownership/EDD controls at onboarding to detect shell-company networks earlier.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on the account-closure decision and update the customer risk-rating and onboarding EDD checklist.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition decided and onboarding EDD controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal account operations under enhanced ongoing monitoring
steps.desc: For any accounts retained, resume normal operations under enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic EDD refresh.
steps.guidance: Apply a heightened monitoring profile to the retained relationship(s) for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced ongoing monitoring active where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update shell-company typology detection rules
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update transaction-monitoring scenario rules/typologies to better detect similar shell-company layering patterns.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership and the Audit Committee as appropriate; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection rules updated.

ITID-53912.def: Financial-crime activity in which proceeds from a successful BEC wire-fraud attack are deposited into an account held by a shell company (often set up specifically for this purpose, or a 'money mule' business front) before being further layered, converted, or withdrawn, breaking the direct trail between the victim's fraudulent wire and the ultimate beneficiary.
ITID-53912.purpose: Captures the specific laundering step of routing Business Email Compromise fraud proceeds through a shell company to obscure their criminal origin.
scopeIncludes: A shell company or mule business account used as the first receiving point for BEC fraud proceeds
Rapid onward movement or withdrawal of funds from the shell account shortly after receipt
Shell company incorporated with a name/purpose designed to appear as a plausible legitimate recipient of the fraudulent wire
scopeExcludes: The underlying BEC attack that generated the fraudulent wire, classified under ITID-53111/53121 and ITID-22411-22415
A broader, non-BEC-specific layered shell company network (ITID-53911)
ITID-53912.severity: High. This is typically the critical, time-sensitive window in which a wire-recall or fund-freeze at the receiving shell account is still possible.
ITID-53912.priority: P1 immediately upon identifying the receiving shell account, given the narrow window for a successful recall/freeze before onward movement.
ITID-53912.escalation: Escalate immediately to the receiving bank (via the FBI IC3 Financial Fraud Kill Chain or equivalent) to request an emergency fund freeze/recall at the shell account.
indicators: Receiving account held by a business entity with no plausible connection to the wire's intended purpose
Shell company incorporated shortly before receiving the fraudulent wire
Rapid, near-complete withdrawal of the wire amount shortly after receipt
vectors: Pre-established shell company bank accounts used specifically as BEC fraud drop accounts
Recruitment of money mules to open accounts under a business front
rootCauses: The upstream BEC attack itself (see ITID-53111/53121) going undetected until after the wire settles
Insufficient receiving-bank scrutiny of newly opened business accounts receiving large, unexplained wire volume
controls: Rapid wire-recall/kill-chain reporting process (e.g., FBI IC3 Financial Fraud Kill Chain) for the finance team
Receiving-bank due-diligence on new business accounts with high early-transaction volume
ITID-53912.detection: No SOC technical telemetry; detection depends on rapid finance-team recognition of the fraudulent wire combined with receiving-bank fraud monitoring.
ITID-53912.response: Finance/treasury and legal immediately pursue the wire-recall/kill-chain process; SOC investigates the upstream BEC email-compromise vector in parallel.
metrics: Percentage of BEC wire fraud recovered via successful recall at the shell account
Median time from wire initiation to recall request
sops: Financial Fraud Kill Chain Reporting SOP
ITID-53912.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination. Cross-reference the originating BEC leaves at ITID-53111 (executive impersonation) and ITID-53121 (vendor invoice fraud), and the underlying technical email-compromise treatment at ITID-22411-22415.

playbook.name: Shell Company Used to Receive Fraudulent Proceeds from BEC
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects that an account held by a shell company received and rapidly moved proceeds traced to a business email compromise (BEC) wire fraud scheme, requiring urgent transaction hold and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Confirm the BEC-proceeds inflow and shell-company characteristics of the receiving account
steps.desc: Validate that the receiving account belongs to a shell entity with limited business activity and confirm the inbound wire is traceable to a reported BEC fraud victim.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the inbound wire against any fraud-recovery/kill-chain notifications received from other institutions or law enforcement, and review the receiving entity's account-opening profile for shell-company red flags.
steps.outcome: Confirmed BEC-proceeds inflow into a shell-company account with the transaction detail documented.
steps.abort: If the receiving entity has legitimate, verifiable business activity explaining the inbound funds, close as false positive.

steps.title: Trace further movement/layering of the fraudulent proceeds
steps.desc: Determine whether the fraudulent proceeds have already been moved out of the receiving account (e.g., to other shell entities, converted to cryptocurrency, or withdrawn as cash) to assess remaining recoverable funds.
steps.guidance: Review the account's transaction history immediately following the fraudulent inflow for outbound transfers.
steps.outcome: Remaining recoverable funds quantified and further layering/movement documented.

steps.title: Immediately freeze the account and any remaining funds
steps.desc: Place an immediate hold on the receiving account to freeze any remaining traceable proceeds before further dissipation, coordinating with the victim's bank if a Financial Fraud Kill Chain request has been received.
steps.guidance: Time is critical — act as soon as the BEC-proceeds link is confirmed to maximize the funds that can be frozen/returned.
steps.outcome: Account frozen with remaining funds secured pending investigation.
steps.abort: If funds have already been fully withdrawn, document the loss and proceed to law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and coordinate with the originating institution/law enforcement
steps.desc: Escalate to the BSA Officer and coordinate with the originating bank and/or FBI IC3/Financial Fraud Kill Chain process to support fund recovery for the BEC victim.
steps.guidance: Respond promptly to any kill-chain hold request and provide the requested account/transaction detail through proper legal channels.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and coordination with originating institution/law enforcement underway.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence on the shell entity and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Complete EDD on the shell entity to determine its true beneficial ownership and purpose, and quantify the full scope of funds that passed through the account.
steps.guidance: Document the EDD findings for the SAR narrative and any law-enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with quantified exposure documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN and return recoverable funds through proper channels
steps.desc: File a SAR with FinCEN documenting the shell-company BEC-proceeds scheme, and return any frozen recoverable funds to the victim/originating institution through the proper legal/banking channel.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline; coordinate fund return through Legal to ensure proper chain of authority.
steps.outcome: SAR filed and recoverable funds returned through proper channels.

steps.title: Close the shell-company account and strengthen onboarding EDD controls
steps.desc: Close the implicated shell-company account per the institution's risk-appetite policy and strengthen beneficial-ownership/EDD controls at onboarding.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on the account-closure decision and update onboarding EDD requirements.
steps.outcome: Account closed and onboarding EDD controls strengthened.

steps.title: Confirm fund-return completion and resume normal AML operations
steps.desc: Confirm the fund-return process to the BEC victim is complete and resume normal AML monitoring operations.
steps.guidance: Reconcile the case outcome with the originating institution/law enforcement to confirm closure.
steps.outcome: Fund-return process confirmed complete and normal operations resumed.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update BEC-proceeds detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update transaction-monitoring scenarios to better detect rapid-movement BEC-proceeds patterns into shell accounts.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53913.def: An unclassified/general leaf for shell company money laundering that has not been further classified into a broader layered-network (ITID-53911) or BEC-proceeds-specific (ITID-53912) subtype at the time of intake.
ITID-53913.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for shell company laundering that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported shell company laundering pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53911 or ITID-53912
ITID-53913.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53913.priority: P2 pending triage given the potential time-sensitivity of a fund-freeze opportunity; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53913.escalation: Escalate to AML/BSA compliance for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53911 or ITID-53912 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Shell-company-linked laundering activity flagged but not yet root-caused
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard shell company laundering triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53913.response: AML/BSA compliance triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-539xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Shell Company Laundering Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53913.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination. Intake bucket only.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Shell Company Laundering
playbook.description: A shell-company money-laundering indicator that does not fit the layered-network or BEC-proceeds patterns, requiring general AML-compliance investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Triage the shell-company laundering indicator
steps.desc: Assess a transaction-monitoring alert or other indicator suggesting shell-company involvement in money laundering not fitting a more specific pattern.
steps.guidance: Review the entity's business purpose, beneficial-ownership disclosures, and transaction pattern against shell-company red-flag typologies.
steps.outcome: Credible indicators documented with the entity and transaction pattern identified.
steps.abort: If the entity has a legitimate documented purpose, close as false positive.

steps.title: Map related entities and fund flow
steps.desc: Determine whether the entity is linked to other related entities or a broader fund-flow pattern.
steps.guidance: Use link analysis across account-opening data and transaction records.
steps.outcome: Scope of related entities and fund flow documented.

steps.title: Place a transaction hold on the implicated accounts
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending transactions and restrict further activity on the implicated accounts pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Account Operations to apply the hold.
steps.outcome: Pending transactions held and further activity restricted.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve relevant records.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Complete EDD on the implicated entities and quantify the scope of activity.
steps.guidance: Document EDD findings for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with quantified exposure documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN if warranted
steps.desc: The BSA Officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN if warranted.
steps.guidance: Apply the institution's SAR decision criteria and complete the filing within the regulatory deadline if warranted.
steps.outcome: SAR filed as warranted.
steps.abort: If criteria are not met, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Resolve the relationship and resume normal operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Determine the account relationship disposition and resume normal operations for any retained accounts under enhanced monitoring.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on the disposition decision.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition resolved and normal operations resumed under enhanced monitoring where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update transaction-monitoring scenarios/typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53921.def: Financial-crime activity in which an individual makes a series of cash deposits, each intentionally kept just under the regulatory reporting threshold (e.g., $10,000 in the US), across one or more accounts or institutions, specifically to avoid triggering a mandatory currency transaction report.
ITID-53921.purpose: Captures structuring in which cash deposits are deliberately kept below the regulatory reporting threshold to avoid triggering mandatory currency-transaction reporting.
scopeIncludes: A single depositor making repeated sub-threshold cash deposits across multiple days or branches
Deliberate splitting of a single cash sum into multiple sub-threshold transactions in immediate succession
Deposits timed or structured specifically in response to a known reporting threshold
scopeExcludes: Use of multiple different individuals to split a large transfer, classified under Smurfing (ITID-53922)
ITID-53921.severity: Medium-High. Structuring is a federal offense in its own right independent of the underlying source of funds, and is a strong AML red flag warranting escalation regardless of transaction size.
ITID-53921.priority: P2 upon pattern confirmation, given mandatory SAR-filing obligations.
ITID-53921.escalation: Escalate immediately to AML/BSA compliance for SAR filing; structuring patterns must be reported regardless of whether the underlying funds' source is otherwise explained.
indicators: Multiple cash deposits by the same individual, each just under the reporting threshold, within a short time window
Deposits made across multiple branches or accounts on the same day
Deposit pattern with no apparent legitimate business rationale for the sub-threshold structuring
vectors: Manual splitting of a cash sum into multiple sub-threshold deposits
Use of multiple bank branches on the same day to avoid a single teller noticing the pattern
rootCauses: Insufficient cross-branch/cross-day transaction-pattern monitoring
Reliance on single-transaction threshold checks without aggregation analysis
controls: Aggregated, cross-branch/cross-day transaction-pattern monitoring for structuring indicators
Mandatory SAR filing workflow for confirmed structuring patterns
ITID-53921.detection: Detected through AML transaction-monitoring systems analyzing aggregated deposit patterns; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53921.response: AML/BSA compliance files the required SAR and may close or restrict the account pending investigation; law-enforcement referral as appropriate.
metrics: Number of structuring patterns identified per quarter
Number of resulting SARs filed
sops: Structuring Detection and SAR Filing SOP
detections: Aggregated deposit-pattern monitoring for sub-threshold structuring
ITID-53921.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination.

playbook.name: Cash Deposit Structuring Below Reporting Threshold
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects a pattern of cash deposits deliberately structured just below the Currency Transaction Report (CTR) reporting threshold to avoid triggering regulatory reporting, requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the structuring pattern via transaction-monitoring alert
steps.desc: Identify a pattern of multiple cash deposits by the same customer/related parties, each just below the $10,000 CTR reporting threshold, made in a manner suggesting deliberate avoidance of reporting.
steps.guidance: Review the transaction-monitoring system's structuring-detection scenario output, including deposit timing, amounts, and branch/channel diversity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed structuring pattern documented with the customer, deposit amounts, dates, and locations identified.
steps.abort: If the deposit pattern reflects legitimate business cash-flow timing with no reporting-avoidance intent, close as false positive.

steps.title: Review account history and customer profile for corroborating context
steps.desc: Review the customer's account-opening profile, stated business purpose, and historical transaction pattern to assess whether the structuring is consistent with known customer activity or represents a material deviation.
steps.guidance: Compare current activity against the customer's expected activity profile established at onboarding.
steps.outcome: Customer profile context documented supporting or refuting the structuring concern.

steps.title: Restrict further cash-deposit activity pending investigation
steps.desc: Place a hold or enhanced review flag on further cash deposits from the customer pending the investigation outcome, without tipping off the customer to the AML investigation.
steps.guidance: Apply the restriction discreetly consistent with the institution's anti-tipping-off policy under BSA confidentiality requirements.
steps.outcome: Further cash-deposit activity restricted/flagged without alerting the customer to the investigation.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and preserve transaction records
steps.desc: Escalate the structuring finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant transaction and account records.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify the total structured amount
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to quantify the total amount deposited through the structuring pattern and confirm the deliberate-avoidance intent where possible.
steps.guidance: Document the full deposit history and pattern analysis for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with the total structured amount quantified and documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN (mandatory reporting consideration)
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the structuring activity, given that structuring to evade CTR reporting is itself a reportable and potentially criminal violation under the Bank Secrecy Act.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline, referencing 31 U.S.C. 5324 structuring indicators in the narrative.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after investigation, the pattern does not meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Reassess customer risk rating and apply enhanced due diligence
steps.desc: Reassess the customer's AML risk rating in light of the structuring finding and apply enhanced due diligence and monitoring going forward.
steps.guidance: Update the customer risk-rating in the AML system and document the EDD requirements applied.
steps.outcome: Customer risk rating updated and EDD applied.

steps.title: Resume normal account operations under enhanced ongoing monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal account operations under enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring appropriate to the updated risk rating.
steps.guidance: Apply a heightened monitoring profile for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update structuring-detection thresholds
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and review/update transaction-monitoring structuring-detection thresholds and scenarios based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection thresholds reviewed/updated.

ITID-53922.def: Financial-crime activity in which an organizer recruits or directs multiple individuals ('smurfs') to each deposit, transfer, or carry a portion of a larger illicit sum through separate accounts or transactions, so that no single individual's activity appears large enough to trigger reporting or scrutiny, before the funds are consolidated for the organizer's benefit.
ITID-53922.purpose: Captures smurfing in which a large sum is split across multiple individuals or accounts to avoid detection and reporting thresholds.
scopeIncludes: Multiple individuals each depositing or transferring a portion of a coordinated large sum on behalf of an organizer
Recruitment of family members, associates, or paid participants to act as smurfs
Subsequent consolidation of the distributed funds back to the organizer or a designated account
scopeExcludes: A single individual structuring their own deposits below the reporting threshold, classified under Structuring (ITID-53921)
ITID-53922.severity: High. Smurfing networks often indicate a larger organized financial-crime operation and involve materially larger aggregate sums than individual structuring.
ITID-53922.priority: P2 upon pattern confirmation, escalating to P1 if an active, ongoing consolidation transfer is identified.
ITID-53922.escalation: Escalate immediately to AML/BSA compliance for SAR filing and to law enforcement given the likely organized-crime nexus.
indicators: Multiple unrelated or loosely connected individuals depositing similar sub-threshold amounts within a short window
Common downstream consolidation account receiving transfers from multiple smurf accounts
Smurf accounts opened in a short time window with limited subsequent legitimate activity
vectors: Recruitment of individuals (often financially vulnerable) to act as smurfs for a fee
Network of accounts opened specifically to support the smurfing scheme
rootCauses: Insufficient network/link analysis connecting seemingly unrelated depositors to a common consolidation point
Onboarding processes that do not flag accounts opened in clusters with limited legitimate activity history
controls: Network/link analysis connecting depositor accounts to common consolidation points
Enhanced due diligence on accounts with limited history receiving/sending clustered sub-threshold transactions
Mandatory SAR filing workflow for confirmed smurfing patterns
ITID-53922.detection: Detected through AML network-analysis and transaction-monitoring systems; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53922.response: AML/BSA compliance files required SARs; law enforcement pursues the organized network given the likely broader criminal nexus.
metrics: Number of smurfing networks identified per quarter
Aggregate dollar value per confirmed network
sops: Smurfing Network Detection and SAR Filing SOP
detections: Cross-account network/link analysis for smurfing patterns
ITID-53922.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination.

playbook.name: Smurfing via Multiple Accounts/Individuals to Split Large Transfer
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects a pattern of multiple individuals (smurfs) making coordinated deposits or transfers across multiple accounts to break a large sum into smaller amounts and obscure its origin, requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the coordinated multi-account/multi-individual pattern
steps.desc: Identify a pattern of multiple individuals making similarly-timed deposits or transfers across multiple accounts that appear coordinated and consistent with splitting a larger sum to obscure origin (smurfing).
steps.guidance: Review the transaction-monitoring system's network-analysis/smurfing-detection scenario output for shared addresses, contact information, timing correlation, or common funding sources across the accounts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed smurfing pattern documented with the network of accounts/individuals and total value identified.
steps.abort: If the multiple deposits reflect legitimate unrelated activity with no coordination evidence, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify the organizing party and ultimate beneficiary of the funds
steps.desc: Determine whether an organizing individual or entity is coordinating the smurfing network and identify the ultimate destination/beneficiary of the aggregated funds.
steps.guidance: Trace outbound transfers from the individual accounts to identify a common consolidation point.
steps.outcome: Organizing party and ultimate fund destination identified where possible.

steps.title: Restrict further activity across the implicated account network
steps.desc: Place a hold or enhanced review flag on further transactions across all accounts identified in the smurfing network pending investigation, without tipping off the individuals involved.
steps.guidance: Apply the restriction discreetly across all implicated accounts simultaneously, consistent with the institution's anti-tipping-off policy.
steps.outcome: Further activity restricted across the network without alerting the individuals involved.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and preserve records across all implicated accounts
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant records across the full implicated account network.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved across the network.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify the total aggregated value
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to quantify the total value moved through the smurfing network and document the coordination evidence.
steps.guidance: Document the full network map, transaction detail, and total aggregated value for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with the total aggregated value quantified and documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN (mandatory reporting consideration)
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the smurfing scheme, given the statutory obligation to report suspicious activity of this nature.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline, referencing the coordinated multi-account pattern in the narrative.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after investigation, the pattern does not meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Close or restrict implicated accounts and strengthen network-detection controls
steps.desc: Determine whether to close or restrict the implicated accounts per the institution's risk-appetite policy, and strengthen transaction-monitoring network-analysis capabilities to detect similar smurfing patterns earlier.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on account-disposition decisions and update the monitoring scenario logic.
steps.outcome: Account dispositions decided and network-detection controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal operations for retained accounts under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal operations for any retained accounts under enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring.
steps.guidance: Apply a heightened monitoring profile for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update smurfing-detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update transaction-monitoring network-analysis scenarios/typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53923.def: An unclassified/general leaf for structuring/smurfing money laundering activity that has not been further classified into single-depositor structuring (ITID-53921) or multi-individual smurfing (ITID-53922) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53923.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for structuring and smurfing activity that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported structuring/smurfing activity pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53921 or ITID-53922
ITID-53923.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53923.priority: P2 pending triage given mandatory SAR-filing timelines; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53923.escalation: Escalate to AML/BSA compliance for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53921 or ITID-53922 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Sub-threshold transaction pattern flagged but not yet root-caused as single-depositor vs. multi-individual
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard structuring/smurfing triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53923.response: AML/BSA compliance triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-539xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Structuring and Smurfing Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53923.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination. Intake bucket only.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Structuring and Smurfing
playbook.description: A structuring/smurfing indicator that does not fit the single-account threshold-avoidance or multi-account coordinated patterns, requiring general AML-compliance investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the structuring/smurfing indicator
steps.desc: Identify a structuring/smurfing indicator not fitting a more specific pattern via transaction-monitoring alert or other referral.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged transaction pattern against structuring/smurfing typologies.
steps.outcome: Confirmed indicator documented with the transaction pattern identified.
steps.abort: If the pattern reflects legitimate activity, close as false positive.

steps.title: Scope the full pattern and any related parties
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of the pattern and identify any related accounts or individuals involved.
steps.guidance: Use link analysis across account and transaction records.
steps.outcome: Scope of the pattern and related parties documented.

steps.title: Restrict further activity pending investigation
steps.desc: Place a hold or enhanced review flag on further transactions pending the investigation outcome, without tipping off the individuals involved.
steps.guidance: Apply the restriction discreetly consistent with the institution's anti-tipping-off policy.
steps.outcome: Further activity restricted without alerting the individuals involved.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve relevant records.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify the pattern
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to quantify the total value and scope of the structuring/smurfing pattern.
steps.guidance: Document all findings for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with the pattern quantified and documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN (mandatory reporting consideration)
steps.desc: The BSA Officer evaluates and files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the confirmed structuring/smurfing activity, given the statutory obligation to report suspicious activity of this nature.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after investigation, the pattern does not meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Resolve account dispositions and resume normal operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Determine account dispositions and resume normal operations for retained accounts under enhanced ongoing monitoring.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on disposition decisions.
steps.outcome: Account dispositions resolved and normal operations resumed under enhanced monitoring where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update transaction-monitoring scenarios/typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53931.def: Financial-crime activity in which parties to an international trade transaction deliberately misstate the price of goods on an invoice — over-invoicing to move excess value to the exporter, or under-invoicing to move excess value to the importer — using the price discrepancy itself as the vehicle for transferring value across borders outside normal financial-transfer scrutiny.
ITID-53931.purpose: Captures trade-based laundering that moves value between parties by misstating the price of goods on a trade invoice.
scopeIncludes: Invoicing goods at a price significantly above fair market value to move value to the receiving (exporting) party
Invoicing goods at a price significantly below fair market value to move value to the paying (importing) party
Repeated trade relationships between related or complicit parties used as an ongoing value-transfer channel
scopeExcludes: Phantom shipment schemes where no goods move at all (ITID-53932)
ITID-53931.severity: Medium-High. Trade-based laundering is difficult to detect through financial-transaction monitoring alone since the funds movement appears tied to a genuine (if mispriced) commercial transaction.
ITID-53931.priority: P2 upon pattern confirmation, given the potential for sanctions or trade-compliance exposure alongside AML concerns.
ITID-53931.escalation: Escalate to AML/BSA compliance and trade-compliance/sanctions teams for joint review; escalate to legal where cross-border regulatory exposure is significant.
indicators: Invoice pricing significantly inconsistent with prevailing market rates for the goods described
Repeated trade relationship with a counterparty in a high-risk jurisdiction with no clear commercial rationale for the pricing pattern
Discrepancy between customs-declared value and invoiced value
vectors: Collusive pricing arrangements between trade counterparties
Use of intermediary trading companies to obscure the true pricing relationship
rootCauses: Insufficient trade-finance review of invoice pricing against market benchmarks
Limited cross-referencing between customs data and trade-finance invoicing data
controls: Trade-finance pricing review against independent market-price benchmarks
Cross-referencing of customs-declared value against invoiced value
Enhanced due diligence on trade counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions
ITID-53931.detection: Detected through trade-finance compliance review and customs-data cross-referencing rather than SOC technical telemetry.
ITID-53931.response: Trade-compliance and AML/BSA teams jointly investigate and file SARs as required; legal manages any sanctions-exposure implications.
metrics: Number of mispriced-invoice schemes identified per quarter
Aggregate value moved per confirmed scheme
ITID-53931.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination.

playbook.name: Over-Invoicing/Under-Invoicing Trade Transaction to Move Value
playbook.description: AML Compliance/Trade Finance detects a trade transaction where invoiced value materially diverges from the fair market value of goods, indicating trade-based money laundering via over- or under-invoicing, requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the invoice-value discrepancy in a trade finance transaction
steps.desc: Identify a trade finance transaction (letter of credit, documentary collection, or open-account trade) where the invoiced value materially diverges from the fair market value of the underlying goods, suggesting deliberate value manipulation to move funds.
steps.guidance: Compare the invoiced unit price/value against independent trade-pricing databases or known market pricing for the commodity/goods class involved.
steps.outcome: Confirmed price discrepancy documented with the transaction, parties, and estimated value gap identified.
steps.abort: If the price variance is explained by legitimate factors (quality grade, market volatility, bulk discount), close as false positive.

steps.title: Review the counterparty relationship and jurisdictional risk factors
steps.desc: Assess the counterparty's jurisdiction, ownership structure, and prior transaction history for additional trade-based money-laundering (TBML) red flags.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the counterparty against sanctions/high-risk-jurisdiction lists and review for other TBML indicators (e.g., commodity type mismatch, unusual shipping routes).
steps.outcome: Additional risk factors documented supporting or refuting the TBML concern.

steps.title: Hold the trade finance instrument/payment pending review
steps.desc: Place a hold on the letter of credit negotiation, documentary collection payment, or open-account settlement pending investigation of the pricing discrepancy.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Trade Finance Operations to place the hold without breaching contractual payment obligations improperly; consult Legal on any contractual notice requirements.
steps.outcome: Payment/negotiation held pending investigation.
steps.abort: If the underlying trade obligation legally requires payment before review can complete, document the constraint and proceed to post-payment investigation.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and Trade Compliance leadership
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer and Trade Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant trade documentation (invoices, bills of lading, shipping records).
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML/trade-compliance case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer/Trade Compliance engaged and relevant documentation preserved.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify the value discrepancy
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to quantify the full value discrepancy across the transaction (and any related transactions with the same counterparty) and document the TBML indicators found.
steps.guidance: Document the full pricing analysis, counterparty risk factors, and transaction history for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with the value discrepancy quantified and documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN and consider trade-relationship exit
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the trade-based money-laundering indicators, and Trade Compliance/Legal determine whether to exit the trade finance relationship.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline; document the relationship-exit rationale if pursued.
steps.outcome: SAR filed and relationship-disposition decision documented.
steps.abort: If, after investigation, the pattern does not meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Strengthen trade-finance pricing-verification controls
steps.desc: Enhance trade-finance underwriting to require independent pricing verification against market benchmarks for high-risk commodity classes and jurisdictions.
steps.guidance: Update the trade finance policy and communicate the change to Trade Finance Operations staff.
steps.outcome: Updated pricing-verification control documented and adopted.

steps.title: Resume normal trade-finance operations under enhanced pricing review
steps.desc: Resume normal trade-finance processing under the strengthened pricing-verification controls and monitor closely for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Track pricing-discrepancy flag rates post-implementation to confirm control effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced pricing review controls active.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update TBML-detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update trade-finance TBML-detection scenarios/typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML/Trade Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53932.def: Financial-crime activity in which parties generate a complete set of trade documentation (invoices, bills of lading, customs paperwork) for a shipment of goods that never actually exists or moves, using the fabricated 'phantom' trade transaction purely as a justification to move funds across borders through the trade-finance system.
ITID-53932.purpose: Captures trade-based laundering in which a trade transaction and its supporting documentation are entirely fabricated with no actual goods ever moving.
scopeIncludes: Fully fabricated bills of lading, customs paperwork, or shipping manifests for goods that never shipped
Payment made against a phantom trade transaction with no corresponding physical goods movement
Reuse of the same fabricated shipment documentation across multiple financing claims
scopeExcludes: Genuine goods movement with mispriced invoicing (ITID-53931)
ITID-53932.severity: High. Phantom shipment schemes represent complete fabrication rather than mere mispricing, and often involve larger, more brazen fund-transfer amounts.
ITID-53932.priority: P1 upon confirmation that no goods movement occurred, given the clear-cut fraud/laundering finding and potential trade-finance facility exposure.
ITID-53932.escalation: Escalate immediately to trade-finance risk, AML/BSA compliance, and legal; escalate to law enforcement given the outright document-fabrication component.
indicators: Bill of lading or shipping manifest that cannot be verified against carrier or port records
Customs declaration with no corresponding physical inspection or clearance record
Trade-finance facility drawn down against documentation for a shipment with no verifiable logistics trail
vectors: Fabrication of shipping and customs documentation using forged or reused templates
Collusion with a complicit freight forwarder or customs broker to validate fabricated paperwork
rootCauses: Insufficient independent verification of shipping/customs documentation against carrier and port records
Trade-finance approval processes relying solely on paper documentation without logistics-trail corroboration
controls: Independent verification of shipping/customs documentation against carrier and port records before trade-finance disbursement
Physical or third-party logistics-trail corroboration for high-value trade-finance transactions
ITID-53932.detection: Detected through trade-finance document verification and logistics-trail cross-referencing rather than SOC technical telemetry.
ITID-53932.response: Trade-finance risk halts further disbursement and investigates prior transactions; AML/BSA compliance files required SARs; legal pursues recovery/prosecution.
metrics: Number of phantom shipment schemes identified per quarter
Aggregate trade-finance exposure per confirmed scheme
sops: Phantom Shipment Trade Fraud Investigation SOP
detections: Shipping/customs documentation verification against carrier and port records
ITID-53932.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination.

playbook.name: Phantom Shipment Trade Laundering (No Actual Goods Moved)
playbook.description: AML Compliance/Trade Finance detects indicators that a trade finance transaction was supported by fraudulent shipping documentation for goods that were never actually shipped (phantom shipment), requiring urgent investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect indicators of a phantom (non-existent) shipment
steps.desc: Identify indicators that the goods purportedly underlying a trade finance transaction were never actually shipped — e.g., a bill of lading referencing a vessel with no matching sailing record, or a shipment inconsistent with known logistics/customs data.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the bill of lading and vessel identification against vessel-tracking/customs databases to confirm whether the shipment actually occurred.
steps.outcome: Confirmed phantom-shipment indicator documented with the transaction, purported shipment, and discrepancy identified.
steps.abort: If the shipment is confirmed to have occurred via independent tracking data, close as false positive.

steps.title: Review the counterparty and financing structure for coordinated fraud indicators
steps.desc: Assess whether the phantom shipment appears to be an isolated documentation error or part of a coordinated scheme to move value between the parties under the guise of legitimate trade.
steps.guidance: Review the counterparty's transaction history and relationship for prior similar patterns or shared documentation preparers.
steps.outcome: Scope of the scheme (isolated vs. coordinated) assessed and documented.

steps.title: Immediately halt payment/negotiation on the trade instrument
steps.desc: Immediately halt any pending payment, letter-of-credit negotiation, or financing disbursement tied to the phantom shipment before funds move based on the fraudulent documentation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Trade Finance Operations and Legal to halt the transaction, given the time-sensitive nature of trade-finance settlement cycles.
steps.outcome: Payment/negotiation halted before disbursement based on fraudulent documentation.
steps.abort: If payment has already been disbursed, document and proceed directly to recovery and law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and Trade Compliance leadership
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer and Trade Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant trade documentation.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML/trade-compliance case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer/Trade Compliance engaged and relevant documentation preserved.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify exposure
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to confirm the phantom-shipment finding, quantify any funds already disbursed, and identify all parties involved.
steps.guidance: Document the full investigation findings for the SAR narrative and any recovery/law-enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with exposure quantified and parties identified.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN and refer to law enforcement
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the phantom-shipment trade-laundering scheme, and refers the matter to law enforcement given the fraudulent-documentation element.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline and coordinate the law-enforcement referral through Legal.
steps.outcome: SAR filed and law-enforcement referral made.

steps.title: Exit the trade-finance relationship and strengthen shipment-verification controls
steps.desc: Exit the implicated trade-finance relationship per the institution's risk-appetite policy and strengthen independent shipment-verification requirements for future trade finance transactions.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on relationship exit and update the trade finance underwriting policy to require independent vessel-tracking verification.
steps.outcome: Relationship exited and shipment-verification controls strengthened.

steps.title: Pursue recovery of any disbursed funds and resume normal operations
steps.desc: Pursue recovery of any funds disbursed based on the fraudulent phantom-shipment documentation and resume normal trade-finance operations under the strengthened controls.
steps.guidance: Track the recovery effort to conclusion and confirm the strengthened verification control is active before resuming similar transaction types.
steps.outcome: Recovery pursued and normal operations resumed under strengthened controls.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update TBML phantom-shipment detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update trade-finance TBML-detection scenarios/typologies to better detect phantom-shipment patterns.
steps.guidance: Brief AML/Trade Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53933.def: An unclassified/general leaf for trade-based money laundering that has not been further classified into mispriced-invoicing (ITID-53931) or phantom-shipment (ITID-53932) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53933.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for trade-based money laundering that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported trade-based laundering pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53931 or ITID-53932
ITID-53933.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53933.priority: P2 pending triage; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53933.escalation: Escalate to AML/BSA and trade-compliance for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53931 or ITID-53932 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Trade-finance anomaly flagged but not yet root-caused as mispricing vs. phantom shipment
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard trade-based laundering triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53933.response: AML/BSA and trade-compliance triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-539xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Trade-Based Money Laundering Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53933.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination. Intake bucket only.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Trade-Based Money Laundering
playbook.description: A trade-based money-laundering indicator that does not fit the invoicing-manipulation or phantom-shipment patterns, requiring general AML-compliance investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the trade-based money-laundering indicator
steps.desc: Identify a trade-finance discrepancy or red flag not fitting a more specific pattern, indicating potential trade-based money laundering.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged trade transaction against TBML red-flag typologies and available documentation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed indicator documented with the transaction and discrepancy identified.
steps.abort: If the transaction is legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Review counterparty and jurisdictional risk factors
steps.desc: Assess the counterparty's jurisdiction, ownership, and transaction history for additional TBML red flags.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against sanctions/high-risk-jurisdiction lists.
steps.outcome: Additional risk factors documented.

steps.title: Hold the trade transaction pending review
steps.desc: Place a hold on the trade finance instrument/payment pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Trade Finance Operations to place the hold, consulting Legal on contractual constraints.
steps.outcome: Transaction held pending investigation.
steps.abort: If payment is contractually required before review completes, document the constraint and proceed to post-payment investigation.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/Trade Compliance leadership and preserve relevant trade documentation.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML/trade-compliance case-escalation procedure.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant documentation preserved.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and quantify the discrepancy
steps.desc: Complete the investigation to quantify the scope of the trade-based laundering indicator.
steps.guidance: Document all findings for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: Investigation completed with findings documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN (mandatory reporting consideration)
steps.desc: The BSA Officer evaluates and files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the confirmed trade-based money-laundering activity.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after investigation, the pattern does not meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Resolve the relationship and resume normal operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Determine the trade-relationship disposition and resume normal operations under enhanced monitoring for any retained relationship.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on disposition decisions.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition resolved and normal operations resumed under enhanced monitoring where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update TBML-detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update trade-finance TBML-detection scenarios/typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML/Trade Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53941.def: Financial-crime activity in which an individual routes cryptocurrency through a mixing or tumbling service — which pools and redistributes funds from many depositors to obscure the direct transactional link between sender and receiver — specifically to launder the origin of illicitly obtained cryptocurrency before cashing out or further using it.
ITID-53941.purpose: Captures laundering that uses a cryptocurrency mixer or tumbler to break the on-chain link between illicit funds and their eventual destination.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate routing of illicit cryptocurrency proceeds through a known mixing/tumbling service
Use of privacy-coin conversion as an intermediate step before or after mixing
Withdrawal of mixed funds to a fresh address with no apparent link to the original illicit source
scopeExcludes: Moving funds across multiple different cryptocurrencies without using a dedicated mixing service (Chain-Hopping, ITID-53942)
Layering via numerous small transactions without a mixing service (ITID-53943)
ITID-53941.severity: High. Successful mixing significantly degrades the ability to trace stolen or illicit funds, materially reducing recovery prospects.
ITID-53941.priority: P1 immediately if detected while funds are still in transit toward a mixing service, to attempt exchange-side flagging before mixing completes; P2 once mixing is confirmed complete.
ITID-53941.escalation: Escalate immediately to blockchain-analytics partners and any exchange in the transaction path to flag/freeze before mixing completes; escalate to law enforcement for post-mixing tracing efforts.
indicators: On-chain transaction path terminating at a known mixing/tumbling service address
Withdrawal from a mixing service to a fresh address shortly after illicit funds enter the mixer
Use of a privacy coin conversion immediately before or after mixing activity
vectors: Direct deposit of stolen/illicit funds into a known mixing service
Layered use of multiple mixing services in sequence
rootCauses: Delayed detection of the upstream theft/fraud event allowing time for funds to reach a mixer before any freeze attempt
Limited real-time blockchain-analytics coverage of newer or less-tracked mixing services
controls: Real-time blockchain-analytics monitoring flagging known mixing-service addresses
Rapid exchange-partner coordination protocol for pre-mixing freeze requests
ITID-53941.detection: On-chain analytics tooling can identify funds flowing toward known mixing services in real time, though tracing funds after successful mixing is materially harder.
ITID-53941.response: Fraud operations and legal coordinate with blockchain-analytics and exchange partners to attempt a freeze before mixing completes; law enforcement engagement for post-mixing tracing.
metrics: Percentage of at-risk funds frozen before mixing completion
Number of mixing-related laundering cases identified per quarter
detections: Blockchain-analytics alerting on known mixing-service addresses
ITID-53941.notes: This is a money-laundering/financial-crime typology with no ATT&CK Enterprise technique directly applying to the laundering activity itself. A mixing service can loosely be thought of as functioning like a third-party relay/obfuscation layer (broadly analogous in spirit to T1102 Web Service, which covers use of a legitimate external service to obscure command-and-control activity), but this is offered only as an illustrative analogy, not a formal mapping — the mixer is a financial-obfuscation tool, not a C2 channel, and mapped_mitre is left empty accordingly.

playbook.name: Crypto Mixer/Tumbler Used to Obscure Fund Origin
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects that funds flowing into or out of a customer's account are linked, via blockchain analytics, to a cryptocurrency mixer/tumbler service used to obscure the true origin of funds, requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the mixer/tumbler exposure via blockchain analytics
steps.desc: Identify that inbound or outbound cryptocurrency transactions associated with a customer's account are linked, via blockchain-analytics tooling, to a known mixing/tumbling service.
steps.guidance: Review the blockchain-analytics platform's address-attribution and risk-scoring output for the transaction(s) in question, confirming the mixer/tumbler linkage with a documented confidence level.
steps.outcome: Confirmed mixer/tumbler exposure documented with the transaction, wallet addresses, and confidence level identified.
steps.abort: If the analytics attribution is low-confidence or the customer provides a credible legitimate explanation (e.g., privacy-focused legitimate use with clear source-of-funds documentation), assess per policy before closing.

steps.title: Assess the customer's overall risk profile and transaction history
steps.desc: Review the customer's account-opening profile, stated purpose for cryptocurrency activity, and historical transaction pattern to assess the materiality and context of the mixer exposure.
steps.guidance: Compare the flagged activity against the customer's expected activity profile and any prior EDD on file.
steps.outcome: Customer risk context documented supporting the investigation's next steps.

steps.title: Restrict the account and hold pending funds
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending cryptocurrency transactions and restrict further account activity pending the investigation outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the digital-asset operations team to apply the hold without violating any applicable customer-notification restrictions.
steps.outcome: Pending transactions held and further account activity restricted.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and preserve blockchain/account records
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant blockchain-analytics reports and account records.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure for virtual-asset-related alerts.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence and quantify the exposure
steps.desc: Complete EDD on the customer and quantify the total value of funds linked to the mixer/tumbler exposure.
steps.guidance: Document the full EDD findings, including source-of-funds inquiry results, for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with quantified exposure documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the mixer/tumbler-linked activity, consistent with the institution's statutory AML reporting obligations for virtual-asset-related suspicious activity.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline, including blockchain-analytics evidence in the narrative.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after EDD, the activity is determined not to meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Determine relationship disposition and strengthen virtual-asset monitoring controls
steps.desc: Determine whether to exit or restrict the customer relationship per the institution's virtual-asset risk-appetite policy, and strengthen blockchain-analytics screening coverage for mixer/tumbler exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on the relationship decision and update the virtual-asset AML monitoring rule set.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition decided and monitoring controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal operations for retained accounts under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal digital-asset account operations for any retained relationship under enhanced ongoing blockchain-analytics monitoring.
steps.guidance: Apply a heightened monitoring profile for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update virtual-asset detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update blockchain-analytics detection typologies/risk-scoring thresholds based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53942.def: Financial-crime activity in which an individual converts illicit cryptocurrency proceeds through a rapid sequence of different cryptocurrencies (e.g., Bitcoin to Monero to Ethereum to a stablecoin) via exchanges or swap services, exploiting the fact that no single blockchain's public ledger captures the full cross-chain trail, to defeat straightforward on-chain tracing.
ITID-53942.purpose: Captures laundering that converts illicit funds across multiple different cryptocurrencies in sequence to break the traceability of a single blockchain's transaction history.
scopeIncludes: Sequential conversion of illicit funds across three or more distinct cryptocurrencies within a short timeframe
Use of a privacy coin as one link in the chain-hopping sequence specifically to break traceability at that hop
Use of decentralized/no-KYC swap services to execute conversions without identity verification
scopeExcludes: Routing funds through a dedicated mixing/tumbling service on a single chain (ITID-53941)
Layering via numerous low-value transactions on a single cryptocurrency (ITID-53943)
ITID-53942.severity: High. Chain-hopping across multiple ledgers and privacy coins significantly complicates cross-chain blockchain-analytics tracing.
ITID-53942.priority: P1 immediately if detected mid-sequence, to attempt flagging at the next exchange hop before the chain-hop completes; P2 once the sequence is confirmed complete.
ITID-53942.escalation: Escalate immediately to blockchain-analytics partners capable of cross-chain tracing and to any exchange/swap service in the path to request a freeze.
indicators: Rapid sequential conversion across multiple distinct cryptocurrencies shortly after illicit funds are received
Use of a privacy coin as an intermediate hop in an otherwise traceable chain
Use of decentralized, no-KYC swap services at one or more hops
vectors: Sequential use of centralized and decentralized exchanges to convert across multiple cryptocurrencies
Insertion of a privacy coin hop specifically to break the traceable chain
rootCauses: Limited cross-chain blockchain-analytics coverage, particularly where privacy coins or decentralized swaps are involved
Delayed detection of the upstream theft/fraud allowing time for the chain-hop sequence to complete
controls: Cross-chain blockchain-analytics monitoring capable of tracing through privacy-coin and decentralized-swap hops
Rapid multi-exchange coordination protocol for freeze requests at any identified hop
ITID-53942.detection: Advanced cross-chain blockchain-analytics tooling provides partial visibility; coverage degrades significantly once a privacy coin or fully decentralized swap is used in the chain.
ITID-53942.response: Fraud operations and legal coordinate with blockchain-analytics and exchange partners at each identifiable hop; law enforcement engagement for post-sequence tracing.
metrics: Percentage of at-risk funds frozen before chain-hop sequence completion
Number of chain-hopping cases identified per quarter
ITID-53942.notes: This is a money-laundering/financial-crime typology with no ATT&CK Enterprise technique directly applying. The obfuscation-infrastructure role that swap services and cross-chain routing play is loosely analogous in spirit to T1090 Proxy (routing traffic through intermediary nodes to obscure origin), offered only as an illustrative analogy rather than a formal mapping — mapped_mitre is left empty accordingly.

playbook.name: Chain-Hopping Across Multiple Cryptocurrencies to Break Trace
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects that a customer rapidly converted funds across multiple different cryptocurrencies (chain-hopping) in a pattern consistent with deliberately breaking the blockchain trace of fund origin, requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the chain-hopping pattern via blockchain analytics
steps.desc: Identify a pattern of rapid, sequential conversion of funds across multiple different cryptocurrencies/blockchains with no apparent legitimate investment rationale, consistent with deliberate trace-breaking (chain-hopping).
steps.guidance: Review the blockchain-analytics platform's cross-chain tracing output for the sequence, timing, and conversion venues used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed chain-hopping pattern documented with the transaction sequence and total value identified.
steps.abort: If the conversion pattern reflects legitimate trading/investment activity with a documented rationale, close as false positive.

steps.title: Trace the pre-hopping fund origin and post-hopping destination
steps.desc: Attempt to trace the funds' origin prior to the chain-hopping sequence and their ultimate destination after, to assess the underlying source-of-funds risk.
steps.guidance: Use available blockchain-analytics attribution to identify origin/destination wallet risk scores (e.g., darknet market, sanctioned entity, mixer).
steps.outcome: Origin and destination risk assessment documented to the extent traceable.

steps.title: Restrict the account and hold pending funds
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending cryptocurrency transactions and restrict further account activity pending the investigation outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the digital-asset operations team to apply the hold.
steps.outcome: Pending transactions held and further account activity restricted.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and preserve blockchain/account records
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant blockchain-analytics reports and account records.
