steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure for virtual-asset-related alerts.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence and quantify the exposure
steps.desc: Complete EDD on the customer, including a direct source-of-funds inquiry, and quantify the total value moved through the chain-hopping sequence.
steps.guidance: Document the full EDD findings and blockchain trace for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with quantified exposure documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the chain-hopping activity, consistent with the institution's statutory AML reporting obligations for virtual-asset-related suspicious activity.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline, including the blockchain-trace evidence in the narrative.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after EDD, the activity is determined not to meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Determine relationship disposition and strengthen cross-chain monitoring controls
steps.desc: Determine whether to exit or restrict the customer relationship per the institution's virtual-asset risk-appetite policy, and strengthen cross-chain blockchain-analytics monitoring coverage.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on the relationship decision and update the virtual-asset AML monitoring rule set to flag rapid cross-chain conversion patterns.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition decided and cross-chain monitoring controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal operations for retained accounts under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal digital-asset account operations for any retained relationship under enhanced ongoing cross-chain monitoring.
steps.guidance: Apply a heightened monitoring profile for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update chain-hopping detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update blockchain-analytics cross-chain detection typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53943.def: Financial-crime activity in which an individual splits illicit cryptocurrency proceeds into a large number of low-value transactions distributed across many addresses over time, exploiting the fact that most transaction-monitoring and exchange risk-scoring thresholds are tuned to flag high-value movements, to move the aggregate sum without any single transaction triggering scrutiny.
ITID-53943.purpose: Captures laundering that layers illicit cryptocurrency through a very large number of small-value transactions to evade value-based monitoring thresholds.
scopeIncludes: Splitting a large illicit cryptocurrency sum into many small transactions across numerous addresses
Distribution of layering transactions over an extended time period to avoid velocity-based detection
Eventual reconsolidation of the layered funds at a low-scrutiny withdrawal point
scopeExcludes: Routing funds through a dedicated mixing/tumbling service (ITID-53941)
Sequential conversion across multiple different cryptocurrencies (ITID-53942)
ITID-53943.severity: Medium-High. Individual layering transactions are low-value by design, but the aggregate laundered sum and the difficulty of pattern detection at scale make this a meaningful laundering vector.
ITID-53943.priority: P2 upon pattern confirmation, given the typically slower, more distributed nature of this technique compared to mixing or chain-hopping.
ITID-53943.escalation: Escalate to blockchain-analytics partners for aggregate pattern-of-life analysis linking the many small transactions back to a common source/destination.
indicators: A large number of small, similarly sized cryptocurrency transactions traceable to a common originating address over an extended period
Many low-value addresses eventually consolidating funds at a common withdrawal point
Transaction volume/velocity inconsistent with any apparent legitimate use case
vectors: Automated scripting to distribute funds across many low-value transactions and addresses
Use of numerous unhosted wallet addresses to avoid any single exchange seeing the full pattern
rootCauses: Transaction-monitoring thresholds tuned only to single-transaction value rather than aggregate pattern-of-life
Limited cross-address clustering analysis to link many small addresses to a common controller
controls: Aggregate pattern-of-life and address-clustering analytics rather than single-transaction value thresholds alone
Blockchain-analytics monitoring for known layering-script behavioral signatures
ITID-53943.detection: Detected through advanced blockchain-analytics clustering and pattern-of-life analysis rather than single-transaction alerting; no SOC technical telemetry involved.
ITID-53943.response: Fraud operations and legal coordinate with blockchain-analytics partners for aggregate tracing; law-enforcement engagement where the aggregate sum is material.
metrics: Aggregate value traced per confirmed layering scheme
Number of layering schemes identified per quarter
ITID-53943.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination.

playbook.name: Cryptocurrency Layering via Numerous Low-Value Transactions
playbook.description: AML Compliance detects a pattern of numerous low-value cryptocurrency transactions across many wallets designed to layer and obscure the trail of a larger sum, requiring investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the low-value layering pattern via blockchain analytics
steps.desc: Identify a pattern of numerous small-value cryptocurrency transactions passed through many intermediate wallets in a manner consistent with deliberately layering and obscuring the trail of a larger aggregate sum.
steps.guidance: Review the blockchain-analytics platform's peeling-chain/layering-detection output, including the number of hops, wallet count, and aggregate value involved.
steps.outcome: Confirmed layering pattern documented with the wallet network, transaction count, and aggregate value identified.
steps.abort: If the pattern reflects legitimate automated micro-transaction activity (e.g., a payment-processing service) with no obscuring intent, close as false positive.

steps.title: Trace the aggregate fund origin and ultimate consolidation point
steps.desc: Attempt to trace the layered transactions back to their origin and forward to any consolidation point where the funds are ultimately reassembled.
steps.guidance: Use available blockchain-analytics attribution to identify origin and consolidation wallet risk scores.
steps.outcome: Origin and consolidation point risk assessment documented to the extent traceable.

steps.title: Restrict the account and hold pending funds
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending cryptocurrency transactions and restrict further account activity pending the investigation outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the digital-asset operations team to apply the hold.
steps.outcome: Pending transactions held and further account activity restricted.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer and preserve blockchain/account records
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve all relevant blockchain-analytics reports and account records.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure for virtual-asset-related alerts.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence and quantify the aggregate layered value
steps.desc: Complete EDD on the customer and quantify the total aggregate value moved through the layering pattern.
steps.guidance: Document the full EDD findings and blockchain trace for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with the aggregate layered value quantified and documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN
steps.desc: The BSA Officer files a SAR with FinCEN documenting the layering activity, consistent with the institution's statutory AML reporting obligations for virtual-asset-related suspicious activity.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline, including the blockchain-trace evidence in the narrative.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after EDD, the activity is determined not to meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Determine relationship disposition and strengthen layering-detection controls
steps.desc: Determine whether to exit or restrict the customer relationship per the institution's virtual-asset risk-appetite policy, and strengthen blockchain-analytics layering-detection coverage.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on the relationship decision and update the virtual-asset AML monitoring rule set to flag peeling-chain/layering patterns earlier.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition decided and layering-detection controls strengthened.

steps.title: Resume normal operations for retained accounts under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Resume normal digital-asset account operations for any retained relationship under enhanced ongoing layering-pattern monitoring.
steps.guidance: Apply a heightened monitoring profile for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced monitoring active where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update layering-detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update blockchain-analytics layering-detection typologies based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-53944.def: An unclassified/general leaf for cryptocurrency money laundering that has not been further classified into mixer/tumbler (ITID-53941), chain-hopping (ITID-53942), or low-value-layering (ITID-53943) subtypes at the time of intake.
ITID-53944.purpose: Serves as the catch-all intake bucket for cryptocurrency money laundering that does not yet fit a more specific documented subtype.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported cryptocurrency laundering pending subtype classification
scopeExcludes: Any case that has been triaged into ITID-53941, ITID-53942, or ITID-53943
ITID-53944.severity: Varies; assign provisional severity consistent with the most severe plausible subtype pending reclassification.
ITID-53944.priority: P2 pending triage given the typically time-sensitive nature of fund-freeze opportunities; re-prioritize once the mechanism is determined.
ITID-53944.escalation: Escalate to fraud operations/blockchain-analytics for initial triage; reclassify to ITID-53941, ITID-53942, or ITID-53943 as soon as the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Cryptocurrency laundering activity flagged but not yet root-caused into a specific technique
vectors: Pending determination
rootCauses: Pending determination
controls: Standard cryptocurrency laundering triage workflow prior to subtype classification
ITID-53944.response: Fraud operations/blockchain-analytics triages within a defined SLA and reclassifies to the appropriate ITID-539xx leaf.
metrics: Volume and average dwell time of cases in the unclassified bucket before reclassification
sops: Cryptocurrency Money Laundering Intake and Triage SOP
ITID-53944.notes: money-laundering/financial-crime typology — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked for AML/BSA compliance and law-enforcement coordination. Intake bucket only.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cryptocurrency Money Laundering
playbook.description: A cryptocurrency money-laundering indicator that does not fit the mixer/tumbler, chain-hopping, or low-value-layering patterns, requiring general AML-compliance investigation and SAR-filing consideration.

steps.title: Detect the cryptocurrency money-laundering indicator
steps.desc: Identify a virtual-asset transaction pattern or blockchain-analytics alert not fitting a more specific pattern, indicating potential money laundering.
steps.guidance: Review the flagged activity against blockchain-analytics risk-scoring output and available typologies.
steps.outcome: Confirmed indicator documented with the transaction and risk factors identified.
steps.abort: If the activity is legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Assess the customer's risk profile and transaction history
steps.desc: Review the customer's account profile and transaction history for additional context on the flagged activity.
steps.guidance: Compare against the customer's expected activity profile and any prior EDD on file.
steps.outcome: Customer risk context documented.

steps.title: Restrict the account and hold pending funds
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending cryptocurrency transactions and restrict further account activity pending the investigation outcome.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the digital-asset operations team to apply the hold.
steps.outcome: Pending transactions held and further account activity restricted.

steps.title: Escalate to the BSA Officer
steps.desc: Escalate the finding to the BSA Officer/AML Compliance leadership and preserve relevant blockchain-analytics and account records.
steps.guidance: Follow the institution's AML case-escalation procedure for virtual-asset-related alerts.
steps.outcome: BSA Officer engaged and relevant records preserved.

steps.title: Complete enhanced due diligence and quantify the exposure
steps.desc: Complete EDD on the customer and quantify the value/scope of the flagged activity.
steps.guidance: Document the full EDD findings for the SAR narrative.
steps.outcome: EDD completed with quantified exposure documented.

steps.title: File a SAR with FinCEN (mandatory reporting consideration)
steps.desc: The BSA Officer evaluates SAR-filing criteria and files with FinCEN documenting the confirmed suspicious virtual-asset activity, consistent with the institution's statutory AML reporting obligations.
steps.guidance: Complete the SAR within the regulatory filing deadline if warranted.
steps.outcome: SAR filed with FinCEN within the required timeframe.
steps.abort: If, after EDD, the activity does not meet the suspicious-activity threshold, document the rationale for non-filing per policy.

steps.title: Resolve relationship disposition and resume normal operations under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Determine the customer-relationship disposition and resume normal operations for any retained relationship under enhanced ongoing monitoring.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on disposition decisions.
steps.outcome: Relationship disposition resolved and normal operations resumed under enhanced monitoring where applicable.

steps.title: Document investigation outcome and update virtual-asset detection typologies
steps.desc: Complete a formal investigation report and update blockchain-analytics detection typologies/risk-scoring thresholds based on findings.
steps.guidance: Brief AML Compliance leadership; track control improvements to completion.
steps.outcome: Investigation report completed and detection typologies updated.

ITID-54111.def: A disruption to company operations caused by an outage, degradation, or control-plane failure within a cloud provider's (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS infrastructure layer) own infrastructure, where no adversary action against the company or the provider is implicated.
ITID-54111.purpose: Captures loss of company-consumed cloud services caused entirely by failure inside the cloud provider's own environment, so it is tracked as a business-continuity event rather than a security intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Regional or availability-zone outage at a hyperscaler (AWS/Azure/GCP) taking down company-hosted workloads
Provider control-plane or API failure (e.g., IAM, orchestration) preventing management of company resources
Provider-side network fabric failure isolating company workloads from the internet
scopeExcludes: Outage caused by the company's own misconfiguration (see Accidental Misconfigurations, ITID-54521)
Outage caused by a DDoS attack against the provider or the company's cloud endpoints (see ITID-548xx)
Provider outage caused by the provider itself being breached (track under the applicable ITID-30000/40000 intrusion category if confirmed)
ITID-54111.severity: High if the affected workloads are business-critical and no failover region is available; Medium if multi-region redundancy absorbs most impact.
ITID-54111.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 when revenue-generating or safety-critical services are down enterprise-wide.
ITID-54111.escalation: Escalate to IT operations and business continuity leadership immediately; SOC involvement is to rule out an adversarial cause and to support communications, not to investigate an intrusion.
indicators: Provider status page confirms an active incident
Simultaneous, correlated failures across unrelated company services hosted in the same region/provider
No corresponding authentication, exfiltration, or malware telemetry
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial event; included here only as a company-impact classification, not an attack technique
rootCauses: Provider hardware failure
Provider software/control-plane defect
Provider capacity exhaustion
Provider human error during maintenance
controls: Multi-region/multi-AZ architecture for critical workloads
Vendor SLA and status-page monitoring integration
Documented cloud failover/runbook procedures
ITID-54111.detection: Detection here relies on provider status pages and internal service-health monitoring rather than security telemetry; SOC's role is confirming absence of adversarial indicators.
ITID-54111.response: SOC confirms the event is not attack-related, then hands ownership to IT operations/business continuity for failover execution and vendor liaison; SOC continues monitoring for opportunistic attacks during the outage window.
metrics: Time to confirm non-adversarial cause
Duration of provider-attributed outage
Business services impacted
SLA credit/claim status
ITID-54111.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/vendor-infrastructure continuity event, not an adversary technique. Distinguish carefully from DDoS-driven cloud disruption (ITID-548xx), which is adversarial.

playbook.name: Cloud Provider Outage Due to Third-Party Infrastructure Failure (Non-Attack)
playbook.description: A business-critical cloud service becomes unavailable because the underlying cloud provider suffered an infrastructure failure unrelated to any attack on the company.

steps.title: Confirm service degradation and correlate with provider status page
steps.desc: Validate that internal monitoring alerts (latency spikes, error-rate increases, health-check failures) correspond to a genuine cloud provider outage rather than an internal fault.
steps.guidance: Check the cloud provider's public status/health dashboard and any subscribed status-API feeds. Cross-reference the affected region/availability zone and service names against internally impacted systems.
steps.outcome: Outage is confirmed as provider-side and scoped to specific regions or services, ruling out an internal misconfiguration or attack.
steps.abort: If the provider status page shows no incident, escalate as a potential internal fault or attack investigation instead of a provider outage.
steps.tool: Cloud provider status dashboard / APM monitoring

steps.title: Determine business impact and affected services
steps.desc: Enumerate all internal applications, integrations, and customer-facing services dependent on the impacted cloud region or service.
steps.guidance: Use the service dependency map / CMDB to trace downstream effects; classify by criticality tier.
steps.outcome: A documented impact list exists showing which business functions are degraded or fully down.

steps.title: Activate multi-region or multi-cloud failover where available
steps.desc: Redirect traffic and workloads to a healthy region, availability zone, or secondary cloud provider per the disaster-recovery runbook.
steps.guidance: Trigger DNS failover or load-balancer weight shift; validate failover targets are not also affected by the same provider incident.
steps.outcome: Traffic is served from an unaffected region/provider with acceptable latency and error rates.
steps.abort: If no failover capability exists, proceed directly to vendor escalation and stakeholder communication.

steps.title: Open provider support escalation and notify stakeholders
steps.desc: File a severity-1 ticket with the cloud provider's enterprise support channel and notify internal stakeholders (IT leadership, affected business units, customer support) of the outage and expected impact.
steps.guidance: Reference the account's support SLA/TAM contact for priority handling; issue a holding statement to customer-facing teams.
steps.outcome: Provider has acknowledged the ticket and an internal communication has gone out with impact scope and next-update time.

steps.title: Throttle or queue non-critical workloads to protect failover capacity
steps.desc: Temporarily deprioritize or queue non-essential batch jobs and background processing so failover-site capacity is preserved for business-critical functions.
steps.guidance: Apply rate limits or scheduling holds via the orchestration platform's priority queues.
steps.outcome: Failover-site resource headroom protected for critical workloads.

steps.title: Monitor provider remediation and validate root-cause resolution
steps.desc: Track the provider's incident updates until they confirm the underlying infrastructure fault is resolved.
steps.guidance: Do not fail back until the provider posts a resolved status and internal health checks against the primary region are stable for a sustained period.
steps.outcome: Provider confirms resolution; primary region health checks pass consistently.
steps.abort: If instability recurs, delay failback and continue operating from the failover region.

steps.title: Fail back to primary region and verify data/service integrity
steps.desc: Restore traffic routing to the primary region and verify no data loss or inconsistency occurred during the failover window.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks on any writes that occurred during failover; validate application functionality end-to-end before declaring full recovery.
steps.outcome: Primary region is serving traffic normally with verified data consistency and no residual customer impact.

steps.title: Document outage timeline and evaluate redundancy/SLA posture
steps.desc: Produce a post-incident report covering timeline, business impact, and whether current multi-region/multi-cloud redundancy and vendor SLA terms are adequate.
steps.guidance: Include recommendations such as additional failover automation, stricter SLA negotiation, or diversification of cloud dependency.
steps.outcome: Report is published with actionable redundancy and vendor-management recommendations tracked to completion.

ITID-54112.def: A cloud service disruption affecting company operations that has not yet been classified as either a confirmed third-party infrastructure failure or another specific cloud-disruption cause.
ITID-54112.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cloud service disruptions affecting the company that have not yet been attributed to a specific cause.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported cloud outages pending root-cause confirmation
Ambiguous cloud disruptions where provider vs. company vs. attacker attribution is still under investigation
scopeExcludes: Any disruption once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54111 or the appropriate specific ITID)
ITID-54112.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified; treat as at least Medium pending triage.
ITID-54112.priority: P2 pending triage; adjust once root cause and scope are known.
ITID-54112.escalation: Escalate to on-call SOC analyst for initial triage; reclassify within the incident lifecycle as soon as cause is determined.
indicators: Service-health alerts without an established cause
User-reported outages of cloud-hosted applications
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54112.detection: Relies on initial alerting only; deeper detection coverage is established once the record is reclassified to a specific leaf.
ITID-54112.response: Perform rapid triage to distinguish provider failure, misconfiguration, or attack, then reclassify to the correct Tier-5 leaf as soon as evidence supports it.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Median time-to-reclassification
ITID-54112.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf. This code should not remain the final classification of a closed incident; use it only during initial triage.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud Service Disruption (Infrastructure Context)
playbook.description: A cloud-hosted service experiences an unclassified disruption whose specific cause has not yet been determined at time of detection.

steps.title: Detect and triage the service disruption
steps.desc: Capture initial alerts (monitoring, user reports, synthetic transaction failures) and perform initial triage to characterize the disruption.
steps.guidance: Gather timestamps, affected endpoints, error codes, and geographic/user scope before assuming root cause.
steps.outcome: An initial incident ticket exists with scope, severity, and observed symptoms documented.

steps.title: Classify disruption as provider-side, internal, or malicious
steps.desc: Determine whether the disruption stems from the cloud provider, an internal change/config, or a security event requiring the attack-response track instead.
steps.guidance: Check provider status pages, recent internal change logs, and security monitoring for indicators of compromise.
steps.outcome: Disruption is classified, and the incident is routed to the appropriate specialized playbook if a more specific cause is identified.
steps.abort: If evidence points to malicious activity, halt this playbook and escalate to the relevant security-incident playbook.

steps.title: Isolate or reroute affected workloads
steps.desc: Limit blast radius by isolating the affected component and rerouting traffic to healthy infrastructure where possible.
steps.guidance: Use existing load-balancing, circuit-breaker, or failover mechanisms; avoid destructive changes until cause is better understood.
steps.outcome: Impact is contained to the smallest practical scope while investigation continues.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and open vendor ticket if applicable
steps.desc: Inform affected business units and, if a cloud vendor is implicated, open a support case for parallel investigation.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear impact statement and estimated next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders are informed; vendor case open if relevant.

steps.title: Establish continuous monitoring cadence during investigation
steps.desc: Set up a dedicated monitoring dashboard and update cadence so responders can track evolving symptoms while cause is investigated.
steps.guidance: Include real-time alerting thresholds tuned to the affected component to catch further degradation.
steps.outcome: Active monitoring in place with a clear escalation trigger if symptoms worsen.

steps.title: Identify and remediate root cause
steps.desc: Once classified, apply the appropriate fix — configuration rollback, provider-side remediation wait, or infrastructure repair.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the owning team (cloud ops, network, or vendor) to apply the fix in a controlled manner.
steps.outcome: Root cause is remediated and the disruption source no longer active.

steps.title: Restore full service and validate functionality
steps.desc: Return all rerouted or isolated workloads to normal operation and confirm end-to-end functionality.
steps.guidance: Run smoke tests and monitor error rates for a stabilization period before closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Service operating normally with no elevated error rates.

steps.title: Document findings and refine detection/classification process
steps.desc: Record how quickly the disruption was classified and identify improvements to speed future root-cause identification.
steps.guidance: Focus on monitoring coverage gaps and decision-tree clarity for provider-vs-internal-vs-security triage.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with process improvements tracked.

ITID-54121.def: A disruption of company data-center-hosted critical systems caused by loss of incoming utility grid power to the facility, considered from the data-center infrastructure-outage angle rather than the facility power-continuity angle.
ITID-54121.purpose: Captures the loss of a company-operated or colocated data center's hosted critical systems caused by an external electrical grid failure reaching the facility.
scopeIncludes: Utility grid outage affecting a primary or DR data center
Regional/municipal power grid failure taking a data center offline
Cascading data center service loss following grid loss, independent of whether backup power engaged
scopeExcludes: The specific failure mode of on-site UPS/generator backup power not engaging after a grid loss (see Power Outages and UPS Failures, ITID-54731)
Office/branch-level (non-data-center) power loss (see ITID-5473x)
ITID-54121.severity: High to Critical, scaled by how many business-critical systems are hosted at the affected data center and whether failover capacity exists.
ITID-54121.priority: P1 if a primary data center loses all critical workloads; P2 if DR/secondary capacity absorbs the load.
ITID-54121.escalation: Escalate immediately to data center operations, IT infrastructure leadership, and business continuity; notify executive stakeholders if customer-facing services are affected.
indicators: Facility power-monitoring alarms
Mass simultaneous loss of telemetry from all systems hosted at one data center
Utility provider outage notifications for the facility's grid region
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial infrastructure event
rootCauses: Utility grid failure or load-shedding
Severe weather affecting regional power distribution
Utility equipment failure upstream of the facility
controls: Dual-utility-feed data center design
Automated failover to DR site
Data center power redundancy (N+1/2N)
ITID-54121.detection: Facility power-monitoring systems and infrastructure-monitoring dashboards provide direct, high-confidence detection.
ITID-54121.response: Activate DR/failover procedures immediately; SOC monitors for and rules out any coincident adversarial activity during the outage window.
metrics: Time to failover activation
Duration of data center outage
Number of critical systems impacted
ITID-54121.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique. Distinct from ITID-54731, which addresses the on-site backup-power failure mode rather than the data-center-outage angle.

playbook.name: Power Failure/Grid Outage Affecting Data Center
playbook.description: A utility grid power failure disrupts data center operations, threatening continuity of hosted systems.

steps.title: Confirm grid outage and backup power engagement status
steps.desc: Verify with facilities/data-center operations that the outage originates at the utility grid and check whether generators/UPS have engaged.
steps.guidance: Consult building management system (BMS) alerts and utility outage notifications; confirm generator start and UPS load transfer.
steps.outcome: Outage cause and current backup-power state are confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Assess systems at risk and estimated runtime remaining
steps.desc: Determine which racks/systems are on UPS-only power and estimate remaining runtime before shutdown.
steps.guidance: Review UPS load and battery capacity telemetry; prioritize critical systems for extended runtime.
steps.outcome: A documented list of at-risk systems with estimated time-to-shutdown exists.

steps.title: Fail over critical workloads to a secondary site
steps.desc: Trigger DR failover for critical workloads to a geographically separate data center or cloud region to avoid dependence on generator runtime.
steps.guidance: Follow the site-failover runbook; validate secondary site capacity before cutover.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads are running from an unaffected site.
steps.abort: If failover infrastructure is unavailable, proceed to graceful shutdown sequencing for non-critical systems to conserve backup power for critical ones.

steps.title: Coordinate with facilities and utility provider on restoration timeline
steps.desc: Engage facilities management and the utility provider to obtain an estimated restoration time and confirm generator fuel supply is sufficient.
steps.guidance: Arrange fuel delivery if extended outage is expected; keep leadership informed of ETA.
steps.outcome: Restoration ETA obtained; fuel/generator sustainability confirmed for the expected duration.

steps.title: Confirm utility power restoration and stable generator shutdown
steps.desc: Verify grid power is stably restored before transitioning load back from generators.
steps.guidance: Monitor for voltage fluctuations for a stabilization window before switching load back to utility feed.
steps.outcome: Utility power confirmed stable; generators cleanly disengaged.
steps.abort: If power is unstable, remain on generator/UPS power and delay transition.

steps.title: Inspect UPS/generator equipment for damage from the outage event
steps.desc: Check batteries, transfer switches, and generator components for wear or damage incurred during the extended discharge/run cycle.
steps.guidance: Follow manufacturer post-event inspection checklists; replace any degraded components before the next outage.
steps.outcome: Backup power equipment confirmed healthy and ready for the next event.

steps.title: Fail back workloads and validate data integrity
steps.desc: Return workloads to the primary data center and verify no data loss occurred during the outage window.
steps.guidance: Run integrity checks on databases/transactions active during failover; confirm application health end-to-end.
steps.outcome: Primary site fully operational with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Review backup power adequacy and DR failover performance
steps.desc: Assess whether generator runtime, UPS capacity, and failover speed met business continuity requirements.
steps.guidance: Identify gaps such as insufficient fuel reserves, aging UPS batteries, or failover automation delays; assign remediation owners.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report with prioritized infrastructure investment recommendations.

ITID-54122.def: A shutdown of company data-center-hosted critical systems triggered by failure of the data center's dedicated precision-cooling infrastructure, resulting in thermal protection shutdowns or forced load-shedding.
ITID-54122.purpose: Captures data-center-wide service loss caused by failure of the facility's engineering cooling plant (CRAC/CRAH/chiller), distinct from localized server-room HVAC issues elsewhere in the tree.
scopeIncludes: CRAC/CRAH unit or chiller plant failure at a primary/DR data center
Automated thermal-protection shutdown of racks/rows following cooling loss
Loss of redundant cooling capacity forcing planned load reduction
scopeExcludes: HVAC failures in general office space or smaller server closets (see HVAC and Cooling System Failures, ITID-5474x)
Cooling failure caused by deliberate sabotage (see ITID-54712)
ITID-54122.severity: High to Critical depending on how much of the data center's compute is thermally protected/shut down.
ITID-54122.priority: P1 if automated shutdowns are cascading across racks; P2 if contained to a single row/zone with redundancy absorbing load.
ITID-54122.escalation: Escalate immediately to data center facilities engineering; involve IT infrastructure to manage graceful shutdown/load-shedding of affected systems.
indicators: Building management system (BMS) temperature alarms
Automated hardware thermal-shutdown events across multiple hosts
Rising ambient temperature trend on facility sensors
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial infrastructure event
rootCauses: Chiller/compressor mechanical failure
Cooling plant maintenance deferred or overdue
Cooling capacity undersized for current heat load
controls: Redundant (N+1) cooling design
BMS temperature alerting thresholds
Preventive maintenance program for cooling plant
ITID-54122.detection: BMS and facility environmental sensors provide direct, high-confidence detection well ahead of hardware failure in most cases.
ITID-54122.response: Facilities engineering leads physical remediation; IT infrastructure executes graceful shutdown/migration of at-risk workloads before uncontrolled thermal shutdown occurs.
metrics: Time from first temperature alarm to remediation
Number of hosts subjected to thermal shutdown
Cooling redundancy margin at time of event
ITID-54122.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique. Distinct from ITID-5474x, which covers broader facility HVAC rather than data-center engineering cooling plant failures.

playbook.name: Cooling System Failure Causing Data Center Shutdown
playbook.description: A data center cooling system failure causes rising ambient temperatures that force an emergency shutdown of hosted equipment.

steps.title: Confirm rising temperature alarms and cooling unit fault
steps.desc: Validate BMS/DCIM temperature alarms and identify which cooling units (CRAC/CRAH/chillers) have failed.
steps.guidance: Cross-check rack inlet temperature sensors against thresholds; identify affected zones.
steps.outcome: Cooling fault confirmed and affected zones/racks identified.

steps.title: Assess time-to-thermal-shutdown for affected equipment
steps.desc: Estimate how quickly temperatures will breach safe operating limits for hardware in the affected zone.
steps.guidance: Use manufacturer thermal thresholds and current temperature rise rate to prioritize response.
steps.outcome: Documented time budget before automatic hardware thermal shutdown occurs.

steps.title: Initiate graceful workload migration or shutdown of affected racks
steps.desc: Proactively migrate workloads off the affected racks or perform an orderly shutdown to prevent uncontrolled hardware failure.
steps.guidance: Prioritize critical systems for migration to unaffected zones or DR site; sequence shutdown to minimize data loss.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads relocated or safely shut down before thermal damage occurs.
steps.abort: If temperatures stabilize before shutdown is required, halt the shutdown sequence and continue monitoring.

steps.title: Deploy portable cooling and engage facilities/HVAC vendor
steps.desc: Bring in spot coolers or portable AC units while engaging the HVAC maintenance vendor for emergency repair.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities team on physical access and safety during remediation.
steps.outcome: Temporary cooling is in place limiting further temperature rise; vendor dispatched.

steps.title: Repair or replace failed cooling unit
steps.desc: Complete root-cause repair of the cooling system (compressor, pump, chiller, or control failure).
steps.guidance: Verify repair against manufacturer specifications; test unit under load before declaring fixed.
steps.outcome: Cooling system restored to full rated capacity.

steps.title: Restore workloads and verify hardware health post-thermal event
steps.desc: Bring migrated/shutdown systems back online and check hardware for thermal damage or degraded components.
steps.guidance: Run hardware diagnostics on equipment that experienced elevated temperatures before returning to full production load.
steps.outcome: All systems restored with confirmed hardware health.

steps.title: Confirm sustained temperature stability under full load
steps.desc: Monitor rack inlet/outlet temperatures for a defined stabilization period after full production load resumes.
steps.guidance: Set temporary tighter alert thresholds during the observation window to catch any recurrence early.
steps.outcome: Temperatures remain within normal operating range under full production load.

steps.title: Evaluate cooling redundancy and monitoring thresholds
steps.desc: Assess whether N+1 cooling redundancy, alarm thresholds, and response times were adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend redundancy upgrades or earlier-warning thresholds as needed.
steps.outcome: Report published with cooling infrastructure improvement recommendations.

ITID-54123.def: Physical damage to a company-operated or colocated data center facility itself — from fire, flooding, or a natural disaster — that destroys or renders unusable the building or the equipment housed within it.
ITID-54123.purpose: Captures loss of a data center's structural or physical integrity from fire, flood, or natural disaster, distinguishing facility-destruction events from power/cooling subsystem failures.
scopeIncludes: Fire within the data center hall or supporting plant
Flooding of the data center facility (internal or external source)
Structural damage from earthquake, storm, or other natural disaster affecting a data center specifically
scopeExcludes: Fire/flood/earthquake damage to general office or branch facilities (see Environmental Disruptions, ITID-5472x)
Power or cooling subsystem failure without structural/physical damage (see ITID-54121, ITID-54122)
Deliberate arson/sabotage of the facility (see ITID-54712)
ITID-54123.severity: Critical — physical destruction of a data center typically threatens total loss of hosted systems and, potentially, data not replicated elsewhere.
ITID-54123.priority: P1, always; treat as a full disaster-recovery invocation.
ITID-54123.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, business continuity/DR teams, facilities, and physical safety personnel; life-safety takes precedence over IT recovery.
indicators: Fire alarm/suppression system activation
Flood/water-intrusion sensor alerts
Total, sustained loss of all telemetry from the facility
Emergency services dispatch to the site
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial physical/environmental event
rootCauses: Electrical fault igniting fire
Fire suppression or sprinkler system failure or discharge
Natural disaster (flood, earthquake, severe storm)
controls: Geographically separated DR site
Off-site, immutable backup replication
Fire suppression and flood detection systems
ITID-54123.detection: Physical fire/flood detection systems and total telemetry loss provide unambiguous, high-confidence detection.
ITID-54123.response: Invoke full disaster recovery to the alternate site; SOC's role is limited to confirming no adversarial contribution and supporting continuity of security monitoring from the DR site.
metrics: Time to DR site activation
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) actual vs. target
Data loss relative to Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
ITID-54123.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an environmental/disaster-recovery continuity event, not an adversary technique, unless investigation confirms deliberate sabotage, in which case reclassify to ITID-54712.

playbook.name: Physical Data Center Damage (Fire/Flood/Natural Disaster)
playbook.description: Physical damage from fire, flood, or a natural disaster incapacitates a data center facility.

steps.title: Confirm facility damage and personnel safety status
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation from facilities/emergency services on the nature and extent of physical damage, and verify all personnel are safe.
steps.guidance: Prioritize life-safety confirmation above all IT considerations; coordinate with building emergency response team.
steps.outcome: Personnel safety confirmed; damage scope reported by facilities/emergency responders.

steps.title: Determine facility accessibility and expected downtime
steps.desc: Establish whether the facility is safe to enter and estimate how long it will remain unusable.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with fire marshal/structural engineers as applicable before permitting any IT recovery access.
steps.outcome: Documented accessibility status and rough downtime estimate for the facility.

steps.title: Declare disaster and activate DR site failover
steps.desc: Formally invoke the business continuity/disaster recovery plan and fail over operations to a geographically separate site.
steps.guidance: Follow the documented DR declaration criteria and notification chain to executive leadership.
steps.outcome: DR site is active and serving critical business functions.

steps.title: Secure the damaged site and notify insurance/regulators as needed
steps.desc: Prevent further loss (e.g., power isolation, water extraction) and notify insurance carriers and any regulators requiring disclosure of the outage.
steps.guidance: Engage physical security to prevent unauthorized access to damaged, potentially unsafe equipment.
steps.outcome: Site secured against further loss; required notifications sent.

steps.title: Assess and remediate damaged infrastructure or plan facility replacement
steps.desc: Determine whether the facility can be repaired or must be decommissioned, and plan permanent infrastructure replacement.
steps.guidance: Engage structural/electrical/mechanical contractors for assessment; coordinate hardware replacement procurement.
steps.outcome: A remediation or replacement plan with timeline is established.

steps.title: Recover or securely dispose of damaged hardware and media
steps.desc: Retrieve any salvageable storage media for forensic-grade data recovery and arrange certified destruction of unsalvageable equipment containing sensitive data.
steps.guidance: Follow data-destruction and chain-of-custody procedures for any media leaving the site.
steps.outcome: Salvageable data recovered where possible; damaged media handled per data-security policy.

steps.title: Restore permanent operations and validate data integrity from backups
steps.desc: Rebuild or relocate infrastructure and restore services, validating restored data against last-known-good backups.
steps.guidance: Run full data reconciliation and application validation before decommissioning temporary DR arrangements.
steps.outcome: Permanent (or long-term interim) operations restored with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Conduct post-disaster review of BCP/DR effectiveness
steps.desc: Evaluate how effectively the business continuity and disaster recovery plans performed, and update facility resilience standards.
steps.guidance: Include recommendations on geographic redundancy, environmental hazard mitigation, and DR activation speed.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report with BCP/DR improvement actions tracked to completion.

ITID-54124.def: A data center outage affecting company-hosted critical systems that has not yet been classified to a specific root cause within this group.
ITID-54124.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for data center outages not yet attributed to a specific power, cooling, or physical-damage cause.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported data center outages pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any outage once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54121, 54122, or 54123)
ITID-54124.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified; treat as at least High pending triage given the data-center blast radius.
ITID-54124.priority: P1 pending triage given potential enterprise-wide impact; downgrade once scope is confirmed.
ITID-54124.escalation: Escalate to data center operations and SOC for immediate joint triage.
indicators: Facility-wide telemetry loss without an established cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54124.detection: Relies on initial facility monitoring alerting only; deeper coverage established after reclassification.
ITID-54124.response: Rapidly triage to power, cooling, or physical-damage cause, then reclassify to the correct Tier-5 leaf.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Median time-to-reclassification
ITID-54124.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Data Center Outage
playbook.description: A data center experiences an outage of undetermined cause requiring initial triage and business-continuity response.

steps.title: Confirm outage scope and gather initial diagnostics
steps.desc: Collect monitoring alerts, BMS/DCIM data, and staff reports to determine which systems and services are impacted.
steps.guidance: Check power, cooling, network, and hardware telemetry simultaneously since cause may span multiple domains.
steps.outcome: Documented outage scope with initial diagnostic data collected.

steps.title: Classify probable cause category
steps.desc: Narrow the cause to power, cooling, network, hardware, or human-error category to route to the most specific applicable procedure.
steps.guidance: Use elimination based on available telemetry; escalate to specialist teams (electrical, mechanical, network) as needed.
steps.outcome: Probable cause category identified, enabling targeted response.
steps.abort: If evidence suggests malicious activity, escalate to the security incident-response track.

steps.title: Fail over affected workloads to alternate capacity
steps.desc: Where DR or redundant capacity exists, redirect critical workloads to minimize downtime while root cause is addressed.
steps.guidance: Follow the applicable failover runbook for the affected system tier.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads running from alternate capacity.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and engage relevant specialist teams
steps.desc: Inform business stakeholders of impact and engage the specialist team (facilities, network, hardware vendor) matching the probable cause.
steps.guidance: Provide impact scope and expected next-update time.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed; specialist response engaged.

steps.title: Stand up an incident bridge for cross-domain coordination
steps.desc: Open a running incident bridge/channel bringing together facilities, network, and hardware teams to coordinate diagnosis and containment actions in real time.
steps.guidance: Assign an incident commander to avoid duplicated or conflicting remediation attempts across teams.
steps.outcome: Coordinated response underway with a single incident commander tracking actions.

steps.title: Remediate identified root cause
steps.desc: Apply the fix appropriate to the diagnosed cause (repair, replacement, reconfiguration).
steps.guidance: Validate the fix in isolation before reintroducing production load.
steps.outcome: Root cause resolved and confirmed stable.

steps.title: Restore full operations and verify system health
steps.desc: Return all systems to normal operating state and confirm functionality and data integrity.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive health checks across power, cooling, network, and application layers before closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Data center fully operational with verified health across all monitored domains.

steps.title: Document root cause and improve cross-domain detection
steps.desc: Record findings and identify gaps in monitoring or response coordination across power/cooling/network/hardware domains.
steps.guidance: Recommend consolidated dashboards or runbook improvements to speed future triage.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54131.def: A disruption to company connectivity or transit-dependent services caused by a physical cut or fault in an undersea fiber-optic cable carrying regional or intercontinental internet traffic.
ITID-54131.purpose: Captures company connectivity loss caused by physical damage to undersea telecommunications cables serving a region.
scopeIncludes: Anchor drag, seismic activity, or accidental damage severing an undersea cable route the company's traffic depends on
Regional internet degradation traced to a confirmed undersea cable fault
scopeExcludes: Terrestrial fiber cuts (see Physical Sabotage of IT Infrastructure, ITID-54713, if deliberate; otherwise general connectivity SOPs)
ISP routing failures not caused by physical cable damage (see ITID-54132)
ITID-54131.severity: High if the company has no diverse-path redundancy for the affected region; Medium if alternate routes absorb traffic with added latency.
ITID-54131.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a business-critical region becomes fully unreachable.
ITID-54131.escalation: Escalate to network operations and ISP/carrier account teams; notify business stakeholders in the affected region.
indicators: Elevated latency or packet loss to a specific region confirmed by carrier notices
Public reporting of a confirmed subsea cable fault
Traffic rerouting through alternate, higher-latency paths
vectors: Not applicable — this leaf is typically non-adversarial physical damage
rootCauses: Ship anchor or fishing gear damage
Underwater seismic activity
Cable aging/fault
controls: Multi-carrier, geographically diverse transit paths
Regional traffic failover automation
ITID-54131.detection: Network performance monitoring and carrier status feeds provide reliable detection; root-cause confirmation depends on carrier disclosure.
ITID-54131.response: Network operations reroutes traffic across alternate carriers/paths; SOC monitors for any coincident adversarial activity but does not lead remediation for confirmed physical cable faults.
metrics: Time to reroute traffic
Duration of regional degradation
Business services affected by region
ITID-54131.notes: Included in the T1584.004/TA0040 mapping only for the rare case where sabotage of physical infrastructure is confirmed; the default case is non-adversarial. Cross-reference ITID-40000's detailed infrastructure-disruption techniques rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Undersea Cable Cut Affecting Regional Connectivity
playbook.description: An undersea fiber cable cut degrades or severs regional internet connectivity affecting company operations dependent on that route.

steps.title: Confirm cable cut via carrier/NOC advisories and traffic analysis
steps.desc: Correlate internal latency/packet-loss alerts with carrier network operations center (NOC) advisories reporting an undersea cable fault.
steps.guidance: Check submarine cable operator status notices and transit provider advisories; verify affected routes via traceroute/BGP looking-glass tools.
steps.outcome: Cable cut confirmed as the cause with affected routes identified.
steps.tool: BGP looking glass / carrier NOC advisories

steps.title: Assess business impact on region-dependent services
steps.desc: Identify which offices, customers, or services rely on the affected regional route.
steps.guidance: Use network topology documentation to trace dependency; classify severity by criticality.
steps.outcome: Documented list of impacted regions/services and severity.

steps.title: Reroute traffic via alternate carriers or paths
steps.desc: Engage secondary transit providers or alternate routing paths to restore connectivity around the damaged segment.
steps.guidance: Adjust BGP routing policy/preferences to prefer healthy alternate paths; verify capacity of alternate routes can absorb the shifted traffic.
steps.outcome: Traffic is flowing via alternate paths with acceptable latency.
steps.abort: If no alternate path has sufficient capacity, prioritize traffic for critical services only.

steps.title: Coordinate with carriers on repair ETA and communicate to stakeholders
steps.desc: Obtain repair timeline from the cable operator/carrier and communicate expected duration and impact to affected stakeholders.
steps.guidance: Repair ships and permits can extend timelines to weeks; set expectations accordingly.
steps.outcome: Repair ETA obtained and communicated internally.

steps.title: Monitor for cable repair completion
steps.desc: Track carrier updates until the physical repair is completed and the original route is restored to full capacity.
steps.guidance: Validate restored path performance before relying on it again.
steps.outcome: Cable repair confirmed complete with normal route performance restored.

steps.title: Validate restored capacity meets pre-incident throughput
steps.desc: Run throughput and latency benchmarks on the repaired cable segment to confirm it meets pre-incident performance levels.
steps.guidance: Compare against baseline performance metrics captured before the outage.
steps.outcome: Repaired segment performance confirmed at or above baseline.

steps.title: Restore normal routing and validate performance
steps.desc: Return to primary routing paths and confirm latency/throughput has returned to baseline.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased cutback to avoid re-overloading the primary path.
steps.outcome: Normal routing restored with baseline performance confirmed.

steps.title: Review carrier diversity and route redundancy adequacy
steps.desc: Evaluate whether sufficient carrier and physical path diversity exists to withstand future cable faults.
steps.guidance: Recommend additional carrier contracts or diverse physical routing where gaps are found.
steps.outcome: Report published with connectivity resilience recommendations.

ITID-54132.def: A disruption to company connectivity caused by a routing, peering, or configuration failure at an internet service provider or backbone transit provider the company depends on.
ITID-54132.purpose: Captures company connectivity loss caused by a routing failure at an ISP or internet backbone provider, independent of physical cable damage.
scopeIncludes: Provider-side route flapping, misconfiguration, or peering dispute affecting company traffic
Backbone provider outage independent of a physical cable fault
scopeExcludes: Physical undersea/terrestrial cable damage (see ITID-54131)
Deliberate BGP hijacking (see the detailed technique breakdown under ITID-40000, and the company-impact lone-child stub at ITID-54311)
ITID-54132.severity: High if a single-homed connection or critical region loses all transit; Medium with multi-homed redundancy.
ITID-54132.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if company-wide connectivity is affected.
ITID-54132.escalation: Escalate to network operations and the provider's NOC; invoke secondary ISP failover if available.
indicators: Provider status page or NOC confirms a routing incident
BGP monitoring shows abnormal route withdrawal/flapping without evidence of hijack
Traffic loss correlated to a single upstream provider
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial provider operational failure in the default case
rootCauses: Provider configuration error
Peering dispute or de-peering event
Provider equipment failure
controls: Multi-homed ISP connectivity
BGP route monitoring
Documented ISP failover procedures
ITID-54132.detection: BGP monitoring and provider status communications give timely, moderate-confidence detection.
ITID-54132.response: Network operations engages the provider and activates secondary transit; SOC confirms absence of a deliberate hijack.
metrics: Time to failover to secondary provider
Duration of provider-attributed outage
ITID-54132.notes: Mapping is retained at a light TA0040/T1584.004 level only for traceability to the infrastructure-disruption family; most instances are provider operational failures, not attacks. This is a brief company-impact framing — see ITID-40000 for the detailed BGP technique breakdown.

playbook.name: ISP/Backbone Provider Routing Failure
playbook.description: A routing failure at an ISP or internet backbone provider disrupts connectivity for services dependent on that provider.

steps.title: Confirm routing failure scope and provider status
steps.desc: Correlate observed connectivity loss with the provider's status advisories and independent route-monitoring services.
steps.guidance: Use tools like route monitoring/looking-glass services and traceroute from multiple vantage points to isolate the failure to the provider's network.
steps.outcome: Routing failure confirmed as provider-side with affected prefixes/routes identified.
steps.abort: If routing anomalies suggest hijacking rather than failure, escalate to the BGP hijacking playbook.

steps.title: Assess impact on dependent services and customers
steps.desc: Determine which internal and customer-facing services are degraded due to loss of the affected route.
steps.guidance: Cross-check with network dependency documentation.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Rule out BGP hijacking as an alternate cause
steps.desc: Check route origin/AS-path data to confirm the failure is a legitimate routing fault rather than a malicious BGP hijack.
steps.guidance: Compare current AS-path and prefix origination against known-good baselines using RPKI validation and route monitoring services.
steps.outcome: Hijacking ruled out, confirming this is a routing failure rather than an attack.
steps.abort: If AS-path or origin anomalies indicate hijacking, escalate immediately to the BGP hijacking response track.

steps.title: Failover to secondary ISP/transit provider
steps.desc: Shift traffic to a redundant ISP or transit link to restore connectivity.
steps.guidance: Adjust BGP preferences/route policy to prefer the healthy transit provider; confirm capacity is sufficient.
steps.outcome: Connectivity restored via alternate provider.

steps.title: Escalate with the affected provider and monitor advisories
steps.desc: Open a priority ticket with the provider's NOC and monitor for updates on the routing failure.
steps.guidance: Reference account SLA for priority handling.
steps.outcome: Provider engaged and providing status updates.

steps.title: Confirm provider routing fix and stability
steps.desc: Wait for provider confirmation of resolution and validate stable routing before relying on the primary path again.
steps.guidance: Monitor route stability for a sustained period post-fix.
steps.outcome: Provider routing confirmed stable.

steps.title: Restore primary routing and validate performance
steps.desc: Return traffic to the primary provider path and confirm normal performance.
steps.guidance: Perform gradual cutback and monitor for regression.
steps.outcome: Primary routing restored with normal performance confirmed.

steps.title: Evaluate ISP redundancy and failover automation
steps.desc: Assess whether failover speed and multi-provider redundancy met business continuity needs.
steps.guidance: Recommend automation or additional provider diversity as needed.
steps.outcome: Report published with tracked improvement recommendations.

ITID-54133.def: An internet backbone disruption affecting company connectivity that has not yet been classified as a physical cable fault or a provider routing failure.
ITID-54133.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for internet backbone disruptions affecting the company that have not yet been attributed to cable damage or provider routing failure.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported backbone connectivity incidents pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any incident once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54131 or 54132)
ITID-54133.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54133.escalation: Escalate to network operations for initial triage.
indicators: Regional/provider connectivity degradation without an established cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54133.detection: Relies on initial network performance monitoring only.
ITID-54133.response: Triage to cable-fault or routing-failure cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54133.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Internet Backbone Disruption
playbook.description: Connectivity is disrupted by an internet backbone issue whose specific cause (cable cut, routing failure, or other) has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm backbone-level connectivity disruption
steps.desc: Collect internal monitoring alerts and external route/looking-glass data to confirm the disruption originates at the internet backbone level rather than internally.
steps.guidance: Check multiple external vantage points and carrier advisories to distinguish backbone issues from local network faults.
steps.outcome: Disruption confirmed as backbone-related with initial scope documented.

steps.title: Narrow probable cause and impacted routes
steps.desc: Determine whether the disruption is likely a physical cable fault, provider routing failure, or hijacking, to route to the appropriate specific procedure.
steps.guidance: Escalate to the more specific playbook (cable cut, ISP routing failure, or BGP hijack) once cause is identified.
steps.outcome: Probable cause identified or incident continues under general handling if cause remains unclear.
steps.abort: If hijacking indicators are found, escalate immediately to the BGP hijacking response track.

steps.title: Reroute via alternate carriers/paths
steps.desc: Shift traffic to alternate transit providers or paths to restore connectivity while the underlying cause is resolved.
steps.guidance: Adjust routing policy and validate alternate path capacity.
steps.outcome: Connectivity restored via alternate path.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and engage carrier support
steps.desc: Communicate impact to stakeholders and open tickets with relevant carriers for parallel investigation.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed; carrier engagement underway.

steps.title: Track service-level impact continuously until root cause is isolated
steps.desc: Maintain a live dashboard of affected-route performance and downstream service health while carriers investigate.
steps.guidance: Set alert thresholds to detect further degradation or improvement automatically.
steps.outcome: Continuous visibility into disruption status maintained throughout the incident.

steps.title: Confirm resolution of the underlying backbone issue
steps.desc: Track carrier/provider confirmation that the backbone fault has been resolved.
steps.guidance: Validate stability before restoring primary routing.
steps.outcome: Backbone issue confirmed resolved.

steps.title: Restore primary routing and validate performance
steps.desc: Return to primary routing path and confirm normal connectivity performance.
steps.guidance: Monitor closely during cutback for regressions.
steps.outcome: Normal connectivity restored.

steps.title: Document incident and refine backbone-issue triage process
steps.desc: Capture lessons on how quickly the cause was identified and whether routing diversity was adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend process or infrastructure improvements as applicable.
steps.outcome: Report published with tracked follow-up actions.

ITID-54141.def: A disruption to company web or API delivery caused by a CDN provider pushing an erroneous configuration (e.g., a bad edge rule, certificate, or routing change) across its network.
ITID-54141.purpose: Captures widespread outage of company-facing web/API services caused by a configuration error made by the CDN provider, not by the company or an attacker.
scopeIncludes: CDN provider-wide configuration push causing 5xx errors or unreachability for company domains
CDN edge rule/WAF misfire caused by a provider-side change, not a company change
scopeExcludes: Company-caused CDN misconfiguration (see Accidental Misconfigurations, ITID-54521)
CDN provider hardware/infrastructure failure unrelated to a configuration push (see ITID-54142)
CDN targeted by DDoS (see ITID-54841)
ITID-54141.severity: High if all company-facing web/API traffic depends on the affected CDN; Medium if only a subset of properties are affected.
ITID-54141.priority: P1 if customer-facing revenue services are down; P2 otherwise.
ITID-54141.escalation: Escalate to the CDN provider's incident channel and internal web operations; communicate to customer support teams for external messaging.
indicators: Sudden, correlated 5xx/timeout errors across multiple company properties on the same CDN
CDN provider status page confirms a configuration-related incident
Error onset immediately follows a known provider maintenance window
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial provider operational error
rootCauses: Provider deployment/change-management failure
Provider configuration validation gap
controls: Multi-CDN failover architecture
Synthetic monitoring of CDN-fronted endpoints
Vendor status-page integration
ITID-54141.detection: Synthetic uptime monitoring and provider status communications give fast, high-confidence detection.
ITID-54141.response: Web operations engages the CDN provider and, where available, fails over to a secondary CDN or origin-direct routing; SOC confirms no coincident attack.
metrics: Time to detect and confirm provider cause
Duration of outage
Revenue/traffic impact
ITID-54141.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a vendor operational/configuration continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: CDN Provider Configuration Error Causing Widespread Outage
playbook.description: A configuration error at the content delivery network provider causes widespread degradation or outage of content and application delivery.

steps.title: Confirm CDN-origin configuration fault via provider status and edge diagnostics
steps.desc: Correlate elevated 4xx/5xx error rates, cache-miss spikes, or edge routing anomalies with the CDN provider's status page or incident advisories.
steps.guidance: Query edge nodes across multiple geographic points-of-presence to confirm the issue is provider-wide rather than localized.
steps.outcome: Fault confirmed as a CDN provider-side configuration error with affected regions/POPs identified.

steps.title: Determine impacted assets and customer-facing severity
steps.desc: Identify which sites, APIs, or static assets are served through the affected CDN configuration and assess customer impact.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference CDN distribution mappings against the service catalog.
steps.outcome: Documented impact list with severity ranking.

steps.title: Bypass CDN or switch to secondary CDN provider
steps.desc: Route traffic directly to origin servers or fail over to a secondary CDN provider to restore content delivery.
steps.guidance: Ensure origin infrastructure can handle the additional direct load before fully bypassing the CDN; use DNS or multi-CDN load-balancing controls.
steps.outcome: Content delivery restored via origin or secondary CDN with acceptable performance.
steps.abort: If origin cannot absorb the load, throttle traffic and prioritize critical endpoints only.

steps.title: Escalate to CDN provider support and request configuration rollback
steps.desc: Open a priority ticket requesting the provider identify and roll back the faulty configuration change.
steps.guidance: Provide affected zone/config identifiers and timestamps to speed provider triage.
steps.outcome: Provider acknowledges the issue and begins rollback procedures.

steps.title: Confirm provider configuration rollback and edge cache health
steps.desc: Verify the provider has rolled back the faulty configuration and edge nodes are serving content correctly.
steps.guidance: Sample multiple POPs to confirm consistent behavior post-rollback.
steps.outcome: Configuration rollback confirmed; edge nodes serving correctly across sampled POPs.

steps.title: Purge and rebuild affected caches
steps.desc: Invalidate and repopulate CDN caches that may hold content served under the faulty configuration.
steps.guidance: Use the provider's cache-purge API and validate refreshed content matches origin.
steps.outcome: Caches purged and rebuilt with correct content confirmed at the edge.

steps.title: Restore primary CDN routing and validate end-to-end performance
steps.desc: Return traffic to the primary CDN path and confirm latency, error rate, and cache-hit ratio are back to baseline.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased traffic shift with continuous monitoring.
steps.outcome: Primary CDN routing restored with baseline performance confirmed.

steps.title: Review multi-CDN resilience and provider change-management visibility
steps.desc: Assess whether multi-CDN failover was fast enough and whether visibility into provider-side configuration changes should be improved contractually.
steps.guidance: Recommend SLA clauses for change notification or additional CDN redundancy.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked resilience recommendations.

ITID-54142.def: A disruption to company web or API delivery caused by failure of the CDN provider's own edge infrastructure (points of presence, hardware, or internal network), independent of any specific configuration change.
ITID-54142.purpose: Captures widespread outage of company-facing web/API services caused by hardware or infrastructure failure within the CDN provider itself, distinct from a configuration push.
scopeIncludes: CDN edge node or POP hardware failure
CDN provider internal network or peering failure
scopeExcludes: Configuration-push-caused outages (see ITID-54141)
CDN targeted by DDoS (see ITID-54841)
ITID-54142.severity: High if the affected POPs serve the company's primary user base; Medium if geographically limited.
ITID-54142.priority: P1 if customer-facing revenue services are down; P2 otherwise.
ITID-54142.escalation: Escalate to the CDN provider's incident channel and internal web operations.
indicators: Elevated errors/latency limited to users in specific geographic regions
CDN provider status page confirms an infrastructure incident unrelated to a recent change
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial provider infrastructure failure
rootCauses: Provider hardware failure
Provider internal network/peering failure
Provider capacity exhaustion
controls: Multi-CDN failover architecture
Synthetic monitoring by geographic region
ITID-54142.detection: Synthetic uptime monitoring segmented by geography, plus provider status communications, give reliable detection.
ITID-54142.response: Web operations fails over to a secondary CDN or alternate POP routing where available; SOC confirms no coincident attack.
metrics: Time to failover
Duration of outage
Geographic scope of impact
ITID-54142.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a vendor infrastructure continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: CDN Provider's Own Infrastructure Failure (Non-Attack)
playbook.description: The CDN provider's own infrastructure suffers a failure unrelated to any attack, degrading content delivery for dependent services.

steps.title: Confirm CDN infrastructure failure via provider status page
steps.desc: Validate that observed content-delivery degradation matches a confirmed infrastructure incident on the provider's public status page.
steps.guidance: Check for correlated regional outages reported by other customers of the same CDN provider on independent monitoring communities.
steps.outcome: Failure confirmed as provider infrastructure issue, not internal or malicious.

steps.title: Assess scope of affected regions and services
steps.desc: Determine which geographic regions and which services depend on the affected CDN infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Use CDN distribution and traffic analytics to scope impact.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected regions/services.

steps.title: Activate multi-CDN or direct-origin failover
steps.desc: Shift affected traffic to a secondary CDN provider or serve directly from origin for critical content.
steps.guidance: Validate secondary CDN/origin capacity handles the shifted load without introducing new bottlenecks.
steps.outcome: Traffic served through an unaffected path with acceptable performance.

steps.title: Engage provider support and monitor incident updates
steps.desc: File a support case and track the provider's public/private incident updates for resolution progress.
steps.guidance: Use enterprise support/TAM channel for priority visibility.
steps.outcome: Provider engaged; regular status updates being received.

steps.title: Confirm provider infrastructure fully restored
steps.desc: Wait for the provider's confirmation that the underlying infrastructure fault is resolved across all affected regions.
steps.guidance: Validate via independent synthetic checks rather than relying solely on the provider's self-reported status.
steps.outcome: Provider infrastructure confirmed stable and fully restored.

steps.title: Fail back to primary CDN and validate performance
steps.desc: Return traffic to the primary CDN provider and confirm performance metrics match baseline.
steps.guidance: Use a gradual cutback with continuous monitoring to catch any residual instability.
steps.outcome: Primary CDN restored with baseline performance confirmed.

steps.title: Validate content integrity across restored edge caches
steps.desc: Spot-check content served from the primary CDN post-restoration to confirm no corruption or stale content persists.
steps.guidance: Compare edge-served content checksums against origin.
steps.outcome: Content integrity confirmed across sampled edge nodes.

steps.title: Evaluate CDN redundancy strategy and vendor SLA terms
steps.desc: Assess whether current multi-CDN posture and vendor SLA commitments are sufficient for this class of provider outage.
steps.guidance: Recommend SLA renegotiation or additional redundancy investment as warranted.
steps.outcome: Report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54143.def: A CDN-related disruption affecting company web/API delivery that has not yet been classified as a provider configuration error or a provider infrastructure failure.
ITID-54143.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for CDN disruptions affecting the company that have not yet been attributed to a configuration error or an infrastructure failure.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported CDN disruptions pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any disruption once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54141 or 54142)
ITID-54143.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54143.priority: P2 pending triage; P1 if customer-facing revenue services are already confirmed down.
ITID-54143.escalation: Escalate to web operations and the CDN provider for initial triage.
indicators: Elevated errors on CDN-fronted properties without an established cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54143.detection: Relies on initial synthetic monitoring only.
ITID-54143.response: Triage to configuration-error or infrastructure-failure cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
