ITID-54143.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General CDN Disruption (Infrastructure Context)
playbook.description: A CDN-related disruption of undetermined specific cause degrades content or application delivery.

steps.title: Detect and characterize the CDN disruption
steps.desc: Gather monitoring data (error rates, latency, cache performance) to characterize the nature and scope of the disruption.
steps.guidance: Check synthetic transactions across multiple regions to confirm scope before assuming cause.
steps.outcome: Disruption characterized with initial scope documented.

steps.title: Classify probable cause as configuration error, infrastructure failure, or attack
steps.desc: Narrow the likely cause to route the incident to the most applicable specific procedure.
steps.guidance: Check provider status pages and recent configuration change logs; review for volumetric attack indicators.
steps.outcome: Probable cause identified, or continued handling under general procedure if unclear.
steps.abort: If attack indicators (e.g., volumetric traffic spike from many sources) are found, escalate to the appropriate DDoS response track.

steps.title: Reroute traffic to alternate CDN or origin
steps.desc: Shift traffic to a secondary CDN or origin path to restore service while the cause is investigated.
steps.guidance: Validate alternate path capacity before full cutover.
steps.outcome: Service restored via alternate path.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and engage provider support
steps.desc: Communicate impact to stakeholders and open a support case with the CDN provider for parallel investigation.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed; provider engaged.

steps.title: Maintain continuous monitoring during investigation
steps.desc: Set up a dedicated monitoring dashboard tracking edge error rates and cache performance while the cause is investigated.
steps.guidance: Configure alerting thresholds to detect further degradation or confirm improvement.
steps.outcome: Active monitoring in place with a clear escalation trigger.

steps.title: Remediate the identified root cause
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix based on classification — configuration correction, provider-side repair, or attack mitigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the responsible team or provider to apply the fix.
steps.outcome: Root cause resolved and confirmed stable.

steps.title: Restore normal CDN routing and validate performance
steps.desc: Return to normal CDN configuration/routing and confirm performance has returned to baseline.
steps.guidance: Monitor for regression during and after cutback.
steps.outcome: Normal performance confirmed.

steps.title: Document findings and refine CDN-disruption triage process
steps.desc: Capture how quickly the disruption was classified and identify improvements to speed future response.
steps.guidance: Focus on monitoring/detection gaps and escalation clarity.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvements.

ITID-54211.def: A ransomware attack in which the adversary compromises a domain controller or abuses Group Policy Objects to deploy encryption payloads across the entire domain-joined estate simultaneously, tracked at the enterprise-wide business-impact level.
ITID-54211.purpose: Captures the specific enterprise-wide ransomware pattern in which an adversary compromises Active Directory (domain controller or Group Policy) to push encryption enterprise-wide from a single point of control.
scopeIncludes: Malicious GPO pushing a ransomware payload/script to all domain-joined endpoints
Ransomware staged and triggered from a compromised domain controller
Domain-wide, near-simultaneous encryption onset consistent with AD-based distribution
scopeExcludes: The malware/technical delivery mechanics of the ransomware family itself (see ITID-311xx)
Ransomware confined to a single business unit without domain-wide GPO abuse (see ITID-54212)
Human-operated targeted deployment without domain-wide scope (see ITID-31141)
ITID-54211.severity: Critical — domain-wide, GPO-driven deployment typically indicates total loss of endpoint availability enterprise-wide with minimal warning.
ITID-54211.priority: P1, always; invoke enterprise crisis management immediately.
ITID-54211.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, executive leadership, legal, and crisis management; isolate domain controllers and disable GPO replication as an emergency containment step.
indicators: Near-simultaneous encryption onset across geographically dispersed endpoints
New or modified GPOs pushing scripts/executables shortly before encryption
Domain controller logs showing anomalous authentication or GPO edits from a privileged account
vectors: Compromised domain admin credentials used to create/modify a malicious GPO
Lateral movement to a domain controller followed by scripted mass deployment
rootCauses: Insufficient tiering/segmentation of privileged access to domain controllers
Lack of monitoring on GPO creation/modification
Delayed detection of initial domain compromise
controls: Tiered administration model (Active Directory tiering)
GPO change monitoring and alerting
Privileged access workstation (PAW) enforcement for DC administration
ITID-54211.detection: Domain controller audit logs and GPO change monitoring provide strong detection when properly instrumented; encryption telemetry confirms scope quickly.
ITID-54211.response: Immediately isolate domain controllers, disable affected GPOs, and invoke the enterprise ransomware playbook; do not restore from backups until the domain is confirmed clean of persistence.
metrics: Time from initial DC compromise to encryption onset
Percentage of domain-joined endpoints encrypted
Time to domain controller isolation
detections: Domain controller privileged logon anomaly detection
ITID-54211.notes: Scoped to the company-wide business-impact angle (enterprise blast radius via AD compromise); the ransomware family's technical delivery and encryption mechanics are covered under ITID-311xx and should be cross-referenced, not restated here.

playbook.name: Domain-Wide Ransomware Deployment via Compromised Domain Controller/GPO
playbook.description: An attacker compromises a domain controller and abuses Group Policy to deploy ransomware domain-wide, encrypting systems across the enterprise.

steps.title: Confirm mass encryption activity and GPO abuse as the deployment vector
steps.desc: Correlate EDR/SIEM alerts of simultaneous mass file encryption across many hosts with evidence of malicious GPO changes or SYSVOL script pushes from a compromised domain controller.
steps.guidance: Check domain controller security/GPO event logs for unauthorized policy edits, new scheduled tasks, or startup scripts pushed enterprise-wide.
steps.outcome: Confirmed that ransomware was deployed via compromised DC/GPO, with the malicious policy object identified.
steps.tool: EDR / SIEM / Active Directory audit logs

steps.title: Determine scope of encrypted and at-risk systems
steps.desc: Enumerate hosts already encrypted, hosts that received the malicious GPO but have not yet executed it, and hosts still unaffected.
steps.guidance: Use EDR telemetry and AD group policy application logs to map affected OUs.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of encrypted, at-risk, and unaffected systems.

steps.title: Isolate the compromised domain controller(s) and disable the malicious GPO immediately
steps.desc: Take the affected domain controller(s) off the network or into a quarantine VLAN and disable/unlink the malicious Group Policy Object to halt further deployment.
steps.guidance: If multiple DCs exist, verify replication status before isolating to avoid inconsistent AD state; prioritize halting GPO propagation above all else.
steps.outcome: Malicious GPO deactivated; no further hosts receive the ransomware payload.

steps.title: Enforce enterprise-wide network segmentation to halt lateral spread
steps.desc: Isolate affected network segments and disable unnecessary SMB/RPC/admin-share traffic to prevent further lateral movement.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with network team to apply emergency ACLs/VLAN isolation on affected subnets.
steps.outcome: Lateral movement halted; unaffected segments protected.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence and engage Legal/Law Enforcement
steps.desc: Capture memory/disk images of the compromised DC and affected hosts before remediation, and notify Legal and law enforcement per the ransomware response policy.
steps.guidance: Follow chain-of-custody procedures; do not pay any ransom demand — coordinate any negotiation decisions solely through Legal/executive leadership.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved; Legal and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Rebuild domain controllers from known-clean state and rotate all privileged credentials
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised DCs from trusted media or a verified clean backup, and force rotation of all domain admin, service account, and krbtgt credentials (double krbtgt reset).
steps.guidance: Follow Microsoft's AD forest-recovery guidance; verify no persistence (malicious GPOs, scheduled tasks, golden tickets) remains before reconnecting to the network.
steps.outcome: Domain controllers rebuilt clean; all privileged credentials rotated.

steps.title: Remove ransomware payloads and persistence from all affected endpoints
steps.desc: Sweep all encrypted and at-risk endpoints for ransomware binaries, persistence mechanisms, and remaining malicious GPO artifacts before reintroducing them to the network.
steps.guidance: Use EDR-driven remediation and reimage where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.outcome: All affected endpoints confirmed free of ransomware and persistence mechanisms.

steps.title: Restore encrypted systems from verified clean backups
steps.desc: Restore data on encrypted systems from backups verified to be free of ransomware/backdoors, prioritizing critical business systems.
steps.guidance: Scan backup images in an isolated environment before restoring to production; validate data integrity post-restore.
steps.outcome: Critical systems restored from clean backups with verified data integrity.
steps.abort: If backups are also found compromised, escalate to the backup-encryption-specific recovery procedure and consider alternate data-recovery options.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review of AD hardening and detection gaps
steps.desc: Document the attack chain, the domain-admin compromise vector, and gaps in AD monitoring/hardening that allowed enterprise-wide GPO abuse.
steps.guidance: Recommend tiered administration model, GPO change alerting, and privileged access management improvements.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with prioritized AD security hardening actions tracked to completion.

ITID-54212.def: A ransomware attack that achieves near-simultaneous impact across multiple, organizationally distinct business units or subsidiaries — whether through shared infrastructure, replicated access, or independent parallel compromises — tracked at the enterprise-wide business-impact level.
ITID-54212.purpose: Captures ransomware that impacts multiple business units or subsidiaries at once without necessarily relying on a single AD/GPO compromise point, distinguishing multi-entity scope from the AD-driven mechanism in the sibling leaf.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware spreading across separately managed subsidiaries via shared trust relationships (e.g., cross-forest trusts, shared VPN, shared MSP)
Coordinated, near-simultaneous ransomware impact across business units that do not share a single AD domain
scopeExcludes: Single-domain, GPO-driven mass deployment (see ITID-54211)
MSP-originated multi-client ransomware spread (see ITID-54921)
ITID-54212.severity: Critical — multi-entity impact multiplies recovery complexity and stakeholder/communications burden.
ITID-54212.priority: P1, always; coordinate response across all affected business units simultaneously.
ITID-54212.escalation: Escalate to CISO, executive leadership, and each affected business unit's leadership; establish a unified incident command structure spanning entities.
indicators: Encryption onset in multiple subsidiaries within a short window
Shared indicators of compromise (same ransomware variant, C2 infrastructure) across business units
Evidence of a shared trust or connectivity path exploited to cross entity boundaries
vectors: Abuse of cross-forest/cross-domain trust relationships
Lateral movement via shared infrastructure (shared VPN concentrators, shared identity provider)
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation between business units/subsidiaries
Shared credentials or identity federation without adequate boundary controls
controls: Segmentation between business units and subsidiaries
Cross-domain trust monitoring
Federated identity anomaly detection
ITID-54212.detection: Cross-entity SIEM correlation is required to recognize the multi-unit pattern; individual business units may otherwise investigate in isolation and miss the shared cause.
ITID-54212.response: Stand up a single incident command spanning all affected entities; contain shared trust paths before independent per-unit remediation.
metrics: Number of business units/subsidiaries affected
Time to establish unified incident command
Time to sever shared trust paths
ITID-54212.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54211 by scope mechanism: this leaf is about multi-entity blast radius via shared trust/infrastructure, not single-domain GPO abuse. Malware-family mechanics are covered under ITID-311xx.

playbook.name: Ransomware Simultaneously Deployed Across Multiple Business Units/Subsidiaries
playbook.description: Ransomware is deployed near-simultaneously across multiple business units or subsidiaries, indicating centralized or federated attack infrastructure and requiring coordinated multi-entity response.

steps.title: Confirm coordinated multi-entity encryption event
steps.desc: Correlate near-simultaneous encryption alerts across multiple business units/subsidiaries to confirm a coordinated attack rather than independent incidents.
steps.guidance: Compare ransom notes, encryption extensions, and timestamps across entities; check for shared infrastructure (identity federation, shared VPN, common MSP) enabling cross-entity spread.
steps.outcome: Coordinated deployment confirmed with the shared propagation vector identified.

steps.title: Map affected entities, shared infrastructure, and encryption scope
steps.desc: Build a consolidated view of which business units/subsidiaries are affected and what shared identity or network infrastructure connects them.
steps.guidance: Engage each affected entity's local IT/security team to gather scope data centrally.
steps.outcome: Consolidated cross-entity impact map produced.

steps.title: Sever shared trust relationships and isolate each entity's network
steps.desc: Disable cross-entity trust relationships (shared AD forests/domains, VPN interconnects, shared identity providers) and isolate each affected entity's network to stop further cross-propagation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate simultaneous isolation actions across entities to avoid the attacker pivoting to a not-yet-isolated unit.
steps.outcome: Cross-entity propagation halted; each affected network isolated.

steps.title: Stand up a centralized incident command for cross-entity coordination
steps.desc: Establish a single incident command structure coordinating response across all affected business units/subsidiaries to ensure consistent decisions on containment, communication, and negotiation stance.
steps.guidance: Include representation from each entity's IT/security leadership, corporate Legal, and executive sponsor.
steps.outcome: Unified incident command in place directing coordinated response.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage Legal/Law Enforcement across all entities
steps.desc: Coordinate forensic evidence preservation and law-enforcement/Legal notification consistently across all affected entities.
steps.guidance: Avoid independent ransom-negotiation attempts by individual subsidiaries; centralize decision-making through corporate Legal.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and Legal/law enforcement engaged for the full multi-entity incident.

steps.title: Eliminate ransomware and shared attacker infrastructure across all entities
steps.desc: Remove ransomware payloads and any shared attacker persistence (compromised shared credentials, federated identity abuse) across every affected entity in a coordinated sequence.
steps.guidance: Rotate all shared/federated credentials simultaneously to prevent re-entry via one still-compromised entity.
steps.outcome: All entities confirmed free of ransomware and attacker persistence.

steps.title: Restore each entity from verified clean backups in a coordinated sequence
steps.desc: Restore affected systems entity-by-entity from verified clean backups, re-establishing cross-entity trust only after each entity is confirmed clean.
steps.guidance: Sequence restoration to avoid re-introducing compromise via a still-recovering entity's shared connections.
steps.outcome: All entities restored with data integrity verified before trust relationships are re-established.

steps.title: Review shared-infrastructure risk and cross-entity incident coordination
steps.desc: Document how shared infrastructure enabled multi-entity spread and evaluate the effectiveness of cross-entity incident command.
steps.guidance: Recommend segmentation of shared trust relationships and improved cross-entity incident-response playbooks.
steps.outcome: Report published with prioritized cross-entity resilience actions.

ITID-54213.def: An enterprise-wide ransomware attack affecting company operations that has not yet been classified as domain/GPO-driven or multi-entity-driven.
ITID-54213.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for enterprise-wide ransomware attacks not yet attributed to a specific spread mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed enterprise-wide ransomware events pending mechanism confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once mechanism is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54211 or 54212)
ITID-54213.severity: Critical pending triage, consistent with enterprise-wide scope.
ITID-54213.priority: P1, always, regardless of pending reclassification.
ITID-54213.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO and executive leadership; do not delay containment pending root-cause classification.
indicators: Encryption impacting a broad, enterprise-wide footprint without a confirmed spread mechanism
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
Enterprise ransomware containment procedures
ITID-54213.detection: Relies on initial encryption/behavioral detection; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54213.response: Contain immediately using the enterprise ransomware playbook while triage determines the specific spread mechanism for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Time to containment regardless of classification
ITID-54213.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Enterprise-Wide Ransomware Attack
playbook.description: An enterprise-wide ransomware attack encrypts systems broadly across the organization with the specific deployment vector not yet determined.

steps.title: Confirm enterprise-wide scope of ransomware encryption
steps.desc: Correlate encryption alerts, ransom notes, and EDR detections across multiple systems to confirm the attack spans the enterprise rather than a single system.
steps.guidance: Check for a common ransomware family/extension and ransom note content across affected hosts.
steps.outcome: Enterprise-wide scope confirmed with ransomware family identified where possible.

steps.title: Determine deployment vector and scope of encrypted vs at-risk systems
steps.desc: Investigate initial access and propagation method (phishing, exploited vulnerability, compromised credentials, GPO abuse) and map encrypted versus still-at-risk systems.
steps.guidance: Use EDR timeline analysis and network logs to trace the propagation path.
steps.outcome: Deployment vector identified and scope documented.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems and segment the network enterprise-wide
steps.desc: Disconnect encrypted and at-risk systems from the network and apply emergency network segmentation to halt further spread.
steps.guidance: Prioritize isolating systems still executing encryption processes; disable unnecessary lateral-movement pathways (SMB, RDP, admin shares).
steps.outcome: Further encryption halted; spread contained.

steps.title: Isolate backups and preserve forensic evidence
steps.desc: Immediately disconnect or air-gap backup systems from the production network to protect them from encryption, and preserve forensic evidence on affected hosts.
steps.guidance: Verify backup isolation before any other remediation activity, since backups are a common secondary target.
steps.outcome: Backups protected; forensic evidence preserved with chain of custody.

steps.title: Engage Legal and Law Enforcement; do not engage ransom negotiation independently
steps.desc: Notify Legal, executive leadership, and law enforcement per the ransomware response policy before any consideration of ransom-related communication.
steps.guidance: All negotiation/payment decisions must go through executive leadership and Legal — no unilateral payment.
steps.outcome: Legal and law enforcement engaged; no unauthorized ransom contact made.

steps.title: Eliminate ransomware payloads and attacker persistence enterprise-wide
steps.desc: Remove ransomware binaries and any persistence mechanisms (backdoors, scheduled tasks, compromised credentials) from all affected systems.
steps.guidance: Rotate all potentially exposed credentials; reimage systems where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed free of ransomware and persistence.

steps.title: Restore systems from verified clean backups in priority order
steps.desc: Restore business-critical systems first from backups verified free of ransomware, validating data integrity before returning to production.
steps.guidance: Scan backup images in an isolated sandbox prior to restoration.
steps.outcome: Systems restored in priority order with verified integrity.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review of initial access and enterprise resilience
steps.desc: Document the full attack chain and identify security control gaps (patching, segmentation, backup isolation, detection) that allowed enterprise-wide impact.
steps.guidance: Recommend prioritized remediation actions with owners and timelines.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked remediation actions.

ITID-54221.def: A ransomware attack that encrypts or otherwise disrupts systems within an industrial control system or operational technology environment (e.g., SCADA, PLC-supporting Windows hosts, HMIs), tracked for its critical-infrastructure targeting angle.
ITID-54221.purpose: Captures ransomware reaching industrial control system (ICS/OT) environments, where impact extends beyond IT availability into physical process safety and requires OT-specific response coordination.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware reaching IT/OT boundary systems that then propagates into OT-adjacent hosts
Encryption of engineering workstations, historians, or HMIs supporting a physical process
Ransomware-driven forced shutdown of an OT process as a precautionary safety measure
scopeExcludes: Ransomware confined entirely to corporate IT with no OT-adjacent exposure (see ITID-54211/54212)
The malware family's technical mechanics (see ITID-311xx)
ITID-54221.severity: Critical — any OT-adjacent ransomware impact carries potential physical safety consequences beyond data/availability loss.
ITID-54221.priority: P1, always; treat as a joint cyber-physical safety incident.
ITID-54221.escalation: Escalate immediately to OT/engineering leadership, safety officers, and executive leadership in parallel with SOC; consider regulatory notification obligations for critical infrastructure operators.
indicators: Ransom notes or encrypted files appearing on engineering workstations or historians
Unexpected process shutdowns or HMI unavailability coincident with IT ransomware activity
IT/OT boundary firewall logs showing lateral movement toward OT segments
vectors: Lateral movement from compromised IT network across an inadequately segmented IT/OT boundary
Compromise of a jump host or engineering laptop with dual IT/OT connectivity
rootCauses: Weak or flat IT/OT network segmentation
OT systems running unsupported operating systems unable to run modern endpoint protection
controls: IT/OT network segmentation with unidirectional gateways where feasible
OT-specific asset inventory and monitoring
Emergency OT isolation procedures
ITID-54221.detection: IT-side detection is often mature; OT-side detection typically has significant gaps and depends on IT/OT boundary monitoring and physical process alarms.
ITID-54221.response: Prioritize physical safety: initiate safe shutdown procedures for at-risk processes before IT remediation; coordinate jointly between SOC and OT engineering throughout.
metrics: Time to IT/OT boundary isolation
Number of OT-adjacent systems affected
Process downtime duration
ITID-54221.notes: Differentiated within its sibling group by target environment (ICS/OT) rather than by attack mechanism; scoped to company-wide critical-infrastructure business impact, with malware mechanics deferred to ITID-311xx.

playbook.name: Ransomware Attack on Industrial Control System (ICS/OT) Environment
playbook.description: Ransomware infects an industrial control system or operational technology environment, threatening physical process safety and requiring coordinated IT/OT incident response.

steps.title: Confirm ransomware presence in the OT/ICS environment and assess physical-safety risk
steps.desc: Confirm ransomware indicators (HMI unavailability, encrypted engineering workstations, ransom notes on OT systems) and immediately assess whether any physical process is at risk of unsafe state due to loss of monitoring/control.
steps.guidance: Engage OT/process safety engineers immediately — physical safety assessment takes priority over technical investigation depth at this stage.
steps.outcome: Ransomware presence confirmed in OT environment; physical-safety risk level established.

steps.title: Determine scope across IT/OT boundary
steps.desc: Identify whether the infection originated in IT and crossed into OT, or vice versa, and map affected systems on both sides of the boundary.
steps.guidance: Review IT/OT network segmentation logs and historian/SCADA connectivity paths.
steps.outcome: Cross-boundary scope and infection vector documented.

steps.title: Initiate safe manual/fail-safe process control if automated systems are compromised
steps.desc: Transition affected physical processes to manual control or a pre-defined fail-safe state per site safety procedures, coordinated with plant operations.
steps.guidance: Follow the facility's emergency shutdown/manual-override procedures; do not attempt technical remediation before physical safety is assured.
steps.outcome: Physical process is in a safe, stable state under manual or fail-safe control.
steps.abort: If a safe manual fallback is not achievable, escalate to full emergency shutdown per site safety protocol.

steps.title: Isolate the OT network from IT and disable remote access paths
steps.desc: Sever or restrict IT/OT network connections (data historians, remote access gateways, engineering workstation links) to prevent further ransomware propagation into or within OT.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with OT engineers to ensure isolation does not itself disrupt safety-instrumented systems.
steps.outcome: OT network isolated from further ransomware spread while safety systems remain functional.

steps.title: Escalate to safety regulators, executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify required safety/regulatory bodies, executive leadership, Legal, and law enforcement given the physical-safety dimension of an OT ransomware incident.
steps.guidance: Follow sector-specific regulatory notification requirements (e.g., process safety, critical infrastructure reporting) in addition to standard breach notification.
steps.outcome: Required regulatory and law-enforcement notifications completed.

steps.title: Remove ransomware from IT and OT systems with vendor/OEM coordination
steps.desc: Eliminate ransomware and persistence from affected engineering workstations, HMIs, and IT systems, coordinating with the ICS/OT equipment vendor to avoid damaging safety-certified configurations.
steps.guidance: Do not apply generic IT remediation tools to safety-instrumented systems without OEM guidance.
steps.outcome: Ransomware removed from all affected IT and OT systems with vendor-validated configurations intact.

steps.title: Restore OT systems from verified clean, vendor-validated backups and re-verify safety systems before resuming automated control
steps.desc: Restore engineering configurations and control logic from clean backups, and have safety engineers re-verify all safety-instrumented functions before returning to automated operation.
steps.guidance: Perform a full functional safety test before transitioning back from manual to automated control.
steps.outcome: OT systems restored and safety-verified before automated control resumes.
steps.abort: If safety verification fails, remain in manual/fail-safe mode until resolved.

steps.title: Conduct joint IT/OT post-incident review with safety and regulatory stakeholders
steps.desc: Document the incident with emphasis on IT/OT segmentation gaps, safety-response effectiveness, and regulatory notification timeliness.
steps.guidance: Include OT vendor, safety engineering, and regulatory affairs in the review; recommend segmentation and OT-specific detection investments.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with prioritized IT/OT security and safety improvement actions.

ITID-54222.def: A ransomware attack that encrypts or disrupts systems supporting direct patient care or clinical operations (e.g., EHR, PACS, clinical devices' supporting infrastructure), tracked for its critical-infrastructure targeting angle.
ITID-54222.purpose: Captures ransomware reaching hospital or healthcare-delivery critical systems, where impact directly threatens patient safety and triggers healthcare-specific regulatory and continuity obligations.
scopeIncludes: Encryption of electronic health record (EHR) or picture archiving (PACS) systems
Ransomware forcing diversion of patients or cancellation of clinical procedures
Ransomware affecting systems supporting medical device connectivity or clinical workflow
scopeExcludes: Ransomware confined to non-clinical corporate/administrative healthcare systems with no patient-care impact (see ITID-54211/54212)
The malware family's technical mechanics (see ITID-311xx)
ITID-54222.severity: Critical — any patient-care-impacting ransomware event carries direct life-safety risk.
ITID-54222.priority: P1, always; treat as a joint cyber-patient-safety incident.
ITID-54222.escalation: Escalate immediately to clinical leadership, patient safety officers, executive leadership, and applicable healthcare regulators; activate downtime/paper-based clinical procedures without delay.
indicators: Ransom notes appearing on clinical workstations or EHR servers
Unplanned EHR/PACS unavailability coincident with encryption indicators
Reports of ambulance diversion or procedure cancellation
vectors: Lateral movement from compromised corporate network into clinical system networks
Compromise of a shared identity/authentication system used by both administrative and clinical systems
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation between clinical and administrative networks
Legacy medical-device-supporting infrastructure unable to run modern endpoint protection
controls: Segmentation between clinical and administrative networks
Downtime/paper-based clinical continuity procedures
Clinical system-specific backup and recovery testing
ITID-54222.detection: IT-side detection is often mature; clinical-system-side detection depends on close coordination with biomedical engineering and clinical IT.
ITID-54222.response: Prioritize patient safety: activate clinical downtime procedures immediately, independent of IT recovery timeline; coordinate jointly between SOC and clinical leadership.
metrics: Time to activate clinical downtime procedures
Number of clinical systems affected
Patient-care impact duration
ITID-54222.notes: Differentiated within its sibling group by target environment (healthcare/clinical) rather than by attack mechanism; scoped to company-wide critical-infrastructure business impact, with malware mechanics deferred to ITID-311xx.

playbook.name: Ransomware Attack on Healthcare/Hospital Critical Systems
playbook.description: Ransomware encrypts critical healthcare/hospital systems, directly threatening patient safety and requiring coordinated clinical/IT incident response.

steps.title: Confirm ransomware impact on clinical systems and assess patient-safety risk
steps.desc: Confirm ransomware indicators affecting EHR, medical devices, or clinical support systems, and immediately assess impact on active patient care and safety.
steps.guidance: Engage clinical leadership/Chief Medical Information Officer immediately; patient-safety triage takes priority over technical investigation.
steps.outcome: Ransomware confirmed on clinical systems; patient-safety risk level established.

steps.title: Determine scope of affected clinical and administrative systems
steps.desc: Map which EHR modules, medical devices, lab systems, and administrative systems are encrypted or at risk.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with clinical engineering/biomedical device teams for medical device inventory impact.
steps.outcome: Documented scope across clinical and administrative systems.

steps.title: Activate downtime/manual clinical procedures per hospital emergency plan
steps.desc: Trigger the hospital's EHR-downtime and manual charting/ordering procedures to maintain safe patient care while systems are contained.
steps.guidance: Follow established clinical downtime protocols (paper charting, manual medication verification, diversion procedures if needed).
steps.outcome: Patient care continues safely under manual/downtime procedures.
steps.abort: If patient safety cannot be assured, escalate to ambulance diversion or patient transfer per hospital emergency protocol.

steps.title: Isolate infected systems and segment network away from life-critical medical devices
steps.desc: Disconnect infected IT systems from the network while ensuring isolation actions do not disrupt connected life-critical medical devices.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with biomedical engineering before isolating any network segment carrying medical device traffic.
steps.outcome: Ransomware spread contained without disrupting life-critical device operation.

steps.title: Notify regulators, Legal, and law enforcement per healthcare breach requirements
steps.desc: Complete required regulatory notifications (e.g., health authority breach reporting) alongside Legal and law-enforcement engagement.
steps.guidance: Follow jurisdiction-specific healthcare breach notification timelines in addition to standard ransomware escalation.
steps.outcome: Required regulatory, Legal, and law-enforcement notifications completed.

steps.title: Remove ransomware and persistence from clinical and IT systems
steps.desc: Eliminate ransomware payloads and persistence from affected systems, coordinating with medical device vendors for any affected biomedical equipment.
steps.guidance: Do not apply generic remediation to regulated medical devices without vendor/FDA-cleared-configuration guidance.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed free of ransomware, with medical device integrity preserved.

steps.title: Restore clinical systems from verified clean backups with clinical validation before go-live
steps.desc: Restore EHR and clinical systems from clean backups, with clinical staff validating data accuracy (medication records, allergies, orders) before resuming full digital operation.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased, clinically-supervised cutover from downtime procedures back to digital systems.
steps.outcome: Clinical systems restored with data accuracy validated by clinical staff before full resumption.

steps.title: Conduct joint clinical/IT post-incident review focused on patient-safety continuity
steps.desc: Document the incident with emphasis on downtime-procedure effectiveness, medical-device segmentation, and detection/response speed.
steps.guidance: Include clinical leadership, biomedical engineering, and regulatory affairs; recommend prioritized improvements.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked patient-safety and security improvement actions.

ITID-54223.def: A ransomware attack that encrypts or disrupts systems supporting utility or energy generation/distribution operations, tracked for its critical-infrastructure targeting angle.
ITID-54223.purpose: Captures ransomware reaching utility or energy-provider critical systems, where impact threatens continuity of an essential public service and carries potential regulatory and national-critical-infrastructure implications.
scopeIncludes: Encryption of systems supporting energy generation, transmission, or distribution operations
Ransomware forcing precautionary shutdown of utility control or billing systems
Ransomware affecting systems in an environment subject to critical-infrastructure regulatory oversight (e.g., NERC CIP or equivalent)
scopeExcludes: Ransomware confined to corporate/administrative utility systems with no operational-technology exposure (see ITID-54211/54212)
The malware family's technical mechanics (see ITID-311xx)
ITID-54223.severity: Critical — utility/energy disruption can cascade to public safety and other dependent critical infrastructure.
ITID-54223.priority: P1, always; treat as a joint cyber-critical-infrastructure incident.
ITID-54223.escalation: Escalate immediately to utility operations leadership, executive leadership, and applicable critical-infrastructure regulators; coordinate with grid/regional reliability authorities where relevant.
indicators: Ransom notes on systems within or adjacent to utility operational networks
Unplanned control-system or billing-system unavailability coincident with encryption indicators
Precautionary manual operation of physical processes
vectors: Lateral movement from compromised corporate network into utility operational networks
Compromise of remote access used for vendor/maintenance support of utility systems
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation between corporate IT and utility operational networks
Legacy utility control systems unable to run modern endpoint protection
controls: Segmentation between corporate IT and utility operational networks
NERC CIP or equivalent regulatory-aligned controls
Manual/fail-safe operational procedures for physical processes
ITID-54223.detection: IT-side detection is often mature; operational-network-side detection depends on close coordination with utility operations and regulatory-mandated monitoring.
ITID-54223.response: Prioritize continuity of essential service and public safety: initiate manual/fail-safe operating procedures where needed, independent of IT recovery timeline.
metrics: Time to isolate operational network
Duration of service impact
Regulatory notification timeliness
ITID-54223.notes: Differentiated within its sibling group by target environment (utility/energy) rather than by attack mechanism; scoped to company-wide critical-infrastructure business impact, with malware mechanics deferred to ITID-311xx.

playbook.name: Ransomware Attack on Utility/Energy Provider
playbook.description: Ransomware encrypts critical systems at a utility or energy provider, threatening public-safety-relevant service delivery and requiring coordinated regulatory/OT incident response.

steps.title: Confirm ransomware impact on utility control/billing systems and assess public-safety/service-continuity risk
steps.desc: Confirm ransomware indicators on SCADA-adjacent IT, billing, or grid-management systems and immediately assess risk to service delivery (power/water/gas continuity) and public safety.
steps.guidance: Engage grid/utility operations leadership immediately; public-safety-relevant service continuity assessment takes priority over technical investigation depth.
steps.outcome: Ransomware presence confirmed; public-safety/service-continuity risk level established.

steps.title: Determine scope across IT and OT/SCADA-adjacent boundary
steps.desc: Map which IT systems are affected and confirm whether the OT/SCADA environment controlling physical delivery has been reached.
steps.guidance: Review IT/OT segmentation and historian connectivity logs.
steps.outcome: Cross-boundary scope documented with OT exposure status confirmed.

steps.title: Transition to manual/fail-safe grid or plant operations if automated systems are at risk
steps.desc: Coordinate with operations to shift to manual control or pre-defined fail-safe procedures for any physical delivery system at risk, ensuring continuity of essential service.
steps.guidance: Follow the utility's emergency operations procedures; prioritize maintaining essential service delivery safely.
steps.outcome: Physical delivery systems operating safely under manual or fail-safe control if needed.
steps.abort: If safe manual operation cannot be assured, escalate per the utility's emergency shutdown protocol.

steps.title: Isolate affected IT systems from OT/SCADA-adjacent networks
steps.desc: Sever or restrict connections between infected IT systems and OT networks to prevent further spread toward systems controlling physical delivery.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with OT engineers to avoid disrupting safety-instrumented systems during isolation.
steps.outcome: Ransomware spread contained away from OT/delivery-critical systems.

steps.title: Notify energy-sector regulators, Legal, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Complete required critical-infrastructure/energy-sector regulatory notifications alongside Legal and law-enforcement engagement.
steps.guidance: Follow sector-specific reporting obligations (e.g., grid reliability authorities) in addition to standard breach notification.
steps.outcome: Required regulatory, Legal, and law-enforcement notifications completed.

steps.title: Remove ransomware and persistence from IT systems with OT-vendor coordination
steps.desc: Eliminate ransomware and persistence mechanisms from affected IT systems, coordinating with OT/SCADA vendors before touching any adjacent control-system components.
steps.guidance: Avoid generic remediation tooling on OT-adjacent or safety-instrumented components without vendor guidance.
steps.outcome: All affected IT systems confirmed free of ransomware; OT-adjacent systems verified unaffected or vendor-remediated.

steps.title: Restore systems from verified clean backups and re-verify delivery-critical functions before resuming automated operation
steps.desc: Restore IT systems from clean backups and have operations engineers re-verify delivery-critical functions before transitioning back from manual to automated control.
steps.guidance: Perform functional verification of grid/delivery control before resuming full automation.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and delivery-critical functions verified before automated control resumes.
steps.abort: If verification fails, remain in manual/fail-safe mode until resolved.

steps.title: Conduct joint operations/IT post-incident review with regulatory stakeholders
steps.desc: Document the incident with emphasis on IT/OT segmentation, service-continuity effectiveness, and regulatory notification timeliness.
steps.guidance: Include operations engineering and regulatory affairs; recommend prioritized security and resilience investments.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with prioritized improvement actions tracked to completion.

ITID-54224.def: A ransomware attack targeting a critical-infrastructure environment that has not yet been classified into the ICS/OT, healthcare, or utility sub-categories.
ITID-54224.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for ransomware attacks on critical infrastructure not yet attributed to a specific sector (ICS/OT, healthcare, or utility).
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed critical-infrastructure ransomware events pending sector confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once sector is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54221, 54222, or 54223)
ITID-54224.severity: Critical pending triage, consistent with critical-infrastructure targeting.
ITID-54224.priority: P1, always, regardless of pending reclassification.
ITID-54224.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO and executive leadership; do not delay containment pending sector classification.
indicators: Ransomware indicators within an environment identified as critical infrastructure, sector not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54224.detection: Relies on initial encryption/behavioral detection; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54224.response: Contain immediately while triage determines sector for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54224.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Targeted Ransomware on Critical Infrastructure
playbook.description: Ransomware targets a critical-infrastructure environment with the specific sector (ICS/OT, healthcare, utility) not yet determined at time of detection.

steps.title: Confirm ransomware presence and assess critical-infrastructure/safety risk
steps.desc: Confirm ransomware indicators and immediately assess whether the affected environment has physical-safety or essential-service-continuity implications.
steps.guidance: Engage operations/facility leadership immediately to assess safety risk before deep technical investigation.
steps.outcome: Ransomware confirmed; safety/continuity risk level established.

steps.title: Determine specific critical-infrastructure sector and route to specialized response
steps.desc: Classify the affected environment as ICS/OT, healthcare, utility/energy, or another critical-infrastructure category to apply sector-specific safety procedures.
steps.guidance: Consult asset inventory and system ownership records to confirm sector classification.
steps.outcome: Sector classified and specialized safety/regulatory procedures activated.

steps.title: Transition to manual/fail-safe operations if physical processes are at risk
steps.desc: Coordinate with operations to shift affected physical processes to manual control or a pre-defined fail-safe state.
steps.guidance: Follow site-specific emergency operations procedures.
steps.outcome: Physical processes operating safely under manual/fail-safe control if needed.
steps.abort: If safe manual operation cannot be assured, escalate to full emergency shutdown per site protocol.

steps.title: Isolate affected IT/OT networks and disable remote access
steps.desc: Sever or restrict connections between infected systems and the rest of the environment to halt further spread.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with engineering to avoid disrupting safety-instrumented systems during isolation.
steps.outcome: Ransomware spread contained.

steps.title: Notify sector regulators, Legal, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Complete required sector-specific regulatory notifications alongside Legal and law-enforcement engagement.
steps.guidance: Follow applicable critical-infrastructure reporting obligations for the identified sector.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed.

steps.title: Remove ransomware and persistence with vendor coordination
steps.desc: Eliminate ransomware and persistence mechanisms, coordinating with equipment/software vendors before touching safety-critical or specialized components.
steps.guidance: Avoid generic remediation tooling on safety-instrumented or regulated components without vendor guidance.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed free of ransomware and persistence.

steps.title: Restore from verified clean backups and re-verify safety/critical functions before resuming automated operation
steps.desc: Restore systems from clean backups and have engineers re-verify critical functions before transitioning back to automated operation.
steps.guidance: Perform functional verification before resuming full automation.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and critical functions verified before automated operation resumes.
steps.abort: If verification fails, remain in manual/fail-safe mode until resolved.

steps.title: Conduct joint operations/IT post-incident review with regulatory stakeholders
steps.desc: Document the incident emphasizing segmentation gaps, safety-response effectiveness, and regulatory notification timeliness.
steps.guidance: Recommend prioritized security and resilience investments.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54231.def: A ransomware attack in which the backup repository (backup server, backup storage target, or backup snapshots) is itself directly targeted and encrypted, aiming to deny recovery.
ITID-54231.purpose: Captures ransomware that specifically and directly encrypts the backup repository itself, distinguishing the direct-encryption pattern from pre-encryption deletion/corruption.
scopeIncludes: Encryption of backup server file systems or backup storage appliances
Encryption of backup snapshot/repository data by the same or a related ransomware payload used against production systems
scopeExcludes: Deletion or corruption of backups performed as a precursor step before primary system encryption (see ITID-54232)
Ransomware confined to production systems with backups unaffected
ITID-54231.severity: Critical — direct backup encryption typically eliminates the primary recovery path, forcing reliance on offline/immutable copies or ransom negotiation.
ITID-54231.escalation: Escalate immediately to backup/infrastructure teams to assess any surviving immutable or offline/air-gapped copies before making recovery decisions.
indicators: Encrypted file extensions or ransom notes present on backup storage targets
Backup jobs failing with corruption errors immediately preceding or during the broader ransomware event
Backup catalog/index unavailability
vectors: Compromised backup administrator credentials used to reach backup infrastructure directly
Backup infrastructure reachable from the same network segment as production, allowing payload propagation
rootCauses: Backup infrastructure not isolated from production network/credentials
No immutable or offline (air-gapped) backup copy maintained
controls: Immutable/WORM backup storage
Air-gapped or offline backup copies
Backup infrastructure network and credential isolation from production
ITID-54231.detection: Backup job monitoring and backup-storage file-integrity alerting provide direct detection when instrumented; often discovered only during recovery attempts if not proactively monitored.
ITID-54231.response: Immediately assess for any surviving immutable/offline backup copy before deciding on ransom negotiation or rebuild-from-scratch recovery.
metrics: Percentage of backup repository encrypted
Availability of surviving immutable/offline copies
Recovery time when a clean copy exists vs. when it does not
ITID-54231.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54232 by mechanism: this leaf is direct encryption of the backup target itself, not deliberate deletion/corruption performed as a precursor.

playbook.name: Ransomware Specifically Targeting and Encrypting Backup Repository
playbook.description: An attacker deliberately targets and encrypts the organization's backup repository as part of a ransomware attack, removing the recovery safety net.

steps.title: Confirm backup repository encryption and assess recovery capability
steps.desc: Confirm that backup storage (repositories, snapshots, backup servers) has been encrypted or corrupted, and assess what recovery capability, if any, remains.
steps.guidance: Check backup software console and repository file listings for encrypted/renamed files or ransom notes.
steps.outcome: Backup encryption confirmed; remaining recoverable backup scope (if any) identified.

steps.title: Determine broader ransomware scope beyond backups
steps.desc: Assess whether production systems are also encrypted as part of the same attack, since backup targeting often accompanies primary-system encryption.
steps.guidance: Correlate with EDR/SIEM alerts across production infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the attack (production plus backup) documented.

steps.title: Immediately isolate any remaining unencrypted or offline backup copies
steps.desc: Air-gap or disconnect any surviving offline, immutable, or offsite backup copies from the network before the attacker can reach them.
steps.guidance: Prioritize this above all other containment actions — surviving backups are the organization's last line of recovery.
steps.outcome: All remaining recoverable backup copies protected from further encryption.

steps.title: Isolate the broader network to halt further ransomware spread
steps.desc: Segment and isolate affected production and backup-infrastructure network segments to prevent continued lateral movement.
steps.guidance: Coordinate emergency ACLs/VLAN isolation across affected subnets.
steps.outcome: Further spread halted.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence and engage Legal/Law Enforcement
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence from affected backup and production systems and notify Legal and law enforcement per ransomware policy.
steps.guidance: Do not pay any ransom demand independently — route all decisions through Legal/executive leadership.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; Legal and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Remove ransomware and persistence from backup infrastructure and production systems
steps.desc: Eliminate ransomware payloads and persistence from backup servers/repositories and affected production systems before any restoration attempt.
steps.guidance: Rebuild backup infrastructure from trusted media where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.outcome: Backup infrastructure and production systems confirmed free of ransomware.

steps.title: Assess recovery options given backup loss and rebuild backup infrastructure
steps.desc: Determine what data can be recovered from any surviving backups, alternate copies (e.g., replicated data, cloud snapshots), or must be reconstructed manually, and rebuild backup infrastructure with hardened, immutable configurations.
steps.guidance: Engage data-recovery specialists if backups are largely unrecoverable; prioritize critical business data reconstruction.
steps.outcome: Maximum feasible data recovered; hardened backup infrastructure rebuilt with immutability/offline copies.
steps.abort: If no recoverable data exists for a system, escalate to business continuity planning for manual reconstruction or data loss acceptance.

steps.title: Review backup architecture resilience against ransomware targeting
steps.desc: Document how backups were reached and encrypted, and evaluate the need for immutable, offline, or air-gapped backup architecture.
steps.guidance: Recommend 3-2-1-1 backup strategy improvements and access-control hardening for backup infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with prioritized backup-resilience investments tracked.

ITID-54232.def: An adversary's deliberate deletion, corruption, or disabling of backup jobs, snapshots, or repositories prior to deploying ransomware against primary systems, intended to remove the victim's recovery option before encryption begins.
ITID-54232.purpose: Captures the deliberate deletion or corruption of backups performed by an adversary as a precursor step before deploying encryption against primary systems, distinguishing the sabotage-before-encryption pattern.
scopeIncludes: Deletion of volume shadow copies or backup snapshots as a documented pre-ransomware step
Disabling or reconfiguring backup jobs/schedules shortly before encryption onset
Deletion of backup catalogs/indexes to prevent restore even if underlying data survives
scopeExcludes: Direct encryption of the backup repository itself (see ITID-54231)
Accidental backup deletion/corruption with no ransomware follow-through (an IT operations matter, not this ITID)
ITID-54232.severity: Critical — this pattern is a strong precursor indicator that full-scale encryption is imminent or already underway.
ITID-54232.priority: P1, always; treat any confirmed backup-deletion activity as an active-ransomware emergency even before encryption is observed.
ITID-54232.escalation: Escalate immediately upon detection of backup-deletion activity, ideally before encryption onset, to attempt emergency isolation of remaining systems.
indicators: Volume shadow copy deletion commands (e.g., vssadmin, wbadmin) executed shortly before encryption
Backup job configuration changes or disablement from an unexpected account/host
Backup catalog corruption or deletion events
vectors: Living-off-the-land binaries used to delete shadow copies/backup catalogs
Compromised backup administrator credentials used to disable or reconfigure jobs
rootCauses: Backup deletion/disable actions not alerted on in real time
Excessive standing privilege allowing backup configuration changes from compromised endpoints
controls: Real-time alerting on shadow-copy deletion and backup job disablement
Immutable/WORM backup storage unaffected by deletion commands
Just-in-time privileged access for backup administration
ITID-54232.detection: This is one of the strongest early-warning signals available for imminent ransomware — real-time alerting on shadow-copy deletion and backup job changes can enable pre-encryption containment.
ITID-54232.response: Treat detected backup-deletion activity as a time-critical pre-encryption warning; isolate the source host and any reachable systems immediately, ahead of encryption onset if possible.
metrics: Time from backup-deletion detection to containment action
Percentage of ransomware cases where this precursor was detected before encryption
ITID-54232.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54231 by mechanism and timing: this leaf is deliberate pre-encryption sabotage of recovery options, not direct encryption of the backup target.

playbook.name: Backup Deletion/Corruption Prior to Primary System Encryption
playbook.description: An attacker deliberately deletes or corrupts backups as a preparatory step before deploying ransomware to encrypt primary systems, ensuring victims cannot recover without paying.

steps.title: Detect backup deletion/corruption activity
steps.desc: Identify alerts or anomalies indicating mass deletion, corruption, or unauthorized modification of backup jobs/repositories, which often precedes ransomware deployment.
steps.guidance: Check backup software audit logs for unusual administrative actions (job deletions, retention policy changes, repository wipes) outside normal change windows.
steps.outcome: Backup tampering confirmed and timeline established relative to any subsequent encryption activity.

steps.title: Determine attacker foothold and assess imminent ransomware deployment risk
steps.desc: Given backup tampering is a precursor indicator, urgently investigate for active attacker presence and imminent signs of ransomware staging.
steps.guidance: Check for recently created privileged accounts, disabled security tooling, or staged encryption binaries.
steps.outcome: Attacker presence and imminent deployment risk assessed with urgency appropriate to a likely pending ransomware event.

steps.title: Immediately isolate any surviving backup copies and revoke attacker access
steps.desc: Air-gap remaining backup copies and revoke/rotate credentials used to tamper with backups before the attacker can proceed to primary-system encryption.
steps.guidance: Treat this as a race against imminent ransomware deployment — act with urgency.
steps.outcome: Surviving backups protected; attacker's backup-tampering access revoked.

steps.title: Isolate potentially compromised hosts and segment network preemptively
steps.desc: Proactively isolate hosts showing attacker activity and segment the network to reduce blast radius before encryption can begin.
steps.guidance: Prioritize isolating privileged/administrative systems and domain controllers.
steps.outcome: Attacker's ability to reach additional systems is significantly reduced.

steps.title: Engage incident response leadership and Legal/Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Escalate immediately given the high likelihood of imminent ransomware deployment; engage Legal and law enforcement in parallel with technical response.
steps.outcome: Leadership, Legal, and law enforcement engaged early in the timeline.

steps.title: Hunt for and remove attacker persistence before ransomware deployment occurs
steps.desc: Conduct an urgent threat hunt to find and remove all attacker footholds, staged payloads, and persistence mechanisms before encryption can be triggered.
steps.guidance: Prioritize speed; use EDR-driven isolation and removal across all systems showing indicators.
steps.outcome: Attacker presence eliminated before primary-system encryption occurs, or if encryption already began, halted as early as possible.
steps.abort: If encryption activity is detected mid-hunt, immediately pivot to full ransomware containment procedures.

steps.title: Rebuild backup infrastructure with hardened, immutable configuration
steps.desc: Reconstruct backup infrastructure with immutable/offline backup copies and stricter access controls to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Verify new backups are protected from the same tampering technique before considering recovery complete.
steps.outcome: Hardened backup infrastructure in place with verified new backup sets.

steps.title: Review detection speed for backup-tampering precursor indicators
steps.desc: Assess how quickly the backup tampering was detected and whether earlier detection could have prevented full ransomware deployment.
steps.guidance: Recommend alerting on backup deletion/retention-policy changes as a high-priority precursor indicator.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with detection improvement actions tracked.

ITID-54233.def: A ransomware event involving impact to backups that has not yet been classified as direct backup encryption or precursor backup deletion/corruption.
ITID-54233.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for backup-targeting ransomware events not yet attributed to direct encryption or precursor deletion/corruption.
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed backup-impacting ransomware events pending mechanism confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once mechanism is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54231 or 54232)
ITID-54233.severity: Critical pending triage, given the recovery-path implications.
ITID-54233.priority: P1, always, regardless of pending reclassification.
ITID-54233.escalation: Escalate immediately; assess backup integrity in parallel with triage.
indicators: Backup unavailability or errors coincident with a broader ransomware event, mechanism not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54233.detection: Relies on initial backup-monitoring alerting; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54233.response: Assess for any surviving clean backup copy immediately while triage determines mechanism for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54233.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Backup System Encryption
playbook.description: Backup systems are found encrypted or corrupted as part of a ransomware event, with the specific attack sequence (pre-emptive targeting vs. incidental) not yet determined.

steps.title: Confirm backup system encryption/corruption and assess recovery capability
steps.desc: Confirm the extent of backup encryption or corruption and assess what recovery capability, if any, remains.
steps.guidance: Check backup console and repository listings for encrypted files, ransom notes, or corrupted catalogs.
steps.outcome: Backup damage scope confirmed and remaining recoverable capability identified.

steps.title: Determine relationship to broader ransomware attack
steps.desc: Establish whether backup encryption is part of a broader ransomware event affecting production systems, and the sequence of events.
steps.guidance: Correlate with EDR/SIEM data across the environment.
steps.outcome: Full attack scope and sequence documented.

steps.title: Isolate any remaining unaffected backup copies
steps.desc: Air-gap or disconnect any surviving backup copies from the network immediately.
steps.guidance: Prioritize above other containment actions since surviving backups are critical to recovery.
steps.outcome: Remaining recoverable backups protected.

steps.title: Isolate affected network segments and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Segment affected systems to halt further spread and preserve forensic evidence for investigation.
steps.guidance: Follow chain-of-custody procedures for evidence handling.
steps.outcome: Spread halted; evidence preserved.

steps.title: Engage Legal and Law Enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal, executive leadership, and law enforcement per the ransomware response policy.
steps.guidance: Route all negotiation/payment decisions through Legal and executive leadership only.
steps.outcome: Legal and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Remove ransomware/corruption cause from backup and production systems
steps.desc: Eliminate the ransomware or root cause of corruption from backup infrastructure and any affected production systems.
steps.guidance: Rebuild backup infrastructure from trusted media where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.outcome: Backup infrastructure confirmed clean.

steps.title: Assess recovery options and rebuild backup infrastructure with hardened configuration
steps.desc: Determine what data is recoverable and rebuild backup infrastructure with immutable/offline protections.
steps.guidance: Engage data-recovery specialists if backups are largely unrecoverable.
steps.outcome: Maximum feasible data recovered; hardened backup infrastructure rebuilt.

steps.title: Review backup architecture resilience
steps.desc: Evaluate the need for immutable, offline, or air-gapped backup architecture to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Recommend 3-2-1-1 backup strategy and access-control hardening.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54241.def: An extortion attempt in which an adversary threatens or launches a denial-of-service attack against company infrastructure unless a ransom is paid, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact.
ITID-54241.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for ransom denial-of-service extortion within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to the detailed DoS/DDoS technique breakdown and the combined DDoS-ransom-extortion leaf elsewhere in the taxonomy.
scopeIncludes: Ransom demand accompanied by or threatening a denial-of-service attack against company-facing services
Business-impact tracking of an RDoS event already detailed technically elsewhere in the taxonomy
scopeExcludes: The detailed DDoS attack technique mechanics (see the Distributed Denial of Service group, ITID-548xx, and ITID-40000)
The combined DDoS-plus-ransomware-extortion demand pattern already tracked at ITID-41342
Encryption-based ransomware without a DoS component (see ITID-542xx)
ITID-54241.severity: High if the threatened/actual DoS targets business-critical services; Medium if targeting non-critical or already-mitigated infrastructure.
ITID-54241.priority: P2 on receipt of a credible extortion demand; escalate to P1 if an actual disruptive attack begins.
ITID-54241.escalation: Escalate to SOC leadership and legal/law enforcement liaison upon receipt of any ransom demand; do not engage with the extortionist without legal/executive sign-off.
indicators: Extortion email or message threatening a DDoS attack with a payment deadline
A demonstrative, short-duration DDoS attack accompanying the demand
Ransom note referencing a specific company asset or service
vectors: Threatened or demonstrative volumetric/application-layer DDoS attack used as leverage
rootCauses: Insufficient DDoS mitigation capacity signaling the company as a viable extortion target
Public exposure of critical service endpoints without protection
controls: DDoS mitigation service/scrubbing capacity
Law enforcement and legal engagement procedures for extortion
ITID-54241.detection: Extortion communications are typically the first indicator; technical DDoS detection is covered in depth under ITID-40000/ITID-548xx.
ITID-54241.response: Preserve the extortion communication as evidence, engage legal/law enforcement, and activate DDoS mitigation capacity proactively regardless of payment decision.
metrics: Time to legal/law enforcement engagement
Whether a demonstrative attack occurred
Payment/no-payment decision outcome
ITID-54241.notes: This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed DoS/DDoS technique breakdown and ITID-41342 for the already-tracked combined DDoS-plus-ransom-demand pattern. Avoid restating DDoS mechanics here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General RDoS (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: An attacker threatens or launches a denial-of-service attack against critical systems and demands ransom payment to stop or prevent the disruption.

steps.title: Validate the RDoS threat/demonstration attack and preserve the ransom communication
steps.desc: Confirm whether a demonstration DDoS attack has occurred or a credible ransom threat has been received, and preserve all threat communications as evidence.
steps.guidance: Check network/traffic monitoring for any demonstration attack correlating with the ransom demand timing; do not reply to the threat actor directly.
steps.outcome: Threat validated and communications preserved with chain of custody.

steps.title: Assess criticality of threatened/targeted systems and potential attack scale
steps.desc: Identify which systems are threatened or already targeted and estimate the potential attack volume based on any demonstration traffic observed.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference with the DDoS mitigation provider on expected attack capacity for the threat actor group if attributable.
steps.outcome: Impact and scale assessment documented.

steps.title: Engage DDoS scrubbing/mitigation provider proactively
steps.desc: Activate or pre-position DDoS mitigation/scrubbing services for the threatened systems ahead of any full-scale attack.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the mitigation provider on traffic profiles and thresholds for automatic mitigation activation.
steps.outcome: Mitigation capacity is active and ready to absorb an attack.

steps.title: Apply rate limiting and traffic filtering on critical services
steps.desc: Implement rate limiting, geo-filtering, or traffic shaping on the threatened services as an additional layer of protection.
steps.guidance: Tune thresholds to avoid impacting legitimate traffic while limiting attacker capacity.
steps.outcome: Additional protective controls in place on critical services.

steps.title: Engage Legal and Law Enforcement; do not pay the ransom
steps.desc: Report the extortion threat to law enforcement and Legal, following the organization's non-payment policy for extortion demands.
steps.guidance: Coordinate any public or customer communication through Legal/PR to avoid signaling vulnerability to the threat actor.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement and Legal engaged; no ransom paid.

steps.title: Mitigate the attack in real time if it materializes
steps.desc: If the attack is launched, actively tune scrubbing and filtering rules in real time to maintain service availability.
steps.guidance: Work with the mitigation provider's SOC for real-time signature updates against the observed attack pattern.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic effectively mitigated with services remaining available.
steps.abort: If mitigation cannot keep pace, activate a maintenance/queueing page to protect backend systems while mitigation is tuned further.

steps.title: Stand down elevated mitigation posture and confirm normal service
steps.desc: Once the threat has subsided, verify normal traffic patterns have resumed and confirm service performance is back to baseline.
steps.guidance: Maintain a reduced level of mitigation readiness for a monitoring period in case of renewed extortion attempts.
steps.outcome: Normal service confirmed; mitigation readiness maintained at an appropriate level.

steps.title: Review RDoS preparedness and mitigation provider readiness
steps.desc: Evaluate how quickly mitigation was activated and whether scrubbing capacity and contracts are adequate for future extortion threats.
steps.guidance: Recommend always-on mitigation or improved activation speed as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54311.def: An attempt by an adversary to hijack or manipulate BGP routing to disrupt company connectivity or redirect company traffic, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than its routing-protocol mechanics.
ITID-54311.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for BGP hijacking within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to the detailed BGP technique breakdown already tracked under Denial of Service impacts.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a BGP hijack event affecting company services
Confirmation that a routing anomaly affecting the company is adversarial rather than a provider operational failure
scopeExcludes: The detailed BGP hijack/leak/session-attack technique mechanics (see ITID-41421 through ITID-41424 under ITID-40000)
Non-adversarial ISP routing failures (see ITID-54132)
ITID-54311.severity: High to Critical depending on how much company traffic is affected and whether traffic is being intercepted or merely blackholed.
ITID-54311.priority: P1 if confirmed adversarial and affecting production traffic; P2 while confirming adversarial intent.
ITID-54311.escalation: Escalate immediately to network operations, the affected ISP/transit provider, and, if traffic interception is suspected, to data protection/legal.
indicators: Unexpected route origin AS for company IP space observed via route-monitoring services
Traffic blackholing or misdirection correlated to an unauthorized route announcement
vectors: Unauthorized announcement of company IP prefixes by a malicious or compromised AS
rootCauses: Lack of Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) route origin validation
Insufficient real-time BGP route monitoring
controls: RPKI route origin validation
BGP route monitoring service
Coordination with upstream providers on route filtering
ITID-54311.detection: Third-party BGP monitoring services provide the primary detection surface; internal telemetry alone is typically insufficient.
ITID-54311.response: Coordinate with upstream providers to filter/withdraw the malicious announcement; engage the affected ISP's NOC immediately.
metrics: Time to detect the unauthorized announcement
Time to route withdrawal/remediation
ITID-54311.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 (ITID-4142x) for the detailed BGP hijack/leak/session-attack technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General BGP Hijacking Attempt (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: An attacker or misconfiguration causes illegitimate announcement of the organization's IP prefixes, hijacking traffic away from legitimate infrastructure.

steps.title: Confirm BGP hijack via route monitoring and RPKI validation
steps.desc: Confirm unauthorized announcement of the organization's prefixes by comparing observed AS-path/origin data against known-good baselines using route monitoring and RPKI validation.
steps.guidance: Use services such as route monitoring platforms and looking-glass tools from multiple vantage points to confirm the hijack and identify the offending AS.
steps.outcome: Hijack confirmed with the illegitimate originating AS and affected prefixes identified.
steps.abort: If no illegitimate origination is found, reclassify as a routing failure and route to that procedure.

steps.title: Assess traffic and service impact of the hijack
steps.desc: Determine which services and customer traffic are being misdirected as a result of the hijack.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference affected prefixes against the service catalog.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Re-announce legitimate routes with more-specific prefixes
steps.desc: Counter the hijack by announcing more-specific (longer prefix-length) legitimate routes to attract traffic back to the correct path.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with upstream transit providers to ensure the more-specific announcement propagates widely.
steps.outcome: Legitimate route regains preference across the majority of the internet.

steps.title: Engage upstream providers, IXPs, and the hijacking AS's network operator
steps.desc: Contact upstream transit providers and, where identifiable, the network operator of the hijacking AS to request the illegitimate announcement be withdrawn.
steps.guidance: Provide RPKI ROA evidence and routing registry (IRR) records to substantiate the legitimate ownership claim.
steps.outcome: Upstream providers filter the illegitimate announcement; hijacking AS operator engaged.

steps.title: Notify affected customers and internal stakeholders
steps.desc: Communicate the hijack event and its status to affected customers and internal stakeholders while remediation is underway.
steps.guidance: Coordinate messaging through Legal/PR given potential data-interception implications of traffic misdirection.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed with accurate status updates.

steps.title: Confirm withdrawal of the illegitimate announcement globally
steps.desc: Monitor global routing tables to confirm the illegitimate announcement has been withdrawn and legitimate routing is restored worldwide.
steps.guidance: Check multiple independent route-collector vantage points before declaring resolution.
steps.outcome: Illegitimate announcement confirmed withdrawn globally.

steps.title: Restore normal routing posture and validate traffic integrity
steps.desc: Return to standard route announcement practices and verify traffic is reaching legitimate infrastructure with no residual misdirection.
steps.guidance: Monitor closely for a sustained period to catch any recurrence.
