steps.outcome: Normal routing confirmed with no residual misdirection.

steps.title: Review RPKI/route-origin-validation coverage and hijack response speed
steps.desc: Assess whether RPKI ROA coverage, monitoring alerting, and response speed were adequate, and identify improvements.
steps.guidance: Recommend broader RPKI deployment and automated hijack-detection alerting.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54321.def: An attack in which company DNS resolution is poisoned, hijacked, or taken down, disrupting the ability of users or systems to reach company services, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than its DNS-attack mechanics.
ITID-54321.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for DNS poisoning or takedown within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to the detailed DNS attack technique breakdown tracked elsewhere in the taxonomy.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed DNS poisoning or takedown event affecting company domains
Confirmation that a DNS resolution failure affecting the company is adversarial rather than a registrar/provider operational failure
scopeExcludes: The detailed DNS cache-poisoning, registrar-account-compromise, or DNS-infrastructure-attack technique mechanics (see the applicable ITID-40000 DNS attack leaves)
Non-adversarial DNS/CDN provider outages (see ITID-54141/54142)
DDoS attacks specifically targeting DNS/CDN infrastructure (see ITID-54841)
ITID-54321.severity: Critical if company domains resolve to attacker-controlled infrastructure (enabling phishing/interception); High if domains simply become unresolvable.
ITID-54321.priority: P1, always, given the potential for both availability loss and downstream phishing/interception risk.
ITID-54321.escalation: Escalate immediately to network operations, the DNS/registrar provider, and communications/legal teams if attacker-controlled resolution is confirmed (customer-facing warning may be required).
indicators: Company domains resolving to unexpected/unauthorized IP addresses
Registrar account activity indicating unauthorized DNS record changes
Reports of users being redirected from legitimate company domains
vectors: Compromise of registrar or DNS provider account credentials used to alter records
Cache poisoning of an upstream or company-operated resolver
rootCauses: Lack of registrar/DNS account MFA or change-approval controls
Missing DNSSEC deployment
controls: Registrar/DNS provider account MFA and change-approval workflow
DNSSEC deployment
DNS change monitoring/alerting
ITID-54321.detection: DNS change monitoring and external resolution monitoring from multiple vantage points provide reliable detection.
ITID-54321.response: Immediately verify and, if unauthorized, revert DNS records; rotate registrar/provider credentials; notify affected users if attacker-controlled resolution was live.
metrics: Time to detect unauthorized DNS change
Time to revert and confirm clean resolution
Duration attacker-controlled resolution was live
ITID-54321.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed DNS attack technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General DNS Poisoning or Takedown (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: The organization's DNS resolution is poisoned or its authoritative DNS service is taken down, disrupting access to critical systems and services.

steps.title: Confirm DNS poisoning/takedown and identify affected records or infrastructure
steps.desc: Confirm whether DNS records have been maliciously altered (poisoning/hijacking) or authoritative DNS infrastructure is unavailable (takedown), and identify affected domains/records.
steps.guidance: Query authoritative and public resolvers from multiple vantage points to compare against expected DNS records; check registrar/DNS provider account activity logs for unauthorized changes.
steps.outcome: DNS issue confirmed and classified as poisoning or takedown with affected records/infrastructure identified.
steps.tool: DNS query tools / registrar audit logs

steps.title: Assess service and security impact of the DNS disruption
steps.desc: Determine which services are unreachable or misdirected, and assess whether poisoned records could be used for credential harvesting or further compromise.
steps.guidance: Prioritize checking authentication and payment-related domains for redirection risk.
steps.outcome: Impact and secondary-risk scope documented.

steps.title: Restore correct DNS records or fail over to a secondary DNS provider
steps.desc: Correct any maliciously altered DNS records, or fail over authoritative DNS service to a secondary provider if the primary is taken down.
steps.guidance: Lock the DNS zone/registrar account immediately after restoring records to prevent re-tampering.
steps.outcome: Correct DNS resolution restored via primary or secondary provider.

steps.title: Lock registrar/DNS accounts and rotate credentials
steps.desc: Enable registry lock, rotate all DNS/registrar account credentials, and enforce MFA to prevent further unauthorized changes.
steps.guidance: Verify no additional unauthorized changes (e.g., nameserver delegation changes) remain.
steps.outcome: Registrar/DNS accounts secured against further tampering.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and, if provider-caused, escalate to the DNS provider
steps.desc: Communicate impact to stakeholders and, if the takedown originated at the DNS provider, escalate through their support channel.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed; provider engaged if applicable.

steps.title: Confirm removal of attacker access and propagation of correct records globally
steps.desc: Verify the attacker no longer has access to DNS management and that correct records have propagated across resolvers globally, accounting for TTL/caching delays.
steps.guidance: Check multiple public resolvers worldwide to confirm consistent correct resolution.
steps.outcome: Attacker access removed; correct DNS resolution confirmed globally.

steps.title: Restore normal DNS operations and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Return to normal DNS operating posture and monitor closely for any renewed tampering attempts.
steps.guidance: Maintain heightened monitoring on DNS records for an extended period post-incident.
steps.outcome: Normal DNS operations confirmed stable with no recurrence.

steps.title: Review DNS security controls and account-protection posture
steps.desc: Assess whether registry lock, MFA, DNSSEC, and access controls on DNS/registrar accounts were adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend DNSSEC deployment and stricter registrar account controls where gaps are found.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54331.def: An attack or attack-driven disruption that degrades or takes down company VoIP telephony infrastructure, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact on voice communications.
ITID-54331.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for VoIP system disruption within the Critical System Disruption domain, tracking business impact to voice communications rather than the underlying attack technique.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed adversarial VoIP disruption (e.g., SIP flood, toll fraud causing service suspension, VoIP infrastructure DoS)
Loss of inbound/outbound calling capability for business-critical lines due to attack
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics of the DoS/flood technique used (see the applicable ITID-40000 DoS leaves)
Non-adversarial VoIP provider outages (a Third-Party SaaS Downtime matter, ITID-5491x)
General DDoS against company infrastructure that happens to include VoIP as one of many affected services (see ITID-548xx)
ITID-54331.severity: High if primary business or emergency-response voice lines are down; Medium if secondary/non-critical extensions are affected.
ITID-54331.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if customer support, sales, or safety-critical call lines are unreachable.
ITID-54331.escalation: Escalate to telecom/network operations and the VoIP provider; activate alternate communication channels (mobile failover, alternate provider) for critical functions.
indicators: Sudden inability to place or receive calls on business lines
Abnormal SIP traffic volume or call-setup failure rate
Unexpected toll-fraud charges or call routing to unauthorized destinations
vectors: SIP flood/DoS against VoIP infrastructure
Compromised VoIP credentials used for toll fraud triggering provider suspension
rootCauses: VoIP infrastructure exposed to the internet without adequate rate-limiting/authentication hardening
Lack of redundant voice communication channel for critical functions
controls: SIP session border controller with rate-limiting
Redundant/alternate voice communication channel for critical functions
VoIP credential hardening and monitoring
ITID-54331.detection: SIP traffic monitoring and call-detail-record anomaly detection provide the primary technical signal.
ITID-54331.response: Activate alternate communication channels for affected critical functions while telecom operations engages the provider and mitigates the flood/fraud source.
metrics: Time to restore voice service
Duration critical lines were unreachable
ITID-54331.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed DoS technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General VoIP System Disruption (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: The organization's VoIP telephony system is disrupted, degrading or eliminating voice communication capability for critical business functions.

steps.title: Confirm VoIP disruption scope and probable cause
steps.desc: Confirm the extent of call-quality degradation or outage across the VoIP platform and gather initial diagnostics on probable cause (provider, network, or attack-related such as TDoS).
steps.guidance: Check SIP trunk provider status, internal call-manager logs, and network QoS metrics.
steps.outcome: Disruption scope confirmed with probable cause category identified.

steps.title: Assess impact on critical business functions dependent on voice communication
steps.desc: Identify which business functions (e.g., customer support, emergency lines, call centers) are impacted and their criticality.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference with business continuity documentation for voice-dependent processes.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented by business criticality.

steps.title: Failover to backup SIP trunk provider or alternate communication channel
steps.desc: Redirect voice traffic to a secondary SIP trunk provider, PSTN fallback, or alternate communication tool to restore critical voice capability.
steps.guidance: Validate the failover path has sufficient capacity for critical call volumes.
steps.outcome: Critical voice communication restored via alternate path.
steps.abort: If no failover path is available, activate manual/alternate communication procedures (mobile phones, messaging apps) for critical functions.

steps.title: Escalate with the VoIP/SIP trunk provider and, if malicious, apply call filtering
steps.desc: Open a priority ticket with the provider and, if the disruption is attack-related (e.g., telephony denial of service), apply call filtering/rate limiting to malicious sources.
steps.outcome: Provider engaged; malicious traffic filtered if applicable.

steps.title: Notify affected teams and activate emergency-line contingency procedures
steps.desc: Inform business units relying on voice communication and activate any documented emergency-line contingency (e.g., alternate emergency contact numbers).
steps.guidance: Prioritize confirming continuity for any regulatory-required emergency lines.
steps.outcome: Affected teams informed; emergency-line contingency confirmed active if applicable.

steps.title: Confirm resolution of the underlying VoIP disruption cause
steps.desc: Verify the provider or internal team has resolved the underlying cause of the disruption.
steps.guidance: Validate call quality and connectivity across sample calls before declaring resolved.
steps.outcome: Underlying cause confirmed resolved.

steps.title: Restore primary VoIP routing and validate call quality
steps.desc: Return to the primary SIP trunk/routing configuration and confirm call quality and availability match baseline.
steps.guidance: Perform test calls across affected lines before declaring full recovery.
steps.outcome: Primary VoIP service restored with baseline call quality confirmed.

steps.title: Review voice-communication redundancy and failover readiness
steps.desc: Assess whether failover speed and redundant communication channels were adequate for critical business functions.
steps.guidance: Recommend additional redundancy or improved failover automation as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54341.def: A disruption to company connectivity caused by an attack against, or failure at, an internet service provider the company depends on, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact.
ITID-54341.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for ISP-level disruption within the Critical System Disruption domain, tracking business impact rather than the underlying attack or provider-failure technique.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed adversarial attack against an ISP the company depends on (e.g., ISP targeted by DDoS, ISP infrastructure compromise)
Company-wide connectivity loss traced to a single upstream ISP under attack
scopeExcludes: Non-adversarial ISP routing/operational failures (see ITID-54132)
The detailed technical mechanics of the attack against the ISP itself (out of the company's direct visibility; see the applicable ITID-40000 leaves for the general technique family)
ITID-54341.severity: High if single-homed to the affected ISP; Medium with multi-homed redundancy absorbing the loss.
ITID-54341.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if company-wide connectivity is lost with no failover path.
ITID-54341.escalation: Escalate to network operations and the ISP's NOC; activate secondary ISP failover.
indicators: ISP confirms it is under active attack (e.g., public disclosure of a DDoS incident)
Company-wide connectivity loss correlated to a single upstream provider with no internal cause identified
vectors: Volumetric DDoS against ISP infrastructure impacting all downstream customers including the company
rootCauses: Single-homed dependency on one ISP without secondary transit
controls: Multi-homed ISP connectivity
Documented ISP failover procedures
ITID-54341.detection: Network performance monitoring plus ISP public status communications provide the primary detection signal; root-cause attribution depends on ISP disclosure.
ITID-54341.response: Activate secondary ISP failover immediately; SOC monitors for any direct targeting of company assets distinct from the upstream ISP attack.
metrics: Time to failover to secondary ISP
Duration of connectivity loss
ITID-54341.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General ISP-Level Disruption (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: An internet service provider serving the organization experiences a disruption affecting the organization's connectivity to critical systems and services.

steps.title: Confirm ISP-level disruption via provider status and independent monitoring
steps.desc: Correlate internal connectivity loss with the ISP's status advisories and independent external monitoring to confirm the disruption originates at the ISP.
steps.guidance: Use multiple external vantage points and traceroute to isolate the failure to the ISP's network.
steps.outcome: Disruption confirmed as ISP-level with affected circuits/services identified.

steps.title: Assess impact on dependent sites and services
steps.desc: Determine which office locations, data centers, or services depend on the affected ISP circuit(s).
steps.guidance: Cross-reference network topology documentation.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Failover to a secondary ISP circuit or backup connectivity method
steps.desc: Shift traffic to a redundant ISP circuit, SD-WAN backup path, or cellular/satellite failover to restore connectivity.
steps.guidance: Verify the backup path has sufficient bandwidth for critical traffic.
steps.outcome: Connectivity restored via alternate path.
steps.abort: If no backup connectivity exists, prioritize critical traffic and notify affected sites of degraded capability.

steps.title: Escalate with the ISP and monitor restoration progress
steps.desc: Open a priority ticket with the ISP's support/NOC and track restoration progress.
steps.guidance: Reference SLA terms for priority handling.
steps.outcome: ISP engaged and providing status updates.

steps.title: Notify affected sites and business stakeholders
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption's status and expected resolution timeline to affected sites and business stakeholders.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Confirm ISP resolution and circuit stability
steps.desc: Verify the ISP has resolved the underlying issue and the circuit is stable before relying on it again.
steps.guidance: Monitor for a sustained stability period post-fix.
steps.outcome: Circuit confirmed stable.

steps.title: Restore primary connectivity and validate performance
steps.desc: Return traffic to the primary ISP circuit and confirm performance has returned to baseline.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased cutback with continuous monitoring.
steps.outcome: Primary connectivity restored with baseline performance confirmed.

steps.title: Review ISP redundancy and failover automation adequacy
steps.desc: Assess whether multi-ISP redundancy and failover speed met business continuity requirements.
steps.guidance: Recommend additional circuit diversity or automation improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54411.def: A disruption to a company critical-infrastructure function that is hosted in the cloud, where the disruption mechanism does not fall neatly into the already-covered cloud-outage, ransomware, network, or DDoS categories, tracked here as an intake/cross-reference leaf.
ITID-54411.purpose: Serves as the intake and cross-reference point for disruptions to cloud-hosted critical infrastructure that do not fit cleanly under the Infrastructure and Service Outages or DDoS groups elsewhere in this Tier-2.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported cloud-hosted critical-infrastructure disruptions pending classification against the more specific ITID-541xx/542xx/543xx/548xx leaves
Cloud-hosted OT/ICS supervisory or control functions disrupted by an event not yet attributed to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any event once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to the applicable specific leaf, e.g., ITID-54111 for a straightforward provider outage, or ITID-542xx for ransomware)
ITID-54411.severity: High to Critical pending triage, given the critical-infrastructure framing.
ITID-54411.priority: P1 pending triage; adjust once mechanism and scope are confirmed.
ITID-54411.escalation: Escalate to IT infrastructure, OT/engineering (if applicable), and SOC for immediate joint triage.
indicators: Cloud-hosted critical-infrastructure function unavailability without an established cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54411.detection: Relies on initial cloud service-health and application monitoring; deeper coverage established after reclassification.
ITID-54411.response: Rapidly triage to determine whether the cause is a straightforward provider outage, an attack, or another specific mechanism, then reclassify to the correct leaf.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Median time-to-reclassification
ITID-54411.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Critical Infrastructure Disruptions Tier-3, scoped specifically to cloud-hosted functions; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident. Cross-reference ITID-541xx, ITID-542xx, and ITID-548xx as appropriate once cause is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud-Based Critical Infrastructure Disruption
playbook.description: A cloud-hosted critical infrastructure component experiences a disruption whose specific cause has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm disruption to cloud-hosted critical infrastructure component
steps.desc: Gather monitoring alerts and initial diagnostics confirming the disruption to the cloud-hosted critical infrastructure component.
steps.guidance: Check cloud provider health dashboards alongside internal application monitoring to scope the disruption.
steps.outcome: Disruption confirmed with initial scope documented.

steps.title: Classify probable cause and criticality of affected function
steps.desc: Determine whether the cause is provider-side, configuration-related, or malicious, and assess the criticality of the affected infrastructure function.
steps.guidance: Escalate to the appropriate specialized playbook once a more specific cause is identified.
steps.outcome: Probable cause classified and criticality assessed.
steps.abort: If evidence indicates malicious activity, escalate to the relevant security incident-response track.

steps.title: Fail over to redundant infrastructure or alternate region
steps.desc: Redirect the critical function to redundant cloud infrastructure or an alternate region to restore availability.
steps.guidance: Validate failover target capacity and health before cutover.
steps.outcome: Critical function restored via redundant infrastructure.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and engage cloud provider support if applicable
steps.desc: Communicate impact to affected stakeholders and open a provider support case if the cause is provider-related.
steps.guidance: Provide clear impact scope and expected update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed; provider engaged if relevant.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix based on classification — configuration correction, provider-side resolution, or infrastructure repair.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the owning team or provider for controlled remediation.
steps.outcome: Root cause resolved and confirmed stable.

steps.title: Fail back and validate service integrity
steps.desc: Return the critical function to primary infrastructure and verify functionality and data integrity.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive health checks before declaring full recovery.
steps.outcome: Primary infrastructure fully operational with verified integrity.

steps.title: Confirm sustained stability post-failback
steps.desc: Monitor the restored critical function for a defined stabilization period to confirm no residual issues.
steps.guidance: Maintain heightened alerting thresholds during the observation window.
steps.outcome: Sustained stability confirmed with no recurrence.

steps.title: Document findings and evaluate redundancy adequacy
steps.desc: Capture lessons on detection speed, failover effectiveness, and whether redundancy for this critical infrastructure component is adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend infrastructure or process improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54511.def: Deliberate sabotage of company systems or services carried out by an individual with authorized access (employee, contractor, or trusted third party) intending to cause operational disruption.
ITID-54511.purpose: Captures deliberate, malicious disruption of company systems carried out by a trusted insider, tracked at the company-wide business-impact level for the disruption these acts cause.
scopeIncludes: Intentional shutdown, deletion, or disabling of production systems by an insider using their legitimate access
Deliberate revocation of critical access, licenses, or configurations by a departing or disgruntled insider intended to cause an outage
scopeExcludes: Accidental disruption caused by an insider's error (see Accidental Misconfigurations, ITID-54521)
Data corruption/deletion specifically (see Insider-Driven Data Corruption, ITID-5454x)
Privileged account misuse that has not yet caused disruption (see ITID-54531)
ITID-54511.severity: High to Critical depending on the scope of systems disrupted and whether the insider held privileged/administrative access.
ITID-54511.priority: P1 if the insider retains any residual access at time of discovery; P2 if access has already been fully revoked.
ITID-54511.escalation: Escalate immediately to HR, legal, and physical/personnel security in parallel with SOC; revoke all access for the individual across all systems as an emergency containment step.
indicators: Disruptive administrative actions performed by an employee outside their normal duties or hours, especially near termination/resignation
Access changes or service shutdowns immediately preceding a known adverse employment event
Use of access after an employee has given notice or been placed on leave
vectors: Abuse of legitimate administrative credentials to shut down or disable production services
Deliberate revocation of licenses, DNS records, or cloud resources
rootCauses: Delayed offboarding/access revocation after notice of termination or resignation
Excessive standing privileged access not tied to a monitored change-management process
controls: Prompt, automated offboarding/access revocation tied to HR events
Change-management approval workflow for production changes
User behavior analytics for anomalous administrative activity
ITID-54511.detection: Administrative action logging and user behavior analytics provide reasonable detection when correlated with HR events (termination, resignation, performance action).
ITID-54511.response: Immediately revoke all access for the individual across every system, preserve logs/evidence for HR and legal action, and assess scope of disruption for recovery.
metrics: Time from adverse HR event to access revocation
Scope of systems disrupted
Time to full access revocation upon detection
ITID-54511.notes: Lone-child leaf for malicious insider sabotage in the disruption context; data-corruption-specific insider acts are differentiated into their own sibling group (ITID-5454x).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malicious Insider Sabotage (Disruption Context)
playbook.description: An insider deliberately sabotages systems or infrastructure, causing critical system disruption, requiring coordinated HR/Legal/security response.

steps.title: Confirm sabotage activity and identify the responsible insider account(s)
steps.desc: Correlate system disruption indicators with user/account activity logs to confirm deliberate insider sabotage and identify the responsible account(s).
steps.guidance: Review privileged action logs, recent access changes, and abnormal administrative activity timed to the disruption.
steps.outcome: Sabotage confirmed with responsible account(s) identified.

steps.title: Assess scope of damage and ongoing access risk
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of systems affected and whether the insider retains active access that could enable further sabotage.
steps.guidance: Check for lingering active sessions, scheduled tasks, or additional accounts controlled by the same individual.
steps.outcome: Scope of damage and ongoing access risk documented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before taking any account action
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence (logs, session data, system state) before disabling access, to preserve evidentiary integrity for potential HR/legal/criminal proceedings.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal and HR on evidence handling procedures before further action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with documented chain of custody.

steps.title: Revoke the insider's access in coordination with HR and Legal
steps.desc: Disable the identified account(s) and revoke physical/logical access in a coordinated action with HR and Legal to ensure appropriate handling.
steps.guidance: Time access revocation to minimize opportunity for further damage while following HR's employee-action procedures.
steps.outcome: Insider access revoked; HR/Legal engaged on personnel action.

steps.title: Contain and stabilize affected systems
steps.desc: Take immediate technical action to stop ongoing disruption and stabilize affected systems.
steps.guidance: Prioritize restoring critical business function availability.
steps.outcome: Disruption halted; affected systems stabilized.

steps.title: Remove any additional unauthorized access or persistence
steps.desc: Search for and remove any additional accounts, backdoors, or scheduled tasks the insider may have established.
steps.guidance: Review all systems the insider had access to, not just the directly sabotaged ones.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized access and persistence mechanisms removed.

steps.title: Restore affected systems and verify integrity
steps.desc: Restore sabotaged systems from clean backups or manual reconstruction and verify data/system integrity.
steps.guidance: Validate no residual sabotage artifacts remain before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with verified integrity.

steps.title: Conduct joint HR/Legal/security post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate access-control, monitoring, and offboarding/behavioral-indicator gaps that allowed the sabotage.
steps.guidance: Recommend least-privilege and separation-of-duties improvements; involve HR and Legal in the review.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54521.def: A disruption to company systems or services caused by an authorized individual's unintentional misconfiguration, error, or omission, with no malicious intent involved.
ITID-54521.purpose: Captures unintentional service disruption caused by human error rather than malicious intent, tracked as an operational-continuity event rather than a threat to contain.
scopeIncludes: Accidental deletion of production resources during routine maintenance
Erroneous configuration change (firewall rule, DNS record, load balancer setting) causing an outage
Unintentional service shutdown during a maintenance window due to human error
scopeExcludes: Any case where investigation reveals deliberate intent (reclassify to Malicious Insider Sabotage, ITID-54511)
Provider-side configuration errors (see ITID-54141)
ITID-54521.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact rather than threat severity: High to Critical if the error affects business-critical production systems; Low to Medium for non-critical/dev-test environments.
ITID-54521.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the error affects customer-facing or safety-critical systems.
ITID-54521.escalation: Escalate to the responsible engineering/operations team for immediate remediation; SOC's role is to confirm absence of malicious intent and to close out the security-relevant portion of the review.
indicators: Change-management ticket or deployment log correlating directly with the outage onset
Individual reports the error themselves or it is evident from standard change records
No indicators of unauthorized access, data staging, or concealment
vectors: Not applicable — this is human error, not an attack
rootCauses: Inadequate change-management review/approval for high-risk changes
Lack of pre-production testing or staged rollout for configuration changes
Insufficient guardrails (e.g., confirmation prompts, blast-radius limits) on destructive operations
controls: Change-management approval workflow with peer review for high-risk changes
Staged/canary rollout for configuration changes
Guardrails and confirmation steps on destructive administrative operations
ITID-54521.detection: Change-management and deployment logs typically provide clear, high-confidence correlation to the responsible change; SOC verification is confirmatory rather than investigative.
ITID-54521.response: Revert or remediate the erroneous change; conduct a blameless post-incident review focused on process/tooling gaps rather than individual fault, framed around business continuity rather than threat containment.
metrics: Time to identify the causal change
Time to revert/remediate
Number of accidental-disruption incidents per quarter (change-management quality signal)
ITID-54521.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is human error, not an attack. It is grouped under Insider Threat-Driven Disruptions for taxonomy consistency (an authorized individual caused the disruption) but must be handled and reported as a business-continuity/process-improvement matter, not a threat investigation.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Accidental Misconfiguration Disruption
playbook.description: An unintentional configuration error by a staff member disrupts critical systems; response follows a blameless, non-punitive process to identify and correct the root cause.

steps.title: Confirm the disruption and correlate with recent configuration changes
steps.desc: Correlate the observed disruption with recent change-management records to identify the configuration change likely responsible.
steps.guidance: Review change-management tickets and infrastructure-as-code commit history around the time the disruption began.
steps.outcome: Responsible configuration change identified and confirmed as accidental (no malicious indicators).
steps.abort: If evidence suggests the change was unauthorized or malicious, escalate to the appropriate insider-threat procedure instead.

steps.title: Assess scope of impact from the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Determine which systems and services are affected by the misconfiguration.
steps.guidance: Use dependency mapping to trace downstream effects of the changed configuration.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Roll back the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Revert the configuration change to the last known-good state using change-management or infrastructure-as-code rollback procedures.
steps.guidance: Validate the rollback target is indeed the correct pre-incident state before applying.
steps.outcome: Configuration reverted, halting further impact.
steps.abort: If rollback is not straightforward, apply a manual corrective configuration under change-management supervision.

steps.title: Notify affected stakeholders in a blameless manner
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption and remediation status to affected stakeholders, framing the incident as a process/system gap rather than individual fault.
steps.guidance: Follow blameless-postmortem communication norms; avoid naming individuals in stakeholder communications.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed without punitive framing.

steps.title: Check for similar misconfigurations elsewhere in the environment
steps.desc: Search for the same or similar configuration pattern in other systems that may share the same root cause, to prevent recurrence elsewhere.
steps.guidance: Use configuration-scanning tools across the fleet for the same setting or pattern.
steps.outcome: Similar misconfigurations, if any, identified and scheduled for correction.

steps.title: Verify no residual effects of the misconfiguration remain
steps.desc: Check dependent systems for any lingering effects (cached bad state, downstream misconfigurations) caused by the original error.
steps.guidance: Run validation scripts across dependent systems.
steps.outcome: No residual misconfiguration effects remain.

steps.title: Restore full service and validate functionality
steps.desc: Confirm all affected systems are functioning normally following the rollback/correction.
steps.guidance: Run end-to-end smoke tests before closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Service confirmed fully operational.

steps.title: Conduct a blameless postmortem and improve change-management safeguards
steps.desc: Facilitate a blameless postmortem focused on process and tooling gaps (e.g., missing change-review, lack of staged rollout, insufficient validation) rather than individual blame.
steps.guidance: Recommend guardrails such as mandatory peer review, staged/canary deployments, or automated configuration validation.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked process-improvement actions, free of punitive framing.

ITID-54531.def: The use of legitimately assigned privileged access by an authorized individual in a manner inconsistent with their role or authorization, creating a risk of or actually causing service disruption.
ITID-54531.purpose: Captures misuse of legitimately held privileged access by an insider to cause or enable disruption, distinguishing account-abuse-in-progress from completed sabotage or accidental error.
scopeIncludes: Use of administrative access outside of approved change windows or documented business justification
Sharing or improper delegation of privileged credentials that is then used to cause disruption
Privilege escalation by an insider beyond their assigned role to reach disruption-capable systems
scopeExcludes: Completed, confirmed deliberate sabotage (see ITID-54511)
Accidental misuse without any policy violation (see ITID-54521)
ITID-54531.severity: Medium while abuse is detected but disruption has not yet occurred, escalating to High/Critical if disruption results.
ITID-54531.priority: P2 upon detection of abuse; escalate to P1 immediately if any disruption has occurred or appears imminent.
ITID-54531.escalation: Escalate to identity/access management and HR for policy violations; escalate to P1 incident response if disruption occurs.
indicators: Privileged actions taken outside approved change windows or without a corresponding ticket
Use of shared/delegated privileged credentials by someone other than the assigned owner
Privilege escalation attempts by an account with no corresponding business justification
vectors: Abuse of standing privileged access without corresponding change-management justification
rootCauses: Excessive standing privileged access not scoped to just-in-time need
Weak enforcement of change-management policy for privileged actions
controls: Just-in-time/least-privilege access model
Privileged access management (PAM) with session recording
Change-management enforcement for privileged actions
ITID-54531.detection: PAM session monitoring and privileged-action alerting against change-management records provide reasonable detection.
ITID-54531.response: Suspend the privileged access pending investigation; determine whether abuse resulted in or was intended to cause disruption, and escalate accordingly.
metrics: Number of privileged actions outside approved change windows
Time to suspend access upon detection
ITID-54531.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54511 by stage/intent-confirmation: this leaf covers detected misuse of standing privilege, whether or not disruption has yet resulted, rather than confirmed completed sabotage.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Privileged Account Abuse (Disruption Context)
playbook.description: A privileged account is abused — by an insider or a compromised credential — to cause critical system disruption, requiring evidence-preserving HR/Legal-coordinated response.

steps.title: Confirm privileged account abuse and distinguish insider misuse from external compromise
steps.desc: Correlate disruptive administrative actions with privileged-account activity logs to confirm abuse, and determine whether the account is being misused by its legitimate holder (insider) or by an external party using a compromised credential.
steps.guidance: Check login geolocation/device fingerprints, MFA logs, and behavior patterns against the account holder's normal usage baseline.
steps.outcome: Abuse confirmed with a working determination of insider vs. compromised-credential scenario.
steps.abort: If clear indicators of external compromise are found, treat access-recovery aspects per standard credential-compromise procedures alongside this playbook.

steps.title: Assess scope of disruptive actions taken with the privileged account
steps.desc: Enumerate all systems and changes affected by actions taken through the abused privileged account.
steps.guidance: Review full privileged-session activity logs for the relevant time window.
steps.outcome: Scope of disruptive actions documented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before revoking access
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence of the privileged account's activity before taking remediation action, given potential HR/legal implications.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence-handling procedures.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with documented chain of custody.

steps.title: Revoke or suspend the privileged account and rotate associated credentials
steps.desc: Disable the abused privileged account and rotate any credentials/secrets it had access to, coordinating with HR if insider misuse is confirmed.
steps.guidance: Consider broader credential rotation if the account had access to shared secrets or other privileged accounts.
steps.outcome: Abused account contained; associated credentials rotated.

steps.title: Stabilize systems affected by the disruptive actions
steps.desc: Take immediate technical action to halt and stabilize any ongoing disruption caused by the abused account's actions.
steps.guidance: Prioritize restoring critical business function availability.
steps.outcome: Disruption halted; affected systems stabilized.

steps.title: Remove any additional unauthorized changes or persistence
steps.desc: Review all systems the privileged account could access for additional unauthorized changes, backdoors, or persistence mechanisms.
steps.guidance: Do not assume the observed disruption was the only action taken with the account.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized changes and persistence removed.

steps.title: Restore affected systems and verify integrity
steps.desc: Restore affected systems to a known-good state and verify data/configuration integrity.
steps.guidance: Validate no residual unauthorized changes remain before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with verified integrity.

steps.title: Conduct joint HR/Legal/security post-incident review of privileged access controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate privileged access management, separation-of-duties, and monitoring gaps.
steps.guidance: Recommend just-in-time privileged access, session recording, or approval-workflow improvements.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54541.def: The deliberate, unauthorized modification or deletion of production database records by an insider using their legitimate access, intended to corrupt data integrity or cause operational disruption.
ITID-54541.purpose: Captures an insider's deliberate corruption or deletion of production database records, distinguishing targeted data manipulation from wholesale system-wiping.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate deletion of production database tables/records by an authorized individual
Unauthorized direct database edits intended to corrupt business data integrity
scopeExcludes: Wholesale destructive scripts targeting entire systems (see ITID-54542)
Deliberate corruption of backup data specifically (see ITID-54543)
Accidental database errors (see ITID-54521)
ITID-54541.severity: High to Critical depending on the business criticality of the affected data and whether clean backups exist.
ITID-54541.priority: P1 if production data integrity is confirmed compromised with no immediate clean restore point.
ITID-54541.escalation: Escalate immediately to database administration, HR, and legal; suspend the individual's access across all systems.
indicators: Direct database modification/deletion queries executed outside of application logic or approved change process
Query activity from an individual account inconsistent with their normal role
Deletion/modification timing correlated with a known adverse employment event
vectors: Direct database access used to execute unauthorized DELETE/UPDATE operations
rootCauses: Excessive direct database access not mediated through application-layer controls
Lack of database activity monitoring/alerting on bulk modification or deletion
controls: Database activity monitoring with alerting on bulk modification/deletion
Least-privilege database access mediated through application layer
Point-in-time database recovery capability
ITID-54541.detection: Database activity monitoring provides strong detection when direct-access logging and bulk-operation alerting are enabled.
ITID-54541.response: Suspend the individual's access immediately, restore affected data from the most recent clean point-in-time backup, and preserve database logs for HR/legal action.
metrics: Volume/scope of records corrupted or deleted
Time to restore from clean backup
Time to access suspension
ITID-54541.notes: Differentiated within its sibling group by target/method: targeted database record manipulation, as opposed to wholesale wiper deployment (ITID-54542) or backup-specific corruption (ITID-54543).

playbook.name: Deliberate Database Record Corruption/Deletion by Insider
playbook.description: An insider deliberately corrupts or deletes database records, requiring urgent scope-of-damage assessment and coordinated HR/Legal response.

steps.title: Confirm deliberate record corruption/deletion and identify the responsible account
steps.desc: Correlate database audit logs with the observed data anomalies to confirm deliberate (not accidental) corruption/deletion and identify the responsible account.
steps.guidance: Review database transaction logs, query history, and access patterns for intentional bulk deletion/modification outside normal application behavior.
steps.outcome: Deliberate action confirmed with responsible account identified.
steps.abort: If evidence suggests an application bug or accidental cause rather than deliberate action, redirect to a standard data-integrity incident procedure.

steps.title: Urgently assess scope of data damage and identify last-known-good state
steps.desc: Determine the full extent of corrupted/deleted records and identify the most recent point-in-time backup or transaction log state that predates the damage.
steps.guidance: Treat scope assessment as urgent — delays increase risk of the damage propagating through downstream systems or being backed up over clean data.
steps.outcome: Scope of damage documented and last-known-good recovery point identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and immediately revoke the insider's database access
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence of the responsible account's activity, then immediately revoke its database access to prevent further damage.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal on evidence handling before/during access revocation.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; further access halted.

steps.title: Halt automated processes that could propagate or overwrite corrupted data
steps.desc: Pause scheduled backups, replication, or ETL jobs that could overwrite clean backup copies with corrupted data or propagate the corruption to downstream systems.
steps.guidance: Identify all replication/backup jobs touching the affected database before pausing.
steps.outcome: Propagation of corrupted data halted.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal for coordinated personnel action
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR and Legal on personnel action against the responsible insider, informed by preserved evidence.
steps.guidance: Follow HR's standard investigation and disciplinary procedures.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged and personnel action coordinated appropriately.

steps.title: Remove any additional unauthorized access or lingering database changes
steps.desc: Check for additional accounts, triggers, or scheduled jobs the insider may have created to hide or extend the damage.
steps.guidance: Review database object permissions and scheduled job definitions comprehensively.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized access and hidden changes removed.

steps.title: Restore corrupted/deleted records from the identified clean recovery point
steps.desc: Restore the affected database records from the last-known-good backup or point-in-time recovery, validating data integrity and referential consistency.
steps.guidance: Reconcile any legitimate transactions that occurred between the recovery point and the corruption event to avoid losing valid data.
steps.outcome: Records restored with verified integrity and minimal legitimate data loss.

steps.title: Conduct joint HR/Legal/security review of database access controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate database access controls, audit logging, and separation-of-duties gaps.
steps.guidance: Recommend row-level auditing, restricted bulk-operation permissions, or approval workflows for destructive operations.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54542.def: An insider's deliberate deployment of a destructive script or tool designed to erase, corrupt, or render unusable data or system state across multiple critical systems at once.
ITID-54542.purpose: Captures an insider's use of a wiper-style destructive script or tool against critical systems, distinguishing broad, automated destruction from targeted database record manipulation.
scopeIncludes: Deployment of a custom or off-the-shelf destructive/wiper script by an authorized individual against production or critical infrastructure systems
Mass file deletion or disk-wiping actions performed programmatically across multiple hosts
scopeExcludes: Targeted manipulation of specific database records (see ITID-54541)
Corruption specifically targeting backup data (see ITID-54543)
ITID-54542.severity: Critical — wiper-style deployment typically causes broad, fast-moving, difficult-to-reverse destruction across multiple systems.
ITID-54542.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, HR, and legal; isolate the responsible account and any systems it can still reach as an emergency containment step.
indicators: Execution of an unfamiliar or unauthorized script with mass file-deletion/disk-wipe behavior
Rapid, correlated data-loss events across multiple hosts traceable to a single account
Script or tool staged shortly before execution by the same account
vectors: Custom or publicly available wiper/destructive script executed using legitimate administrative access
rootCauses: Excessive standing access allowing a single account to reach many critical systems
Lack of application allowlisting/execution controls on administrative endpoints
controls: Application allowlisting on privileged/administrative endpoints
Behavioral detection for mass file-deletion activity
Least-privilege segmentation limiting single-account blast radius
ITID-54542.detection: Endpoint behavioral detection for mass file-deletion/disk-wipe activity provides strong technical detection when EDR coverage extends to the affected systems.
ITID-54542.response: Immediately isolate the account and any reachable systems; assess scope of destruction and restore from clean backups; preserve forensic evidence for legal action.
metrics: Number of systems affected
Time to isolate the responsible account
Recovery time from clean backup
ITID-54542.notes: Differentiated within its sibling group by scale and method: automated, multi-system destructive tooling, as opposed to targeted database manipulation (ITID-54541) or backup-specific corruption (ITID-54543).

playbook.name: Insider Deploying Wiper-Style Script Against Critical Systems
playbook.description: An insider deploys a destructive wiper-style script against critical systems, causing irreversible data/system loss and requiring urgent scope-of-damage assessment.

steps.title: Confirm wiper activity and identify the responsible insider account
steps.desc: Confirm destructive wiper behavior (mass file/data deletion, disk-wipe commands, corrupted boot records) and correlate with account activity to identify the responsible insider, treating this as a high-urgency event given irreversible impact.
steps.guidance: Check EDR/SIEM for execution of destructive commands/scripts and correlate timing with privileged account sessions.
steps.outcome: Wiper activity confirmed with responsible account identified; urgency elevated given irreversibility.

steps.title: Urgently assess scope of destruction across systems
steps.desc: Rapidly determine which systems have been wiped, which are actively being targeted, and which remain untouched.
steps.guidance: Prioritize speed — wiper attacks can spread or execute across multiple systems within minutes.
steps.outcome: Scope of destruction and at-risk systems documented urgently.

steps.title: Immediately isolate the insider's access and any systems not yet wiped
steps.desc: Revoke the responsible account's access and isolate/power down systems not yet affected to prevent the wiper script from reaching them.
steps.guidance: Act with maximum urgency — every additional minute risks further irreversible loss.
steps.outcome: Further destruction halted; unaffected systems protected.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence from wiped and unaffected systems
steps.desc: Capture whatever forensic evidence remains (partial disk images, logs shipped to a SIEM before destruction, network telemetry) to support investigation and any legal proceedings.
steps.guidance: Prioritize evidence from centralized/off-host logging sources since local evidence on wiped systems may be unrecoverable.
steps.outcome: Available evidence preserved with documented chain of custody.

steps.title: Engage Legal, HR, and law enforcement given the severity of destructive action
steps.desc: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and law enforcement given the deliberate, destructive, and potentially criminal nature of the act.
steps.outcome: Legal, HR, and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Remove any remaining wiper artifacts or scheduled destructive tasks
steps.desc: Search all systems the insider had access to for additional staged wiper scripts, scheduled tasks, or persistence intended for delayed execution.
steps.guidance: Do not assume the observed destruction was the only staged action.
steps.outcome: All destructive artifacts and persistence removed.

steps.title: Rebuild wiped systems and restore data from backups
steps.desc: Rebuild destroyed systems from clean media and restore data from the most recent verified-clean backups, accepting that data created after the last backup may be permanently lost.
steps.guidance: Validate restored data integrity before returning systems to production.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and restored with maximum feasible data recovery confirmed.
steps.abort: If no backup exists for certain systems, escalate to business continuity planning for manual reconstruction or documented data loss.

steps.title: Conduct joint HR/Legal/security post-incident review of insider-risk controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate insider-threat detection, privileged access controls, and backup resilience against destructive insider action.
steps.guidance: Recommend behavioral monitoring, least-privilege enforcement, and immutable backup investments.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54543.def: The deliberate, unauthorized corruption or deletion of backup data by an insider using their legitimate access, intended to prevent recovery from data loss or system disruption.
ITID-54543.purpose: Captures an insider's deliberate corruption of backup data specifically, to prevent recovery from a related or separate disruptive act, distinguishing the backup-targeting angle from production-data manipulation.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate deletion or corruption of backup repositories/snapshots by an authorized individual
Disabling or reconfiguring backup jobs by an insider to prevent future recoverable copies from being created
scopeExcludes: Backup encryption/corruption performed by external ransomware actors (see ITID-54231/54232)
Targeted production database manipulation without backup involvement (see ITID-54541)
ITID-54543.severity: Critical — corrupting backups removes the organization's recovery safety net, compounding the impact of any related disruption.
ITID-54543.priority: P1, always; treat as removing the organization's last line of defense against data loss.
ITID-54543.escalation: Escalate immediately to backup/infrastructure teams, HR, and legal; assess for any surviving offline/immutable copy immediately.
indicators: Unauthorized deletion or modification of backup repository contents by an insider account
Backup job disablement or reconfiguration outside of approved change process by the same individual
Timing correlated with a separate act of sabotage or a known adverse employment event
vectors: Direct access to backup infrastructure used to delete or corrupt stored backups
Disabling backup schedules/jobs to silently stop future protection
rootCauses: Backup administration access not separated from general IT administrative access
Lack of immutable/offline backup copies resistant to insider deletion
controls: Immutable/WORM backup storage resistant to deletion by any single account
Segregation of duties for backup administration
Backup job change monitoring/alerting
ITID-54543.detection: Backup-storage integrity monitoring and job-change alerting provide direct detection when instrumented.
ITID-54543.response: Immediately assess for any surviving immutable/offline backup copy; suspend the individual's access and preserve evidence for legal action.
metrics: Availability of surviving clean backup copies
Time to access suspension
ITID-54543.notes: Differentiated within its sibling group by target: backup data specifically, as opposed to production database records (ITID-54541) or wholesale multi-system wiping (ITID-54542).

playbook.name: Insider Corrupting Backup Data to Prevent Recovery
playbook.description: An insider deliberately corrupts backup data to prevent recovery from a related or planned disruption, requiring urgent scope assessment and coordinated response.

steps.title: Confirm deliberate backup corruption and identify the responsible account
steps.desc: Correlate backup system audit logs with observed corruption to confirm deliberate insider action and identify the responsible account.
steps.guidance: Review backup software administrative logs for unusual retention-policy changes, job deletions, or manual data manipulation.
steps.outcome: Deliberate corruption confirmed with responsible account identified.

steps.title: Urgently assess remaining recoverable backup scope and related disruption risk
steps.desc: Determine what backup data, if any, remains uncorrupted, and assess whether this action is a precursor to a broader planned disruption (e.g., accompanying sabotage or data destruction).
steps.guidance: Treat this with urgency similar to a ransomware backup-targeting scenario given the loss-of-recovery-capability risk.
steps.outcome: Remaining recoverable backup scope documented; related disruption risk assessed.

steps.title: Immediately isolate any surviving backup copies and revoke insider access
steps.desc: Air-gap or disconnect any surviving backup copies from the network and revoke the responsible insider's access to backup infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Prioritize this above investigative depth — protecting remaining backups is time-critical.
steps.outcome: Surviving backups protected; insider access to backup systems revoked.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage HR/Legal
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence of the insider's backup-tampering activity and engage HR and Legal for coordinated personnel and evidentiary handling.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged.

steps.title: Check for related sabotage or ongoing disruption elsewhere in the environment
steps.desc: Given backup corruption often accompanies a broader planned disruption, check other systems the insider accessed for signs of related sabotage.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the security monitoring team for a broader sweep.
steps.outcome: Related sabotage, if any, identified and contained.

steps.title: Remove insider persistence and any additional backup-tampering mechanisms
steps.desc: Review backup infrastructure and related systems for additional unauthorized changes or persistence established by the insider.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized access and tampering mechanisms removed.

steps.title: Rebuild backup infrastructure with hardened, immutable configuration and recover maximum feasible data
steps.desc: Reconstruct backup infrastructure with immutable/offline protections and restricted administrative access, and recover what data is feasible from surviving or alternate copies.
steps.guidance: Engage data-recovery specialists if backups are largely unrecoverable.
steps.outcome: Hardened backup infrastructure rebuilt; maximum feasible data recovered.

steps.title: Conduct joint HR/Legal/security review of backup access controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate access controls, separation of duties, and monitoring gaps in backup infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Recommend immutable backups, restricted administrative access, and anomaly alerting on backup configuration changes.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54544.def: An insider-driven data-corruption event that has not yet been classified as targeted database manipulation, wiper-style destruction, or backup corruption.
ITID-54544.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for insider-driven data corruption events not yet attributed to a specific target (database, wiper tooling, or backup).
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed insider data-corruption events pending target/method confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once target/method is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54541, 54542, or 54543)
ITID-54544.severity: High to Critical pending triage, given the insider-access context.
ITID-54544.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, and SOC for immediate joint triage; suspend the individual's access pending investigation.
indicators: Unauthorized data-integrity impact traced to an insider account, target/method not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54544.detection: Relies on initial database/endpoint/backup monitoring alerting; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54544.response: Suspend access immediately while triage determines target/method for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54544.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Insider-Driven Data Corruption
playbook.description: An insider causes data corruption of undetermined specific method (database, wiper, or backup-targeted), requiring urgent scope assessment and coordinated response.

steps.title: Confirm insider-driven data corruption and identify the responsible account
steps.desc: Correlate audit logs with observed data corruption to confirm deliberate insider action and identify the responsible account.
steps.guidance: Review relevant system/database/backup audit logs for intentional actions outside normal behavior.
steps.outcome: Insider action confirmed with responsible account identified.

steps.title: Urgently assess scope and method of corruption
steps.desc: Determine the specific method used (database manipulation, destructive script, backup tampering) and the full scope of affected data/systems.
steps.guidance: Escalate to the more specific insider-corruption procedure once the method is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Scope and method documented, enabling targeted response.

steps.title: Immediately revoke the insider's access across all systems
steps.desc: Revoke the responsible account's access to prevent further corruption, after evidence preservation considerations are addressed.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with Legal/HR to preserve evidentiary value where feasible.
steps.outcome: Insider access revoked; further corruption halted.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and protect any surviving clean data/backups
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence and isolate any surviving clean backup copies or data stores from further risk.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; surviving clean data protected.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal for coordinated personnel action
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR and Legal on personnel action against the responsible insider.
steps.guidance: Follow standard HR investigation and disciplinary procedures.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged.

steps.title: Remove any additional unauthorized access or persistence
steps.desc: Review all systems the insider accessed for additional unauthorized changes or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized access and persistence removed.

steps.title: Restore affected data from the most recent clean recovery point
steps.desc: Restore corrupted data from clean backups or reconstruction, validating integrity and reconciling any legitimate changes since the recovery point.
steps.outcome: Data restored with verified integrity and minimal legitimate data loss.

steps.title: Conduct joint HR/Legal/security review of access controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate access control, monitoring, and separation-of-duties gaps.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements to detection and privileged access management.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54611.def: An operational failure in which an attempt to roll back a failed software deployment does not restore service, resulting in an extended outage beyond the initial deployment failure.
ITID-54611.purpose: Captures the operational-failure scenario where a rollback of a failed deployment does not succeed, extending an outage beyond the original deployment failure window.
scopeIncludes: Rollback procedure failing to fully revert application or infrastructure state
Rollback introducing a new, secondary failure (e.g., data schema mismatch after reverting code)
Extended outage duration directly attributable to rollback failure rather than the original deployment issue
scopeExcludes: The original deployment failure itself if rollback succeeds normally (see ITID-54612)
Deliberate tampering with deployment/rollback tooling (see Code Injection and Tampering, ITID-5464x)
ITID-54611.severity: High to Critical, scaled by total outage duration and business criticality of the affected service; frame around business-continuity impact.
ITID-54611.priority: P1 while the outage remains extended with no clear resolution path; downgrade once service is restored.
ITID-54611.escalation: Escalate to engineering leadership and site reliability/DevOps teams; consider manual/alternate restoration procedures if automated rollback continues to fail.
indicators: Rollback job/pipeline reports failure or partial completion
Service remains degraded or unavailable after rollback is reported complete
Error signatures inconsistent with the original deployment issue, indicating a new rollback-induced problem
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial operational failure
rootCauses: Rollback procedures not regularly tested against current production state
Database schema or data migrations not designed to be reversible
Insufficient automated validation before declaring rollback successful
controls: Regularly tested, automated rollback procedures
Backward-compatible/reversible database migration practices
Post-rollback automated health validation gating
ITID-54611.detection: Deployment pipeline telemetry and service health monitoring provide direct, high-confidence detection of rollback failure.
ITID-54611.response: Engage engineering to manually restore service using an alternate path (e.g., restore from a known-good artifact or infrastructure snapshot) if automated rollback cannot be made to succeed quickly.
metrics: Total outage duration including rollback failure time
Number of rollback attempts before successful restoration
ITID-54611.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational software-release failure, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Rollback Failure Extending Outage Duration
playbook.description: An attempt to roll back a failed software deployment itself fails, extending the outage duration and requiring escalated change-management response.

steps.title: Confirm rollback failure and current system state
steps.desc: Confirm that the rollback procedure did not restore the previous working state and determine the current (possibly partially rolled-back) state of affected systems.
steps.guidance: Check deployment/rollback pipeline logs and application health checks to characterize the failed rollback's effects.
steps.outcome: Rollback failure confirmed with current system state documented.

steps.title: Assess extended business impact from the prolonged outage
steps.desc: Reassess business impact given the outage is now extended beyond the original expected rollback window.
steps.guidance: Update stakeholders on revised impact and timeline expectations.
steps.outcome: Updated impact assessment documented.

steps.title: Halt further automated rollback/deployment attempts and stabilize manually
steps.desc: Stop any automated pipeline from making further changes and manually stabilize the environment to prevent compounding the issue.
steps.guidance: Freeze the environment in its current state while a manual remediation plan is formed.
steps.outcome: Environment stabilized with no further automated changes occurring.

steps.title: Escalate to senior engineering and change-advisory leadership
steps.desc: Escalate the failed rollback to senior engineering leadership and the change-advisory board for a decision on manual remediation approach.
steps.guidance: Provide clear options: manual rollback, forward-fix, or full environment rebuild.
steps.outcome: Senior leadership engaged and remediation approach decided.

steps.title: Execute manual remediation to reach a known-good state
steps.desc: Manually restore the previous working configuration/version, or apply a forward-fix, based on the decided remediation approach.
steps.guidance: Validate each step against a checklist to avoid repeating the rollback failure.
steps.outcome: System reaches a confirmed known-good, stable state.
steps.abort: If manual remediation is not achievable in a reasonable timeframe, escalate to full environment rebuild from infrastructure-as-code and clean data restore.

steps.title: Validate rollback pipeline integrity for future use
steps.desc: Investigate why the automated rollback mechanism itself failed and confirm the pipeline is trustworthy before relying on it again.
steps.guidance: Test the rollback path in a staging environment before it is used again in production.
steps.outcome: Rollback pipeline validated and confirmed reliable, or replaced with a documented manual procedure.

steps.title: Restore full service and validate functionality
steps.desc: Confirm all affected systems and services are functioning normally following manual remediation.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive smoke tests across all affected functionality.
steps.outcome: Service confirmed fully operational.

steps.title: Review deployment/rollback pipeline reliability and change-management process
steps.desc: Conduct a blameless review of why the rollback mechanism failed and what change-management safeguards (staged rollout, automated rollback testing) should be added.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements to rollback testing and deployment pipeline resilience.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked process-improvement actions.

ITID-54612.def: An operational failure in which a configuration change that was not adequately tested prior to deployment causes a production service outage.
ITID-54612.purpose: Captures the operational-failure scenario where an untested configuration change directly causes a production outage, distinguishing the root-cause pattern from a rollback subsequently failing.
scopeIncludes: Firewall, load balancer, DNS, or application configuration change deployed without adequate pre-production testing that causes an outage
Configuration drift introduced through an untested manual change
scopeExcludes: Failure of the subsequent rollback attempt itself (see ITID-54611)
Deliberate malicious configuration tampering (see Code Injection and Tampering, ITID-5464x, or Malicious Insider Sabotage, ITID-54511)
ITID-54612.severity: High to Critical depending on the criticality of the affected system; frame around business-continuity impact.
ITID-54612.priority: P1 if customer-facing production is down; P2 for internal/non-critical systems.
ITID-54612.escalation: Escalate to the change owner's engineering team and change-management leadership for immediate revert.
indicators: Outage onset immediately follows a recent configuration change in the change log
Error signatures directly attributable to the changed configuration parameter
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial operational failure
rootCauses: Configuration change deployed without pre-production/staging validation
Inadequate change-management review for the risk level of the change
Lack of automated configuration validation/linting before deployment
controls: Pre-production/staging validation requirement for configuration changes
Automated configuration validation/linting in the deployment pipeline
Change-management risk-based review process
ITID-54612.detection: Change-management logs and service health monitoring provide direct, high-confidence correlation between the change and the outage.
ITID-54612.response: Revert the configuration change immediately; conduct a blameless post-incident review of the change-management gap.
metrics: Time to identify the causal configuration change
Time to revert
Number of untested-change outages per quarter
ITID-54612.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational change-management failure, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Deployment Failure Due to Untested Configuration Change
playbook.description: A software deployment fails in production because an accompanying configuration change was not adequately tested, causing critical system disruption.

steps.title: Confirm the failure and correlate with the untested configuration change
steps.desc: Correlate the production failure with the deployment's configuration change to confirm it as the root cause.
steps.guidance: Review deployment logs, configuration diffs, and the change-management ticket for testing coverage gaps.
steps.outcome: Configuration change confirmed as the root cause of the failure.
steps.tool: CI/CD pipeline logs / change management system

steps.title: Assess business impact and affected systems
steps.desc: Determine which systems and business functions are affected by the deployment failure.
steps.guidance: Use dependency mapping to trace downstream effects.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Roll back the deployment and configuration change
steps.desc: Revert the deployment and its configuration change to the last known-good state.
steps.guidance: Use the standard rollback pipeline; verify the rollback target is correct.
steps.outcome: Deployment rolled back, halting further impact.
steps.abort: If automated rollback fails, escalate to manual remediation procedures.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders of the disruption and rollback status
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption and remediation status to affected stakeholders.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Verify no residual effects of the failed configuration remain
steps.desc: Check dependent systems for lingering effects of the failed configuration change.
steps.guidance: Run validation scripts across dependent systems.
steps.outcome: No residual effects remain.

steps.title: Restore full service and validate functionality
steps.desc: Confirm all affected systems are functioning normally following rollback.
steps.guidance: Run end-to-end smoke tests before closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Service confirmed fully operational.

steps.title: Re-plan the configuration change with adequate testing
steps.desc: Develop a revised deployment plan for the configuration change that includes staged rollout and adequate pre-production testing.
steps.guidance: Require sign-off from testing/QA before the next deployment attempt.
steps.outcome: Revised deployment plan with testing safeguards documented.

steps.title: Review testing and change-management process gaps
steps.desc: Conduct a blameless review of why the configuration change was not adequately tested and recommend process safeguards.
steps.guidance: Recommend mandatory staging environment testing, canary deployments, or automated configuration validation.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked process-improvement actions.

ITID-54613.def: A failed software deployment causing production impact that has not yet been classified as a rollback failure or an untested-configuration-change failure.
ITID-54613.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for failed software deployment events not yet attributed to rollback failure or untested configuration change.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported deployment failures pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any failure once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54611 or 54612)
ITID-54613.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54613.priority: P2 pending triage; P1 if customer-facing production is already confirmed down.
ITID-54613.escalation: Escalate to engineering/DevOps for initial triage.
indicators: Deployment-correlated service degradation without an established specific cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54613.detection: Relies on initial deployment pipeline and service health monitoring only.
ITID-54613.response: Triage to rollback-failure or untested-configuration-change cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54613.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Failed Software Deployment
playbook.description: A software deployment fails and disrupts critical systems, with the specific failure mode not yet determined.

steps.title: Confirm the deployment failure and gather initial diagnostics
steps.desc: Confirm the deployment has caused a disruption and gather initial diagnostic data (error logs, health checks, deployment pipeline status).
steps.guidance: Check deployment pipeline status and application health dashboards.
steps.outcome: Deployment failure confirmed with initial diagnostics documented.

steps.title: Assess business impact and affected systems
