steps.desc: Determine which systems and business functions are affected by the deployment failure.
steps.guidance: Use dependency mapping to trace downstream effects.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Roll back the deployment
steps.desc: Revert the deployment to the last known-good state using the standard rollback procedure.
steps.guidance: Verify the rollback target is correct before applying.
steps.outcome: Deployment rolled back, halting further impact.
steps.abort: If rollback fails, escalate to manual remediation procedures per the rollback-failure playbook.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders of the disruption and remediation status
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption and remediation status to affected stakeholders.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Verify no partial-deployment inconsistency remains across the fleet
steps.desc: Check whether the failed deployment left some instances/nodes on the new version and others on the old, creating an inconsistent fleet state.
steps.guidance: Query the deployment orchestrator's per-instance version status.
steps.outcome: Fleet version consistency confirmed or corrected.

steps.title: Identify the specific root cause of the deployment failure
steps.desc: Investigate the deployment to determine the specific failure mode (code defect, untested configuration, infrastructure incompatibility, etc.).
steps.guidance: Review deployment logs, test coverage, and change records.
steps.outcome: Specific root cause identified and documented.

steps.title: Restore full service and validate functionality
steps.desc: Confirm all affected systems are functioning normally following rollback.
steps.guidance: Run end-to-end smoke tests before closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Service confirmed fully operational.

steps.title: Review deployment process and testing safeguards
steps.desc: Conduct a blameless review of the deployment failure and recommend process improvements (staged rollout, automated testing, canary deployments).
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked process-improvement actions.

ITID-54621.def: A confirmed compromise resulting from exploitation of a vulnerability for which a critical patch was available but had not yet been applied within the vendor-recommended timeframe.
ITID-54621.purpose: Captures the specific scenario where a critical patch was delayed past the vendor-recommended timeline and the resulting exposure window was then exploited, tying patch-management delay directly to a successful attack.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known, patchable vulnerability on a system past its patch SLA
Confirmed compromise where patch-deployment delay is established as the enabling root cause
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of an end-of-life system for which no patch exists at all (see ITID-54622)
Delayed patching that did not result in confirmed exploitation (a vulnerability-management/patch-compliance metric, not this ITID)
ITID-54621.severity: High to Critical depending on the criticality of the exploited system and the nature of post-exploitation activity observed.
ITID-54621.priority: P1 upon confirmation of active exploitation.
ITID-54621.escalation: Escalate to vulnerability management leadership and the system owner in parallel with standard intrusion incident escalation.
indicators: Exploit activity matching a CVE for which an internal patch record shows the fix was available but not deployed
Patch-compliance/vulnerability-scan history showing the system was known non-compliant prior to the incident
vectors: Exploitation of a public-facing application or service running unpatched, publicly known vulnerable software
rootCauses: Patch SLA not enforced or not tracked for the affected system
Patching deferred due to change-freeze or business-continuity concerns without compensating controls
controls: Enforced patch SLA with executive-visible compliance reporting
Compensating controls (WAF/virtual patching) for systems awaiting patch deployment
Vulnerability scanning with exploitability prioritization
ITID-54621.detection: Vulnerability scan history combined with exploit/IOC detection at the point of compromise provides strong retrospective correlation.
ITID-54621.response: Handle as a standard intrusion incident for containment and eradication; in parallel, drive a vulnerability-management corrective action review to close the SLA gap.
metrics: Days between patch availability and exploitation
Patch SLA compliance rate for critical vulnerabilities
Time to contain the resulting intrusion
detections: Exploit/IOC detection at the network or endpoint layer
ITID-54621.notes: Distinguished from ITID-54622 in that a patch existed and was available but not yet applied, rather than the system being unpatchable due to end-of-life status.

playbook.name: Critical Patch Delayed Past Vendor-Recommended Timeline, Then Exploited
playbook.description: A critical security patch was not applied within the vendor-recommended timeline, and an attacker subsequently exploited the unpatched vulnerability to disrupt critical systems.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation of the known unpatched vulnerability
steps.desc: Correlate observed compromise/disruption indicators with the specific CVE that remained unpatched past the vendor's recommended timeline.
steps.guidance: Check EDR/SIEM alerts and exploit signatures matching the known vulnerability; confirm the affected system's patch status.
steps.outcome: Exploitation of the known vulnerability confirmed on identified systems.

steps.title: Assess scope of compromise and attacker actions taken
steps.desc: Determine what the attacker accessed, modified, or disrupted after exploiting the vulnerability.
steps.guidance: Perform timeline analysis from initial exploitation to current state.
steps.outcome: Scope of compromise and attacker actions documented.

steps.title: Isolate the exploited system(s) from the network
steps.desc: Disconnect or segment the affected systems to halt further attacker activity.
steps.guidance: Preserve system state for forensic analysis where possible before isolation.
steps.outcome: Attacker activity contained.

steps.title: Apply the overdue critical patch immediately across the environment
steps.desc: Urgently deploy the vendor patch to the exploited system and any other systems sharing the same unpatched vulnerability.
steps.guidance: Treat this as an emergency change; expedite through change-management with appropriate approvals.
steps.outcome: Patch applied enterprise-wide to close the exploited vulnerability.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and revoke attacker-established access
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for accounts accessible from the exploited system and revoke any unauthorized access the attacker established.
steps.outcome: Attacker access revoked; exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Remove attacker persistence and malicious artifacts
steps.desc: Sweep affected systems for backdoors, webshells, or other persistence mechanisms installed via the exploit.
steps.guidance: Reimage systems where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed free of attacker persistence.

steps.title: Restore affected systems and validate functionality
steps.desc: Restore any disrupted systems/data and confirm functionality and data integrity.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive validation before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with verified integrity.

steps.title: Review patch-management SLA adherence and prioritization process
steps.desc: Document why the critical patch timeline was missed and recommend improvements to patch-prioritization and SLA-enforcement processes.
steps.guidance: Recommend automated patch-compliance tracking and escalation for overdue critical patches.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked patch-management improvement actions.

ITID-54622.def: A confirmed compromise resulting from exploitation of a vulnerability on a system that has reached vendor end-of-life status and no longer receives security patches.
ITID-54622.purpose: Captures the specific scenario where a system past its vendor end-of-life, and therefore no longer eligible for security patches, was exploited, tying unsupported-software risk directly to a successful attack.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known vulnerability on an end-of-life operating system, application, or firmware with no available vendor fix
Confirmed compromise where EOL/unsupported status is established as the enabling root cause
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a currently supported system where a patch existed but was simply not yet applied (see ITID-54621)
ITID-54622.severity: High to Critical depending on the criticality of the exploited system and the nature of post-exploitation activity observed.
ITID-54622.priority: P1 upon confirmation of active exploitation.
ITID-54622.escalation: Escalate to IT asset management/vulnerability management leadership regarding the EOL inventory gap, in parallel with standard intrusion incident escalation.
indicators: Exploit activity against a system confirmed to be past vendor end-of-support/end-of-life
Asset inventory or vulnerability-scan records flagging the system as unsupported prior to the incident
vectors: Exploitation of remote services on a legacy, unsupported system exposed to the network
rootCauses: Business/application dependency preventing timely decommission or upgrade of an EOL system
Lack of a tracked EOL inventory with compensating-control requirements
controls: Tracked EOL/unsupported-asset inventory with mandatory compensating controls
Network segmentation isolating legacy systems that cannot be upgraded
Prioritized decommission/upgrade roadmap for EOL assets
ITID-54622.detection: Asset inventory combined with exploit/IOC detection at the point of compromise provides strong retrospective correlation; proactive detection depends on maintaining an accurate EOL inventory.
ITID-54622.response: Handle as a standard intrusion incident for containment and eradication; in parallel, drive an accelerated decommission or compensating-control plan for the EOL system.
metrics: Number of EOL assets in production
Time to decommission/replace or apply compensating controls
Time to contain the resulting intrusion
detections: Exploit/IOC detection at the network or endpoint layer
ITID-54622.notes: Distinguished from ITID-54621 in that no vendor patch exists at all due to end-of-life status, rather than a patch simply not yet being applied.

playbook.name: End-of-Life System No Longer Receiving Patches, Then Exploited
playbook.description: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in a system that has reached end-of-life and no longer receives vendor patches, disrupting critical operations.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation of the end-of-life system's vulnerability
steps.desc: Correlate observed compromise/disruption indicators with a known vulnerability affecting the end-of-life system, confirming no vendor patch exists.
steps.guidance: Check EDR/SIEM alerts and cross-reference the system's software version against vendor end-of-life documentation.
steps.outcome: Exploitation confirmed with the system's unsupported status verified.

steps.title: Assess scope of compromise and business dependency on the EOL system
steps.desc: Determine what the attacker accessed/disrupted and how critical the EOL system's function is to the business.
steps.guidance: Review business-continuity documentation for the system's role.
steps.outcome: Scope of compromise and business dependency documented.

steps.title: Isolate the end-of-life system from the network
steps.desc: Disconnect or heavily restrict network access to the affected EOL system to halt further attacker activity, since no patch is available.
steps.guidance: Apply compensating network controls (firewall rules, VLAN isolation) since a vendor patch cannot be applied.
steps.outcome: Attacker activity contained; EOL system isolated.

steps.title: Deploy virtual patching or compensating controls
steps.desc: Apply IPS/WAF virtual-patch signatures or other compensating controls to mitigate the specific vulnerability since no vendor patch exists.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the security tooling team to deploy targeted signatures for the known exploit.
steps.outcome: Compensating controls in place reducing further exploitation risk.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and revoke attacker-established access
steps.desc: Rotate credentials accessible from the compromised system and revoke unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Remove attacker persistence from the affected system
steps.desc: Sweep the system for backdoors or persistence mechanisms; reimage if feasible using the last known-good configuration.
steps.outcome: System confirmed free of attacker persistence, or replaced.

steps.title: Restore business function and evaluate accelerated EOL system replacement
steps.desc: Restore the affected business function, either via the remediated legacy system under compensating controls or by accelerating migration to a supported replacement.
steps.guidance: Treat this incident as strong justification for expediting the EOL system's decommissioning/replacement.
steps.outcome: Business function restored; replacement/migration plan initiated or accelerated.

steps.title: Review technology lifecycle management and EOL risk-acceptance process
steps.desc: Document why the system remained in production past end-of-life and recommend improvements to lifecycle management and risk-acceptance review cadence.
steps.guidance: Recommend a formal EOL tracking and forced-migration policy.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked lifecycle-management improvement actions.

ITID-54623.def: A confirmed exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability that has not yet been classified as a delayed-patch scenario or an end-of-life scenario.
ITID-54623.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for unpatched-vulnerability exploitation events not yet attributed to a delayed-patch or end-of-life root cause.
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed unpatched-vulnerability exploitation events pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54621 or 54622)
ITID-54623.severity: High to Critical pending triage, consistent with confirmed exploitation.
ITID-54623.priority: P1 upon confirmation of active exploitation, regardless of pending reclassification.
ITID-54623.escalation: Escalate immediately as a standard intrusion incident; classify patch-status root cause in parallel.
indicators: Confirmed exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability, patch-availability status not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54623.detection: Relies on initial exploit/IOC detection; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54623.response: Contain immediately as a standard intrusion while triage determines patch-availability status for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
detections: Exploit/IOC detection at the network or endpoint layer
ITID-54623.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Unpatched Vulnerability Exploitation
playbook.description: An attacker exploits an unpatched vulnerability of undetermined specific patch-management failure mode to disrupt critical systems.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability
steps.desc: Correlate observed compromise/disruption indicators with a specific unpatched vulnerability (CVE) on the affected system.
steps.guidance: Check EDR/SIEM alerts and exploit signatures against the system's patch status.
steps.outcome: Exploitation confirmed with the specific vulnerability identified.

steps.title: Assess scope of compromise and why the patch was missing
steps.desc: Determine what the attacker accessed/disrupted and the reason the patch had not been applied (delayed timeline, EOL, missed scan, etc.).
steps.guidance: Escalate to the more specific patch-failure procedure once the cause is identified.
steps.outcome: Scope of compromise and root cause of the patch gap documented.

steps.title: Isolate the exploited system from the network
steps.desc: Disconnect or segment the affected system to halt further attacker activity.
steps.outcome: Attacker activity contained.

steps.title: Apply the missing patch or compensating controls immediately
steps.desc: Urgently deploy the available vendor patch, or if none exists, apply compensating controls (virtual patching, network isolation).
steps.guidance: Expedite through emergency change-management procedures.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability closed or mitigated across the environment.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and revoke attacker-established access
steps.desc: Rotate credentials accessible from the compromised system and revoke unauthorized access established by the attacker.
steps.outcome: Attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Remove attacker persistence and malicious artifacts
steps.desc: Sweep affected systems for backdoors or persistence mechanisms installed via the exploit.
steps.guidance: Reimage where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed free of attacker persistence.

steps.title: Restore affected systems and validate functionality
steps.desc: Restore any disrupted systems/data and confirm functionality and data integrity.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive validation before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with verified integrity.

steps.title: Review patch-management process gaps
steps.desc: Document why the vulnerability remained unpatched and recommend improvements to vulnerability/patch-management processes.
steps.guidance: Recommend automated patch-compliance tracking and SLA enforcement.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54631.def: A disruption to company operations caused by a compromised third-party software component or update that the company depends on, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact.
ITID-54631.purpose: Provides a company-impact framing for supply chain software compromise within the Critical System Disruption domain, tracking business-continuity impact rather than restating the detailed compromise-vector taxonomy tracked elsewhere.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed upstream software supply chain compromise affecting the company (e.g., a compromised vendor update deployed into production)
Precautionary shutdown of systems running a component confirmed compromised upstream, pending remediation
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics and initial-access taxonomy of software supply chain compromise (see ITID-31114 and the Software Supply Chain Attacks group, ITID-5494x)
CI/CD pipeline compromise originating within the company's own build environment (see Code Injection and Tampering, ITID-5464x)
ITID-54631.severity: Critical if the compromised component is deployed broadly across production; High if confined to a limited set of systems.
ITID-54631.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a deployed component is compromised.
ITID-54631.escalation: Escalate immediately to application security, the affected system owners, and vendor management; consider precautionary isolation of affected systems pending validation.
indicators: Vendor security advisory confirming a compromised update or component
Unexpected behavior or unauthorized network activity from systems running the affected component
Threat intelligence reporting matching the company's software bill of materials
vectors: Trojanized vendor software update deployed through normal patch/update channels
rootCauses: Lack of software bill of materials (SBOM) visibility into third-party components
Automatic trust of vendor-signed updates without independent verification
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Software bill of materials (SBOM) tracking
Staged/canary rollout of vendor updates before broad deployment
Network segmentation limiting blast radius of any single third-party component
ITID-54631.detection: Detection typically depends on vendor disclosure or threat intelligence rather than internal telemetry alone, given the trusted nature of the compromised update channel.
ITID-54631.response: Isolate or roll back the affected component immediately upon vendor confirmation; hunt for indicators of compromise across all systems running the affected version.
metrics: Time from vendor disclosure to internal identification of affected systems
Time to isolate/remediate affected systems
ITID-54631.notes: Lone-child cross-reference leaf. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-31114 and ITID-5494x for the detailed supply chain compromise technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Software Compromise (Disruption Context)
playbook.description: A third-party software component or vendor's build/distribution pipeline is compromised, introducing malicious code that disrupts critical systems.

steps.title: Confirm supply chain compromise and identify the affected component
steps.desc: Correlate observed disruption/compromise indicators with a specific third-party software component, library, or update to confirm a supply chain compromise.
steps.guidance: Check vendor security advisories, threat intelligence feeds, and software composition analysis (SCA) results for the affected component.
steps.outcome: Supply chain compromise confirmed with the affected component/version identified.

steps.title: Determine full deployment scope of the compromised component
steps.desc: Identify every system, application, and environment where the compromised component or update is deployed.
steps.guidance: Use the software bill of materials (SBOM) and asset inventory to trace all deployments.
steps.outcome: Full deployment scope documented.

steps.title: Isolate systems running the compromised component
steps.desc: Disconnect or restrict network access for all systems running the compromised component to prevent further impact.
steps.guidance: Prioritize business-critical systems for immediate isolation.
steps.outcome: Further impact from the compromised component contained.

steps.title: Halt further distribution/deployment of the compromised component
steps.desc: Block automatic updates or deployment pipelines from distributing the compromised version further within the environment.
steps.guidance: Pin package managers/deployment pipelines to the last known-good version.
steps.outcome: Further distribution of the compromised component halted.

steps.title: Notify the vendor, affected stakeholders, and relevant authorities
steps.desc: Report the compromise to the vendor for coordinated disclosure and notify internal stakeholders and, if required, regulatory bodies.
steps.outcome: Vendor and stakeholders notified.

steps.title: Remove the compromised component and any malicious artifacts
steps.desc: Uninstall or replace the compromised component with a verified clean version, and remove any malicious code or persistence it introduced.
steps.guidance: Verify the replacement version's integrity via vendor-provided checksums/signatures before redeployment.
steps.outcome: Compromised component and associated artifacts removed from all systems.

steps.title: Redeploy the verified clean component and validate system functionality
steps.desc: Redeploy the clean, verified version of the component and confirm affected systems function correctly.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive validation and integrity checks before declaring recovery complete.
steps.outcome: Systems restored to normal function with the clean component verified.

steps.title: Review software supply chain security controls
steps.desc: Assess SBOM coverage, vendor security assessment processes, and update-verification practices; recommend improvements.
steps.guidance: Recommend signed-artifact verification and stronger vendor risk-management practices.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked supply-chain security improvement actions.

ITID-54641.def: The deliberate injection of malicious or unauthorized code into a company's CI/CD pipeline — via a compromised build tool, pipeline configuration, or dependency — that results in a production outage upon deployment.
ITID-54641.purpose: Captures deliberate malicious code injected into a CI/CD pipeline that causes a production outage, distinguishing pipeline-level compromise from compromise via a developer's own account credentials.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized modification of pipeline configuration/scripts to inject malicious code into a build artifact
Compromise of a build agent, artifact repository, or dependency resolution step causing tainted code to reach production
Resulting production outage traced to the injected code
scopeExcludes: Compromise achieved specifically via a compromised developer account's legitimate commit/push access (see ITID-54642)
Non-malicious deployment failures (see ITID-5461x)
ITID-54641.severity: Critical — pipeline-level compromise can affect every downstream deployment until identified and purged.
ITID-54641.priority: P1, always; treat as an active supply chain compromise investigation, not just an outage.
ITID-54641.escalation: Escalate immediately to application security, DevOps/platform engineering, and executive leadership; halt all further deployments from the pipeline pending investigation.
indicators: Build artifact hash mismatch against expected/signed source
Unauthorized changes to pipeline configuration files or build scripts
Malicious code or unexpected network calls identified in the deployed artifact
vectors: Compromise of a build server or CI/CD service account
Unauthorized modification of pipeline-as-code configuration in the source repository
Compromise of a build-time dependency (dependency confusion, typosquatting)
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls or code review on pipeline configuration changes
Build agents with excessive privileges or network access
Lack of build artifact integrity verification (signing/hashing)
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Mandatory code review and branch protection for pipeline-as-code changes
Build artifact signing and integrity verification
Least-privilege, ephemeral build agents
ITID-54641.detection: Build artifact integrity verification and pipeline configuration change monitoring provide strong detection when implemented; otherwise discovery often occurs only after production impact.
ITID-54641.response: Halt the pipeline immediately, roll back to the last known-good artifact, and conduct a full forensic review of pipeline configuration and build history before resuming deployments.
metrics: Time to halt further deployments
Time to identify the injection point
Number of production deployments affected before detection
ITID-54641.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54642 by compromise vector: pipeline/build-infrastructure compromise, as opposed to compromise via a legitimate developer account's own credentials.

playbook.name: CI/CD Pipeline Code Injection Causing Production Outage
playbook.description: An attacker injects malicious code into the CI/CD pipeline, which is then deployed to production, causing a critical system outage.

steps.title: Confirm malicious code injection in the CI/CD pipeline and the resulting production impact
steps.desc: Correlate the production outage with an unauthorized or malicious commit/build-step change in the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.guidance: Review pipeline execution logs, commit history, and build artifacts for unauthorized modifications.
steps.outcome: Malicious injection confirmed with the injection point identified.
steps.tool: CI/CD pipeline logs / version control audit

steps.title: Determine scope of affected builds, artifacts, and deployed environments
steps.desc: Identify which builds, artifacts, and production/staging environments received the malicious code.
steps.guidance: Trace artifact provenance from the injection point through all downstream deployments.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected builds and environments documented.

steps.title: Lock down the CI/CD pipeline and halt further deployments
steps.desc: Freeze the CI/CD pipeline to prevent further deployment of the malicious code and disable automated deployment triggers.
steps.guidance: Notify engineering teams of the pipeline freeze and reason.
steps.outcome: Pipeline locked down; no further malicious deployments possible.

steps.title: Roll back production to the last known-good build
steps.desc: Deploy the last verified-clean build to production to restore service and remove the malicious code from live systems.
steps.guidance: Verify the rollback build's integrity before deployment.
steps.outcome: Production restored to a clean, functioning state.
steps.abort: If rollback fails, escalate to manual remediation per the rollback-failure procedure.

steps.title: Rotate CI/CD credentials, secrets, and access tokens
steps.desc: Rotate all pipeline credentials, API tokens, and secrets that may have been exposed or used to perform the injection.
steps.outcome: Compromised or at-risk pipeline credentials rotated.

steps.title: Audit commit history and pipeline configuration for the full attack path
steps.desc: Conduct a full audit of commit history, pipeline configuration, and access logs to identify how the injection occurred and remove any remaining malicious artifacts or persistence.
steps.guidance: Verify build-provenance/signing mechanisms to confirm no additional tampering remains.
steps.outcome: Full attack path identified; all malicious artifacts removed.
steps.tool: Version control audit / build provenance tooling

steps.title: Re-enable the CI/CD pipeline with hardened controls and validate production stability
steps.desc: Restore pipeline operation with additional security controls (mandatory code review, signed commits, restricted deploy permissions) and confirm production stability.
steps.guidance: Perform a staged re-enablement with close monitoring.
steps.outcome: Pipeline restored with hardened controls; production confirmed stable.

steps.title: Conduct full software-supply-chain post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the injection vector and recommend pipeline hardening, commit-signing, and access-control improvements.
steps.guidance: Recommend build-provenance verification (e.g., SLSA-aligned controls) and mandatory peer review for pipeline changes.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked security-hardening actions.

ITID-54642.def: The introduction of malicious or unauthorized code into a company codebase or deployment through the use of a compromised developer's legitimate source-control or deployment credentials.
ITID-54642.purpose: Captures malicious code introduced through a compromised developer account's legitimate commit/push access, distinguishing account-compromise-driven tampering from direct pipeline/build-infrastructure compromise.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized commits or merges made using a compromised developer's source-control credentials
Malicious code reaching production through the normal review/deployment process due to a compromised legitimate account bypassing suspicion
scopeExcludes: Compromise of pipeline/build infrastructure itself without use of a developer's own credentials (see ITID-54641)
ITID-54642.severity: Critical — code introduced via a trusted developer identity is likely to pass normal review scrutiny and reach production quickly.
ITID-54642.priority: P1, always; treat as both an account-compromise incident and a supply chain compromise investigation.
ITID-54642.escalation: Escalate immediately to application security, identity/access management, and executive leadership; suspend the compromised account and halt deployments pending review.
indicators: Commits/merges from a developer account at unusual times or from an unusual location/device
Code changes inconsistent with the developer's normal work pattern or ticket assignments
Authentication anomalies (impossible travel, new device) on the developer's account preceding the malicious commit
vectors: Phishing or credential-stuffing compromise of a developer's source-control account
Session token theft enabling code changes without re-authentication
rootCauses: Lack of MFA enforcement on source-control/developer accounts
Insufficient anomaly detection on developer account activity
Code review process not catching subtle malicious changes
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Mandatory MFA on all source-control and deployment accounts
Behavioral anomaly detection on developer account activity
Mandatory peer code review with attention to unexpected/unexplained changes
ITID-54642.detection: Identity anomaly detection (impossible travel, new device) combined with commit-pattern analysis provides reasonable detection; sophisticated compromises may pass initial review.
ITID-54642.response: Suspend the compromised account, roll back the malicious changes, and conduct a full review of all code changes made by that account since the estimated compromise window.
metrics: Time to detect the account compromise
Time to identify and roll back all affected commits
Number of deployments affected before detection
ITID-54642.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54641 by compromise vector: a compromised developer's own legitimate credentials, as opposed to direct compromise of pipeline/build infrastructure.

playbook.name: Malicious Code Tampering Introduced via Compromised Developer Account
playbook.description: An attacker compromises a developer's account credentials and uses that access to introduce malicious code tampering, disrupting critical systems.

steps.title: Confirm the compromised developer account and the malicious code introduced
steps.desc: Correlate suspicious commits/code changes with anomalous developer-account login activity to confirm account compromise as the vector.
steps.guidance: Check login geolocation/device anomalies, MFA logs, and commit signing status against the developer's normal pattern.
steps.outcome: Account compromise confirmed with the malicious code changes identified.
steps.abort: If evidence suggests this was insider action by the legitimate account holder rather than external compromise, redirect to the insider-threat procedure.

steps.title: Determine scope of code changes and deployed impact
steps.desc: Identify all commits, branches, and deployed artifacts affected by the compromised account's malicious activity.
steps.guidance: Trace artifact provenance from the malicious commits through deployment pipelines.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected code and deployments documented.

steps.title: Immediately disable the compromised developer account and rotate credentials
steps.desc: Suspend the compromised account and rotate its credentials, SSH keys, and any tokens it had access to.
steps.guidance: Also review and revoke any active sessions for the account.
steps.outcome: Compromised account access revoked.

steps.title: Roll back the malicious code changes and halt affected deployments
steps.desc: Revert the malicious commits and halt any in-progress deployments of the tampered code.
steps.guidance: Verify the rollback target predates the compromise.
steps.outcome: Malicious code changes reverted; deployments halted.

steps.title: Rotate broader credentials/secrets accessible to the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate any shared secrets, API keys, or credentials the compromised developer account had access to, given potential broader exposure.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed secrets rotated.

steps.title: Audit all code contributed by the compromised account and remove any remaining malicious artifacts
steps.desc: Review the account's full contribution history for other potentially malicious changes and remove any remaining tampered code or persistence.
steps.guidance: Verify build integrity across all artifacts the account had access to.
steps.outcome: All malicious code and persistence removed.

steps.title: Redeploy verified clean code and validate production stability
steps.desc: Redeploy the clean, verified codebase and confirm production systems are functioning correctly.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive validation before declaring recovery complete.
steps.outcome: Production restored and confirmed stable with clean code.

steps.title: Review developer account security controls and code-review safeguards
steps.desc: Assess MFA enforcement, commit-signing requirements, and code-review processes; recommend improvements to prevent recurrence.
steps.guidance: Recommend mandatory MFA, commit signing, and peer review for all production code changes.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked security-hardening actions.

ITID-54643.def: A code injection or tampering event affecting company software that has not yet been classified as pipeline-based or developer-account-based.
ITID-54643.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for code injection and tampering events not yet attributed to CI/CD pipeline compromise or compromised developer account.
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed code tampering events pending compromise-vector confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once compromise vector is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54641 or 54642)
ITID-54643.severity: Critical pending triage, consistent with confirmed code tampering.
ITID-54643.priority: P1, always, regardless of pending reclassification.
ITID-54643.escalation: Escalate immediately; halt further deployments while triage proceeds.
indicators: Confirmed unauthorized code present in a build or production artifact, vector not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54643.detection: Relies on initial artifact-integrity or code-review findings; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54643.response: Halt deployments and roll back to a known-good state while triage determines the compromise vector for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54643.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Code Injection and Tampering
playbook.description: Malicious code injection or tampering disrupts critical systems, with the specific injection vector not yet determined.

steps.title: Confirm code injection/tampering and its production impact
steps.desc: Correlate the observed disruption with unauthorized code changes to confirm injection/tampering as the cause.
steps.guidance: Review version control history, build logs, and deployment records for unauthorized modifications.
steps.outcome: Code injection/tampering confirmed with the affected code identified.

steps.title: Determine the injection vector and full scope of impact
steps.desc: Investigate how the malicious code was introduced (compromised pipeline, compromised developer account, or other vector) and the full scope of affected systems.
steps.guidance: Escalate to the more specific procedure once the vector is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Injection vector and impact scope documented.

steps.title: Lock down affected pipelines/accounts and halt further deployment
steps.desc: Freeze the relevant CI/CD pipeline or disable the implicated account to prevent further malicious deployment.
steps.outcome: Further malicious deployment halted.

steps.title: Roll back to the last known-good code state
steps.desc: Deploy the last verified-clean build/code state to restore service and remove the malicious code from production.
steps.guidance: Verify rollback target integrity before deployment.
steps.outcome: Production restored to a clean state.
steps.abort: If rollback fails, escalate to manual remediation per the rollback-failure procedure.

steps.title: Rotate potentially exposed credentials and secrets
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, tokens, and secrets that may have been exposed as part of the injection.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Audit for and remove any remaining malicious artifacts or persistence
steps.desc: Conduct a full audit of code, pipeline configuration, and access to remove any remaining malicious artifacts.
steps.guidance: Verify build-provenance/signing to confirm no additional tampering remains.
steps.outcome: All malicious artifacts and persistence removed.

steps.title: Redeploy verified clean code and validate production stability
steps.desc: Redeploy the clean, verified codebase and confirm production systems function correctly.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive validation before declaring recovery complete.
steps.outcome: Production restored and confirmed stable.

steps.title: Review software supply chain and access-control safeguards
steps.desc: Assess the gaps that allowed the injection and recommend pipeline hardening, code-review, and access-control improvements.
steps.guidance: Recommend build-provenance verification and mandatory peer review.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked security-hardening actions.

ITID-54711.def: The deliberate, physical destruction or damage of server, storage, or network equipment by a person with or without authorized facility access, intended to cause operational disruption.
ITID-54711.purpose: Captures deliberate physical destruction of server or network hardware, tracked for physical security correlation given the absence of a corresponding ATT&CK Enterprise technique.
scopeIncludes: Physical smashing, disconnection, or destruction of servers, switches, or storage hardware
Deliberate physical damage to networking equipment in a data center, wiring closet, or comms room
scopeExcludes: Sabotage of supporting power/cooling systems rather than the IT hardware itself (see ITID-54712)
Cutting of fiber/cable lines specifically (see ITID-54713)
Logical/remote destruction of data without physical hardware damage (see Insider-Driven Data Corruption, ITID-5454x)
ITID-54711.severity: High to Critical depending on the criticality and redundancy of the destroyed equipment.
ITID-54711.priority: P1 if the destroyed equipment hosts business-critical services with no immediate failover.
ITID-54711.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, facilities, law enforcement (if the perpetrator is not an authorized insider or has fled), and IT infrastructure for recovery.
indicators: Physical security camera footage or access logs showing tampering with equipment
Sudden, unexplained hardware failure alarms with no corresponding logical/environmental cause
Physical evidence of forced entry or damage at the equipment location
vectors: Unauthorized or authorized physical access used to directly damage hardware
rootCauses: Inadequate physical access controls to server rooms/data center floors
Insufficient monitoring/camera coverage of critical equipment locations
controls: Physical access control (badge/biometric) restricting server room entry
Camera coverage of all critical equipment locations
Redundant/geographically separated hardware for critical services
ITID-54711.detection: Physical security systems (access logs, cameras) provide the primary detection surface; IT monitoring detects the resulting outage but not the physical cause.
ITID-54711.response: Secure the scene and preserve physical evidence for law enforcement/HR action while IT infrastructure executes failover or hardware replacement.
metrics: Time to detect the physical tampering
Time to restore service via failover/replacement
ITID-54711.notes: Physical sabotage — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies, tracked for physical security correlation rather than a MITRE-mapped adversary technique.

playbook.name: Deliberate Physical Destruction of Server/Network Equipment
playbook.description: An individual deliberately physically destroys server or network equipment, causing critical system disruption and requiring coordinated physical security/HR/Legal response.

steps.title: Confirm physical destruction and identify responsible party via access/surveillance records
steps.desc: Confirm the physical damage to equipment and use badge access logs/surveillance footage to identify who was present and responsible.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security to pull access logs and camera footage for the affected area and time window.
steps.outcome: Destruction confirmed with the responsible party identified where possible.

steps.title: Assess scope of destroyed equipment and business impact
steps.desc: Determine which systems/services are affected by the destroyed equipment and the resulting business impact.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference destroyed asset tags against the CMDB.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Secure the area and preserve physical evidence
steps.desc: Restrict access to the affected area to preserve evidence (fingerprints, tool marks, damaged equipment) for investigation and potential law enforcement involvement.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security/facilities to cordon off the area.
steps.outcome: Area secured; physical evidence preserved.

steps.title: Fail over affected services to redundant infrastructure
steps.desc: Redirect affected workloads to redundant or backup infrastructure to restore service availability.
steps.guidance: Follow the applicable DR/failover runbook.
steps.outcome: Critical services restored via redundant infrastructure.

steps.title: Engage physical security, HR/Legal, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the incident to physical security leadership, HR/Legal, and law enforcement given the deliberate criminal nature of the act.
steps.outcome: Physical security, HR/Legal, and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Remove or replace damaged equipment and verify no tampering remains on adjacent systems
steps.desc: Remove the destroyed equipment and check adjacent/connected systems for any additional tampering.
steps.outcome: Damaged equipment removed; adjacent systems verified untampered.

steps.title: Replace destroyed equipment and restore data/configuration
steps.desc: Procure and install replacement equipment, restoring configuration and data from backups, and validate full functionality.
steps.guidance: Verify restored configuration matches the pre-incident state.
steps.outcome: Replacement equipment operational with verified configuration and data integrity.

steps.title: Review physical security controls for critical infrastructure areas
steps.desc: Evaluate access controls, surveillance coverage, and physical security posture for server/network equipment locations.
steps.guidance: Recommend improved physical access controls (e.g., restricted badge access, additional cameras) for critical infrastructure areas.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked physical-security improvement actions.

ITID-54712.def: The deliberate tampering with or sabotage of a building's power distribution or cooling infrastructure, by a person with or without authorized facility access, intended to cause an IT service outage.
ITID-54712.purpose: Captures deliberate sabotage of a building's power or cooling systems intended to cause an IT outage indirectly, tracked for physical security correlation given the absence of a corresponding ATT&CK Enterprise technique.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate tripping of circuit breakers or tampering with UPS/generator systems
Deliberate disabling or sabotage of HVAC/cooling systems supporting IT equipment
scopeExcludes: Direct physical destruction of IT hardware itself (see ITID-54711)
Non-deliberate power/cooling failures (see ITID-5473x/5474x)
ITID-54712.severity: High to Critical depending on the scope of IT services dependent on the sabotaged infrastructure.
ITID-54712.priority: P1 if business-critical services lose power/cooling as a result.
ITID-54712.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, facilities engineering, and law enforcement if the perpetrator is not accounted for.
indicators: Physical security footage or access logs showing tampering with electrical panels or HVAC controls
Facility alarms indicating manual intervention rather than equipment failure
Physical evidence of forced access to restricted mechanical/electrical rooms
vectors: Unauthorized or authorized physical access used to sabotage electrical or HVAC control systems
rootCauses: Inadequate physical access controls to mechanical/electrical rooms
Insufficient monitoring/alerting distinguishing deliberate tampering from equipment failure
controls: Physical access control restricting mechanical/electrical room entry
Tamper-evident/alarmed electrical and HVAC control panels
Redundant power/cooling paths
ITID-54712.detection: Physical security systems and facility BMS tamper alarms provide the primary detection surface.
ITID-54712.response: Secure the scene and preserve physical evidence while facilities engineering restores power/cooling and IT infrastructure manages any resulting service impact.
metrics: Time to detect tampering
Time to restore power/cooling
ITID-54712.notes: Physical sabotage — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies, tracked for physical security correlation rather than a MITRE-mapped adversary technique.

playbook.name: Sabotage of Building Power/Cooling Systems to Cause IT Outage
playbook.description: An individual deliberately sabotages building power or cooling infrastructure to cause an IT outage, requiring coordinated facilities/security/Legal response.

steps.title: Confirm deliberate sabotage of power/cooling systems
steps.desc: Work with facilities engineering to distinguish deliberate tampering from equipment failure, using physical inspection and access records.
steps.guidance: Look for signs of forced access, tampered controls, or deliberately disabled safety interlocks.
steps.outcome: Sabotage confirmed and distinguished from accidental failure.
steps.abort: If evidence points to equipment failure rather than sabotage, redirect to the appropriate non-malicious power/cooling failure procedure.

steps.title: Identify responsible party via access/surveillance records
steps.desc: Use badge access logs and surveillance footage to identify who accessed the power/cooling infrastructure area.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security.
steps.outcome: Responsible party identified where possible.

steps.title: Restore power/cooling via backup systems and fail over IT workloads
steps.desc: Activate generators/UPS or portable cooling as applicable, and fail over critical IT workloads to a secondary site if the sabotage cannot be immediately reversed.
steps.guidance: Follow standard power/cooling failure containment procedures in parallel with the security investigation.
steps.outcome: IT service restored via backup power/cooling or failover site.

steps.title: Secure the facility area and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Restrict access to the sabotaged infrastructure area to preserve physical evidence.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security/facilities.
steps.outcome: Area secured; evidence preserved.

steps.title: Engage physical security, HR/Legal, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the incident given its deliberate, potentially criminal nature.
steps.outcome: Physical security, HR/Legal, and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Repair sabotaged power/cooling systems
steps.desc: Repair or replace the sabotaged components and restore normal power/cooling capability.
steps.guidance: Verify repairs against manufacturer specifications; test under load.
steps.outcome: Power/cooling systems restored to full rated capacity.

steps.title: Fail back IT workloads and validate operational stability
steps.desc: Return IT workloads to the primary site once power/cooling is confirmed stable, and verify system health.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive health checks before declaring full recovery.
steps.outcome: Primary site fully operational with verified stability.

steps.title: Review physical security controls for facilities infrastructure
steps.desc: Evaluate access controls and monitoring for power/cooling infrastructure areas.
steps.guidance: Recommend improved physical access restrictions and tamper alerting.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked physical-security improvement actions.

ITID-54713.def: The deliberate, physical cutting or damaging of fiber-optic or copper cable lines serving company facilities or connectivity, intended to disrupt operations.
ITID-54713.purpose: Captures deliberate cutting of fiber or cable lines as a distinct physical sabotage act, tracked for physical security correlation given the absence of a corresponding ATT&CK Enterprise technique.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate cutting of terrestrial fiber or cable lines at or near a company facility
Deliberate damage to cabling within a facility's telecom/network entry point
scopeExcludes: Undersea cable damage from non-deliberate causes such as anchor drag (see ITID-54131)
Destruction of the networking hardware itself rather than the cabling (see ITID-54711)
ITID-54713.severity: High to Critical depending on whether redundant/diverse cable paths exist.
ITID-54713.priority: P1 if the cut severs the sole connectivity path for a business-critical facility.
ITID-54713.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, network operations, and law enforcement; engage the carrier for emergency repair.
indicators: Sudden, complete loss of connectivity at a facility with a physical cause confirmed on inspection
Camera footage or witness reports of tampering at a cable entry point or nearby conduit
Carrier confirmation of a physical cut rather than an equipment fault
vectors: Physical access to a cable entry point, conduit, or manhole used to deliberately sever cabling
rootCauses: Lack of diverse/redundant physical cable entry points
Insufficient physical protection or monitoring of cable entry points and nearby conduits
controls: Diverse, physically separated cable entry paths
Physical protection (locked conduits/vaults) for cable entry points
Camera coverage of cable entry points
ITID-54713.detection: Connectivity loss monitoring provides immediate detection of impact; physical security systems and carrier inspection confirm the deliberate cause.
ITID-54713.response: Engage the carrier for emergency repair while failing over to any available redundant path; secure the scene for law enforcement.
metrics: Time to detect the cut
Time to restore connectivity via repair or failover
detections: Physical access control and camera monitoring at cable entry points
ITID-54713.notes: Physical sabotage — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies, tracked for physical security correlation rather than a MITRE-mapped adversary technique.

playbook.name: Cut Fiber/Cable Lines (Deliberate Physical Attack)
playbook.description: An individual deliberately cuts fiber or network cable lines, disrupting connectivity and requiring coordinated physical security/network response.

steps.title: Confirm deliberate cable cut and locate the physical damage
steps.desc: Confirm connectivity loss is due to a physically cut cable (not a routing/provider issue) and dispatch technicians to locate the exact damage point.
steps.guidance: Use fiber optic time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) testing to pinpoint the cut location.
steps.outcome: Cable cut confirmed and physical damage location identified.

steps.title: Assess whether the cut indicates deliberate sabotage and identify responsible party if possible
steps.desc: Inspect the cut for signs of deliberate action (clean cuts, accessed conduit/manhole) versus accidental damage, and check nearby surveillance/access records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security for evidence gathering if sabotage is suspected.
steps.outcome: Deliberate sabotage confirmed or ruled out, with responsible party identified where possible.
steps.abort: If damage appears accidental (e.g., construction activity), redirect to a standard connectivity-outage procedure.

steps.title: Reroute traffic via alternate paths or redundant cabling
steps.desc: Shift traffic to alternate physical paths, redundant cabling, or wireless backup links to restore connectivity.
steps.guidance: Validate alternate path capacity before full cutover.
steps.outcome: Connectivity restored via alternate path.
steps.abort: If no redundant path exists, prioritize critical traffic over available limited-capacity alternatives.

steps.title: Secure the damage site and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Restrict access to the cable damage site to preserve evidence for investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security/facilities and, if on public property, local authorities.
steps.outcome: Site secured; evidence preserved.

steps.title: Engage physical security, Legal, and law enforcement if sabotage is confirmed
steps.desc: Report the incident to physical security, Legal, and law enforcement given the deliberate, potentially criminal nature of the act.
steps.outcome: Physical security, Legal, and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Repair or replace the damaged cable segment
steps.desc: Splice or replace the damaged fiber/cable segment to restore the primary physical path.
steps.guidance: Test the repaired segment thoroughly before returning it to service.
steps.outcome: Cable segment repaired and tested.

steps.title: Restore primary routing and validate performance
steps.desc: Return traffic to the repaired primary path and confirm latency/throughput matches baseline.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased cutback with monitoring.
steps.outcome: Primary routing restored with baseline performance confirmed.

steps.title: Review physical cable path security and redundancy
steps.desc: Evaluate physical security of cable paths (conduit locks, manhole security) and adequacy of redundant path diversity.
steps.guidance: Recommend physical hardening or additional path diversity where gaps are found.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54714.def: A physical sabotage event affecting IT infrastructure that has not yet been classified as hardware destruction, power/cooling sabotage, or cable cutting.
ITID-54714.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for physical sabotage of IT infrastructure events not yet attributed to hardware destruction, power/cooling sabotage, or cable cutting.
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed physical sabotage events pending method confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once method is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54711, 54712, or 54713)
ITID-54714.severity: High to Critical pending triage, consistent with confirmed deliberate physical sabotage.
ITID-54714.priority: P1 pending triage given the deliberate nature of the act.
ITID-54714.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security for joint triage.
indicators: Confirmed deliberate physical interference with IT-supporting infrastructure, method not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54714.detection: Relies on initial physical security system alerting; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54714.response: Secure the scene and triage to the specific sabotage method for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
detections: Physical access control and camera monitoring
ITID-54714.notes: Physical sabotage — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies. Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Physical Sabotage of IT Infrastructure
playbook.description: IT infrastructure is deliberately physically sabotaged with the specific method not yet determined, requiring coordinated physical security response.

steps.title: Confirm physical sabotage and assess the specific method
steps.desc: Confirm the disruption is due to deliberate physical sabotage (not accidental failure) and determine the specific method (equipment destruction, power/cooling tampering, cable cutting).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities and physical security for on-site inspection.
steps.outcome: Sabotage confirmed and method identified, enabling routing to a more specific procedure if applicable.
steps.abort: If evidence points to accidental failure, redirect to the appropriate non-malicious procedure.

steps.title: Identify responsible party via access/surveillance records
steps.desc: Use badge access logs and surveillance footage to identify individuals present at the affected location during the relevant time window.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security.
steps.outcome: Responsible party identified where possible.

steps.title: Secure the affected area and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Restrict access to the sabotaged area to preserve physical evidence for investigation.
steps.outcome: Area secured; evidence preserved.

steps.title: Restore affected services via redundant infrastructure or workarounds
steps.desc: Fail over or work around the sabotaged infrastructure to restore critical service availability.
steps.guidance: Apply the containment approach appropriate to the specific sabotage method identified.
steps.outcome: Critical services restored.

steps.title: Engage physical security, HR/Legal, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the incident given its deliberate, potentially criminal nature.
steps.outcome: Physical security, HR/Legal, and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Repair or replace sabotaged infrastructure
steps.desc: Repair or replace the damaged infrastructure component appropriate to the specific sabotage method.
steps.outcome: Infrastructure repaired/replaced and verified functional.

steps.title: Restore full operations and validate stability
steps.desc: Confirm all affected systems are functioning normally and validate stability over an observation period.
steps.outcome: Operations restored and confirmed stable.

steps.title: Review physical security controls for IT infrastructure
steps.desc: Evaluate access controls, surveillance, and physical security posture across IT infrastructure locations.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54721.def: Damage to IT equipment at a company office or branch location caused by fire, where no deliberate sabotage or adversarial cause is implicated.
ITID-54721.purpose: Captures fire damage to office or branch IT equipment as a non-adversarial environmental continuity event, distinct from data-center-specific fire damage and from deliberate arson/sabotage.
scopeIncludes: Fire damage to network closets, local servers, or end-user equipment at an office or branch
Business disruption resulting from fire-related evacuation or facility closure affecting IT operations
scopeExcludes: Fire damage to a primary/DR data center facility (see ITID-54123)
Deliberate arson or sabotage (see ITID-54712)
ITID-54721.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High if the branch/office hosts locally unique systems or data with no off-site backup; Medium if centrally backed-up/replicated.
ITID-54721.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if life safety is involved or the location supports a business-critical function.
ITID-54721.escalation: Escalate to facilities, business continuity, and safety personnel immediately; IT recovery follows once the site is declared safe.
indicators: Fire alarm/suppression system activation at the office/branch
Emergency services dispatch to the location
Sudden loss of telemetry from locally hosted systems at the affected site
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial environmental event
rootCauses: Electrical fault
Equipment overheating
External fire spreading into the facility
controls: Off-site/cloud backup of branch-local data
Fire detection and suppression systems at branch locations
Business continuity plan for branch-level outages
ITID-54721.detection: Physical fire detection systems and total telemetry loss from the site provide unambiguous detection.
ITID-54721.response: Once the site is declared safe, restore affected systems from off-site backup or reroute the branch's function to an alternate location.
metrics: Time to restore branch function via failover/alternate site
Data loss relative to RPO for locally hosted systems
ITID-54721.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique, unless investigation confirms deliberate arson, in which case reclassify to ITID-54712.

playbook.name: Fire Damage to Office/Branch IT Equipment
playbook.description: A fire causes physical damage to IT equipment at an office or branch location, disrupting local and potentially connected business operations.

steps.title: Confirm fire damage and personnel safety status
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation from facilities/fire department on the extent of fire damage and verify all personnel are safe.
steps.guidance: Prioritize life-safety confirmation above all IT considerations.
steps.outcome: Personnel safety confirmed; damage scope reported.

steps.title: Assess IT equipment damage and business impact
steps.desc: Determine which IT equipment and business functions at the affected location are impacted once the site is declared safe to assess.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with local site management for damage assessment.
steps.outcome: Damage and business impact scope documented.

steps.title: Fail over affected business functions to alternate location or DR site
steps.desc: Redirect affected business functions to an alternate office, remote work arrangement, or DR site to maintain continuity.
steps.guidance: Follow the business continuity plan for the affected site.
steps.outcome: Business functions continuing from an alternate location.

steps.title: Secure the site and notify insurance
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities to secure the damaged site against further loss and notify insurance carriers.
steps.outcome: Site secured; insurance notified.

steps.title: Assess and remediate or replace damaged equipment
steps.desc: Determine which equipment can be salvaged versus must be replaced, and plan procurement/replacement.
steps.guidance: Engage restoration specialists for smoke/water-damaged equipment assessment.
steps.outcome: Remediation/replacement plan established.

steps.title: Restore IT equipment and validate data integrity from backups
steps.desc: Replace/repair damaged equipment and restore data from backups, validating integrity before returning to normal operation.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks on any data affected by the outage window.
steps.outcome: IT equipment restored with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Transition business functions back to the restored location
steps.desc: Move business functions back from the alternate location/DR site once the primary site is confirmed operational and safe.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased transition to avoid disruption.
steps.outcome: Business functions restored to the primary location.

steps.title: Review fire-safety and business-continuity preparedness
steps.desc: Evaluate fire-suppression systems, equipment placement, and business continuity plan effectiveness for the affected site.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54722.def: Damage to company IT-supporting facilities and equipment caused by flooding resulting from a natural disaster (storm, hurricane, river/coastal flooding), where no deliberate sabotage is implicated.
ITID-54722.purpose: Captures flood damage to company facilities from a natural disaster as a non-adversarial environmental continuity event, distinguishing weather/water-driven flooding from data-center-specific flood damage.
scopeIncludes: Flood water intrusion into an office, branch, or non-primary facility damaging IT equipment
Business disruption from facility closure due to flooding, independent of direct equipment damage
scopeExcludes: Flooding specifically affecting a primary/DR data center (see ITID-54123)
Deliberate water-based sabotage (an unusual case; treat as ITID-54712 if confirmed deliberate)
ITID-54722.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High if the facility hosts locally unique systems or data without off-site backup; Medium if centrally backed-up/replicated.
ITID-54722.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if life safety is involved or the facility supports a business-critical function.
ITID-54722.escalation: Escalate to facilities, business continuity, and safety personnel immediately; IT recovery follows once the site is declared safe to enter.
indicators: Water-intrusion sensor alerts
Weather service flood warnings for the facility's region
Sudden loss of telemetry from locally hosted systems coincident with reported flooding
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial environmental event
rootCauses: Severe weather/natural disaster
Facility located in a flood-prone area without adequate flood mitigation
controls: Off-site/cloud backup of facility-local data
Flood detection sensors and mitigation (barriers, elevated equipment placement)
Business continuity plan for facility-level outages
ITID-54722.detection: Water-intrusion sensors and total telemetry loss from the site provide unambiguous detection; weather monitoring provides advance warning.
ITID-54722.response: Once the site is declared safe, restore affected systems from off-site backup or reroute the facility's function to an alternate location.
metrics: Time to restore facility function via failover/alternate site
Data loss relative to RPO for locally hosted systems
ITID-54722.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Flood Damage from Natural Disaster
playbook.description: Flooding from a natural disaster causes physical damage to a facility's IT infrastructure, disrupting business operations.

steps.title: Confirm flood damage and personnel safety status
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation from facilities/emergency services on the extent of flood damage and verify all personnel are safe.
steps.guidance: Prioritize life-safety confirmation above all IT considerations; do not permit entry until declared safe.
steps.outcome: Personnel safety confirmed; damage scope reported.

steps.title: Assess IT equipment damage and business impact once site is safe
steps.desc: Determine which IT equipment and business functions are impacted by the flooding.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities for damage assessment once water has receded and the site is declared safe.
steps.outcome: Damage and business impact scope documented.

steps.title: Fail over affected business functions to an alternate site
steps.desc: Redirect affected business functions to an alternate office, remote work arrangement, or DR site.
steps.guidance: Follow the business continuity plan for the affected site.
steps.outcome: Business functions continuing from an alternate location.

steps.title: Secure the site, cut power if needed for safety, and notify insurance
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities to secure the site (including electrical safety shutoffs as needed) and notify insurance carriers.
steps.outcome: Site secured; insurance notified.

steps.title: Assess and remediate water-damaged equipment or plan replacement
steps.desc: Determine which equipment can be salvaged versus must be replaced, and plan procurement/replacement.
steps.guidance: Engage water-damage restoration specialists for equipment assessment; be cautious of hidden corrosion/mold risk.
steps.outcome: Remediation/replacement plan established.

steps.title: Restore IT equipment and validate data integrity from backups
steps.desc: Replace/repair damaged equipment and restore data from backups, validating integrity before returning to normal operation.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks on any data affected by the outage window.
steps.outcome: IT equipment restored with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Transition business functions back to the restored location
steps.desc: Move business functions back from the alternate location once the primary site is confirmed operational and safe.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased transition to avoid disruption.
steps.outcome: Business functions restored to the primary location.

steps.title: Review flood-risk mitigation and business-continuity preparedness
steps.desc: Evaluate flood-risk mitigation measures (elevated equipment, drainage, sump pumps) and business continuity plan effectiveness.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements as warranted, particularly for facilities in flood-prone areas.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54723.def: Structural or equipment damage to a company facility caused by an earthquake or other seismic event, where no deliberate sabotage is implicated.
ITID-54723.purpose: Captures earthquake or seismic damage to a company facility as a non-adversarial environmental continuity event, distinguishing structural/seismic risk from fire and flood.
scopeIncludes: Structural damage to an office, branch, or facility from seismic activity
Equipment damage (server racks toppled, cabling severed) from earthquake shaking
Business disruption from facility closure or safety inspection following a seismic event
scopeExcludes: Seismic damage specifically to a primary/DR data center (see ITID-54123)
ITID-54723.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High to Critical if the facility is structurally compromised or hosts locally unique systems; Medium if minor and centrally backed-up/replicated.
ITID-54723.priority: P1 if the facility is structurally unsafe or hosts a business-critical function with no failover; P2 otherwise.
ITID-54723.escalation: Escalate to facilities, business continuity, and safety personnel immediately; life safety and structural inspection take precedence over IT recovery.
indicators: Seismic activity reports for the facility's region
Structural damage observed during safety inspection
Sudden loss of telemetry from locally hosted systems coincident with a reported seismic event
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial environmental event
rootCauses: Natural seismic activity
Facility not built/retrofitted to current seismic standards
Equipment racks not adequately seismically braced
controls: Seismic bracing for equipment racks
Off-site/cloud backup of facility-local data
Business continuity plan for facility-level outages
ITID-54723.detection: Seismic monitoring services and total telemetry loss from the site provide detection; structural damage assessment requires physical inspection.
ITID-54723.response: Once the site is declared structurally safe, restore affected systems from off-site backup or reroute the facility's function to an alternate location.
metrics: Time to restore facility function via failover/alternate site
Data loss relative to RPO for locally hosted systems
ITID-54723.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Earthquake/Seismic Damage to Facility
playbook.description: An earthquake causes structural or equipment damage to a facility, disrupting IT operations and business continuity.

steps.title: Confirm structural safety and personnel status post-earthquake
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation from facilities/structural engineers on building safety and verify all personnel are accounted for and safe.
steps.guidance: Prioritize life-safety and structural-integrity confirmation above all IT considerations; do not permit entry until declared safe.
steps.outcome: Personnel safety confirmed; structural safety status established.

steps.title: Assess IT equipment damage and business impact once site is declared safe
steps.desc: Determine which IT equipment and business functions are impacted by the seismic event.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities for damage assessment.
steps.outcome: Damage and business impact scope documented.

steps.title: Fail over affected business functions to an alternate/geographically separate site
steps.desc: Redirect affected business functions to an alternate office or DR site outside the affected seismic zone.
steps.guidance: Follow the business continuity plan; account for potential aftershocks when planning site access.
steps.outcome: Business functions continuing from an alternate location.

steps.title: Secure the site and notify insurance
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities/structural engineers to secure the site against further risk (aftershocks, structural collapse) and notify insurance carriers.
steps.outcome: Site secured; insurance notified.

steps.title: Assess facility repair feasibility or plan permanent relocation
steps.desc: Determine whether the facility can be structurally repaired or must be decommissioned, and plan permanent infrastructure replacement/relocation.
steps.guidance: Engage structural engineers and contractors for assessment.
steps.outcome: Remediation or relocation plan with timeline established.

steps.title: Restore IT operations and validate data integrity from backups
steps.desc: Rebuild or relocate infrastructure and restore data from backups, validating integrity before resuming normal operation.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive reconciliation and application validation before declaring recovery complete.
steps.outcome: IT operations restored with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Transition business functions back to the restored or new facility
steps.desc: Move business functions back once the primary or replacement facility is confirmed operational and safe.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased transition to avoid disruption.
steps.outcome: Business functions restored.

steps.title: Review seismic resilience and business-continuity preparedness
steps.desc: Evaluate seismic-resilience measures (equipment bracing, structural standards) and business continuity plan effectiveness.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements for facilities in seismically active regions.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54724.def: An environmental disruption affecting a company facility that has not yet been classified as fire, flood, or earthquake damage.
ITID-54724.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for environmental disruptions not yet attributed to fire, flood, or earthquake.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported environmental disruptions pending cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any disruption once cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54721, 54722, or 54723)
ITID-54724.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54724.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate if life safety is involved.
ITID-54724.escalation: Escalate to facilities and business continuity for initial triage.
indicators: Facility disruption without an established environmental cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
