rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54724.detection: Relies on initial facility monitoring alerting only.
ITID-54724.response: Triage to fire, flood, or earthquake cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54724.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — environmental continuity events are non-adversarial. Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Environmental Disruption
playbook.description: An environmental event of undetermined specific type (fire, flood, seismic, or other) disrupts a facility's IT operations.

steps.title: Confirm environmental event, personnel safety, and specific event type
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation from facilities/emergency services on the nature of the environmental event and verify all personnel are safe.
steps.guidance: Prioritize life-safety confirmation above all IT considerations.
steps.outcome: Personnel safety confirmed; specific event type identified where possible.

steps.title: Assess facility accessibility and business impact
steps.desc: Determine whether the facility is safe to enter and assess the resulting business impact.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities/emergency responders before permitting any IT recovery access.
steps.outcome: Accessibility status and impact scope documented.

steps.title: Fail over affected business functions to an alternate site
steps.desc: Redirect affected business functions to an alternate office or DR site.
steps.guidance: Follow the business continuity plan for the affected site.
steps.outcome: Business functions continuing from an alternate location.

steps.title: Secure the site and notify insurance/regulators as needed
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities to secure the site against further loss and notify insurance carriers and any regulators requiring disclosure.
steps.outcome: Site secured; required notifications sent.

steps.title: Assess damage and plan remediation or facility replacement
steps.desc: Determine whether the facility can be repaired or must be replaced, and plan accordingly.
steps.guidance: Engage appropriate specialists (structural, water-damage, fire-restoration) based on the event type.
steps.outcome: Remediation or replacement plan established.

steps.title: Restore IT operations and validate data integrity from backups
steps.desc: Rebuild or relocate infrastructure and restore data from backups, validating integrity before resuming normal operation.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive reconciliation and application validation.
steps.outcome: IT operations restored with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Transition business functions back to the restored facility
steps.desc: Move business functions back once the primary facility is confirmed operational and safe.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased transition to avoid disruption.
steps.outcome: Business functions restored.

steps.title: Review environmental-hazard resilience and business-continuity preparedness
steps.desc: Evaluate environmental-hazard mitigation measures and business continuity plan effectiveness for the affected facility.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54731.def: A facility power outage in which loss of utility grid power is compounded by the failure of on-site backup power systems (UPS or generator) to engage, resulting in an uncontrolled loss of power to IT systems.
ITID-54731.purpose: Captures the specific failure mode of grid power loss combined with backup power (UPS/generator) failing to engage, as a non-adversarial business-continuity event distinct from the data-center-level grid outage framing elsewhere in the tree.
scopeIncludes: Generator failing to start or transfer switch failing to engage after grid loss
UPS failing to sustain load during the transfer window
Uncontrolled shutdown of systems resulting from the combined grid-and-backup failure
scopeExcludes: Grid outage where backup power engages successfully and only the data-center-outage angle is relevant (see ITID-54121)
Battery depletion after a successfully engaged UPS during an extended outage (see ITID-54732)
ITID-54731.severity: Critical — an uncontrolled power loss risks both extended outage and hardware/data damage from ungraceful shutdown.
ITID-54731.escalation: Escalate immediately to facilities engineering and IT infrastructure; assess for hardware damage or data corruption from the ungraceful shutdown.
indicators: BMS/generator alarm indicating failure to start or transfer
Uncontrolled, simultaneous loss of telemetry across systems rather than a graceful shutdown sequence
Post-event hardware diagnostics indicating ungraceful shutdown damage
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial infrastructure/maintenance failure
rootCauses: Deferred or inadequate generator/UPS maintenance and load testing
Automatic transfer switch misconfiguration or failure
Fuel supply issues for the generator
controls: Regular generator load testing and maintenance schedule
UPS runtime and health monitoring
Redundant (N+1) backup power design
ITID-54731.detection: BMS and generator/UPS monitoring provide direct, high-confidence detection of the backup-power failure mode.
ITID-54731.response: Restore power as quickly as possible via manual intervention or alternate source; assess all affected systems for hardware/data integrity before returning to service, framing recovery around business continuity rather than threat containment.
metrics: Time to restore power
Number of systems requiring integrity checks post-outage
Generator/UPS test-pass rate prior to the event
ITID-54731.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique. Distinct from ITID-54121, which frames the equivalent scenario from the data-center-outage angle rather than the backup-power-failure-mode angle.

playbook.name: Grid Power Outage with UPS/Generator Failure to Engage
playbook.description: A utility grid power outage occurs and the backup UPS/generator system fails to engage as expected, causing an uncontrolled loss of power to IT systems.

steps.title: Confirm grid outage and diagnose backup power engagement failure
steps.desc: Confirm the grid outage and determine why the UPS/generator failed to engage (transfer switch failure, generator start failure, UPS battery failure).
steps.guidance: Review BMS logs and generator/UPS diagnostic data for the failure point.
steps.outcome: Outage confirmed and backup-power failure point identified.

steps.title: Assess systems impacted by the uncontrolled power loss
steps.desc: Determine which systems experienced ungraceful shutdown and assess potential for hardware/data damage from the uncontrolled loss of power.
steps.guidance: Review server/storage logs for signs of dirty shutdown.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented including potential data-integrity risk.

steps.title: Manually engage backup power or expedite emergency repair
steps.desc: Attempt manual generator start or transfer-switch override, or expedite an emergency electrician/generator technician dispatch if manual engagement is not possible.
steps.guidance: Follow facility emergency power procedures; prioritize restoring power to critical systems first.
steps.outcome: Backup power restored manually or emergency repair dispatched.

steps.title: Fail over critical workloads to a secondary site if power cannot be quickly restored
steps.desc: If power restoration will take significant time, fail over critical workloads to a geographically separate site.
steps.guidance: Follow the site-failover runbook.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads running from an unaffected site.

steps.title: Repair or replace the failed transfer switch/generator/UPS component
steps.desc: Complete root-cause repair of the backup power system component that failed to engage.
steps.guidance: Test the repaired component under simulated outage conditions before declaring fixed.
steps.outcome: Backup power system confirmed to engage correctly under test.

steps.title: Restore power to systems and check for hardware/data damage from the ungraceful shutdown
steps.desc: Bring systems back online in a controlled sequence and check for filesystem corruption or hardware damage caused by the uncontrolled power loss.
steps.guidance: Run filesystem checks and hardware diagnostics before returning systems to full production use.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with no undetected corruption or hardware damage.

steps.title: Fail back workloads and validate data integrity
steps.desc: Return any failed-over workloads to the primary site and verify data integrity.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks for any transactions active during the outage window.
steps.outcome: Primary site fully operational with verified data integrity.

steps.title: Review backup power testing regimen and failure root cause
steps.desc: Determine why the routine backup-power failover testing (if any) did not catch this failure mode, and recommend testing/maintenance improvements.
steps.guidance: Recommend more frequent load-bank testing and transfer-switch maintenance.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54732.def: A facility power event in which on-site battery backup (UPS) successfully engages upon grid loss but is depleted before power is restored or a generator takes over, resulting in a delayed loss of power to IT systems.
ITID-54732.purpose: Captures the specific failure mode of battery backup depleting during an extended outage after successfully engaging, distinct from the initial transfer-failure scenario.
scopeIncludes: UPS successfully bridging the initial outage but running out of charge before generator startup or grid restoration
Extended grid outages exceeding designed battery runtime with no generator or an insufficient generator fuel supply
scopeExcludes: Backup power failing to engage at all (see ITID-54731)
ITID-54732.severity: High to Critical depending on whether the eventual shutdown was graceful (systems given warning to shut down cleanly) or abrupt.
ITID-54732.priority: P1 if shutdown is imminent/occurring without a graceful shutdown having completed; P2 if graceful shutdown procedures completed successfully before depletion.
ITID-54732.escalation: Escalate to facilities engineering as soon as extended outage is identified, well before battery depletion, to arrange alternate power or expedited restoration.
indicators: UPS runtime/battery-charge monitoring showing declining reserve during an extended outage
Grid restoration or generator startup not occurring within the UPS's rated runtime
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial infrastructure/maintenance failure
rootCauses: Extended utility outage beyond planned backup runtime
No generator present or generator fuel/maintenance issue preventing timely startup
UPS battery capacity degraded below rated runtime
controls: UPS runtime/battery-health monitoring with proactive alerting
Generator with adequate fuel reserve as a secondary backup
Automated graceful-shutdown procedures triggered before full battery depletion
ITID-54732.detection: UPS runtime monitoring provides advance warning well ahead of depletion, enabling proactive graceful shutdown if configured.
ITID-54732.response: Trigger automated or manual graceful shutdown procedures before depletion if restoration is not imminent; frame recovery around business continuity rather than threat containment.
metrics: UPS runtime achieved vs. rated capacity
Percentage of systems gracefully shut down before depletion
ITID-54732.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Battery Backup Depletion During Extended Outage
playbook.description: During an extended grid power outage, UPS battery backup capacity is depleted before power is restored or generator support engages, threatening an uncontrolled shutdown.

steps.title: Confirm battery depletion trajectory and remaining runtime
steps.desc: Monitor UPS battery capacity and discharge rate to determine remaining runtime before systems lose power.
steps.guidance: Use UPS/DCIM telemetry to project time-to-depletion based on current load and discharge curve.
steps.outcome: Remaining runtime estimated with confidence.

steps.title: Assess which systems will lose power first and their criticality
steps.desc: Determine load-shedding order and identify which systems are on which UPS circuits to prioritize response.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference UPS circuit mapping against system criticality tiers.
steps.outcome: Prioritized list of at-risk systems by criticality documented.

steps.title: Initiate graceful shutdown of non-critical systems to extend runtime for critical systems
steps.desc: Proactively and gracefully shut down lower-priority systems to conserve remaining battery capacity for critical systems.
steps.guidance: Follow the documented load-shedding sequence; avoid abrupt/dirty shutdowns.
steps.outcome: Battery runtime extended for critical systems through load shedding.
steps.abort: If power or generator support arrives before shedding is complete, halt the shutdown sequence.

steps.title: Escalate for emergency generator repair or portable power and expedite utility restoration inquiry
steps.desc: Engage facilities/generator technicians for emergency repair or portable generator deployment, and press the utility provider for a restoration ETA.
steps.outcome: Emergency power support engaged; utility ETA obtained.

steps.title: Fail over remaining critical workloads to an unaffected site if depletion is imminent
steps.desc: If battery depletion is imminent and power/generator support will not arrive in time, fail over critical workloads to a geographically separate site.
steps.guidance: Follow the site-failover runbook.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads relocated before an uncontrolled shutdown occurs.

steps.title: Confirm stable power restoration before reversing load-shedding
steps.desc: Verify utility or generator power is stably restored before bringing shed systems back online.
steps.guidance: Monitor for voltage fluctuations for a stabilization window.
steps.outcome: Stable power confirmed.
steps.abort: If power is unstable, remain in the load-shed state.

steps.title: Bring systems back online in priority order and validate integrity
steps.desc: Restore shed and failed-over systems in a controlled sequence and verify no data loss or hardware damage occurred.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks on any transactions active during the event.
steps.outcome: All systems restored with verified integrity.

steps.title: Review UPS capacity planning and load-shedding procedure effectiveness
steps.desc: Assess whether UPS battery capacity, load-shedding automation, and generator reliability are adequate for expected outage durations.
steps.guidance: Recommend capacity upgrades or automation improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54733.def: A power outage or UPS-related event affecting company systems that has not yet been classified as a backup-power-transfer failure or a battery-depletion scenario.
ITID-54733.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for power outage/UPS failure events not yet attributed to a backup-power-transfer failure or a battery-depletion-during-extended-outage scenario.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported power/UPS events pending failure-mode confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once failure mode is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54731 or 54732)
ITID-54733.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified; treat as at least High pending triage.
ITID-54733.escalation: Escalate to facilities engineering for initial triage.
indicators: Power/UPS-related service disruption without an established specific failure mode
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54733.detection: Relies on initial BMS/UPS monitoring alerting only.
ITID-54733.response: Triage to the specific power/UPS failure mode, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54733.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — power/UPS events are non-adversarial. Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Power Outage/UPS Failure
playbook.description: A power outage or UPS failure of undetermined specific cause disrupts IT operations.

steps.title: Confirm power/UPS failure and gather initial diagnostics
steps.desc: Confirm the nature of the power event (grid outage, UPS failure, or both) and gather BMS/DCIM diagnostic data.
steps.guidance: Check BMS alarms and UPS status telemetry.
steps.outcome: Power event confirmed with initial diagnostics documented.

steps.title: Assess systems at risk and estimated time before impact
steps.desc: Determine which systems are at risk and estimate time remaining before a forced shutdown.
steps.guidance: Review UPS/generator telemetry for runtime estimates.
steps.outcome: At-risk systems and time budget documented.

steps.title: Engage backup power systems or fail over critical workloads
steps.desc: Activate generator/UPS support or fail over critical workloads to a secondary site depending on the nature of the failure.
steps.guidance: Follow the applicable power-failure or DR runbook.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads protected from power loss.

steps.title: Coordinate with facilities/utility/UPS vendor on restoration
steps.desc: Engage the relevant party (facilities, utility provider, or UPS vendor) to obtain a restoration timeline.
steps.outcome: Restoration ETA obtained.

steps.title: Confirm stable power restoration
steps.desc: Verify power is stably restored before reversing any containment actions.
steps.guidance: Monitor for voltage fluctuations before transitioning load back.
steps.outcome: Stable power confirmed.

steps.title: Restore systems and validate data integrity
steps.desc: Bring systems back online and verify no data loss or hardware damage occurred.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks and hardware diagnostics as applicable.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with verified integrity.

steps.title: Fail back workloads to primary infrastructure
steps.desc: Return any failed-over workloads to primary infrastructure once stability is confirmed.
steps.guidance: Perform a phased failback with monitoring.
steps.outcome: Primary infrastructure fully operational.

steps.title: Review backup power adequacy and monitoring
steps.desc: Assess whether backup power capacity and monitoring/alerting were adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend infrastructure or process improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54741.def: A shutdown of IT equipment triggered by unplanned failure of an HVAC unit cooling a server room, closet, or non-data-center IT space, resulting in a thermal-protection shutdown.
ITID-54741.purpose: Captures a discrete HVAC unit failure causing localized server overheating shutdown, distinct from planned-maintenance-driven thermal shutdowns.
scopeIncludes: Unplanned HVAC compressor or unit failure in a server closet or small server room
Automated thermal-protection shutdown of affected equipment following the failure
scopeExcludes: Precision cooling plant (CRAC/CRAH/chiller) failure at a primary/DR data center (see ITID-54122)
Thermal shutdown resulting from a known, planned maintenance activity (see ITID-54742)
ITID-54741.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: Medium to High depending on the criticality of systems in the affected space.
ITID-54741.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the affected space hosts business-critical systems with no redundancy elsewhere.
ITID-54741.escalation: Escalate to facilities engineering for expedited repair; IT infrastructure manages graceful shutdown/migration of at-risk equipment.
indicators: Temperature sensor alarms in the affected space
Automated hardware thermal-shutdown events
HVAC unit fault code or alarm
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial infrastructure event
rootCauses: HVAC unit mechanical/electrical failure
Insufficient redundancy for small server room/closet cooling
Deferred maintenance
controls: Temperature monitoring with proactive alerting
Redundant cooling for server rooms/closets
Preventive HVAC maintenance program
ITID-54741.detection: Temperature sensors and hardware thermal-shutdown telemetry provide direct, high-confidence detection.
ITID-54741.response: Facilities engineering repairs or replaces the failed unit; IT infrastructure relocates or shuts down at-risk equipment gracefully in the interim.
metrics: Time from temperature alarm to remediation
Number of hosts subjected to thermal shutdown
ITID-54741.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique. Distinct from ITID-54122, which addresses data-center-scale precision cooling plant failure.

playbook.name: HVAC Unit Failure Causing Server Overheating Shutdown
playbook.description: An HVAC unit failure causes server room temperatures to rise, forcing an overheating-related shutdown of hosted equipment.

steps.title: Confirm HVAC failure and rising temperature alarms
steps.desc: Validate BMS/DCIM temperature alarms and identify the failed HVAC unit.
steps.guidance: Cross-check rack inlet temperature sensors against thresholds; identify the affected zone.
steps.outcome: HVAC failure confirmed and affected zone identified.

steps.title: Assess time-to-thermal-shutdown for affected equipment
steps.desc: Estimate how quickly temperatures will breach safe operating limits for hardware in the affected zone.
steps.guidance: Use manufacturer thermal thresholds and current temperature rise rate.
steps.outcome: Documented time budget before automatic hardware thermal shutdown.

steps.title: Initiate graceful workload migration or shutdown of affected racks
steps.desc: Proactively migrate workloads off the affected racks or perform an orderly shutdown to prevent uncontrolled hardware failure.
steps.guidance: Prioritize critical systems for migration to unaffected zones or DR site.
steps.outcome: Critical workloads relocated or safely shut down before thermal damage occurs.
steps.abort: If temperatures stabilize before shutdown is required, halt the shutdown sequence.

steps.title: Deploy portable cooling and engage HVAC maintenance vendor

steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities for physical access and safety during remediation.
steps.outcome: Temporary cooling in place; vendor dispatched.

steps.title: Repair or replace the failed HVAC unit
steps.desc: Complete root-cause repair of the HVAC unit (compressor, fan, control failure).
steps.guidance: Verify repair against manufacturer specifications; test under load.
steps.outcome: HVAC unit restored to full rated capacity.

steps.title: Restore workloads and verify hardware health post-thermal event
steps.desc: Bring migrated/shutdown systems back online and check hardware for thermal damage.
steps.guidance: Run hardware diagnostics before returning to full production load.
steps.outcome: All systems restored with confirmed hardware health.

steps.title: Confirm sustained temperature stability under full load
steps.desc: Monitor rack temperatures for a defined stabilization period after full production load resumes.
steps.guidance: Set temporary tighter alert thresholds during the observation window.
steps.outcome: Temperatures remain within normal operating range under full load.

steps.title: Review cooling redundancy and monitoring thresholds
steps.desc: Assess whether N+1 cooling redundancy and alarm thresholds were adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend redundancy upgrades or earlier-warning thresholds as needed.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54742.def: A thermal-protection shutdown of IT equipment caused by a failure or gap in cooling system maintenance procedures — such as a maintenance activity performed incorrectly, or scheduled maintenance being skipped or overdue.
ITID-54742.purpose: Captures thermal shutdown resulting from a cooling system maintenance failure or gap, distinguishing planned/maintenance-process breakdowns from unplanned unit failures.
scopeIncludes: Cooling system left in a degraded state following an incomplete or improperly executed maintenance activity
Thermal shutdown resulting from overdue/skipped preventive maintenance allowing gradual degradation to go unaddressed
scopeExcludes: A discrete, unplanned HVAC unit failure unrelated to a maintenance activity or gap (see ITID-54741)
ITID-54742.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: Medium to High depending on the criticality of systems in the affected space.
ITID-54742.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the affected space hosts business-critical systems with no redundancy elsewhere.
ITID-54742.escalation: Escalate to facilities engineering for expedited correction; review the maintenance process for the gap that allowed the failure.
indicators: Thermal shutdown occurring during or shortly after a scheduled maintenance window
Maintenance records showing overdue/skipped service on the affected cooling system
Temperature trend showing gradual degradation prior to the shutdown, consistent with deferred maintenance
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial operational/maintenance-process event
rootCauses: Maintenance procedure not fully validated before returning the system to service
Preventive maintenance schedule not enforced/tracked
Maintenance vendor error
controls: Post-maintenance validation checklist before returning cooling systems to service
Enforced, tracked preventive maintenance schedule
Temperature trend monitoring to catch gradual degradation
ITID-54742.detection: Temperature trend monitoring can catch gradual degradation ahead of a full shutdown if reviewed proactively; otherwise detection is reactive to the shutdown event itself.
ITID-54742.response: Correct the maintenance gap immediately, validate the fix, and review the maintenance process to prevent recurrence, framing the response around business continuity and process improvement.
metrics: Preventive maintenance schedule compliance rate
Time from degradation onset to shutdown (early-warning window missed)
ITID-54742.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is an operational/environmental continuity event, not an adversary technique. Distinguished from ITID-54741 by root cause: a maintenance-process gap rather than a discrete unplanned unit failure.

ITID-54743.def: An HVAC or cooling-related thermal shutdown event affecting company IT equipment that has not yet been classified as a discrete unit failure or a maintenance-process gap.
ITID-54743.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for HVAC/cooling system failure events not yet attributed to a discrete unit failure or a maintenance-process gap.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported cooling-related thermal shutdowns pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54741 or 54742)
ITID-54743.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54743.escalation: Escalate to facilities engineering for initial triage.
indicators: Thermal-shutdown event without an established specific cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage

ITID-54743.response: Triage to unit-failure or maintenance-process cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54743.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — cooling failures are non-adversarial. Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

ITID-54811.def: A volumetric, network-layer DDoS attack that saturates company network capacity or upstream links, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than the underlying flood-technique mechanics.
ITID-54811.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for high-volume volumetric DDoS attacks within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to ITID-40000's detailed technique breakdown.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed high-volume network-layer flood (e.g., UDP/ICMP/amplification flood) affecting company connectivity
Activation of DDoS scrubbing/mitigation capacity in response to a volumetric attack
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics of specific flood/amplification techniques (see the DoS/DDoS technique breakdown under ITID-40000)
Application-layer DDoS specifically (see ITID-54821)
Non-adversarial ISP capacity/routing failures (see ITID-54132/54341)
ITID-54811.severity: High if the attack saturates all available upstream capacity; Medium if scrubbing/mitigation absorbs the volume with minimal customer impact.
ITID-54811.priority: P1 if customer-facing services are unreachable; P2 if mitigation is largely effective.
ITID-54811.escalation: Escalate to network operations and the DDoS mitigation provider immediately upon confirmation of volumetric attack traffic.
indicators: Sudden, massive spike in inbound traffic volume from a large number of distinct sources
Upstream link saturation alerts
DDoS mitigation provider confirms active scrubbing
vectors: UDP/ICMP flood, DNS/NTP amplification, or other high-volume flood techniques against company IP space
rootCauses: Insufficient upstream DDoS scrubbing capacity relative to observed attack volumes
Public exposure of critical service endpoints without protection
controls: Upstream DDoS scrubbing/mitigation service
Anycast network architecture to absorb/distribute volumetric load
Rate-limiting and traffic filtering at network edge
ITID-54811.detection: Network traffic volume monitoring and mitigation-provider alerting provide immediate, high-confidence detection.
ITID-54811.response: Activate DDoS scrubbing/mitigation immediately; monitor for attack technique shifts (e.g., pivot to application-layer) throughout the event.
metrics: Peak attack volume
Time to mitigation activation
Duration of customer-facing impact
ITID-54811.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed volumetric DDoS technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General High-Volume DDoS Attack (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: A high-volume volumetric DDoS attack overwhelms network capacity, disrupting availability of critical systems.

steps.title: Confirm volumetric attack and characterize traffic pattern
steps.desc: Confirm the traffic surge is a volumetric DDoS attack and characterize its pattern (protocol, source distribution, amplification technique).
steps.guidance: Use flow-analysis/NetFlow data and DDoS mitigation provider telemetry to characterize the attack.
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed and characterized with traffic pattern documented.
steps.tool: NetFlow analysis / DDoS mitigation provider console

steps.title: Assess impact on critical systems and available headroom
steps.desc: Determine which critical systems/services are degraded and how much network/mitigation capacity headroom remains.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference with the service catalog.
steps.outcome: Impact and remaining headroom documented.

steps.title: Activate DDoS scrubbing/mitigation service
steps.desc: Route traffic through the DDoS scrubbing/mitigation provider to filter attack traffic before it reaches origin infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Verify mitigation is engaged and effectively filtering, not just routing.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic scrubbed with legitimate traffic reaching origin.

steps.title: Apply rate limiting and upstream provider coordination
steps.desc: Apply rate limiting at the network edge and coordinate with upstream transit providers for additional filtering closer to the attack source.
steps.guidance: Engage upstream provider NOC for blackhole routing or additional filtering if the attack exceeds local mitigation capacity.
steps.outcome: Additional filtering capacity engaged.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and activate the incident communication plan
steps.desc: Communicate the attack's impact and mitigation status to affected stakeholders and customer-facing teams.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Tune mitigation rules in real time as the attack evolves
steps.desc: Continuously adjust scrubbing/filtering rules to counter attacker adaptation (changing source IPs, protocols, or amplification vectors).
steps.guidance: Work with the mitigation provider's SOC for real-time signature updates.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic effectively mitigated with service availability maintained.
steps.abort: If mitigation cannot keep pace, activate a maintenance/queueing page to protect backend systems.

steps.title: Stand down elevated mitigation posture and confirm normal service
steps.desc: Once the attack subsides, verify normal traffic patterns have resumed and confirm service performance is back to baseline.
steps.guidance: Maintain a reduced level of mitigation readiness for a monitoring period in case of renewed attack.
steps.outcome: Normal service confirmed; mitigation readiness maintained appropriately.

steps.title: Review mitigation capacity and activation speed
steps.desc: Evaluate how quickly mitigation was activated and whether scrubbing capacity/contracts are adequate for future attacks of this scale.
steps.guidance: Recommend always-on mitigation or improved activation speed as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54821.def: An application-layer (Layer 7) DDoS attack that exhausts company web/API server resources through high volumes of seemingly legitimate requests, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than the underlying request-flood mechanics.
ITID-54821.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for application-layer DDoS attacks within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to ITID-40000's detailed technique breakdown.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed HTTP/HTTPS request flood or similar Layer 7 exhaustion attack affecting company applications
Activation of application-layer mitigation (rate-limiting, bot management, WAF rules) in response
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics of specific Layer 7 attack techniques (see the DoS/DDoS technique breakdown under ITID-40000)
Network-layer volumetric DDoS specifically (see ITID-54811)
ITID-54821.severity: High if the attack renders customer-facing applications unresponsive; Medium if mitigation absorbs the load with degraded but functional service.
ITID-54821.priority: P1 if customer-facing applications are down; P2 if mitigation is largely effective.
ITID-54821.escalation: Escalate to application/web operations and the CDN/WAF provider immediately upon confirmation of a Layer 7 attack pattern.
indicators: Sudden spike in request rate to specific endpoints with request patterns inconsistent with legitimate user behavior
Application server resource exhaustion (CPU, connection pool) despite normal-looking individual requests
WAF/bot-management alerts flagging coordinated automated traffic
vectors: High-volume HTTP/HTTPS request floods targeting resource-intensive endpoints (e.g., search, login)
rootCauses: Lack of rate-limiting or bot-management controls on resource-intensive endpoints
Insufficient application-layer scaling/caching to absorb legitimate-looking request spikes
controls: WAF and bot-management with rate-limiting on resource-intensive endpoints
Application-layer caching and auto-scaling
CAPTCHA/challenge mechanisms for suspicious traffic patterns
ITID-54821.detection: Application performance monitoring and WAF/bot-management alerting provide reliable detection of the request-pattern anomaly.
ITID-54821.response: Activate rate-limiting, bot-management, and WAF rules immediately; scale application resources where feasible to absorb legitimate traffic during mitigation.
metrics: Peak request rate
Time to mitigation activation
Application availability during the attack
ITID-54821.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed application-layer DDoS technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Application-Layer DDoS (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: An application-layer (Layer 7) DDoS attack overwhelms application resources with seemingly legitimate requests, disrupting critical systems.

steps.title: Confirm application-layer attack and distinguish from legitimate traffic surge
steps.desc: Analyze request patterns (URI targeting, request rate per source, user-agent anomalies) to confirm a Layer 7 DDoS attack rather than a legitimate traffic spike.
steps.guidance: Use web application firewall (WAF) and application performance monitoring logs to distinguish attack traffic from genuine load.
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed and distinguished from legitimate traffic with targeted endpoints identified.
steps.abort: If the surge appears to be legitimate (e.g., a marketing event), reclassify as a capacity/scaling issue instead.

steps.title: Assess impact on application resources and critical functions
steps.desc: Determine which application resources (database connections, compute, specific endpoints) are being exhausted and the resulting business impact.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Apply WAF rules and challenge-based filtering to targeted endpoints
steps.desc: Deploy WAF rules, rate limiting, and challenge mechanisms (CAPTCHA, JS challenges) targeting the abused endpoints.
steps.guidance: Tune rules to minimize impact on legitimate users while filtering attack traffic.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic significantly reduced at targeted endpoints.

steps.title: Scale application resources and engage mitigation provider
steps.desc: Temporarily scale up application/database resources to absorb residual load and engage the DDoS mitigation provider for Layer 7-specific mitigation.
steps.outcome: Additional capacity and specialized mitigation engaged.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and activate the incident communication plan
steps.desc: Communicate the attack's impact and mitigation status to affected stakeholders and customer-facing teams.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Tune filtering rules in real time as the attack evolves
steps.desc: Continuously adjust WAF/challenge rules to counter attacker adaptation (rotating user-agents, distributed source IPs, request pattern changes).
steps.guidance: Work with the mitigation provider's SOC for real-time rule updates.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic effectively mitigated with application availability maintained.
steps.abort: If mitigation cannot keep pace, temporarily disable the most heavily targeted non-essential feature/endpoint.

steps.title: Stand down elevated mitigation posture and confirm normal service
steps.desc: Once the attack subsides, verify normal request patterns have resumed and confirm application performance is back to baseline.
steps.guidance: Maintain a reduced level of mitigation readiness for a monitoring period.
steps.outcome: Normal service confirmed.

steps.title: Review application-layer defenses and rate-limiting posture
steps.desc: Evaluate WAF rule coverage, rate-limiting defaults, and detection speed for Layer 7 attacks.
steps.guidance: Recommend improved bot-detection or rate-limiting defaults as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54831.def: A DDoS attack against company infrastructure generated by a botnet of compromised Internet of Things (IoT) devices, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than the botnet's own build-out mechanics.
ITID-54831.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for IoT-botnet-driven DDoS attacks within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to ITID-40000's detailed technique breakdown.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed DDoS attack attributed to an IoT botnet (e.g., Mirai-family or similar) affecting company connectivity or applications
Threat intelligence correlation confirming the attacking source infrastructure is IoT-device-based
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics of IoT botnet formation/C2 (a separate malware/infrastructure topic covered elsewhere in the taxonomy)
Non-IoT-sourced volumetric or application-layer DDoS (see ITID-54811/54821)
ITID-54831.severity: High if attack volume/scale is amplified by a large botnet; Medium if scrubbing/mitigation absorbs the load.
ITID-54831.priority: P1 if customer-facing services are unreachable; P2 if mitigation is largely effective.
ITID-54831.escalation: Escalate to network operations and the DDoS mitigation provider; share observed source indicators with threat intelligence for broader botnet tracking.
indicators: Attack traffic sourced from a very large, geographically diverse number of consumer/IoT-associated IP addresses
Threat intelligence attribution linking the attack to a known IoT botnet
Traffic signatures consistent with known IoT botnet malware families
vectors: Volumetric or application-layer flood generated by a large-scale compromised-IoT-device botnet
rootCauses: Insufficient upstream DDoS scrubbing capacity relative to large botnet-generated volumes
Public exposure of critical service endpoints without protection
controls: Upstream DDoS scrubbing/mitigation service sized for large botnet volumes
Threat intelligence integration for known botnet source tracking
Anycast network architecture
ITID-54831.detection: Network traffic volume monitoring combined with threat intelligence source attribution provides strong detection and confirmation.
ITID-54831.response: Activate DDoS scrubbing/mitigation immediately; share indicators with threat intelligence and industry information-sharing bodies to support broader botnet takedown efforts.
metrics: Peak attack volume
Number of distinct source IPs observed
Time to mitigation activation
ITID-54831.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed DDoS technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here. T1584.005 reflects the botnet-infrastructure angle specifically.

ITID-54841.def: A DDoS attack specifically targeting company or provider DNS/CDN infrastructure, aiming to prevent resolution of or access to company domains, tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than the underlying attack-technique mechanics.
ITID-54841.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for DDoS attacks specifically targeting DNS or CDN infrastructure within the Critical System Disruption domain, pointing back to ITID-40000's detailed technique breakdown.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed DDoS attack against authoritative DNS servers or a CDN provider serving company domains
Loss of domain resolution or CDN-fronted service availability attributable to a confirmed DDoS attack
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics of DNS/CDN-targeted attack techniques (see the DoS/DDoS technique breakdown under ITID-40000)
Non-adversarial CDN provider outages or configuration errors (see ITID-54141/54142)
DNS poisoning/takedown via non-DDoS means (see ITID-54321)
ITID-54841.severity: Critical if company domains become unresolvable; High if resolution is degraded but partially functional.
ITID-54841.priority: P1, always, given the cascading impact of DNS/CDN unavailability across all dependent services.

indicators: Sudden spike in DNS query volume against authoritative servers from a large number of sources
CDN provider confirms an active DDoS incident affecting the company's distribution
Widespread reports of company domains failing to resolve
vectors: Volumetric flood against authoritative DNS servers
DDoS attack against a CDN provider's edge infrastructure serving company domains
rootCauses: Single point of failure in DNS provider without redundant/secondary DNS
Insufficient DDoS mitigation capacity at the DNS/CDN layer
controls: Redundant, multi-provider authoritative DNS
DDoS-protected/anycast DNS and CDN services
Rapid DNS TTL adjustment procedures for emergency failover
ITID-54841.detection: DNS query volume monitoring and CDN provider alerting provide reliable detection; broad customer-reported resolution failures corroborate impact.
ITID-54841.response: Engage the DNS/CDN provider's incident response immediately; failover to secondary DNS/CDN capacity where available.
metrics: Duration of resolution/availability impact
Time to failover to secondary provider
ITID-54841.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-40000 for the detailed DNS/CDN-targeted DDoS technique breakdown rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General DNS and CDN Targeted DDoS (Critical System Disruption Context)
playbook.description: A DDoS attack specifically targets DNS or CDN infrastructure, disrupting the resolution or delivery of critical systems and services.

steps.title: Confirm the attack is specifically targeting DNS/CDN infrastructure
steps.desc: Confirm elevated query/request volumes are specifically targeting authoritative DNS servers or CDN edge nodes, distinguishing this from a general volumetric attack.
steps.guidance: Use DNS server query logs and CDN provider traffic analytics to confirm the targeted infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed as DNS/CDN-targeted with affected infrastructure identified.

steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.outcome: DNS resolution/content delivery restored via mitigation or secondary provider.

steps.title: Apply rate limiting and anycast/traffic distribution adjustments
