ITID-54911.def: A disruption to a company business-critical function caused by an outage of a SaaS application the company depends on, where the outage originates within the vendor's own environment and no compromise is implicated.
ITID-54911.purpose: Captures loss of a business-critical function caused by an outage at a third-party SaaS vendor, tracked as a non-adversarial vendor continuity event.
scopeIncludes: SaaS vendor-wide outage affecting a business-critical function (e.g., CRM, HR, finance, collaboration platform)
SaaS vendor degraded performance materially impacting business operations
scopeExcludes: SaaS vendor data loss/corruption specifically (see ITID-54912)
SaaS disruption caused by an MSP/vendor breach (see ITID-54921/54922)
SaaS disruption caused by DDoS against the vendor (see ITID-548xx if the vendor is identified as company-owned infrastructure, otherwise track as vendor-side and note here)
ITID-54911.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High if the function is business-critical with no manual/alternate process; Medium if a workaround exists.
ITID-54911.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the function is critical to revenue, payroll, or regulatory obligations with a hard deadline.
ITID-54911.escalation: Escalate to the business function owner and vendor management; engage the vendor's support/incident channel per the contractual escalation path.
indicators: Vendor status page confirms an active incident
Business users report application unavailability consistent with a vendor-wide event
No corresponding company-side authentication or configuration change correlates with the outage
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial vendor operational event
rootCauses: Vendor infrastructure failure
Vendor deployment/change-management failure
Vendor capacity exhaustion
controls: Documented manual/alternate process for business-critical functions during vendor outages
Vendor SLA monitoring and escalation contacts
Vendor risk assessment prioritizing availability track record for critical functions
ITID-54911.detection: Vendor status pages and business-user reports provide the primary detection signal; SOC's role is confirming absence of a company-side or adversarial cause.
ITID-54911.response: Activate manual/alternate process for the affected function where available; escalate through the vendor's contractual support channel and track toward SLA remedies.
metrics: Duration of vendor outage
Business impact duration (accounting for any manual workaround)
SLA credit/claim status
ITID-54911.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a vendor operational continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: SaaS Vendor Outage Affecting Business-Critical Function
playbook.description: A third-party SaaS vendor experiences an outage that disrupts a business-critical function dependent on that service.

steps.title: Confirm SaaS vendor outage via status page and internal monitoring
steps.desc: Correlate internal service failures with the SaaS vendor's status page or incident advisories to confirm a vendor-side outage.
steps.guidance: Check the vendor's public status page and any subscribed status-API feeds; cross-reference with internal synthetic monitoring of the integration.
steps.outcome: Outage confirmed as vendor-side with affected functionality identified.

steps.title: Assess business-critical function impact and available workarounds
steps.desc: Determine which business-critical functions depend on the SaaS service and identify any manual workarounds or alternate tools available.
steps.guidance: Consult the vendor risk register/business impact analysis for this SaaS dependency.
steps.outcome: Impact scope and available workaround options documented.

steps.title: Activate manual workaround or alternate tooling for the critical function
steps.desc: Switch affected business processes to a documented manual workaround or alternate tool to maintain critical function continuity.
steps.guidance: Follow the business continuity plan's SaaS-outage contingency procedure.
steps.outcome: Critical business function continuing via workaround.
steps.abort: If no workaround exists, prioritize communicating the limitation to affected teams and customers.

steps.title: Engage the vendor relationship manager and open a support case
steps.desc: Contact the vendor's support/account team, referencing contractual SLA terms, to escalate priority and obtain a resolution timeline.
steps.guidance: Engage the internal vendor-relationship manager to leverage the account relationship for priority handling.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged with a resolution ETA obtained.

steps.title: Notify affected internal teams and customers as appropriate
steps.desc: Communicate the outage's status and expected resolution to affected internal teams and, if customer-facing, to customers.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Monitor vendor remediation and validate resolution
steps.desc: Track the vendor's incident updates until they confirm the outage is resolved, and independently validate via synthetic checks.
steps.guidance: Do not fully revert workarounds until vendor service is confirmed stable.
steps.outcome: Vendor outage confirmed resolved and independently validated.

steps.title: Revert to normal SaaS-based operations and validate data consistency
steps.desc: Transition business processes back from the workaround to normal SaaS-based operation, reconciling any data entered during the workaround period.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks between workaround-period data and the SaaS system before fully closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Normal operations restored with data consistency verified.

steps.title: Review vendor SLA terms and contingency plan effectiveness
steps.desc: Assess whether the vendor's SLA commitments and the internal contingency/workaround plan were adequate for this outage.
steps.guidance: Recommend SLA renegotiation, alternate-vendor evaluation, or workaround-plan improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54912.def: An incident in which a SaaS vendor experiences loss or corruption of company data hosted within its platform, where the cause originates within the vendor's own environment (e.g., a failed migration or backup failure) and no compromise is implicated.
ITID-54912.purpose: Captures data loss or corruption occurring within a SaaS vendor's environment that affects company data, tracked as a non-adversarial vendor continuity event distinct from a simple availability outage.
scopeIncludes: Vendor-side data loss from a failed migration, upgrade, or backup/restore error affecting company records
Vendor-side data corruption discovered during normal use, attributed to a vendor operational error
scopeExcludes: Simple vendor availability outage with no data loss (see ITID-54911)

Data loss/corruption resulting from a confirmed vendor breach (an MSP/vendor-attack matter, see ITID-54921/54922, or a third-party data-breach ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy if data confidentiality rather than availability/integrity is the primary concern)
ITID-54912.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High if the lost/corrupted data cannot be reconstructed from other sources; Medium if the company retains an independent copy or audit trail.
ITID-54912.priority: P1 if business-critical or regulatory-relevant data is unrecoverable; P2 if recoverable from an independent source.
ITID-54912.escalation: Escalate to the business function owner, vendor management, and legal/compliance if regulatory-relevant data is affected; engage the vendor's incident/support channel for root-cause and recovery details.
indicators: Vendor discloses a data-loss or corruption incident affecting customer tenants
Business users report missing or corrupted records inconsistent with normal use
No corresponding company-side deletion/change activity correlates with the loss
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial vendor operational event
rootCauses: Vendor migration/upgrade error
Vendor backup/restore failure
Vendor database corruption
controls: Independent company-side export/backup of critical SaaS data where feasible
Vendor data-recovery SLA and contractual commitments
Regular reconciliation of critical SaaS data against independent records
ITID-54912.detection: Vendor disclosure and business-user reports provide the primary detection signal; independent company-side reconciliation, where performed, can catch corruption earlier.
ITID-54912.response: Engage the vendor for root-cause and recovery; restore from an independent company-side copy if the vendor cannot recover the data.
metrics: Volume/scope of data affected
Recoverability outcome (full/partial/none)
Time to vendor resolution
ITID-54912.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a vendor operational continuity event, not an adversary technique, unless investigation confirms the vendor itself was breached, in which case reclassify to ITID-54921/54922.

playbook.name: SaaS Vendor Data Loss/Corruption Incident Affecting Customer
playbook.description: A third-party SaaS vendor experiences a data loss or corruption incident affecting the organization's data hosted within that service.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor-reported or self-detected data loss/corruption event
steps.desc: Confirm the scope and nature of the data loss/corruption, whether reported by the vendor or detected internally.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference vendor incident notifications with internal data validation checks against known-good exports or snapshots.
steps.outcome: Data loss/corruption confirmed with affected data scope identified.
steps.tool: Vendor incident notification / data validation tools

steps.title: Assess business impact and data criticality
steps.desc: Determine which business processes and decisions depend on the affected data, and classify its criticality/sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Impact and data-criticality scope documented.

steps.title: Halt further data synchronization with the affected SaaS system
steps.desc: Pause any automated data sync/integration with the SaaS system to prevent further propagation of corrupted data into downstream internal systems.
steps.guidance: Identify all integration points before pausing.
steps.outcome: Further propagation of corrupted data halted.

steps.title: Engage the vendor for incident details, root cause, and recovery options
steps.desc: Escalate to the vendor's support/account team for full incident details, root cause, and available recovery options (vendor-side backup restoration).
steps.guidance: Reference contractual data-protection and breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged with recovery options identified.

steps.title: Notify Legal and, if required, regulators/affected customers
steps.desc: Assess whether the data loss/corruption triggers regulatory notification or customer disclosure obligations, and engage Legal accordingly.
steps.guidance: Consider data sensitivity and applicable breach-notification regulations.
steps.outcome: Legal engaged; required notifications identified and initiated.

steps.title: Validate vendor's remediation and root-cause resolution
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has resolved the underlying cause and implemented safeguards against recurrence before resuming integration.
steps.guidance: Request a vendor root-cause analysis and remediation confirmation.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation confirmed.

steps.title: Recover data from vendor backups or internal copies and validate integrity
steps.desc: Restore affected data from the vendor's backup/recovery process or from any internal copies/exports, and validate completeness and integrity.
steps.guidance: Reconcile restored data against internal records where available.
steps.outcome: Data recovered to the maximum feasible extent with integrity verified.
steps.abort: If data cannot be fully recovered, document the permanent data loss and its business impact.

steps.title: Review vendor data-protection posture and independent backup strategy
steps.desc: Assess whether the organization should maintain independent backups/exports of critical SaaS-hosted data and whether the vendor's data-protection controls meet expectations.
steps.guidance: Recommend independent backup practices for critical SaaS data going forward.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54913.def: A SaaS-vendor-related disruption affecting company operations that has not yet been classified as a straightforward availability outage or a data loss/corruption incident.
ITID-54913.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for third-party SaaS downtime events not yet attributed to a straightforward outage or a data loss/corruption incident.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported SaaS vendor incidents pending nature-of-impact confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any incident once nature of impact is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54911 or 54912)
ITID-54913.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54913.escalation: Escalate to the business function owner and vendor management for initial triage.
indicators: Vendor-related disruption without an established specific nature of impact
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54913.detection: Relies on initial vendor status/user-report signals only.
ITID-54913.response: Triage to outage or data-loss cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54913.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Third-Party SaaS Downtime
playbook.description: A third-party SaaS service experiences downtime of undetermined specific cause, disrupting dependent business functions.

steps.title: Confirm SaaS downtime and gather initial diagnostics
steps.desc: Confirm the SaaS service is down or degraded and gather initial diagnostic data (vendor status, internal monitoring).
steps.guidance: Check the vendor's status page alongside internal synthetic monitoring.
steps.outcome: Downtime confirmed with initial scope documented.

steps.title: Assess business impact and available workarounds
steps.desc: Determine which business functions depend on the SaaS service and identify any available manual workarounds.
steps.outcome: Impact and workaround options documented.

steps.title: Activate manual workaround or alternate tooling
steps.desc: Switch affected business processes to a documented workaround or alternate tool where available.
steps.guidance: Follow the business continuity plan's SaaS-outage contingency procedure.
steps.outcome: Critical business function continuing via workaround where possible.

steps.title: Engage vendor support and monitor status updates
steps.desc: Open a support case with the vendor and monitor their status updates for resolution progress.
steps.guidance: Reference SLA terms for priority handling.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and providing updates.

steps.title: Notify affected internal teams of the disruption status
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption's status and expected resolution timeline to affected internal teams.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Confirm vendor resolution of the downtime
steps.desc: Track the vendor's confirmation of resolution and independently validate service restoration.
steps.guidance: Use synthetic monitoring to confirm before reverting workarounds.
steps.outcome: Vendor downtime confirmed resolved.

steps.title: Revert to normal SaaS operations and validate data consistency
steps.desc: Transition back from any workaround to normal SaaS-based operation, reconciling any data entered during the outage.
steps.guidance: Run reconciliation checks before closing the incident.
steps.outcome: Normal operations restored with data consistency verified.

steps.title: Review vendor SLA and contingency plan adequacy
steps.desc: Assess whether the vendor SLA and contingency workaround plan were adequate for this incident.
steps.guidance: Recommend improvements as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54921.def: A confirmed breach of a company's managed service provider (MSP) in which the adversary uses the trusted relationship and access the MSP holds into multiple downstream client environments — including the company's — as a pivot point for further compromise.
ITID-54921.purpose: Captures the scenario where a breach of a managed service provider is used as a pivot point to reach multiple downstream client environments, distinguishing the multi-client pivot pattern from single-tool RMM abuse.
scopeIncludes: Adversary compromise of an MSP subsequently used to access the company's environment via the MSP's trusted connection/credentials
Confirmed multi-client impact where the company is one of several downstream victims of a single MSP breach
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the MSP's remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool specifically used for mass deployment of a payload (see ITID-54922)
A direct attack against company infrastructure with no MSP involvement
ITID-54921.severity: Critical — trusted-relationship compromise typically bypasses many perimeter controls and can affect multiple systems simultaneously.
ITID-54921.priority: P1, always; treat as an active supply chain intrusion.
ITID-54921.escalation: Escalate immediately to the MSP, executive leadership, and legal; sever or restrict the MSP's access to company systems pending investigation.
indicators: Unusual activity originating from the MSP's known access path/IP range or service account
MSP discloses a confirmed breach affecting multiple clients
Authentication or administrative activity via MSP-held credentials inconsistent with normal support patterns
vectors: Compromise of MSP administrative credentials or infrastructure, then use of the MSP's standing trusted access into client environments
rootCauses: Overly broad or standing access granted to the MSP without least-privilege scoping
Lack of monitoring/anomaly detection on MSP-originated activity
No MFA or conditional access requirement on the MSP's access path
controls: Least-privilege, time-bound access scoping for MSP connections
MFA and conditional access enforcement on all MSP access paths
Dedicated monitoring/alerting on MSP-originated administrative activity
ITID-54921.detection: Detection depends heavily on monitoring the MSP access path specifically; without dedicated instrumentation, MSP-originated malicious activity can closely resemble legitimate support activity.
ITID-54921.response: Immediately restrict or sever the MSP's access pending investigation; hunt for indicators of compromise across all systems the MSP could reach; coordinate closely with the MSP's own incident response.
metrics: Time to restrict/sever MSP access upon detection
Number of company systems reachable via the MSP's access
Time to complete hunt across MSP-reachable systems
ITID-54921.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54922 by mechanism: general trusted-relationship pivot via the MSP's standing access, as opposed to abuse of a specific RMM tool for mass payload deployment.

playbook.name: MSP Breach Used as Pivot Point into Multiple Downstream Clients
playbook.description: An attacker compromises a managed service provider and uses that foothold to pivot into multiple downstream client environments, requiring urgent cross-client notification and response.

steps.title: Confirm the MSP breach and assess exposure via the MSP relationship
steps.desc: Confirm the MSP has been breached and urgently assess what access the MSP has into the organization's environment (remote access tools, shared credentials, management consoles).
steps.guidance: Contact the MSP's incident response team immediately for details on the breach scope and confirmed pivot activity.
steps.outcome: MSP breach confirmed with the organization's exposure via the MSP relationship assessed.

steps.title: Determine whether the pivot has reached the organization's environment
steps.desc: Investigate internal systems accessible to the MSP for indicators of unauthorized access or lateral movement originating from the MSP's compromised infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Focus on remote access tool logs, MSP-managed admin accounts, and any recent unusual activity from MSP-originated connections.
steps.outcome: Determination made on whether the organization's environment has been reached, with scope documented if so.

steps.title: Immediately sever or restrict the MSP's remote access to the environment
steps.desc: Disable or heavily restrict all MSP remote access tools, VPN connections, and administrative accounts pending confirmation the MSP's environment is secure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the MSP on any legitimate access needed for remediation support while blocking all other paths.
steps.outcome: MSP access to the environment severed or tightly controlled.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and secrets accessible to or managed by the MSP
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, API keys, and secrets that the MSP had access to or that were provisioned through MSP-managed tooling.
steps.guidance: Treat all MSP-touched credentials as potentially compromised.
steps.outcome: MSP-accessible credentials and secrets rotated.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Law Enforcement, and coordinate with other affected downstream clients if identifiable
steps.desc: Notify Legal and law enforcement given the multi-client pivot nature of the attack, and where possible coordinate threat intelligence sharing with the MSP and other affected clients.
steps.outcome: Legal and law enforcement engaged; cross-client coordination initiated where feasible.

steps.title: Hunt for and remove any attacker persistence introduced via the MSP pivot
steps.desc: Conduct a thorough threat hunt across all systems the MSP had access to, removing any backdoors, unauthorized accounts, or persistence mechanisms.
steps.guidance: Assume the attacker may have established persistence beyond the initially identified access points.
steps.outcome: All attacker persistence introduced via the MSP pivot removed.

steps.title: Re-establish MSP access only after independent verification of MSP remediation
steps.desc: Restore MSP access and managed services only after independently verifying the MSP has fully remediated their breach and hardened their access controls.
steps.guidance: Require evidence of the MSP's remediation (e.g., third-party audit) before restoring trust.
steps.outcome: MSP access restored only after verified remediation, with monitoring in place.
steps.abort: If the MSP cannot demonstrate adequate remediation, consider transitioning to an alternate provider.

steps.title: Review third-party/MSP access controls and zero-trust segmentation
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether MSP access was appropriately scoped, monitored, and segmented from critical systems.
steps.guidance: Recommend least-privilege MSP access, dedicated monitoring for third-party remote access, and contractual security requirements.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54922.def: A confirmed compromise of an MSP's remote monitoring and management (RMM) software, or of the MSP's control over it, used by an adversary to mass-deploy a malicious payload (e.g., ransomware) across the company's endpoints managed through that tool.
ITID-54922.purpose: Captures the scenario where a compromised MSP remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool is specifically abused to mass-deploy a malicious payload across client endpoints, distinguishing the RMM-tool-abuse mechanism from a general trusted-relationship pivot.
scopeIncludes: Adversary abuse of a compromised RMM console or agent to push a malicious payload to company endpoints
Confirmed mass deployment traced specifically to the RMM management channel rather than a general MSP account/credential compromise
scopeExcludes: General trusted-relationship pivot via MSP access not specifically involving the RMM deployment mechanism (see ITID-54921)
ITID-54922.severity: Critical — RMM tools typically have privileged, wide-reaching deployment capability across all managed endpoints simultaneously.
ITID-54922.priority: P1, always; treat as an active mass-deployment emergency.
ITID-54922.escalation: Escalate immediately to the MSP, executive leadership, and legal; disable or isolate the RMM agent/console access across all company endpoints as an emergency containment step.
indicators: Unexpected software/script deployment pushed via the RMM tool to multiple endpoints simultaneously
RMM console access from an unrecognized location/account
The MSP or RMM vendor discloses a confirmed compromise of the platform
vectors: Compromise of RMM vendor infrastructure or the MSP's RMM console credentials, used to push a malicious deployment job
rootCauses: RMM agent granted broad, unrestricted deployment privilege across all endpoints without segmentation
Lack of monitoring/alerting on unexpected RMM-initiated deployment jobs
No MFA on the RMM console
controls: MFA and access restriction on the RMM console
Segmentation/tiering of RMM deployment scope rather than all-endpoints-at-once capability
Alerting on unexpected/unscheduled RMM deployment jobs
ITID-54922.detection: EDR/endpoint monitoring can catch the resulting payload execution; dedicated alerting on unexpected RMM deployment jobs provides earlier warning if implemented.
ITID-54922.response: Immediately disable or isolate RMM agent access across all endpoints, halt any in-progress deployment jobs, and hunt for the deployed payload across all managed endpoints.
metrics: Time to disable RMM access upon detection
Number of endpoints affected by the malicious deployment
Time to complete hunt across all managed endpoints
ITID-54922.notes: Differentiated from ITID-54921 by mechanism: specific abuse of the RMM mass-deployment capability, as opposed to a general trusted-relationship access pivot.

playbook.name: Compromised MSP Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) Tool Used for Mass Deployment
playbook.description: An attacker compromises an MSP's remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool and abuses it to mass-deploy malicious payloads across managed endpoints.

steps.title: Confirm RMM tool compromise and mass-deployment activity
steps.desc: Confirm the RMM tool has been used to push unauthorized/malicious payloads and urgently assess the scope of endpoints affected within the organization.
steps.guidance: Contact the MSP/RMM vendor immediately for details on the compromise and the list of commands/payloads pushed.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with the malicious deployment scope identified for the organization's endpoints.

steps.title: Determine payload behavior and current endpoint impact
steps.desc: Analyze the deployed payload's behavior (ransomware, backdoor, wiper, etc.) and assess current impact across affected endpoints.
steps.guidance: Use EDR telemetry and, if available, threat intelligence on the specific campaign.
steps.outcome: Payload behavior understood and current endpoint impact documented.

steps.title: Immediately disconnect the RMM agent/tool from all endpoints
steps.desc: Disable or block the RMM agent across all managed endpoints to halt further malicious command execution.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the MSP on a safe method to disable the agent without causing additional disruption.
steps.outcome: RMM tool no longer able to push further malicious commands.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints from the network
steps.desc: Network-isolate endpoints confirmed or suspected to have received the malicious payload to prevent lateral spread.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Rotate RMM credentials and any secrets accessible through the tool
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials and secrets accessible via the compromised RMM tool, including any local admin credentials it manages.
steps.outcome: RMM-accessible credentials rotated.

steps.title: Remove the malicious payload and any persistence from all affected endpoints
steps.desc: Sweep all affected endpoints for the malicious payload and any persistence mechanisms it established, reimaging where clean removal cannot be verified.
steps.guidance: Prioritize based on payload severity (e.g., ransomware/wiper endpoints first).
steps.outcome: All affected endpoints confirmed free of the malicious payload and persistence.

steps.title: Restore affected endpoints and re-enable RMM only after verified remediation
steps.desc: Restore affected endpoints from clean backups where needed, and re-enable the RMM tool only after the MSP/vendor has verified and remediated the compromise.
steps.guidance: Require evidence of RMM vendor remediation before re-establishing trust.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; RMM tool re-enabled only after verified remediation.

steps.title: Review RMM tool access scope and MSP security requirements
steps.desc: Evaluate whether RMM tool permissions were appropriately scoped and whether contractual MSP security requirements need strengthening.
steps.guidance: Recommend least-privilege RMM configuration and independent monitoring of MSP tool activity.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54923.def: A confirmed or suspected MSP-related attack affecting company operations that has not yet been classified as a general trusted-relationship pivot or specific RMM tool abuse.
ITID-54923.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for MSP attack events not yet attributed to a general trusted-relationship pivot or specific RMM tool abuse.
scopeIncludes: Newly confirmed MSP-attack events pending mechanism confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any event once mechanism is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54921 or 54922)
ITID-54923.severity: Critical pending triage, consistent with MSP-attack targeting.
ITID-54923.priority: P1, always, regardless of pending reclassification.
ITID-54923.escalation: Escalate immediately; restrict MSP access pending investigation while triage proceeds.
indicators: Confirmed or suspected malicious activity traced to the MSP relationship, specific mechanism not yet confirmed
vectors: Not yet determined — pending investigation
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending investigation
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54923.detection: Relies on initial MSP-access-path anomaly monitoring; full coverage established once reclassified.
ITID-54923.response: Restrict MSP access immediately while triage determines the specific mechanism for reclassification.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54923.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General MSP Attack
playbook.description: A managed service provider is attacked in a manner affecting the organization's environment, with the specific attack method not yet determined.

steps.title: Confirm the MSP attack and assess exposure via the MSP relationship
steps.desc: Confirm the MSP has been attacked and urgently assess what access or services the MSP provides into the organization's environment.
steps.guidance: Contact the MSP's incident response team immediately for details on the attack scope.
steps.outcome: MSP attack confirmed with the organization's exposure assessed.

steps.title: Determine attack method and whether it has reached the organization's environment
steps.desc: Investigate the specific attack method (breach/pivot, compromised RMM tool, or other) and whether the organization's systems have been affected.
steps.guidance: Escalate to the more specific MSP-incident procedure once the method is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Attack method and organizational impact scope documented.

steps.title: Restrict or sever the MSP's access to the environment
steps.desc: Disable or heavily restrict MSP remote access, tooling, and administrative accounts pending confirmation the MSP's environment is secure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the MSP on any legitimate access needed for remediation support.
steps.outcome: MSP access to the environment severed or tightly controlled.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and secrets accessible to the MSP
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, API keys, and secrets that the MSP had access to or that were provisioned through MSP-managed tooling.
steps.outcome: MSP-accessible credentials and secrets rotated.

steps.title: Engage Legal and coordinate cross-client threat intelligence where applicable
steps.desc: Notify Legal and, where feasible, coordinate threat intelligence sharing with the MSP and other potentially affected clients.
steps.outcome: Legal engaged; coordination initiated where feasible.

steps.title: Hunt for and remove any attacker persistence introduced via the MSP
steps.desc: Conduct a threat hunt across all systems the MSP had access to, removing any backdoors, unauthorized accounts, or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: All attacker persistence removed.

steps.title: Re-establish MSP access only after independent verification of remediation
steps.desc: Restore MSP access and managed services only after independently verifying the MSP has fully remediated their incident.
steps.guidance: Require evidence of remediation before restoring trust.
steps.outcome: MSP access restored only after verified remediation.
steps.abort: If the MSP cannot demonstrate adequate remediation, consider transitioning to an alternate provider.

steps.title: Review third-party/MSP access controls and monitoring
steps.desc: Evaluate whether MSP access was appropriately scoped, monitored, and segmented from critical systems.
steps.guidance: Recommend least-privilege MSP access and contractual security requirements.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked improvement actions.

ITID-54931.def: A disruption to company order fulfillment or supply-chain operations caused by an outage or degradation of a supplier's ERP, order-management, or logistics system, where no compromise of the company or the supplier is implicated.
ITID-54931.purpose: Captures disruption to company fulfillment operations caused by an outage in a supplier's ERP or order-management system, tracked as a non-adversarial vendor continuity event.
scopeIncludes: Supplier ERP/order-management system outage preventing order placement, fulfillment, or shipment tracking
Supply-chain disruption traced to a supplier's system unavailability rather than a company-side issue
scopeExcludes: Supplier system failure resulting from the supplier's sudden business failure/bankruptcy (see ITID-54932)
Supplier system compromised by an attacker (a supply chain compromise matter, see ITID-54941)
ITID-54931.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High if the supplier is a sole-source or critical-path provider; Medium if alternate suppliers can absorb demand.
ITID-54931.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if fulfillment for a critical product line is halted with no alternate supplier available.
ITID-54931.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain management and the affected business unit; engage alternate suppliers or manual order-processing procedures where available.
indicators: Supplier confirms a system outage via their support/status channel
Order/fulfillment processing errors or delays correlated with a specific supplier's system
No corresponding company-side integration or configuration change correlates with the disruption
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial vendor operational event
rootCauses: Supplier infrastructure failure
Supplier system capacity exhaustion during peak demand
Supplier deployment/change-management failure
controls: Diversified supplier base reducing sole-source dependency
Manual/alternate order-processing procedure for critical suppliers
Supplier risk assessment prioritizing system reliability
ITID-54931.detection: Supplier status communications and internal order-processing error monitoring provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-54931.response: Activate manual/alternate order-processing procedures and engage alternate suppliers where available; track resolution through the supplier's support channel.
metrics: Duration of supplier system outage
Fulfillment/order-processing impact (orders delayed/lost)
Time to activate alternate supplier/manual process
ITID-54931.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a vendor operational continuity event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Supplier ERP/Order System Outage Disrupting Fulfillment
playbook.description: A key supplier's ERP or order-management system experiences an outage, disrupting the organization's fulfillment operations dependent on that integration.

steps.title: Confirm the supplier system outage and its effect on fulfillment integration
steps.desc: Confirm the supplier's ERP/order system is down and identify how it is affecting order placement, inventory visibility, or fulfillment processing.
steps.guidance: Check integration monitoring/error logs and contact the supplier for outage confirmation.
steps.outcome: Outage confirmed with fulfillment impact identified.

steps.title: Assess order backlog and fulfillment SLA risk
steps.desc: Determine the volume of orders/transactions affected and assess risk to customer-facing fulfillment SLAs.
steps.outcome: Backlog and SLA risk documented.

steps.title: Activate manual order processing or alternate supplier channel
steps.desc: Switch to manual order placement/processing or route orders through an alternate supplier or channel to maintain fulfillment continuity.
steps.guidance: Follow the supply-chain contingency plan for this supplier relationship.
steps.outcome: Fulfillment continuing via manual process or alternate channel.
steps.abort: If no alternate exists, communicate delays proactively to affected customers.

steps.title: Engage the supplier's account/support team and monitor SLA commitments
steps.desc: Escalate through the supplier relationship manager, referencing contractual SLA terms, to obtain a resolution timeline.
steps.outcome: Supplier engaged with a resolution ETA obtained.

steps.title: Notify affected internal teams and customers of expected delays
steps.desc: Communicate the outage's status and expected impact on fulfillment to affected internal teams and customers.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Confirm supplier system restoration
steps.desc: Track the supplier's confirmation of resolution and validate integration functionality before resuming automated order flow.
steps.guidance: Perform a test transaction before full cutover.
steps.outcome: Supplier system confirmed restored and integration validated.

steps.title: Reconcile manually processed orders with the restored system
steps.desc: Enter or reconcile orders processed manually during the outage into the restored supplier system, validating data accuracy.
steps.guidance: Cross-check order counts and details between manual records and the supplier system.
steps.outcome: Order backlog reconciled with verified accuracy.

steps.title: Review supplier redundancy and contingency plan effectiveness
steps.desc: Assess whether alternate-supplier options and manual contingency procedures were adequate for this outage.
steps.guidance: Recommend supplier diversification or improved contingency procedures as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54932.def: A disruption to company operations caused by a supplier's sudden business failure, insolvency, or bankruptcy resulting in an abrupt loss of contracted service, independent of any technical system failure.
ITID-54932.purpose: Captures sudden loss of a supplier's service due to the supplier's own business failure or bankruptcy, tracked as a non-adversarial supply-chain continuity event distinct from a technical system outage.
scopeIncludes: Supplier ceasing operations or entering insolvency proceedings with no notice or transition plan
Sudden loss of a critical service or component supply due to the supplier's business closure
scopeExcludes: A supplier's technical system outage while the supplier remains a going concern (see ITID-54931)
ITID-54932.severity: Frame around business-continuity impact: High to Critical if the supplier is sole-source for a critical function or component; Medium if alternate suppliers exist and can be onboarded quickly.
ITID-54932.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if a critical business function has no viable near-term alternate.
ITID-54932.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain management, legal (for contractual/data-recovery obligations), and the affected business unit; initiate emergency supplier-transition procedures.
indicators: Public reporting or direct notification of the supplier's insolvency/closure
Sudden, unexplained unresponsiveness from a previously reliable supplier
Supplier's systems/services becoming unavailable with no restoration timeline
vectors: Not applicable — non-adversarial business-continuity event
rootCauses: Supplier financial distress not identified during vendor risk assessment
Lack of contractual data-escrow or transition-assistance provisions with the supplier
controls: Vendor financial-health monitoring as part of supplier risk assessment
Contractual data-escrow and transition-assistance provisions
Identified alternate/backup suppliers for critical functions
ITID-54932.detection: Detection relies on external notification, public reporting, or the supplier simply becoming unresponsive; proactive financial-health monitoring can provide advance warning.
ITID-54932.response: Initiate emergency transition to an alternate supplier; pursue contractual data-recovery/escrow provisions to retrieve company data or assets held by the failed supplier.
metrics: Time to identify and onboard an alternate supplier
Business function downtime during transition
Data/asset recovery outcome from the failed supplier
ITID-54932.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a business-continuity event driven by supplier insolvency, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Supplier Bankruptcy/Business Failure Causing Sudden Service Loss
playbook.description: A key supplier's bankruptcy or sudden business failure results in an abrupt loss of a service or product the organization depends on.

steps.title: Confirm the supplier's business failure and immediate service loss
steps.desc: Confirm the supplier has ceased operations or filed for bankruptcy, and determine which services/products are immediately affected.
steps.guidance: Verify through public filings, direct supplier communication, or industry news; confirm actual service cessation versus rumor.
steps.outcome: Business failure confirmed with immediate service impact identified.

steps.title: Assess business impact and contractual/legal exposure
steps.desc: Determine the business impact of the sudden service loss and assess contractual obligations, prepaid amounts, or legal exposure related to the supplier relationship.
steps.guidance: Engage Legal and procurement to review the supplier contract.
steps.outcome: Business impact and contractual exposure documented.

steps.title: Activate alternate supplier or emergency sourcing
steps.desc: Engage a pre-identified alternate supplier or initiate emergency sourcing to restore the affected service/product.
steps.guidance: Follow the supply-chain contingency plan; expedite onboarding/contracting where necessary.
steps.outcome: Alternate supplier engaged to restore service continuity.
steps.abort: If no alternate supplier is readily available, prioritize which business functions can operate without the service temporarily.

steps.title: Engage Legal and procurement regarding contractual and asset recovery matters
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal and procurement on any recoverable assets, prepaid funds, data extraction from the failed supplier, and bankruptcy proceedings participation if applicable.
steps.outcome: Legal and procurement engaged on contractual/asset matters.

steps.title: Notify affected internal teams and customers of the service change
steps.desc: Communicate the supplier's business failure and its impact on the affected service/product to internal teams and customers.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Extract any organizational data or assets held by the failed supplier
steps.desc: Urgently attempt to retrieve any organizational data, systems access, or physical assets held by the supplier before access is permanently lost.
steps.guidance: Act quickly, as access to the failed supplier's systems may be revoked or the company liquidated.
steps.outcome: Data/assets recovered to the maximum feasible extent.
steps.abort: If data/assets cannot be recovered, document the loss and its business impact.

steps.title: Fully onboard the alternate supplier and validate service continuity
steps.desc: Complete onboarding of the alternate supplier/sourcing arrangement and validate that the affected business function is fully restored.
steps.guidance: Run validation checks on the new supplier relationship's service quality and integration.
steps.outcome: Business function fully restored via the alternate supplier.

steps.title: Review supplier financial-health monitoring and diversification strategy
steps.desc: Assess whether supplier financial-health monitoring and diversification (avoiding single points of failure) were adequate.
steps.guidance: Recommend ongoing supplier financial-risk monitoring and multi-sourcing strategies for critical dependencies.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54933.def: A supplier-related disruption affecting company operations that has not yet been classified as a technical system outage or a business-failure/bankruptcy event.
ITID-54933.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for supplier system failure events not yet attributed to a technical outage or a business-failure/bankruptcy cause.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported supplier disruptions pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any disruption once root cause is confirmed (reclassify to ITID-54931 or 54932)
ITID-54933.severity: Inherit from observed business impact until reclassified.
ITID-54933.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain management for initial triage.
indicators: Supplier-related disruption without an established specific cause
vectors: Not yet determined — pending triage
rootCauses: Not yet determined — pending triage
controls: Incident triage and classification workflow
ITID-54933.detection: Relies on initial supplier communication/status signals only.
ITID-54933.response: Triage to technical-outage or business-failure cause, then reclassify.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
ITID-54933.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf; should not remain the final classification of a closed incident.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supplier System Failure
playbook.description: A key supplier's system failure of undetermined specific cause disrupts the organization's dependent operations.

steps.title: Confirm the supplier system failure and its operational impact
steps.desc: Confirm the supplier's system has failed and identify how it is affecting dependent organizational operations.
steps.guidance: Check integration monitoring/error logs and contact the supplier for confirmation.
steps.outcome: Failure confirmed with operational impact identified.

steps.title: Assess business impact and available alternatives
steps.desc: Determine the scope of business impact and identify available manual workarounds or alternate suppliers.
steps.outcome: Impact and alternatives documented.

steps.title: Activate manual workaround or alternate supplier channel
steps.desc: Switch to a manual process or alternate supplier channel to maintain operational continuity.
steps.guidance: Follow the supply-chain contingency plan for this supplier relationship.
steps.outcome: Operations continuing via workaround or alternate channel.

steps.title: Engage the supplier's support/account team for resolution status
steps.desc: Escalate through the supplier relationship, referencing contractual SLA terms, to obtain a resolution timeline.
steps.outcome: Supplier engaged with a resolution ETA obtained.

steps.title: Notify affected internal teams of the disruption status
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption's status and expected resolution timeline to affected internal teams.
steps.guidance: Provide a clear next-update cadence.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Confirm supplier system restoration
steps.desc: Track the supplier's confirmation of resolution and validate integration functionality before resuming normal operations.
steps.guidance: Perform a test transaction before full cutover.
steps.outcome: Supplier system confirmed restored and validated.

steps.title: Reconcile workaround-period data with the restored system
steps.desc: Reconcile any manually processed transactions or data with the restored supplier system, validating accuracy.
steps.outcome: Data reconciled with verified accuracy.

steps.title: Review supplier redundancy and contingency plan effectiveness
steps.desc: Assess whether alternate-supplier options and contingency procedures were adequate for this failure.
steps.guidance: Recommend supplier diversification or improved contingency procedures as warranted.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked recommendations.

ITID-54941.def: A disruption to company operations caused by a confirmed software supply chain attack — a deliberate compromise of a third-party software vendor's build, update, or distribution process — tracked here for its critical-system-disruption business impact rather than the detailed compromise mechanics.
ITID-54941.purpose: Provides a brief company-impact framing for software supply chain attacks within the Critical System Disruption / Third-Party Disruptions domain, pointing back to the detailed compromise taxonomy tracked elsewhere.
scopeIncludes: Business-impact tracking of a confirmed software supply chain attack affecting company-deployed third-party software
Precautionary isolation/shutdown of systems running a component confirmed compromised via a supply chain attack
scopeExcludes: The detailed technical mechanics and initial-access taxonomy of software supply chain compromise (see ITID-31114)
Non-adversarial vendor outages or business failures (see ITID-5491x/5493x)
Compromise originating within the company's own CI/CD pipeline (see Code Injection and Tampering, ITID-5464x)
ITID-54941.severity: Critical if the compromised third-party software is deployed broadly across company production; High if confined to a limited set of systems.
ITID-54941.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a deployed third-party component was compromised via a supply chain attack.
ITID-54941.escalation: Escalate immediately to application security, the affected system owners, and vendor management; consider precautionary isolation of affected systems pending validation.
indicators: Vendor or industry disclosure confirming a supply chain compromise of a specific software product/update
Threat intelligence reporting matching the company's software bill of materials
Unexpected behavior or unauthorized network activity from systems running the affected software
vectors: Trojanized software update or installer distributed through the vendor's legitimate distribution channel
rootCauses: Lack of software bill of materials (SBOM) visibility into third-party software
Automatic trust of vendor-signed updates without independent verification
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Software bill of materials (SBOM) tracking
Staged/canary rollout of vendor updates before broad deployment
Network segmentation limiting blast radius of any single third-party component
ITID-54941.detection: Detection typically depends on vendor/industry disclosure or threat intelligence rather than internal telemetry alone, given the trusted nature of the compromised distribution channel.
ITID-54941.response: Isolate or roll back the affected component immediately upon confirmation; hunt for indicators of compromise across all systems running the affected version.
metrics: Time from disclosure to internal identification of affected systems
Time to isolate/remediate affected systems
ITID-54941.notes: Lone-child cross-reference leaf. This is a brief company-impact framing; see ITID-31114 for the detailed supply chain compromise technique breakdown, and ITID-54631 for the closely related Software and Patch Failures framing, rather than re-describing the mechanism here.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Software Supply Chain Attack (Third-Party Disruption Context)
playbook.description: A third-party software supply chain attack disrupts organizational operations through a compromised vendor product or update, with the specific vector not yet determined.

steps.title: Confirm the software supply chain attack and identify the affected vendor product
steps.desc: Correlate observed disruption/compromise indicators with a specific third-party software product, library, or update to confirm a supply chain attack.
steps.guidance: Check vendor security advisories, threat intelligence feeds, and software composition analysis (SCA) results for the affected product.
steps.outcome: Supply chain attack confirmed with the affected product/version identified.

steps.title: Determine full deployment scope of the compromised product
steps.desc: Identify every system, application, and environment where the compromised third-party product or update is deployed.
steps.guidance: Use the software bill of materials (SBOM) and asset inventory to trace all deployments.
steps.outcome: Full deployment scope documented.

steps.title: Isolate systems running the compromised product
steps.desc: Disconnect or restrict network access for all systems running the compromised product to prevent further impact.
steps.guidance: Prioritize business-critical systems for immediate isolation.
steps.outcome: Further impact from the compromised product contained.

steps.title: Halt further distribution/deployment of the compromised product
steps.desc: Block automatic updates or deployment pipelines from distributing the compromised version further within the environment.
steps.guidance: Pin package managers/deployment pipelines to the last known-good version.
steps.outcome: Further distribution of the compromised product halted.

steps.title: Notify the vendor, affected stakeholders, and relevant authorities
steps.desc: Report the compromise to the vendor for coordinated disclosure and notify internal stakeholders and, if required, regulatory bodies.
steps.outcome: Vendor and stakeholders notified.

steps.title: Remove the compromised product and any malicious artifacts
steps.desc: Uninstall or replace the compromised product with a verified clean version, and remove any malicious code or persistence it introduced.
steps.guidance: Verify the replacement version's integrity via vendor-provided checksums/signatures before redeployment.
steps.outcome: Compromised product and associated artifacts removed from all systems.

steps.title: Redeploy the verified clean product and validate system functionality
steps.desc: Redeploy the clean, verified version of the product and confirm affected systems function correctly.
steps.guidance: Run comprehensive validation and integrity checks before declaring recovery complete.
steps.outcome: Systems restored to normal function with the clean product verified.

steps.title: Review software supply chain security controls
steps.desc: Assess SBOM coverage, vendor security assessment processes, and update-verification practices; recommend improvements.
steps.guidance: Recommend signed-artifact verification and stronger vendor risk-management practices.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published with tracked supply-chain security improvement actions.
